What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, chest, urinary tract and other areas. It does not work against viral infections like the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall, which helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Disperse the tablet in water before taking it if instructed on the product label or by the pharmacist. Do not share or reuse leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion and vomiting may occur. Skin rash can also occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any allergy to cefixime, cephalosporins or penicillin-type antibiotics, and about kidney disease. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can cause resistance.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ears, throat, airways, urinary tract and other infections when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall, which helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. The dispersible tablet should be taken as directed on the product label or by the doctor. Do not share leftover antibiotics with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, vomiting, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporins or certain penicillin antibiotics, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a widespread skin rash.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ears, throat, lungs, urinary tract and other areas. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from making their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve, and do not share it with others. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion and vomiting. Mild rash may also occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney disease or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
Cefixime interferes with the formation of the bacterial cell wall. Ofloxacin blocks bacterial enzymes needed for growth and multiplication.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take it with antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc at the same time; follow the prescriber's or product label's instructions about spacing.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, indigestion, headache, dizziness or vomiting.

Precautions
Do not use if there is a known allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporins, penicillins or ofloxacin/other quinolone antibiotics. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash or breathing difficulty, unusual nerve symptoms, or pain/swelling in a tendon. Use only on medical advice during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in people with kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, seizures or a history of tendon disorders.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of acidity, heartburn, indigestion and gas-related bloating or discomfort.

How does it work?
Aluminium hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide neutralise excess stomach acid. Simethicone helps gas bubbles join together so trapped gas can pass more easily.

How to take/use it
Shake the suspension well before use. Measure it with the supplied measuring device and take it exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Keep a 2–4 hour gap from other medicines unless a doctor or pharmacist advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Constipation or loose stools, nausea, stomach cramps and a chalky or unpleasant taste may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease. Do not use for a prolonged period without medical advice. Consult a doctor if symptoms are severe, keep returning, or do not improve. Tell a doctor or pharmacist about other medicines, as antacids can affect their absorption.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat a range of bacterial infections caused by susceptible bacteria. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills bacteria by interfering with their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes that can make some bacteria resistant to it.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Swallow with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share this medicine or use leftover tablets.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxicillin, other penicillin-type antibiotics or certain cephalosporins. Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related jaundice or severe diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe skin rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with potassium clavulanate injection is used to treat certain bacterial infections, including serious infections when treatment by injection is needed. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against a wider range of infections.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and other factors, so it should be used exactly as prescribed. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash, injection-site discomfort and irritation of the vein may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillins, cephalosporins or similar antibiotics. Tell the healthcare professional about kidney or liver problems and any previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea or colitis. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Amoxicillin with clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ears, sinuses, throat, lungs, skin, urinary tract and teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxicillin kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps protect amoxicillin from enzymes produced by some bacteria, allowing it to work against a wider range of infections.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet with water, complete the prescribed course, and do not share it with others. Do not take an extra dose if a dose is missed without following medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, headache, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take this medicine if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxicillin, clavulanate or similar antibiotics. Tell the prescriber about liver problems, previous antibiotic-related jaundice, kidney disease, allergies or current medicines. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial or throat swelling, severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can promote resistance.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ears, sinuses, throat, lungs, skin, urinary tract and teeth, when prescribed by a healthcare professional. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes made by some resistant bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics or take them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach discomfort, headache, skin rash and oral or vaginal thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, clavulanate or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Tell the healthcare professional about liver disease, kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, or glandular fever. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe skin rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can lead to resistance.

What is it used for?
Used to treat various bacterial infections when prescribed by a healthcare professional. It does not work against viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Potassium clavulanate helps amoxycillin work against bacteria that can otherwise resist it.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed and preferably with food. Swallow with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin or related antibiotics. Inform the prescriber about liver or kidney problems, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, pregnancy, and other medicines being used. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, a severe rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, nose, throat, chest, skin, urinary tract and teeth, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes that can make some bacteria resistant to it.

How to take/use it
Use only in the dose and for the duration prescribed. Shake the suspension well before each use and measure it with the supplied measuring device. Take it with a meal if advised, and complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not use leftover medicine or share it with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and mild skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxicillin, clavulanate or similar antibiotics. Inform the doctor about previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, kidney disease, or allergies. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, or a severe skin rash. Contact a doctor for severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Use the reconstituted suspension only as directed on the label and store it as advised.

What is it used for?
This antibiotic is used to treat bacterial infections, such as certain infections of the ear, sinuses, throat, lungs, urinary tract, skin and teeth, when caused by bacteria sensitive to it. It does not treat viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Potassium clavulanate helps prevent some bacteria from breaking down amoxycillin, making it effective against a wider range of bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. If supplied as a dry syrup, it must be prepared as directed and shaken well before each use. Measure each dose with the supplied measuring device. Do not use leftover medicine or share it with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to penicillin, amoxycillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, kidney disease, or a history of severe antibiotic allergy. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, a severe rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only on medical advice, especially in children.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, nose, throat, chest, skin, urinary tract and teeth. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria. Clavulanic acid helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against a wider range of infections.

How to take/use it
Reconstitute the dry syrup exactly as directed on the label or by the pharmacist. Shake well before each use and measure with an oral syringe or measuring spoon. Take it with food if advised to reduce stomach upset, and complete the prescribed course even if feeling better. Do not use leftover medicine or share it with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to amoxycillin, penicillins or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Tell the doctor about previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, kidney disease, or a history of severe allergies. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe skin rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose, and watery or itchy eyes. It may also be prescribed as an add-on treatment for asthma related to allergies, but it does not relieve a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, a substance responsible for many allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, chemicals that contribute to allergic inflammation and narrowing of the airways.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. It may cause drowsiness in some people, so avoid driving until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhoea.

Precautions
This medicine is not a rescue treatment for a sudden asthma attack. Seek medical advice promptly if new or worsening mood or behaviour changes, nightmares, agitation, anxiety, depression, or suicidal thoughts occur. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other medicines that cause drowsiness.

What is it used for?
Used to help improve appetite and support weight gain in people with poor appetite or inadequate nutritional intake, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Cyproheptadine blocks certain histamine and serotonin effects and may stimulate appetite. Tricholine citrate and sorbitol are included as supportive ingredients in the formulation.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by the doctor. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device and do not take more than prescribed. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, increased appetite, nausea and stomach discomfort. Sorbitol may cause loose stools or abdominal discomfort in some people.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and use caution with sleeping tablets, sedatives or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Tell the doctor if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, prostate problems, asthma, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe sleepiness, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This syrup is used for temporary relief of dry cough and cold symptoms such as a blocked or runny nose, sneezing and watery eyes.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps reduce the urge to cough. Chlorpheniramine reduces allergy-like symptoms, while phenylephrine helps relieve nasal blockage.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Shake the bottle well and measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device, not a household spoon. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other cough, cold or decongestant medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea and stomach upset. Some people may experience nervousness, a fast heartbeat or increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if sleepy or dizzy. Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, prostate or urination problems, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not use with MAO inhibitor medicines or within 14 days of stopping them; check before use with antidepressants or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice if the cough is severe, lasts several days, or is accompanied by breathing difficulty, chest pain or high fever.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cough, blocked or runny nose, sneezing and other symptoms associated with common cold or allergy-related upper respiratory conditions.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps suppress coughing. Chlorpheniramine reduces allergy symptoms such as sneezing and runny nose, while phenylephrine helps relieve nasal congestion.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth only as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other cough, cold or decongestant medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, nervousness or difficulty sleeping. Phenylephrine may cause a fast heartbeat or a temporary increase in blood pressure.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, difficulty passing urine or liver disease. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines, and check with a healthcare professional before use with antidepressants or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice for breathing difficulty, severe or persistent cough, or symptoms that do not improve.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cough, blocked nose, runny nose and sneezing associated with the common cold.

How does it work?
Chlorpheniramine reduces allergy-like symptoms such as runny nose and sneezing. Dextromethorphan helps reduce coughing, while phenylephrine relieves nasal blockage by narrowing swollen blood vessels in the nose.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the softgel whole. Do not take more than recommended or combine it with other cough-and-cold medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, nervousness, headache, increased blood pressure or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines or within 14 days of stopping them. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, difficulty passing urine or an enlarged prostate. Consult a doctor during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty or a persistent or worsening cough.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of dry cough and cold- or allergy-related symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan reduces the urge to cough. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that helps relieve symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Use the measuring device provided. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea or stomach discomfort.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines, and check with a doctor or pharmacist before using it with antidepressants or other cough, cold or antihistamine medicines. Seek medical advice for breathing difficulty, persistent or worsening cough, or a cough with significant phlegm. Use in children only as directed by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
This syrup is used to relieve dry, irritating cough associated with colds or allergies. It may also help reduce allergy-related symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan reduces the cough reflex. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that helps relieve allergy symptoms such as runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Use the measuring device provided and do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not combine with other cough, cold or allergy medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea or stomach upset may occur.

Precautions
This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol until its effects are known. Seek medical advice before use if taking antidepressants or monoamine oxidase inhibitors, or if there is glaucoma, difficulty urinating or prostate enlargement. Consult a doctor for children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, severe dizziness, confusion or a cough that persists or worsens.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with phlegm and chest congestion, especially when mucus is difficult to bring up and there is wheezing or narrowing of the airways.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus, making it easier to cough out. Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles of the airways and helps improve breathing.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Shake the bottle well before use and measure the syrup with a proper measuring device. Do not exceed the recommended amount or combine it with other cough medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, headache, dizziness, tremor, nervousness, fast heartbeat or palpitations.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Seek medical help for worsening breathing difficulty, chest pain, severe palpitations, or signs of an allergic reaction. Consult a doctor if the cough persists or is accompanied by high fever or blood-stained mucus.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve productive cough with mucus and chest congestion, and to help ease wheezing or breathing difficulty caused by narrowed airways.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus so it can be coughed out more easily. Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping improve airflow.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Shake the bottle well before use and measure each dose with a proper measuring device. Do not exceed the recommended amount or combine with other cough, cold or bronchodilator medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Trembling, nervousness, headache, dizziness, fast heartbeat or palpitations, nausea, vomiting, stomach upset and diarrhoea.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Seek urgent medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, or signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood, bones and joints, and meningitis. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a doctor or nurse as an injection into a vein or muscle. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, swelling or redness at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, rash and changes in blood-test results may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to ceftriaxone, cephalosporin or penicillin antibiotics, or a history of severe antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or yellowing of the skin or eyes. This injection requires special medical consideration in newborn babies and in people with liver or kidney problems.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone is an antibiotic injection used to treat a wide range of serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin, abdomen, blood, bones and joints. It may also be used for certain sexually transmitted bacterial infections when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How to take/use it
Ceftriaxone is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and should be decided by the prescriber. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; rash; and changes in blood test results.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillin or other cephalosporin antibiotics, and about liver, kidney or gallbladder problems. Seek medical help for difficulty breathing, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Do not use it for viral infections or without medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone is an antibiotic used to treat a wide range of serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, blood, urinary tract, skin, abdomen and brain. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional into a muscle or vein. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, swelling or tenderness at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; and skin rash.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any previous allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillin or other cephalosporin antibiotics. Seek medical help urgently for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Contact a doctor if severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea develops during or after treatment. Use only under medical supervision, especially in newborn babies or people with liver or kidney problems.

What is it used for?
This injection is used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood, bones and joints, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps ceftriaxone work against certain bacteria that can otherwise resist some antibiotics.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a doctor or nurse as an injection into a vein or muscle. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, age, and kidney or liver function. Do not self-inject or stop treatment early unless advised by the doctor.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; rash; and changes in blood test results may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics, and about kidney, liver or gallbladder problems. Seek urgent medical help for difficulty breathing, facial swelling, a severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. This medicine should be used in newborns and during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone with sulbactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin and soft tissues, blood, bones or joints. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps protect ceftriaxone from enzymes produced by some bacteria, improving its activity.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or nurse into a vein or muscle. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and should be decided by the prescriber. Complete the prescribed course unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, rash and changes in liver test results may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics, and about liver, kidney or gallbladder problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
This prescription injection is used to treat serious bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Tazobactam helps protect ceftriaxone from enzymes made by some resistant bacteria.

How to take/use it
It is given by a doctor or nurse as an injection into a vein or muscle. The dose, frequency and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, so follow the healthcare professional’s instructions. Do not self-inject or stop treatment early.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, skin rash, and pain, redness or swelling at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, other cephalosporins, penicillins or other antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems, gallbladder disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe skin rash, or severe or bloody diarrhoea. This medicine requires special precautions in newborn babies and with calcium-containing intravenous solutions.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with potassium clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills bacteria by disrupting their protective cell wall. Potassium clavulanate helps prevent some bacteria from breaking down amoxycillin, making the antibiotic effective against a wider range of bacteria.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions for the route, timing and duration of treatment. Do not stop treatment early or share it with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin or similar antibiotics. Inform the doctor about previous antibiotic-related liver problems or jaundice. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ear, sinuses, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, and teeth. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by interfering with their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps protect amoxycillin from bacterial enzymes that can make it ineffective.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Take it with a meal or snack to help reduce stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them for a future illness.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, cephalosporin antibiotics or this medicine. What is it used for?
Hydrocortisone sodium injection is a corticosteroid used in hospitals for severe allergic or inflammatory conditions and when the body needs urgent replacement of the hormone cortisol, such as in adrenal insufficiency. It may also be used for other serious conditions when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone cortisol and reduces inflammation, swelling and overactive immune reactions. It also helps support the body during cortisol deficiency.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and duration depend on the condition and response to treatment.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar or blood pressure, stomach upset, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, fluid retention and pain at the injection site may occur. The risk of side effects is higher with higher doses or prolonged treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body’s ability to fight infections and may mask infection symptoms. Do not stop prolonged treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, severe swelling, vision changes or signs of a serious infection.

What is it used for?
This syrup is used to relieve cough with mucus and breathing difficulty or wheezing associated with certain respiratory conditions. It helps loosen and clear mucus and relaxes narrowed airways.

How does it work?
Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles around the airways to improve airflow. Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus, making it easier to cough up.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or as stated on the label. Use the measuring device provided and do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not use it for longer than advised without medical guidance.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, tremors, throat irritation or palpitations may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, seizure disorder or a history of sensitivity to any ingredient. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, a fast or irregular heartbeat, or an allergic reaction. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole dusting powder is used to treat fungal infections of the skin, such as athlete’s foot, ringworm and fungal infections in skin folds.

How does it work?
It prevents fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which stops their growth and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply the powder to clean, dry, affected skin as directed on the pack or by a healthcare professional. Keep the area dry and wash hands before and after use. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, burning, itching, redness or discomfort at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to clotrimazole. Avoid applying to the eyes or swallowing it. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops, or if the infection does not improve or becomes worse.

What is it used for?
Linezolid is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by certain Gram-positive bacteria, including some types of pneumonia, skin and soft-tissue infections, and infections caused by vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE).

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a healthcare professional. It should be used only as prescribed, and the treatment course should not be stopped without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, and changes in blood counts such as anaemia or low platelets.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any blood disorder, liver or kidney problem, or allergy to linezolid. Medicines such as antidepressants, monoamine oxidase inhibitors, and some cold or decongestant medicines may interact with linezolid. Blood tests may be needed, especially during prolonged treatment. Seek medical help for unusual bruising or bleeding, severe or persistent diarrhoea, vision changes, numbness, or weakness.

What is it used for?
Luliconazole 1% cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch. It helps relieve symptoms such as itching, redness and scaling caused by these infections.

How does it work?
It blocks the production of an important substance that fungi need to build their cell membranes. This stops the growth of the fungus and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin as directed by a doctor or the product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not cover the area with a tight dressing unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site may occur.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Do not apply to broken or severely irritated skin unless advised by a doctor. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs. Consult a doctor if the infection worsens or does not improve as expected.

What is it used for?
Luliconazole 1% cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch. It helps relieve symptoms such as itching, redness and scaling caused by these infections.

How does it work?
It is an antifungal medicine that blocks the growth of fungi by interfering with the formation of an essential part of their cell membrane.

How to take/use it
For use on the skin only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed by the doctor or product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not swallow or apply inside the eyes, mouth or vagina. Avoid applying to broken skin unless advised by a doctor. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Use only for the condition it was prescribed or recommended for.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and swelling, such as pain affecting muscles, joints or after minor injuries or procedures.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps relieve pain and reduce fever. Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation, while serratiopeptidase may help reduce inflammatory swelling.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache. Allergic reactions may occur rarely.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine or seek medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or asthma triggered by painkillers. Tell the doctor if taking blood thinners or other painkillers. Avoid during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless specifically prescribed. Stop and seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin rash.

What is it used for?
Acetaminophen (paracetamol) is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, body pain, toothache and aches associated with colds.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of chemicals in the brain that contribute to pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Use the measuring device provided. Do not take it with other medicines containing acetaminophen or paracetamol, and do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
It is usually well tolerated when used as directed. Nausea, vomiting or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Use only after medical advice if there is liver disease or regular alcohol use. An overdose can cause serious liver damage, even if there are no immediate symptoms. Stop use and seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction, severe rash, or suspected overdose.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold and flu symptoms such as fever, headache, body aches, blocked nose and runny nose.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and pain. Phenylephrine helps relieve nasal congestion, while diphenhydramine reduces runny nose and sneezing; caffeine may enhance pain relief and reduce tiredness.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol, diphenhydramine, phenylephrine or similar decongestants.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, headache, nervousness, difficulty sleeping, or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving, alcohol and activities requiring alertness until its effects are known. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, or difficulty passing urine. Ask a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, allergic reactions, or symptoms that worsen or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Acetaminophen is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, headache, toothache and pain from colds.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the body that contribute to pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Shake the suspension well and measure it with the supplied measuring device. Do not take it with other medicines containing acetaminophen or paracetamol.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur. Side effects are usually uncommon when used as directed.

Precautions
Do not exceed the recommended amount, as overdose can cause serious liver damage even before symptoms appear. Consult a doctor before use if there is liver disease, regular alcohol use, or an allergy to acetaminophen. Stop use and seek medical help for severe rash, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful musculoskeletal conditions, such as muscle pain, joint pain, inflammation, stiffness and muscle spasms.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces inflammation and pain, while paracetamol helps relieve pain. Chlorzoxazone relaxes painful, tight muscles and helps reduce muscle spasm.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the modified-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Taking it after food may help reduce stomach discomfort. Do not take other medicines containing paracetamol or aceclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness, drowsiness and headache may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery if dizzy or drowsy. Inform the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart problems, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to painkillers. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed, particularly during the last three months. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or unusual severe weakness.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions. It may also help reduce fever and general body pain.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to painkillers. Avoid excessive alcohol. Do not use during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically advised. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, facial swelling or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful muscle spasms, stiffness and inflammation associated with musculoskeletal conditions such as back pain and other muscle or joint problems.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Thiocolchicoside helps relax tense skeletal muscles and relieve muscle spasm.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness, drowsiness and headache.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, seizures, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid taking it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised. It should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for painful muscle spasms and pain caused by muscle, joint or other musculoskeletal conditions. It helps reduce pain, swelling and muscle stiffness.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Thiocolchicoside helps relax tight or spasming muscles.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid driving if it causes dizziness or drowsiness.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and drowsiness may occur. Serious stomach bleeding, allergic reactions, liver or kidney problems and seizures are uncommon but require prompt medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems, seizures, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially the later months, and while breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor. Do not combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac or aspirin unless advised. Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty, swelling or a seizure.

What is it used for?
Amikacin injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections caused by susceptible bacteria, including certain infections of the blood, lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, bones and joints. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amikacin kills bacteria by interfering with their ability to make essential proteins.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein or muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, body weight and kidney function. Do not self-inject or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea, vomiting and headache may occur. More serious effects can include hearing or balance problems and kidney problems.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and any muscle or nerve disorder. Kidney function and, when needed, hearing may be monitored during treatment. Seek medical help for reduced urine, swelling, ringing in the ears, hearing loss, severe dizziness or difficulty breathing. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially those that may affect the kidneys or hearing.

What is it used for?
Amikacin injection is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, especially infections caused by certain bacteria that may not respond to other antibiotics. It is usually given in a hospital or clinic under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents them from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and response to treatment. Do not self-inject or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea, vomiting and headache may occur. More serious effects include hearing or balance problems and kidney problems.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, or muscle-weakness disorders. Kidney function and, when needed, hearing should be monitored during treatment. Seek medical help for reduced urination, swelling, ringing in the ears, hearing loss, dizziness or severe weakness. Inform the doctor if pregnant, breastfeeding or taking other medicines that may affect the kidneys or hearing.

What is it used for?
Amikacin injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, especially infections caused by certain bacteria that may be resistant to other antibiotics. It is commonly used in hospitals under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills or prevents them from growing.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type of infection, kidney function and other factors. Do not self-inject or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea, vomiting and headache may occur. More serious effects include kidney problems, hearing loss, ringing in the ears or dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Kidney function and hearing may need monitoring during treatment. Seek medical help urgently for reduced urination, ringing in the ears, hearing changes, severe dizziness, muscle weakness or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
This topical gel is used for temporary relief of minor muscle and joint aches and pains, including discomfort related to strains, sprains or arthritis.

How does it work?
Menthol produces a cooling sensation that helps reduce the feeling of pain. Capsaicin acts on pain-sensing nerves and may reduce pain signals with repeated use.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a small amount to the affected area as directed on the product label. Wash hands after application, unless the hands are being treated. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Temporary burning, stinging, warmth, redness, itching or skin irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth, nose and other sensitive areas. Do not cover tightly or apply with a heating pad. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe burning, swelling, blistering or an allergic reaction occurs. Keep away from children and avoid inhaling the gel or touching the eyes after application.

What is it used for?
Meropenem injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and other body areas. It is used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall, helping to stop the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
Meropenem is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse, usually in a hospital or clinical setting. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and other medical factors. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, headache, rash, and pain or inflammation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to meropenem, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, seizures or brain-related conditions, and if taking sodium valproate or valproic acid. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, seizures, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to provide vitamins and minerals and help prevent or correct dietary deficiencies. It is not a substitute for a balanced diet.

How does it work?
The vitamins and minerals support normal body functions, including energy metabolism, immunity and maintenance of bones, blood and tissues. The Pinus roxburghii extract provides an additional plant-based ingredient, but its specific benefit depends on the formulation.

How to take/use it
Take the tablet with water and follow the dose stated on the product label or recommended by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, stomach upset, constipation or diarrhoea. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur.

Precautions
Avoid taking it with other multivitamin or mineral supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or regular medicine use. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Betamethasone injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce severe inflammation and overactive immune reactions in conditions such as severe allergies, inflammatory disorders and some autoimmune conditions. Its exact use depends on the medical condition and the doctor's assessment.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune activity.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or nurse. The route, dose and duration depend on the condition being treated and should be decided by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Injection-site pain or redness, indigestion, increased appetite, sleep problems, mood changes, and temporary increases in blood sugar or blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions, liver or kidney problems, or any current or recent infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body's ability to fight infections and may mask infection symptoms. Do not stop repeated or prolonged treatment suddenly unless advised. Seek medical help for signs of infection, severe mood changes, breathing difficulty, or a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Fluconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections, including vaginal yeast infections, oral thrush and other susceptible fungal infections.

How does it work?
It blocks the production of an essential part of the fungal cell membrane, helping stop the fungus from growing.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth and swallow with water, with or without food, exactly as prescribed. Do not take extra doses or stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea and indigestion.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver or kidney disease, a heart-rhythm problem, or an allergy to antifungal medicines. Fluconazole can interact with several medicines, including warfarin and some medicines affecting heart rhythm. Use during pregnancy only on medical advice. Seek urgent help for severe rash, facial swelling, breathing difficulty, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or an unusual heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with phlegm and help ease wheezing or breathing difficulty caused by narrowed airways.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help loosen and clear mucus from the airways. Terbutaline relaxes the airway muscles, helping to improve breathing.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more or more often than advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, shakiness, nervousness, or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, chest pain, worsening breathing difficulty, or signs of an allergic reaction. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This prescription combination is used to treat certain bacterial and parasitic infections, including some mixed intestinal infections that may cause diarrhoea or dysentery. It should be used only when prescribed for a confirmed or suspected infection.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin stops susceptible bacteria from multiplying. Ornidazole damages the genetic material of certain parasites and anaerobic bacteria, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Do not take it with antacids or mineral supplements such as iron, calcium or magnesium at the same time; follow the advised time gap. Do not self-medicate for diarrhoea.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, metallic or unpleasant taste and indigestion.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 3 days after the last dose. Inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney or liver disease, seizures, heart-rhythm problems, tendon disorders or previous reactions to quinolone antibiotics. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, rash, breathing difficulty, or severe dizziness. This medicine does not treat viral infections.

What is it used for?
Used to treat certain bacterial and protozoal infections, including some gastrointestinal infections, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin is an antibiotic that stops susceptible bacteria from multiplying. Ornidazole acts against certain protozoa and anaerobic bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course. Do not stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Inform the doctor about other medicines, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and any history of seizures, tendon problems or heart rhythm disorders. Avoid alcohol during treatment with ornidazole and for at least 3 days after the last dose.

What is it used for?
Sildenafil 100 mg is used to treat erectile dysfunction (difficulty getting or keeping an erection firm enough for sexual activity). It helps achieve an erection only when there is sexual stimulation.

How does it work?
It improves blood flow to the penis by relaxing blood vessels during sexual stimulation. It works by blocking an enzyme called PDE5.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow it with water. Do not take more than prescribed. Follow the doctor's instructions about when to take it and whether it should be taken with food.

Common side effects
Headache, facial flushing, indigestion, stuffy nose, dizziness, nausea and visual changes such as blurred vision or changes in colour perception.

Precautions
Do not use sildenafil with nitrate medicines for chest pain or with riociguat, as this can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure. Tell the doctor about heart or blood-pressure problems, recent stroke or heart attack, liver or kidney disease, or use of alpha-blockers. Seek urgent medical help for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, sudden vision or hearing loss, chest pain, or severe dizziness.

What is it used for?
Sildenafil is mainly used to treat erectile dysfunction (difficulty getting or keeping an erection firm enough for sexual activity). It works only when there is sexual stimulation.

How does it work?
It increases blood flow to the penis by helping relax the blood vessels during sexual stimulation, making an erection easier to achieve and maintain.

Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. For erectile dysfunction, it is generally taken before sexual activity. Do not take it more often than advised, and follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Headache, flushing, indigestion, blocked or stuffy nose, dizziness, and changes in vision may occur.

Precautions

Seek urgent medical help for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, sudden vision or hearing loss, chest pain, or severe dizziness.

What is it used for?
Nimesulide is used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and fever, such as body pain, muscle or joint pain, and dental pain.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain, swelling and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor and do not use it for longer than recommended. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably after food. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or combine it with other painkillers unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Nimesulide can rarely cause serious liver problems. Stop taking it and seek medical help if there is yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, unusual tiredness, severe nausea or pain in the upper abdomen. Avoid it if there is liver disease, a stomach ulcer or bleeding, or an allergy to NSAIDs, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Avoid alcohol and consult a doctor before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or with kidney disease or blood-thinning medicines.

What is it used for?
Nimesulide is used for short-term relief of acute pain and inflammation, including painful joint or muscle conditions. It may also help reduce fever.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain, swelling and fever.

Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, preferably after food, with water. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than prescribed. Do not combine it with other painkillers or NSAIDs unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Artemether and lumefantrine is an antimalarial medicine used to treat uncomplicated malaria, especially malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum. It is not used to prevent malaria or to treat severe malaria, which needs urgent medical care.

It works by killing malaria parasites in the blood. Artemether acts quickly, while lumefantrine helps clear the remaining parasites.

Avoid other medicines that may affect heart rhythm unless advised by a doctor. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, severe dizziness, breathing difficulty, an irregular heartbeat, confusion, seizures or worsening malaria symptoms.

What is it used for?
Luliconazole 1% lotion is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch.

How does it work?
It blocks the production of an essential part of the fungal cell membrane, helping stop the growth of the fungus.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are the treated area. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes.

Common side effects
Mild application-site reactions such as redness, itching, irritation or burning may occur.

Do not use in the eyes, mouth or on other sensitive internal areas. Avoid applying to severely damaged skin unless advised by a doctor. What is it used for?
Eperisone is a muscle relaxant used to relieve painful muscle spasms, stiffness and increased muscle tightness associated with musculoskeletal conditions. It may also be used for muscle spasticity when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It acts mainly on the central nervous system to reduce excessive muscle tension and spasms. This can help improve movement and relieve related pain and stiffness.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food if advised. Swallow the sustained-release capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects

Precautions

What is it used for?

It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

This injection must be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. Do not self-inject. Use it only for the prescribed duration and do not take additional diclofenac or other painkillers of the same type unless advised by a doctor.

Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and pain or irritation at the injection site.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems, or an allergy to diclofenac or other NSAID painkillers. What is it used for?
Alpha-Beta Arteether is an injectable antimalarial used to treat malaria, especially severe or complicated malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum. Severe malaria requires urgent hospital treatment.

How does it work?
It is an artemisinin-based medicine that damages the malaria parasite and helps clear it from the blood.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional, usually in a hospital or clinic. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the severity of malaria and must be decided by the doctor. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, weakness, fever, and pain or reactions at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to artemisinin medicines, liver or kidney disease, heart rhythm problems, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical care for fainting, severe weakness, breathing difficulty, worsening fever, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Complete the treatment and attend follow-up as advised.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of pain, swelling and inflammation affecting the muscles and joints, including painful joint conditions.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain, while serratiopeptidase may help reduce swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor. Take it with or after food and swallow it with water. Do not take more than the prescribed amount, use it for longer than advised, or combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol or NSAIDs unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or a bleeding disorder. Avoid alcohol and use during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, only on medical advice. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin reactions, breathing difficulty or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Etoricoxib is used to reduce pain, swelling and inflammation in conditions such as osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis and acute gout. The specific condition and treatment duration should be decided by a doctor.

How does it work?
It selectively blocks COX-2 enzymes involved in producing prostaglandins, substances that cause pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than prescribed or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac or naproxen unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, headache, dizziness, swelling of the feet or legs and increased blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor before use if there is a history of heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure, stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney disease, liver disease or allergy to painkillers. It may increase the risk of heart attack, stroke, fluid retention and stomach bleeding, especially with long-term or high-dose use. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Seek medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, black stools, severe skin reactions or swelling of the face or throat.

What is it used for?
Etoricoxib is used to relieve pain and swelling caused by osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis. It may also be prescribed for acute gout or short-term dental pain.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation. It belongs to a group of medicines called selective COX-2 anti-inflammatory medicines.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth with water, exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole and do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. It may be taken with or without food.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, headache, dizziness, swelling of the feet or legs and increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about high blood pressure, heart disease, previous heart attack or stroke, stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, or an allergy to aspirin or other anti-inflammatory medicines. Avoid taking it with other anti-inflammatory painkillers unless advised. It may increase the risk of heart problems, especially with higher doses or long-term use. Seek medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, black stools, severe skin reactions or swelling of the face or throat. It should generally be avoided during pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks, unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve painful muscle spasms and the associated pain in musculoskeletal conditions, such as painful back or neck problems. It is generally used for short-term treatment when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Etoricoxib reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Thiocolchicoside helps relax tight or spasming muscles.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Do not take more often or for longer than advised. It may cause dizziness or sleepiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery if affected. Do not take it with other painkillers or anti-inflammatory medicines unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and sleepiness may occur. Seek medical help for severe stomach pain, black stools, swelling, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems, asthma triggered by painkillers, or seizures. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially late pregnancy, and while breastfeeding unless specifically advised. Women who could become pregnant should follow the prescriber’s advice about effective contraception. Avoid alcohol and seek advice before using this medicine with other medicines.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve pain and inflammation, especially in joint and muscle conditions such as arthritis. It may also be prescribed for other short-term painful conditions when considered suitable by a doctor.

How does it work?
Etoricoxib reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

Precautions

Avoid taking it with other etoricoxib-containing medicines or NSAIDs unless prescribed. It may not be suitable during pregnancy, especially later pregnancy. What is it used for?
Aceclofenac 100 mg is used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness caused by joint and muscle conditions such as osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow it with water. Do not take more than recommended or combine it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid or use only under medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to NSAIDs. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty or facial swelling. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially blood thinners, steroids and other painkillers. It should generally be avoided during the last 3 months of pregnancy and used in pregnancy only on medical advice.
