Used for short-term relief of pain, swelling and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint, bone and soft-tissue conditions.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac and paracetamol help reduce pain and inflammation through different actions. Trypsin and chymotrypsin are enzymes used to help reduce inflammatory swelling.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. It is generally taken with or after food to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more than the recommended dose, and do not combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol or painkillers such as ibuprofen unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for signs of stomach bleeding, severe allergy or breathing difficulty.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, bleeding disorders, or allergies to painkillers. Use caution with blood thinners and avoid excessive alcohol. It should generally be avoided during the last three months of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Do not use it with other paracetamol-containing medicines without medical advice.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of painful muscle spasms and other painful musculoskeletal conditions, such as back, neck, joint or soft-tissue pain, when inflammation and muscle tightness are present.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces pain and inflammation, while paracetamol provides additional pain relief. Thiocolchicoside helps relax tightened muscles and reduce muscle spasm.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor, preferably with or after food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take additional paracetamol-containing medicines or other painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor. Use for the shortest duration prescribed.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness, drowsiness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if allergic to any ingredient or if it has previously caused asthma, wheezing or an allergic reaction. Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma, or a history of seizures. Thiocolchicoside should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised; effective contraception may be required during treatment. Avoid alcohol and driving if dizzy or drowsy. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty or facial swelling.

What is it used for?
This is a topical antibacterial combination generally used to treat bacterial infections of the eye, when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Neomycin, bacitracin and sulphacetamide act against susceptible bacteria, helping stop their growth or kill them.

How to take/use it
Use only in the form and amount directed by the doctor or product label. Wash hands before and after use. If it is an eye preparation, do not touch the dropper or tube tip to the eye or other surfaces. Complete the prescribed course unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Temporary burning, stinging, irritation, redness or itching at the application site. Allergic reactions such as swelling or rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any of its ingredients or if a previous antibiotic caused a serious reaction. Use only for the prescribed infection; it does not treat viral or fungal infections. Seek medical advice for worsening symptoms, eye pain, vision changes, marked swelling or lack of improvement. Avoid wearing contact lenses during an eye infection unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming the protective cell wall they need to survive.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Do not skip doses or use leftover antibiotics. Swallow with water and follow the instructions on the prescription or product label.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and headache. Mild skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the prescriber about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections, including certain infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, chest, urinary tract and skin. It does not treat viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the prescribed dose and treatment duration, and complete the course even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them for colds and flu.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and headache. Mild skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to cefuroxime, penicillin or other cephalosporin antibiotics. Inform the doctor if there is kidney disease or a previous severe reaction to antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, a severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
This is a prescription antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefuroxime stops bacteria from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps protect cefuroxime from enzymes made by some resistant bacteria, allowing it to work more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share it with others or use leftover medicine. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics, penicillins, or related antibiotics. Seek medical advice for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, or a severe rash. Contact a doctor if severe or persistent diarrhoea develops, as this can occur during or after antibiotic treatment. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, chest, skin, and urinary tract. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Take the medicine with water and do not share it with others. Do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, cephalosporins, penicillins, or related antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, or any medicine allergies. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use antibiotics only when prescribed.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold and flu symptoms such as fever, headache, body aches, blocked or stuffy nose, runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Paracetamol reduces fever and pain. Phenylephrine helps reduce nasal congestion, while diphenhydramine reduces runny nose and sneezing; caffeine may support pain relief and reduce tiredness.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended or use it with other medicines containing paracetamol, diphenhydramine or a decongestant.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, nervousness, difficulty sleeping, palpitations or increased blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, overactive thyroid, difficulty urinating or regular heavy alcohol use. Check with a doctor or pharmacist during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or before use in children. Avoid use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold or allergy-related symptoms such as blocked or stuffy nose, runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Phenylephrine reduces swelling in the nasal passages, helping relieve congestion. Chlorpheniramine blocks histamine, which helps reduce sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid combining it with other cold or allergy medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea and headache may occur. Phenylephrine may sometimes cause a fast heartbeat or increased blood pressure.

Precautions
This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, diabetes, difficulty urinating or prostate problems. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) medicines, or within 14 days of stopping them, unless advised by a doctor. Consult a doctor before giving it to children, during pregnancy or while breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Triamcinolone acetonide is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and allergic reactions in conditions prescribed by a doctor. The exact use depends on the formulation and the condition being treated.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation, swelling, redness and allergic symptoms.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. The dose, treatment duration and route depend on the condition and formulation. Products containing 40 mg are often given as an injection by a healthcare professional and should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Pain or discomfort at the injection site, facial flushing, increased blood sugar, indigestion, mood or sleep changes, and fluid retention may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, liver or kidney problems, or any infection. Corticosteroids can weaken immunity and may mask signs of infection. Do not receive live vaccines or stop repeated treatment suddenly without medical advice. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only when specifically advised.

What is it used for?
Hydrocortisone sodium succinate injection is used under medical supervision to quickly reduce severe inflammation or allergic reactions. It may also be used to replace cortisol in people whose adrenal glands do not produce enough of this hormone. It is commonly given in hospital or emergency settings.

How does it work?
It is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation and overactivity of the immune system. It also provides a form of cortisol needed for important body functions.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a doctor or nurse as an injection into a vein or muscle. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the medical condition and response to treatment.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar or blood pressure, fluid retention, stomach upset, headache, dizziness, mood changes and difficulty sleeping may occur. Pain or irritation at the injection site is also possible.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions, liver or kidney problems, or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body's ability to fight infections and may hide infection symptoms. Do not stop prolonged treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor. Medical advice is needed before receiving live vaccines while using this medicine.

What is it used for?
Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactivity of the immune system. Doctors may prescribe it for severe allergies, inflammatory or autoimmune conditions, swelling, and certain other medical conditions.

How does it work?
It acts like natural steroid hormones made by the body. It reduces inflammation and suppresses excessive immune reactions.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food if it causes stomach upset. Do not change the dose or stop it suddenly, especially if it has been used for several days or longer, unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, fluid retention, increased blood sugar, and increased risk of infections may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health problems, or any infection. Avoid close contact with people who have infections and check before receiving vaccines. Long-term treatment requires medical monitoring. Seek medical advice for signs of infection, severe mood changes, vision problems, or severe stomach pain.

What is it used for?
Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and suppress an overactive immune response. It may be prescribed for certain allergic, inflammatory, autoimmune and other serious medical conditions, only under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and limits excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, especially after prolonged use. If it is taken by mouth, taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset.

Common side effects
Indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, increased blood sugar, fluid retention and weight gain. Longer use may cause skin thinning and increased risk of infections.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health problems, glaucoma or any current infection. Dexamethasone can mask signs of infection and may worsen some infections. Avoid live vaccines unless approved by the doctor. Seek medical advice before stopping it after regular or prolonged use.

What is it used for?
Faropenem is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the respiratory tract, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it without medical advice if there has been an allergy to faropenem, penicillins, cephalosporins or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or severe/persistent diarrhoea. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Used for the short-term relief of mild to moderate pain and fever, including body aches, headache, toothache, muscle pain and period pain.

How does it work?
Ibuprofen reduces pain, inflammation and fever. Paracetamol reduces pain and fever through a different mechanism, providing combined relief.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow with water; taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol, ibuprofen or other NSAIDs.

Common side effects
Indigestion, nausea, stomach pain, vomiting, dizziness and headache may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney or liver disease, or an allergy to ibuprofen, paracetamol, aspirin or other NSAIDs. Seek medical advice before use with blood thinners or other regular medicines, or if there is asthma, heart disease or high blood pressure. Avoid excessive alcohol. Do not use ibuprofen during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Stop and seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin reactions or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Gentamicin is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, especially infections caused by certain gram-negative bacteria. It is generally used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents them from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. The dose, frequency, duration and route depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function, and the product formulation. If supplied as an injection, it is usually administered by a healthcare professional. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, pain or irritation at the injection site, and skin rash may occur. More serious effects can include reduced urine output, hearing changes, ringing in the ears, dizziness or balance problems.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy, or neuromuscular disorders. Kidney function and, when needed, blood levels, hearing and balance may require monitoring. Use caution with other medicines that can affect the kidneys, hearing or nervous system. Seek medical advice promptly for reduced urination, swelling, unusual weakness, ringing in the ears, hearing loss or severe dizziness.

What is it used for?
Metronidazole infusion is used to treat serious infections caused by anaerobic bacteria and certain protozoa. It may be used when treatment through a vein is needed, as decided by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Metronidazole enters susceptible bacteria and protozoa and damages their genetic material, stopping them from surviving and multiplying.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a healthcare professional. The dose, infusion rate and treatment duration depend on the infection and clinical condition. It must not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, metallic taste and irritation at the infusion site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to metronidazole or similar medicines, liver disease, or a history of nerve problems or seizures. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose. Tell the doctor about all medicines being used, especially warfarin. Report numbness, tingling, severe rash, confusion or seizures promptly.

What is it used for?
Nimesulide is used for short-term relief of pain, swelling and inflammation, such as muscle or joint pain, toothache, period pain and other acute painful conditions. It may also help reduce fever when prescribed.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain, swelling and fever.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, preferably with or after food. Use the lowest effective amount for the shortest period advised. Do not take more than recommended or combine it with other painkillers without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain or indigestion, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it without medical advice if there is liver disease, a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney or heart problems, or an allergy to NSAIDs. Avoid alcohol and other medicines that may affect the liver. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding; it should not be used in the last three months of pregnancy. Stop it and seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe abdominal pain, unusual bleeding, breathing difficulty or a serious skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Cod liver oil is used as a dietary supplement to provide omega-3 fatty acids and vitamins A and D. It may help meet nutritional requirements when dietary intake is insufficient.

How does it work?
It supplies omega-3 fatty acids and fat-soluble vitamins that the body needs for normal health and body functions.

How to take/use it
Take the softgel capsules exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow with water, preferably with food. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Fishy aftertaste or burping, nausea, indigestion, stomach discomfort, or heartburn may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to fish or seafood. Avoid taking more than the recommended amount, as excess vitamins A and D can be harmful. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, if taking blood-thinning medicines, or if there is a bleeding disorder or liver disease. Tell a healthcare professional about other vitamin A or D supplements being taken.

What is it used for?
Sertaconazole 2% is a topical antifungal used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch, and other superficial fungal infections of the skin.

How does it work?
It damages the fungal cell membrane by interfering with the production of ergosterol, a substance fungi need to survive. This stops fungal growth and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Use it for the prescribed duration and avoid contact with the eyes, mouth, and other mucous membranes.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness, or irritation at the application site may occur.

Precautions
For external use only. Do not apply to the eyes, mouth, or severely broken skin. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash, or signs of an allergic reaction occur. Consult a doctor if the infection does not improve or worsens.

What is it used for?
ORS Liquid helps prevent and treat dehydration caused by diarrhoea, vomiting, or other fluid loss by replacing water and essential salts.

How does it work?
It contains water, salts and glucose, which help the intestines absorb fluids and restore the body's fluid and electrolyte balance.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth in small, frequent sips. Use it as supplied and follow the product label for storage and the time limit after opening. Do not add extra water or other ingredients unless instructed. If vomiting occurs, wait briefly and restart with small sips.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort or bloating may occur, especially if taken too quickly.

Precautions
Seek medical help for severe dehydration, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, blood in the stool, very little or no urine, unusual drowsiness, or inability to drink. Use with medical advice in severe kidney disease or when fluid or salt intake is restricted. Keep infants and children under close observation during diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
ORS Liquid is used to prevent or treat dehydration caused by diarrhoea, vomiting, or loss of fluids. It replaces water and essential salts lost from the body.

How does it work?
It contains a balanced combination of water, salts, and glucose. These help the intestine absorb fluids and restore the body's fluid and electrolyte balance.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Take small, frequent sips, especially if there is vomiting. Do not dilute or add ingredients unless instructed on the label. Use only within the recommended period after opening.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, or bloating may occur in some people.

Precautions
Seek medical care for severe dehydration, persistent vomiting, blood in the stool, high fever, confusion, very little urine, or worsening diarrhoea. Infants, older adults, and people with kidney disease, heart failure, or conditions requiring salt or fluid restriction should use it only with medical advice. ORS does not replace medical treatment when diarrhoea is severe or prolonged.

What is it used for?
ORS liquid is used to prevent and treat dehydration caused by diarrhoea, vomiting, or loss of fluids and salts. It replaces the water and electrolytes the body loses.

How does it work?
It contains a balanced combination of water, salts and glucose. These help the intestine absorb fluids and electrolytes more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth as supplied, in small, frequent sips. Do not dilute or mix it with other drinks unless the product label directs. Follow the storage and use instructions on the pack, and do not use it if it is past its expiry date.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, bloating or stomach discomfort may occur, especially if taken too quickly.

Precautions
Seek medical advice if there is severe dehydration, persistent vomiting, blood in the stool, confusion, very little urine, or inability to drink. People with kidney disease, heart failure, or other conditions requiring fluid or salt restriction should use it only on medical advice. Infants, young children and older adults may need prompt medical assessment if dehydration is suspected.

What is it used for?
Vancomycin is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by certain Gram-positive bacteria, including some infections caused by MRSA. When taken by mouth, it is used for certain infections of the intestine, such as Clostridioides difficile infection.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from growing.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. The route depends on the formulation and infection: injectable vancomycin is usually given into a vein by a healthcare professional, while oral vancomycin is used for specific intestinal infections. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, pain or inflammation at the injection site, and infusion-related flushing or itching. Kidney problems and hearing changes can occur, especially with injectable treatment, and require medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing problems, or previous allergy to vancomycin. Kidney function and, when needed, blood levels may be monitored during injectable treatment. Injectable vancomycin must be given at the recommended rate because rapid infusion can cause flushing, itching, low blood pressure, or breathing difficulty. Seek urgent medical help for severe rash, breathing difficulty, reduced urination, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Vancomycin is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by certain bacteria, including some resistant Gram-positive infections such as MRSA. Depending on the formulation, oral vancomycin may be used for certain intestinal infections, including Clostridioides difficile infection.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall, causing the bacteria to die.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. The route depends on the formulation: injectable vancomycin is usually given into a vein by a healthcare professional, while oral vancomycin is taken by mouth. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain or irritation at the injection site, nausea, rash, itching, flushing, and headache may occur. Diarrhoea can occur with antibiotics.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing problems, previous allergy to vancomycin, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Kidney function and sometimes blood levels may need monitoring, especially with injectable treatment. Rapid infusion can cause flushing, itching, low blood pressure, or breathing difficulty; seek urgent medical help if these occur. Use only for the infection prescribed, as it does not treat viral infections.

What is it used for?
This vitamin combination is used to help prevent or correct deficiencies of vitamin C, vitamin B12, folic acid and nicotinamide when dietary intake is inadequate or the body needs extra supplementation. These vitamins support normal blood cell formation, nerve function and general body processes.

How does it work?
It supplies essential vitamins needed for normal red blood cell production, nerve function, tissue maintenance and energy-related processes.

How to take/use it
Take or use it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount or take multiple vitamin products containing the same ingredients unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort or diarrhoea may occur. Unusual reactions are possible.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional about any kidney disease or history of kidney stones, iron-overload disorders, vitamin deficiencies or regular medicines. Folic acid may mask some signs of vitamin B12 deficiency, so unexplained anaemia or nerve symptoms should be medically assessed. Stop use and seek help if signs of an allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
This supplement is used to provide vitamin C and zinc, help prevent or correct dietary deficiencies, and support normal immune function, collagen formation and wound healing.

How does it work?
Vitamin C acts as an antioxidant and helps the body make collagen, which is important for skin and tissues. Zinc supports normal immune function and many enzyme processes in the body.

How to take/use it
Chew the tablet thoroughly and take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Taking it with food may reduce stomach upset.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, heartburn, diarrhoea, or a metallic taste may occur, especially with excessive intake.

Precautions
Avoid excessive or prolonged use. Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, iron-storage disease, or an allergy to any ingredient. Long-term high-dose zinc may cause copper deficiency. Ask a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking other medicines; zinc may interfere with the absorption of some antibiotics and thyroid medicines.

What is it used for?
Alkemvit Q10 Capsule is a Coenzyme Q10 supplement used to support normal energy production in cells and provide antioxidant support.

How does it work?
Coenzyme Q10 helps cells produce energy, particularly in tissues that need high energy. It also has antioxidant activity that helps protect cells from oxidative damage.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Swallow the capsule with water, preferably with food if advised. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, nausea, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, headache or difficulty sleeping may occur.

Precautions
Check with a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if taking warfarin, medicines for diabetes or blood pressure, or if there is an ongoing medical condition. Stop use and seek advice if an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for cough with phlegm, especially when mucus is thick or there is wheezing or narrowing of the airways. It helps loosen and clear mucus and makes breathing easier.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus so it can be coughed out more easily. Terbutaline relaxes the airway muscles and helps open the airways.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed by the doctor or as directed on the product label. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. If it is a liquid, measure each dose with the supplied measuring device.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach upset, headache, dizziness, tremor, nervousness, muscle cramps or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use only with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, low potassium or a history of seizures. Tell the doctor about pregnancy or breastfeeding before use. Seek medical attention for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, or a skin rash or swelling. Do not combine with other cough medicines unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Amoxicillin and cloxacillin are antibiotics used to treat bacterial infections caused by susceptible bacteria. They do not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Both medicines stop susceptible bacteria from making their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the prescribed timing and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share this medicine or use leftover antibiotics. Do not take a dose more often or for longer than prescribed.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin or related antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems and any previous antibiotic-related allergic reaction. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can cause resistance.

What is it used for?
Piperacillin + tazobactam is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, and other hospital-acquired infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Piperacillin kills bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Tazobactam helps protect piperacillin from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against a wider range of infections.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection or intravenous infusion by a doctor or nurse, usually in a hospital or clinical setting. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Use it only as prescribed and complete the prescribed course unless the treating doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, rash, headache, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it without medical advice if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, other beta-lactam antibiotics, or cephalosporins. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, bleeding problems, seizures, or previous antibiotic-related severe diarrhoea. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, a severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea. The doctor may monitor kidney function and blood tests during prolonged treatment.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat scabies and lice infestations. It should be used only when recommended by a doctor or pharmacist.

How does it work?
Gamma benzene hexachloride kills scabies mites and lice by affecting their nervous system. Cetrimide acts as an antiseptic on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the affected skin exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Avoid the eyes, mouth, inside of the nose, and broken or inflamed skin. Wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated. Do not swallow or use more than recommended.

Common side effects
Temporary skin irritation, redness, burning, dryness, itching, or rash may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice in children, older adults, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or in people with a history of seizures. Avoid use on large areas, broken skin, or under airtight coverings unless specifically advised. Stop use and seek urgent medical help if severe dizziness, tremors, confusion, or seizures occur. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain, inflammation and swelling associated with muscle or joint injuries, arthritis, dental pain and inflammation after some procedures.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Serratiopeptidase is an enzyme that may help reduce inflammatory swelling.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Take it with or after food and swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not take it with other diclofenac or NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache. Serratiopeptidase may also cause stomach upset or skin rash.

Precautions
Avoid use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney or liver disease, serious heart disease, or allergy to diclofenac, aspirin or other NSAIDs. Use only on medical advice during pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks and in the last 3 months. Inform the doctor about asthma triggered by painkillers, high blood pressure, bleeding problems, or use of blood thinners. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, chest pain or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
This supplement provides calcium, vitamin D3 and folic acid. It helps support strong bones and teeth, calcium absorption, and normal red blood cell formation. It may be used when dietary intake of these nutrients is inadequate or when supplementation is recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Calcium helps maintain bones, teeth, muscles and nerves. Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium, while folic acid supports normal cell growth and red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, so ask a pharmacist about the appropriate time to take it with other medicines.

Common side effects
Constipation, gas, bloating, nausea or stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, or high calcium levels. Seek advice before use with thyroid medicines, certain antibiotics, iron supplements or other calcium/vitamin D products. The listed folic acid strength is high; use this product under healthcare professional guidance, especially if there may be vitamin B12 deficiency.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to support bone health and help manage conditions such as osteoporosis or low calcium levels, when prescribed by a doctor. It may help maintain bone strength and calcium balance.

How does it work?
Calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D, helps the body absorb calcium. Calcium supports bone strength, while vitamin K2-7 helps direct calcium toward bones and supports normal bone metabolism.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Calcium carbonate is generally better absorbed with food. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and do not use additional calcium or vitamin D supplements unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort or abdominal pain may occur. Excess calcium can cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness or vomiting.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or other vitamin D or calcium supplements. Use cautiously with medicines such as warfarin, thyroid medicines, iron supplements, and certain antibiotics; these may need dose separation or medical supervision. Seek medical advice if symptoms of high calcium develop.

What is it used for?
Amorolfine 0.25% is a topical antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the affected skin exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Keep the area clean and dry, and wash hands before and after use. Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or stinging at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to amorolfine or any of its ingredients. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs, or if the infection worsens or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Amorolfine 0.25% is used on the skin to treat fungal infections such as athlete’s foot, ringworm, fungal infections of the groin or body, pityriasis versicolor and some yeast infections of the skin.

How does it work?
It blocks the production of substances that fungi need to build their cell membrane. This stops the growth and spread of the fungus.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to clean, dry, affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor or the product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site. Stop use and seek medical advice if a severe rash or allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Do not apply to the eyes or swallow it. Avoid applying to severely damaged or irritated skin unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical advice if the infection does not improve, gets worse or keeps returning. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Keep the affected area clean and dry, and do not share towels or clothing.

What is it used for?
Atropine sulphate is used by healthcare professionals to treat certain dangerously slow heartbeats. It may also be used in emergencies such as some types of poisoning and to reduce excessive body secretions before certain procedures.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of acetylcholine, a chemical messenger in the body. This can increase the heart rate and reduce certain secretions.

How to take/use it
This medicine should be given only by a healthcare professional. The route and dose depend on the medical condition being treated and the prescribed formulation.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, blurred vision, increased heart rate, constipation, difficulty passing urine, dizziness and reduced sweating may occur.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about glaucoma, prostate or urinary problems, heart conditions, fever, or sensitivity to atropine. Reduced sweating can cause overheating. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, confusion, breathing difficulty, or inability to pass urine.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of itching and minor skin irritation, such as from insect bites, mild rashes, sunburn, or other minor skin reactions.

How does it work?
Calamine helps soothe and protect irritated skin. Diphenhydramine reduces itching by blocking the action of histamine in the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected area as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Do not apply to large areas, broken skin or infected skin unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Mild skin dryness, redness, burning, irritation or rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not swallow or use near the eyes. Stop use if irritation or an allergic reaction develops. Avoid covering the treated area tightly unless advised. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, widespread, worsening or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Artesunate injection is used under medical supervision to treat severe malaria, especially when rapid treatment is needed or oral medicines cannot be taken.

How does it work?
Artesunate rapidly kills malaria parasites in the blood, helping to reduce the severity of the infection.

How to take/use it
This medicine must be reconstituted and given by a qualified healthcare professional by injection. The route, dose and treatment schedule depend on the severity of malaria and the treatment protocol. It should not be self-administered. A complete follow-on antimalarial treatment may be needed as prescribed.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, fever, abdominal discomfort and injection-site discomfort may occur. Delayed loss of red blood cells (haemolytic anaemia) can occur after treatment and requires medical monitoring.

Precautions
Severe malaria is a medical emergency and requires hospital care. Tell the doctor about any previous reaction to artesunate or other antimalarial medicines. Medical follow-up may be needed for several weeks after treatment to check for delayed anaemia or other complications. Seek urgent medical attention for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe weakness, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or dark urine.

What is it used for?
Artesunate injection is used for the emergency treatment of severe malaria, including malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum. It is usually given in a hospital or healthcare setting and followed by a suitable oral antimalarial treatment when the patient can take medicines by mouth.

How does it work?
Artesunate is rapidly converted into an active substance that kills malaria parasites in the blood, helping to reduce the severity of the infection.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a trained healthcare professional. The supplied sodium bicarbonate and sodium chloride solutions are used to prepare the injection. The dose and treatment schedule must be decided by the treating doctor based on the severity of malaria and the patient’s condition.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, fever, chills, rash or itching, and injection-site reactions may occur. Delayed anaemia due to breakdown of red blood cells can occur after treatment.

Precautions
Severe malaria is a medical emergency and requires hospital care. Do not self-inject this medicine. Medical monitoring is needed during and after treatment, including monitoring for anaemia or other blood-related problems. Seek urgent medical attention for worsening weakness, pale skin, yellowing of the eyes or skin, dark urine, breathing difficulty, or signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Cinnarizine is used to prevent and relieve motion sickness and to treat dizziness or vertigo, including symptoms such as spinning sensation, nausea and vomiting caused by inner-ear problems.

How does it work?
It reduces excessive stimulation of the balance centre in the inner ear and has an antihistamine effect, helping to control dizziness, nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than recommended. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dry mouth, indigestion, stomach discomfort and weight gain may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and use caution with other medicines that cause drowsiness. Consult a doctor before use if there is Parkinson’s disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if dizziness is severe, new, persistent or associated with hearing loss, weakness or severe headache.

What is it used for?
Clindamycin is used to treat certain bacterial infections, including serious infections caused by bacteria that are sensitive to it. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Clindamycin stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor or pharmacist. The dose, frequency, treatment duration and method of use depend on the infection and the product. Do not self-use or stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to clindamycin or similar antibiotics, or a history of colitis or severe diarrhoea after antibiotics. Seek medical help for severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, even after treatment has ended. Use in newborns, premature babies, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or liver disease should be guided by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat acne, including pimples and inflamed acne spots.

How does it work?
Clindamycin helps reduce acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Nicotinamide also helps reduce skin inflammation and supports acne control.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to clean, dry acne-affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips, inside of the nose, and broken or irritated skin. Wash hands after applying.

Common side effects
Dryness, redness, burning, itching, irritation, or peeling at the application site.

Precautions
For external use only. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, persistent diarrhoea, or stomach cramps occur. Avoid applying other irritating skin products unless advised by a healthcare professional. Keep away from children.

What is it used for?
Used to treat fungal skin infections that cause redness, itching, swelling or irritation. It should be used only when recommended by a healthcare professional, as the steroid component may mask or worsen some skin infections.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole stops the growth of fungi on the skin. Beclomethasone reduces inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not cover the area tightly unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, irritation, redness or itching at the application site. Prolonged or repeated use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Do not use on the face, skin folds, broken skin or near the eyes unless specifically advised. Do not use for an undiagnosed rash or for longer than recommended. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens, spreads or does not improve. Consult a doctor before use in children, during pregnancy or while breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat fungal infections that are also causing inflammation, redness, itching or irritation. It should be used only when recommended by a doctor or pharmacist, as the steroid component can mask or worsen some infections.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole stops the growth of fungi. Beclomethasone reduces inflammation, redness and itching in the affected skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not cover the area tightly unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, colour changes or stretch marks.

Precautions
Use only on the affected skin and do not use it for longer than recommended. Avoid self-treatment of undiagnosed rashes, and seek medical advice if the infection spreads, worsens or does not improve. Do not apply to broken skin, the face, groin or skin folds unless specifically advised. Stop use and seek medical help for severe irritation or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole 1% is used to treat fungal infections of the skin, such as athlete’s foot, ringworm, jock itch and fungal skin rashes.

How does it work?
It is an antifungal medicine that damages the fungus and stops it from growing.

How to take/use it
Use on the affected skin only, following the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions. Keep the area clean and dry, and wash hands before and after use. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, redness, itching, irritation or rash may occur where it is applied.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to clotrimazole or any ingredient in the product. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve with treatment. For external use only unless specifically directed otherwise.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole 1% is an antifungal medicine used on the skin to treat fungal infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch and fungal skin rashes.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which prevents the infection from growing.

How to take/use it
Use on clean, dry skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Apply only to the affected area and wash hands before and after use. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or rash at the application site.

Precautions
For external use unless specifically directed otherwise. Do not use if allergic to clotrimazole or any ingredient. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve with treatment.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to reduce redness, swelling, itching and thick, scaly patches in inflammatory skin conditions such as psoriasis and eczema, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Clobetasol is a very potent corticosteroid that reduces skin inflammation and itching. Salicylic acid helps soften and remove thick, scaly skin so the medicine can work more effectively.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected area exactly as prescribed. Wash hands after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not cover the treated area with a bandage or dressing unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Burning or stinging, irritation, dryness, itching and redness may occur. Prolonged or excessive use can cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
This is a very potent steroid and should be used only on medical advice. Avoid use on the face, groin, underarms, broken skin or infected skin unless specifically directed. Do not use on large areas or for longer than prescribed. Seek medical advice if the condition worsens or shows signs of infection. Children, pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should use it only after medical advice.

What is it used for?
Drotaverine is used to relieve painful cramps and spasms caused by tightening of smooth muscles. It may help with stomach and intestinal cramps, menstrual cramps, and spasms of the urinary or biliary tract.

How does it work?
It relaxes smooth muscles in the stomach, intestines, uterus, and urinary or biliary tract, helping to reduce cramping and pain.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, nausea, palpitations, and low blood pressure may occur. Allergic reactions such as rash or swelling are uncommon but require medical attention.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is low blood pressure or severe liver, kidney, or heart disease. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop using it and seek urgent help for severe dizziness, fainting, breathing difficulty, or swelling of the face or throat.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve abdominal cramps or spasms, bloating and discomfort caused by excess gas, including symptoms associated with functional digestive problems such as irritable bowel syndrome.

How does it work?
Dicyclomine relaxes the muscles of the intestine to reduce painful spasms. Activated dimethicone helps combine and disperse gas bubbles, making gas easier to pass.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. Do not take more than the recommended amount. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, nausea, constipation and drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, prostate enlargement, intestinal blockage or severe bowel inflammation. Drowsiness or blurred vision may occur; avoid driving or operating machinery if affected. Avoid overheating because reduced sweating can occur. Discuss use during pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor. Seek medical help for severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or worsening symptoms.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve abdominal cramps, spasms, bloating and discomfort caused by intestinal gas. It may be used for symptom relief in conditions such as irritable bowel syndrome, when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Dicyclomine relaxes spasms in the muscles of the intestine, helping reduce cramp-like pain. Simethicone helps gas bubbles combine and pass more easily, reducing bloating and fullness.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. If symptoms are severe, recurrent or do not improve, seek medical advice.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, constipation, nausea and stomach discomfort may occur. Simethicone is generally well tolerated.

Precautions
Dicyclomine may cause dizziness or blurred vision; avoid driving or operating machinery if affected. Seek medical advice before use if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, prostate-related urinary problems, intestinal blockage or myasthenia gravis. Seek medical attention for severe or persistent abdominal pain, vomiting, fever, blood in the stool or marked abdominal swelling. Keep out of reach of children and do not give to infants unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid used under specialist supervision mainly for certain bone-loss conditions, including osteoporosis. It may also be used in selected blood disorders or other conditions when specifically prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It has androgen-like and anabolic effects that increase protein production and support bone and tissue formation. It may also stimulate red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the condition being treated and must be decided by the prescribing doctor. It should not be self-injected or used for bodybuilding.

Common side effects
Acne or oily skin, swelling due to fluid retention, changes in sexual desire, mood changes, injection-site discomfort, and changes in menstrual periods. Women may develop increased facial or body hair or a deeper voice.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about prostate or breast cancer, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high cholesterol, or a history of blood clots. Children require specialist monitoring because it can affect growth and puberty. Regular medical check-ups and blood tests may be needed. Seek medical advice promptly for yellowing of the skin, severe swelling, chest pain, or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid used under specialist supervision for selected conditions such as osteoporosis (bone thinning) and, in some settings, anaemia associated with kidney disease. Its exact use depends on the doctor's assessment. It should not be used for bodybuilding or muscle enhancement.

How does it work?
It acts like a modified male hormone and increases protein production in the body. This can support bone and muscle tissue and may help stimulate red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as a deep injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and injection schedule depend on the condition being treated and must be decided by the prescriber.

Common side effects
Acne or oily skin, swelling due to fluid retention, changes in mood or sexual desire, injection-site discomfort, menstrual changes, increased facial or body hair, and deepening of the voice. It may also affect the liver, cholesterol levels, or prostate.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about prostate or breast cancer, liver or kidney disease, heart problems, high cholesterol, or a history of blood clots. Women may develop irreversible voice deepening or excess hair growth. Children require specialist monitoring because growth may be affected. Regular medical check-ups and blood tests may be needed.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat fungal infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch.

How does it work?
Luliconazole is an antifungal medicine that stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed by the doctor or product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation where it is applied.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not apply to broken or severely irritated skin unless advised by a doctor. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Keep the area clean and dry, and do not share towels or clothing. Seek medical advice if the infection does not improve or keeps returning.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin for inflamed skin conditions with suspected or confirmed fungal and bacterial infection. It should be used only when prescribed, as the strong steroid component is not suitable for every rash or skin infection.

How does it work?
Clobetasol reduces redness, swelling and itching. Miconazole treats fungal organisms, while neomycin acts against certain bacteria. Chlorocresol helps preserve the product.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless treating the hands. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and do not cover the area unless advised.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, itching, irritation, redness or dryness at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Do not use on the face, groin, skin folds, broken skin or large areas unless specifically advised. Avoid use on untreated viral skin infections, such as cold sores or chickenpox. Stop using it and seek medical advice if the rash worsens or an allergic reaction occurs. Prolonged use, use in children, pregnancy or breastfeeding should be only under medical advice.

What is it used for?
This skin medicine is used for inflamed fungal skin infections, especially when a bacterial infection may also be present. It should be used only when recommended by a doctor or pharmacist.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole kills or stops the growth of fungi. Neomycin helps fight certain bacteria, while beclomethasone reduces redness, swelling and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin exactly as directed by the doctor or product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless treating the hands. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not cover the area with a bandage or tight dressing unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation may occur. Prolonged or repeated use may cause skin thinning, skin colour changes or increased sensitivity. Stop use and seek medical advice if a severe rash or allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Use only on the area and for the duration advised. Avoid using it on the face, groin, skin folds, broken skin or large areas unless specifically prescribed. Do not use for untreated viral skin infections or without medical advice for acne. Avoid prolonged use, as the steroid may mask or worsen an infection. Seek medical advice if the infection does not improve or becomes worse.

What is it used for?
Diclofenac sodium is used to relieve pain, swelling and inflammation in conditions affecting the muscles and joints, including arthritis and other painful musculoskeletal conditions.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use it exactly as prescribed or directed on the product label. Do not use more than recommended, and do not combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or naproxen unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Diclofenac can increase the risk of stomach bleeding, heart attack and stroke, especially with long-term or high-dose use. Avoid use during the last 3 months of pregnancy and seek medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, breathing difficulty, severe rash or swelling.

What is it used for?
Diclofenac sodium is used to relieve pain and reduce inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed or directed on the label. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. If taking it by mouth, taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not combine it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell a doctor before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAIDs. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin reaction. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised, particularly after 20 weeks. Inform the doctor about blood thinners, steroids, other painkillers or regular medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Used as a topical antiseptic to help prevent or control infection in minor cuts, wounds, scratches, burns and other superficial skin injuries.

How does it work?
Silver nitrate, chlorhexidine and chlorocresol act as antiseptics that kill or inhibit the growth of microorganisms on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean and gently dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed by a doctor or on the product label. Do not use more or for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Mild stinging, burning, redness, itching or skin irritation. Allergic reactions may rarely occur.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Do not apply to large, deep or seriously infected wounds, or extensive burns, unless advised by a healthcare professional.
