What is it used for?
Esomeprazole injection reduces excess stomach acid. It is used for acid-related conditions such as heartburn, acid reflux (GERD) and stomach or intestinal ulcers, particularly when treatment by mouth is not suitable.

How does it work?
Esomeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI). It reduces the production of acid in the stomach, helping relieve symptoms and support healing of acid-related damage.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection or infusion into a vein by a doctor or nurse. It should not be self-administered. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and medical assessment.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain, gas and irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to esomeprazole or other proton pump inhibitors, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Inform the doctor about all medicines being used, as esomeprazole can interact with some medicines. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash, swelling or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Etamsylate Injection is used to help control or reduce bleeding, including bleeding from small blood vessels, heavy menstrual bleeding, and bleeding around surgery when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It helps strengthen small blood vessels and improves the ability of platelets to form a plug at the bleeding site.

How to take/use it
This injection should be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose, route and duration depend on the cause and severity of bleeding.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, skin rash and discomfort at the injection site may occur. A temporary fall in blood pressure may occur, particularly if given rapidly.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to etamsylate or similar medicines, a history of blood clots, or other medical conditions. It should be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding only when prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for difficulty breathing, facial swelling, severe rash or unusual worsening of symptoms.

What is it used for?
Etamsylate is used to help reduce excessive bleeding, especially heavy menstrual bleeding. It may also be prescribed for certain small-vessel or capillary bleeding and to control bleeding around some medical or surgical procedures.

How does it work?
It helps improve the strength of small blood vessels and supports the early formation of a platelet plug, helping bleeding to stop. It does not replace treatment for the underlying cause of bleeding.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the prescribed dose and schedule, and do not take it for unexplained bleeding without medical advice. Seek medical attention if bleeding is heavy, persistent or keeps returning.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, headache and skin rash may occur. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction or unusual worsening of symptoms.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to etamsylate. Tell the doctor about porphyria, bleeding or clotting problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding before use. Unexplained bleeding should be medically evaluated rather than treated repeatedly with this medicine.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to reduce excessive bleeding, particularly heavy menstrual bleeding (menorrhagia), when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Tranexamic acid helps prevent the breakdown of blood clots, while etamsylate helps strengthen small blood vessels and support clot formation. Together, they help reduce bleeding.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the prescribed dose and duration, and do not take extra doses or continue treatment longer than advised. If heavy or unusual bleeding continues, seek medical evaluation.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of blood clots, stroke, kidney disease, or vision problems before use. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathlessness, sudden weakness, severe leg pain or swelling, or changes in vision. Do not use it to treat unexplained bleeding without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat anaemia caused by iron, folic acid or vitamin B12 deficiency, when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It provides iron needed to make haemoglobin and red blood cells. Folic acid and vitamin B12 support normal red blood cell formation.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed or directed on the label. Do not take more than recommended. Follow the advice of a healthcare professional about timing with food and other medicines.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and dark-coloured stools may occur.

Precautions
Do not self-treat unexplained anaemia; the cause should be assessed. Tell the doctor if there is iron overload, another blood disorder, or an allergy to any ingredient. Iron-containing products can be harmful in overdose—keep out of reach of children. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines, including antacids, calcium supplements and antibiotics.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron-deficiency anaemia and support red blood cell production when iron, folic acid or vitamin B12 supplementation is needed.

How does it work?
It provides iron needed to make haemoglobin, along with folic acid and vitamin B12, which support the formation of healthy red blood cells.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended. If it causes stomach upset, ask a healthcare professional whether it should be taken with food. Keep it out of the reach of children.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and dark or black stools may occur.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if the cause of anaemia is unknown or if there is iron overload or a condition that causes excess iron. Tell a doctor or pharmacist about other medicines, especially antacids, calcium supplements, thyroid medicines or certain antibiotics, as iron may affect their absorption. Seek medical advice if side effects are severe or persistent.

What is it used for?
Iron sucrose is used to treat iron-deficiency anaemia, especially when iron tablets are not effective, cannot be tolerated, or iron replacement is needed under medical supervision. It is commonly used in people with chronic kidney disease and in other situations decided by a doctor.

How does it work?
It supplies iron to the body, helping restore iron stores and support the production of haemoglobin and red blood cells.

How to take/use it
Iron sucrose is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and number of treatments depend on the severity of iron deficiency and the individual’s medical condition. It is not for self-injection or oral use.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, changes in blood pressure, muscle or joint pain, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
It should be used only after confirming iron deficiency. Tell the healthcare professional about previous reactions to intravenous iron, allergies, liver disease, or conditions causing iron overload. Serious allergic reactions can rarely occur, so monitoring during and shortly after treatment is important. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe dizziness, or fainting.

What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It may also be used for hives (urticaria) and related itching when prescribed.

How does it work?
It is an antihistamine that blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the package instructions. Swallow the tablet with water. Avoid taking it with fruit juice, such as apple, orange or grapefruit juice. If using aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids, take them at a different time as advised by a pharmacist or doctor.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, dizziness and tiredness may occur. Drowsiness is uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Seek medical advice if allergy symptoms are severe, unusual or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It is also used to relieve itching and hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce itching, sneezing, runny nose and other allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or as stated on the label. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take it with apple, orange or grapefruit juice, as these may reduce its effect. Keep a gap between this medicine and aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids, as advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, dizziness and mild drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Seek medical advice if symptoms do not improve or if an allergic reaction develops.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and itchy or watery eyes caused by allergies.

How does it work?
Fexofenadine blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which can contribute to nasal swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed or directed on the label. Swallow with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Avoid taking it with fruit juice unless advised by a healthcare professional. Do not use it to treat a sudden asthma attack.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, dizziness, dry mouth, stomach discomfort, or tiredness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or any history of mental health problems. Stop the medicine and seek medical advice if mood or behaviour changes, unusual dreams, depression, or suicidal thoughts occur. Avoid aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids close to the dose unless advised otherwise. Seek medical advice if allergy symptoms do not improve or worsen.

What is it used for?
Tranexamic acid is used to reduce or control excessive bleeding, including heavy menstrual bleeding. It may also be prescribed for certain other types of bleeding.

How does it work?
It helps prevent blood clots from breaking down too quickly, which helps reduce bleeding.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more than the prescribed amount. The dose and treatment duration depend on the cause and severity of bleeding.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of blood clots, kidney disease, vision problems or an allergy to tranexamic acid. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, coughing blood, or painful swelling in an arm or leg. Report changes in vision or unusually heavy or persistent bleeding. Extra caution may be needed with hormonal contraceptives or medicines that affect blood clotting.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold symptoms such as fever, body aches, blocked or runny nose, sneezing, throat irritation and cough with mucus.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and pain. Phenylephrine helps relieve nasal blockage, chlorpheniramine reduces allergy-related sneezing and runny nose, while ammonium chloride and menthol help loosen or soothe mucus and throat irritation.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and avoid other medicines containing paracetamol or similar cold-relief ingredients.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, stomach upset, headache or palpitations may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine or prostate enlargement. Ask a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not use with other paracetamol-containing or cold medicines unless advised.

What is it used for?
Used to help prevent or treat calcium and vitamin D deficiency and support healthy bones. It may be prescribed when the body needs active vitamin D along with calcium; use it only for the purpose advised by the doctor.

How does it work?
Calcitriol is an active form of vitamin D that helps the body absorb and use calcium. Calcium supports bone strength, while zinc contributes to normal tissue and immune function.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, preferably with food if advised, and swallow with water. Do not take extra calcium or vitamin D supplements unless recommended by a doctor. Do not exceed the prescribed amount.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort, or vomiting may occur. Excess calcium can cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness, or confusion.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or other disorders affecting calcium or vitamin D. Avoid taking other calcium- or vitamin D-containing products without medical advice. Seek medical advice if symptoms of excess calcium occur. Long-term use may require blood tests to check calcium and kidney function.

What is it used for?
Hyoscine butylbromide is used to relieve painful muscle spasms and cramps in the stomach and intestines, including abdominal cramps associated with conditions such as irritable bowel syndrome. It may also be used for spasms of the urinary tract when prescribed.

How does it work?
It relaxes the smooth muscles in the stomach, intestines and urinary tract, helping to reduce spasms and cramping.

How to take/use it
Use it only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. The dose, frequency and route of use depend on the formulation and medical condition. Do not use it for persistent or unexplained abdominal pain without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, fast heartbeat, dizziness and difficulty passing urine may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is glaucoma, prostate-related difficulty passing urine, suspected bowel blockage, severe constipation, myasthenia gravis or a fast heartbeat. Seek urgent medical care for severe or worsening abdominal pain, especially with vomiting, fever, fainting or blood in the stool. Consult a doctor during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, especially when other suitable antibiotics cannot be used. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Use only when prescribed by a doctor. Take or use it exactly as directed on the prescription or product label, and complete the prescribed course unless advised otherwise. Do not share it or use leftover medicine.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, and skin rash may occur. Rarely, it can cause serious blood-related problems, including bone-marrow suppression.

Precautions
Chloramphenicol should be used under medical supervision because it can rarely cause serious or delayed blood disorders. Tell the doctor about any previous blood disorder, liver disease, medicine allergy, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical advice for unusual bruising or bleeding, persistent fever, sore throat, marked weakness, or pale skin. Keep it away from newborns and young infants unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Chloramphenicol 500 mg is used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, such as typhoid fever and some meningitis infections, when a doctor considers it appropriate. It is usually reserved for situations where other antibiotics are unsuitable because it can cause serious blood-related side effects.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Take it only on a doctor's prescription and follow the prescribed dose and duration. Swallow the tablet or capsule with water and complete the full course, unless the doctor tells otherwise. Do not self-medicate or share this medicine.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and temporary changes in blood-cell counts may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, previous blood disorders, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Medical monitoring, including blood tests, may be needed during treatment. Seek urgent medical advice for unusual bruising or bleeding, unusual tiredness, pale skin, fever, sore throat or severe diarrhoea. Do not use it for minor infections unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Chloramphenicol is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, usually when other suitable antibiotics cannot be used. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the prescription. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise. Do not share it or use leftover medicine. Medical monitoring may be needed during treatment.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision because it can rarely cause serious blood disorders, including bone-marrow suppression. Tell the doctor about any blood, liver, or kidney problems, allergies, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for unusual tiredness, pale skin, fever, sore throat, easy bruising, or bleeding. Avoid prolonged or repeated courses unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Betamethasone sodium phosphate is a corticosteroid injection used under medical supervision to reduce inflammation and severe allergic or immune-related reactions. The exact condition and treatment plan depend on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation, swelling and allergic reactions.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose, injection site and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Pain or discomfort at the injection site, increased appetite, indigestion, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, fluid retention and increased blood sugar may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health problems or any current infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body's ability to fight infection and may mask infection symptoms. Inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding and any medicines being taken. Do not stop prolonged treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Bacillus clausii spores are probiotic bacteria used to help restore the natural balance of beneficial bacteria in the intestine, especially during or after diarrhoea or antibiotic treatment. They may help reduce loose motions, but oral rehydration remains important during diarrhoea.

How does it work?
It adds beneficial bacteria to the intestine and helps support the normal balance of gut microorganisms.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If diarrhoea is severe, persistent, or associated with dehydration, seek medical advice.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort, nausea, or temporary changes in bowel movements may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if immunocompromised, seriously ill, or using a central venous catheter, as rare bloodstream infections have been reported with probiotic products. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur. This product does not replace oral rehydration during diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat deficiencies of vitamin B12, vitamin B6 and nicotinamide (vitamin B3). It may also be prescribed as nutritional support for normal nerve function when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It replaces B vitamins needed for nerve function, red blood cell formation and energy metabolism.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed by the doctor or as stated on the product label. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea or headache may occur. Stop use and seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction, such as rash, swelling or breathing difficulty.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about other medicines and medical conditions before use. Avoid prolonged use of high doses unless medically advised, as excess vitamin B6 may cause nerve damage. Seek medical advice if numbness, tingling or weakness persists or worsens.

What is it used for?
Omeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be used for stomach or duodenal ulcers and other acid-related conditions when prescribed.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of acid in the stomach by blocking the stomach’s acid-producing pumps.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed timing and duration, even if symptoms improve.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, allergy to omeprazole or other medicines, or if it is being used for a long period. Seek medical advice for unexplained weight loss, difficulty swallowing, repeated vomiting, vomiting blood, black stools or persistent symptoms. Omeprazole can interact with some medicines, so provide a complete list of medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux, especially when these symptoms are accompanied by nausea or vomiting.

How does it work?
Omeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps stomach contents move forward and can help relieve nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the medicine with water and do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation, nausea, dry mouth or dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart disease, an irregular heartbeat, or a history of electrolyte imbalance. Domperidone may rarely cause serious heart-rhythm problems and can interact with some medicines, including certain antibiotics, antifungals and heart medicines. Seek medical advice for fainting, palpitations, severe or persistent diarrhoea, vomiting blood or black stools. Do not use for prolonged periods unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Etophylline + theophylline is used to help relieve and prevent wheezing, chest tightness and breathing difficulty caused by asthma and chronic obstructive airway disease (COPD). It should be used only as prescribed.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them open and allowing air to move more easily into and out of the lungs.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the recommended times. Do not take extra doses or stop treatment without medical advice. Avoid taking other theophylline-containing medicines unless advised by a doctor. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the prescriber or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, shakiness and fast or pounding heartbeat.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision because theophylline levels can become too high. Inform the doctor about heart disease, seizures, liver or kidney problems, stomach ulcers, persistent fever, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Smoking and stopping smoking can affect its action. Limit excessive caffeine, as it may worsen side effects. Seek urgent medical help for repeated vomiting, severe or irregular heartbeat, fainting or seizures.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% is an antifungal medicine used in topical products to treat fungal infections of the skin and scalp. Some formulations are also used for dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which prevents the fungus from growing.

How to take/use it
Use the cream, shampoo or other formulation exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. If it is a topical product, apply or use it only on the affected skin or scalp and wash hands after use. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas unless specifically directed.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site.

Precautions
For external use unless the product label or healthcare professional says otherwise. Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole or any ingredient. Avoid applying to the eyes or severely damaged skin. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs, or if the condition does not improve.

What is it used for?
Ketorolac is used for the short-term relief of moderate to severe acute pain. It is generally intended for short-term use and is not suitable for routine long-term pain control.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The route of use depends on the prescribed formulation; ketorolac 30 mg may be given by a healthcare professional. Do not self-inject or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach pain, headache, dizziness and drowsiness.

Precautions
It can cause stomach ulcers or bleeding and may affect kidney function. Avoid using it with other NSAID painkillers, such as ibuprofen or diclofenac, unless specifically advised. Tell the doctor about a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney disease, heart disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, bleeding disorders, or use of blood thinners. Seek urgent help for severe stomach pain, black stools, vomiting blood, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or very little urine. It should generally be avoided during pregnancy, especially later pregnancy, unless prescribed by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is an anti-seizure medicine used to control epilepsy and prevent seizures. It may be prescribed alone or with other medicines, depending on the type of seizures.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by affecting the release of chemical signals between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, as this may trigger seizures. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, nausea, irritability, agitation, and mood or behaviour changes.

Precautions
Seek medical advice if there are severe mood changes, depression, aggression, confusion, or thoughts of self-harm. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizzy or sleepy. Do not stop levetiracetam suddenly without medical advice.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and itchy or watery eyes.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, a substance that causes allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which also contribute to allergic inflammation and nasal congestion.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not change the dose or duration, and do not take more than recommended. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, headache, tiredness, dry mouth, and stomach pain may occur.

Precautions
Avoid driving or operating machinery if drowsy, and avoid alcohol or other medicines that cause sleepiness unless advised by a doctor. Stop the medicine and seek medical advice if unusual changes in mood or behaviour, nightmares, agitation, depression, or suicidal thoughts occur. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. This medicine is not intended to treat a sudden asthma attack.

What is it used for?
Levocetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It is also used for hives (urticaria) and related itching.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or as stated on the medicine label. It may generally be taken with or without food. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness or sleepiness, tiredness, headache, and dry mouth may occur.

Precautions
Drowsiness may affect driving or operating machinery; avoid alcohol if it increases sleepiness. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
Ayurvedic liver tonics are generally used to support liver health and normal liver function. They should not be used to self-treat jaundice, hepatitis, fatty liver or other liver diseases without medical advice.

How does it work?
The exact action depends on the Ayurvedic ingredients in the product. The ingredients were not provided, so a specific mechanism cannot be confirmed.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by an Ayurvedic doctor or healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Specific common side effects cannot be confirmed without knowing the ingredients. Some people may experience digestive discomfort with herbal products.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list before use. Seek medical advice if there is existing liver disease, jaundice, persistent abdominal symptoms, pregnancy, breastfeeding or regular use of other medicines. Stop use and seek medical advice if unusual symptoms develop.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used for certain liver and bile-duct conditions, including primary biliary cholangitis. It may also be prescribed to dissolve selected cholesterol gallstones when suitable.

How does it work?
It changes the composition of bile, helping bile flow more easily and reducing the amount of cholesterol in bile. This can help protect liver cells and gradually dissolve some cholesterol gallstones.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the medicine with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Treatment may require regular liver tests and follow-up.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, loose stools, stomach discomfort, abdominal pain, nausea or indigestion.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about gallbladder inflammation, blocked bile ducts, frequent biliary pain or liver disease. It is not suitable for all types of gallstones. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, worsening jaundice or severe diarrhoea. Pregnancy, breastfeeding and use of other medicines should be discussed with a doctor.

What is it used for?
Loratadine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching or hives on the skin.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions on the label or ask a pharmacist.

Common side effects
Headache, mild drowsiness, tiredness, and dry mouth.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional about liver or kidney disease before use. Seek advice before taking it during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid taking it if there has been a previous allergy to loratadine or any of its ingredients. Although it usually causes little drowsiness, avoid driving or operating machinery if affected.

What is it used for?
Meropenem is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including certain infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, and other parts of the body. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection or infusion into a vein by a doctor or nurse, usually in a hospital or clinic. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function, and medical advice. Complete the prescribed course unless the prescriber advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, headache, skin rash, and pain or inflammation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to meropenem, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney problems. Use caution in people with a history of seizures. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, as it may indicate a serious bowel infection. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially valproate medicines, because meropenem can reduce their effect.

What is it used for?
Meropenem injection is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as severe infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin, blood, or brain. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Meropenem kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall. Sodium carbonate helps maintain the stability of the injection.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. It should be used only as prescribed and the full prescribed course should be completed.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea or vomiting, headache, skin rash, and pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to meropenem, penicillins, cephalosporins, or other antibiotics; kidney disease; or a history of seizures. The dose may need adjustment in kidney problems. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, or seizures. Meropenem can interact with valproate medicines.

What is it used for?
Meropenem with sulbactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections caused by bacteria that may resist some other antibiotics. It is used only when prescribed and administered by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Meropenem kills bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps meropenem work against certain bacteria that can otherwise break down antibiotics.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and the patient's response. Do not self-inject or stop treatment early unless advised by the doctor.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, headache, rash, and pain, redness or swelling at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to penicillin, cephalosporin, carbapenem or other antibiotics. The dose may need adjustment in kidney disease. Inform the doctor about a history of seizures or other brain disorders. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, seizures, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only for bacterial infections; it does not treat viral infections.

What is it used for?
Methylergometrine is used after childbirth or pregnancy-related procedures to help the uterus contract and control or prevent heavy bleeding caused by poor uterine contraction. It is used only under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It causes the muscles of the uterus to contract firmly, helping reduce bleeding. It can also narrow blood vessels, which may raise blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor or other healthcare professional. Follow the prescribed route, dose and schedule; do not self-medicate or use it during pregnancy before delivery.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, abdominal or uterine cramps, and increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is high blood pressure, pre-eclampsia or eclampsia, heart disease, blood-vessel disease, or severe liver or kidney problems. Seek urgent medical help for severe headache, chest pain, breathing difficulty, seizures, or very high blood pressure. Tell the doctor about all medicines being used, especially other ergot medicines or medicines that can raise blood pressure.

What is it used for?
Amikacin is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, especially infections caused by bacteria that may not respond to other antibiotics. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from multiplying.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Amikacin is commonly given by injection by a healthcare professional; the dose, route and treatment duration depend on the infection and kidney function. Do not self-administer or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur. Kidney problems and hearing or balance changes are important serious effects that need prompt medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Kidney function and sometimes hearing may need monitoring during treatment. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially those that can affect the kidneys, hearing, or muscle function. Seek medical help for reduced urination, ringing in the ears, hearing loss, severe dizziness, or unusual muscle weakness.

What is it used for?
Amikacin is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, often in hospital care. It is used only when the infecting bacteria are likely to respond to it.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills the bacteria or prevents their growth.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. It is usually given by a healthcare professional, often as an injection. The dose and treatment length depend on the infection, body weight and kidney function; do not self-use or change the treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea or vomiting may occur. More serious effects can include reduced urine output, hearing changes, ringing in the ears, dizziness or balance problems.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Kidney function and hearing may need monitoring during treatment. Inform the doctor about all medicines, especially other medicines that can affect the kidneys or hearing. Seek medical help for reduced urination, unusual weakness, ringing in the ears, hearing loss or severe dizziness.

What is it used for?
Amikacin 500 mg is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, especially infections caused by certain bacteria that may not respond to other antibiotics. It may be used for severe infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, blood, bones or joints, and skin, only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from making essential proteins needed for their growth and survival.

How to take/use it
Amikacin is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the infection, body weight and kidney function. Complete the prescribed course and do not self-administer it.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea or vomiting may occur. Serious effects can include reduced urine, ringing in the ears, dizziness, balance problems or hearing loss.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Kidney function and sometimes hearing should be monitored during treatment. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially other medicines that may affect the kidneys or hearing. Seek medical attention promptly for reduced urination, severe dizziness, ringing in the ears or any hearing change.

What is it used for?
Mometasone furoate 0.1% is a topical corticosteroid used to reduce redness, swelling and itching caused by inflammatory skin conditions such as eczema, dermatitis and some forms of psoriasis.

How does it work?
It reduces inflammation and overactivity of the immune response in the skin, helping relieve redness, swelling and itching.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use unless the hands are being treated. Use only on the skin and avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, irritation, dryness or itching at the application site. Prolonged or extensive use may cause skin thinning or other skin changes.

Precautions
For external use only. Do not apply to the eyes, face, broken skin or infected skin unless specifically advised. Avoid covering the treated area tightly unless instructed. Use cautiously in children and avoid prolonged or extensive use. Seek medical advice if the skin condition worsens or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Mupirocin is a topical antibiotic used to treat bacterial skin infections, such as impetigo and infected minor cuts or wounds.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins needed for their growth and survival.

How to take/use it
Use on the affected skin only and apply as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after application. Do not use it in the eyes, mouth or other body openings unless specifically prescribed for that use.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to mupirocin or any ingredient. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs. Avoid prolonged or repeated use unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of cough with mucus, blocked nose, runny nose and sneezing associated with common cold or allergy-related upper respiratory symptoms.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help loosen and clear mucus. Phenylephrine reduces nasal swelling, while cetirizine reduces allergy symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the package instructions. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other cold, cough, antihistamine or decongestant medicines unless advised. If it is a liquid, measure each dose with a proper measuring device.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, headache, nausea, stomach upset, restlessness or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid alcohol and take care when driving or operating machinery. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, diabetes or difficulty passing urine. Do not use with MAO inhibitor medicines or other decongestants unless advised by a doctor. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding or in children.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve cough with mucus (phlegm), chest congestion and wheezing or breathing difficulty associated with some respiratory conditions.

How does it work?
Terbutaline helps relax and open the airways. Guaiphenesin helps loosen mucus, while ambroxol thins it so it can be cleared more easily; menthol may soothe throat irritation.

How to take/use it
Take or use exactly as prescribed or as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If it is a liquid, measure each dose accurately using a suitable measuring device.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach upset, headache, dizziness, shakiness or tremor, nervousness, dry mouth, and a fast or pounding heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use only with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical attention if breathing difficulty worsens, wheezing is severe, or symptoms do not improve. Do not combine with other cough medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
This combination provides temporary relief from cough, blocked or runny nose, sneezing and related symptoms of the common cold. It may also relieve cough and nasal symptoms linked with allergies.

How does it work?
Chlorpheniramine reduces allergy symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose. Dextromethorphan suppresses cough, while phenylephrine helps reduce nasal blockage by narrowing swollen blood vessels in the nose.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and do not combine it with other cough, cold or decongestant medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, nervousness, difficulty sleeping, palpitations or increased blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, an overactive thyroid, difficulty urinating or prostate problems. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines or within 14 days of stopping them. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or in children. Seek medical help if the cough lasts, worsens or is accompanied by breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for temporary relief of cough, blocked or stuffy nose, runny nose and sneezing associated with common cold and similar upper-respiratory conditions.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps reduce the cough reflex. Chlorpheniramine reduces allergy-like symptoms such as runny nose and sneezing, while phenylephrine helps relieve nasal congestion.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking it with other cough, cold or allergy medicines unless advised, as they may contain the same ingredients.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, headache, nervousness or difficulty sleeping. Phenylephrine may cause a fast heartbeat or increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful with driving or operating machinery because drowsiness or reduced alertness may occur. Ask a doctor before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, difficulty urinating, thyroid disease or other long-term medical conditions. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines, and check with a doctor before combining with antidepressants, sedatives or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice for children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if the cough lasts, worsens or is associated with breathing difficulty or high fever.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve cough with mucus, especially when it is associated with wheezing or narrowed airways in respiratory conditions. It helps loosen and clear phlegm and makes breathing easier.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus so it can be cleared more easily. Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping to relieve bronchospasm and wheezing.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by the doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Do not combine it with other cough, cold or bronchodilator medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, tremor, muscle cramps or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, seizures or a history of sensitivity to bronchodilators. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, or worsening symptoms. Consult a doctor if the cough persists or is accompanied by high fever or blood in the mucus.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for symptomatic relief of cough with phlegm and associated wheezing or breathing difficulty caused by narrowed airways. It helps loosen mucus and makes it easier to clear from the airways.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin thin and loosen mucus, while levosalbutamol helps relax and open the airways. Menthol may provide a soothing effect in the throat and airways.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. If symptoms do not improve or breathing difficulty worsens, seek medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach upset, headache, shakiness, nervousness, palpitations or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor before use if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, seizures, or low potassium. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice. Stop use and seek urgent help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, or signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with mucus and breathing difficulty or wheezing associated with narrowed airways. It helps loosen and clear phlegm while relaxing the airway muscles.

How does it work?
Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles of the airways to improve breathing. Ambroxol thins mucus, and guaiphenesin helps loosen and remove phlegm.

How to take/use it
Take or use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Follow the prescribed amount and do not exceed it. If it is a liquid, measure it with the provided measuring device rather than a household spoon.

Common side effects
Trembling, headache, nervousness, fast heartbeat or palpitations, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Use cautiously in people with heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help if breathing difficulty worsens, severe palpitations occur, or a rash, swelling, or other signs of allergy develop.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for temporary relief of dry cough, blocked nose, runny nose and sneezing associated with common cold or allergy-related upper respiratory symptoms.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan reduces the cough reflex. Phenylephrine helps reduce nasal congestion, while cetirizine blocks histamine to relieve runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended or combine it with other cough-and-cold medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, headache, nausea, nervousness, increased blood pressure or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery, as drowsiness or dizziness may occur. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, difficulty passing urine, or liver or kidney problems. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs), and check with a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Consult a doctor if the cough lasts, worsens, or is accompanied by breathing difficulty or high fever.

What is it used for?
This combination provides temporary relief from cough, phlegm, blocked nose, runny nose and sneezing associated with common cold or allergies.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps reduce the cough reflex, while ambroxol helps loosen mucus. Chlorpheniramine reduces allergy symptoms, phenylephrine helps relieve nasal congestion, and menthol provides a soothing sensation.

How to take/use it
Take or use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. If it is a liquid, measure each dose with the supplied measuring device. Avoid taking other cough, cold or allergy medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, stomach upset, headache, nervousness or increased heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, difficulty passing urine, liver disease, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines, and inform a healthcare professional about all other medicines being taken. Seek medical advice if the cough is severe, lasts several days, or is associated with breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold and flu symptoms such as fever, headache, body aches, blocked or stuffy nose, runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and relieve pain. Phenylephrine helps reduce nasal blockage, while chlorpheniramine helps relieve runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and do not use it with other medicines containing paracetamol or similar cold and flu ingredients.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, stomach discomfort, headache or palpitations may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving or using machinery if affected. Avoid alcohol. Seek medical advice before use in liver disease, high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid problems or difficulty passing urine. Check with a doctor before use in children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe allergic symptoms, very fast heartbeat or persistent symptoms.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, headache, toothache, muscle pain or pain associated with common illnesses.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever. Ibuprofen reduces substances in the body that cause pain, fever and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. The dose depends on the person’s age, weight and the product form. Do not take more than the recommended dose, and do not use it with other medicines containing paracetamol or ibuprofen unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach discomfort, dizziness or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to ibuprofen, paracetamol, aspirin or other similar painkillers. Seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, dehydration or heart problems. Avoid ibuprofen-containing medicines during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Stop use and seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin rash, vomiting blood or black stools.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and fever, including pain affecting the muscles and joints.

How does it work?
Nimesulide reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and reduce fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor, preferably after food. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or nimesulide unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use in liver disease, severe kidney disease, stomach ulcers or bleeding unless specifically advised by a doctor. Avoid alcohol. Stop using it and seek medical help if yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe skin reactions, unusual bleeding or severe stomach pain occurs. It should not be used during pregnancy, especially in the last three months, unless prescribed. Inform the doctor about all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of acidity, heartburn, indigestion and gas-related bloating.

How does it work?
Aluminium hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide neutralise excess stomach acid. Activated dimethicone helps reduce gas bubbles and related bloating.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not exceed the recommended amount or use it for prolonged periods without medical advice. Keep a gap between this medicine and other oral medicines, as it may affect their absorption.

Common side effects
Constipation or diarrhoea may occur. Nausea or stomach discomfort can also occur.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, persistent vomiting, severe or ongoing stomach pain, black stools or difficulty swallowing. Seek medical advice if symptoms continue or recur frequently. Check with a doctor or pharmacist before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or with other medicines.

What is it used for?
Pantoprazole 40 mg is used to reduce excess stomach acid. It helps treat acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), and stomach or intestinal ulcers, as prescribed.

How does it work?
It blocks the acid-producing pumps in the stomach, reducing the amount of acid made. This helps relieve acid-related symptoms and allows irritated tissues or ulcers to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually before a meal. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed dose and treatment duration, and do not stop long-term treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain, gas, or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is difficulty swallowing, persistent vomiting, unexplained weight loss, vomiting blood, or black stools. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea. Inform the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Long-term use may require medical monitoring because it can affect vitamin B12 or magnesium levels and bone health.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine is used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be prescribed for stomach or duodenal ulcers.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the amount of acid produced.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Swallow with water. Do not use it for prolonged or recurring symptoms without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, constipation or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease and all other medicines being taken. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, persistent vomiting, unexplained weight loss, black stools or vomiting blood. In some countries, ranitidine products have been withdrawn or restricted because of contamination concerns; use it only when a healthcare professional confirms that it is appropriate.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine reduces excess stomach acid. It is used for acidity and heartburn, acid reflux, and stomach or duodenal ulcers.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine-2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the amount of acid produced.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist, and follow the instructions on the product label. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Ranitidine products have been withdrawn or restricted in many countries because of impurity concerns; use it only if specifically approved and supplied by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, constipation, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, or dizziness.

Precautions
Inform the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or use of other medicines. Seek medical advice for persistent or worsening symptoms, difficulty swallowing, unexplained weight loss, vomiting blood, or black stools. Do not self-treat possible ulcer symptoms without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine reduces excess stomach acid. It may be used for acidity, heartburn, acid reflux and some stomach or duodenal ulcers, as directed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the amount of acid produced.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised. Swallow with water. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or keep returning.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, constipation, diarrhoea and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional about kidney or liver disease, porphyria, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being used. Seek urgent medical advice for vomiting blood, black stools, difficulty swallowing, unexplained weight loss or severe chest or stomach pain. Some ranitidine products have been withdrawn or restricted in many countries; check current local regulatory advice and use only a product supplied through an authorised source.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine reduces excess stomach acid. It may be used for heartburn, acid reflux, indigestion and acid-related stomach or intestinal ulcers. Ranitidine has been withdrawn or restricted in many countries because of concerns about contamination; use it only if specifically prescribed or approved by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine-2 (H2) receptors in the stomach, reducing the amount of acid produced.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist, and follow the instructions on the product label. Do not start, restart or continue ranitidine without checking whether it is approved and appropriate for use. Swallow with water unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, a history of porphyria, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or use of other medicines. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss, persistent vomiting or symptoms that do not improve. Stop and seek urgent help for swelling, breathing difficulty or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Omeprazole reduces excess stomach acid. It is used for acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), and stomach or intestinal ulcers.

How does it work?
It blocks the final step of acid production in the stomach, reducing irritation and allowing acid-related damage to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually before food. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop a long-term treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, gas, diarrhoea, constipation, or vomiting.

Precautions
Tell a doctor about liver disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding, and mention all medicines being taken. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss, or persistent symptoms. Long-term use should be medically supervised.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including nausea and vomiting related to surgery or cancer treatment.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals in the body that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Do not take more or use it more often than directed. The dose and duration depend on the reason for treatment and the patient's condition.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, dizziness, tiredness, and flushing may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of heart rhythm problems, low potassium or magnesium levels, liver disease, or an allergy to ondansetron. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or serotonin levels. Seek medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic symptoms, or unusual agitation, sweating, fever, or muscle stiffness.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including those caused by chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery, or certain illnesses.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals in the body that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Use it only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the instructions on the label and do not take more than recommended. The correct dose and treatment duration depend on the reason for use and individual health factors.

Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, dizziness, and tiredness.

Precautions

What is it used for?
Ondansetron is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including those related to medical treatments such as chemotherapy or radiotherapy, and after surgery. The exact use depends on the prescriber's advice.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals in the body that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed or as directed on the label. The dose and duration depend on the cause of nausea or vomiting, age, and medical condition. Do not take extra doses or use it for longer than advised.

Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, dizziness, and tiredness.

Precautions

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 120 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, headache, toothache or pain from minor illnesses.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of certain chemicals in the body involved in pain and fever, helping lower temperature and relieve pain.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and do not use it together with other medicines containing paracetamol.

Common side effects
Paracetamol is usually well tolerated. Nausea, vomiting or a skin rash may occur. Serious side effects are uncommon when used correctly.

Precautions
Check with a doctor before use if there is liver disease, regular heavy alcohol use, or use of other medicines containing paracetamol. Do not exceed the recommended amount, as an overdose can cause serious liver damage. Seek urgent medical help after taking more than recommended, even if feeling well. Stop and seek medical help for swelling, breathing difficulty, or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 250 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, body pain, toothache and muscle aches.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of chemicals involved in pain and fever, helping to lower body temperature and relieve pain.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended, and avoid using other medicines that also contain paracetamol.

Common side effects
Usually none when used at the recommended dose. Nausea or a skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use more than the recommended amount, as overdose can cause serious liver damage. Consult a doctor before use if there is liver disease, regular heavy alcohol use, or use of other paracetamol-containing medicines. Stop use and seek urgent medical help for swelling, breathing difficulty, or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 500 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, toothache, body pain, muscle pain and period pain.

How does it work?

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine is an antiseptic used to clean and disinfect the skin, including minor cuts, grazes and wounds, and to help prevent infection. Some formulations are used for skin preparation before medical procedures.

It slowly releases iodine, which kills or inactivates many types of germs, including bacteria, viruses and fungi.

Seek medical advice for worsening redness, swelling, pain, pus or fever. What is it used for?

It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune activity.

Use only as prescribed. Depending on the product, it may be taken by mouth or administered by a healthcare professional. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice, especially after prolonged use.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions, liver or kidney problems, or any ongoing infection. Avoid close contact with people who have contagious infections and ask the doctor before receiving vaccines. Seek medical advice for signs of infection, severe mood changes, vision problems, or severe stomach pain.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the urinary tract, lungs, skin, and other parts of the body. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

It kills bacteria by blocking enzymes needed for bacterial DNA replication and growth.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor and complete the prescribed course. Swallow with water. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium, or zinc; follow the advised time gap. Do not share this medicine or use leftover tablets.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?

It acts mainly inside the intestine and stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins needed for their growth.

Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not self-medicate for diarrhoea without medical advice.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?

Take exactly as prescribed, usually with food to reduce stomach upset. Take it at the same time each day and drink adequate fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not stop or change the medicine without medical advice.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, recurrent urinary or genital infections, heart problems, pancreatitis, or heavy alcohol use. Seek urgent medical help for severe weakness, vomiting, stomach pain, breathing difficulty, confusion, or signs of severe dehydration. This medicine may need to be stopped temporarily during serious illness, prolonged fasting, surgery, or certain contrast-dye procedures. Discuss use during pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain, soreness and inflammation in the mouth and gums, including mouth ulcers and sore gums.

How does it work?
Choline salicylate helps reduce pain and inflammation. Lignocaine locally numbs the area, while benzalkonium chloride helps limit the growth of some germs.

How to take/use it
For use inside the mouth only. Apply a small amount directly to the affected area with a clean finger or cotton bud, as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not swallow intentionally, and do not use more or for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Temporary numbness, mild burning or stinging, irritation, or an unpleasant taste may occur. Stop using it and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to choline salicylate, aspirin or other salicylates, lignocaine, or any ingredient. Use cautiously in children and only under healthcare professional advice. Avoid eating or drinking hot food and beverages while the mouth is numb. Do not apply to large areas, use excessively, or swallow it. Seek medical advice if mouth sores or pain persist or keep returning. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole 1% is an antifungal medicine used on the skin to treat fungal infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch.

How does it work?
It damages the protective outer membrane of fungi, stopping their growth and helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to clean, dry, affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, redness, itching, irritation or discomfort at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to clotrimazole or any ingredient. Avoid the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops, or if the infection worsens or does not improve as expected.

What is it used for?
Used as an antiseptic oral rinse to help reduce plaque and bacteria, support the treatment of gingivitis (gum inflammation), and help maintain oral hygiene. The fluoride may also help protect teeth against decay.

How does it work?
Chlorhexidine and triclosan reduce harmful bacteria in the mouth. Sodium fluoride helps strengthen tooth enamel and protect against dental decay.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a dentist. Rinse around the mouth and spit out; do not swallow. Do not dilute unless instructed. Keep the rinse away from the eyes.

Common side effects
Temporary staining of the teeth or tongue, altered taste, mouth irritation, dryness, or a mild burning sensation may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to chlorhexidine or any ingredient. Do not swallow. Stop using it and seek medical help if swelling, rash, breathing difficulty, or other signs of a serious allergic reaction occur. Prolonged use may cause tooth staining or taste changes; follow the dentist’s recommended duration. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of pain and inflammation, such as muscle, joint, back, dental or other mild-to-moderate painful conditions.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain, swelling and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not take it together with other paracetamol-containing medicines or painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, acidity or stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or blood-thinning medicine use. Avoid excessive alcohol. Do not use during the last 3 months of pregnancy, and seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop and seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, chest pain or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and reduce fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor, preferably with or after food, and swallow with water. Do not take more than the recommended dose or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other medicines containing diclofenac, paracetamol or other painkillers unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Stomach pain or discomfort, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAIDs. Avoid excessive alcohol. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin reactions, breathing difficulty or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially the last trimester, unless specifically prescribed.
