How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different mechanism.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more than the prescribed amount, and do not use it with other medicines containing diclofenac, other NSAIDs, or paracetamol unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Indigestion, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache may occur.

Precautions

Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, or asthma triggered by painkillers. Avoid excess alcohol. It may not be suitable during pregnancy, especially the third trimester. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin reactions, breathing difficulty or swelling of the face or throat.

What is it used for?
Dydrogesterone is used to treat conditions related to low progesterone, such as irregular or painful periods, heavy or abnormal menstrual bleeding, premenstrual symptoms and endometriosis. It may also be prescribed to support fertility treatment or as part of hormone replacement therapy, according to the doctor's advice.

How does it work?
It is a synthetic form of the natural hormone progesterone. It helps regulate the menstrual cycle and supports the lining of the uterus.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day, with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions in the package leaflet or ask a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Headache or migraine, nausea, breast tenderness, stomach or abdominal discomfort, changes in menstrual bleeding and mood changes may occur. Skin rash or itching can occur less commonly.

Precautions
Use during pregnancy only when specifically prescribed, and inform the doctor if pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about unexplained vaginal bleeding, liver problems, migraine, a history of blood clots or hormone-sensitive cancer. Seek medical advice for yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe abdominal pain, unusual bleeding or signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used to treat depression, anxiety disorders, panic disorder and social anxiety disorder.

How does it work?
Increases serotonin levels in the brain, helping regulate mood and reduce anxiety.

How to take/use it
Take orally as prescribed by the doctor, usually once daily. Do not stop suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, sleepiness, difficulty sleeping, sweating and dry mouth.

Precautions
Use under medical supervision. Inform the doctor about other medicines. Seek medical advice if mood worsens or suicidal thoughts occur.

What is it used for?
This combination is generally prescribed for bacterial infections with inflammation, most commonly affecting the eye or ear. The exact use depends on the prescribed formulation and the healthcare professional’s diagnosis.

How does it work?
Gentamicin kills susceptible bacteria. Dexamethasone reduces inflammation, redness and swelling.

Use only in the eye or ear as directed on the label or by the healthcare professional. Follow the prescribed instructions and do not use it for longer than advised. Do not use an eye product in the ear, or an ear product in the eye, unless specifically instructed.

Temporary burning, stinging, irritation, itching or blurred vision may occur after application. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Febuxostat is used to lower high uric acid levels in adults with gout. It helps prevent gout attacks and complications caused by uric acid crystals, but it does not provide immediate relief during an acute gout attack.

How does it work?
It blocks xanthine oxidase, an enzyme involved in producing uric acid. This lowers uric acid levels in the blood and helps prevent crystal build-up in the joints.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Continue taking it regularly even if feeling well. Do not stop it without medical advice. Gout attacks can occur when treatment is first started; follow the prescribed treatment for such attacks.

Common side effects
Nausea, joint pain or a gout flare, rash, and changes in liver function tests may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about heart disease, stroke, liver disease, or kidney problems. Febuxostat may increase cardiovascular risk in some people. It should not be taken with azathioprine or mercaptopurine unless specifically directed by a specialist. Seek urgent medical help for severe rash, facial swelling, breathing difficulty, chest pain, or sudden weakness.

It blocks xanthine oxidase, an enzyme involved in making uric acid. This lowers uric acid levels in the blood and helps prevent urate crystal build-up in the joints.

What is it used for?
Gatifloxacin 0.3% eye drops are used to treat bacterial eye infections, such as bacterial conjunctivitis.

How does it work?
It is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic that stops the growth of bacteria by blocking enzymes needed for bacterial DNA production.

How to take/use it
Use in the affected eye(s) exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before use and do not let the dropper tip touch the eye or any surface. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not use contact lenses while the eye is infected unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Temporary burning or stinging, eye irritation, redness, itching, blurred vision or watering may occur after application.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to gatifloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe swelling, rash, breathing difficulty or worsening eye symptoms occur. This medicine treats bacterial infections and will not treat viral or fungal eye infections.

What is it used for?
Gliclazide is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes.

How does it work?
It is a sulfonylurea medicine that helps the pancreas release more insulin. This lowers blood sugar levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with or just before food if directed. Take it at the same time each day and do not skip meals. If a dose is missed, do not take an extra dose; follow the prescriber's instructions.

Common side effects
Low blood sugar, which may cause sweating, shaking, hunger, dizziness or confusion; nausea, indigestion, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea or constipation; headache and weight gain.

Precautions
The risk of low blood sugar is higher if meals are skipped, alcohol is consumed, exercise is unusually intense, or other diabetes medicines are used. Carry a quick source of sugar and seek medical help for severe or repeated low-sugar symptoms. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines. Do not use for type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis unless specifically directed by a specialist.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin lowers LDL (“bad”) cholesterol by reducing cholesterol production and increasing its removal from the blood. Aspirin reduces the ability of platelets to stick together, helping prevent blood clots.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Swallow with water and do not stop it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist rather than taking extra medicine.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach discomfort, nausea, easy bruising or bleeding, headache, and muscle aches may occur. Seek medical help for unusual muscle weakness or severe or persistent bleeding.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers, bleeding problems, liver or kidney disease, asthma triggered by aspirin, or previous allergy to aspirin or other painkillers. Inform the doctor about all medicines, especially blood thinners and other medicines that increase bleeding risk. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised. Report unexplained muscle pain or weakness, dark urine, black stools, or vomiting blood promptly.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to lower high cholesterol and reduce the risk of harmful blood clots that can cause a heart attack or stroke. It is commonly prescribed for people with heart or blood-vessel disease, including after certain heart procedures, when both cholesterol control and antiplatelet treatment are needed.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin lowers the liver’s production of cholesterol, reducing harmful LDL cholesterol in the blood. Clopidogrel makes platelets less likely to stick together, helping prevent blood clots.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor and use it regularly. Do not stop taking it, especially clopidogrel, without medical advice. If a procedure or surgery is planned, inform the doctor that this medicine is being taken.

Common side effects
Bruising or easier bleeding, nosebleeds, headache, stomach pain, indigestion, nausea, diarrhoea or constipation, and muscle aches may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe weakness, or unexplained muscle pain or weakness with dark urine. Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, a history of bleeding, stomach ulcers, or any planned surgery or dental procedure. Inform the doctor about all medicines being used, particularly blood thinners, painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin, and other medicines that increase bleeding risk. Rosuvastatin should not be used during pregnancy and is generally avoided during breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to help reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and other blood-vessel problems in people with cardiovascular disease or a high risk of blood clots. It also lowers high cholesterol and helps prevent further heart-related events.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin lowers harmful LDL cholesterol made by the liver. Clopidogrel reduces the ability of blood platelets to stick together and form harmful clots.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, usually at the same time each day. Do not stop it without medical advice, especially after a heart procedure or stent. If a dose is missed, follow the doctor’s or pharmacist’s instructions.

Common side effects
Easy bruising or bleeding, headache, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, and muscle aches may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any history of bleeding, stomach ulcers, liver disease, kidney disease, or muscle problems. Seek medical help for unusual or prolonged bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe muscle pain or weakness, or dark urine. Tell the doctor or dentist before surgery or dental treatment. Avoid pregnancy and breastfeeding unless specifically advised, and report all other medicines because some can increase bleeding or muscle-related side effects.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat high cholesterol and high triglyceride levels in the blood, especially mixed dyslipidaemia. It helps reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke when used along with a suitable diet and other lifestyle measures.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin reduces the liver’s production of cholesterol, helping lower LDL (bad) cholesterol. Fenofibrate mainly lowers triglycerides and may increase HDL (good) cholesterol.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor and do not change or stop the treatment without medical advice. Follow the recommended diet and attend blood tests or follow-up visits as advised.

Common side effects
Muscle pain, headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and changes in liver blood tests may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, gallbladder problems, thyroid disorders, heavy alcohol use, or previous muscle problems with cholesterol medicines. Seek medical advice promptly for unexplained muscle pain or weakness, dark urine, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe abdominal pain. It should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, especially other cholesterol medicines and blood thinners, because interactions may increase side effects.

What is it used for?
This combination is used in people with coronary artery disease to lower cholesterol and help prevent blood clots, heart attacks and strokes. It may be prescribed after a heart attack or coronary stent procedure, as directed by a cardiologist.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin lowers harmful LDL cholesterol. Aspirin and clopidogrel reduce the ability of platelets to stick together, helping prevent harmful blood clots.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with water. Do not stop this medicine or skip doses without medical advice, especially after a stent. Do not take additional aspirin or other painkillers such as ibuprofen unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Easy bruising or bleeding, indigestion, nausea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and muscle aches may occur.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical help for heavy or prolonged bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe headache or weakness. Tell the doctor about a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, liver disease, kidney disease, planned surgery or dental treatment, or use of blood thinners or other medicines that increase bleeding risk. Report unexplained severe muscle pain, weakness or dark urine. Rosuvastatin is generally avoided during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and blood clots in people with coronary artery disease, including those recovering from a heart attack or undergoing angioplasty or stent treatment. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin lowers harmful LDL cholesterol and helps reduce cholesterol build-up in blood vessels. Aspirin and clopidogrel reduce platelet clumping, helping prevent harmful blood clots.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop taking it suddenly without medical advice, especially after a stent or heart attack. Do not take extra doses if one is missed; follow the prescribed instructions.

Common side effects
Easy bruising or bleeding, nosebleeds, indigestion, stomach discomfort, headache and muscle pain may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of stomach ulcer, bleeding disorder, liver or kidney disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, or muscle problems. Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe muscle pain or weakness, or dark urine. Inform the doctor or dentist before surgery or dental procedures. Avoid starting painkillers or blood-thinning medicines without medical advice. Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Rosuvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, especially LDL (“bad”) cholesterol and triglycerides. It may also be prescribed to reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It reduces cholesterol production in the liver by blocking an enzyme involved in making cholesterol. This helps lower LDL cholesterol in the blood.

Take it exactly as prescribed, usually once daily, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water and take it at the same time each day. Continue a healthy diet and exercise as advised by the doctor. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, muscle pain, weakness, nausea, stomach pain and constipation may occur. Contact a doctor promptly for unexplained or severe muscle pain or weakness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, thyroid problems, a history of muscle problems, or regular alcohol use. It should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, as some medicines can increase the risk of muscle-related side effects. Liver tests may be needed during treatment.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?

What is it used for?
Helps control dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis, which can cause flaky, itchy scalp or skin.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole and zinc pyrithione reduce the growth of fungi and yeast associated with dandruff. Glycerine and aloe vera help soothe and moisturise the skin.

For external use only. Apply to the affected scalp or skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not swallow.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Avoid applying to the eyes, mouth or severely broken skin. Rinse thoroughly if it gets into the eyes. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen, persist or frequently return.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is an anti-seizure medicine used to control seizures in epilepsy. It may be used alone or together with other anti-seizure medicines, as prescribed.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain, thereby lowering the likelihood of seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop taking it suddenly, as this may worsen seizures. If a dose is missed or vomiting occurs after taking it, follow the prescriber's instructions.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, weakness, nausea, and irritability or other mood changes may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or any history of depression or other mental health problems. Seek medical help for severe mood or behaviour changes, thoughts of self-harm, serious skin rash, swelling of the face or throat, or breathing difficulty. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known, and avoid alcohol unless the doctor permits it.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is an anti-seizure medicine used to prevent and control seizures in people with epilepsy, including focal seizures and certain generalized seizures. It may be used alone or with other anti-seizure medicines, as prescribed.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by acting on a nerve-cell protein involved in the release of chemical signals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop taking it suddenly, as seizures may worsen. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

What is it used for?

Temporary blurred vision, mild stinging, irritation or redness may occur after use.

Precautions

What is it used for?

It forms a lubricating layer over the surface of the eye, helping retain moisture and reduce friction and irritation.

Use in the eyes exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before use and do not let the dropper tip touch the eye or other surfaces. If contact lenses are worn, follow the product instructions about removing and replacing them.

Temporary blurred vision, mild stinging, burning or eye irritation may occur after use.

Precautions
For external eye use only. Do not use if the solution is cloudy, discoloured or contaminated. Seek medical advice for eye pain, vision changes, marked redness, discharge or symptoms that persist or worsen. Stop using it and seek advice if significant irritation or an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Used as lubricating eye drops to relieve dryness, burning, irritation and discomfort caused by dry eyes.

Polyethylene glycol 400 and propylene glycol form a moistening layer over the eye surface, helping keep the eyes lubricated.

How to take/use it
Use in the eyes exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface. If symptoms persist or worsen, seek medical advice.

What is it used for?

It stops the growth of fungi by interfering with the production of an essential part of the fungal cell membrane.

For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not use it in the eyes, mouth or other internal areas.

Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation where it is applied.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and broken or severely irritated skin. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Use only on the skin areas advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which helps clear the infection.

Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin exactly as prescribed. For external use only. Wash hands before and after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Do not apply in the eyes, mouth or other sensitive areas unless directed by a healthcare professional.

Mild burning, stinging, redness, itching or irritation where it is applied.

Precautions

Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Use only for the condition it was prescribed for and seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve.

What is it used for?
This product is used to supplement the diet with vitamins, minerals and other nutrients when dietary intake may be inadequate or nutritional needs are increased. It is not intended to replace a balanced diet or treat a specific illness unless advised by a healthcare professional.

It provides vitamins and minerals needed for normal body functions. Lycopene, beta-carotene and lutein are antioxidant nutrients, while L-lysine is an essential amino acid.

Precautions
Do not exceed the recommended amount, as excessive intake of some vitamins and minerals can be harmful. What is it used for?
Metoprolol tartrate is used to treat high blood pressure and certain heart conditions, such as angina (heart-related chest pain), fast or irregular heartbeat, and after a heart attack. It may also be prescribed for other heart-related conditions by a doctor.

It is a beta-blocker that slows the heartbeat and reduces the force with which the heart pumps. This lowers blood pressure and reduces the heart’s workload.

Take it exactly as prescribed. Follow the product instructions for whether it should be swallowed whole or allowed to dissolve. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Seek urgent medical help for new, severe, or persistent chest pain.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, flushing, nausea, weakness, and low blood pressure. A fast heartbeat may also occur.

Precautions
Do not use with sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil, or similar medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary hypertension, as this can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure. Rise slowly if dizzy, and avoid alcohol if it worsens dizziness or low blood pressure. Tell the doctor about low blood pressure, anaemia, or heart problems. Seek immediate medical help for fainting, severe dizziness, or worsening chest pain.

What is it used for?
Nitroglycerin is mainly used to prevent or relieve angina (chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart). It should be used as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens blood vessels, helping improve blood flow to the heart and reducing the heart's workload.

How to take/use it
Use it exactly as directed on the label or by the doctor. The instructions depend on the product form, so do not change the dose or how it is used. If chest pain is severe, new, or does not improve as instructed, seek emergency medical help.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, flushing, weakness, nausea, and low blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Stand up slowly because dizziness or fainting can occur. Do not use with sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil, or similar medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary hypertension, as this can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure. Avoid alcohol unless the doctor advises otherwise. Tell the doctor if there is low blood pressure, severe anaemia, glaucoma, or a recent head injury. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent chest pain, fainting, or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of acidity, heartburn, indigestion and discomfort caused by excess gas or bloating.

How does it work?
Magaldrate neutralises excess stomach acid. Simethicone breaks up gas bubbles in the stomach and intestines, helping gas pass more easily.

How to take/use it
Take or use exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Keep a gap of at least 2 hours from other medicines unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Constipation or diarrhoea, nausea, and mild stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, persistent or severe stomach pain, repeated vomiting, black stools or difficulty swallowing. Seek medical advice if symptoms continue or frequently return. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals and those taking other medicines should ask a doctor or pharmacist before use.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 200 mg is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the urinary tract, lungs, skin, or other parts of the body. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making and repairing their genetic material, which prevents the bacteria from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium, or zinc; ask a doctor or pharmacist about the appropriate interval.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, and sleep disturbance may occur.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice. Tell the doctor about allergy to ofloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics, kidney disease, heart-rhythm problems, seizures, tendon problems, nerve problems, or myasthenia gravis. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or burning sensations, severe mood or nerve symptoms, a severe skin rash, breathing difficulty, or persistent severe diarrhoea. Avoid driving if dizzy or affected by vision or nervous-system symptoms. Discuss use during pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor.

What is it used for?
Olanzapine is an antipsychotic medicine used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, including manic episodes. It may also help prevent the return of mood episodes in bipolar disorder when prescribed for this purpose.

How does it work?
It helps balance certain chemical messengers in the brain, including dopamine and serotonin. This can reduce hallucinations, delusions, severe mood changes and agitation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and at the same time each day. It can usually be taken with or without food. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice, even if symptoms improve. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, increased appetite, weight gain, dry mouth, constipation, tiredness and swelling of the hands or feet. It may also increase blood sugar and blood cholesterol levels.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about diabetes, high cholesterol, seizures, liver disease, heart problems or a history of stroke. Avoid alcohol because it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Blood sugar, weight and cholesterol may need monitoring. Seek urgent medical help for severe muscle stiffness with fever, uncontrolled movements, fainting, or symptoms of very high blood sugar. In older adults with dementia-related psychosis, this medicine may increase the risk of stroke and death and is not usually recommended.

What is it used for?
Olanzapine is an antipsychotic medicine used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, including episodes of unusually high mood, energy or activity. It may also be used with other medicines for certain mood disorders when prescribed by a specialist.

How does it work?
It helps balance dopamine and serotonin, chemical messengers in the brain involved in mood, thinking and behaviour.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day if possible. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, increased appetite, weight gain, dizziness, dry mouth and constipation may occur. Blood sugar and cholesterol levels may also increase.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high cholesterol, liver disease, seizures, heart problems or glaucoma. Avoid alcohol because it can increase drowsiness. Regular monitoring of weight, blood sugar and cholesterol may be needed. Seek medical help for severe muscle stiffness, high fever, confusion, uncontrolled movements or extreme drowsiness. It is not generally recommended for treating behavioural problems in older adults with dementia unless specifically advised by a specialist.

What is it used for?
Olanzapine is an antipsychotic medicine used to treat schizophrenia and manic episodes associated with bipolar disorder. It may also be used to help prevent these symptoms from returning when prescribed for ongoing treatment.

How does it work?
It helps balance the activity of certain chemical messengers in the brain, including dopamine and serotonin. This can reduce symptoms such as hallucinations, delusions, severe mood changes and agitation.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Take it at the recommended time each day and do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, increased appetite, weight gain, dizziness, dry mouth, constipation and tiredness. It may also increase blood sugar and cholesterol levels.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about diabetes, high cholesterol, liver disease, seizures, heart problems or a history of stroke. Weight, blood sugar and cholesterol may need monitoring. Seek urgent medical help for severe muscle stiffness, high fever, confusion, uncontrolled movements or fainting. Older adults with dementia-related psychosis have an increased risk of serious complications with this medicine.

What is it used for?
Olmesartan medoxomil is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and other complications.

How does it work?
It is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB). It relaxes and widens blood vessels, helping blood flow more easily and lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food, and try to take it at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, diarrhoea, nausea and tiredness may occur. Contact a doctor if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, or high potassium levels. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor. Do not use during pregnancy; contact a doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing. Blood pressure, kidney function and potassium levels may need monitoring.

What is it used for?
Olmesartan medoxomil is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering blood pressure helps reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and other complications.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of angiotensin II, a substance that narrows blood vessels and raises blood pressure. This helps relax the blood vessels and lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food, and preferably at the same time each day. Do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, diarrhoea, nausea and tiredness may occur. Contact a doctor if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, or use of potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes, diuretics or other blood-pressure medicines. Medical monitoring may be needed for blood pressure, kidney function and potassium levels. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips or tongue, or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension), especially when blood pressure is not adequately controlled with one medicine alone. Lowering blood pressure helps reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and other complications.

How does it work?
Olmesartan relaxes blood vessels by blocking a hormone that tightens them. Amlodipine relaxes the blood vessels, while hydrochlorothiazide helps the body remove excess salt and water through urine.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment without medical advice. Follow the prescribed monitoring schedule for blood pressure and blood tests.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, ankle or leg swelling, increased urination, nausea and stomach discomfort. Changes in kidney function or blood salt levels may also occur.

Precautions
May cause dizziness, especially when starting treatment or after a dose change; rise slowly from sitting or lying down. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, diabetes, gout, dehydration or low blood pressure. Blood pressure, kidney function and electrolytes may need monitoring. Do not use during pregnancy; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure when treatment with more than one medicine is needed. Controlling blood pressure helps lower the risk of complications such as heart attack and stroke.

How does it work?
Olmesartan blocks a hormone that narrows blood vessels, while amlodipine relaxes blood vessels. Hydrochlorothiazide helps the body remove extra salt and water through urine, together lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Do not take a double dose if a dose is missed; follow the prescriber's instructions.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, ankle or leg swelling, increased urination, nausea, and stomach upset may occur. Changes in blood salts or kidney function can also occur.

Precautions
Rise slowly if feeling dizzy, and use caution while driving until the effects are known. Regular blood pressure, kidney function, and blood-salt checks may be needed. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, gout, or diabetes. Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically advised; contact a doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Inform the doctor about potassium supplements, salt substitutes, lithium, painkillers such as ibuprofen, or other blood-pressure medicines.

What is it used for?
Used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) when a combination of medicines is required.

How does it work?
Olmesartan relaxes blood vessels, while Hydrochlorothiazide helps remove excess salt and water through urine.

How to take/use it
Take orally as prescribed by the doctor, preferably at the same time each day.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, weakness and increased urination.

Precautions
Monitor blood pressure, kidney function and electrolyte levels. Inform the doctor about kidney problems, dehydration or pregnancy.

What is it used for?
Used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension).

How does it work?
Olmesartan relaxes blood vessels, while Hydrochlorothiazide removes excess salt and water from the body.

How to take/use it
Take orally according to the doctor's prescription. Do not adjust the dose yourself.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, weakness and increased urination.

Precautions
Regularly monitor blood pressure and kidney function. Inform the doctor about pregnancy, kidney problems or dehydration.

What is it used for?
Esomeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be prescribed for stomach or intestinal ulcers and other acid-related conditions.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of acid in the stomach by blocking the stomach’s acid-producing pumps. This helps relieve symptoms and allows acid-damaged tissues to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually before food. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it unless specifically instructed. Follow the prescribed dose and treatment duration.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, allergies to acid-reducing medicines, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or persistent symptoms. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor and may affect some medicines and nutrient levels.

What is it used for?
Lactulose is mainly used to relieve constipation by making stools softer and easier to pass. It may also be prescribed by a doctor for certain liver-related complications.

How does it work?
It draws water into the bowel, which softens the stool and helps stimulate bowel movements. It is broken down by natural bacteria in the colon.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the label or by the doctor. Measure the prescribed amount carefully; it may be taken alone or mixed with water or another suitable drink. Drink enough fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, stomach cramps, nausea and diarrhoea. Diarrhoea may occur if too much is taken.

Precautions
Do not use it if there is suspected bowel blockage or severe unexplained abdominal pain. Seek medical advice if constipation does not improve, or if severe or persistent diarrhoea occurs. People with diabetes or those on prolonged or high-dose treatment should use it under medical supervision, as fluid and electrolyte disturbances may occur.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve occasional constipation and help make hard stools easier to pass.

How does it work?
Milk of magnesia draws water into the bowel to soften stool and encourage bowel movement. Liquid paraffin lubricates the stool and bowel, helping it pass more easily.

How to take/use it
For oral use only. Take exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Measure the liquid accurately and do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not use regularly or for a long period without medical advice.

Common side effects
Loose stools or diarrhoea, abdominal cramps, bloating, nausea and stomach discomfort. Liquid paraffin may occasionally cause leakage or irritation around the anus.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is severe or persistent abdominal pain, vomiting, abdominal swelling or suspected bowel blockage. Use cautiously in kidney disease, swallowing difficulties, or in people who are elderly or bedridden, as liquid paraffin may enter the lungs if swallowed incorrectly. Keep a gap from other oral medicines if advised by a healthcare professional, as milk of magnesia may affect their absorption. Consult a healthcare professional during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of constipation and to help make hard stools easier to pass.

How does it work?
Liquid paraffin lubricates and softens the stool, while milk of magnesia draws water into the bowel. Sodium picosulfate stimulates bowel movement.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Measure the liquid accurately using a measuring device. Do not take more than recommended or use it for a prolonged period without medical advice.

Common side effects
Abdominal cramps, bloating, nausea and loose stools or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is severe abdominal pain, vomiting, suspected bowel blockage or unexplained rectal bleeding. Drink adequate fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised. Prolonged or excessive use may cause dehydration or electrolyte imbalance. Seek medical advice if constipation persists or keeps returning.

What is it used for?
This combination provides short-term relief of common cold and flu-like symptoms such as fever, headache, body aches, blocked or runny nose, sneezing and nasal congestion. It relieves symptoms but does not cure the underlying infection.

How does it work?
Nimesulide reduces pain and fever, phenylephrine helps reduce nasal congestion, and cetirizine reduces allergy-related sneezing and runny nose. Caffeine may enhance pain relief and help reduce drowsiness.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow with water, preferably after food. Do not take more than recommended or combine it with other cold, antihistamine, decongestant or pain-relief medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, dizziness, drowsiness, dry mouth, headache, palpitations, restlessness or difficulty sleeping may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol. Consult a doctor before use if there is liver disease, stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney disease, high blood pressure, heart disease, thyroid disease or glaucoma. Stop use and seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, vomiting blood, breathing difficulty or allergic swelling. Drowsiness may occur; avoid driving if affected. Avoid excess caffeine. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 500 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, body pain, toothache and muscle aches.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of chemical signals involved in pain and helps lower raised body temperature.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth with water, following the dose and timing on the package or as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it with other medicines containing paracetamol.

Common side effects
It is usually well tolerated when used correctly. Nausea or a skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if there is liver disease, regular alcohol use or poor nutrition. Avoid combining it with other paracetamol-containing products. Taking more than recommended can cause serious liver damage; seek urgent medical help after an overdose, even if feeling well. Stop use and seek medical help for swelling, breathing difficulty or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, headache, toothache and muscle pain.

How does it work?
It works mainly in the brain to reduce the substances that cause pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take or use exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than recommended or use it with other medicines containing paracetamol. Check the strength carefully, especially when giving it to a child.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when used correctly. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to paracetamol. Ask a healthcare professional before use if there is liver disease, regular heavy alcohol use, severe kidney disease or poor nutrition. Overdose can cause serious liver damage, even if the person feels well; seek urgent medical help after taking too much.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 250 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, toothache, body pain and muscle aches.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol. Do not exceed the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when used as directed. Nausea or mild skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is liver disease or regular heavy alcohol use. Check other medicines for paracetamol to avoid an overdose. Seek urgent medical help after taking more than the recommended amount, even if feeling well. Stop use and seek help for swelling, breathing difficulty or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 650 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, body pain, toothache and muscle aches.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of certain chemical messengers involved in pain and fever, helping lower body temperature and relieve pain.

Take it by mouth with water, exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol, and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Side effects are uncommon when used as directed. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is liver disease, regular alcohol use or an allergy to paracetamol. Seek urgent medical help after taking more than the recommended amount, even if feeling well. Stop use and seek advice if a serious allergic reaction or severe skin rash occurs.

What is it used for?
Ramipril 2.5 mg is mainly used to treat high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed for heart failure or to help reduce the risk of certain heart and blood-vessel problems.

It is an ACE inhibitor that relaxes and widens blood vessels. This lowers blood pressure and makes it easier for the heart to pump blood.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, including pain from sprains, strains and arthritis.

How does it work?
Diclofenac helps reduce pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling or warming sensation that may help relieve local muscle and joint discomfort.

For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the painful area as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands after application and avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site. Stop use if severe skin irritation or an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, including sprains, strains and arthritis-related pain.

How does it work?
Diclofenac is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine that reduces substances causing pain and inflammation. Methyl salicylate provides additional local pain-relieving action when applied to the skin.

For external use only. Apply to clean, intact skin over the painful area as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Application-site burning, redness, itching, dryness, rash or irritation.

Precautions

Avoid using other diclofenac or NSAID products at the same time unless advised.

What is it used for?
Used to treat bacterial eye infections accompanied by redness, swelling or inflammation. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

Ofloxacin is an antibiotic that stops the growth of susceptible bacteria. Dexamethasone reduces eye inflammation, while hydroxypropylmethylcellulose helps lubricate the eye.

Temporary stinging or burning, eye irritation, blurred vision after application, watery eyes or an unpleasant taste in the mouth may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ofloxacin, dexamethasone or similar medicines. Steroid-containing eye medicines may worsen undiagnosed viral or fungal eye infections and may increase eye pressure or delay healing when used for too long. What is it used for?
Used to treat bacterial infections of the eye. The hydroxypropylmethylcellulose component helps lubricate and soothe the eye surface. It will not treat viral or fungal eye infections.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin is an antibiotic that stops the growth of bacteria by interfering with essential bacterial enzymes. Hydroxypropylmethylcellulose forms a lubricating layer over the eye surface.

Use only in the eye and exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before use, avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or other surfaces, and do not share the bottle. If temporary blurred vision occurs, avoid driving until vision is clear.

Common side effects
Temporary burning or stinging, eye irritation, redness, itching, watering, or blurred vision may occur after application.

Precautions

Sacubitril helps increase substances that relax blood vessels and reduce salt and fluid retention. Valsartan blocks a hormone effect that can narrow blood vessels and put extra strain on the heart.

What is it used for?
Sacubitril 97 mg + valsartan 103 mg is used for the long-term treatment of certain types of heart failure, especially heart failure with reduced pumping ability. It helps reduce the risk of worsening heart failure and hospitalisation.

How does it work?
Sacubitril helps relax blood vessels and reduce strain on the heart. Valsartan blocks a hormone that can narrow blood vessels and increase blood pressure, helping the heart pump more efficiently.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually at the same times each day, with or without food. Do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice. Do not take it together with an ACE inhibitor; a suitable gap is required when switching between these medicines.

Dizziness, low blood pressure, cough, increased potassium levels, and changes in kidney function.

Thyroxine sodium is used as thyroid hormone replacement to treat an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism). It may also be used when the thyroid gland is not producing enough thyroid hormone for other medical reasons.

How does it work?
It replaces the thyroxine hormone normally produced by the thyroid gland, helping restore normal body functions affected by low thyroid hormone levels.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and at the same time each day. It is usually taken on an empty stomach with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Calcium, iron, antacids and some other medicines may reduce its absorption, so ask a doctor or pharmacist about suitable separation.

Common side effects
Side effects are more likely if the dose is too high and may include fast or irregular heartbeat, nervousness, tremor, sweating, difficulty sleeping, headache, diarrhoea and weight loss.

Precautions
Regular blood tests are needed to check thyroid hormone levels and adjust the dose. Tell the doctor about heart disease, diabetes, pregnancy, adrenal problems or any other medicines being taken. Seek medical help for chest pain, severe palpitations or shortness of breath.

How does it work?
It supplies a synthetic form of thyroxine, a hormone normally made by the thyroid gland. This helps restore normal body functions affected by low thyroid hormone levels.

Take exactly as prescribed, preferably on an empty stomach with water and at the same time each day. Do not stop or change the dose without medical advice. Keep a suitable gap between this medicine and iron or calcium supplements, as they can reduce its absorption.

When the dose is higher than needed, side effects may include fast or irregular heartbeat, nervousness, tremor, sweating, difficulty sleeping, headache, diarrhoea and weight loss.

This medicine should not be used for weight loss.

What is it used for?
Ticagrelor is an antiplatelet medicine used with prescribed treatment to help prevent harmful blood clots and reduce the risk of heart attack or stroke in people with acute coronary syndrome or a previous heart attack.

How does it work?
It stops blood platelets from sticking together and forming clots by blocking the P2Y12 platelet receptor.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Take it regularly and do not stop it without medical advice, as stopping suddenly may increase the risk of a heart attack or clot. If a procedure or surgery is planned, inform the doctor or dentist.

Common side effects
Bleeding or bruising, shortness of breath, headache, dizziness, nausea and diarrhoea.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, or sudden severe headache. Tell the doctor about any bleeding disorder, past brain bleeding, liver disease, planned surgery, or use of aspirin, blood thinners, painkillers such as ibuprofen, or other medicines. Do not take it without medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used to treat bacterial eye infections accompanied by redness, swelling or other inflammation. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Tobramycin is an antibiotic that stops the growth of susceptible bacteria. Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation, redness and swelling.

How to take/use it
Use in the eye exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before use and avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or any surface. Do not use it for longer than advised, and do not share the medicine. Remove contact lenses before use unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Temporary burning, stinging, irritation or blurred vision after application. Prolonged use may increase eye pressure, delay healing or cause other eye problems.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is glaucoma, a history of herpes eye infection, or an eye injury. This medicine may worsen untreated viral or fungal eye infections. Seek medical advice if eye pain, vision changes, worsening redness or swelling develops, or if symptoms do not improve. Avoid driving until blurred vision clears.

What is it used for?
Tobramycin is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections caused by susceptible bacteria. The exact site of treatment depends on the product formulation; use it only for the route and infection stated on the label or prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents them from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed and only by the route stated on the product label. Do not use it for viral or fungal infections, and do not share it with others. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include irritation, redness, burning or stinging at the application site, and allergic reactions. Side effects depend on the formulation and route of use.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to tobramycin or similar aminoglycoside antibiotics. Seek medical help for severe rash, swelling, breathing difficulty, worsening infection, or other serious symptoms. If using an eye preparation, avoid touching the applicator tip and remove contact lenses unless advised otherwise.

What is it used for?
Tofacitinib is used to treat certain autoimmune inflammatory conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and ulcerative colitis. The exact use depends on the doctor's prescription.

How does it work?
It blocks Janus kinase (JAK) enzymes involved in immune-system signals. This helps reduce the inflammation and symptoms caused by an overactive immune response.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole with water; do not crush, split or chew it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Upper respiratory tract infections, headache, diarrhoea, nausea and increased cholesterol levels may occur.

Precautions
This medicine can increase the risk of serious infections, including tuberculosis and hepatitis. Screening and regular blood tests may be needed. Tell the doctor about any infection, liver disease, cancer, blood-clotting or heart problems, or use of other medicines that weaken the immune system. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically advised. Seek urgent medical help for severe infection symptoms, chest pain, breathing difficulty, sudden weakness or a painful swollen leg.

What is it used for?
Tofacitinib is used to treat inflammatory autoimmune conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ulcerative colitis and certain types of juvenile arthritis. It is usually prescribed when other treatments have not worked well enough or are not suitable.

How does it work?
It blocks Janus kinase (JAK) proteins involved in immune-system signalling. This helps reduce the inflammation and overactive immune response that causes symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water; it may generally be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Upper respiratory infections, headache, diarrhoea, nausea, high blood pressure and increased cholesterol levels may occur. Shingles and other infections can also occur.

Precautions
Tofacitinib can increase the risk of serious infections, tuberculosis, shingles, blood clots, heart problems and certain cancers. Tell the doctor about any current or repeated infection, tuberculosis or hepatitis, heart disease, cancer, blood-clot history, or liver or kidney problems. Screening and blood tests may be needed during treatment. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically advised. Seek urgent medical help for severe infection symptoms, chest pain, sudden breathlessness, or painful swelling of an arm or leg. Tell the doctor if pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding, and before taking other medicines that suppress the immune system.

What is it used for?
Used under specialist supervision for certain conditions involving low blood sodium (hyponatraemia). Tolvaptan may also be prescribed for specific kidney conditions, depending on the treatment plan and product indication.
How does it work?
Tolvaptan blocks vasopressin V2 receptors in the kidneys, increasing the excretion of water while helping retain sodium. This can increase blood sodium levels in selected patients.
How to take/use it
Take only under specialist supervision and follow the prescribed dose. Do not change your fluid intake or dose without medical advice.
Common side effects
Thirst, dry mouth, increased urination, and dehydration may occur.
Precautions
Close monitoring of blood sodium and hydration is important because sodium correction that occurs too quickly can cause serious neurological injury. Liver function monitoring may also be required. Inform your doctor about liver disease, kidney problems, dehydration, or other medicines. Seek urgent medical attention for confusion, difficulty speaking, seizures, or severe weakness.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat anaemia caused by deficiency of iron, folic acid or vitamin B12. It helps support healthy red blood cell formation.

How does it work?
It supplies iron, folic acid and vitamin B12, which are needed to make haemoglobin and healthy red blood cells.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than the recommended amount. If it causes stomach upset, taking it with food may help. Keep it out of the reach of children.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and dark-coloured stools may occur.

Precautions
Use under medical advice, especially if the cause of anaemia is unknown. Tell the doctor about iron-overload disorders, other blood disorders, or stomach and bowel problems. Iron may interact with some medicines, including antacids and certain antibiotics; ask a pharmacist about suitable spacing between doses.

What is it used for?
Torsemide is used to reduce excess fluid retention (oedema), which may occur with heart, kidney or liver problems. It may also be prescribed to help control high blood pressure.

How does it work?
It is a diuretic, or “water tablet.” It helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water from the body through urine, reducing swelling and sometimes lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. It is usually taken earlier in the day because it increases urination. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, headache, nausea, stomach upset, weakness, dehydration and changes in body salts such as low potassium.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is kidney or liver disease, low blood pressure, dehydration, diabetes or gout. Rise slowly if dizziness occurs, and follow advice about fluid and salt intake. Seek medical help for severe weakness, fainting, confusion, irregular heartbeat, very little urine or signs of severe dehydration. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially lithium or other medicines that lower blood pressure or affect body salts.

What is it used for?
Torsemide is a diuretic used to remove excess fluid from the body, such as swelling related to heart failure or certain kidney or liver conditions. It may also be prescribed to help control high blood pressure.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water from the body through urine. This reduces fluid buildup and may lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Because it increases urination, it is generally best taken at a time that will not disturb sleep. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, headache, weakness, stomach upset, dehydration, low blood pressure, and changes in body salts such as sodium or potassium.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Regular monitoring of blood pressure, kidney function, and blood salts may be needed. Tell the doctor about severe vomiting or diarrhoea, dehydration, gout, diabetes, liver or kidney disease, or hearing problems. Seek medical help for fainting, severe weakness, confusion, irregular heartbeat, or very little urine. Inform the doctor about all medicines, especially lithium, digoxin, blood-pressure medicines, and anti-inflammatory painkillers.

What is it used for?
Torsemide is a diuretic used to reduce swelling caused by fluid buildup, often related to heart failure or kidney or liver problems. It may also be prescribed to help control high blood pressure.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water from the body through urine. This reduces fluid buildup and may lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. It increases urination, so follow the prescribed timing and do not change the dose without medical advice. Regular monitoring of blood pressure, kidney function and blood electrolyte levels may be needed.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, headache, low blood pressure, dehydration, nausea and changes in blood electrolyte levels such as low potassium or sodium.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, low blood pressure, gout or diabetes. Seek medical advice for severe dizziness, fainting, extreme thirst, muscle cramps, confusion or very little urine. Some medicines, including lithium, certain painkillers such as NSAIDs and other blood-pressure medicines, may interact with torsemide.

What is it used for?
Torsemide is a prescription diuretic used to reduce excess fluid swelling (oedema), especially in heart failure and sometimes in kidney or liver-related fluid retention. It may also be prescribed to help control high blood pressure.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water from the body through urine. This reduces fluid buildup and can lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow it with water. Because it increases urination, follow the prescribed timing and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, headache, weakness, low blood pressure, dehydration, and changes in blood salts such as low potassium or sodium.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, low blood pressure, dehydration, gout, diabetes, or an allergy to diuretics. Medical monitoring of kidney function, blood pressure, and electrolytes may be needed. Seek medical advice for severe dizziness, fainting, confusion, very low urine output, or signs of dehydration.

What is it used for?
Torsemide 10 mg + spironolactone 50 mg is used to remove excess salt and water from the body and reduce swelling (oedema), commonly in conditions such as heart failure. It may also be prescribed for fluid retention related to liver or kidney problems, only when directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Torsemide and spironolactone are diuretics (water tablets) that help the kidneys remove extra salt and water through urine. Spironolactone also blocks the action of a hormone that causes salt and water retention and helps retain potassium.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day if possible. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Because it increases urination, follow the prescriber's instructions about fluid intake and monitoring.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, low blood pressure, dehydration, weakness, nausea, and changes in blood potassium or other body salts. Spironolactone may also cause breast tenderness or enlargement.

Precautions
This medicine requires monitoring of kidney function, blood pressure, potassium, and other electrolytes. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, liver disease, dehydration, low blood pressure, or high potassium levels. Do not use potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Inform the doctor about all medicines, especially ACE inhibitors, ARBs, other diuretics, NSAID painkillers, or lithium. Seek medical help for fainting, severe weakness, confusion, very low urine output, or an irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
This medicine helps remove excess salt and water from the body and is used to reduce swelling or fluid retention related to conditions such as heart failure, liver disease or kidney problems. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Torsemide increases urine production, helping the body remove excess fluid. Spironolactone also removes fluid while helping the body retain potassium.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may increase urination, so avoid taking it close to bedtime unless directed otherwise. Do not change the dose or stop it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist and do not double the next dose.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, low blood pressure, dehydration, weakness, nausea and changes in blood potassium or sodium levels. Spironolactone may also cause breast tenderness or enlargement.

Precautions
Regular blood tests may be needed to check kidney function and electrolytes, especially potassium. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, low blood pressure, high potassium or Addison’s disease. Avoid potassium supplements and potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Inform the doctor about use of blood-pressure medicines, other diuretics, painkillers such as ibuprofen, or lithium. Seek medical help for severe dizziness, fainting, very low urine output, confusion, or an irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used for certain liver and bile-flow conditions, including primary biliary cholangitis. It may also be prescribed to dissolve selected cholesterol gallstones when suitable.

How does it work?
It changes the composition of bile, helping reduce cholesterol build-up and improve bile flow. It may also help protect liver cells from the effects of harmful bile acids.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with water. Follow the prescribed timing and treatment duration, and do not stop it without medical advice. The medicine may need to be taken for a long period and works only for suitable types of gallstones.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea or loose stools, abdominal discomfort, nausea, and itching may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is blockage of the bile ducts, acute gallbladder inflammation, or significant liver disease. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other medicines being taken. Antacids containing aluminium and some cholesterol-lowering bile acid medicines may reduce its absorption and may need to be taken separately.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used to treat certain liver and bile-flow disorders, including primary biliary cholangitis. It may also be prescribed to dissolve selected cholesterol gallstones when the gallbladder is functioning properly.

How does it work?
It improves the flow and composition of bile, making bile less likely to damage liver cells and less likely to form cholesterol deposits. This can help dissolve some cholesterol gallstones over time.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Take it regularly and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular liver tests or scans may be needed during treatment.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, loose stools, abdominal discomfort, nausea, or indigestion. Contact a doctor if diarrhoea is severe or persistent.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is liver disease, gallbladder inflammation, or suspected blockage of the bile ducts. It may not be suitable for all types of gallstones. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other medicines, particularly antacids containing aluminium or medicines that bind bile acids, as these may reduce its absorption.

What is it used for?
Used to treat high blood pressure, heart failure and certain patients after a heart attack.

How does it work?
Relaxes blood vessels by blocking the action of angiotensin II, helping the heart pump blood more easily.

How to take/use it
Take orally as prescribed by the doctor, with or without food.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache and increased potassium levels.

Precautions
Monitor blood pressure, kidney function and potassium levels. Not recommended during pregnancy.

What is it used for?
Used to treat high blood pressure and heart failure. It may also be prescribed after a heart attack.

How does it work?
Blocks angiotensin II receptors, helping blood vessels relax and reducing blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take orally according to the doctor's instructions, with or without food.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache and increased potassium levels.

Precautions
Monitor kidney function and blood pressure. Avoid use during pregnancy.

What is it used for?
Used to manage high blood pressure, heart failure and certain conditions following a heart attack.

How does it work?
Blocks angiotensin II, allowing blood vessels to relax and improving blood flow.

How to take/use it
Take orally as prescribed by the doctor.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache and increased potassium levels.

Precautions
Regularly monitor blood pressure and kidney function. Inform the doctor about pregnancy or kidney problems.

What is it used for?
Vildagliptin is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It may be used alone or together with other diabetes medicines.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called DPP-4, helping the body release insulin after meals and reduce the release of excess glucose from the liver. This helps lower blood sugar levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. It may be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If used with other diabetes medicines, follow the prescribed schedule carefully.

Common side effects
Nausea, dizziness, headache, constipation and shaking or tremor may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when it is taken with insulin or sulfonylurea medicines.

Precautions
It is intended for type 2 diabetes and should not be used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems; dose adjustment or monitoring may be needed. Seek medical help for severe, persistent abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, swelling of the face or throat, or a serious skin reaction. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Vildagliptin is used to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes, usually along with diet and exercise. It may be used alone or with other diabetes medicines when needed.

How does it work?
It helps the body release more insulin after meals and reduces the amount of sugar made by the liver. This helps lower blood sugar levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Take it regularly and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Continue the recommended diet, exercise and blood sugar monitoring.

Common side effects
Nausea, dizziness, headache, shaking or low blood sugar (especially when taken with insulin or sulfonylureas), constipation, and joint pain may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, heart failure, or a history of pancreatitis before use. Seek medical help for severe, persistent abdominal pain, especially if it spreads to the back, as this may indicate pancreatitis. Report yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness, which may indicate liver problems. The risk of low blood sugar is higher when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used to help control blood glucose in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus when prescribed by a doctor, alongside diet and exercise.
How does it work?
Vildagliptin inhibits the DPP-4 enzyme, helping regulate incretin hormones and glucose-dependent insulin release. Dapagliflozin blocks the SGLT2 protein in the kidneys, increasing urinary glucose excretion.
How to take/use it
Take orally as prescribed. Follow the product-specific instructions for the sustained-release formulation. Swallow the tablet as directed and do not crush or chew it unless the leaflet permits it.
Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, genital fungal infections, urinary tract infections, and dehydration may occur.
Precautions
Monitor blood glucose and kidney function as advised. Maintain adequate hydration according to your doctor's instructions. Seek urgent medical attention for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, or difficulty breathing, which may indicate diabetic ketoacidosis even if blood glucose is not very high. Inform your doctor about liver disease, kidney problems, or planned surgery.

What is it used for?
Vildagliptin 50 mg + metformin 1000 mg is used with diet and exercise to control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Vildagliptin helps the body release insulin when blood sugar is high and reduces the release of glucagon. Metformin lowers glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or after food, to reduce stomach upset. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain or discomfort, vomiting, gas, headache and dizziness may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, liver disease, heart failure, pancreatitis, heavy alcohol use, or any planned surgery or contrast-dye scan. Kidney and liver function may need monitoring. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, unusual weakness, difficulty breathing, or signs of a serious allergic reaction. Avoid excessive alcohol. What is it used for?
Vildagliptin 50 mg + metformin 500 mg is used with diet and exercise to control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It helps improve blood glucose control when one medicine alone is not enough.

How does it work?
Vildagliptin helps the body release insulin when blood sugar is high and reduces excess glucose production. Metformin mainly reduces glucose production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with or after food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet whole and do not stop treatment without medical advice. Do not take extra doses if a dose is missed; follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain or discomfort, vomiting, reduced appetite, headache, dizziness and a metallic taste. Low blood sugar may occur, especially when used with insulin or sulfonylure medicines.
