Seek medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, unusual weakness, breathing difficulty or severe drowsiness. This medicine is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis. Inform the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding, and before surgery or procedures involving contrast dye.

What is it used for?
Voglibose is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in people with type 2 diabetes, especially the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How does it work?
It slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates in the intestine. This helps reduce the increase in blood sugar after eating.

How to take/use it
Take it just before meals, exactly as prescribed. Follow the recommended diet and blood sugar monitoring plan. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort or pain, diarrhoea, and constipation.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is kidney or liver disease, digestive or intestinal disease, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Low blood sugar may occur when used with insulin or other diabetes medicines; seek medical advice if symptoms such as sweating, shakiness, dizziness, or confusion occur. Report severe abdominal pain or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Used to control the rise in blood sugar levels after meals in people with type 2 diabetes.

How does it work?
Slows the breakdown and absorption of carbohydrates in the intestine, reducing the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How to take/use it
Take immediately before meals as prescribed by the doctor.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort and diarrhoea.

Precautions
Monitor blood sugar regularly. Inform the doctor about intestinal disorders. Low blood sugar may require glucose rather than ordinary table sugar.

What is it used for?
Used to manage blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes, particularly after meals.

How does it work?
Voglibose slows carbohydrate absorption, while Metformin reduces glucose production in the liver and improves insulin sensitivity.

How to take/use it
Take with meals as prescribed by the doctor.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, diarrhoea, nausea and abdominal discomfort.

Precautions

What is it used for?
Pancreatin is used as pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy when the pancreas does not produce enough digestive enzymes. It helps the body digest fats, proteins and carbohydrates, such as in pancreatic insufficiency.

How does it work?
It supplies enzymes similar to those normally made by the pancreas. These enzymes help break down food so nutrients can be absorbed.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed or as stated on the product label, usually with meals or snacks. If the product is enteric-coated, swallow it whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose without medical advice.

Precautions

What is it used for?
Pancreatin is used as digestive enzyme replacement when the pancreas does not produce enough enzymes. It helps improve the digestion and absorption of fats, proteins and carbohydrates, including in conditions such as chronic pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis or after pancreatic surgery.

How does it work?
It supplies pancreatic enzymes, including lipase, amylase and protease, to help break down food in the intestine.

Use exactly as prescribed or directed on the product label. It is generally taken with meals and snacks. Swallow the medicine as directed; do not crush or chew enteric-coated preparations unless specifically advised.

Abdominal pain, bloating, nausea, constipation or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about an allergy to pancreatin or pork proteins, cystic fibrosis, gout or high uric acid levels. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, constipation or vomiting. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
This product provides L-arginine and proanthocyanidins as a nutritional supplement. Its specific medical use depends on the product formulation and the advice of a healthcare professional; it should not be used to self-treat a particular condition.

How does it work?
L-arginine is used by the body to make nitric oxide, which helps support normal blood vessel function. Proanthocyanidins are plant compounds with antioxidant activity.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or prescribed by a healthcare professional. Follow the instructions for preparing the granules and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is low blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease, liver disease, asthma, or recurrent herpes infection. Discuss its use with a healthcare professional if taking blood-pressure medicines, nitrates, medicines for erectile dysfunction, or blood thinners. Stop use and seek advice if troublesome effects occur.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is an anabolic steroid prescribed mainly to help manage osteoporosis and bone loss. In some cases, a specialist may use it for certain types of anemia or severe loss of body tissue.

How does it work?
It acts like a modified male hormone and promotes protein production and tissue building. It may also support bone formation and the production of red blood cells.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. It is generally administered by a healthcare professional; do not self-inject or use it for bodybuilding or performance enhancement. The dose and treatment duration depend on the medical condition and response to treatment.

Common side effects
Acne or oily skin, swelling due to fluid retention, changes in cholesterol, mood changes, menstrual irregularities, increased body or facial hair, and changes in sexual function. Long-term use may affect the liver, fertility, or natural hormone production.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about liver, kidney, heart, prostate, or breast problems, diabetes, high cholesterol, or use of blood thinners. It may cause masculinising effects in women and may affect growth in children. Regular medical monitoring is important.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid that may be used under specialist supervision for certain types of osteoporosis (bone thinning) and some anaemias, particularly when other treatments are unsuitable. Its exact use depends on the doctor’s assessment.

How does it work?
It acts like an androgen hormone and increases protein production. This can support bone and muscle tissue and may stimulate red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
It is given as a deep intramuscular injection by a healthcare professional. The dose and injection schedule depend on the condition being treated and must be decided by the prescriber. It should not be used for bodybuilding or without medical supervision.

Common side effects
Acne or oily skin, swelling due to fluid retention, changes in sexual desire, mood changes, injection-site pain, menstrual changes, increased facial or body hair, and voice deepening in women. It may also affect liver function, cholesterol levels, or blood cell counts.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Inform the doctor about prostate or breast cancer, liver, kidney or heart disease, high cholesterol, or sleep apnoea. Women should report voice deepening, increased hair growth, or menstrual changes promptly; some effects may be irreversible. Regular medical monitoring may be needed, including blood counts, liver function, cholesterol, and prostate checks where appropriate.

What is it used for?
Atorvastatin is used to lower high levels of cholesterol and other fats in the blood. It also helps reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme involved in making cholesterol in the liver. This lowers LDL (bad) cholesterol and helps reduce fatty build-up in the arteries.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water, with or without food. Continue taking it regularly and do not stop without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, indigestion, diarrhoea and muscle pain may occur. Contact a doctor if muscle pain or weakness is severe or persistent.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, thyroid problems or a history of muscle problems. Seek medical advice promptly for unexplained muscle pain, weakness, dark urine or yellowing of the skin or eyes. It is generally not used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, including antibiotics and antifungal medicines, before starting treatment.

What is it used for?
Atorvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, especially LDL (“bad”) cholesterol and triglycerides. It also helps reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It reduces cholesterol production in the liver and helps the liver remove more LDL cholesterol from the blood.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually once daily, with or without food. Take it at the same time each day and do not stop it without medical advice. Continue diet and lifestyle measures recommended by the prescriber.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, indigestion and muscle aches may occur. Contact a doctor promptly for unexplained or severe muscle pain, weakness or dark urine.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, thyroid problems or a history of muscle problems. Seek medical advice before using it with other medicines, as some medicines can increase the risk of muscle problems. It should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor. Liver tests may be needed during treatment.

What is it used for?
Atorvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, especially LDL (“bad”) cholesterol and triglycerides. It also helps reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme involved in cholesterol production in the liver. This lowers cholesterol levels in the blood.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. It may be taken with or without food, preferably at the same time each day. Do not stop or change the dose without medical advice.

Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, indigestion, and muscle aches may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney problems, thyroid problems, heavy alcohol use, or any unexplained muscle pain or weakness. What is it used for?
This medicine is used to help prevent heart attacks and strokes in people at increased cardiovascular risk, especially those with established heart disease. It helps lower cholesterol and reduce the formation of harmful blood clots.

How does it work?
Atorvastatin lowers harmful LDL cholesterol production in the liver. Aspirin reduces the ability of platelets to stick together, helping prevent blood clots.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach discomfort, nausea, easy bruising or bleeding, headache, and muscle aches may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, liver disease, kidney disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, or bleeding disorders. Seek medical advice for unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe muscle pain or weakness, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially blood thinners, other painkillers, and medicines that may affect the liver. This medicine is generally not used during pregnancy; ask a doctor before use while breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This combination is prescribed to reduce the risk of blood clots, heart attack and certain types of stroke in people with coronary artery disease or after certain heart-related events or procedures.

How does it work?
Atorvastatin lowers harmful LDL cholesterol and helps protect blood vessels. Aspirin and clopidogrel reduce platelet clumping, helping prevent blood clots.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Do not stop this medicine or skip doses without medical advice, as this may increase the risk of a blood clot. Follow the prescribed instructions regarding food and other medicines.

Common side effects
Easy bruising or bleeding, nosebleeds, indigestion, stomach discomfort, nausea, and muscle aches may occur. Mild changes in liver tests can also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of bleeding, stomach ulcers, liver disease, kidney disease, or muscle problems. Inform the doctor and dentist before surgery or dental procedures. Seek urgent medical care for uncontrolled bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe headache, or sudden weakness. Report severe muscle pain or weakness, especially with dark urine. Avoid pregnancy and breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor, and check before using painkillers or other medicines that may increase bleeding.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to help prevent harmful blood clots and reduce the risk of heart attack or stroke in people with coronary artery disease, including after certain heart-related events or procedures. The exact reason for prescribing it depends on the patient's condition.

How does it work?
Atorvastatin lowers LDL (“bad”) cholesterol and helps stabilise fatty deposits in blood vessels. Aspirin and clopidogrel reduce platelet clotting, helping prevent blood clots from forming.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor, at the same time each day. Do not stop it without medical advice, especially after a heart procedure. If a dose is missed, follow the prescribed instructions and do not take an extra dose unless advised.

Common side effects
Easy bruising or bleeding, nosebleeds, indigestion, stomach discomfort, nausea, headache, and muscle aches may occur.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe weakness, or unexplained severe muscle pain. Tell the doctor about ulcers, bleeding disorders, liver disease, kidney disease, or any planned surgery or dental procedure. Avoid starting painkillers such as ibuprofen or other medicines, including blood thinners, without medical advice. Avoid alcohol or limit it, as it may increase bleeding or liver-related risks. This medicine is generally not used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Bilastine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It is also used to relieve itching and hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce itching, sneezing, redness and other allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. It is generally taken with water on an empty stomach—1 hour before or 2 hours after food or fruit juice. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Headache, sleepiness, dizziness and tiredness may occur.

Precautions
Use only as advised if there is kidney disease or if taking other medicines. Avoid driving or operating machinery if sleepy or dizzy. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis (hay fever), such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and itchy or watery eyes.

How does it work?
Bilastine blocks histamine, a chemical that causes allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, substances involved in allergic inflammation and swelling of the airways.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the instructions on the label, and do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Do not stop or change treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, sleepiness or tiredness, stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Montelukast may rarely cause mood or behaviour changes, disturbed sleep, nightmares, irritability, anxiety, depression, or suicidal thoughts. Seek medical advice promptly if these occur. It is not intended to treat a sudden asthma or breathing attack. Drowsiness may occur; take care when driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Tell the doctor about other medicines and any liver or kidney problems.

How does it work?
Bilastine blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which can contribute to inflammation and congestion in the airways and nose.

Avoid driving or operating machinery if sleepy or dizzy. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver disease, or other medicines being used.

What is it used for?
Kaolin clay with aloe vera is used in topical skin-care products to absorb excess oil and help soothe the skin. The exact use depends on the product formulation.

How does it work?
Kaolin clay absorbs oil and impurities from the skin. Aloe vera may help soothe and moisturise irritated or dry-feeling skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use exactly as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not apply to broken or infected skin unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Skin dryness, tightness, redness, itching or irritation may occur. Allergic reactions are uncommon.

Precautions
Stop use if significant irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Keep away from the eyes and mouth. Seek medical advice if irritation persists or the skin condition worsens.

What is it used for?
This supplement provides calcium and active vitamin D (calcitriol) to support calcium absorption and maintain strong bones and teeth. It may also help provide omega-3 fatty acids, vitamin B12 and folic acid when supplementation is needed.

How does it work?
Calcium provides minerals needed for bones and teeth, while calcitriol helps the body absorb calcium. Vitamin B12 and folic acid support normal blood-cell and nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or as stated on the product label. Swallow the softgel whole with water, preferably with food. Do not take additional calcium or vitamin D supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Constipation, stomach upset, nausea, bloating or diarrhoea may occur. Excess calcium may cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness or confusion and requires medical attention.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high blood calcium, or a disorder that increases calcium levels. Calcitriol may require blood-calcium monitoring. Inform the doctor about anticoagulants and other medicines, especially thyroid medicines, iron supplements or certain antibiotics. Seek medical advice if symptoms of excess calcium occur.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to supplement calcium and active vitamin D (calcitriol) and support bone health, particularly when additional calcium and vitamin D are needed. It may be prescribed for calcium or vitamin D deficiency and related bone disorders.

How does it work?
Calcium provides the mineral needed for bones, while calcitriol helps the body absorb calcium. Vitamin K, magnesium, zinc, vitamin B12 and L-methylfolate support normal bone and body functions.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Swallow the capsule whole with water, preferably with food unless otherwise advised. Do not take additional calcium or vitamin D supplements without medical advice.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating or diarrhoea may occur. Excess calcium may cause increased thirst or urination, weakness, or confusion and requires medical attention.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium or vitamin D levels, or parathyroid disease. Calcitriol can raise blood calcium, so monitoring may be needed. Calcium can reduce the absorption of iron, thyroid medicines and some antibiotics; ask a pharmacist or doctor about suitable separation between medicines. Avoid exceeding the recommended dose.

What is it used for?
Luliconazole 1% cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch. It helps clear the infection and relieve related itching, redness and scaling.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which prevents their growth and helps eliminate the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the clean, dry affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor or on the product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not cover the area tightly unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild application-site irritation, redness, itching, burning or stinging may occur.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not use if allergic to luliconazole or any ingredient. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens, causes severe irritation, or does not improve as expected. Use on the scalp or nails only if specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Luliconazole cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, jock itch and athlete’s foot. It helps relieve the associated itching, redness and scaling.

How does it work?
It prevents fungi from making ergosterol, an essential part of their cell membrane. This stops the growth of the fungus and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Mild irritation, redness, itching, burning or stinging at the application site.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not apply to broken or severely irritated skin unless advised by a doctor. Do not cover the area tightly unless instructed. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens, causes severe irritation or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Luliconazole 1% cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch.

How does it work?
It stops the growth of fungi by blocking the production of ergosterol, a substance fungi need to maintain their cell membrane.

How to take/use it
For use on the skin only. Apply a thin layer to the clean, dry affected area and surrounding skin exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Mild application-site irritation, redness, itching, burning or stinging may occur.

What is it used for?
Omega-3 fatty acid capsules are used as a dietary supplement to provide omega-3 fats. They may also be used under medical supervision to help manage high triglyceride levels.

How does it work?
Omega-3 fatty acids are important fats used by the body. In prescribed amounts, they can help reduce the production of triglycerides in the liver.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by the doctor. Swallow the capsule whole, preferably with food. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Fishy taste or burping, nausea, indigestion, stomach discomfort and diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to fish or seafood, a bleeding disorder, or use of blood-thinning medicines. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or before surgery. This product does not replace prescribed treatment or a balanced diet.

What is it used for?
Traditionally used in babies to help relieve colic, gas and mild digestive discomfort. Evidence for gripe water is limited, and benefits may vary by formulation.

How does it work?
Its ingredients are intended to soothe the digestive tract and reduce gas-related discomfort. The exact action depends on the Ayurvedic formulation.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount or give it to a baby unless the label permits it. Consult a paediatrician before use, especially in newborns or young infants.

Side effects depend on the ingredients and may include digestive upset or an allergic reaction.

Precautions
Check the ingredients and age recommendation before use. Stop use and seek medical advice if rash, vomiting, diarrhoea or breathing difficulty occurs. Persistent crying, fever, poor feeding, a swollen abdomen or blood in the stool requires prompt medical attention.

What is it used for?
Metronidazole 400 mg is used to treat infections caused by certain bacteria and parasites, including some infections of the stomach and intestines, teeth and gums, vagina, skin and other parts of the body. It may also be used for amoebiasis, giardiasis and trichomoniasis when prescribed.

How does it work?
It enters susceptible bacteria and parasites and damages their genetic material, stopping them from growing and surviving.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for temporary relief of common cold symptoms such as cough, blocked or runny nose, sneezing and nasal congestion.

Dextromethorphan helps reduce coughing, phenylephrine relieves nasal blockage, and chlorpheniramine helps reduce allergy-like symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose.

Omega-3 fatty acids such as EPA and DHA are important fats used by the body. They help support normal fat metabolism and other body functions.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to amoxicillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Contact a doctor for severe or persistent diarrhoea, especially during or after treatment. Tell the doctor about liver or kidney problems, previous antibiotic-related jaundice, or other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain bacterial and protozoal infections that may cause diarrhoea or dysentery. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Norfloxacin stops the growth of susceptible bacteria. Tinidazole damages certain bacteria and parasites, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with a full glass of water, and complete the prescribed course. Do not self-medicate or stop early. Avoid taking it with milk or dairy products, and separate antacids or mineral supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc as advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 72 hours after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and a metallic taste in the mouth may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney disease, seizures, nerve problems, tendon disorders or myasthenia gravis. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, severe rash, breathing difficulty, or unusual confusion. Avoid driving if dizziness or blurred vision occurs. Keep hydrated unless fluid restriction has been advised.

What is it used for?
Sodium chloride infusion is given through a vein in hospitals or clinics to replace lost fluids and sodium (salt), such as during dehydration or certain conditions causing fluid or salt loss. Its exact use depends on the solution strength and the patient's medical needs.

How does it work?
It supplies water, sodium and chloride to the bloodstream, helping restore fluid and electrolyte balance.

How to take/use it
This infusion must be given into a vein by a healthcare professional. The amount and speed are decided by the doctor based on the patient's condition and monitoring results. It must not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Fluid retention, swelling, irritation or pain at the injection site, and changes in blood sodium levels may occur.

Precautions
Use cautiously in people with heart failure, kidney problems, high blood pressure or a tendency to retain fluid. Medical monitoring may be needed to check fluid balance and electrolyte levels. Tell the healthcare professional about existing heart or kidney disease before treatment.

What is it used for?
Oral rehydration solution (ORS) helps prevent and treat dehydration caused by diarrhoea, vomiting, excessive sweating or other fluid loss. It replaces lost water and essential salts.

How does it work?
ORS contains glucose and salts that help the intestine absorb water more effectively, restoring the body's fluid and electrolyte balance.

How to take/use it
Dissolve the entire sachet in the exact amount of clean water stated on the package. Stir well and drink in frequent small sips. Do not take the powder directly or prepare it with less or more water than recommended. Use the prepared solution only as directed on the label.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, bloating or mild stomach discomfort may occur, especially if taken too quickly.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical care for severe dehydration, persistent vomiting, blood in the stool, high fever, confusion, very little urination or inability to drink. Use only with medical advice in severe kidney disease, heart failure or other conditions requiring fluid or salt restriction. ORS does not replace medical treatment for the cause of diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Ayurvedic Piles Care Cream is used for the local relief of discomfort, irritation and itching associated with piles (haemorrhoids).

How does it work?
The exact action depends on the Ayurvedic ingredients, which are not specified here. Applied to the affected area, it is intended to provide local soothing relief.

How to take/use it
Use only on the affected area and follow the directions on the product label or advice of a pharmacist or doctor. Clean and gently dry the area before application, and wash hands before and after use. Do not use more often or for longer than directed.

Common side effects
Local irritation, redness, itching or an allergic skin reaction may occur. Stop use if symptoms worsen or a severe reaction develops.

Precautions
For external use only unless the product label specifically says otherwise. Avoid contact with the eyes and other sensitive areas. Do not apply to severely damaged or infected skin. Seek medical advice for persistent bleeding, severe pain, a lump, or symptoms that do not improve.

What is it used for?
Ayurvedic tablets intended to help manage piles (haemorrhoids), which may cause pain, itching, swelling or bleeding around the anus.

How does it work?
The exact action depends on the Ayurvedic ingredients, which are not provided. It is intended to relieve piles-related symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by an Ayurvedic doctor. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Check the ingredient list before use.

Common side effects
Specific side effects cannot be confirmed without the ingredient list. Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction or other troublesome symptoms occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice for heavy or persistent rectal bleeding, severe pain, dizziness, or recurring piles, as bleeding may have other causes. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, in children, or if taking other medicines or having a long-term medical condition. Do not use if allergic to any ingredient.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ear, throat, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Reconstitute the dry syrup exactly as directed using the supplied water, shake well before each use, and measure with an appropriate measuring device. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not use leftover medicine for another illness.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and headache may occur. Mild rash can also occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, cephalosporins or other penicillin-type antibiotics without medical advice. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea or antibiotic allergies. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a widespread rash. Keep out of children's reach and follow the label for storage after mixing.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ears, throat, sinuses, lungs, urinary tract and skin, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Disperse the tablet in water as directed on the product label or by the pharmacist. Do not skip doses or share this antibiotic with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion and headache. Mild skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to cefpodoxime, cephalosporins, penicillins or other antibiotics. Medical advice is important if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Contact a doctor for severe or persistent diarrhoea, or seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, sinuses, chest, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share it or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, indigestion and headache may occur. Mild skin rash can also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to cefpodoxime, cephalosporins or penicillin-type antibiotics. Inform the doctor if there is kidney disease, as the dose may need adjustment. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, or signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling, breathing difficulty or a widespread rash. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, lungs, urinary tract or skin. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall, which prevents the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. If supplied as a dry powder, reconstitute it exactly as directed on the label or by the pharmacist. Shake well before each use and measure with an oral syringe or measuring spoon. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and headache. Mild skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there is a history of serious allergy to cefpodoxime, cephalosporins or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney disease or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
This is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections when prescribed by a healthcare professional. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefpodoxime kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall. Potassium clavulanate helps cefpodoxime work against certain bacteria that can otherwise resist it.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve, and do not share it with others. If a dose is missed, follow the advice provided by the prescriber or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain or indigestion, and headache. Skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics, penicillins, or related antibiotics. Inform the prescriber about kidney problems, allergies, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or a severe skin rash. Use only for a prescribed bacterial infection.

What is it used for?
This is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
Cefpodoxime stops bacteria from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps protect cefpodoxime from enzymes made by some resistant bacteria.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Prepare and measure the suspension exactly as directed on the label, shake well before each use, and use a proper measuring device. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not use leftover antibiotics or share them.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or related antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, or a history of severe allergies. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Vitamin E 400 mg is a vitamin supplement used to prevent or treat vitamin E deficiency, usually when recommended by a healthcare professional. Vitamin E deficiency is uncommon in people with a balanced diet.

How does it work?
Vitamin E is a fat-soluble antioxidant that helps protect cells from damage caused by free radicals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. It is generally absorbed better when taken with food. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it long term without medical advice.

Common side effects
High doses may cause nausea, diarrhoea, stomach cramps, headache or tiredness.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional before use if there is a bleeding disorder, upcoming surgery, or use of blood-thinning medicines such as warfarin, aspirin or clopidogrel. High-dose vitamin E may increase the risk of bleeding. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking other vitamin supplements.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve dryness, burning, grittiness and irritation caused by dry eyes. It helps lubricate and moisturise the surface of the eye.

How does it work?
Sodium hyaluronate forms a moisture-retaining lubricating layer over the eye surface, helping reduce friction and discomfort. Stabilized oxychloro complex helps maintain the sterility of the eye drops.

How to take/use it
Use in the eyes exactly as directed on the label or by an eye-care professional. Wash hands before use and do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or other surfaces. If contact lenses are worn, follow the product instructions regarding removal and reinsertion.

Common side effects
Mild, temporary stinging, burning, irritation, redness or blurred vision may occur after application.

Precautions
For ophthalmic use only. Do not use if the solution is discoloured or the container is damaged. Stop use and seek medical advice if eye pain, marked redness, vision changes or persistent irritation occurs. Do not share the bottle.

What is it used for?
Cinnarizine is used to prevent and relieve vertigo (a spinning or dizzy sensation) and related nausea. It is also used to help prevent motion sickness.

How does it work?
It reduces the sensitivity of the balance centre in the inner ear and blocks certain signals that can cause dizziness and nausea.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food if it causes stomach upset. Do not drive or operate machinery until its effect on alertness is known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dry mouth, indigestion, nausea and weight gain may occur.

Precautions
It may cause drowsiness; avoid alcohol and take care when driving. Inform the doctor if there is Parkinson’s disease, as cinnarizine may worsen its symptoms. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if side effects are severe or persistent.

What is it used for?
Metronidazole is used to treat certain infections caused by anaerobic bacteria and parasites such as amoebiasis and giardiasis. It may also be prescribed for conditions such as bacterial vaginosis and some dental or abdominal infections, as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It enters susceptible bacteria and parasites and damages their genetic material, stopping them from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Follow the product label for measuring and taking the medicine; do not take extra doses for a missed dose. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, metallic taste and dizziness.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to metronidazole or similar medicines. Tell the doctor about pregnancy or breastfeeding, liver disease, nervous system disorders, or medicines such as warfarin, lithium, disulfiram or seizure medicines. Seek medical help for numbness, tingling, seizures, severe rash or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Cilnidipine 10 mg is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It helps lower blood pressure and reduces the risk of complications related to uncontrolled hypertension.

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens the blood vessels by reducing calcium entry into the muscle cells of the vessel walls. This allows blood to flow more easily and lowers blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, at the same time each day. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; do not take two doses together.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, palpitations and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur.

Precautions
Rise slowly if dizziness occurs, especially when starting treatment. Inform the doctor about low blood pressure, liver or kidney problems, or swelling of the legs. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if swelling is severe, fainting occurs or blood pressure remains uncontrolled.

What is it used for?
Cilnidipine 20 mg is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It helps lower blood pressure and reduces the risk of complications related to uncontrolled hypertension.

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens the blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily and reducing the pressure inside the blood vessels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop taking it suddenly without medical advice. Do not change the dose or treatment duration on your own.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, palpitations, and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur.

Precautions
Use with caution if there is low blood pressure, liver disease, or heart-related illness. Rise slowly if dizziness occurs. Avoid driving or operating machinery if feeling dizzy. Inform the doctor if pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding, and tell them about all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to manage high cholesterol and high triglyceride levels, especially mixed dyslipidaemia. It may be prescribed when both LDL cholesterol and triglycerides need to be reduced.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin reduces the liver’s production of cholesterol and lowers LDL (bad) cholesterol. Fenofibrate helps reduce triglycerides and may increase HDL (good) cholesterol.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular cholesterol, liver and kidney tests may be recommended.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, indigestion or stomach pain, diarrhoea, and muscle aches may occur. Mild increases in liver enzymes can also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, gallbladder problems, thyroid problems, heavy alcohol use, or any history of muscle problems with cholesterol medicines. The combination can rarely cause serious muscle damage; seek medical help for severe or unexplained muscle pain, weakness, fever, or dark urine. Seek medical advice for yellowing of the skin or eyes or severe stomach pain. It is generally avoided during pregnancy and breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, especially blood thinners or other cholesterol-lowering medicines.

What is it used for?
Used for bacterial eye infections accompanied by inflammation, such as bacterial conjunctivitis, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Ciprofloxacin kills susceptible bacteria causing the infection. Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces redness, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use in the affected eye(s) exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before use and avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or other surfaces. Do not wear contact lenses during treatment unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Temporary burning, stinging, irritation, blurred vision or discomfort after application. These effects are usually short-lived.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice, as steroid-containing eye medicines may worsen some viral or fungal infections and may increase eye pressure or delay healing if used for too long. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen, vision changes, severe pain or swelling develops, or there is no improvement. Do not use if the solution is contaminated or the seal is damaged.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat bacterial infections of the eye, such as bacterial conjunctivitis, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic that stops the growth of bacteria causing the infection. Benzalkonium helps preserve the solution.

How to take/use it
Use in the eye only if the product is labelled for ophthalmic use, and follow the dose and duration prescribed. Wash hands before use, do not touch the dropper tip, and do not share the bottle. Remove contact lenses before use and ask a doctor when they can be worn again.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, burning, irritation, redness, itching or blurred vision may occur after application.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ciprofloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics. Stop use and seek medical help for swelling, rash, breathing difficulty, severe eye pain or worsening vision. Consult a doctor if symptoms do not improve or worsen. Benzalkonium may irritate the eyes and may affect soft contact lenses.

What is it used for?
Ciprofloxacin infusion is an antibiotic used in hospitals to treat serious bacterial infections when treatment through a vein is needed. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking enzymes they need to copy and repair their DNA.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment length depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, rash, and pain or irritation at the infusion site.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to ciprofloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics, kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, tendon disorders, seizures, nerve problems, or myasthenia gravis. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve changes, palpitations, or a serious allergic reaction. Use in children, pregnancy, or breastfeeding only when specifically prescribed. It should be administered under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% is an antifungal medicine used on the skin or scalp to treat fungal infections, including dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis when prescribed or labelled for these conditions.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making ergosterol, an essential part of their cell membrane. This prevents the fungi from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only on the affected skin or scalp and follow the product label or prescriber's instructions. Clean and dry the area before application if advised. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site.

Precautions
For external use unless specifically directed otherwise. Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole or any ingredient. Avoid contact with the eyes and rinse well with water if this occurs. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty develops, or if the condition worsens or does not improve as expected.

What is it used for?
Dapagliflozin is mainly used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is also prescribed for some adults with heart failure or chronic kidney disease to reduce the risk of worsening disease and hospitalisation.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove excess glucose and some sodium from the body through urine. This lowers blood sugar and may also reduce the workload on the heart and kidneys.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow it with water. It may usually be taken with or without food. Drink enough fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not stop it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, thirst, dehydration, dizziness, urinary tract infection, and genital fungal infection. Low blood sugar may occur, especially when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, low blood pressure, dehydration, or frequent urinary or genital infections. Seek urgent medical help for nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, breathing difficulty, or confusion, as these may indicate diabetic ketoacidosis even if blood sugar is not very high. It may need to be temporarily stopped during severe illness, prolonged fasting, or before surgery, only on medical advice. Discuss its use during pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes.

How does it work?
Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin better. Dapagliflozin helps the kidneys remove excess glucose from the body through urine.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole; do not crush, chew or split it. Drink enough fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, increased urination, urinary tract infection, and genital fungal infection. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, heavy alcohol use, or planned surgery or prolonged fasting. Seek urgent medical help for severe nausea or vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, difficulty breathing, confusion, or signs of severe dehydration. Report burning urination, fever, or genital itching or swelling. This medicine may need to be stopped temporarily during serious illness or some medical procedures, only as advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Used along with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when treatment with other diabetes medicines is not enough. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes.

How does it work?
Dapagliflozin helps the kidneys remove excess glucose through urine. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver, while sitagliptin helps the body release insulin and reduce glucose production after meals.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, preferably with food if advised, and at the same time each day. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Drink adequate fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised.

Common side effects
Increased urination, urinary or genital infections, nausea, diarrhoea, stomach upset, headache and dizziness. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or sulfonylurea medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, recurrent urinary or genital infections, heart problems, or heavy alcohol use. Seek urgent medical help for severe nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness or difficulty breathing, as these may indicate ketoacidosis or lactic acidosis. Kidney function should be checked regularly. Inform the doctor before surgery, prolonged fasting, or receiving contrast dye, and before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when one or more diabetes medicines are not enough. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Dapagliflozin helps the kidneys remove excess sugar through urine. Metformin reduces sugar production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin, while sitagliptin helps the body release insulin and reduce sugar production after meals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food, and swallow it as directed. Do not crush or split the tablet unless advised. Maintain adequate fluid intake and continue the recommended diet and exercise plan. Do not stop it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, increased urination, urinary tract infection and genital fungal infection. Low blood sugar may occur, especially when used with insulin or sulfonylureas.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, recurrent urinary or genital infections, pancreatitis, heart failure, or heavy alcohol use. Seek urgent medical help for severe vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, breathing difficulty, confusion, or symptoms of severe dehydration. Discuss its use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Kidney function and blood sugar should be monitored as advised. Temporarily stopping it may be necessary during serious illness, prolonged fasting, or before some procedures—follow medical advice.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat various bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as common cold or flu. Lactobacillus is included as a probiotic to help support the normal balance of bacteria in the gut.

How does it work?
Doxycycline stops susceptible bacteria from making proteins they need to grow and multiply. Lactobacillus is a beneficial bacterium that helps support normal intestinal flora.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the capsule with a full glass of water while sitting or standing, and do not lie down immediately afterwards. Avoid taking it close to milk or dairy products, antacids, iron, calcium or magnesium supplements unless advised otherwise. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort and increased sensitivity to sunlight may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to doxycycline or other tetracycline antibiotics. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice. It is generally avoided in children under 8 years unless specifically prescribed. Use sun protection and limit prolonged exposure to sunlight. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, difficulty swallowing, severe headache or vision changes.

What is it used for?
Dydrogesterone is a progesterone-like medicine used to treat conditions caused by low progesterone, such as irregular or painful periods, endometriosis, and some menstrual or reproductive problems. It may also be prescribed during pregnancy or fertility treatment when progesterone support is needed.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone progesterone. It helps support the lining of the uterus and regulate the menstrual cycle.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably at the same time each day. Do not stop it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache or migraine, nausea, abdominal discomfort, breast tenderness, spotting or changes in menstrual bleeding, and mood changes.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about unexplained vaginal bleeding, liver disease, a history of depression, migraine, or hormone-sensitive conditions. Seek medical advice for heavy or persistent bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe headache. Tell the doctor if pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding. This medicine is not a contraceptive.

What is it used for?
Used to moisturise and soften dry, rough, cracked skin on the heels and help improve heel cracks.

How does it work?
It generally helps by moisturising the skin and improving its softness, which may support healing of dryness-related cracks. The exact action depends on the herbal ingredients.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry heels as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching or an allergic reaction may occur in sensitive people.

Precautions
Stop use if significant irritation or an allergic reaction develops. Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Seek medical advice if the cracks are deep, painful, bleeding, infected, or do not improve. People with diabetes or poor circulation should seek medical advice for persistent or severe heel cracks.

What is it used for?
Itraconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections, including infections of the skin, nails, mouth, vagina and, in some cases, internal organs. The exact use depends on the type and severity of the infection.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making ergosterol, a substance needed to maintain their cell membranes. This prevents the fungi from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course. If this is an itraconazole capsule, take it immediately after a full meal and swallow it whole. Do not change the dose or stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea or constipation, headache, dizziness, rash and changes in liver function tests.

Precautions
Itraconazole has many important medicine interactions, so inform the doctor about all prescription medicines, over-the-counter medicines and supplements being taken. Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, heart failure or a history of heart problems. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe rash, breathing difficulty or swelling of the legs. Use during pregnancy only when specifically prescribed. Antacids and medicines that reduce stomach acid may affect absorption; ask a doctor or pharmacist how to take them with itraconazole.

What is it used for?
Itraconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, nails, mouth, vagina and other parts of the body. The exact use depends on the infection and the doctor's prescription.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making ergosterol, a substance they need to build and maintain their cell membranes. This prevents the fungi from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take or use it exactly as prescribed. Do not change the dose or stop treatment early. Instructions may differ depending on the formulation, so follow the product label and medical advice. Tell the doctor about all other medicines being taken because itraconazole has important drug interactions.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, heart failure, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or an allergy to antifungal medicines. Itraconazole can interact with many medicines. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, breathing difficulty, swelling of the legs, or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Linezolid is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, including some types of pneumonia, skin and soft-tissue infections, and infections caused by resistant bacteria. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and survive.

How to take/use it
Take the tablet exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not share it with others or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, and changes in taste may occur. Longer treatment can affect blood counts.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about antidepressants or other medicines that affect serotonin, as serious interactions may occur. Inform the doctor about high blood pressure, blood disorders, or liver problems. During prolonged treatment, blood tests may be needed. Seek medical advice for unusual bruising, persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, vision changes, or severe headache. Avoid self-medication and use only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Losartan 50 mg is mainly used to treat high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed to help protect the kidneys in some people with diabetes and to reduce the risk of stroke in certain people with high blood pressure.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of a hormone that causes blood vessels to narrow. This helps the blood vessels relax, lowering blood pressure and reducing strain on the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Continue it regularly even if feeling well, and do not stop it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, low blood pressure, and stomach upset may occur. Blood potassium levels or kidney function may change.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy, especially after the first three months; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, or use of potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes, or medicines that can affect the kidneys. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Losartan 50 mg with hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of complications such as stroke and heart disease.

How does it work?
Losartan relaxes blood vessels by blocking the action of a hormone that raises blood pressure. Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic (‘water tablet’) that helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water from the body.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food and should be swallowed with water. Do not stop or change the medicine without medical advice. Regular blood pressure, kidney function and electrolyte checks may be recommended.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, increased urination and a drop in blood pressure may occur. Changes in potassium or sodium levels can also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, gout, diabetes, or electrolyte problems. Do not use during pregnancy; seek medical advice promptly if pregnancy occurs. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Some medicines, including painkillers such as ibuprofen, lithium and other blood-pressure medicines, may interact with it. Rise slowly if dizzy and seek medical help for fainting, severe weakness, swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Trypsin-chymotrypsin is used to help reduce swelling, inflammation and discomfort after injuries, surgery or other soft-tissue inflammation. It may also be prescribed for some muscle and joint conditions.

How does it work?
These enzymes help break down proteins involved in inflammation and swelling, which may support the body's recovery from tissue injury.

How to take/use it
Take only in the dose and for the duration prescribed by the doctor. If supplied as a tablet, swallow it whole with water; do not chew or crush it unless advised. Do not self-medicate.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, nausea, diarrhoea, skin rash or other allergic reactions may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about bleeding disorders, liver or kidney problems, allergies, or use of blood-thinning medicines. Use only under medical advice before surgery, during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Stop the medicine and seek urgent help for signs of a serious allergic reaction or unusual bleeding.

What is it used for?
Acebrophylline 100 mg is used to help manage breathing problems such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It helps reduce airway narrowing and loosen thick mucus, making breathing easier. It is not usually used for the immediate relief of a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways and helps reduce the thickness of mucus. This allows air to move more easily through the lungs.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Continue to keep any prescribed rescue inhaler available for sudden breathing difficulty.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, palpitations and difficulty sleeping may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, an irregular heartbeat, high blood pressure, liver or kidney problems, or a history of stomach ulcers. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, chest pain or worsening breathing difficulty. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding and all other medicines being taken. Do not take it if allergic to acebrophylline or similar medicines.

What is it used for?
Acebrophylline 200 mg Sustained Release is used to help relieve breathing difficulty, wheezing and cough caused by asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It helps open the airways and loosen thick mucus.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them widen, and helps reduce the thickness of mucus so it can be cleared more easily.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is not meant for immediate relief during a sudden breathing attack—use the prescribed rescue inhaler if one has been provided.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, tremor or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, high blood pressure, irregular heartbeat, seizures, thyroid problems, or liver or kidney disease. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially other theophylline-containing medicines. Avoid taking more than prescribed and limit excessive caffeine, as this may increase side effects. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, persistent vomiting, seizures or worsening breathing difficulty. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used as prescribed to help manage asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with breathing difficulty, wheezing and thick mucus. It helps loosen phlegm and clear mucus from the airways. It is not a rescue medicine for a sudden breathing attack.

How does it work?
Acebrophylline helps relax and widen the airways, while acetylcysteine thins thick mucus so it can be coughed out more easily.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Use the appropriate rescue inhaler or seek urgent medical care for sudden or severe breathing difficulty.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, tremor or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, high blood pressure, seizures, stomach ulcers, or liver or kidney problems before use. Seek medical advice if palpitations, severe vomiting, rash or worsening breathing occurs. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice. Keep this medicine away from children.

What is it used for?
Minoxidil Topical Solution 5% is used to help treat pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) by promoting hair growth on the scalp.

How does it work?
It helps increase blood flow around hair follicles and may prolong the active hair-growth phase, supporting the growth of thicker hair.

How to take/use it
Apply only to the dry scalp and use exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands after application and avoid contact with the eyes, face and other areas of the body. Do not apply to broken, irritated or sunburned skin.

Common side effects
Scalp itching, dryness, redness or irritation; temporary increased hair shedding; unwanted facial or body hair. Headache or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Do not use for sudden, patchy or unexplained hair loss without medical advice. Stop using it and seek medical advice if chest pain, rapid or irregular heartbeat, fainting, severe dizziness or swelling occurs. Consult a healthcare professional during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Keep away from children and open flames, as the solution may be flammable.

What is it used for?
Used to help treat androgenetic alopecia (pattern hair loss), helping reduce hair loss and support hair regrowth on the scalp.

How does it work?
Minoxidil helps stimulate hair follicles and support the hair-growth phase. Finasteride lowers dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone involved in pattern hair loss.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by the prescriber. If supplied for scalp application, apply to the clean, dry scalp as directed and wash hands after use. Do not use more than recommended or apply to irritated or broken skin.

Common side effects
Scalp irritation, itching, dryness, redness or flaking, and temporary increased hair shedding may occur. Finasteride may rarely cause decreased sexual desire, erection problems or reduced semen volume.

Precautions
For external use only unless otherwise directed. Avoid contact with the eyes and wash thoroughly if contact occurs. Stop use and seek medical advice for severe scalp irritation, dizziness, fainting, chest pain, rapid heartbeat or swelling. Finasteride can harm a developing male baby; women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should not use this product or handle leaking product. Discuss use with a doctor if there is heart disease, low blood pressure or unexplained hair loss.

What is it used for?
Used to treat bacterial infections of the eye, such as bacterial conjunctivitis. It does not treat viral or fungal eye infections.

How does it work?
Moxifloxacin is an antibiotic that stops susceptible bacteria from growing and multiplying. Benzalkonium solution acts as a preservative.

How to take/use it
Use in the eye only and follow the dose and duration prescribed by the doctor. Wash hands before use, do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or other surfaces, and close the container after use. Remove contact lenses before application and ask a doctor when they can be worn again.

Common side effects
Temporary burning or stinging, eye irritation, redness, itching, dryness, blurred vision, or a change in taste may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to moxifloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics. Stop using it and seek medical help if there is swelling, rash, severe itching, breathing difficulty, severe eye pain, or worsening vision. Seek medical advice if symptoms do not improve or become worse.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve migraine headaches and help control associated nausea or vomiting.

How does it work?
Naproxen reduces pain and inflammation involved in migraine. Domperidone helps reduce nausea and vomiting and supports movement of the stomach.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow it with water and do not take more than recommended. Taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach irritation from naproxen.

Indigestion, stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, dry mouth, dizziness or drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is an allergy to naproxen, other painkillers or domperidone. Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney, liver or heart problems, or asthma triggered by painkillers. Domperidone may affect heart rhythm, so inform the doctor about heart disease or medicines that affect heart rhythm. Avoid combining it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest palpitations or fainting. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, or while breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This medicine is usually used to relieve migraine headache and associated nausea or vomiting.

Naproxen reduces pain and inflammation by blocking substances involved in pain. Domperidone helps control nausea and vomiting and may improve stomach movement.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed or directed on the label. Swallow with water; taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more than recommended or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Stomach upset, indigestion, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, dry mouth, dizziness or headache.

Tell the doctor about kidney, liver or heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or heart rhythm problems. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest palpitations or fainting. Check with a doctor or pharmacist before use with blood thinners, steroids, other NSAIDs or medicines that can affect heart rhythm.

Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and fever, such as body aches, muscle or joint pain, and other painful conditions. Use only when recommended by a healthcare professional.

Nimesulide reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, dizziness or skin rash. Stop use and seek medical help if yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe rash or unusual bleeding occurs.

Do not combine with other paracetamol-containing products or painkillers without medical advice.

Nimesulide reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and fever, such as body aches, muscle or joint pain, and other painful conditions when prescribed by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Norethisterone is a progesterone-like medicine used to treat heavy, painful or irregular menstrual bleeding. It may also be prescribed for endometriosis or to delay a period, depending on medical advice.

It acts like the natural hormone progesterone and helps control the lining of the womb, reducing or regulating bleeding.

What is it used for?
Oxymetazoline nasal medicine provides short-term relief from a blocked or stuffy nose caused by colds, allergies or sinus congestion.

How does it work?
It narrows swollen blood vessels in the lining of the nose, helping reduce swelling and improve airflow.

Use in the nose exactly as directed on the package or by a healthcare professional. Do not use it for longer than 3 days unless advised, as prolonged use can cause worsening or rebound nasal congestion.

What is it used for?
Xylometazoline 0.05% nasal spray provides short-term relief from a blocked or stuffy nose caused by common colds, sinus congestion or nasal allergies.

It narrows swollen blood vessels in the lining of the nose, helping reduce swelling and improve airflow.

What is it used for?

It adds moisture to the nasal passages and helps wash away mucus, dust and other irritants.
