What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of a blocked nose and nasal discomfort associated with the common cold.

Its volatile aromatic ingredients release vapours that provide a cooling sensation and may temporarily make nasal breathing feel easier.

What is it used for?
Xylometazoline nasal drops or spray provide short-term relief from a blocked or stuffy nose due to colds, sinus congestion or allergic rhinitis.

It narrows swollen blood vessels inside the nose, reducing swelling and helping air pass more easily.

It stops bacteria from making the enzymes needed for their growth and multiplication, helping to clear the infection.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse, usually in a hospital or clinic. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type of infection and kidney function. Do not self-administer or stop treatment early unless advised by the doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, difficulty sleeping, and pain or irritation at the infusion site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, heart rhythm problems, tendon disorders, seizures, diabetes, or myasthenia gravis, and about all medicines being used. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, palpitations, fainting, or signs of a serious allergic reaction. Avoid strenuous exercise if tendon pain develops.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux symptoms. The domperidone component may also help with nausea, bloating and slow stomach emptying associated with these symptoms.

How does it work?
Rabeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps food move through the stomach and may reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. It is generally taken before food. Swallow the sustained-release capsule or tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain, nausea, dry mouth and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney problems, heart disease, an irregular heartbeat, or a history of low potassium or magnesium. Domperidone can rarely affect heart rhythm, so inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or certain antibiotics and antifungals. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, fast or irregular heartbeat, vomiting blood or black stools.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve symptoms of acid reflux, including heartburn and acid regurgitation.

How does it work?
Sodium alginate forms a protective barrier that helps prevent stomach contents from flowing back into the food pipe. Sodium bicarbonate and calcium carbonate help neutralise stomach acid.

How to take/use it
Use as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. The exact dose and frequency depend on the formulation. Do not exceed the recommended dose.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include nausea, constipation, diarrhoea or stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use if you have kidney disease, are on a sodium-restricted diet or have persistent symptoms. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Amlodipine 5 mg + atenolol 50 mg is mainly used to treat high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed to help prevent chest pain due to angina.

How does it work?
Amlodipine relaxes and widens blood vessels, while atenolol slows the heart rate and reduces the heart’s workload. Together, they help lower blood pressure and reduce strain on the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice, especially if it is being used for heart-related problems.

Common side effects
Dizziness, tiredness, headache, flushing, ankle swelling, nausea, low blood pressure, or a slow heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about asthma or other breathing problems, a slow heartbeat, heart block, heart failure, diabetes, kidney disease, liver disease, or pregnancy. Atenolol may hide some warning signs of low blood sugar. Avoid driving if dizzy, and seek medical help for fainting, severe breathing difficulty, or an unusually slow heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Amlodipine is used to treat high blood pressure. It is also used to help prevent chest pain caused by angina.

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens blood vessels, helping blood flow more easily. This lowers blood pressure and reduces the workload on the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. It can be taken with or without food. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Ankle or foot swelling, headache, dizziness, flushing, tiredness, palpitations, nausea and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is very low blood pressure, liver disease or heart problems. Rise slowly if dizziness occurs. Seek urgent medical help for severe dizziness, fainting, worsening chest pain or signs of an allergic reaction. Discuss use during pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor.

What is it used for?
Rifaximin 200 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections of the intestine, especially some cases of travellers’ diarrhoea caused by non-invasive bacteria. It should be used only when prescribed, as it is not suitable for every type of diarrhoea.

How does it work?
It acts mainly inside the intestine by stopping susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins needed for their growth.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. It may be taken with or without food. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise. Do not self-medicate for diarrhoea.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain or discomfort, bloating, gas, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Do not use it if there is an allergy to rifaximin or other rifamycin antibiotics. Seek medical advice if diarrhoea is accompanied by fever or blood, becomes severe, or does not improve. Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and about all other medicines being taken. Stop the medicine and seek urgent help for signs of a serious allergic reaction or severe, persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Rifaximin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections in the intestine, including some cases of infectious or traveller’s diarrhoea. It may also be prescribed for other conditions, such as reducing episodes of hepatic encephalopathy, depending on the doctor’s assessment.

How does it work?
It acts mainly inside the intestine and stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents them from growing. Very little of the medicine is absorbed into the bloodstream.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not use it for diarrhoea unless a healthcare professional has advised it.

Common side effects
Nausea, abdominal pain or discomfort, bloating, constipation, headache and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to rifaximin or other rifamycin antibiotics. Seek medical advice for diarrhoea with blood, high fever, severe abdominal pain, dehydration or symptoms that do not improve. Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop treatment and seek urgent help if severe rash, swelling or breathing difficulty occurs.

What is it used for?
Rifaximin 550 mg is used to reduce the risk of repeated episodes of hepatic encephalopathy in adults with liver disease. It may also be prescribed for irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhoea (IBS-D), under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It is a gut-acting antibiotic that reduces the growth of certain bacteria in the intestines. This can help reduce the production of substances linked with hepatic encephalopathy and improve diarrhoea-related symptoms in some patients.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water; it may generally be taken with or without food. Do not self-treat diarrhoea with this medicine or change the prescribed treatment duration.

Common side effects
Nausea, abdominal pain or bloating, headache, dizziness, constipation, and tiredness may occur. Seek medical advice if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergy to rifaximin or other rifamycin antibiotics, liver disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Contact a doctor promptly for severe or persistent diarrhoea, fever, blood or mucus in the stool, or worsening symptoms, as antibiotic-associated diarrhoea can occur. Use only under medical supervision, especially in severe liver impairment.

What is it used for?
Rosuvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, particularly LDL (bad) cholesterol, and to reduce cardiovascular risk in eligible patients.

How does it work?
It reduces cholesterol production in the liver, which lowers LDL cholesterol in the blood.

How to take/use it
Take as prescribed by a doctor, with or without food. Do not stop taking it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, constipation and muscle pain may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about liver or kidney problems, thyroid disorders and other medicines. Seek medical advice promptly for unexplained muscle pain or weakness. Rosuvastatin should generally be avoided during pregnancy.

What is it used for?
Rosuvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, particularly LDL (bad) cholesterol, and to reduce cardiovascular risk in eligible patients.

How does it work?
It reduces cholesterol production in the liver, which lowers LDL cholesterol in the blood.

How to take/use it
Take as prescribed by a doctor, with or without food. Do not stop taking it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, constipation and muscle pain may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about liver or kidney problems, thyroid disorders and other medicines. Seek medical advice promptly for unexplained muscle pain or weakness. Rosuvastatin should generally be avoided during pregnancy.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to manage abnormal blood cholesterol and triglyceride levels when a doctor considers both medicines necessary.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin reduces cholesterol production in the liver. Fenofibrate helps lower triglycerides and can increase HDL (good) cholesterol.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by a doctor. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include muscle pain, headache, nausea and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems and all other medicines being taken. Seek medical help promptly for unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness, especially with fever or dark urine.

What is it used for?
This combination is prescribed for selected patients to lower cholesterol and help prevent blood clots that can cause heart attack or stroke.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin lowers LDL cholesterol. Clopidogrel and aspirin reduce platelet clumping, helping prevent blood clots.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Do not stop clopidogrel or aspirin without medical advice.

Common side effects
Stomach discomfort, nausea, easy bruising and bleeding may occur. Muscle pain may also occur.

Precautions
This medicine increases bleeding risk. Inform the doctor about ulcers, bleeding disorders and other medicines, especially blood thinners and painkillers. Seek urgent medical help for severe bleeding, black stools or vomiting blood.

What is it used for?
This combination is prescribed for selected patients to lower cholesterol and help prevent blood clots that can cause heart attack or stroke.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin lowers LDL cholesterol. Clopidogrel and aspirin reduce platelet clumping, helping prevent blood clots.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Do not stop clopidogrel or aspirin without medical advice.

Common side effects
Stomach discomfort, nausea, easy bruising and bleeding may occur. Muscle pain may also occur.

Precautions
This medicine increases bleeding risk. Inform the doctor about ulcers, bleeding disorders and other medicines, especially blood thinners and painkillers. Seek urgent medical help for severe bleeding, black stools or vomiting blood.

What is it used for?
Sacubitril 49 mg + valsartan 51 mg is used to treat chronic heart failure. It helps reduce the strain on the heart and may lower the risk of hospitalisation due to worsening heart failure.

How does it work?
Sacubitril increases substances that help relax blood vessels and reduce salt and fluid buildup. Valsartan blocks a hormone effect that can narrow blood vessels and put extra strain on the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber’s instructions.

Common side effects
Low blood pressure, dizziness, increased potassium levels, cough, and changes in kidney function may occur.

Precautions
Medical monitoring of blood pressure, kidney function, and potassium levels may be needed. Do not use during pregnancy. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, high potassium, low blood pressure, or any previous swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat caused by medicines. Do not take with an ACE inhibitor; a suitable gap is required when switching from an ACE inhibitor. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Sacubitril 24 mg + valsartan 26 mg is used for the long-term treatment of certain types of heart failure, especially when the heart has reduced pumping function. It helps reduce heart failure symptoms and the risk of hospitalisation.

How does it work?
Sacubitril helps widen blood vessels and reduce strain on the heart. Valsartan blocks a hormone that tightens blood vessels and raises blood pressure, helping the heart pump more efficiently.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor, at the recommended times. Do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, low blood pressure, cough, increased potassium levels, and changes in kidney function.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, liver disease, low blood pressure, high potassium, or a previous allergic swelling reaction (angioedema). Do not take with an ACE inhibitor; a suitable gap is required when switching from one to the other. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Silodosin 8 mg is used to relieve urinary symptoms caused by an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia, or BPH), such as difficulty starting urination, weak urine flow, frequent urination and the need to urinate at night.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the prostate and bladder outlet, helping urine flow more easily.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with a meal. Swallow the capsule whole with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Reduced or absent semen during ejaculation, dizziness, low blood pressure on standing, stuffy nose, diarrhoea and headache.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is kidney or liver disease. Rise slowly from sitting or lying down, as dizziness or fainting may occur. Tell the doctor before cataract surgery. Inform the doctor about medicines for high blood pressure, erectile dysfunction or other prostate medicines. Avoid driving until the effects are known.

What is it used for?
Used in adult men to treat symptoms of an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia, or BPH), such as difficulty starting urination, weak urine flow, frequent urination and incomplete bladder emptying. It may also help reduce the risk of worsening urinary symptoms and urinary retention.

How does it work?
Silodosin relaxes the muscles around the prostate and bladder outlet to improve urine flow. Dutasteride reduces the hormone that contributes to prostate enlargement, which can gradually shrink the prostate.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions on the pack. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Swallow the medicine as directed; do not crush or open it unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Dizziness, especially on standing; reduced or absent semen during ejaculation; decreased sex drive; erectile difficulties; headache; and breast tenderness or enlargement. Some people may experience low blood pressure or fainting.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Rise slowly from sitting or lying down, particularly when starting treatment. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, low blood pressure, or planned cataract surgery. Dutasteride can affect PSA blood-test results, so inform the doctor that it is being taken. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should not handle leaking or broken capsules. Do not donate blood during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose unless advised otherwise.

What is it used for?
Sitagliptin is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
It helps the body increase insulin release after meals and reduce the release of glucagon, a hormone that raises blood sugar. This helps lower blood glucose levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment without medical advice. The dose may need adjustment in people with kidney problems.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, and symptoms of a cold or upper respiratory infection may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when it is taken with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, previous pancreatitis, or allergies to this medicine. Seek medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, especially if it spreads to the back, or for signs of a serious allergic reaction. Report severe or persistent joint pain or blistering skin. Continue monitoring blood sugar as advised.

What is it used for?
Sitagliptin is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It may be used alone or with other diabetes medicines, as prescribed.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called DPP-4, helping the body increase insulin release when blood sugar is high and reduce the release of hormones that raise blood sugar.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Take it at the same time each day. If a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; do not take two doses together. The dose may need adjustment in people with kidney problems.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort and cold-like symptoms may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when it is taken with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, previous pancreatitis, or allergies to diabetes medicines. Seek medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, blistering skin, or severe joint pain. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

What is it used for?
Used along with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Sitagliptin helps the body release more insulin after meals and reduces the release of sugar by the liver. Dapagliflozin helps the kidneys remove excess sugar from the body through urine.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the prescribed schedule and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Maintain adequate fluid intake unless a doctor has advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Increased urination, genital fungal infections, urinary tract infections, nausea, headache, dizziness and dehydration. Low blood sugar may occur, especially when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about kidney disease, repeated urinary or genital infections, dehydration, low blood pressure, pancreatitis, or use of insulin or sulfonylureas. Seek urgent medical help for severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, difficulty breathing, unusual weakness, or confusion, as these may indicate ketoacidosis or another serious problem. Discuss its use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, prolonged fasting, serious illness or before surgery with a doctor.

What is it used for?
Sitagliptin 50 mg + metformin 1000 mg is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Sitagliptin helps the body release more insulin after meals and reduces the amount of glucose made by the liver. Metformin also reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet as directed and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the prescriber or package leaflet.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, indigestion, reduced appetite, headache and symptoms of an upper respiratory infection may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or sulfonylurea medicines.

Precautions
Kidney function should be checked before and during treatment; this medicine may not be suitable in severe kidney disease. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent vomiting, diarrhoea, dehydration, unusual weakness, breathing difficulty or severe abdominal pain. Tell the doctor about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, pancreatitis, or planned surgery or contrast-dye investigations. Long-term metformin use may reduce vitamin B12 levels. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Sitagliptin 50 mg + Metformin 500 mg is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Sitagliptin helps the body release insulin when blood sugar is high and reduces the release of glucagon, a hormone that raises blood sugar. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin better.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with food to reduce stomach upset. Do not change the dose, stop treatment, or crush or split the tablet unless advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Follow the prescribed diet, exercise and blood sugar monitoring plan.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, abdominal pain, vomiting, headache and reduced appetite. Low blood sugar may occur, especially when used with insulin or sulfonylurea medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, heavy alcohol use, heart failure, or a history of pancreatitis. Kidney function should be checked before and during treatment. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, breathing difficulty, extreme weakness, or signs of a serious allergic reaction. Long-term metformin use may reduce vitamin B12 levels. Inform the doctor before surgery or certain contrast-dye scans.

What is it used for?
Tamsulosin is used to relieve urinary symptoms caused by an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia), such as difficulty starting urination, weak urine flow, urgency and frequent urination.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles in the prostate and the bladder outlet, helping urine flow more easily. It does not shrink the prostate.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually after the same meal each day. Swallow the prolonged-release capsule/tablet whole with water; do not crush, chew or open it.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, blocked or runny nose, and ejaculation problems may occur.

Precautions
It may cause dizziness or a fall in blood pressure, especially when standing up; rise slowly. Avoid driving if affected. Tell the doctor about dizziness or fainting, severe liver or kidney problems, or if cataract or glaucoma surgery is planned. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially medicines for erectile dysfunction or blood pressure.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat symptoms of an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia, or BPH), such as difficulty starting urination, weak or interrupted urine flow, frequent urination, and a feeling that the bladder has not emptied completely.

How does it work?
Tamsulosin relaxes the muscles around the prostate and bladder outlet to help urine flow more easily. Dutasteride reduces the hormone that contributes to prostate enlargement and may gradually reduce prostate size.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not chew, crush, or open it. Use it regularly as directed, and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, especially when standing up; reduced sex drive; difficulty getting or maintaining an erection; ejaculation problems or reduced semen; breast tenderness or enlargement; and headache.

Precautions
Rise slowly from sitting or lying down because dizziness or fainting may occur. Tell the doctor about liver disease, low blood pressure, or any allergy to this medicine. Inform the eye surgeon before cataract or glaucoma surgery. Dutasteride can lower PSA blood-test results, so doctors must be told that it is being used. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should not handle leaking or broken capsules. Seek medical help for severe dizziness, allergic swelling, or inability to pass urine.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve gas, bloating and discomfort caused by trapped wind, including colic-like symptoms.

How does it work?
Simethicone helps combine and disperse gas bubbles so they can pass more easily. Dill and fennel oils may help ease digestive discomfort associated with gas.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Measure the recommended amount carefully and do not exceed the stated dose. For babies and children, use only an age-appropriate product and dose.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Mild digestive upset may occur. Rarely, an allergic reaction may develop.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to simethicone, dill, fennel or any other ingredient. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, persistent, or occur with repeated vomiting, fever, a swollen abdomen, blood in the stool or marked pain. Consult a doctor before use in very young babies or if symptoms are unexplained.

What is it used for?
Ticagrelor is used with prescribed treatment to reduce the risk of blood clots, heart attack and stroke in people with acute coronary syndrome, such as a heart attack or unstable angina. It may also help prevent clots in a coronary stent.

How does it work?
It prevents blood platelets from sticking together and forming harmful clots by blocking the P2Y12 platelet receptor.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, with or without food. Do not stop taking it without medical advice, as this may increase the risk of a heart attack or blood clot. Tell the doctor before surgery or dental procedures that it is being taken.

Common side effects
Bleeding, easy bruising, nosebleeds, shortness of breath, headache, dizziness, nausea and diarrhoea.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical help for severe or uncontrolled bleeding, blood in the urine or stools, vomiting blood, or sudden severe headache or weakness. Inform the doctor about a history of bleeding, stomach ulcers, stroke or brain bleeding, liver disease, or breathing problems. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, especially blood thinners and medicines that may increase bleeding risk. Avoid stopping treatment or taking painkillers such as ibuprofen without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used for the short-term treatment of melasma, a condition causing dark or brown patches on the face. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Hydroquinone reduces melanin production, helping lighten dark patches. Tretinoin increases skin cell turnover, while mometasone reduces skin inflammation and irritation.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Avoid the eyes, lips, inside of the nose and broken or irritated skin. Wash hands after applying. Use sun protection and avoid unnecessary sunlight during treatment.

Common side effects
Redness, burning, stinging, dryness, peeling, itching and skin irritation may occur. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, visible small blood vessels or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision and do not use for longer than prescribed. Avoid other irritating skin products unless advised by a doctor. Stop and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, blistering or worsening skin changes occur. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically approved by a doctor; consult a doctor before use while breastfeeding. Keep away from children and do not apply to infected skin.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used for certain liver and bile-duct conditions, including primary biliary cholangitis. It may also be prescribed to dissolve selected cholesterol gallstones when appropriate.

How does it work?
It is a bile acid that improves the flow and composition of bile. It can reduce cholesterol buildup in bile and may help protect liver cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Take it consistently as directed. Do not stop treatment without medical advice. Regular liver-function tests or other monitoring may be needed.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort or pain, nausea, and vomiting may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about gallbladder, bile-duct, or liver problems. It may not be suitable if the bile ducts are blocked or for some types of gallstones. Antacids containing aluminium and medicines that bind bile acids may reduce its absorption; medical advice is needed about timing. Seek medical advice if severe abdominal pain, worsening jaundice, or persistent diarrhoea occurs.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used to help dissolve certain cholesterol-based gallstones and to treat some long-term liver and bile-flow problems, including primary biliary cholangitis. It is used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It changes the composition of bile, helping reduce cholesterol buildup and improve bile flow. It may also help protect liver cells from the harmful effects of bile acids.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea or loose stools, abdominal discomfort, nausea and itching may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about gallbladder or bile-duct blockage, severe liver disease, or frequent diarrhoea. Medical monitoring may be needed during treatment. Antacids containing aluminium and some cholesterol-binding medicines can reduce its absorption; tell the doctor or pharmacist about all medicines being taken. Consult a doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This combination is used as a nutritional supplement to provide vitamin B6, niacinamide and folic acid. It also contains Bacillus spores, which may help support normal intestinal bacteria and digestive health.

How does it work?
Vitamin B6, niacinamide and folic acid support normal energy production, nerve function and blood-cell formation. Bacillus spores are beneficial bacteria that help maintain the balance of microorganisms in the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not use it as a substitute for a balanced diet.

Common side effects
Mild nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating or changes in bowel movements may occur. Seek medical advice if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Inform a healthcare professional about any allergy to the ingredients or if taking other vitamin, folic acid or probiotic products. Do not take additional supplements containing high doses of vitamin B6 or folic acid without advice. People with known vitamin B12 deficiency should seek medical advice before using folic acid supplements, as folic acid may mask some signs of the deficiency.

What is it used for?
This supplement is used to support healthy intestinal bacteria and provide folic acid, vitamin B6, niacinamide and zinc. It may be used as nutritional support when advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

How does it work?
Lactic acid bacillus helps support the natural balance of bacteria in the intestine. The vitamins and zinc support normal energy metabolism, blood formation, nerve function and immune function.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If taking antibiotics, ask a pharmacist about the appropriate time to take this product.

Common side effects
Mild bloating, gas, stomach discomfort, nausea or loose stools may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if signs of an allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Inform a doctor before use if there is severe illness, a weakened immune system or a history of allergy to any ingredient. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about all medicines and supplements being taken, especially antibiotics or other mineral supplements.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve wet or productive cough with thick mucus, especially when airway narrowing causes wheezing or breathing difficulty.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help loosen and clear mucus from the airways. Terbutaline relaxes the airway muscles, helping improve airflow.

How to take/use it
Take/use only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If it is a liquid, measure each dose with the supplied measuring device rather than a household spoon.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, tremors, nervousness, muscle cramps or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid or a history of seizures. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, or a serious skin rash. Do not use this medicine to self-treat a persistent or unexplained cough without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with mucus and help clear phlegm from the airways. It may also help ease wheezing or breathing difficulty caused by narrowed airways.

How does it work?
Levosalbutamol relaxes the airway muscles and helps open the airways. Ambroxol loosens mucus, while guaiphenesin helps thin and clear phlegm.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not combine with other cough or cold medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, tremor, nervousness, dry mouth and a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Seek medical advice if breathing difficulty worsens, wheezing is severe, or the cough persists. Stop use and seek urgent help for rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Vildagliptin is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It may be used alone or together with other diabetes medicines when additional blood sugar control is needed.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called DPP-4, which helps increase the body’s natural incretin hormones. This supports insulin release after meals and reduces the release of glucagon, helping lower blood sugar.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. It can usually be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If used with other diabetes medicines, follow the prescribed schedule carefully.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, nausea, constipation, and symptoms of a common cold such as a sore throat or blocked nose may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when it is taken with certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about liver disease, kidney problems, pancreatitis, or allergies to diabetes medicines. Liver function may need monitoring. Seek medical advice promptly for severe, persistent abdominal pain, especially if it spreads to the back, or signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness. This medicine is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

What is it used for?
Vildagliptin + metformin is used with diet and exercise to control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when blood sugar is not adequately controlled with metformin alone or when both medicines are needed. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Vildagliptin helps the body release more insulin when blood sugar is high and reduces excess sugar production. Metformin mainly reduces sugar production by the liver and helps the body use insulin better.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with or after food to reduce stomach upset. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Swallow the tablet as directed. Continue the recommended diet, exercise and blood sugar monitoring.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain or discomfort, reduced appetite, headache and dizziness may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or sulfonylurea medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, heart failure, heavy alcohol use, or a history of pancreatitis. Seek urgent medical help for severe, persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, unusual extreme tiredness, breathing difficulty or severe weakness. Long-term metformin use may reduce vitamin B12 levels. Kidney function may need checking during treatment. Avoid excessive alcohol and inform the doctor before surgery or investigations using contrast dye.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It may be prescribed when blood sugar is not adequately controlled with metformin alone or other treatment.

How does it work?
Vildagliptin helps the body release insulin when blood sugar is high and reduces excess sugar production by the liver. Metformin mainly reduces sugar production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with or after food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet whole and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the prescriber or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain or discomfort, vomiting, reduced appetite, headache and dizziness. Low blood sugar may occur, especially when used with other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, heart failure, heavy alcohol use, or any planned surgery or contrast-dye scan. Seek urgent medical help for severe weakness, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, or unusual sleepiness. Kidney function may need monitoring, and long-term use may reduce vitamin B12 levels. This medicine is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

What is it used for?
Voglibose is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in people with type 2 diabetes, particularly the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How does it work?
It slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates from food in the intestine. This helps reduce the increase in blood sugar after meals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually immediately before or with the first mouthful of a meal. Take it with food and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort and diarrhoea. These effects may be more noticeable when treatment is started.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice, especially if there is kidney or liver disease, intestinal blockage or a significant digestive disorder. Low blood sugar may occur when used with insulin or other diabetes medicines. If this happens, use glucose (dextrose) rather than table sugar, and seek medical advice if symptoms are severe or persistent.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when one medicine alone is not enough. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Glimepiride helps the pancreas release insulin, while metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin. Voglibose slows the breakdown and absorption of carbohydrates, helping reduce the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with or just before meals. Do not skip meals, change the dose, or stop treatment without medical advice. Monitor blood sugar as recommended. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber's instructions and do not take an extra dose unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, gas, bloating, and loss of appetite may occur. Low blood sugar can cause sweating, shaking, dizziness, hunger, or weakness.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is kidney or liver disease, heavy alcohol use, heart failure, or a history of low blood sugar. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent weakness, vomiting, breathing difficulty, unusual sleepiness, or symptoms of very low blood sugar. Tell the doctor before surgery, medical procedures involving contrast dye, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid alcohol unless the doctor advises that it is safe.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when one medicine alone is not enough.

How does it work?
Glimepiride helps the pancreas release more insulin, while metformin reduces sugar production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin. Voglibose slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates, helping reduce the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with or just before a meal, and swallow it with water. Do not skip meals, change the dose, or stop treatment without medical advice. Follow the prescribed diet and blood sugar monitoring plan.

Common side effects
Low blood sugar, nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, gas, bloating and loss of appetite. Low blood sugar may cause sweating, shaking, dizziness, hunger or weakness.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, heavy alcohol use, or if surgery, a contrast scan or prolonged fasting is planned. The risk of low blood sugar is higher if meals are skipped or with alcohol. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent weakness, breathing difficulty, unusual sleepiness, or severe abdominal symptoms. This medicine is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

What is it used for?
Used as a medicated cleansing soap for acne-prone skin, pimples and excess oil. It may help reduce acne-causing bacteria and support cleaner skin.

How does it work?
Benzoyl peroxide, triclosan and tea tree oil help reduce microorganisms on the skin, while cleansing removes excess oil. Allantoin helps soothe the skin.

How to take/use it
Wet the affected skin, apply the soap to make a gentle lather, rinse thoroughly and pat dry. Use as directed on the product label. Avoid scrubbing the skin.

Common side effects
Dryness, redness, peeling, burning, itching or skin irritation may occur, especially at the beginning of use.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not apply to broken or severely irritated skin. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops. Benzoyl peroxide may bleach hair, clothing or fabrics.

What is it used for?
Activated charcoal is mainly used in emergency treatment to help bind certain swallowed poisons or medicines in the stomach and intestines. It should only be used for poisoning when advised by a doctor or poison-control professional.

How does it work?
It binds some substances in the digestive tract, reducing their absorption into the body. It does not work for every type of poisoning.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not use it to treat suspected poisoning without urgent medical advice. Keep it away from other oral medicines because it may reduce their absorption.

Common side effects
Black stools, constipation, nausea and vomiting may occur.

Precautions
Do not give activated charcoal to an unconscious or very drowsy person, or to anyone who may have difficulty swallowing, unless directed by a healthcare professional, due to the risk of breathing it into the lungs. It may be unsuitable for bowel blockage or after swallowing corrosive chemicals or petroleum-based products. Seek urgent medical help for suspected poisoning.

What is it used for?
This gel is used to treat acne, including pimples, blackheads and whiteheads.

How does it work?
Adapalene helps prevent blocked pores and reduces acne-related inflammation. Benzoyl peroxide helps reduce acne-causing bacteria and clears excess oil and dead skin from the pores.

How to take/use it
Use only on the skin and apply as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, acne-affected skin. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips, inside of the nose and broken or sunburned skin. Wash hands after use.

Common side effects
Dryness, redness, peeling, itching, burning, stinging or skin irritation may occur, especially when starting treatment. Benzoyl peroxide may bleach hair, clothing or fabrics.

Precautions
Avoid excessive sunlight and use sunscreen during treatment. Do not use with other irritating skin products unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical help if severe swelling, blistering, severe irritation or signs of an allergic reaction occur. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy; avoid applying it to the breast or nipple before breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Cetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth with water, with or without food, as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or tiredness, headache, dry mouth, nausea, and dizziness.

Precautions
Cetirizine may cause sleepiness or dizziness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or drinking alcohol until its effects are known. People with kidney problems, or those who are pregnant or breastfeeding, should seek medical advice before use. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This face wash is used to gently cleanse the face while helping maintain skin moisture and support the skin barrier. It may be suitable for dry, dehydrated or sensitive skin.

How does it work?
Cleansing agents remove dirt, oil and impurities. Hyaluronic acid, glycerin and aloe vera help attract or retain moisture, while ceramides help support the skin barrier.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Wet the face, apply a small amount, gently massage and rinse thoroughly. Avoid contact with the eyes. Follow the product label instructions.

Common side effects
Mild irritation, redness, stinging or dryness may occur, especially on sensitive skin. Allergic reactions are uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes and do not swallow. Stop use if significant irritation, swelling or a rash develops. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or are severe.

What is it used for?
Used as a moisturising lotion to help relieve dryness and keep the skin soft and hydrated.

How does it work?
Glycerine and propylene glycol help attract moisture to the skin, while cetyl alcohol, lecithin and oils help soften the skin and reduce moisture loss.

How to take/use it
Apply a suitable amount to clean, dry skin and gently massage until absorbed. Use as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. For external use only.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching or a stinging sensation may occur, especially in sensitive skin.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes and mucous membranes. Do not apply to broken or infected skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops.

What is it used for?
A cleansing soap for washing the skin. Aloe vera, glycerine, vitamin E and skimmed milk may help leave the skin feeling moisturised after cleansing.

How does it work?
The soap removes dirt, oil and impurities from the skin. Glycerine and the other moisturising ingredients help reduce the dry feeling that can occur after washing.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Wet the skin, apply the soap to make a lather, rinse thoroughly and dry gently. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Some people may experience skin dryness, irritation, redness or an allergic reaction.

Precautions
Do not use on broken or severely irritated skin. Stop using it if irritation or a rash develops. Seek medical advice if the reaction is severe or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Used to treat high blood pressure. It may also help prevent chest pain related to angina when prescribed for this purpose.

How does it work?
Amlodipine relaxes and widens blood vessels. Atenolol slows the heart rate and reduces the heart's workload, helping lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, tiredness, slow heartbeat, ankle or foot swelling, nausea and cold hands or feet.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about asthma or other breathing problems, a slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart conduction problems, diabetes, kidney disease or liver disease. Atenolol may hide some warning signs of low blood sugar. Seek medical help for fainting, severe dizziness, breathing difficulty, or a very slow or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Amla fruit powder is a herbal dietary supplement traditionally used to support general health and digestion. It is not a substitute for treatment of a specific medical condition.

How does it work?
Amla contains naturally occurring plant compounds, including antioxidants. Its exact health effects may vary depending on the product and the amount used.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label. It may be mixed with water or food. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
It may cause stomach upset, nausea, loose stools or acidity in some people.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to amla or any product ingredient. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking medicines for diabetes or blood thinning. Stop use and seek medical help if a serious allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Terminalia arjuna bark powder is traditionally used to support heart and cardiovascular health. It should not replace prescribed treatment for heart disease, high blood pressure or other cardiac conditions.

How does it work?
Its exact mechanism is not fully established. Traditional use suggests that it may help support normal heart function and provide antioxidant effects, but clinical evidence is limited.

How to take/use it
Use only according to the product label or the advice of an Ayurvedic practitioner or healthcare professional. Do not use a dose or treatment duration unless specifically advised.

Common side effects
Safety information is limited. Stomach discomfort or other digestive symptoms may occur.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use if taking medicines for heart conditions or blood pressure, or medicines that affect blood clotting. Seek advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or before surgery. Do not use it as a substitute for prescribed cardiac treatment.

What is it used for?
Used for moisturising the skin, supporting the skin barrier and improving the appearance of dry or rough skin. Retinol-containing lotions may also help improve the appearance of fine lines and uneven skin texture.

How does it work?
Ceramides and vitamin E help moisturise and support the skin barrier. Retinol supports skin renewal, while peptides may help support the skin’s overall appearance.

How to take/use it
Apply a small amount to clean, dry skin as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips and broken or irritated skin. Use sunscreen during the day, especially when using retinol-containing products.

Common side effects
Dryness, redness, itching, stinging, peeling or irritation may occur, especially when starting retinol.

Precautions
For external use only. Stop use if severe irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Avoid using on broken or sunburned skin. Use cautiously with other irritating skincare products. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before using retinol-containing products.

What is it used for?
Withania somnifera (ashwagandha) root powder is a herbal supplement commonly used to help manage stress and support restful sleep. It is not a substitute for treatment of anxiety or other medical conditions.

How does it work?
Its natural compounds may influence the body's stress response and nervous system. The exact mechanism is not fully understood.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, diarrhoea, nausea and drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice before use if breastfeeding, or if there is thyroid disease, an autoimmune condition, liver disease, or use of medicines that cause drowsiness. Stop use and seek medical help if symptoms of liver problems, such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine or severe abdominal pain, occur.

What is it used for?
This herbal combination is traditionally used to support breast milk production in breastfeeding mothers. Evidence for its effectiveness may be limited, and it should not replace advice from a doctor or lactation specialist for low milk supply.

How does it work?
Asparagus racemosus, fenugreek and fennel are traditionally used as herbal galactagogues, which may help support lactation. The exact way they work is not fully established.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Take with water and inform a healthcare professional if milk supply remains low or if the baby is not feeding or gaining weight properly.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, gas, bloating or loose stools may occur. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if pregnant, allergic to fenugreek, fennel or similar plants, or if there is diabetes, a bleeding disorder, or use of blood-thinning or blood-sugar-lowering medicines. Stop use and seek medical help for rash, swelling, breathing difficulty or other signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Atorvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, especially LDL (“bad”) cholesterol and triglycerides. It also helps reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It reduces cholesterol production in the liver and helps the liver remove more LDL cholesterol from the blood.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food, and preferably at the same time each day. Continue the recommended diet and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, indigestion and muscle pain may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, thyroid problems or any history of muscle problems. Report unexplained or severe muscle pain, weakness, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes promptly. It should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised. Ask a doctor or pharmacist about possible medicine interactions, and avoid excessive grapefruit or grapefruit juice.

What is it used for?
Atorvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, especially “bad” LDL cholesterol, and to help reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It reduces the liver’s production of cholesterol and helps the liver remove more LDL cholesterol from the blood.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Do not stop treatment without medical advice. Continue any recommended cholesterol-lowering diet and lifestyle measures.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, indigestion and muscle aches may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, or any unexplained muscle pain or weakness. Seek medical help if severe muscle pain, dark urine, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or unusual tiredness occurs. It should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines, as some can interact with atorvastatin.

What is it used for?
Used to treat abnormal blood fat levels, including high cholesterol and high triglycerides, when diet and lifestyle changes alone are not enough. It helps reduce the risk of cardiovascular complications associated with unhealthy cholesterol levels.

How does it work?
Atorvastatin reduces the production of cholesterol in the liver and lowers LDL (bad) cholesterol. Fenofibrate mainly lowers triglycerides and can help improve other blood fat levels.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet whole with water. Take it at the same time each day, with or without food as directed by the prescriber. Continue recommended diet and lifestyle changes. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Muscle aches, headache, nausea, indigestion, diarrhoea or stomach discomfort, and increased liver enzyme levels may occur.

Precautions
Tell the prescriber about liver, kidney or gallbladder disease, heavy alcohol use, thyroid problems, or a history of muscle problems with cholesterol medicines. The risk of muscle injury may increase with some medicines; report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness, especially with dark urine, immediately. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe abdominal pain, or an allergic reaction. Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised. Used to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency. It supports calcium absorption and helps maintain healthy bones and muscles.

How does it work?
Cholecalciferol is vitamin D3. It helps the body absorb calcium and phosphate, which are needed for strong bones and normal muscle function.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth and swallow the softgel as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Follow the prescribed schedule and do not take it more often than recommended. Do not combine it with other vitamin D or calcium supplements unless advised.

Common side effects
Usually none when taken as directed. Excessive intake may cause nausea, vomiting, constipation, stomach pain, weakness, excessive thirst or frequent urination.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels or conditions that may increase calcium levels. Avoid excessive use. Seek medical advice if symptoms of high calcium develop, such as persistent nausea, vomiting, unusual thirst or frequent urination.

What is it used for?
Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) drops are used to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and supports healthy bones and teeth.

How does it work?
It is converted in the body into an active form of vitamin D. This helps improve calcium and phosphate absorption and supports normal bone health.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Measure the drops carefully using the supplied dropper or measuring device. Do not take it with other vitamin D supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Usually none when used as directed. Excessive intake may cause nausea, vomiting, constipation, stomach pain, unusual thirst, or frequent urination.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or conditions that may increase calcium levels. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Seek medical help if symptoms of excessive vitamin D or high calcium levels develop.

What is it used for?
Used as a vitamin D3 and vitamin K2 supplement to support bone health and normal calcium use in the body.

How does it work?
Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium. Vitamin K2 helps activate proteins involved in maintaining healthy bones.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated at recommended amounts. Mild nausea or stomach upset may occur. Excessive vitamin D intake can cause constipation, weakness, increased thirst or frequent urination.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high blood calcium, or a condition affecting calcium levels. Vitamin K2 may interact with warfarin and other vitamin K-sensitive blood thinners. Avoid taking additional vitamin D or calcium supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Cholecalciferol injection is used to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency. Vitamin D helps maintain strong bones and supports the absorption of calcium and phosphate.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamin D3, which helps the body absorb calcium and phosphate from the intestine. This supports normal bone and muscle health.

How to take/use it
This injection should be given by a healthcare professional. The dose and timing depend on vitamin D levels and medical advice. Do not self-inject or take additional high-dose vitamin D without guidance.

Common side effects
Injection-site pain or redness, nausea, constipation, or stomach discomfort may occur. Excessive vitamin D can raise calcium levels in the blood.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially with kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or conditions that increase sensitivity to vitamin D. Avoid taking other vitamin D or calcium supplements unless advised. Seek medical help for severe nausea, vomiting, unusual thirst, frequent urination, confusion, or marked weakness.

What is it used for?
Used to reduce tooth sensitivity and help protect teeth against cavities. It also helps reduce plaque and support gum health.

How does it work?
Potassium nitrate helps calm the nerves inside sensitive teeth. Sodium monofluorophosphate strengthens tooth enamel and helps prevent decay, while triclosan helps reduce plaque-forming bacteria.

How to take/use it
Brush the teeth with this toothpaste as directed on the product label. Spit out after brushing and avoid swallowing. Do not use more often or for longer than advised by a dentist or the product label.

Common side effects
Mild mouth irritation or an altered taste may occur. Stop using it if significant irritation or an allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
For external oral use only; do not swallow. Keep out of reach of young children. Children should use it only under adult supervision and according to the product label. Consult a dentist if tooth sensitivity continues, worsens, or is associated with pain, swelling or damaged teeth.

What is it used for?
Cissus quadrangularis is a herbal supplement traditionally used to support bone health and healing after bone injuries. Evidence for these uses is limited, and it should not replace medical treatment for a fracture or bone disease.

How does it work?
It may support processes involved in bone formation and repair. Its exact effects in humans are not fully established.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Consult a doctor before using it for a fracture, osteoporosis or another bone condition.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache or dry mouth may occur.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is diabetes or another long-term medical condition. Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use with regular medicines. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe or persistent side effects occur.

What is it used for?
Clarithromycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the chest and lungs, throat, sinuses, skin and soft tissues. It may also be used with other medicines to help treat Helicobacter pylori infection. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making proteins needed for their growth and survival.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take extra doses if one is missed; follow the product label or prescriber's instructions. Do not share antibiotics with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, indigestion, headache and a changed or bitter taste.

Precautions
Tell the prescriber about allergies to clarithromycin or other macrolide antibiotics, liver or kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, or low potassium or magnesium levels. Clarithromycin can interact with several medicines, including some cholesterol, blood-thinning and heart medicines, so provide a complete list of medicines being taken. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, a fast or irregular heartbeat, swelling, or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
This gel is used to treat acne, including pimples and inflamed acne lesions.

How does it work?
Clindamycin helps reduce acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Nicotinamide (vitamin B3) also helps reduce skin inflammation and may support overall acne control.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin exactly as directed by the doctor or product label. For external use only. Wash hands before and after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose.

Common side effects
Dryness, redness, peeling, itching, burning or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to clindamycin, nicotinamide or any ingredient. Avoid applying to broken or severely irritated skin. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe skin irritation or persistent diarrhoea, especially watery or bloody diarrhoea, occurs. Use only as directed to reduce the risk of antibiotic resistance.

What is it used for?
Clobetasol propionate cream is a very strong steroid cream used to reduce inflammation, redness, swelling and itching in skin conditions such as eczema, psoriasis and dermatitis, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the overactive immune and inflammatory response in the skin, helping relieve redness, swelling and itching.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Use it only on the skin and avoid contact with the eyes. Wash hands after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Do not cover the area with a bandage or dressing unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, irritation, itching, dryness and skin thinning at the application site. Stretch marks or changes in skin colour may occur, especially with prolonged use.

Precautions
This is a very potent steroid and should not be used for longer or on larger areas than prescribed. Avoid the face, groin, underarms, broken skin and skin infections unless specifically advised by a doctor. Use in children, during pregnancy or while breastfeeding only on medical advice. Seek medical advice if the condition worsens, shows signs of infection, or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin for certain fungal infections with inflammation and an associated bacterial infection, when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Miconazole stops the growth of fungi, while neomycin helps control susceptible bacteria. Clobetasol is a strong corticosteroid that reduces redness, swelling and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as directed by the healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and broken skin. Do not cover the area tightly unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation. Prolonged or repeated use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or other skin changes. Neomycin may cause an allergic skin rash.

Precautions
Clobetasol is a very potent steroid and should not be used for longer than prescribed. Avoid using it on the face, groin, skin folds or in children unless specifically advised. Do not use it for undiagnosed rashes, acne or viral skin infections. Stop and seek medical advice if the infection worsens, the skin becomes severely irritated, or signs of allergy such as swelling or breathing difficulty occur.

What is it used for?
L-Carnosine syrup is used as a dietary supplement to provide L-carnosine. The supplied information does not identify a specific disease or medical condition it is intended to treat.

How does it work?
L-Carnosine is a naturally occurring dipeptide found in the body. It may help support cellular protection against oxidative stress.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Stomach discomfort, nausea or other digestive upset may occur.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, in children, or if there is an existing medical condition or ongoing medication. Stop use and seek medical advice if an unusual or severe reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold symptoms such as blocked or stuffy nose, runny nose, sneezing, fever and body aches.

How does it work?
Phenylephrine helps reduce nasal blockage, while chlorpheniramine reduces allergy-like symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose. Paracetamol helps relieve fever and mild body aches.

How to take/use it

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, blurred vision or difficulty sleeping may occur. Some people may experience a fast heartbeat or a rise in blood pressure.

Precautions
This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or alcohol if affected. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine or prostate enlargement. Check with a healthcare professional before giving it to children, and use only the age-appropriate dose on the label. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, breathing difficulty, allergic reactions or symptoms that worsen or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement providing collagen and biotin, nutrients involved in maintaining normal skin, hair and nails.

How does it work?
Collagen provides amino acids used by the body to form connective tissues. Biotin supports normal energy metabolism and the maintenance of skin, hair and nails.

Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Precautions
Tell a doctor before use if pregnant, breastfeeding, allergic to any ingredient or taking regular medicines. Biotin may interfere with some blood test results; inform the doctor or laboratory before testing. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

It contains several Ayurvedic herbs traditionally used to support reproductive and general wellness. A specific medical mechanism and proven effectiveness for a particular condition have not been established from the supplied information.

The ingredients provide plant compounds with antioxidant and other biological effects. The exact intended benefit and mechanism of this combination cannot be determined from the supplied information.

Salicylic acid loosens and removes dead, thickened skin. Glycerin, aloe vera and dimethicone help moisturise the skin and support its protective barrier.

Oat extract and panthenol help soothe and hydrate the skin. Ceramides and squalane help replenish skin lipids and reduce moisture loss.

Curcuminoids in turmeric may help regulate inflammatory processes and neutralise oxidative stress in the body.

Curcuminoids, the active compounds in turmeric, may influence inflammatory processes in the body. The extent of benefit can vary between individuals.

Used to relieve painful acidity, heartburn and irritation of the stomach or upper digestive tract. It may also be prescribed for acid-related ulcers or gastritis.

Sucralfate forms a protective coating over irritated or ulcerated areas in the stomach. Oxetacaine is a local anaesthetic that helps reduce pain from the irritated lining.

What is it used for?
Dapagliflozin is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It may also be prescribed to reduce the risk of worsening heart failure or chronic kidney disease in suitable patients.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove excess glucose from the blood into the urine. It also causes the body to remove some extra salt and fluid, which can benefit some people with heart or kidney problems.

How to take/use it
Take the tablet exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Drink adequate fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Passing urine more often, increased thirst, dehydration, dizziness, urinary tract infections and fungal infections of the genitals. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, low blood pressure, dehydration, or medicines that increase urine production. Seek urgent medical help for nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, difficulty breathing, or confusion, as these may indicate diabetic ketoacidosis. This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes.

Dapagliflozin helps the kidneys remove extra glucose through urine. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin better.

What is it used for?

It reduces the urge to cough by suppressing the cough reflex in the brain.
