Febuxostat is used long term to lower high uric acid levels in people with gout. It helps prevent gout attacks and the formation of uric acid crystals, but it does not provide immediate relief during an acute gout attack.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called xanthine oxidase, which reduces the body's production of uric acid.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop treatment without medical advice. Continue drinking fluids unless a doctor has advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Nausea, joint pain, rash, diarrhoea, headache and abnormal liver function tests. Gout attacks may temporarily become more frequent when treatment is started.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, stroke, liver disease or kidney disease before use. Liver function tests may be needed. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, sudden weakness, or a severe skin rash, blistering or swelling. Do not take with azathioprine or mercaptopurine unless specifically directed by a specialist. This medicine is not a treatment for immediate relief of an acute gout attack.

What is it used for?
This combined oral contraceptive is used to prevent pregnancy when taken as directed. It may also help make periods more regular and reduce menstrual bleeding or cramps in some people.

How does it work?
It contains two hormones that mainly prevent ovulation. It also thickens cervical mucus and changes the lining of the womb, making pregnancy less likely.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions in the pack. Try to take it at the same time each day and do not skip tablets. If a tablet is missed, follow the product leaflet or ask a pharmacist or doctor for advice. It does not protect against sexually transmitted infections.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, breast tenderness, mood changes, and spotting or changes in menstrual bleeding may occur, especially during the first few months.

Precautions
Tell the doctor before use if there is a history of blood clots, stroke, heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, migraine with aura, liver disease, breast cancer, or if the person smokes—particularly if over 35. Seek urgent medical help for sudden chest pain, breathlessness, coughing blood, severe headache, vision changes, or painful swelling in one leg. Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for short-term relief of common cold symptoms such as fever, headache, body aches, blocked or stuffy nose, runny nose and sneezing. It helps relieve symptoms but does not treat the underlying infection.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac and paracetamol help reduce pain and fever. Phenylephrine relieves nasal blockage, while cetirizine reduces allergy-like symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose. Caffeine may support the pain-relieving effect.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the package instructions, with water. Do not take more than recommended. Avoid using it with other medicines containing paracetamol, aceclofenac or other NSAIDs, phenylephrine, or cetirizine unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach discomfort, dry mouth, dizziness, drowsiness, headache, difficulty sleeping, increased blood pressure or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use medical advice is important if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, high blood pressure, heart disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, or kidney or liver problems. Avoid alcohol. Cetirizine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving if affected. Do not use during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, unless prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for severe stomach pain, black stools, vomiting blood, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of pain, swelling and muscle spasms associated with painful muscle, joint or other musculoskeletal conditions.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces pain and inflammation, while paracetamol helps relieve pain. Chlorzoxazone acts on the central nervous system to relax painful muscle spasms.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Swallow the modified-release tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more than the prescribed amount, and avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or painkillers unless advised by a healthcare professional. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach discomfort, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness, drowsiness and headache.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness and the risk of liver damage. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe abdominal pain. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain and inflammation, including muscle and joint pain and pain associated with arthritis. It may also help reduce fever.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and reduce fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or NSAIDs unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid or seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, or asthma triggered by painkillers. Avoid alcohol. Do not use during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, unless specifically advised. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin rash or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain, inflammation and swelling, such as in muscle, joint, bone, dental or after-injury conditions, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever, while serratiopeptidase may help reduce swelling.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache. Skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid excessive alcohol. Use during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, only on medical advice. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful muscle spasms and musculoskeletal pain, including pain affecting the muscles, joints or back.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac and paracetamol help reduce pain and inflammation. Thiocolchicoside helps relax painful muscle spasms.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more than prescribed or combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol or NSAIDs unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and drowsiness.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is an allergy to its ingredients, a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe liver or kidney disease, or sensitivity to painkillers such as aspirin or other NSAIDs. Use only on medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding; thiocolchicoside should not be used during pregnancy. Avoid alcohol and driving if dizzy or drowsy. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin reactions, breathing difficulty or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and swelling, such as in muscle, joint, bone or soft-tissue injuries and after some surgical procedures. It may also help reduce associated fever.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation, while paracetamol helps relieve pain and fever. Trypsin and chymotrypsin are enzymes used to help reduce inflammatory swelling.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or painkillers such as ibuprofen unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache. Skin rash or itching may occur.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, bleeding problems or an allergy to painkillers. Use during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, only if specifically prescribed. Avoid excessive alcohol. Stop taking it and seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron and folate deficiencies, which may cause anaemia. It also provides vitamin B12 and zinc to support healthy red blood cell formation and normal body functions.

How does it work?
Iron, folate and vitamin B12 are nutrients needed to make healthy red blood cells. Zinc supports several normal processes, including immune function and tissue maintenance.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist; the correct dose and duration depend on individual needs. Swallow with water. Iron may cause stomach upset, so it may be taken with food if needed. Avoid taking it at the same time as tea, coffee, milk, antacids or certain medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, diarrhoea and dark-coloured stools may occur.

Precautions
Keep out of the reach of children, as an iron overdose can be dangerous. Consult a doctor before use if there is iron overload, a blood disorder, or unexplained anaemia. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines, as iron can reduce the absorption of some medicines.

What is it used for?
This supplement is commonly used by women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) to support hormonal balance, insulin sensitivity and normal ovarian function. It also provides folic acid, vitamin D and chromium as nutritional support.

How does it work?
Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol help support insulin signalling and ovarian function. Folic acid, vitamin D and chromium support normal cell function, bone health and glucose metabolism.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Mild nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea or headache may occur.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is diabetes, kidney disease or treatment with blood-sugar-lowering medicines. This supplement should not replace prescribed PCOS treatment or medical follow-up.

What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and an itchy nose or throat.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms without usually causing much drowsiness.

How to take/use it
Swallow the tablet with water as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Avoid taking it with fruit juice, as this may reduce its effect. Do not take aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids at the same time; ask a pharmacist about suitable spacing.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, dizziness, and mild tiredness. Drowsiness can occur in some people.

Precautions
Tell a doctor or pharmacist if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips or throat, breathing difficulty, or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose or throat, and watery or itchy eyes.

How does it work?
Fexofenadine blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergic symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, substances that can contribute to nasal swelling and other allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Swallow with water and do not change the dose or duration without medical advice. Avoid taking it with fruit juices, as they may reduce the absorption of fexofenadine. Keep aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids at least 2 hours apart from this medicine.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness, tiredness, or dry mouth may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Although fexofenadine usually causes little drowsiness, avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Montelukast may rarely cause mood or behaviour changes, sleep problems, depression, or suicidal thoughts; seek medical help promptly if these occur.

What is it used for?
Provides dietary protein from whey, pea and brown rice, along with vitamins and minerals. It may be used to supplement daily nutritional intake. The added digestive enzymes and lactic acid bacillus may support digestion and gut health.

How does it work?
The protein ingredients supply amino acids needed for normal body functions and muscle maintenance. Vitamins and minerals provide essential nutrients, while digestive enzymes help break down food and lactic acid bacillus is a probiotic microorganism.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended serving. Use with adequate fluids unless otherwise advised.

Common side effects
Bloating, gas, stomach discomfort, nausea, loose stools or constipation may occur. People sensitive to dairy may experience digestive symptoms from whey protein. Green tea extract may cause restlessness, difficulty sleeping or a fast heartbeat in sensitive individuals.

Precautions
Check the ingredients for milk, soy or other allergens. People who are pregnant or breastfeeding, have liver disease, caffeine sensitivity, or take regular medicines should seek medical advice before use, particularly because of Garcinia cambogia and green tea extract. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction or severe stomach symptoms occur.

What is it used for?
This probiotic combination is used to support healthy gut bacteria and digestive health. It may help restore the balance of intestinal bacteria during or after diarrhoea or antibiotic use.

How does it work?
The beneficial bacteria help replenish and maintain the normal balance of microorganisms in the intestine. Fructo-oligosaccharides act as a prebiotic to support the growth of beneficial bacteria, while L-glutamine supports the intestinal lining.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the capsule with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. If taking antibiotics, ask a pharmacist or doctor about the appropriate timing.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort or changes in bowel movements may occur, especially when starting treatment.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use if there is a severely weakened immune system, a serious underlying illness, or a history of allergy to any ingredient. Seek medical advice for persistent or severe diarrhoea, blood in the stool, fever, or signs of dehydration.

What is it used for?
Fluticasone 0.05% Cream is used to reduce redness, swelling and itching in inflammatory skin conditions such as eczema and dermatitis. It may also be prescribed for other steroid-responsive skin conditions.

How does it work?
It is a topical corticosteroid that reduces inflammation and the skin's overactive immune response, helping relieve redness and itching.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin only, exactly as prescribed. For external use only. Wash hands after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Do not cover the area with a tight dressing unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, irritation or dryness at the application site. Prolonged or excessive use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and open wounds. Do not use on infected skin unless advised by a doctor. Avoid prolonged use, large amounts or use on the face, skin folds or in children unless specifically prescribed. Seek medical advice if the skin condition worsens or does not improve.

What is it used for?
This vitamin supplement helps provide pyridoxine (vitamin B6), folate, vitamin B12 and vitamin D when dietary intake may be inadequate or supplementation is recommended. These nutrients support normal blood formation, nerve function, bones and general health.

How does it work?
It supplies essential vitamins used in processes such as red blood cell formation, nerve function and bone maintenance. Vitamin D also helps the body absorb calcium.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and swallow the capsule with water.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Nausea, stomach discomfort or headache may occur.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional about all other supplements and medicines being used. Avoid taking additional vitamin D, folic acid or vitamin B supplements unless advised. Seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Pantoprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acidity, heartburn and acid reflux (GERD). It may also be prescribed for stomach or intestinal ulcers and other acid-related conditions.

How does it work?
It is a proton pump inhibitor that blocks the final step of acid production in the stomach, helping relieve acid-related symptoms and allowing irritated tissues to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed timing in relation to meals and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, vomiting, gas and constipation.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, an allergy to acid-reducing medicines, or long-term use of pantoprazole. Prolonged use may lower magnesium or vitamin B12 levels and may increase the risk of certain infections or fractures. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, unexplained weight loss, vomiting blood, black stools or persistent symptoms. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially warfarin, methotrexate, HIV medicines or other medicines requiring stomach acid for absorption.

What is it used for?
Used to treat acidity, heartburn and acid reflux (GERD). It may also help relieve reflux-related nausea and stomach discomfort when prescribed.

How does it work?
Pantoprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps improve stomach movement and supports the movement of stomach contents into the intestine, which can reduce nausea and reflux symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is generally taken before food, as directed by the doctor. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, constipation, dizziness or dry mouth may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, irregular heartbeat, liver disease or low potassium or magnesium levels. Domperidone can rarely cause serious heart-rhythm problems, especially at higher doses or with certain medicines; avoid self-medication and inform the doctor about all medicines being taken. Seek medical help for fainting, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe or persistent diarrhoea, vomiting blood or black stools. Consult a doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also help with nausea or vomiting associated with these digestive symptoms.

How does it work?
Pantoprazole reduces the production of acid in the stomach. Domperidone helps improve movement of the stomach and upper digestive tract and can reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, gas, dry mouth or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart rhythm problems, heart disease, liver disease, or low potassium or magnesium levels. Domperidone may rarely cause serious heart rhythm problems and should not be combined with certain medicines. Seek medical help for fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting or severe dizziness. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Pantoprazole 40 mg injection reduces excess stomach acid. It is used for acid-related conditions such as acidity, heartburn, acid reflux and ulcers when treatment by injection is needed.

How does it work?
It blocks the acid-producing proton pumps in the stomach, lowering the amount of acid released.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. It should not be self-injected. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, gas and redness or discomfort at the injection site.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to pantoprazole or other acid-reducing medicines, liver disease, or other medicines being taken. Seek urgent medical help for facial swelling, breathing difficulty, severe skin rash or persistent severe diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Simethicone is used to relieve discomfort caused by excess gas, including bloating, fullness and flatulence.

How does it work?
It reduces the surface tension of gas bubbles in the stomach and intestines, helping them combine and pass more easily.

How to take/use it
Swallow the softgel with water and use it as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Simethicone is generally well tolerated. Mild nausea, constipation or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to simethicone or any ingredient in the product. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, marked swelling of the abdomen, or blood in the stool. If gas symptoms continue or keep returning, consult a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve heartburn, acid reflux and indigestion. It can help reduce the burning sensation caused by stomach acid moving up into the food pipe.

How does it work?
Sodium alginate forms a protective layer that helps stop stomach contents from flowing back up. Sodium bicarbonate and calcium carbonate help neutralise excess stomach acid.

How to take/use it
Shake well before use and take by mouth using the measuring device provided. Follow the dose and timing instructions on the product label or as advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Constipation, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort or bloating may occur.

Precautions
Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if there is kidney disease, heart failure, a low-salt diet, high calcium levels or a history of calcium kidney stones. Antacids may affect the absorption of other medicines; separate this product from other medicines as advised by a pharmacist. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist, worsen or occur frequently.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Glimepiride helps the pancreas release more insulin, while metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with a meal. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Take it regularly and do not stop it without medical advice. If a meal is missed, follow the instructions provided by the prescriber rather than taking an extra dose.

Common side effects
Low blood sugar, nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, loss of appetite, headache, dizziness and weight gain.

Precautions
The risk of low blood sugar is higher if meals are skipped, alcohol is consumed, or during unusual physical activity. Kidney or liver disease, dehydration, heavy alcohol use, or a history of heart problems should be discussed with a doctor before use. Seek urgent medical help for severe or repeated low blood sugar, extreme weakness, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting, severe abdominal discomfort or unusual drowsiness. Blood sugar and kidney function may need regular monitoring.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when one medicine alone is not enough.

How does it work?
Glimepiride helps the pancreas release more insulin. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with food. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Take it regularly and do not change or stop treatment without medical advice. Do not skip meals while taking it.

Common side effects
Low blood sugar, nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, vomiting, loss of appetite, headache and weight gain may occur.

Precautions
Be alert for low blood sugar, especially if meals are missed, alcohol is consumed, or extra exercise is taken. Symptoms may include sweating, shaking, dizziness, hunger, fast heartbeat or confusion. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, heavy alcohol use, or if contrast dye or surgery is planned. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent weakness, breathing difficulty, unusual sleepiness, severe vomiting or abdominal pain. This medicine is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

What is it used for?
This combination is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when one medicine alone is not enough.

How does it work?
Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin. Glimepiride helps the pancreas release insulin, while voglibose slows carbohydrate digestion and helps reduce the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions about meals. Swallow the prolonged-release tablet whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not skip meals unless advised by a healthcare professional. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, gas, indigestion and loss of appetite may occur. Low blood sugar can occur, especially with missed meals, and may cause sweating, shakiness, dizziness, hunger or confusion.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is kidney or liver disease. Tell the doctor about severe vomiting, diarrhoea, dehydration, serious infection, planned surgery or an X-ray scan using contrast dye. Avoid excessive alcohol. Seek urgent medical help for severe weakness, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting or unusual sleepiness. Monitor blood sugar as advised.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes.

How does it work?
Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin. Glimepiride helps the pancreas release insulin, while voglibose slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates after meals.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with food. Swallow the prolonged-release tablet whole; do not crush or chew it. Take voglibose-containing medicine with meals as directed. Do not skip meals, and do not change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, gas, indigestion, loss of appetite, headache and dizziness. Low blood sugar may occur, especially with missed meals or increased physical activity.

Precautions
Monitor blood sugar as advised. Be alert for low blood sugar symptoms such as sweating, shaking, dizziness, confusion or unusual hunger. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, heavy alcohol use, dehydration, or if surgery or a contrast-dye scan is planned. Seek urgent medical help for severe weakness, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting or unusual drowsiness.

What is it used for?
This face wash is used to cleanse the face and remove excess oil, dirt and impurities. Its ingredients may also help support a brighter, more even-looking complexion.

How does it work?
The cleanser removes impurities from the skin’s surface. Vitamin C, glutathione, niacinamide and papaya extract are commonly used in skincare for their antioxidant and skin-conditioning properties.

How to take/use it
Use on wet skin and gently massage over the face, avoiding the eye area. Rinse thoroughly and follow the product label’s instructions.

Common side effects
Mild dryness, stinging, redness or skin irritation may occur, especially on sensitive skin.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes. Patch-test before regular use, particularly if the skin is sensitive. Stop use if significant irritation or an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
This nutritional supplement provides antioxidant nutrients, including glutathione, lycopene, grape seed extract, beta-carotene, lutein, selenium, zinc, magnesium and vitamin C. It may be used to support the body's normal antioxidant and nutritional needs. It is not a treatment for a specific disease unless prescribed for that purpose.

The ingredients help provide antioxidant activity, which protects cells from oxidative stress. Zinc, selenium, magnesium and vitamin C also support normal body functions, including immune function and metabolism.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional, with water. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If taking other supplements, check the total intake of selenium, zinc and vitamin A-related ingredients.

Common side effects
May cause mild stomach upset, nausea, diarrhoea or a metallic taste. Stop use and seek medical advice if unusual or severe symptoms occur.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is kidney disease or another long-term medical condition. Zinc and magnesium may reduce the absorption of some antibiotics and thyroid medicines; separate their use as advised by a healthcare professional. Avoid taking other products containing high amounts of selenium, zinc or vitamin A without advice.

What is it used for?
The supplied information identifies glutathione 600 mg injection but does not state a specific approved therapeutic use. Its use should be decided by a qualified healthcare professional; it should not be used for skin lightening or other purposes without medical advice.

Glutathione is a naturally occurring antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative damage and supports certain detoxification processes in the body.

How to take/use it
This is an injection and must be administered only by a qualified healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the medical reason for use and should be prescribed by a doctor.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include injection-site discomfort, nausea, abdominal discomfort and skin rash. Serious allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to glutathione or any ingredient in the injection. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial or throat swelling, severe rash or dizziness after the injection. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only when specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
L-Glutamine is an amino-acid nutritional supplement used to provide extra glutamine when advised by a doctor or dietitian, including in some situations where nutritional support is needed.

How does it work?
Glutamine is a building block of proteins and is used by several cells in the body, including cells in the intestine and immune system.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or dietitian. Mix and use the sachet as instructed. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, abdominal discomfort, bloating or constipation may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if it is intended for a child. Stop use and seek medical help if severe or persistent side effects occur.

What is it used for?
This topical serum is used to exfoliate the skin and help improve rough, dull or uneven-looking skin texture. It also provides moisturising support.

How does it work?
Glycolic acid and gluconolactone help loosen and remove dead skin cells from the skin's surface. Panthenol, betaine and sodium hyaluronate help support skin hydration.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to clean, dry skin as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips and other sensitive areas. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Mild stinging, redness, dryness, peeling or irritation may occur, especially when starting use.

Precautions
Patch-test before use. Stop using it if significant irritation occurs. Use sunscreen and limit sun exposure while using this product, as exfoliating acids can increase sun sensitivity. Avoid using it at the same time as other strong exfoliating or irritating skin products unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Used to help treat pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia), especially male pattern hair loss, and support hair regrowth on the scalp.

How does it work?
Minoxidil helps stimulate hair follicles and prolongs the hair-growth phase. Finasteride lowers dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone linked to pattern hair loss.

How to take/use it
Apply to the affected scalp only as directed by the prescriber or product label. Use on a dry scalp, avoid contact with the eyes and other body areas, and wash hands after application. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Scalp irritation, itching, dryness, redness or flaking; temporary increased hair shedding may occur initially. Unwanted hair growth may occur outside the scalp. Finasteride may rarely cause decreased sexual desire, erectile difficulties or mood changes.

Precautions
Finasteride must not be used during pregnancy or by women who may become pregnant; pregnant women should not handle leaking lotion. Seek medical advice for chest pain, rapid heartbeat, severe dizziness, significant mood changes or an allergic reaction. Consult a doctor before use if there is heart disease or a scalp condition.

What is it used for?
Minoxidil 5% lotion is applied to the scalp to help slow hair loss and support hair regrowth in pattern hair loss.

How does it work?
It helps improve blood flow around hair follicles and may prolong the hair-growth phase, supporting the growth of existing hair.

How to take/use it
Apply only to the scalp as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Use on a clean, dry scalp, avoid contact with the eyes and other body areas, and wash hands after application. Do not apply to broken, inflamed or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Scalp itching, dryness, redness or irritation; unwanted hair growth on the face or other areas. Dizziness, fast heartbeat or swelling may rarely occur.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless advised by a doctor. Consult a doctor before use if there is heart disease, low blood pressure or unexplained, sudden or patchy hair loss. Stop using it and seek medical help for chest pain, fainting, severe dizziness, fast or irregular heartbeat, or swelling.

What is it used for?
Used in hair and scalp products to help control dandruff and support hair conditioning and scalp care.

How does it work?
Piroctone olamine helps reduce the growth of fungi associated with dandruff. Panthenol, hydrolyzed keratin, L-arginine and rosemary extract help condition and support the hair and scalp.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use on the hair and scalp exactly as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes; rinse thoroughly with water if contact occurs.

Common side effects
Scalp or skin irritation, itching, redness or an allergic reaction may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Stop use if significant irritation or a rash develops and seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen. Keep out of reach of children and do not swallow.

What is it used for?
This is a nutritional supplement that provides biotin, vitamins, minerals, methylsulfonylmethane (MSM) and amino acids. It may be used to help meet nutritional needs when dietary intake is insufficient. The specific benefits depend on the amounts of each ingredient.

How does it work?
It supplies nutrients that support normal body functions, including energy metabolism and the maintenance of tissues. Biotin, vitamins, minerals and amino acids each have different roles in the body.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach discomfort.

Common side effects
Some people may experience nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea or headache. Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
Tell a doctor or laboratory professional that biotin is being taken before blood tests, as it can interfere with some test results. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or other regular medicine use. Do not use if allergic to any ingredient.

What is it used for?
This combination is generally used as supportive treatment for liver health and in some liver-related conditions. It may also help provide B vitamins and selenium when nutritional support is needed.

How does it work?
Silymarin provides antioxidant support for liver cells. L-ornithine L-aspartate supports the body's processing of ammonia, while the vitamins and selenium support normal energy metabolism and antioxidant functions.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or as stated on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount. The dose and duration depend on the individual's condition.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, vomiting or headache may occur. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Use under medical advice if there is liver disease, severe kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about all other medicines and supplements being used. Avoid taking additional selenium or vitamin supplements unless advised, as excessive intake can be harmful.

What is it used for?
Used to help stimulate appetite in people with poor appetite and support nutritional intake and weight gain when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Cyproheptadine blocks certain histamine and serotonin effects and may increase appetite. Tricholine citrate provides choline, while sorbitol helps give the solution its liquid form and may have a mild laxative effect.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth only as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Measure the solution accurately using a suitable measuring device and do not take more than prescribed.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, increased appetite, nausea, stomach discomfort and loose motions or diarrhoea.

Precautions
May cause sleepiness or reduced alertness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Use cautiously in glaucoma, urinary retention, asthma, liver or kidney problems, and in older adults. Sorbitol may cause diarrhoea and should be avoided or used only with medical advice in hereditary fructose intolerance. Seek medical advice if excessive sleepiness, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
This multipurpose pain-relief bag is used to provide temporary relief from body aches and localised muscle or joint pain.

How does it work?
It provides therapeutic warmth or cooling to the painful area, which may help soothe discomfort.

How to take/use it
Use it only as directed on the product packaging. Apply to the affected area for the recommended period, preferably with a cloth between the bag and skin. Do not use if the bag is damaged or leaking.

Common side effects
Prolonged or direct contact may cause skin redness, irritation, burns or cold injury.

Precautions
Do not apply to broken, infected, numb or very sensitive skin. Avoid excessive heat or cold and do not sleep while using it. Stop use if significant discomfort or a skin reaction occurs. Seek medical advice for severe, persistent or unexplained pain.

What is it used for?
Used to moisturise dry skin and help support the skin’s natural protective barrier.

How does it work?
Ceramides and squalane help replenish skin lipids, while hyaluronic acid and panthenol help attract and retain moisture. This helps soften and hydrate the skin.

How to take/use it
Apply to clean, dry skin as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild irritation, stinging, redness or itching may occur in some people.

Precautions
For external use only. Stop use if significant irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
This nutritional supplement is used to support male reproductive health and sperm health. It provides antioxidant nutrients that may help protect cells from oxidative stress.

How does it work?
Coenzyme Q10, selenium, lycopene and vitamin E act as antioxidants. Zinc and L-arginine support normal reproductive function and other normal body processes.

How to take/use it
Swallow the capsule with water and follow the dose and duration stated on the product label or recommended by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, heartburn or headache may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if taking blood-pressure medicines, nitrates, blood thinners such as warfarin, diabetes medicines or medicines for erectile dysfunction. Use cautiously with kidney or liver disease. Stop use and seek medical help if an allergic reaction or severe symptoms occur.

What is it used for?
This nutritional supplement is generally used to support male reproductive health, including sperm health and fertility. It should not be considered a treatment for infertility unless recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It combines amino acids, vitamins, minerals and plant-based ingredients that may support antioxidant protection, energy production and normal reproductive function. The benefits of some herbal ingredients may vary between individuals.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If it is supplied as a sachet, use it according to the preparation instructions on the pack.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness or drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney, liver, thyroid, autoimmune or heart disease, low blood pressure, diabetes, or if medicines are being taken for blood pressure, diabetes, blood clotting or heart conditions. Stop use and seek medical help if an allergic reaction or severe symptoms occur.

What is it used for?
Used for routine care and conditioning of the hair and scalp. It may help improve hair softness, smoothness and manageability and reduce the feeling of dryness.

How does it work?
Hydrolysed rice protein can form a light conditioning film on the hair, while vitamin E and the plant extracts provide emollient and antioxidant support. This helps improve the feel and appearance of the hair.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to clean, dry or damp hair and scalp as directed on the product label. Avoid using more than recommended, and do not apply to broken or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Mild scalp irritation, itching, redness or an allergic skin reaction may occur in sensitive individuals.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes. Perform a small patch test before first use, especially if the scalp is sensitive. Stop use if irritation or rash develops. Do not swallow.

What is it used for?
This topical skincare combination is used to improve the appearance of uneven skin tone, dark spots and dryness, while supporting smoother-looking skin. The exact approved use depends on the product formulation and label.

How does it work?
Its ingredients help moisturise the skin and may support a more even-looking complexion. Arbutin and kojic acid help reduce excess melanin formation, while retinyl palmitate supports skin renewal; titanium dioxide and zinc oxide may provide some physical protection from ultraviolet light when present in an appropriate sunscreen formulation.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to clean, dry skin as directed on the product label. Avoid the eyes, lips and broken or irritated skin. Do not use more often or in larger amounts than recommended. A patch test is advisable before regular use.

Common side effects
Mild redness, dryness, itching, burning or skin irritation may occur, especially in sensitive skin.

Precautions
Stop use if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops. Avoid contact with the eyes and rinse with water if contact occurs. Use sun protection during the day, as some ingredients may increase sensitivity to sunlight. People who are pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding should seek medical advice before use because it contains a vitamin A derivative.

What is it used for?
This nutritional supplement provides lutein, zeaxanthin, antioxidant vitamins and minerals to support eye health. It may be used as part of nutritional support for the macular area of the eye, but it should not replace treatment prescribed for an eye condition.

How does it work?
Lutein and zeaxanthin are pigments found in the eye that help filter light. Vitamins C and E, zinc, copper, manganese and selenium support antioxidant protection and normal eye function.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach discomfort.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Mild nausea, stomach upset or other digestive discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Check with a doctor or pharmacist before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or use of other vitamin or mineral supplements. Avoid taking more than the recommended amount. Seek medical advice for new or worsening vision changes, eye pain or sudden loss of vision.

What is it used for?
Ferric carboxymaltose injection is used to treat iron-deficiency anaemia and replenish low iron levels, especially when oral iron is not suitable, has not worked well, or iron needs to be replaced quickly.

How does it work?
It supplies iron to the body. Iron is then used to make haemoglobin, the part of red blood cells that carries oxygen.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by intravenous injection or infusion by a healthcare professional. The dose and number of treatments depend on iron levels, haemoglobin, body weight and medical condition. It must not be self-injected.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, dizziness, flushing, temporary changes in blood pressure, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur. Low phosphate levels can occur, particularly after repeated or high-dose treatment.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about any previous reaction to intravenous iron, iron overload, or other medical conditions. Medical supervision is required during administration and for at least 30 minutes afterwards because serious allergic reactions can rarely occur. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, fainting or severe rash. The injection should only be used when iron deficiency has been confirmed.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron and folic acid deficiency, including deficiency-related anaemia, when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Iron helps the body make haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood. Folic acid supports the formation of healthy red blood cells.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device. Do not take more than recommended, as iron overdose can be dangerous. Follow medical advice about taking it with food or other medicines.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and dark or black stools may occur.

Precautions
Keep out of reach of children; accidental iron overdose can be life-threatening. Tell the doctor if there is unexplained anaemia, a history of iron overload, or vitamin B12 deficiency. Iron may interact with some medicines and can reduce the absorption of certain medicines; ask a doctor or pharmacist about suitable spacing. Seek medical help for severe stomach pain, repeated vomiting, bloody stools, or signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This nutritional supplement helps prevent or correct iron and folate deficiencies and supports the formation of healthy red blood cells. It also provides vitamin B12, vitamin C, zinc, copper and vitamin B6.

How does it work?
Iron, folate and vitamin B12 are needed to make red blood cells and haemoglobin. Vitamin C helps the body absorb iron, while zinc, copper and vitamin B6 support normal body functions.

How to take/use it
Take the tablet with water as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. If it causes stomach upset, taking it with food may help. Keep iron-containing products out of reach of children.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, diarrhoea and dark-coloured stools may occur.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional about any medical conditions or other medicines being taken. Iron may interact with antacids, calcium supplements, some antibiotics and thyroid medicines; these may need to be taken at different times. Do not use it to treat unexplained anaemia without medical advice. Seek urgent help after taking more than the recommended amount, especially in a child.

What is it used for?
Used to help prevent or treat nutritional anaemia caused by low iron, folic acid or vitamin B12. It may also support red blood cell formation and nutritional needs in women.

How does it work?
Iron, folic acid and vitamin B12 provide nutrients needed to make healthy red blood cells and haemoglobin. Moringa, ashoka and shatavari are herbal ingredients commonly included in women’s nutritional supplements.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Iron supplements may be better tolerated with food if they cause stomach upset.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, diarrhoea and dark-coloured stools may occur.

Precautions
Keep out of reach of children, as an iron overdose can be dangerous. Consult a healthcare professional if anaemia has not been diagnosed, symptoms continue, or there is unusual bleeding. Tell the healthcare professional about all medicines and supplements being taken, as iron can interact with some medicines.

What is it used for?
This supplement helps prevent or treat iron and folic acid deficiencies, including iron-deficiency anaemia, when recommended by a healthcare professional. It also provides zinc, which may help correct zinc deficiency.

How does it work?
Iron is needed to make haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood. Folic acid supports the formation of healthy blood cells, while zinc supports normal immune function and other body processes.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow with water. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Avoid taking it at the same time as tea, coffee, milk, calcium supplements or antacids, as these may reduce iron absorption.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, diarrhoea and dark-coloured stools. Zinc may sometimes cause nausea or a metallic taste.

Precautions
Do not take iron supplements unless advised if there is a risk of iron overload or if the anaemia is not due to iron deficiency. Keep out of reach of children, as accidental iron overdose can be dangerous. Tell a healthcare professional about other medicines or supplements being taken. Folic acid may mask vitamin B12 deficiency; medical advice is important if vitamin B12 deficiency is possible.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat fungal infections that cause inflammation, redness or itching. It should be used only when recommended by a healthcare professional, as the steroid component may worsen some rashes or infections.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole stops the growth of fungi. Beclomethasone reduces inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
Apply to clean, dry skin only as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, itching, irritation, dryness or redness at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning or skin-colour changes.

Precautions
For external use only. Do not use on the face, groin, skin folds, broken skin or under bandages unless specifically advised. Avoid prolonged or unsupervised use. Do not use for an undiagnosed rash. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens, spreads or does not improve as expected.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch, pityriasis versicolor and some yeast infections of the skin. It may also be used for seborrhoeic dermatitis when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It is an antifungal medicine that blocks the production of substances fungi need to grow and survive, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin and use it exactly as directed on the label or by the doctor. Wash hands before and after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole or any ingredient in the cream. Avoid applying it to the eyes or inside the mouth. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs. Consult a doctor if the infection worsens or does not improve as expected.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to help treat fungal skin infections and fungal-related conditions such as dandruff or seborrhoeic dermatitis.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, helping control fungal growth. Cetrimide is an antiseptic that helps reduce microorganisms on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Wet the affected skin, apply the soap and work into a lather, then rinse thoroughly. Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes and rinse immediately if contact occurs.

Common side effects
Skin irritation, burning, itching, dryness or redness may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole, cetrimide or any ingredient. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or a widespread rash occurs.

What is it used for?
Used to treat dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis, which can cause flaky, itchy or oily scalp. It may also be used for certain fungal skin infections when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole and zinc pyrithione help reduce the growth of fungi on the skin and scalp, helping relieve flaking and itching.

How to take/use it
Use on the scalp or affected skin exactly as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Apply to wet hair or affected skin, gently lather, and rinse well. Avoid contact with the eyes; rinse thoroughly with water if contact occurs.

Common side effects
Scalp or skin irritation, itching, burning, dryness, or changes in hair texture.

Precautions
For external use only. Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole, zinc pyrithione or any ingredient. Avoid contact with the eyes and broken skin. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs, or if symptoms do not improve.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to help treat superficial fungal infections, such as fungal rashes. Use only for the condition advised by a doctor or stated on the product label.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole is an antifungal medicine that stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, helping control the infection. Glycerin helps moisturise the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Wet the skin, apply the soap to form a lather, gently wash the affected area and rinse well. Follow the product label or the doctor's instructions. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, burning, itching, redness or dryness may occur at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole or any ingredient. Avoid applying to severely irritated, broken or injured skin unless advised by a doctor. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement providing leucine, an essential amino acid, and vitamin B6 in its active form. It may help support normal protein and energy metabolism, but it is not a treatment for a specific disease.

How does it work?
Leucine is used by the body to help build proteins. Pyridoxal-5-phosphate, the active form of vitamin B6, supports protein, carbohydrate and fat metabolism.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, nausea or bloating may occur.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney or liver disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding or use of other vitamin or amino-acid supplements. Stop use and seek medical advice if unusual numbness or tingling develops.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin for fungal infections that may also have bacterial infection or inflammation, such as infected, itchy and irritated skin rashes. Use only when prescribed or recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole treats fungal infection, while neomycin acts against certain bacteria. Beclomethasone reduces redness, swelling and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin as directed by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not cover the area tightly unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation at the application site. Prolonged or repeated use may cause skin thinning or other skin changes.

Precautions
Do not use on untreated viral skin infections, wounds or broken skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Avoid prolonged use, large areas of skin and use on the face, groin or skin folds unless specifically prescribed. Stop using it and seek medical advice if the rash worsens, severe irritation develops or there is no improvement. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole 1% Soap is used on the skin to help treat fungal skin infections, such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and other superficial fungal infections.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole is an antifungal medicine that damages the protective outer layer of fungal cells, helping stop their growth.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use on the affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and wash hands after use.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, burning, itching, dryness or peeling may occur where it is applied.

Precautions
Do not use on the eyes or inside the body. Avoid applying to severely irritated or broken skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs, or if the infection does not improve.

What is it used for?
This cream is used to help reduce the appearance of dark spots, uneven skin tone and hyperpigmentation, including marks left after skin inflammation. It is intended for external use on the skin.

How does it work?
Kojic acid and arbutin help reduce melanin production, while glycolic acid gently removes dead skin cells. Niacinamide may help improve uneven skin tone, and aloe vera helps soothe the skin.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips and broken or irritated skin. Use sunscreen during the day, as sun exposure can worsen pigmentation.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, redness, dryness, itching, peeling or skin irritation may occur.

Precautions
For external use only. Patch-test before wider use. Stop using it if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops. Avoid using it together with other strong exfoliating or irritating skin products unless advised by a healthcare professional. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Used to help reduce the appearance of dark spots, hyperpigmentation and uneven skin tone.

How does it work?
Kojic acid helps reduce melanin production by inhibiting an enzyme involved in skin pigmentation. Vitamin C and vitamin E provide antioxidant support.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use the soap as directed on the product label, then rinse thoroughly. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not use on broken or irritated skin. A small patch test is advisable before regular use.

Common side effects
Dryness, redness, itching, burning or skin irritation may occur.

Precautions
Stop use if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops. Avoid contact with the eyes. Use sun protection during treatment, as sun exposure can worsen dark spots. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Colostrum capsules are dietary supplements used to provide naturally occurring proteins and antibodies, mainly for general immune and digestive support. They are not a substitute for treatment of an infection or other medical condition.

How does it work?
Colostrum contains immunoglobulins, lactoferrin and other proteins that may support normal immune and intestinal function.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth with water and follow the dose and directions on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause mild stomach discomfort, nausea, bloating or loose stools.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to milk or milk proteins. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or ongoing treatment. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
The specific therapeutic use cannot be determined from the available information about this peptide-based diet powder.

How does it work?
Its mechanism of action cannot be reliably explained without details about the product's ingredients and intended use.

How to take/use it
Follow the instructions on the product packaging or as advised by a qualified healthcare professional. Do not use it without checking the ingredients and recommended directions.

Common side effects
Cannot be identified reliably without the complete ingredient list and product information.

Precautions
Check the full ingredients before use. Seek advice from a healthcare professional if pregnant, breastfeeding, managing a medical condition, or taking other medicines. Do not use if the product details or directions are unclear.

What is it used for?
This herbal combination is commonly used to support breast milk production in breastfeeding women. Evidence for its effectiveness may be limited, and it should not replace advice for breastfeeding or low milk supply problems.

How does it work?
Asparagus racemosus, fenugreek and fennel are traditionally used as herbal galactagogues, which are substances believed to support lactation. The exact way they may work is not fully established.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, gas or diarrhoea may occur. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice before use if there is diabetes, a bleeding disorder, an allergy to legumes or fennel-family plants, or if blood-thinning or blood-sugar-lowering medicines are being taken. Stop use and seek help for signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Lansoprazole injection reduces excess stomach acid. It is used for acid-related conditions such as heartburn, gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and stomach or intestinal ulcers, particularly when medicine by mouth is not suitable.

How does it work?
It is a proton pump inhibitor that blocks the stomach’s final step of acid production, helping reduce irritation and allowing acid-related damage to heal.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. It should not be self-injected. The dose and duration depend on the condition and medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, constipation or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to lansoprazole or other acid-reducing medicines, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Inform the doctor about all medicines being used, especially warfarin, digoxin, methotrexate or medicines for HIV. Seek medical help for severe diarrhoea, swelling, breathing difficulty or a serious skin reaction. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Letrozole is mainly used to treat hormone-sensitive breast cancer, especially in women after menopause. It may also be prescribed by fertility specialists to help induce ovulation in some women.

How does it work?
Letrozole reduces the production of oestrogen in the body. This can slow the growth of some breast cancers and may help stimulate ovulation when used for fertility treatment.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. When used for fertility, follow the specialist's exact treatment instructions.

Common side effects
Hot flushes, increased sweating, tiredness, headache, dizziness, nausea, mood changes, and joint, muscle or bone pain may occur.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about liver or kidney problems, weak bones or osteoporosis, high cholesterol, or other medicines being taken. Long-term treatment may affect bone strength and may require monitoring. Seek medical help for severe allergic symptoms, chest pain, sudden weakness, or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
This capsule is used as supportive care for liver health and may be recommended in some liver-related conditions. It should not replace medical evaluation or treatment for liver disease.

How does it work?
Silymarin may help protect liver cells from oxidative damage. Lecithin and choline support normal fat metabolism and liver function.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Swallow the capsule with water and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, bloating or headache may occur. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use if there is liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or allergy to milk thistle or related plants. Seek medical advice before using it with other medicines, as interactions may occur. It is not a substitute for treatment of hepatitis or other serious liver conditions.

What is it used for?
Milk Thistle and Choline is a nutritional supplement commonly used to support normal liver function and fat metabolism in the liver. It is not a substitute for treatment of liver disease.

How does it work?
Milk thistle provides silymarin, which has antioxidant activity. Choline is an essential nutrient involved in the normal transport and metabolism of fats in the liver.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause stomach upset, bloating or diarrhoea. Milk thistle may rarely cause an allergic reaction, especially in people allergic to ragweed-family plants.

Precautions

What is it used for?

It blocks the action of a substance called angiotensin II, which normally narrows blood vessels. This helps relax the blood vessels and lower blood pressure.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
Losartan relaxes blood vessels by blocking the action of angiotensin II, a substance that raises blood pressure. Hydrochlorothiazide helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water through urine, which also lowers blood pressure.

Precautions

Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Blood pressure, kidney function, and electrolyte levels may need monitoring. What is it used for?

It stops the growth of fungi by interfering with the production of an important part of the fungal cell membrane.
