Used to supplement calcium and vitamin D, helping maintain normal bones and teeth and prevent or treat deficiency when recommended.

How does it work?
Calcium provides the mineral needed for bones, teeth and normal muscle and nerve function. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium from the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Constipation, stomach discomfort, bloating or nausea.

Precautions
Ask a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels or excess vitamin D. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, including iron, thyroid medicines and certain antibiotics; these may need to be taken at separate times. Seek medical advice if severe nausea, vomiting, unusual thirst or frequent urination occurs.

What is it used for?
Used to supplement calcium and active vitamin D, helping support bone strength and calcium absorption. It may also help provide nutrients such as vitamin B12, folic acid and omega-3 fatty acids when dietary intake is inadequate.

How does it work?
Calcium and calcitriol, an active form of vitamin D, help the body absorb and use calcium for normal bones and muscles. Vitamin B12 and folic acid support normal blood-cell and nerve function, while omega-3 fatty acids provide nutritional support.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Calcium carbonate is generally better absorbed with food. Swallow the softgel with water and do not combine it with other calcium or vitamin D products unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Constipation, bloating, nausea or stomach discomfort may occur. Fishy aftertaste or burping may occur because of the omega-3 component.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels or vitamin D-related disorders. Avoid taking additional calcium or vitamin D without medical advice. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, including iron supplements, thyroid medicines and certain antibiotics; separate dosing may be needed. Seek medical advice for persistent vomiting, unusual thirst, frequent urination, confusion or severe weakness.

What is it used for?
This supplement provides calcium and vitamin D to help maintain healthy bones and teeth and support the body's calcium needs. It may be used to help prevent or treat calcium or vitamin D deficiency when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Calcium is needed for strong bones and teeth and for normal muscle and nerve function. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the package or by a healthcare professional. Swallow with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Tell a doctor or pharmacist about other medicines being taken, as calcium can affect the absorption of some medicines.

Common side effects
Constipation, gas, bloating, nausea or stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels or excessive vitamin D levels. Avoid taking additional calcium or vitamin D supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
This nutritional supplement provides calcium, vitamin D3, vitamin K2, magnesium and zinc to support normal bone and teeth health and help supplement dietary deficiencies.

How does it work?
Calcium and vitamin D help build and maintain bones, while vitamin K2 supports the normal use of calcium in bone. Magnesium and zinc support normal bone and mineral functions.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label, preferably with water. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Keep a suitable gap from other medicines if advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Some people may experience nausea, stomach upset, constipation or diarrhoea. Excessive intake may cause high calcium levels or other mineral-related problems.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels or other mineral disorders. Vitamin K2 may interact with warfarin and similar blood thinners. Calcium and magnesium can affect the absorption of some medicines, including certain antibiotics, thyroid medicines and iron supplements; ask a doctor or pharmacist about suitable timing. Do not combine with other calcium or vitamin D products unless advised.

What is it used for?
Used to provide calcium, calcitriol and other minerals that support normal bone and teeth health, and to help prevent or treat calcium or vitamin D deficiency when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It supplies elemental calcium and minerals needed for bone and muscle function. Calcitriol, an active form of vitamin D, helps the body absorb calcium from the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take additional calcium or vitamin D supplements without medical advice. Separate it from certain medicines, such as thyroid medicines, antibiotics and osteoporosis medicines, as advised by a pharmacist or doctor.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort or bloating. Excess calcium may cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness or confusion.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high blood calcium, or disorders affecting vitamin D or mineral levels. Because it contains calcitriol, use should be medically supervised. Seek medical help if severe vomiting, confusion, marked weakness or irregular heartbeat occurs.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn, indigestion and discomfort caused by excess gas or bloating.

How does it work?
Magaldrate neutralises excess stomach acid. Simethicone helps gas bubbles combine and pass more easily, reducing bloating and discomfort.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth as directed on the label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Shake the suspension well before use and measure it carefully. Avoid taking it at the same time as other medicines; ask a pharmacist about the appropriate time gap.

Common side effects
Constipation or diarrhoea, nausea, stomach discomfort, or an altered/chalky taste may occur.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, keep returning, or do not improve. Do not use for prolonged periods without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Levosulpiride injection is used to relieve nausea and vomiting and to improve symptoms caused by slow movement of food through the stomach, such as indigestion, bloating and early fullness. It is generally used when an injection is needed.

How does it work?
It blocks certain dopamine receptors and helps increase movement of the upper digestive system. This can help food pass through the stomach more normally and reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or nurse. The dose and duration depend on the condition being treated and should be decided by the healthcare professional. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, headache, restlessness, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea or constipation may occur. Increased prolactin levels can sometimes cause breast tenderness or menstrual changes.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, heart rhythm problems, kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. It may not be suitable in gastrointestinal bleeding, blockage or perforation, or in people with prolactin-dependent conditions. Avoid driving if drowsy or dizzy. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, abnormal heartbeats, severe muscle stiffness, unusual involuntary movements or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This cream is used for inflamed skin conditions that have, or may have, a bacterial infection, such as infected eczema or dermatitis. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Fluticasone reduces skin inflammation, redness and itching. Mupirocin stops the growth of susceptible bacteria on the skin.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before and after use, unless treating the hands. For external use only. Avoid the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not cover the area with a tight dressing unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, dryness, redness or irritation at the application site. Prolonged or excessive use may cause skin thinning or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Do not use on fungal or viral skin infections unless specifically advised. Avoid prolonged use or application to the face, skin folds or large areas unless prescribed. Stop using it and seek medical advice if the infection worsens, the skin becomes severely irritated, or there is swelling or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Mupirocin 2% ointment is a topical antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial skin infections, such as impetigo and infected minor cuts, wounds or abrasions.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, helping control the infection.

How to take/use it
Use on the skin only and apply a thin layer to the affected area as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Clean and dry the area first, and wash hands before and after use. Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to mupirocin. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, rash or swelling occurs. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve. Avoid applying it to large areas or using it for longer than recommended. Do not swallow it.

What is it used for?
This is an amino acid supplement that provides L-arginine and L-citrulline. It may help support nitric oxide production and healthy blood flow, but it should not replace treatment prescribed for a medical condition.

How does it work?
L-citrulline is converted in the body to L-arginine. These amino acids help the body produce nitric oxide, which relaxes blood vessels and supports blood flow.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Stomach discomfort, nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness or flushing may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is low blood pressure, kidney or liver disease, or a history of heart problems. It may further lower blood pressure when taken with blood-pressure medicines, nitrates or medicines for erectile dysfunction. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to provide L-arginine, an amino acid, and vitamin B6 when additional dietary support is needed. The specific medical use should be based on a healthcare professional’s advice.

How does it work?
L-arginine is used by the body to produce nitric oxide, which helps blood vessels relax. Vitamin B6 supports normal protein metabolism and nervous system function.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Mix or dissolve the granules as instructed. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, bloating, headache or dizziness.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney or liver disease, low blood pressure, heart disease, or a history of recurrent herpes infections. Consult a healthcare professional if pregnant or breastfeeding, or if taking medicines for blood pressure, nitrates or erectile dysfunction. Stop use and seek medical help for severe dizziness, allergic reactions or persistent side effects.

What is it used for?
L-Arginine is an amino acid supplement used to provide additional arginine when needed. The specific purpose of this product cannot be confirmed from the available information alone.

How does it work?
Arginine is used by the body to produce nitric oxide, which helps relax and widen blood vessels. It also supports normal protein production and other body functions.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow the tablet with water and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating, diarrhoea, headache or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is low blood pressure, kidney or liver disease, asthma, or a recent heart attack. It may further lower blood pressure when taken with blood-pressure medicines, nitrates or medicines for erectile dysfunction. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding or in children.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 200 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops bacteria from making the genetic material they need to grow and survive, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or mineral supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, iron or calcium; follow the spacing instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, headache, dizziness and sleep disturbances.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ofloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, mood or nerve-related changes, an irregular heartbeat, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only under medical advice, especially during pregnancy, breastfeeding, in children, or if there is a history of tendon problems, seizures, heart rhythm problems or kidney disease.

What is it used for?
This cream is used under medical guidance for inflamed skin infections caused by fungi, sometimes with a bacterial infection. It may help relieve redness, swelling, itching and irritation along with treating the infection.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole and tolnaftate act against fungi, while gentamicin acts against certain bacteria. Clobetasol reduces inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not cover the area with a bandage or dressing unless advised.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, itching, irritation, redness or dryness at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice, as clobetasol is a strong steroid. Avoid the eyes, face, groin, armpits and broken skin unless specifically prescribed. Do not use for undiagnosed rashes or viral skin infections. Avoid prolonged use or use over large areas. Stop and seek medical advice if the infection worsens, spreads, or causes severe irritation or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used to treat certain bacterial or protozoal infections of the intestine that may cause diarrhoea or dysentery. Simethicone helps relieve associated gas, bloating and abdominal discomfort. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin and metronidazole act against certain bacteria and protozoa causing intestinal infections. Simethicone helps gas bubbles combine and pass more easily.

How to take/use it
Use only in the dose and for the duration prescribed. Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with an oral syringe or measuring spoon. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise. Do not self-medicate for diarrhoea.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain or discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, metallic taste and indigestion may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver or kidney problems, seizures, or a history of tendon or nerve problems. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for a severe allergic reaction, tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, or bloody or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat certain mixed bacterial and protozoal infections, especially infectious diarrhoea and dysentery, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin stops the growth of susceptible bacteria. Ornidazole acts against certain protozoa and anaerobic bacteria that can cause intestinal infections.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not take it with alcohol during treatment and for at least 3 days after the last dose. Do not self-medicate for diarrhoea, as some cases do not require antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and a metallic or unpleasant taste.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ofloxacin, other quinolone antibiotics, ornidazole, or similar medicines. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, confusion, seizures, or a serious allergic reaction. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney or liver problems, seizures, or previous tendon problems. Avoid driving if dizzy or drowsy.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 50 mg/5 ml suspension is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the enzymes they need to grow and multiply, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Shake the suspension well before each use and measure it with an oral syringe or measuring spoon. Complete the prescribed course unless a doctor advises otherwise. Do not share this medicine.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ofloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics. Use in children only when specifically prescribed. Stop using it and seek medical advice for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, allergic symptoms, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizzy or less alert.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to soothe itching, irritation and minor rashes, including irritation from insect bites, mild sunburn and other minor skin discomforts.

How does it work?
Calamine and zinc oxide form a protective layer that helps soothe irritated skin and reduce discomfort. Aloe vera and light liquid paraffin help moisturise and protect the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Shake well if instructed on the label, then apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin as directed by the product label or a healthcare professional. Wash hands after use. Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Common side effects
Mild dryness, stinging or skin irritation may occur. Stop use if a rash or other signs of allergy develop.

Precautions
Do not apply to the eyes, inside the mouth, deep wounds or severely damaged skin. Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Seek medical advice if the irritation worsens, shows signs of infection or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Used to help lighten dark patches and areas of uneven skin pigmentation, such as dark spots. The exact suitability depends on the product formulation and the cause of the pigmentation.

How does it work?
Hydroquinone reduces the production of melanin, the pigment that gives skin its colour. The soap base helps cleanse the skin, while titanium dioxide provides opacity.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips and other sensitive areas, and do not apply to broken or irritated skin. Do not use for prolonged periods unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Skin dryness, redness, burning, stinging, itching or irritation.

Precautions
Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, blistering or worsening skin discolouration occurs. Patch-test before wider use. Avoid using with other irritating skin products unless advised. Hydroquinone should not be used continuously or on large areas without medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Potassium citrate and citric acid syrup is used to make urine less acidic and help prevent or manage certain kidney stones, especially uric acid and cystine stones. It may also be prescribed for other conditions involving excess urine acidity.

How does it work?
It increases urinary citrate and makes the urine more alkaline. This can help reduce the formation of certain kidney stones.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Measure the syrup with a proper measuring device. Follow the product instructions about diluting it with water and taking it with or after food. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, abdominal pain, diarrhoea or loose motions, and indigestion may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is kidney disease, high potassium levels, heart disease, or dehydration. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially potassium supplements, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, potassium-sparing diuretics, or other medicines that can increase potassium. Seek medical help for severe weakness, tingling, confusion, or an irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Hydroxyzine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as itching, hives and skin rashes. It may also be prescribed for short-term relief of anxiety or to cause drowsiness before a procedure, depending on medical advice.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. It also slows activity in the brain, which can cause a calming and drowsy effect.

How to take/use it
Take this tablet only as prescribed. Swallow it with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, headache, constipation and tiredness.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and other medicines that cause drowsiness unless advised by a doctor. Use cautiously if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, heart rhythm problems, or liver or kidney disease. Older adults may be more sensitive to its sedating effects. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, fainting, breathing difficulty or a serious allergic reaction. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
A topical skin-care cream used to moisturise the skin and support a brighter, healthier-looking appearance. It may be used as part of routine care for dull or uneven-looking skin.

How does it work?
Glutathione and ascorbic acid have antioxidant properties that may help protect skin from oxidative stress. Collagen peptides help condition the skin.

How to take/use it
Apply a small amount to clean, dry skin as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not apply to broken or irritated skin. Perform a patch test before wider use.

Common side effects
Mild irritation, redness, itching, burning or dryness may occur at the application site.

Precautions
Stop use if severe irritation, swelling or rash develops. Avoid contact with the eyes. People with sensitive skin should use it cautiously and perform a patch test first. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
This topical serum is used as part of skincare to help brighten dull or uneven-looking skin, provide hydration and support the appearance of fine lines and sun-related skin changes.

How does it work?
Vitamin C and ferulic acid provide antioxidant support, while hyaluronic acid helps retain moisture in the skin. Aloe vera and D-panthenol help soothe and moisturise the skin.

How to take/use it
Apply a small amount to clean, dry skin as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes. Use sunscreen during the day, especially when using products containing vitamin C.

Common side effects
Mild stinging, redness, irritation, dryness or itching may occur, particularly on sensitive skin.

Precautions
Patch test before first use. Stop using it if severe or persistent irritation occurs. Avoid applying to broken or irritated skin and avoid contact with the eyes. Store as directed on the product label.

What is it used for?
Used to reduce melasma and other areas of excess skin pigmentation, such as dark facial patches. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Hydroquinone reduces melanin production, while tretinoin helps increase skin-cell turnover. Mometasone reduces inflammation and irritation.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected pigmented areas exactly as directed by the prescriber. Avoid the eyes, lips, broken skin and inside of the nose. Wash hands after applying. Use sun protection during treatment, as sunlight can worsen pigmentation.

Common side effects
Redness, burning, stinging, dryness, peeling, itching or irritation at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, acne-like changes or worsening skin discolouration.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision and do not apply for longer than advised. Avoid using on large areas, broken skin or under airtight coverings. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, blistering or marked skin discolouration occurs. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor; consult a doctor before use while breastfeeding. Keep away from children.

What is it used for?
This serum is used to help reduce the appearance of dark spots, uneven skin tone and hyperpigmentation, and to improve overall skin brightness.

How does it work?
Alpha arbutin, niacinamide and 3-O-ethyl ascorbic acid help reduce the formation and transfer of excess melanin, while glutathione provides antioxidant support. Together, these ingredients may help improve uneven pigmentation over time.

How to take/use it
Apply to clean, dry skin as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes and use sunscreen during the day. Patch-test before regular use, especially if the skin is sensitive.

Common side effects
Mild stinging, redness, dryness or skin irritation may occur, particularly in sensitive skin.

Precautions
For external use only. Stop using it if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin. Keep away from children and avoid contact with the eyes.

What is it used for?
Used to help reduce dark patches and uneven skin pigmentation. Hydroquinone is a skin-lightening ingredient; the exact indication and suitability depend on the product label and formulation.

How does it work?
Hydroquinone reduces the production of melanin, the pigment that gives skin its colour. Titanium dioxide provides an opaque, protective coating but does not replace sunscreen.

How to take/use it
Use only on the affected skin and exactly as directed on the product label. If it is a soap, lather gently and rinse thoroughly. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips and broken or irritated skin. Do not use more often or for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Dryness, stinging, itching, redness or skin irritation may occur.

Precautions
Avoid prolonged or unsupervised use of hydroquinone, as it can rarely cause persistent dark bluish-black skin discolouration. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops. Protect treated skin from sunlight, as sun exposure can worsen pigmentation. Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary supplement to provide glutathione, vitamin C and zinc. These nutrients support antioxidant protection and normal immune function, and help maintain normal cellular functions.

How does it work?
Glutathione and vitamin C act as antioxidants that help protect cells from oxidative damage. Zinc supports normal immune function and several body processes.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, stomach discomfort or loose motions. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones or any other medical condition. Ask about possible interactions if taking antibiotics, penicillamine or other medicines. Avoid taking additional zinc or vitamin C supplements unless advised.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary source of protein to help supplement protein intake when dietary protein is insufficient or increased protein is needed.

How does it work?
Soy protein isolate and skimmed milk powder provide proteins that are digested into amino acids, which the body uses for tissue maintenance and repair.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label. Mix with the recommended food or drink, and do not exceed the stated serving. It should supplement, not replace, a balanced diet.

Common side effects
Bloating, gas, stomach discomfort, nausea, diarrhoea or constipation may occur, especially in people sensitive to milk or soy products.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to soy or milk proteins. People with lactose intolerance may experience digestive symptoms. Those with kidney disease or other conditions requiring protein restriction should seek medical advice before use. Stop using and seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction, such as swelling, breathing difficulty or widespread rash.

What is it used for?
Used to supplement calcium and vitamin D intake and support the normal maintenance of bones and teeth. Vitamin K2 also supports normal bone-related processes.

How does it work?
Calcium provides a mineral needed for bones and teeth, while vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium. Vitamin K2 helps activate proteins involved in bone health.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Check with a healthcare professional if using other calcium, vitamin D or vitamin K supplements.

Common side effects
May include constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort or bloating. Excessive calcium intake may cause high calcium levels.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels or other medical conditions. Vitamin K2 may interact with warfarin and other blood-thinning medicines. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, including thyroid medicines, iron and certain antibiotics; ask a pharmacist about suitable spacing.

What is it used for?
Methylcobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 used to prevent or treat vitamin B12 deficiency. It may also help manage nerve-related symptoms associated with low vitamin B12, such as tingling or numbness.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamin B12, which is needed for healthy red blood cell formation and normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water, and do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, headache, or skin rash may occur. Seek medical advice if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to methylcobalamin or any ingredient in the tablet. Consult a doctor if symptoms continue, worsen, or if vitamin B12 deficiency has not been confirmed. Tell the doctor about other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
This combination helps provide B vitamins and alpha-lipoic acid. It is used to support normal nerve function and may help prevent or manage vitamin-related nerve problems when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Methylcobalamin, pyridoxine, folic acid and thiamine provide vitamins needed for healthy nerves and blood-cell formation. Alpha-lipoic acid acts as an antioxidant and supports nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take the capsule exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow it with water and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, headache or diarrhoea may occur. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use if there is diabetes, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or a history of vitamin B12 deficiency. Alpha-lipoic acid may affect blood sugar and could interact with diabetes medicines. Long-term or excessive use of vitamin B6 can cause nerve problems; do not take more than recommended.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve neuropathic (nerve-related) pain, which may feel like burning, tingling, shooting or electric-shock-like pain.

How does it work?
Pregabalin and nortriptyline help reduce abnormal pain signals in the nerves and brain. Methylcobalamin, a form of vitamin B12, supports normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, nausea, tiredness and weight gain.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful with other medicines that cause drowsiness. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, glaucoma, urinary retention, heart problems, depression or suicidal thoughts. Seek medical help for severe allergy, extreme sleepiness, breathing difficulty or new or worsening mood changes.

What is it used for?
Used mainly to relieve nerve pain, such as burning, tingling or shooting pain caused by irritated or damaged nerves. The vitamin ingredients support normal nerve function.

How does it work?
Pregabalin reduces the abnormal nerve signals that cause nerve pain. Methylcobalamin, pyridoxine, folic acid and benfotiamine provide nutrients involved in nerve health.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the capsule whole with water, with or without food. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, blurred vision, dry mouth, tiredness, nausea, swelling of the legs or feet and weight gain.

Precautions
Do not drive or operate machinery if dizzy or sleepy. Avoid alcohol, as it can increase drowsiness. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking other medicines that cause sleepiness. Seek medical help for severe swelling, breathing difficulty, serious allergic symptoms or unusual mood changes.

What is it used for?
Used as a moisturising skin-care lotion to support the skin barrier and help improve the appearance of dry, oily or uneven-looking skin.

How does it work?
Ceramides help support the skin’s protective barrier, while niacinamide helps maintain skin moisture and may help regulate excess oil. Zinc PCA and green tea extract provide additional skin-conditioning and antioxidant support.

How to take/use it
Apply a small amount to clean skin as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes. Patch test on a small area before wider use, especially if the skin is sensitive.

Common side effects
Mild stinging, redness, dryness, itching or irritation may occur, especially on sensitive skin.

Precautions
For external use only. Stop use if significant irritation, swelling or rash develops. Seek medical advice if the reaction is severe or does not improve. Avoid applying to broken or infected skin unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and discomfort from mouth ulcers, sore gums and other minor painful areas inside the mouth. It may also help relieve gum discomfort during teething when specifically suitable for the child.

How does it work?
Choline salicylate helps reduce pain and inflammation, while lignocaine temporarily numbs the area. Benzalkonium chloride helps limit the growth of some germs on the treated area.

How to take/use it
Apply a small amount to the affected area only as directed on the product label or by a doctor, dentist or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use. Avoid swallowing large amounts and take care not to bite or burn the numb area.

Common side effects
Temporary numbness, mild stinging or irritation at the application site. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to salicylates such as aspirin, lignocaine or any ingredient in the gel. Children under 16 years should use choline salicylate-containing oral gels only if specifically advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Avoid contact with the eyes. Seek dental or medical advice if symptoms are severe, keep returning or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Olmesartan medoxomil is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering blood pressure helps reduce the risk of serious problems such as stroke and heart disease.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of a hormone called angiotensin II, which normally narrows blood vessels. This helps blood vessels relax and lowers blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take this medicine exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and take it regularly. Do not stop treatment without medical advice, even if feeling well.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, diarrhoea, nausea and weakness may occur. Contact a doctor if diarrhoea is severe or persistent.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, liver disease, dehydration or high potassium levels. Olmesartan should not be used during pregnancy; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering blood pressure helps reduce the risk of serious problems such as stroke and heart disease.

How does it work?
Olmesartan blocks the action of a substance that narrows blood vessels. Amlodipine relaxes and widens blood vessels, helping blood flow more easily and lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop taking it or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, flushing, nausea, and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, dehydration, low blood pressure, or high potassium levels. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor. Do not use during pregnancy; seek medical advice promptly if pregnancy occurs. Seek urgent help for swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to provide protein, amino acids, vitamins, minerals and DHA when dietary intake may be inadequate. Its specific use depends on the product formulation and healthcare advice.

How does it work?
Protein and amino acids provide building blocks for body tissues. Vitamins, minerals, L-arginine and DHA support normal body functions and nutritional requirements.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Mix the powder as instructed and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, bloating, stomach discomfort or diarrhoea in some people.

Precautions
Check the ingredients for allergies, including milk, soy, fish or other sources that may be present. Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking regular medicines. Stop use and seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This tablet is a nutritional supplement containing antioxidant vitamins and minerals. It helps provide nutrients such as vitamins C and E, zinc, selenium, copper and folic acid when dietary intake may be insufficient.

How does it work?
Its vitamins and minerals support normal body functions. Lycopene and vitamins C and E have antioxidant activity, which helps protect cells from oxidative damage.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Avoid taking other supplements containing the same nutrients unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea or constipation may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if unusual or severe symptoms develop.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional about any medical conditions, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all medicines or supplements being taken. Do not exceed the recommended amount, as excessive intake of zinc, selenium, copper or vitamins can be harmful.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary supplement to provide omega-3, omega-6 and omega-9 fatty acids when dietary intake may be insufficient.

How does it work?
These fatty acids are used by the body as components of cell membranes and for normal body functions, including cell signalling and energy use.

How to take/use it
Take the softgel as directed on the product label, preferably with food. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Fishy aftertaste or burping, nausea, stomach discomfort, loose stools or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Check the ingredients if there is an allergy to fish, seafood, soy or other listed ingredients. Seek medical advice before use if taking blood thinners, having a bleeding disorder, or before surgery. Consult a healthcare professional during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary supplement to provide omega-3 fatty acids, which support normal heart, brain and overall body functions.

How does it work?
Omega-3 fatty acids are essential fats used by the body in cell membranes and other normal body processes. Certain omega-3 products may also help reduce high triglyceride levels when used under medical advice.

How to take/use it
Take the softgel with food and follow the product label or a healthcare professional’s instructions. Swallow it whole unless the label says otherwise.

Common side effects
Fishy taste or burping, nausea, indigestion, stomach discomfort or loose stools.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional before use if there is a fish allergy, a bleeding disorder, or use of blood-thinning medicines. Seek advice before taking high doses or before surgery. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

What is it used for?
This syrup is a nutritional supplement that provides multivitamins and omega-3 fatty acids to help meet daily nutritional needs when the diet may not provide enough.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamins and omega-3 fatty acids needed for normal body functions and general nutrition.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Measure the syrup with a proper measuring device and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, loose stools, or a fishy taste or aftertaste may occur.

Precautions
Check the ingredients before use if allergic to fish or seafood. Consult a healthcare professional before use if taking blood thinners, having a bleeding disorder, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid taking more than the recommended amount, as excessive intake of some vitamins can be harmful.

What is it used for?
Folic acid 5 mg is used to treat or prevent folate deficiency and related types of anaemia. It may also be prescribed during pregnancy to support the baby’s development and help prevent certain birth defects, when recommended by a doctor.

How does it work?
Folic acid is a form of vitamin B9 needed to make healthy red blood cells and for normal cell growth and development.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with water. It may be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, bloating, stomach discomfort or diarrhoea may occur. Skin rash or other allergic reactions are uncommon.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any vitamin B12 deficiency or unexplained anaemia, as folic acid can improve some blood findings while allowing nerve damage from B12 deficiency to progress. Seek medical help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty or a severe rash. Use the 5 mg strength during pregnancy only as advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
This supplement helps prevent or treat deficiencies of vitamin B12, folate and vitamin B6. These nutrients support healthy red blood cell formation and normal nerve function.

How does it work?
Methylcobalamin, L-methyl folate and pyridoxal-5-phosphate provide active forms of B12, folate and B6. They help support blood-cell production and the normal functioning of the nervous system.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea or headache may occur. Seek medical advice if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any vitamin B12, folate or vitamin B6 deficiency diagnosis, allergies, or other medicines being taken. Folic acid-containing products may improve anaemia while an underlying vitamin B12 deficiency continues to affect the nerves, so unexplained anaemia or numbness should be medically evaluated. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
This combination is used as a supplement in some fertility treatment plans, particularly to support ovarian function and reproductive health. Its suitability and benefits vary, so it should be used only under medical guidance.

How does it work?
Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) is a hormone precursor that can be converted into sex hormones. Melatonin helps regulate the sleep-wake cycle and has antioxidant activity, while ubiquinol supports energy production in cells.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a fertility specialist or other healthcare professional. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice. Melatonin may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or alcohol if affected.

Common side effects
Acne, oily skin, increased facial or body hair, mood or menstrual changes, drowsiness, headache, dizziness, nausea, stomach upset or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially during fertility treatment. Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised. Tell the doctor about hormone-sensitive conditions, polycystic ovary syndrome, liver problems, mood disorders, or medicines that cause drowsiness or affect hormones. Seek medical advice if significant mood changes, abnormal bleeding or allergic symptoms occur.

What is it used for?
Pancreatin is used to help digestion when the pancreas does not produce enough digestive enzymes. It may help the body digest fats, proteins and carbohydrates more effectively.

How does it work?
It provides digestive enzymes that break down fats, proteins and carbohydrates in food so they can be absorbed by the body.

How to take/use it
Take it with or immediately after food, as directed by a doctor or the product label. Swallow the capsule whole with water. Do not crush or chew it unless specifically instructed.

Common side effects
Stomach pain, bloating, constipation, diarrhoea, nausea or vomiting may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to pancreatin or pork-derived products. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, vomiting, constipation or bloating. Use only under medical advice if there is a history of gout, high uric acid levels or bowel problems.

What is it used for?
A syndet bathing bar is used for gentle cleansing of the skin. It may be suitable when regular soap causes dryness or irritation.

How does it work?
It contains mild synthetic cleansing agents that remove dirt, sweat and excess oil from the skin while generally being less drying than regular soap.

How to take/use it
Wet the skin and the bar, gently lather, then rinse thoroughly with water. For external use only.

Common side effects
Mild dryness, redness, itching or skin irritation may occur in some people.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes. Stop using it if significant irritation, rash or swelling develops. Do not use on broken or infected skin unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
This nutritional powder is used to supplement the diet with protein, calories and nutrients from milk, grains, plant proteins, nuts and flaxseed. It may support general nutritional needs when included as part of a balanced diet.

How does it work?
It provides dietary protein and energy, along with nutrients from its milk, grains, nuts, dates and flaxseed ingredients. It is a nutritional supplement and is not intended to treat a specific disease.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label. Mix with the recommended liquid or food and consume as instructed. Do not use it as a replacement for a varied, balanced diet unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
May cause bloating, gas, stomach discomfort or nausea in some people. Allergic reactions may occur in sensitive individuals.

Precautions
Contains milk, soy, cashew, almond and wheat; avoid it if allergic to any of these ingredients. It may not be suitable for people with lactose intolerance or gluten sensitivity. People with diabetes or other medical conditions should check the nutritional information and seek healthcare advice before use. Stop use and seek medical help for swelling, breathing difficulty or other signs of a serious allergy.

What is it used for?
This is a nutritional supplement that provides taurine, choline, omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids, vitamins and minerals. It may help provide these nutrients when dietary intake is insufficient. Its specific benefits depend on the product formulation and individual nutritional needs.

How does it work?
The nutrients support normal functions such as energy metabolism, brain and nerve function, cell health and general body processes.

How to take/use it
Mix and take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Use the measuring scoop, if provided, and store as instructed on the pack.

Common side effects
Some people may experience nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating, loose stools or an unpleasant aftertaste.

Precautions
Check the ingredients for allergies, especially if the omega-3 source is fish or seafood. Seek medical advice before use if pregnant or breastfeeding, if there is a medical condition, or if taking regular medicines, particularly blood-thinning medicines. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to help meet the body's needs for vitamins, minerals and lysine, especially when dietary intake is inadequate or nutritional requirements are increased.

How does it work?
The vitamins and minerals support normal body functions, while lysine is an essential amino acid used for protein synthesis and tissue growth and repair.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, stomach upset, constipation or diarrhoea in some people.

Precautions
Check the ingredients before use if there is a known allergy. Do not combine with other vitamin or mineral supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in case of kidney or other long-term medical conditions.

What is it used for?
This syrup is used to relieve cough with mucus and chest congestion. It may also help open narrowed airways and make phlegm easier to cough out.

How does it work?
Terbutaline relaxes the muscles around the airways to help breathing. Bromhexine and guaiphenesin thin and loosen mucus, while menthol may soothe throat irritation.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed by a doctor or as stated on the label. Shake the bottle well before use and measure each dose with the supplied measuring device. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Shaking or tremors, nervousness, headache, dizziness, nausea, stomach upset, or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Avoid use if allergic to any ingredient. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, or a very fast or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
This syrup is used for cough with mucus, especially when breathing is associated with wheezing or narrowed airways. It helps loosen and clear phlegm and may relieve airway tightness.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus, making it easier to cough out. Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles around the airways and helps improve airflow.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Shake the bottle well before use and measure each dose with the supplied measuring cup or spoon. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, shakiness, nervousness, muscle cramps or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use cautiously if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid or a history of seizures. Seek medical help for severe or worsening breathing difficulty, chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, or an allergic reaction. Do not use it to self-treat a persistent cough without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve wet or productive cough with mucus and chest congestion. It may also help ease wheezing caused by tightening of the airways.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus, making it easier to cough up. Terbutaline relaxes the airway muscles, while menthol may provide a soothing sensation.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Shake the bottle well and measure the syrup with a proper measuring device. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach upset, headache, dizziness, shakiness, nervousness, or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, chest pain, worsening breathing difficulty, or signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used to help protect exposed skin from the sun’s ultraviolet (UV) rays and help prevent sunburn during sun exposure.

How does it work?
Its sunscreen ingredients absorb, reflect or scatter some UV rays. Aloe vera and vitamin E help condition the skin.

How to take/use it
Apply evenly to clean, exposed skin before sun exposure. Reapply regularly, especially after swimming, sweating or towel drying, and follow the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching or rash may occur. Stop use if a severe skin reaction develops.

Precautions
For external use only. Keep away from the eyes and mucous membranes. Test on a small area first if the skin is sensitive. Sunscreen does not replace protective clothing, shade and avoiding intense midday sun. Seek medical advice if irritation persists or is severe.

What is it used for?
Piroxicam is an anti-inflammatory painkiller used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness in conditions such as osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. If it is a dispersible tablet, dissolve it in water as directed before taking it. Take with or after food and do not take more than the recommended amount. Do not combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache.

Precautions
Piroxicam can cause stomach ulcers or bleeding, and may affect the kidneys, heart or blood pressure. Tell the doctor about any history of ulcers, kidney or heart problems, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to NSAIDs. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks and in the last 3 months, unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest pain, breathing difficulty or facial swelling.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to help prevent or treat infection in wounds such as cuts, abrasions, burns, ulcers and other infected or at-risk wounds, as directed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Povidone-iodine acts as an antiseptic against many germs. Metronidazole helps act against certain bacteria, while aloe vera may help soothe and moisturise the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean and gently dry the affected area, then apply the ointment as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use. Do not apply inside the eyes, mouth or other body openings, and do not swallow.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, redness, itching or skin irritation may occur at the application site. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to povidone-iodine, metronidazole or any ingredient. Do not use on large areas, deep wounds or for prolonged periods unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical care if the wound becomes more painful, swollen, produces pus, or does not improve, or if fever develops. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or if there is thyroid disease or significant kidney problems.

What is it used for?
Used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acid reflux, heartburn and related acid-related stomach conditions. It may also be prescribed as part of treatment for certain stomach ulcers or Helicobacter pylori infection, along with other medicines.

How does it work?
Vonoprazan blocks the final step involved in stomach acid production. This reduces acidity and helps relieve irritation in the food pipe and stomach.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, constipation, nausea, stomach pain or discomfort, and flatulence.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, a history of stomach cancer or other serious stomach problems, or if other medicines are being taken. Seek medical advice for persistent or worsening symptoms, vomiting blood, black stools, difficulty swallowing, or unexplained weight loss. Do not use for prolonged periods unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Himalayan pink salt, sea salt and black salt are primarily used as food seasonings. They are not established medicines for treating a specific health condition.

How does it work?
These salts mainly provide sodium chloride. Sodium and chloride help support fluid balance, nerve function and muscle function, but the body needs only limited amounts.

How to take/use it
Use small amounts in food as a seasoning. Do not use it as a treatment or take large amounts. Follow medical advice if a low-sodium diet has been recommended.

Common side effects
Excess intake may cause increased thirst, water retention, bloating and raised blood pressure.

Precautions
Use sparingly, especially with high blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease or swelling, or when following a sodium-restricted diet. Himalayan, sea and black salts can still contain significant sodium and should not be assumed to be safer than regular salt.

What is it used for?
Levocetirizine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching or hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth with water, with or without food, exactly as directed by a doctor or as stated on the label. It may cause drowsiness in some people, so avoid driving until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, and sore throat.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful with driving or operating machinery if drowsy. People with kidney disease may need medical advice before use. Consult a doctor during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is difficulty passing urine. Seek medical help for signs of a severe allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve allergy-related breathing and nose symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and mucus or phlegm-related cough. It may be prescribed for other allergic respiratory conditions as directed by a doctor. It is not intended to treat a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, which causes many allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes involved in airway inflammation, while ambroxol helps thin and clear mucus.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not take more than the prescribed amount.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or tiredness, headache, dry mouth, nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, or dizziness may occur. Tell a doctor if these effects are troublesome or persistent.

Precautions
This medicine may cause sleepiness or dizziness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Seek medical advice if unusual mood or behaviour changes, disturbing dreams, depression, or suicidal thoughts occur. It is not a substitute for emergency treatment during an asthma attack. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or any allergy to these ingredients. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with phlegm and associated allergy or cold symptoms such as a runny nose, sneezing and throat irritation.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, which helps reduce allergy symptoms. Ambroxol thins and loosens mucus, making it easier to clear from the airways.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Avoid taking more than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dry mouth, headache, nausea, stomach discomfort or indigestion.

Precautions
Drowsiness may occur; avoid driving or alcohol until the effects are known. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking other medicines that cause drowsiness. Stop use and seek medical help for a severe rash, swelling or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose, and watery or itchy eyes.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergic symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, chemicals that can contribute to inflammation and swelling in the airways and nose.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with the supplied measuring device. Do not take more or use it more often than recommended.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or tiredness, headache, dry mouth, stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Levocetirizine may cause drowsiness; avoid activities requiring alertness until its effect is known. Seek medical advice promptly if unusual dreams, sleep problems, agitation, aggression, depression, or thoughts of self-harm occur. This medicine is not intended to relieve a sudden asthma attack. Tell the doctor about any other medicines being used and any liver or kidney problems.

What is it used for?
Used mainly to relieve allergy-related symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, nasal itching, and itchy or watery eyes. It may also be prescribed as an additional treatment for some people with asthma, but it does not relieve a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, which causes many allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, substances involved in allergic inflammation and airway narrowing.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than recommended, and do not use it as a rescue medicine for sudden breathing difficulty.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Drowsiness may occur; avoid driving or alcohol until the effect is known. Seek medical advice promptly for mood or behaviour changes, nightmares, anxiety, depression, suicidal thoughts, or unusual agitation. People with kidney problems, or those who are pregnant or breastfeeding, should consult a doctor before use. Seek urgent help for severe breathing difficulty or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat.

What is it used for?
Levocetirizine oral suspension is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the effects of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce itching and other allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Shake well before use and measure the prescribed amount with a proper measuring device. Use it only as directed by a doctor or the product label, and do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, and sometimes stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Drowsiness may occur; take care when driving or operating machinery, and avoid alcohol if it increases sleepiness. Seek medical advice if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Children should receive this medicine only in the dose recommended for their age and weight by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
This is a combination dietary supplement containing herbal ingredients, amino acids, vitamins and minerals. Its exact intended therapeutic use cannot be confirmed from the ingredients alone; it should not be used as a substitute for prescribed treatment.

How does it work?
The ingredients have different nutritional and antioxidant properties, but there is no single established mechanism for this combination.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache or dizziness. Green tea may cause restlessness or difficulty sleeping in sensitive people.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is diabetes, liver disease or any long-term medical condition. Bitter gourd, chromium and alpha-lipoic acid may affect blood sugar and could interact with diabetes medicines. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe or unusual symptoms occur.

What is it used for?
This is a nutritional supplement providing protein, carbohydrates, fibre, vitamins and minerals. It may help supplement the diet when additional nutrition is needed. The supplied information is not enough to confirm a specific use such as weight loss or meal replacement.

How does it work?
It provides nutrients from protein, maltodextrin, inulin, vitamins, minerals and plant-based ingredients. Protein supports normal body tissue maintenance, while vitamins and minerals support normal body functions.

How to take/use it
Mix and use only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended serving. It should not replace a varied, balanced diet unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Bloating, gas, abdominal discomfort or changes in bowel movements may occur, especially because of inulin. Allergic reactions may occur in people sensitive to soy or milk.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to soy, milk or any other ingredient. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or regular medicine use. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
This is a nutritional supplement that provides protein, carbohydrates, fibre, vitamins and minerals. It may be used to help supplement daily nutritional intake. Its specific purpose, such as meal replacement or weight management, cannot be confirmed from the supplied information.

How does it work?
It supplies nutrients from protein, maltodextrin, inulin, vitamins, minerals and flaxseed oil. Inulin provides dietary fibre, while the other ingredients contribute nutritional calories and nutrients.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended serving. The correct serving size and frequency cannot be determined from the supplied information.

Common side effects
Bloating, gas, abdominal discomfort or loose stools may occur, particularly due to inulin. Allergic reactions may occur in people sensitive to soy or milk. Green tea extract may cause stomach upset, nervousness or difficulty sleeping in some people.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to soy or milk. Check with a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is diabetes, a digestive disorder, or sensitivity to caffeine. Green tea extract may interact with some medicines. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?

Iron and folic acid support the production of haemoglobin and red blood cells. The other vitamins, minerals, protein and lysine provide nutritional support.

Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist, as the dose depends on age and individual needs. Shake the bottle well and measure the syrup with a proper measuring device. If it causes stomach upset, taking it after food may help. Do not take more than recommended.

Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea may occur. Iron may cause dark-coloured stools.

Do not use iron-containing supplements without medical advice if there is iron overload or an anaemia not caused by iron deficiency. What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to provide protein, vitamins and minerals. The digestive enzyme blend may help support the breakdown and digestion of food.

How does it work?
It supplies nutrients needed for normal body functions. Digestive enzymes help break down proteins, carbohydrates and fats during digestion.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Take with food if advised on the label.

Whey protein provides amino acids that the body uses for tissue maintenance and muscle function. The added vitamins, minerals and digestive enzymes provide nutrients and may help with digestion of the supplement.

Mix and use according to the product label. Do not exceed the recommended serving. Use as part of a balanced diet and adequate fluid intake.

What is it used for?
Used to help relieve pain, stiffness and reduced movement associated with osteoarthritis and other degenerative joint conditions.

Diacerein helps reduce inflammatory activity involved in osteoarthritis. Glucosamine and methylsulfonylmethane (MSM) support joint and connective-tissue health and may help reduce joint discomfort.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain, inflammation and swelling associated with muscle, joint and other musculoskeletal conditions or injuries.

Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Trypsin, bromelain and rutoside may help reduce inflammation and swelling.

Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food, and do not take more than the prescribed amount. Do not combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and skin rash.

Precautions

How does it work?
Trypsin and bromelain are enzymes that may help reduce inflammatory swelling. Rutoside may help support small blood vessel stability.

How to take/use it

What is it used for?

It binds phosphate from food in the digestive tract, reducing the amount absorbed into the blood. The bound phosphate is then passed out in the stool.

Use only under medical supervision, with regular monitoring of blood phosphate and other mineral levels. What is it used for?

It is an antibiotic that acts mainly inside the intestine. It reduces the growth of certain harmful gut bacteria and lowers the production of substances that can contribute to symptoms or hepatic encephalopathy.

What is it used for?
This combination is prescribed to help reduce the risk of blood clots, heart attack and stroke in people with certain heart or blood-vessel conditions, including after some heart procedures. It also helps lower high cholesterol.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin lowers harmful LDL cholesterol. Aspirin and clopidogrel make platelets less likely to stick together and form blood clots.

Easy bruising or bleeding, indigestion, nausea, headache and muscle pain. Mild stomach discomfort may also occur.

Precautions

Avoid starting painkillers such as ibuprofen or other blood-thinning medicines unless advised. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, sudden weakness, chest pain, or unexplained severe muscle pain with dark urine. This medicine should not be used during pregnancy, and medical advice is needed during breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Rosuvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, especially “bad” LDL cholesterol and triglycerides. It may also help reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It reduces the liver’s production of cholesterol and helps the liver remove more LDL cholesterol from the blood.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, weakness, and muscle pain.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid problems, or a history of muscle problems with cholesterol medicines. It is generally not used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe or unexplained muscle pain or weakness, dark urine, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe allergic symptoms. Tell the doctor about all other medicines being taken, as some may interact with rosuvastatin.

What is it used for?
Rosuvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, especially LDL ("bad") cholesterol, and to help reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It reduces cholesterol production in the liver and helps the liver remove more LDL cholesterol from the blood.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme in the liver that is needed to make cholesterol. This helps the liver remove more LDL cholesterol from the blood.

Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day and continue it for as long as advised. Do not stop it without medical advice.

Headache, nausea, stomach pain, constipation, dizziness, weakness, or muscle aches may occur.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to manage high cholesterol and high triglyceride levels, especially when both cholesterol and triglycerides are elevated. It helps reduce the risk of complications related to abnormal blood fats when prescribed with a suitable diet and lifestyle changes.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin reduces the liver’s production of cholesterol, while fenofibrate helps lower triglycerides and improve levels of other blood fats.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin lowers harmful LDL cholesterol. Aspirin and clopidogrel reduce the ability of platelets to stick together, helping prevent blood clots.

Seek urgent medical help for severe or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, sudden severe headache, weakness, severe muscle pain, or dark urine. Permethrin affects the nervous system of lice and kills them. Cetrimide has antiseptic activity against some microorganisms.

Niacinamide, a form of vitamin B3, helps support the skin barrier and may help regulate oil production and reduce the appearance of redness and uneven tone.
