This product is a dietary supplement containing multiple vitamins, minerals and botanical ingredients. It is used to supplement the diet when nutritional intake may be inadequate. Its specific benefits depend on the ingredients and their amounts.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamins and minerals needed for normal body functions. The botanical ingredients may have additional effects, depending on their identity and amount.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount or combine it with other supplements containing the same ingredients unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Some people may experience nausea, stomach upset, constipation or diarrhoea. Side effects may vary depending on the ingredients.

Precautions
Check the full ingredient list before use, especially if pregnant, breastfeeding, taking medicines, or having a medical condition. Seek medical advice if an allergic reaction or severe side effect occurs.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to provide protein, branched-chain amino acids, vitamins and minerals when dietary intake is inadequate or nutritional support is needed. The specific medical indication depends on the product label and healthcare professional’s advice.

How does it work?
It supplies protein and amino acids used for body tissue maintenance and repair, along with vitamins and minerals that support normal body functions. It also contains immunoglobulin G (IgG), an antibody protein.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Mix or prepare it as instructed, and do not use more than the recommended amount.

Digestive symptoms such as bloating, nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea or constipation may occur.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list for possible allergens or intolerances. Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney or liver disease, a prescribed protein- or mineral-restricted diet, or another significant medical condition. Stop use and seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This is a dietary supplement used to provide vitamins and minerals, with added cranberry, soy isoflavones and shatavari. It may help support general nutritional wellness; the exact benefits depend on the product formulation and individual needs.

How does it work?
The vitamins and minerals provide nutrients needed for normal body functions. Cranberry, soy isoflavones and shatavari provide plant-based compounds, but this supplement should not be considered a treatment for any disease.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach discomfort.

Common side effects
Mild nausea, stomach upset, bloating, diarrhoea or constipation may occur.

Precautions
Check the label for allergens, especially soy. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a hormone-sensitive medical condition, kidney disease or regular medicine use. Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction or severe side effects occur.

What is it used for?
Vitamin E cream is generally used to moisturise and soften dry, rough skin. It may also help support the skin barrier.

How does it work?
Vitamin E has antioxidant properties and helps protect the skin from oxidative damage. The cream base helps reduce dryness by moisturising the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, itching, redness or rash may occur, especially in people with sensitive skin.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to vitamin E or any ingredient in the cream. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a spreading rash develops. Do not apply to infected or seriously damaged skin unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Voglibose is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar after meals in people with type 2 diabetes.

How does it work?
It slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates in the intestine, helping reduce the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth with or just before meals, exactly as prescribed. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea or constipation may occur, especially when starting treatment.

Precautions
Monitor blood sugar as advised. The risk of low blood sugar may increase when used with insulin or other diabetes medicines. Seek medical advice if severe or persistent stomach or bowel problems occur. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver disease, intestinal disorders, pregnancy or breastfeeding. If low blood sugar occurs with another diabetes medicine, glucose may be needed rather than table sugar.

What is it used for?
Voglibose is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in people with type 2 diabetes, particularly the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How does it work?
It slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates in the intestine. This helps reduce the increase in blood sugar after eating.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually immediately before meals. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Continue the recommended diet and exercise plan.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort, stomach pain and diarrhoea.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice, especially if there is a digestive disorder, intestinal blockage or severe kidney or liver disease. When taken with other diabetes medicines, it may contribute to low blood sugar. If low blood sugar occurs, glucose or dextrose is preferred because ordinary table sugar may work more slowly. Seek medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, vomiting or diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It helps reduce blood sugar rises after meals.

How does it work?
Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin better. Voglibose slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates, reducing the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with or just before meals. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed diet and blood sugar monitoring plan, and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, gas or bloating, and reduced appetite. Low blood sugar is more likely if used with other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, heavy alcohol use, dehydration, severe infection, or planned surgery or contrast-dye scans. Kidney function may need regular monitoring. Seek urgent medical help for severe weakness, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, or unusual drowsiness. Take medical advice if symptoms of low blood sugar occur, such as sweating, shaking, dizziness, or confusion.

What is it used for?
It is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes.

How does it work?
Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin better. Voglibose slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates, helping reduce the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and at the advised time in relation to meals. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort, nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite. Low blood sugar is possible, especially when used with other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, severe dehydration, a serious infection, heart failure, or heavy alcohol use. Medical advice may be needed before surgery or certain scans using contrast dye. Seek urgent help for severe weakness, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting or unusual sleepiness. Monitor blood sugar as advised.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron 2 mg injection is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including those caused by chemotherapy, radiotherapy or surgery.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals in the body that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein or muscle by a doctor or other trained healthcare professional. The dose and timing depend on the cause of nausea or vomiting and should be decided by the prescriber.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, flushing, dizziness and tiredness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any heart-rhythm problem, low potassium or magnesium levels, liver disease, or previous allergy to ondansetron. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, breathing difficulty, swelling, or signs of a severe allergic reaction. Ondansetron can rarely affect heart rhythm and may interact with some medicines.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including nausea and vomiting related to medical treatments or surgery.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of serotonin, a natural chemical that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Place the orally disintegrating tablet on the tongue and allow it to dissolve before swallowing. Do not push the tablet through the foil; follow the pack instructions for removing it.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, tiredness and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a heart rhythm problem, low potassium or magnesium levels, liver disease, or a history of seizures. Seek medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic reaction, or symptoms such as agitation, sweating, fever, muscle stiffness or diarrhoea, especially when taking other medicines that affect serotonin. Do not take with apomorphine.

What is it used for?
Used to help prevent or correct vitamin and zinc deficiencies and support normal nutrition and overall health.

How does it work?
It provides essential vitamins and zinc needed for normal body functions, including immune function, growth and development, and metabolism.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Measure the drops carefully using the supplied dropper or measuring device. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine with other multivitamin or zinc products unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, vomiting, diarrhoea or constipation, and an unpleasant taste may occur.

Precautions
Do not exceed the recommended amount, as excessive intake of vitamins or zinc can be harmful. Check with a healthcare professional before use if already taking other supplements or medicines, or if there is a medical condition affecting the kidneys or liver. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Rabeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be used for stomach or intestinal ulcers and other acid-related conditions when prescribed.

How does it work?
It belongs to a group of medicines called proton pump inhibitors. It reduces the production of acid in the stomach, helping relieve symptoms and allowing acid-related irritation or ulcers to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed timing and duration, even if symptoms improve.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to rabeprazole or other acid-reducing medicines, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or persistent symptoms. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor, as it may affect magnesium, vitamin B12 levels or bone health and may interact with other medicines.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn, acid reflux and related indigestion. It may also help with nausea or a feeling of fullness associated with reflux.

How does it work?
Rabeprazole reduces the production of acid in the stomach. Domperidone helps stomach contents move forward and can reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is generally taken before food, as directed by the doctor. Do not use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, constipation, dry mouth or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, or a history of low potassium or magnesium. Domperidone can rarely cause serious heart rhythm problems, so seek medical help for a fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting or severe dizziness. Check with a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or with other medicines—especially medicines that affect heart rhythm.

What is it used for?
Used to treat acidity, heartburn and acid reflux (GERD). It may also help relieve reflux-related nausea, fullness or indigestion.

How does it work?
Rabeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps food move through the stomach and improves nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not take more than the recommended dose or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain, nausea, dry mouth and dizziness. Domperidone may rarely cause changes in heartbeat or increased prolactin levels.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart rhythm problems, low potassium or magnesium levels, or a history of gastrointestinal bleeding or blockage. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm. Seek medical help for fainting, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe diarrhoea, vomiting blood or black stools.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also help indigestion and related nausea or fullness caused by reduced movement of the stomach.

How does it work?
Rabeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Levosulpiride improves movement of the upper digestive tract and helps reduce nausea.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed timing in relation to meals.

What is it used for?
Dydrogesterone is a progesterone-like medicine used to treat menstrual problems caused by low progesterone, such as painful or irregular periods, absent periods, endometriosis and abnormal uterine bleeding. How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone progesterone. It helps regulate the menstrual cycle and supports the lining of the uterus.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, according to the schedule recommended by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Headache or migraine, nausea, stomach discomfort, breast tenderness, spotting or changes in menstrual bleeding, and abdominal pain.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver problems, unexplained vaginal bleeding, a history of hormone-sensitive cancers or blood clots, and all other medicines being taken. Seek medical advice for heavy or persistent bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe headache, vision changes, chest pain or leg swelling. Use during pregnancy only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Aceclofenac 100 mg + Paracetamol 325 mg is used to relieve pain and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take this medicine only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist, preferably with or after food. Swallow it with water. Do not take other medicines containing paracetamol or aceclofenac unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney or liver disease, or allergy to painkillers, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Use cautiously in people with heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma or dehydration. Avoid alcohol because it may increase the risk of liver damage. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a doctor before use.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and reduce fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow with water, preferably with or after food, to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it with other medicines containing paracetamol or aceclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache.

Precautions

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve pain, inflammation and swelling associated with muscle, joint and other painful inflammatory conditions. It may be prescribed for short-term pain relief when an anti-inflammatory medicine is needed.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and fever, while serratiopeptidase may help reduce inflammation and swelling.

Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache may occur.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful muscle and joint conditions associated with muscle spasm, such as acute back or neck pain, sprains and strains. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Thiocolchicoside helps relax painful muscle spasms.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed. It is generally taken with or after food to reduce stomach irritation. Swallow with water and do not take it for longer than advised. Avoid driving if dizziness or sleepiness occurs.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and sleepiness. Serious stomach bleeding or allergic reactions require urgent medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney, liver or heart problems, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, seizures, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid combining with other NSAID painkillers or excessive alcohol unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Azithromycin 500 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the chest, throat, skin and soft tissues, and some sexually transmitted infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. It may usually be taken with or without food; follow the instructions on the prescription. Do not share antibiotics or use leftover medicine.

Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, vomiting and headache.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to azithromycin or other macrolide antibiotics, liver disease, heart rhythm problems, or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe rash, swelling, breathing difficulty, or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, especially those that can affect heart rhythm or antacids containing aluminium or magnesium.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to help improve appetite in people with poor appetite and support healthy weight gain when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Cyproheptadine can increase appetite by blocking certain histamine and serotonin effects in the body. Tricholine citrate is included as a nutritional support ingredient.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, nausea and increased appetite may occur.

Precautions
Cyproheptadine may cause sleepiness. Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery. Tell the doctor about glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, breathing problems, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Use in children only under medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron and folic acid deficiency, which can lead to deficiency-related anaemia. Zinc provides additional nutritional supplementation when needed.

How does it work?
Iron and folic acid help the body make healthy red blood cells and haemoglobin. Zinc supports normal growth, tissue repair and immune function.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow with water. Avoid taking it at the same time as tea, coffee, milk, calcium supplements or antacids, as these may reduce iron absorption. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, constipation or diarrhoea, metallic taste and dark-coloured stools may occur.

Precautions
Keep out of reach of children; an iron overdose can be dangerous. Tell a healthcare professional about other medicines being taken, especially antacids, calcium supplements, thyroid medicines or certain antibiotics. Do not use for anaemia without medical advice, as anaemia can have causes that require different treatment.

What is it used for?
Gripe water is traditionally used to help soothe mild colic, gas and digestive discomfort in babies. Its effectiveness can vary, and different products may contain different ingredients.

How does it work?
Its action depends on the ingredients in the product. Some ingredients may help ease gas or digestive discomfort, but gripe water does not have one standard mechanism.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label and check the recommended age. Do not give more than the stated amount. Check the ingredient list, as formulations differ. Seek medical advice if the baby has persistent crying, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, poor feeding or a swollen abdomen.

Common side effects
Possible side effects may include vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach upset or an allergic reaction such as a rash. Side effects depend on the formulation.

Precautions
Check the ingredients carefully and avoid products containing alcohol or ingredients unsuitable for babies. Do not use in infants below the labelled age limit. Stop use and seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or severe rash. Gripe water should not replace medical assessment for ongoing or severe symptoms.

What is it used for?
Neem soap is used for cleansing the skin and removing dirt, oil and sweat. It may be used as part of routine skin hygiene.

How does it work?
The soap cleans the skin by helping remove oils, dirt and impurities. Neem is a plant-based ingredient commonly included in skin-cleansing products.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Wet the skin, apply the soap, gently lather and rinse thoroughly. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Skin dryness, irritation, redness or itching may occur, especially in sensitive skin.

Precautions
Stop use if irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Avoid using on broken or severely irritated skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Keep away from the eyes and do not swallow. Consider a small patch test before regular use if the skin is sensitive.

What is it used for?
Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some urinary, gastrointestinal, respiratory, skin and other infections. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops bacteria from making and repairing their genetic material, which prevents them from growing and causes them to die.

Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the course unless the prescriber advises otherwise. Swallow with water. Nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, stomach pain, headache and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice urgently for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nervous-system changes, severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash, breathing difficulty or swelling. Tell the prescriber about tendon problems, nerve disorders, myasthenia gravis, heart-rhythm problems, kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Ciprofloxacin can interact with several medicines, so provide a complete list of medicines and supplements being used.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?
Itraconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, nails, mouth, vagina and other parts of the body. The exact use depends on the type and location of the infection.

It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which prevents them from growing and helps clear the infection.

Take it exactly as prescribed. Itraconazole capsules are usually taken immediately after a full meal and should be swallowed whole with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment early without medical advice. The treatment schedule varies depending on the infection.

Nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart failure, pregnancy or breastfeeding before use. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, breathing difficulty, leg swelling or a fast heartbeat.

Cefuroxime kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps protect cefuroxime from enzymes produced by some resistant bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Take it after food if advised, and swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not share or reuse leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain or discomfort, indigestion, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, other cephalosporins, penicillins or related antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Contact a doctor if diarrhoea is severe, persistent or bloody. Inform the doctor about kidney problems, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being used.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used on the skin for inflamed fungal infections, especially when a bacterial infection may also be present. It should be used only when prescribed, as the strong steroid component can worsen some infections if used incorrectly.

How does it work?
Miconazole fights fungal growth and neomycin acts against susceptible bacteria. Clobetasol reduces inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Clean and dry the area first and wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not use more often or for longer than directed.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, irritation, dryness or redness may occur. Prolonged or inappropriate use can cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Do not apply to the face, groin, skin folds, broken skin or large areas unless specifically advised by a doctor. Do not cover the area with a tight dressing unless directed. Avoid prolonged use, particularly in children. Stop and seek medical advice if the infection worsens, spreads, or causes severe irritation or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Diclofenac sodium is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine used to relieve pain, swelling and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of prostaglandins, substances involved in pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed and follow the instructions for the specific product, as diclofenac 75 mg may be available in different forms. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney or liver disease, heart disease, or allergy to diclofenac, aspirin or other NSAIDs unless specifically advised by a doctor. It may increase the risk of stomach bleeding and heart or kidney problems. Do not combine it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest pain, breathing difficulty or facial swelling. It should generally be avoided during the last three months of pregnancy and used during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to relieve pain and inflammation associated with muscle aches, joint pain, sprains, strains and arthritis.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Methyl salicylate and menthol provide additional soothing and cooling effects on the affected area.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the affected area as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not apply to cuts, broken or irritated skin, and wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, dryness, burning or rash at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other NSAIDs, salicylates or any ingredient in the product. Avoid tight bandages, heating pads and other sources of heat over the treated area. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe skin reactions, breathing difficulty or swelling occur. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months, while breastfeeding, or with a history of stomach ulcers, kidney disease or NSAID-related asthma. Avoid using with other diclofenac or NSAID products unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food and with water. Do not take more often or for longer than advised. Do not combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol, diclofenac or similar painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAID painkillers. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase the risk of liver damage. Do not use during the last 3 months of pregnancy; seek medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop and seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe rash, breathing difficulty, chest pain, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain and inflammation, especially muscle, joint and arthritis-related pain.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces substances in the body that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take it with other medicines containing diclofenac, paracetamol or other NSAIDs unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache.

Precautions
Avoid or seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, allergy to painkillers or NSAIDs, asthma triggered by painkillers, or liver, kidney or heart disease. Avoid excess alcohol. Do not use during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain and reduce inflammation in conditions affecting the muscles, joints and bones, such as arthritis, sprains and other painful musculoskeletal conditions.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and swelling. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take it with other medicines containing diclofenac, paracetamol or other painkillers unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Indigestion, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use or seek medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, or asthma triggered by painkillers. Avoid excessive alcohol, as it may increase the risk of liver damage and stomach problems. Inform the doctor if pregnant, especially during the last three months, or if taking blood thinners or other regular medicines. Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic symptoms, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, including sprains, strains and arthritis-related pain.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling and warming counter-irritant effect that may help ease discomfort.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected area as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands after application unless treating the hands. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin, and avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Common side effects
Application-site irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other painkillers such as ibuprofen, or salicylates. Avoid applying over large areas, under tight bandages or with heat. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe skin irritation, breathing difficulty or facial swelling occurs. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially in the last three months, or while breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Dydrogesterone is used to treat conditions related to low progesterone, such as irregular or painful periods, endometriosis and some menstrual problems. It may also be prescribed for progesterone support in fertility treatment, pregnancy-related care or as part of hormone replacement therapy, depending on the doctor's advice.

How does it work?
It is a progestogen that acts similarly to the body's natural progesterone. It helps regulate the womb lining and menstrual cycle and provides progesterone support when needed.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, with water. It may be taken with or without food, but should be taken consistently as directed. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache or migraine, nausea, stomach discomfort, breast tenderness, spotting or changes in menstrual bleeding, and skin rash or itching.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, unexplained vaginal bleeding, a history of hormone-sensitive conditions, or depression. Report heavy or unusual bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or a severe allergic reaction. If prescribed during pregnancy or after delivery, use it only as directed and do not stop it without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used to treat acidity, heartburn and acid reflux (gastro-oesophageal reflux disease or GERD), particularly when these symptoms are associated with nausea or a feeling of fullness.

How does it work?
Esomeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps improve movement of food through the stomach and can reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor or according to the product label. Swallow the medicine whole with water; do not crush or chew it unless specifically instructed. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain, nausea, dry mouth and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, an irregular heartbeat, liver disease, or low potassium or magnesium levels. Domperidone may cause serious heart-rhythm problems and should not be used with certain medicines; mention all prescription and non-prescription medicines being taken. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, severe dizziness or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or for prolonged treatment.

What is it used for?
Febuxostat is used to lower high uric acid levels in people with gout and help prevent gout attacks over time. It is not meant to provide immediate relief during a sudden gout attack.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called xanthine oxidase, reducing the body's production of uric acid.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Use it regularly even when gout symptoms are not present. Do not stop or change the treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Gout flare-ups, nausea, joint pain, skin rash, and changes in liver function tests may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, stroke, liver disease, or any previous allergy to febuxostat. Liver function may need monitoring. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, weakness on one side, or a severe skin rash. Do not take it with azathioprine or mercaptopurine unless specifically directed by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Febuxostat is used to lower high uric acid levels in adults with gout. It helps prevent future gout attacks and uric acid crystal buildup, but it does not provide immediate relief during an acute gout attack.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called xanthine oxidase, which reduces the body’s production of uric acid.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Take it regularly even when symptoms are not present. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Other medicines may be prescribed at the start of treatment to help prevent gout flares.

Common side effects
Gout flare-ups, nausea, joint pain, rash, and abnormal liver function test results may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, stroke, liver disease, kidney disease, or any previous allergy to febuxostat. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, severe rash, facial swelling, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Do not use with azathioprine or mercaptopurine unless specifically directed by a specialist. Regular medical follow-up and blood tests may be needed.

What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching. It may also be used to relieve hives (urticaria) and skin itching.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water. Avoid taking it with apple, orange or grapefruit juice, as these may reduce its effect. Keep aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids separate from this medicine as advised by a pharmacist or doctor.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, dizziness and tiredness may occur. Drowsiness is possible but is less common than with some other antihistamines.

Precautions
Tell a doctor or pharmacist if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Ask a healthcare professional before combining it with other medicines, especially antacids or other antihistamines.

What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching or hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions, helping reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by the doctor or product label. Swallow with water. Avoid taking it with fruit juice, such as apple, orange or grapefruit juice. If using aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids, ask a pharmacist or doctor how to separate their use from fexofenadine.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, dizziness and mild drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Tell a doctor or pharmacist about kidney problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding before use. Do not take it if allergic to fexofenadine or any of its ingredients. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, persistent or worsening.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis (nasal allergy), such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose, and watery or itchy eyes.

How does it work?
Fexofenadine blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, chemicals that can contribute to inflammation and nasal congestion.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Do not take more than recommended. Avoid taking fexofenadine with fruit juices, and check with a pharmacist before using aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, tiredness, or dizziness may occur. Sleepiness is possible but is generally less common with fexofenadine.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Stop the medicine and seek medical advice if unusual mood or behaviour changes, agitation, nightmares, depression, or suicidal thoughts occur. This medicine is not intended to treat a sudden asthma attack. Avoid driving if dizziness or sleepiness occurs.

What is it used for?
Folic acid 5 mg is used to prevent or treat folate deficiency and folate-deficiency anaemia. A higher-strength dose may also be prescribed before and during pregnancy to help reduce the risk of neural tube defects in the baby.

How does it work?
Folic acid is a form of vitamin B9. It helps the body make healthy red blood cells and supports normal cell growth and development.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow with water. It can usually be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Possible effects include nausea, bloating, abdominal discomfort or a skin rash.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any vitamin B12 deficiency or unexplained anaemia, as folic acid may improve the anaemia while allowing nerve damage from B12 deficiency to continue. Tell the doctor about allergies and all medicines being taken. High-strength folic acid should be used in pregnancy only as advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve neuropathic (nerve-related) pain, such as burning, tingling, numbness or shooting pain caused by irritated or damaged nerves.

How does it work?
Gabapentin reduces abnormal pain signals in the nerves. Methylcobalamin, a form of vitamin B12, supports normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Swallow the tablet/capsule whole with water. Do not stop gabapentin suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, tiredness, blurred or double vision, swelling of the hands or feet, nausea and dry mouth.

Precautions
It may cause sleepiness or dizziness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney problems. Inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, breathing problems, or use of opioids or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or serious mood changes.

What is it used for?
This combination is mainly used to relieve neuropathic pain, which is pain caused by irritated or damaged nerves. It may help with burning, shooting, tingling or electric-shock-like pain.

How does it work?
Gabapentin reduces abnormal nerve signalling, while nortriptyline changes pain-related chemical signals in the nervous system. Together, they help reduce nerve pain.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, tiredness, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, nausea and difficulty concentrating may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and use caution with sleeping tablets, opioid painkillers or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, heart problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe mood changes, suicidal thoughts, extreme sleepiness, fainting or breathing problems.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to prevent or treat low calcium and vitamin D levels and to support healthy bones. It may also be prescribed as part of treatment for certain bone conditions.

How does it work?
Calcitriol is an active form of vitamin D that helps the body absorb calcium. Calcium supports bones and teeth, while zinc helps support normal body functions and tissue health.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed or as directed on the label. Do not take more than recommended or use additional calcium or vitamin D supplements without medical advice. Swallow with water and follow any food-related instructions provided by the pharmacist or doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, constipation, stomach discomfort, or diarrhoea may occur. Excess calcium can cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness, or confusion.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or a parathyroid disorder. Avoid taking other calcium or vitamin D products unless advised. Seek medical advice if severe vomiting, unusual thirst, frequent urination, marked weakness, confusion, or irregular heartbeat occurs. This medicine may interact with some antibiotics, thyroid medicines, heart medicines, and osteoporosis treatments; separate doses or monitoring may be needed.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanic acid is a prescription antibiotic used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, sinuses, lungs, skin, urinary tract and teeth. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills bacteria by damaging their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps amoxycillin work against bacteria that can otherwise resist it.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share it or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach discomfort, skin rash and oral or vaginal thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take this medicine if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, other beta-lactam antibiotics or clavulanic acid. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver disease, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, or previous jaundice or liver problems with antibiotics. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, a severe skin rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ears, sinuses, throat, lungs, skin, urinary tract and teeth. It does not treat viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps prevent some bacteria from resisting amoxycillin.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxicillin, clavulanic acid or similar antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems and any previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash. Contact a doctor for severe or persistent diarrhoea, especially during or after treatment.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ears, sinuses, throat, chest, skin, urinary tract and teeth, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by interfering with their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps prevent some bacteria from breaking down amoxycillin, making the combination effective against a wider range of bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Take doses with food to help reduce stomach upset, and complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur. Oral or vaginal fungal infections can also develop.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, other similar antibiotics or cephalosporins. Inform the doctor about previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, kidney disease, glandular fever, or a history of severe antibiotic-associated diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, blistering, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ears, sinuses, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against them.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not share it or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion and skin rash may occur. Thrush can also develop.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxicillin or similar antibiotics. Tell the doctor about previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, kidney problems, glandular fever, allergies, or other medicines being used. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, a severe rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can cause resistance.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat fungal infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch and other yeast-related skin infections.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole stops the growth of fungi by interfering with an essential part of their cell membrane. Cetrimide is an antiseptic that helps reduce microorganisms on the treated area.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply or use it only on the affected area and in the manner directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not use more often or for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not apply to severely broken or irritated skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs. Seek medical advice if the infection does not improve or gets worse.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% is an antifungal medicine used for fungal infections of the skin or scalp. Depending on the formulation, it may also be used for dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis.

How does it work?
It blocks the growth of fungi by interfering with the formation of ergosterol, a substance fungi need to maintain their cell membranes.

How to take/use it
Use only on the affected skin or scalp and follow the instructions on the product label or from a healthcare professional. The exact directions depend on whether it is a cream, shampoo or another formulation. For external use only unless specifically prescribed otherwise. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole or any ingredient in the product. Avoid the eyes and mouth, and do not apply to severely broken or irritated skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash occurs, or if the condition does not improve.

What is it used for?
Used on the scalp to treat dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis, which can cause flaking, itching and irritation.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole and zinc pyrithione help reduce the fungi associated with dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis, helping control scalp flaking and inflammation.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the affected scalp as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Avoid contact with the eyes; rinse thoroughly with water if contact occurs.

Common side effects
Scalp irritation, itching, burning, dryness or increased flaking may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole, zinc pyrithione or any ingredient. Avoid use on broken or severely irritated skin unless advised by a doctor. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with mucus and help ease wheezing or narrowed airways in respiratory conditions such as bronchitis. It is not intended to replace prescribed treatment for asthma or other serious breathing problems.

How does it work?
Terbutaline helps relax and open the airways. Bromhexine loosens mucus, while guaiphenesin helps bring it up; menthol may soothe throat irritation.

How to take/use it
Take/use only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than recommended. If it is a liquid, measure each dose carefully and shake the bottle if instructed on the label.

Common side effects
Shakiness, nervousness, headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, or a fast heartbeat/palpitations may occur.

Precautions
Use only with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, or a very fast or irregular heartbeat. Consult a doctor if the cough persists or worsens.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with phlegm and help ease wheezing or chest tightness associated with some breathing conditions.

How does it work?
Terbutaline helps relax and open the airways. Bromhexine loosens thick mucus, while guaiphenesin helps clear it; menthol may soothe throat irritation.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than recommended. If it is a liquid, use the supplied measuring device and follow any shaking instructions on the label.

Common side effects
Shaking or tremors, nervousness, headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, fast heartbeat or palpitations may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, seizures, or a history of abnormal heart rhythm. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, and any other medicines, especially other bronchodilators or beta-blockers. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, or a persistent or worsening cough.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of dry cough and cold or allergy symptoms such as a runny nose, sneezing and watery eyes.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan reduces the cough reflex. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that helps relieve allergy-related symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or as advised by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other cough, cold or antihistamine medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea or stomach upset.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) medicines or within 14 days of stopping them. Seek medical advice before use if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, breathing problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Consult a healthcare professional if the cough persists or worsens.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for temporary relief of cough, blocked or runny nose, sneezing and other common cold symptoms. It may be particularly helpful for a dry cough with nasal congestion.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps reduce the urge to cough. Chlorpheniramine reduces allergy-related symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose, while phenylephrine helps relieve nasal blockage.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and avoid using other cough, cold or allergy medicines containing the same ingredients.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, restlessness or difficulty sleeping. Phenylephrine may cause a fast heartbeat or increased blood pressure.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness—avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Consult a healthcare professional before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, prostate or urination problems. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines or within 14 days of stopping them; check with a healthcare professional before use with antidepressants or other medicines. Seek medical advice if the cough is severe, lasts several days, or is associated with breathing difficulty or high fever.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve a wet or phlegmy cough when mucus is difficult to clear and there is wheezing or bronchospasm. It may be prescribed in respiratory conditions such as bronchitis or asthma-related breathing symptoms.

How does it work?
Ambroxol thins mucus, while guaiphenesin helps loosen and clear phlegm. Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles of the airways to help ease wheezing and breathing difficulty.

How to take/use it
Take or use only as directed by the doctor or according to the product label. The strength supplied does not specify the dose, frequency or treatment duration. Do not take more than recommended, and use a proper measuring device if it is a liquid medicine.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach upset, headache, tremor, nervousness, palpitations or a fast heartbeat.

Precautions

What is it used for?
Used to relieve productive (phlegmy) cough and chest congestion, especially when cough is associated with wheezing or tightening of the airways.

Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help loosen and clear mucus from the airways. Levosalbutamol relaxes the airway muscles, helping improve breathing and wheezing.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Do not self-medicate for persistent cough or breathing difficulty.

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, tremor or shakiness, muscle cramps, fast heartbeat and palpitations.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, glaucoma, seizures or low potassium levels. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, especially other bronchodilators or beta-blockers. Seek urgent medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain or a very fast or irregular heartbeat. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve a wet or productive cough with mucus, especially when it is associated with wheezing or breathing difficulty caused by narrowed airways. Use it only for the condition for which it has been prescribed.

How does it work?
Ambroxol helps thin and loosen mucus, while guaiphenesin helps clear mucus from the airways. Levosalbutamol relaxes the airway muscles and helps improve airflow.

How to take/use it
Take or use exactly as directed by the doctor or as stated on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Do not share this medicine with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, tremors, nervousness, muscle cramps, or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, seizures, or a history of sensitivity to any ingredient. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, or signs of an allergic reaction. Consult a doctor if the cough worsens or does not improve.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve productive (phlegmy) cough and chest congestion. It may also help ease wheezing or breathing difficulty caused by narrowed airways in some respiratory conditions.

How does it work?
Ambroxol helps thin and loosen mucus, while guaiphenesin helps clear mucus from the airways. Terbutaline relaxes the airway muscles to improve airflow.

How to take/use it
Use only in the dose and manner prescribed by the doctor. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised. If supplied as a liquid, measure each dose with the provided measuring device.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, shakiness or tremor, muscle cramps, and fast or pounding heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, seizures, or glaucoma. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if breathing difficulty worsens, severe palpitations occur, or the cough persists. Do not combine with other cough, cold, or bronchodilator medicines unless advised.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve wet or productive cough with mucus and may help ease wheezing or breathing difficulty caused by narrowed airways in conditions such as bronchitis. It is not generally intended for a dry cough without mucus.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help loosen and thin mucus so it can be coughed out more easily. Terbutaline relaxes the muscles of the airways, helping improve airflow.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more often or for longer than advised. The correct dose and duration depend on the person's age, symptoms and the product form.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, nervousness, trembling or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, a seizure disorder or an allergy to any ingredient. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice. Seek medical attention if breathing difficulty becomes severe, wheezing worsens or symptoms do not improve.

What is it used for?
Levocetirizine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching. It is also used for hives (urticaria) and related skin itching.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take the tablet exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Swallow it with water; it may generally be taken with or without food. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, dry mouth, headache, and occasionally stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Drowsiness may occur; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase sleepiness. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with Lactic Acid Bacillus is used to treat infections caused by susceptible bacteria. It does not treat viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall. Lactic Acid Bacillus is a probiotic that helps support the balance of beneficial bacteria in the gut during antibiotic treatment.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food, but taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not share or reuse leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur. Probiotics may also occasionally cause gas or bloating.

Precautions
Do not take it if there is a previous serious allergy to amoxycillin, penicillins or related antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or persistent/severe diarrhoea. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, glandular fever (mononucleosis), pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat bacterial infections when prescribed by a doctor. It is not effective for viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin is an antibiotic that kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Lactic Acid Bacillus is a probiotic that helps support the balance of beneficial bacteria in the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at evenly spaced times, and complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Do not stop or change the treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, and mild skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there is a known allergy to amoxycillin, penicillins, or related antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, or a history of serious allergic reactions. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only when prescribed, since unnecessary antibiotics can lead to resistance.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 500 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, body pain, toothache, muscle pain and period pain.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain and fever, helping to lower temperature and provide pain relief.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth with water, with or without food. Follow the dose and timing on the product label or as advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take with other medicines containing paracetamol, as this can cause an overdose. Seek medical advice before use if there is liver disease, regular heavy alcohol use, or an allergy to paracetamol. Get urgent medical help after taking more than the recommended amount, even if feeling well.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 650 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, body pain, toothache and muscle aches.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of pain- and fever-causing chemicals in the body, helping lower temperature and relieve pain.

How to take/use it
Swallow the tablet with water, following the dose and timing advised on the label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than recommended, and avoid using it with other medicines that contain paracetamol.

Common side effects
Usually, there are no side effects when used as directed. Nausea or a skin rash may occasionally occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to paracetamol. Seek medical advice before use if there is liver disease or regular heavy alcohol use. Avoid taking more than the recommended amount, as an overdose can cause serious liver damage. Stop use and seek urgent help for swelling, breathing difficulty, severe rash or suspected overdose.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol Paediatric Oral Suspension is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain in children, such as headache, body aches, toothache or pain associated with colds.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of pain- and fever-causing substances in the body, helping lower temperature and relieve pain.

How to take/use it
Shake the bottle well before use. Measure the dose with the supplied measuring device and give it exactly as directed on the package or by the doctor, based on the child’s age and weight. Do not give more than recommended or use it with any other medicine containing paracetamol.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when used correctly. Nausea, vomiting or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Check the strength carefully and use only the recommended dose. Do not use in children allergic to paracetamol. Seek medical advice before use if the child has liver disease or is taking other medicines. Get urgent medical help after an overdose, even if the child seems well, or if swelling, breathing difficulty or a severe skin rash develops.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol injection is used in hospitals or clinics for the short-term relief of pain and reduction of fever when treatment by injection is needed, such as when medicines cannot be taken by mouth.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of chemical substances involved in pain and helps lower an elevated body temperature.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration are decided by the healthcare professional based on factors such as age, body weight, and liver and kidney function. Do not use it without medical supervision or with other paracetamol-containing medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, and discomfort at the injection site may occur. Serious allergic reactions are uncommon but require immediate medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, kidney disease, regular heavy alcohol use, poor nutrition, dehydration, or an allergy to paracetamol. Do not exceed the prescribed amount, as an overdose can cause severe liver damage. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Mecobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 used to treat vitamin B12 deficiency, including deficiency-related anaemia and nerve problems such as tingling or numbness.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamin B12, which is needed for healthy red blood cell production and normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
This is an injection in a prefilled syringe and should be given by a healthcare professional. Use it only as prescribed; the dose and treatment schedule depend on the severity and cause of the deficiency.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; skin rash, nausea or headache may occur.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about any previous reaction to vitamin B12 or injections. Seek urgent medical help for difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a severe rash. Do not self-inject unless specifically trained and instructed to do so.

What is it used for?
Mecobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 used to prevent or treat vitamin B12 deficiency. It may help manage vitamin B12 deficiency-related megaloblastic anaemia and nerve problems such as tingling or numbness.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamin B12, which is needed for healthy red blood cell formation and normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take or use it only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the severity of deficiency and the product form. Do not self-treat unexplained anaemia, numbness or weakness without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache or skin rash may occur. Seek urgent medical help for signs of a severe allergic reaction.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to mecobalamin, vitamin B12 or cobalt. Inform the doctor about any previous medicine allergies and seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen. The underlying cause of vitamin B12 deficiency may need evaluation.

What is it used for?
This tablet is used as a nutritional supplement to provide alpha-lipoic acid, folic acid, methylcobalamin (vitamin B12), vitamin B6 and vitamin D3. It may be recommended to help meet nutritional needs and support normal nerve, blood and bone health.

How does it work?
These nutrients support normal nerve function, red blood cell formation, energy metabolism and bone health. Alpha-lipoic acid also acts as an antioxidant.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Swallow the tablet with water and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, headache or an unpleasant taste may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if a severe allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is diabetes, as alpha-lipoic acid may affect blood sugar levels. People taking medicines for diabetes should monitor their blood sugar as advised. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking other vitamin or mineral supplements. Do not take more than the recommended amount, especially for long-term use.

What is it used for?
This tablet is used as a nutritional supplement to provide L-carnitine, vitamin B12 (mecobalamin) and folic acid. It may be prescribed when these nutrients are low or when additional nutritional support is needed.

How does it work?
L-carnitine helps the body use fatty acids for energy. Vitamin B12 and folic acid support normal nerve function and the formation of healthy red blood cells.

Take only as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, a history of seizures, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines or supplements being used. Do not use it to self-treat anaemia or vitamin deficiency without medical advice.

What is it used for?

It helps the body make healthy red blood cells and supports normal nerve function. It also helps maintain normal cell metabolism.

Take or use it exactly as directed on the product label or by the doctor. Do not exceed the recommended amount. The dose and duration depend on the reason for treatment and the product form.

Methylcobalamin and pyridoxine help support nerve function and normal blood-cell formation. Alpha lipoic acid acts as an antioxidant and supports normal energy metabolism.

Take it only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised.

Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache, or skin rash may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction develops.

Inform a doctor about any allergies, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or existing medical conditions before use. People with diabetes should monitor their blood sugar, as alpha lipoic acid may affect glucose levels. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
Mecobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 used to prevent or treat vitamin B12 deficiency. It may help manage deficiency-related problems such as certain types of anaemia and nerve symptoms, including tingling or numbness.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamin B12, which is needed for healthy red blood cell formation, DNA production and normal nerve function.
