Use exactly as directed by the doctor or stated on the product label. Do not change the dose or treatment duration without medical advice. The method of use depends on the formulation.

What is it used for?
Metronidazole is used to treat certain bacterial infections, especially infections caused by anaerobic bacteria, and some parasitic infections such as amoebiasis, giardiasis and trichomoniasis. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It damages the DNA of susceptible bacteria and parasites, stopping them from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Avoid alcohol while taking metronidazole and for at least 48 hours after the last dose.

What is it used for?
Used mainly to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itching, and watery eyes. It may also be prescribed when allergies are linked with asthma, but it is not a rescue medicine for sudden breathing difficulty.

Levocetirizine blocks histamine, which causes allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, chemicals involved in allergic inflammation and airway symptoms.

Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Continue any other asthma medicines as directed and do not use this medicine for a sudden asthma attack.

Sleepiness, headache, tiredness, dry mouth, and stomach discomfort or abdominal pain.

Precautions
Levocetirizine may cause sleepiness; use caution with driving, alcohol, or other medicines that cause drowsiness. What is it used for?
An Ayurvedic liver tonic is generally used to support liver health. Its exact use depends on the ingredients and product label.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 200 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the enzymes needed for their growth and reproduction, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, iron or zinc; follow the spacing instructions given by the doctor or pharmacist.

Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and difficulty sleeping.

What is it used for?
Omeprazole reduces excess stomach acid. It is mainly used to relieve acidity and heartburn, including symptoms caused by acid reflux, and may also be used for stomach ulcers as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It blocks the stomach’s acid-producing proton pumps, thereby reducing the amount of acid released into the stomach.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as advised by the doctor or stated on the label. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the recommended timing in relation to meals.

Headache, nausea, stomach pain, gas, diarrhoea or constipation.

Precautions
Seek medical advice for persistent symptoms, difficulty swallowing, repeated vomiting, unexplained weight loss, vomiting blood or black stools. Tell the doctor about other medicines being taken, especially clopidogrel, blood thinners, seizure medicines or medicines for HIV. Long-term use should be medically monitored.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn, indigestion and gas-related bloating or discomfort.

Magnesium hydroxide and aluminium hydroxide neutralise excess stomach acid. Activated dimethicone helps break up gas bubbles, making trapped gas easier to pass.

Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with the provided measuring device. Take it only as directed on the label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Antacids can affect the absorption of some medicines, so check with a doctor or pharmacist about spacing other medicines.

Constipation, loose stools or diarrhoea, nausea and stomach cramps may occur.

Precautions

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of acidity, heartburn, indigestion, gas and bloating.

How does it work?
Magnesium hydroxide and aluminium hydroxide neutralise excess stomach acid. Activated dimethicone helps break up gas bubbles, which may reduce bloating and discomfort.

How to take/use it
Shake the suspension well before use. Take it only as directed on the product label or by a doctor, using the measuring cup or spoon provided. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended.

Constipation or loose stools, nausea, stomach discomfort, and a chalky or minty taste may occur.

Precautions
Tell a doctor or pharmacist if there is kidney disease, persistent or recurrent stomach pain, vomiting, difficulty swallowing, or unexplained weight loss. Antacids may affect the absorption of other medicines; keep a suitable gap between this product and other medicines as advised by a pharmacist or doctor. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
ORS (oral rehydration solution) powder is used to prevent and treat dehydration caused by diarrhoea, vomiting, or loss of fluids and salts. It helps replace water and essential electrolytes such as sodium and potassium.

How does it work?
The glucose and salts in ORS help the intestine absorb water and electrolytes more effectively, restoring the body's fluid balance.

Dissolve the powder in the exact amount of clean water stated on the packet. Do not use less or more water, and do not add sugar or salt. Sip the prepared solution frequently. Prepare it fresh and follow the packet instructions for storage and disposal.

Nausea, vomiting, bloating, or mild stomach discomfort may occur, especially if taken too quickly.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical care for severe dehydration, extreme weakness, confusion, very little or no urine, inability to drink, persistent vomiting, blood in the stool, or diarrhoea that does not improve. What is it used for?

It contains glucose and electrolytes that help the intestine absorb water and salts, restoring the body's fluid balance.

Dissolve the powder in the exact amount of clean drinking water stated on the sachet. Do not use less or more water, and do not take the powder dry. Sip the prepared solution frequently, especially after loose motions or vomiting. Prepare a fresh solution as directed on the pack.

Nausea, vomiting, bloating, or mild stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Use only the recommended amount of water; an incorrectly diluted solution can be harmful. Seek urgent medical care for severe dehydration, persistent vomiting, blood in stools, very little urine, extreme weakness, confusion, or inability to drink. People with kidney disease, heart failure, or conditions requiring restricted salt or fluid intake should seek medical advice before use. Continue breastfeeding and normal feeding where possible.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve painful menstrual cramps and the associated lower abdominal pain or spasms.

Dicyclomine relaxes the muscles of the abdomen and uterus to reduce spasms. Mefenamic acid reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation.

Take only as prescribed by the doctor, preferably with or after food and with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin unless advised.

What is it used for?
Permethrin Lotion 5% is used to treat scabies, a skin infestation caused by tiny mites. It kills the mites and helps stop the infestation from spreading.

How does it work?
It acts on the nervous system of scabies mites, causing them to die. It also helps kill mite eggs.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the skin exactly as directed by the doctor or product instructions. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and wash hands after applying. Do not apply more often or use for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Temporary itching, redness, burning, stinging, tingling or a mild rash may occur after application.

Precautions
Do not swallow or use near the eyes or inside the mouth. Avoid applying to severely irritated or broken skin unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical advice if symptoms do not improve, become worse, or if severe skin irritation occurs. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding or in young children.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when one medicine alone is not enough.

Vildagliptin helps the body release insulin when blood sugar is high and reduces the release of glucagon. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin better.

It releases iodine, which kills or inactivates many types of bacteria, viruses and fungi.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine 5% is an antiseptic used to reduce germs on the skin and help prevent infection in minor cuts, wounds and burns, when intended for topical use.

It slowly releases iodine, which kills or inactivates many types of germs, including bacteria, viruses and fungi.

Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. For topical products, apply to clean, affected skin as directed and do not swallow. Do not use in the eyes unless the product is specifically meant for ophthalmic use.

For external use only unless specifically prescribed otherwise. Avoid use if allergic to povidone iodine or other iodine-containing antiseptics. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling or breathing difficulty occurs.

What is it used for?
Vonoprazan reduces excess stomach acid and is mainly used to treat acid reflux, heartburn and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), including acid-related irritation or damage of the food pipe. It may also be prescribed for other acid-related conditions.

How does it work?
Vonoprazan blocks the final step in stomach acid production. This lowers acidity and helps relieve acid reflux symptoms and allows acid-related irritation to heal.

Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water; it may generally be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or treatment duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, constipation, nausea, stomach pain, gas and headache.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a previous allergic reaction to vonoprazan. Inform the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Seek medical advice for persistent or worsening symptoms, difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood or black stools. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Acnebuster containing salicylic acid and glycolic acid is used for acne-prone skin. It may help unclog pores, reduce blackheads and whiteheads, and improve rough or uneven skin texture.

How does it work?
Salicylic acid helps remove excess oil and dead skin from inside pores. Glycolic acid exfoliates the skin surface, helping prevent pore blockage and improve skin texture.

How to take/use it
Use on clean, dry skin exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips and other sensitive areas. Wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Dryness, peeling, redness, stinging, burning or skin irritation may occur, especially when starting treatment.

Precautions
For external use only. Do not apply to broken, sunburned or irritated skin. Avoid using it with other strong exfoliants or irritating acne products unless advised by a healthcare professional. What is it used for?
Acnebuster containing salicylic acid and glycolic acid is a topical product used to help manage acne, pimples, clogged pores and excess dead skin on the face or other affected areas.

How does it work?
Salicylic acid helps unclog pores and remove excess oil and dead skin. Glycolic acid exfoliates the skin surface, helping improve blocked pores and uneven skin texture.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to clean, dry, affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips and other sensitive areas. Wash hands after use.

Common side effects
Mild stinging, dryness, redness, irritation, peeling or burning may occur, especially when starting treatment.

Precautions
Avoid using on broken, sunburned or irritated skin. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Use sun protection, as these ingredients may increase sensitivity to sunlight. Avoid combining with other harsh exfoliating or irritating skin products unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
This topical medicine is primarily used to help manage acne, unclog pores and improve uneven skin texture. It may also help reduce the appearance of mild dark spots and uneven pigmentation.

How does it work?
ATRA (tretinoin) increases skin cell turnover and helps prevent blocked pores. Glycolic acid exfoliates the skin, while niacinamide helps support the skin barrier and reduce irritation.

How to take/use it
For skin use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, completely dry skin exactly as directed by the doctor or product instructions. Avoid the eyes, lips, nostrils and broken or irritated skin. Use sunscreen during the day.

Common side effects
Dryness, redness, peeling, burning, stinging, itching and increased sensitivity to sunlight may occur, especially during the first few weeks.

Precautions
Avoid excessive sun exposure and use sunscreen regularly. Do not use on sunburned, broken or severely irritated skin. Avoid combining it with other irritating exfoliants or acne treatments unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or blistering occurs. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This is a topical skincare product intended to support skin hydration, smoothness and overall appearance. It is not enough information to confirm treatment of a specific skin disease or medical condition.

Mild stinging, redness, dryness or irritation may occur, particularly in sensitive skin.

Stop use if significant irritation, swelling or rash develops. Avoid using on damaged skin. Use cautiously with other exfoliating or irritating skincare products. Seek medical advice for persistent or severe skin reactions.

Glycolic acid exfoliates the skin surface, while salicylic acid helps loosen dead skin and oil from clogged pores. Vitamin E helps provide antioxidant support.

It is converted into alkaline substances in the body, which increase the pH of urine and reduce its acidity.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve dry cough associated with cold or allergy symptoms. It may also help reduce sneezing, runny nose and watery eyes.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan reduces the cough reflex. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that reduces allergy-related symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the label or by a doctor. Use the measuring device supplied if it is a liquid, and do not take more than the recommended amount. Do not combine with other cough, cold or antihistamine medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Use medical advice in children, older adults, glaucoma, prostate or urinary problems, and during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This product is used as a nutritional supplement providing L-arginine and proanthocyanidins. It may support nitric oxide production, blood-vessel function and antioxidant protection. The exact medical use should be confirmed with a doctor or pharmacist.

L-arginine is used by the body to produce nitric oxide, which helps blood vessels relax. Proanthocyanidins are antioxidant plant compounds that help protect cells from oxidative damage.

What is it used for?

How to take/use it

Common side effects

Precautions
Use cautiously and seek medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. What is it used for?
Atorvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, especially “bad” LDL cholesterol and triglycerides. It also helps reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It reduces the liver’s production of cholesterol by blocking an enzyme involved in cholesterol formation. This helps lower cholesterol levels in the blood.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Take it regularly and do not stop treatment without medical advice. Continue recommended diet, exercise and follow-up blood tests.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, indigestion and muscle aches or pain may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, thyroid problems or a history of muscle problems. Seek medical advice promptly for unexplained or severe muscle pain, weakness, fever or dark urine. It is not usually used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, including certain antibiotics, antifungals and cholesterol medicines, because interactions can increase side effects.

What is it used for?
Atorvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol, especially LDL (bad) cholesterol, and to help reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme involved in making cholesterol in the liver. This lowers LDL cholesterol and helps reduce the build-up of fatty deposits in blood vessels.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, with or without food, preferably at the same time each day. Continue dietary and lifestyle advice given by the doctor. Do not stop it without medical advice.

Common side effects

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, or any unexplained muscle pain or weakness. Seek medical advice promptly for severe muscle pain, weakness, or dark urine. What is it used for?

What is it used for?

Used for certain inflamed fungal skin infections, especially when there may also be a bacterial infection. It should be used only when prescribed, as the steroid component can worsen or mask some skin infections.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole and iodochlorhydroxyquinoline act against fungi, while gentamicin acts against certain bacteria. Clobetasol reduces redness, swelling and itching caused by inflammation.

How to take/use it
For use on the skin only. Apply a thin layer to the affected area exactly as directed by the doctor. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and do not cover the area with a bandage unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks, or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice and only for the prescribed condition. Avoid prolonged use and use on the face, groin, skin folds, broken skin or in children unless specifically advised. Stop and seek medical advice if the infection worsens, spreads, or causes severe irritation. Avoid the eyes and seek medical advice if accidental contact occurs.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 200 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the urinary tract, respiratory tract, skin and other tissues, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops bacteria from multiplying by blocking enzymes needed for bacterial DNA replication.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water and do not take it at the same time as antacids or mineral supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, iron or zinc; follow the prescribed spacing instructions. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and sleep disturbances.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice. Stop taking it and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, a severe rash, breathing difficulty or persistent watery or bloody diarrhoea. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, seizures, heart rhythm problems, tendon disorders, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Avoid driving if dizziness or other nervous-system effects occur.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat certain bacterial and protozoal infections, especially infectious diarrhoea and dysentery, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin kills susceptible bacteria. Ornidazole acts against certain parasites and bacteria that can cause intestinal infections.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the recommended course. Swallow with water, with or without food. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc; keep a suitable time gap as advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not self-medicate for diarrhoea.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and a metallic or bitter taste may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol during treatment and ask a doctor when it is safe to drink after the last dose. Seek medical advice if severe or persistent diarrhoea, tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, seizures, severe dizziness, or an irregular heartbeat occurs. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney or liver problems, seizures, heart-rhythm problems, tendon disorders, or medicines being taken. Avoid driving if dizzy or drowsy.

What is it used for?
Fusidic acid cream is used to treat bacterial skin infections, including infected cuts, wounds and conditions such as impetigo, when caused by bacteria sensitive to fusidic acid.

How does it work?
It is a topical antibiotic that stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, burning, stinging, itching, redness or rash at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use for fungal or viral infections unless advised by a healthcare professional. Avoid prolonged or repeated use, as this may encourage antibiotic resistance. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or worsening infection occurs.

What is it used for?
Used for bacterial skin infections accompanied by inflammation, redness, itching or swelling, such as infected eczema or dermatitis, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Fusidic acid stops the growth of certain bacteria on the skin. Beclomethasone dipropionate is a corticosteroid that reduces skin inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as directed by the doctor. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, irritation, redness or dryness at the application site. Prolonged or repeated use may cause skin thinning or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Use only on the condition for which it was prescribed. Do not use on untreated fungal or viral skin infections, acne, or large areas of skin unless advised by a doctor. Avoid prolonged use, covering the area tightly, or applying it to the face, skin folds or broken skin unless specifically directed. Stop and seek medical advice if the infection worsens, the skin becomes severely irritated, or there is no improvement.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of migraine headaches, especially when the migraine is accompanied by nausea or vomiting.

How does it work?
Naproxen reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Domperidone helps control nausea and vomiting and supports movement of the stomach.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow with water, preferably with or after food to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Avoid taking other naproxen or NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness, headache, dry mouth or stomach cramps may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an irregular heartbeat. Domperidone may affect heart rhythm and may interact with some medicines. Naproxen can increase the risk of stomach bleeding, kidney problems and cardiovascular events, particularly with prolonged use. Avoid during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed, especially in the later months. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or fainting.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve migraine headache and associated nausea or vomiting.

How does it work?
Naproxen reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Domperidone helps control nausea and vomiting and may improve the absorption of naproxen.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow with water, preferably with or after food, to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take it with other naproxen, ibuprofen, diclofenac or similar painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dry mouth, dizziness or headache. Naproxen may rarely cause stomach ulcers or bleeding.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or allergy to aspirin or other NSAID painkillers. Domperidone may affect heart rhythm; inform the doctor about heart problems or medicines that affect heart rhythm. Avoid during pregnancy, particularly after 20 weeks and in the last trimester, unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest discomfort, fainting or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Lactic acid bacillus helps restore the balance of healthy bacteria in the intestines. It may be used to support digestive health, including during or after diarrhoea or antibiotic treatment. The added vitamins provide nutritional supplementation.

How does it work?
It supplies beneficial bacteria that help support the normal balance of microorganisms in the gut. The vitamins support normal body functions, depending on the specific vitamins present.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Follow any storage instructions on the pack.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating or mild abdominal discomfort may occur. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use if there is a weakened immune system, serious illness or a central venous catheter. Seek medical advice for diarrhoea with fever, blood in the stool, signs of dehydration or symptoms that do not improve. Check with a healthcare professional if taking antibiotics or other medicines.

What is it used for?
Doxycycline is an antibiotic used to treat a range of bacterial infections. It may also be prescribed for certain skin conditions, such as acne, when considered appropriate by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making proteins needed for their growth and survival, helping control the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course. Swallow with a full glass of water while sitting or standing, and do not lie down immediately afterwards. Keep it separate from antacids and supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc as advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Follow the product label or prescription for the exact dose and timing.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach upset, heartburn or irritation of the food pipe, headache, and increased sensitivity to sunlight.

Precautions
Avoid excessive sunlight and use protective clothing and sunscreen. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, plans for pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver problems, or an allergy to tetracycline antibiotics. Use in young children only when specifically prescribed. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, difficulty swallowing, severe skin reactions, or signs of an allergic reaction. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about all medicines and supplements being used.

What is it used for?
This medicine is an antibiotic used to treat infections caused by susceptible bacteria. The lactic acid bacillus is included to help support healthy intestinal bacteria during antibiotic treatment.

How does it work?
Doxycycline stops susceptible bacteria from making proteins needed for their growth. Lactic acid bacillus is a beneficial bacterium that may help maintain the normal balance of gut bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with a full glass of water. Do not lie down immediately after taking it. Avoid taking it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium or magnesium; follow a healthcare professional’s advice about spacing them. Complete the prescribed course unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, diarrhoea and increased sensitivity to sunlight may occur.

Precautions
Avoid unnecessary sunlight and use sun protection. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, difficulty swallowing, severe headache or vision changes. Tell the healthcare professional about pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver problems, swallowing or food-pipe problems, or allergy to tetracycline antibiotics. Doxycycline is generally avoided in pregnancy and in children under 8 years unless specifically prescribed. Take medical advice about other medicines and supplements.

What is it used for?
Dydrogesterone is used to treat conditions caused by low or ineffective progesterone, such as irregular or painful periods, endometriosis, and some fertility or pregnancy-related problems. It may also be prescribed with oestrogen during hormone replacement therapy to protect the lining of the womb.

How does it work?
It is a synthetic form of the natural hormone progesterone. It helps regulate the womb lining and supports a normal menstrual cycle.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, as the dose and treatment schedule vary depending on the condition. Swallow the tablet with water and try to take it at the same time each day. Do not stop treatment or take a double dose after a missed dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache or migraine, nausea, abdominal discomfort, breast tenderness, changes in menstrual bleeding, or spotting may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about unexplained vaginal bleeding, liver problems, a history of hormone-sensitive cancer, migraine, or depression. Seek medical advice if jaundice, severe abdominal pain, or unusual bleeding occurs. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only when prescribed. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines being taken, as some medicines may reduce its effect.

What is it used for?
Eberconazole cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch. It may also be used for other fungal infections of the skin as prescribed.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which prevents their growth and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to eberconazole or any ingredient in the cream. Avoid applying to the eyes, inside the mouth, or severely broken skin. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve as expected.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron oral solution is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including those related to cancer treatment, surgery, or other medical conditions.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals that can trigger nausea and vomiting in the brain and digestive system.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Measure the oral solution with the provided measuring device, not a household spoon. Do not take more or use it for longer than directed.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, tiredness, dizziness, and flushing may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ondansetron or similar medicines, liver disease, heart rhythm problems, or low potassium or magnesium levels. It may affect heart rhythm, especially with certain medicines or in people with heart conditions. Seek medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic symptoms, or symptoms such as agitation, sweating, fever, muscle stiffness, or diarrhoea while taking medicines that affect serotonin.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron 4 mg tablets are used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including nausea and vomiting related to chemotherapy, radiotherapy or surgery. Use it only as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Ondansetron blocks serotonin signals that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Follow the timing instructions given by the doctor, especially if it is being used around chemotherapy, radiotherapy or surgery. Do not take more or for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, tiredness and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of abnormal heart rhythm, long QT syndrome, low potassium or magnesium levels, liver disease, or an allergy to ondansetron. It may affect heart rhythm and can interact with some medicines, including apomorphine and certain medicines that affect heart rhythm or serotonin levels. Seek medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic symptoms or severe agitation with sweating, fever and muscle stiffness.

What is it used for?
Bacillus clausii spores suspension is a probiotic used to help restore the balance of healthy bacteria in the intestine, especially during or after diarrhoea or antibiotic treatment.

How does it work?
It contains spores of Bacillus clausii, which can survive in the intestine and help support the normal balance of intestinal microorganisms.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not inject it. Shake the suspension if instructed on the label, and use it only within the recommended storage and expiry period.

Common side effects
It is generally well tolerated. Mild gas, bloating or stomach discomfort may occasionally occur. Allergic reactions are rare.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to Bacillus clausii or any ingredient in the product. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, fever or signs of dehydration. People with severely weakened immunity or serious illness should use it only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used to treat acidity, heartburn and acid reflux (GERD). It may also be prescribed when reflux is accompanied by nausea or vomiting.

How does it work?
Esomeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps improve movement of the upper digestive tract and helps control nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed. Swallow the enteric-coated/sustained-release medicine whole with water; do not crush, chew or break it. It is generally taken before food, but follow the product label or prescriber’s instructions.

Common side effects
Headache, abdominal discomfort or pain, diarrhoea, constipation, nausea, dry mouth and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Domperidone can rarely affect heart rhythm. Tell the prescriber about heart disease, an irregular heartbeat, liver disease, electrolyte problems, or any medicines being taken, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or certain antibiotics/antifungals. Do not use without medical advice if there is gastrointestinal bleeding, blockage or perforation, or a prolactin-related tumour. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, severe dizziness or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Consult a doctor during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used to treat acid reflux (GERD), heartburn and indigestion, especially when symptoms are associated with delayed stomach emptying, bloating or nausea.

How does it work?
Esomeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Levosulpride helps improve stomach movement and the passage of food, which may reduce reflux and digestive discomfort.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the enteric-coated sustained-release medicine whole with water; do not crush, chew or break it. Follow the prescribed timing in relation to meals and do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Headache, nausea, abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhoea or constipation, dizziness, drowsiness and restlessness. Increased breast fullness or milk production may occur due to levosulpride.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver or kidney problems, a history of seizures, intestinal obstruction or bleeding, or hormone-related conditions. Levosulpride may cause drowsiness or dizziness; avoid driving if affected. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially sedatives, antipsychotics and medicines that affect heart rhythm. Seek medical advice for black stools, vomiting blood, severe abdominal pain or persistent symptoms.

What is it used for?
Etoricoxib is used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness caused by arthritis, including osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis. It may also be prescribed for short-term treatment of acute gout and other painful conditions.

How does it work?
It selectively blocks COX-2 enzymes that produce chemicals responsible for pain and inflammation. This helps reduce pain, swelling and stiffness.

Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet whole with water; it may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or combine it with other anti-inflammatory painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, swelling of the feet or legs, and increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure, stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney disease, liver disease, or allergy to aspirin or other anti-inflammatory medicines. It may increase the risk of heart attack or stroke, especially with long-term use or in people with cardiovascular risk factors. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, black stools, severe allergic reactions or unusual swelling.

What is it used for?
Etoricoxib is used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness caused by osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and other joint conditions. It may also be prescribed for short-term treatment of acute gout or other severe pain, as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It selectively blocks COX-2 enzymes that produce substances responsible for pain and inflammation. This helps reduce pain, swelling and stiffness.

Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water, with or without food. Do not take more than prescribed or use it for longer than recommended.

Tell the doctor if there is a history of heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure, stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney disease, liver disease or allergy to painkillers. Febuxostat is used for the long-term treatment of gout and high uric acid levels. It helps prevent uric acid crystal build-up and future gout attacks. It is not a painkiller and does not provide immediate relief during an acute gout attack.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called xanthine oxidase, which reduces the body's production of uric acid.

Take it exactly as prescribed and continue it regularly, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop or change the dose without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Provides DHA, vitamin B12 and folic acid. These nutrients support normal nerve function and red blood cell formation. DHA and folate are also important during pregnancy.

How does it work?
DHA is an omega-3 fatty acid found in brain and retinal structures. Vitamin B12 and folic acid support cell division and red blood cell production.

Use according to prescribed directions. Do not determine dose from the ingredient list alone.

Digestive discomfort or nausea may occur.

The listed folic acid strength is 5 mg. Use under medical guidance, particularly during pregnancy or when taking other vitamin supplements.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron and folic acid deficiency, which can lead to nutritional anaemia and tiredness. It supports the formation of healthy red blood cells and may be prescribed when increased nutritional needs occur, such as during pregnancy.

How does it work?
Iron helps make haemoglobin, the substance that carries oxygen in the blood. Folic acid and vitamin B12 support the formation and normal development of red blood cells.

Take by mouth exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. It is usually better absorbed on an empty stomach, but it may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Keep out of reach of children, as an iron overdose can be dangerous. Tell the doctor if there is iron overload, a blood disorder, or a history of stomach or intestinal problems. Folic acid may mask some signs of vitamin B12 deficiency, so medical advice is important when anaemia has not been properly diagnosed. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about other medicines and supplements being taken.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron and folic acid deficiency, including nutritional anaemia caused by low levels of these nutrients. It may also be prescribed when the body's need for iron and folate is increased.

How does it work?
Iron helps the body make haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood. Folic acid supports the formation of healthy red blood cells, while vitamin C helps improve iron absorption.

Take exactly as directed by the doctor or as stated on the product label. Swallow with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. If stomach upset occurs, taking it with food may help. Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and dark-coloured stools. Dark stools are common with iron supplements.

Keep out of reach of children, as an iron overdose can be dangerous.

What is it used for?
Fexofenadine 120 mg tablets are used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching. Fexofenadine may also be used to relieve itching and hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It is an antihistamine that blocks the action of histamine, a substance responsible for many allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take the tablet exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the package instructions. Swallow it with water. Avoid taking it with fruit juice, as this may reduce its effect. If using antacids containing aluminium or magnesium, ask a pharmacist about separating their use from fexofenadine.

Headache, nausea, dizziness, and mild drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Tell a doctor or pharmacist if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, persistent, or worsening.

What is it used for?
Used as a topical skincare product to exfoliate dead skin cells, help unclog pores, and improve the appearance of uneven skin texture and tone. It may be useful for oily or acne-prone skin.

How does it work?
Glycolic acid and salicylic acid exfoliate the skin and help clear excess oil and blocked pores. Niacinamide, vitamin E and Rosa canina fruit extract help support the skin’s appearance and condition.

For external use only. Apply to clean, dry skin as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips and broken or irritated skin. Do not use more often than recommended.

Patch test before wider use. Use sunscreen during the day, as exfoliating acids can increase sensitivity to sunlight. Avoid combining with other strong exfoliating or irritating products unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use if severe irritation or an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Used in skincare to exfoliate dead skin cells, help unclog pores and improve uneven skin texture. It may also help reduce excess oil and the appearance of blemishes.

How does it work?
Glycolic acid and salicylic acid exfoliate the skin, helping remove surface dead cells and clear blocked pores. Niacinamide, vitamin E and Rosa canina fruit extract help support and condition the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to clean, dry skin exactly as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips and broken or irritated skin. Use sunscreen during the day.

Mild stinging, redness, dryness, peeling or irritation may occur, especially when starting use.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve heartburn, acid indigestion and symptoms of acid reflux, such as a burning feeling in the chest or an unpleasant taste caused by stomach acid.

Sodium alginate forms a protective layer that helps prevent stomach contents from flowing back into the food pipe. Sodium bicarbonate and calcium carbonate help neutralise excess stomach acid.

Shake the suspension well before use. Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If symptoms continue or keep returning, seek medical advice.

Bloating, nausea, constipation or diarrhoea may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if troublesome or unusual symptoms develop.

Precautions
Tell a doctor or pharmacist before use if there is kidney disease, heart failure, or a need to follow a low-sodium or low-calcium diet. Antacids can affect the absorption of some medicines, so check with a pharmacist about separating this product from other medicines. Seek medical advice for severe, persistent or unexplained symptoms, difficulty swallowing, vomiting, weight loss or chest pain.

What is it used for?
Finasteride 1 mg is used in adult men to treat male pattern hair loss. It may help slow hair loss and support hair regrowth with regular use as prescribed.

How does it work?
It reduces the formation of dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone that can shrink hair follicles and contribute to male pattern hair loss.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole and take it regularly. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Reduced sexual desire, difficulty getting or keeping an erection, and changes in ejaculation may occur. Mood changes, including low mood or depression, can also occur.

For adult men only unless specifically prescribed otherwise. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should not handle crushed or broken tablets, as finasteride may harm a developing male baby. Seek medical advice if breast lumps, pain, or nipple discharge occur.

What is it used for?
A pregnancy diagnostic kit is used to check for pregnancy by detecting human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) in urine.

How does it work?
The test detects hCG, a hormone produced during pregnancy. A positive result usually indicates pregnancy.

How to take/use it
Use the urine sample and follow the instructions provided with the kit. Check the result only within the time stated in the instructions. If the result is negative but pregnancy is still suspected, repeat the test later or seek medical advice.

No side effects are expected from using the test kit.

Do not use an expired or damaged kit. A test taken very early may show a false-negative result. A positive result should be confirmed with a healthcare professional, especially if there is pain or bleeding.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of indigestion, bloating and gas, especially when related to meals.

Papain and fungal diastase are digestive enzymes that help break down proteins and carbohydrates. Simethicone helps combine gas bubbles, making trapped gas easier to pass.

Dissolve the effervescent tablet in a glass of water and take it exactly as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Do not swallow it dry, and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Do not use if allergic to papain, fungal diastase, simethicone or any other ingredient. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, blood in the stool or ongoing digestive symptoms. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?

Permethrin soap 1% is used to help treat parasitic infestations of the skin, such as scabies or lice, when recommended for that use. Follow the product label or medical advice, as the exact use may vary by product.

How does it work?
Permethrin kills parasites by affecting their nervous system. It works on parasites present on the skin or hair.

How to take/use it
Use only on the skin and follow the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Rinse thoroughly if directed, wash hands after use, and do not use more often than recommended.

Common side effects
Temporary skin irritation, burning, redness, dryness or itching may occur.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid use on broken or severely irritated skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Keep away from children and avoid contact with the eyes. If symptoms continue or return, consult a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to reduce redness, swelling, itching and thick, scaly skin in steroid-responsive conditions such as psoriasis, eczema and dermatitis, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Clobetasol is a very strong corticosteroid that reduces skin inflammation and itching. Salicylic acid helps soften and remove thick, scaly skin, allowing the medicine to work better.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected area exactly as prescribed. Wash hands after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid the eyes, face, groin, underarms and broken or infected skin unless specifically advised. Do not cover the treated area with a tight dressing unless directed by a doctor.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, irritation, dryness, itching, skin thinning, stretch marks or small bumps around hair follicles may occur at the application site.

Precautions
Clobetasol is a very potent steroid and should not be used on large areas or for longer than prescribed. Avoid prolonged use, especially in children. Do not use on untreated skin infections or near the eyes. Stop and seek medical advice if the condition worsens or signs of infection develop. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used to treat certain inflamed, itchy, thickened or scaly skin conditions, including psoriasis and eczema, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Clobetasol reduces skin inflammation, redness and itching. Salicylic acid softens and removes thick scales, helping the medicine reach the affected skin.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Use it only on the affected areas and do not cover with a bandage or dressing unless directed. Wash hands after applying, unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, itching, irritation, dryness or redness at the application site. Prolonged or excessive use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid the eyes, face, groin, armpits and broken or infected skin unless specifically advised by a doctor. Do not use for longer or on larger areas than prescribed, as clobetasol is a very potent steroid. Stop and seek medical advice if the condition worsens or signs of infection develop. Use in children only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used when prescribed for certain bacterial or protozoal intestinal infections that may cause diarrhoea, dysentery, stomach discomfort and gas.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin and metronidazole act against certain bacteria and parasites causing intestinal infection. Simethicone helps break up gas bubbles and may relieve bloating and discomfort.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with the supplied measuring device. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not self-medicate for diarrhoea.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, metallic taste, headache and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney problems, seizures, heart-rhythm problems or tendon disorders. Keep antacids and supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc separate from this medicine as advised by the doctor or pharmacist. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe rash, breathing difficulty, or severe watery or bloody diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain bacterial and protozoal infections of the stomach and intestines, which may cause diarrhoea, loose motions, dysentery or stomach infection. Simethicone helps relieve gas and bloating.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin kills susceptible bacteria, while metronidazole acts against certain anaerobic bacteria and parasites. Simethicone helps gas bubbles join together so they can pass more easily.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with the supplied measuring device. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not take antacids or iron, calcium or zinc supplements at the same time without medical advice, as they may reduce ofloxacin absorption.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, metallic taste, headache or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose. Tell the doctor if pregnant, breastfeeding, or if there is kidney disease, epilepsy, nerve problems or a history of tendon problems. Seek medical help for a serious allergic reaction, severe or persistent diarrhoea, tendon pain or swelling, or numbness and tingling. Use in children only when specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
This topical skincare formulation is typically used to help improve the appearance of uneven skin tone and dullness while supporting skin moisturisation. The exact intended use should be confirmed from the product label.

How does it work?
Liquorice and green tea extracts are commonly used in skincare for their skin-soothing and antioxidant properties. Jojoba esters help soften and moisturise the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply as directed on the product label to clean, dry skin. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not apply to broken or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Mild irritation, redness, itching or dryness may occur, especially in sensitive skin.

Precautions
Patch-test before wider use. Stop using if significant irritation or an allergic reaction develops. Avoid contact with the eyes. Keep out of reach of children and follow the product label instructions.

What is it used for?
Zinc oxide sunscreen is used to protect the skin from harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays and help prevent sunburn and sun-related skin damage.

How does it work?
It forms a mineral barrier on the skin that reflects and scatters UV rays, reducing their exposure to the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply evenly to all exposed skin before sun exposure, following the product label. Reapply as directed, especially after swimming, sweating or towel drying. Use protective clothing and avoid prolonged direct sun exposure.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, dryness or itching may occur. Serious allergic reactions are uncommon.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes. Stop use if severe irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Do not apply to significantly damaged skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Sunscreen does not provide complete protection from UV rays.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful cramps and spasmodic pain, especially menstrual cramps. It may also be prescribed for cramp-like abdominal pain.

How does it work?
Drotaverine relaxes spasming muscles in the abdomen and uterus. Mefenamic acid reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow with or after food to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness, headache, or skin rash.

Precautions
Avoid if there is an allergy to mefenamic acid, drotaverine, aspirin, or other painkillers. Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart problems, asthma triggered by painkillers, or low blood pressure. Avoid combining it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, or swelling. It should generally be avoided in the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of mild to moderate pain and fever. It may help with pain where inflammation is also present, but it should be used only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever. Mefenamic acid is an anti-inflammatory painkiller that reduces substances involved in pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed or as directed on the label, with water and preferably after food. Do not take more than the recommended amount, use it for longer than advised, or take other medicines containing paracetamol or mefenamic acid/NSAIDs unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine or seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, asthma or allergy triggered by painkillers, or use of blood thinners. Avoid alcohol. Do not use during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, unless specifically prescribed. Stop and seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin rash, vomiting blood or black stools.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve mild to moderate pain, reduce fever and help ease inflammation.

How does it work?
Mefenamic acid reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist, especially for children. Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with an accurate measuring device. Taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, dizziness or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to mefenamic acid, paracetamol or other painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin. Seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, heart problems or dehydration. Avoid combining it with other paracetamol-containing or anti-inflammatory medicines unless advised. Avoid excessive alcohol. Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve painful menstrual cramps and spasmodic abdominal pain. It should be used only for the condition and duration advised by a doctor.

How does it work?
Mefenamic acid reduces pain and inflammation, while dicyclomine relaxes spasms in the muscles of the abdomen and intestines.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food and with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea or constipation, dizziness, dry mouth and blurred vision may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if allergic to mefenamic acid, dicyclomine or similar painkillers. Inform the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, or bowel blockage. Avoid alcohol and driving if dizzy or if vision is blurred. Do not use during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for severe stomach pain, black stools, vomiting blood, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole 1% Dusting Powder is used to treat fungal skin infections such as athlete’s foot, ringworm, jock itch and fungal rashes in skin folds. It helps reduce itching, redness and irritation caused by these infections.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole is an antifungal medicine that damages the protective outer layer of fungi, stopping their growth and helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply the powder to clean, completely dry affected skin and nearby skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Keep the area dry and wash hands before and after use. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and do not inhale the powder.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, burning, stinging, itching or dryness may occur at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to clotrimazole or any ingredient. Avoid applying to the eyes, mouth, open wounds or severely irritated skin. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops. Consult a healthcare professional if the infection worsens or does not improve with treatment.

What is it used for?
Prickly heat powder is used to help relieve itching, irritation and discomfort caused by prickly heat or heat rash. It also helps keep the skin dry and reduce friction in sweaty areas.

How does it work?
The powder absorbs excess moisture from the skin and helps reduce rubbing, which may soothe irritation associated with heat and sweating.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a small amount to clean, dry skin, especially in areas prone to sweating. Avoid inhaling the powder and keep it away from the eyes, nose and mouth.

Common side effects
Skin irritation, dryness or an allergic rash may occur in sensitive people.

Precautions
Do not apply to broken, infected or severely irritated skin. Stop use if irritation or rash develops. Avoid inhaling the powder, and keep away from children. Seek medical advice if the rash is severe, spreading or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Used to help prevent and relieve prickly heat (heat rash), sweating-related skin discomfort and irritation.

How does it work?
The powder helps absorb excess moisture and reduce friction on the skin, which may soothe irritation caused by heat and sweating.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a light layer to clean, dry skin as directed on the product label. Avoid inhaling the powder.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, dryness or an allergic reaction may occur in sensitive individuals.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and broken or damaged skin. Do not inhale the powder. Stop use if irritation or rash worsens. Seek medical advice if the heat rash is severe or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Used to help relieve prickly heat-related itching, skin irritation and discomfort, while helping keep the skin dry.

How does it work?
The powder helps absorb moisture and reduce friction on the skin, which may help relieve discomfort associated with prickly heat.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a small amount to clean, dry skin as directed on the product label. Avoid inhaling the powder and keep it away from the eyes.

Common side effects
Skin dryness or irritation may occur in sensitive individuals.

Precautions
Do not apply to broken, infected or severely irritated skin. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and nose, and do not inhale the powder. Stop use if irritation or an allergic reaction develops.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergies, especially allergic rhinitis such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes.

How does it work?
Bilastine blocks histamine, a substance responsible for many allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which can contribute to swelling and inflammation in the airways and nose.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor and follow the instructions on the label. Swallow the tablet with water. Bilastine is generally taken on an empty stomach, as food or fruit juice may reduce its absorption. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Headache, drowsiness, dizziness, stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Use cautiously if there is a history of severe liver or kidney problems, or allergy to either ingredient. Montelukast may rarely cause sleep problems, mood changes, unusual behaviour, anxiety, depression, or suicidal thoughts; contact a doctor promptly if these occur. This medicine is not a substitute for a prescribed quick-relief inhaler during an asthma attack. Avoid driving or operating machinery if drowsiness or dizziness occurs.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, a runny or blocked nose, nasal itching, and itchy or watery eyes.

How does it work?
Desloratadine blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, substances that contribute to allergic inflammation and nasal congestion.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice. It is not intended to provide immediate relief during a sudden asthma attack.

Common side effects
Headache, dry mouth, tiredness, stomach pain, nausea, or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding before use. Montelukast may rarely cause mood or behaviour changes, disturbed sleep, agitation, depression, or suicidal thoughts; seek medical advice promptly if these occur. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or sleepiness occurs. Seek urgent help for signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as facial swelling or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose, and watery or itchy eyes.

How does it work?
Fexofenadine blocks histamine, a chemical that causes allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, substances that contribute to inflammation and nasal allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid taking it with apple, orange, or grapefruit juice, and ask a pharmacist about the timing of aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, dizziness, or tiredness may occur.

Precautions
Montelukast may rarely cause mood or behaviour changes, sleep problems, depression, or suicidal thoughts; seek medical help promptly if these occur. Use only under medical advice during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in liver disease. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or sleepiness occurs. This medicine is not a rescue treatment for a sudden asthma attack.

What is it used for?
This medicine is mainly used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, nasal itching, and itchy or watery eyes. It may also be prescribed as an add-on treatment for some people with asthma. It is not meant to relieve a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, chemicals that can cause swelling and narrowing of the airways and contribute to allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid driving or operating machinery if it causes drowsiness.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving if drowsy. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other medicines being used. Stop the medicine and seek medical advice promptly if unusual dreams, sleep problems, agitation, depression, aggressive behaviour, or thoughts of self-harm occur. Do not use it as a rescue medicine for a sudden asthma attack.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergies such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose, and watery or itchy eyes. It may also be prescribed as an add-on treatment for asthma, but it does not relieve a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, a substance that causes allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, chemicals involved in allergic inflammation and airway narrowing.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device and do not use a household spoon. Shake the bottle well before use. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Sleepiness may occur; avoid driving or alcohol until the effect is known. Seek medical advice promptly if mood or behaviour changes, disturbing dreams, agitation, depression, or suicidal thoughts occur. This medicine is not a rescue treatment for a sudden asthma attack. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding, and about other medicines that may cause drowsiness.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergies, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It may be prescribed for allergic rhinitis, including seasonal or dust-related allergies.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which can contribute to inflammation and nasal or breathing symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take only in the dose and frequency prescribed by the doctor. Follow the product label, and do not take more than recommended. This medicine is not intended to relieve a sudden asthma attack.

Common side effects
Drowsiness or sleepiness, headache, tiredness, dry mouth, stomach pain, nausea, or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions

What is it used for?
N,N-Diethylbenzamide 12% w/w is used as a topical insect repellent to help protect exposed skin from insect bites, such as mosquito bites.

How does it work?
It works by interfering with the ability of insects to detect and approach the smell of human skin. It repels insects rather than killing them.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to exposed skin or clothing as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and broken or irritated skin. Wash hands after application.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching or a burning sensation may occur. Eye irritation can occur if the product gets into the eyes.

Precautions
Do not swallow or apply near the eyes or mouth. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Keep out of reach of children and follow the product label for age restrictions and reapplication instructions.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanic acid is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ears, sinuses, throat, lungs, urinary tract, skin and teeth. It does not treat viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria. Clavulanic acid helps protect amoxycillin from bacterial enzymes that can make the antibiotic ineffective.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and preferably at the start of a meal to reduce stomach upset. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not double the next dose if a dose is missed.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion and skin rash may occur. Fungal infections such as oral or vaginal thrush can also occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, other beta-lactam antibiotics or this medicine. Inform the doctor about previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, kidney disease, allergies, or glandular fever. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Contact a doctor for severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Use only when prescribed and do not share leftover antibiotics.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat a range of bacterial infections, such as infections of the ears, sinuses, throat, lungs, skin, urinary tract and teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes that can make some bacteria resistant to it.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Take it with a meal or snack to reduce stomach upset. Do not share this medicine or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, other beta-lactam antibiotics or this medicine. Inform the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, and any medicines being used. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, a severe skin rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Amoxicillin with clavulanic acid is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, sinuses, throat, chest, skin, urinary tract and teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxicillin kills susceptible bacteria. Clavulanic acid helps protect amoxicillin from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against a wider range of infections.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not use leftover antibiotics or stop treatment early, even if symptoms improve. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur. Mild thrush can also occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxicillin, other beta-lactam antibiotics or clavulanic acid. Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, or a history of jaundice or liver problems with antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Amoxicillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, sinuses, throat, lungs, skin, urinary tract and teeth, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxicillin kills susceptible bacteria. Clavulanic acid helps protect amoxicillin from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against a wider range of infections.

How to take/use it
Take or give it exactly as prescribed. If it is a liquid suspension, shake the bottle well before each use and measure it with an oral syringe or measuring device. Taking it with a meal may help reduce stomach upset. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve, unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise.

Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur. Thrush can also develop.
