Telmisartan 40 mg is mainly used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It may also be prescribed to help reduce the risk of certain heart and blood-vessel problems in selected high-risk adults.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of a hormone called angiotensin II, which normally narrows blood vessels and raises blood pressure. This helps relax the blood vessels and lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop treatment without medical advice, even if feeling well.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, low blood pressure, tiredness, diarrhoea, and back pain may occur. Contact a doctor if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, or high potassium levels. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially lithium, diuretics, or painkillers such as ibuprofen. Rise slowly if dizziness occurs.

What is it used for?
Used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It may be prescribed when one medicine alone does not control blood pressure adequately.

How does it work?
Telmisartan relaxes blood vessels by blocking the action of a hormone that causes blood vessels to tighten. Amlodipine also relaxes and widens blood vessels, helping blood flow more easily and lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, and swallow with water. It may be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, tiredness, ankle or leg swelling, palpitations, and low blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
May cause dizziness, especially when starting treatment or standing up quickly. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, heart problems, or high potassium levels. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Do not use during pregnancy; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, especially blood-pressure medicines, diuretics, painkillers such as ibuprofen, and lithium.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension), especially when blood pressure is not adequately controlled with one or two medicines. Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of serious heart and blood vessel problems.

How does it work?
Telmisartan and amlodipine relax and widen blood vessels. Hydrochlorothiazide helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water, which lowers blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, ankle or leg swelling, increased urination, nausea, and stomach upset. Changes in blood salts or kidney function may also occur.

Precautions
May cause dizziness, especially when starting treatment or when standing up; rise slowly and avoid driving if affected. Medical advice is important if there is kidney or liver disease, dehydration, gout, diabetes, or an imbalance of body salts. Blood pressure, kidney function, and electrolytes may need monitoring. Do not use during pregnancy; inform the doctor if pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, including potassium supplements or salt substitutes.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) when treatment with both telmisartan and metoprolol is needed.

How does it work?
Telmisartan relaxes and widens blood vessels, while metoprolol slows the heart rate and reduces the heart's workload. Together, they help lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor and at the same time each day. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop taking it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, tiredness, headache, low blood pressure, slow heartbeat, and stomach upset may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma or breathing difficulty, a slow heartbeat, heart conduction problems, diabetes, kidney or liver disease, or high potassium levels. Telmisartan should not be used during pregnancy. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor. Dizziness may occur, especially when standing up; rise slowly and avoid driving if affected.

What is it used for?
This combination medicine is used to lower high blood pressure (hypertension) and help reduce the risk of related heart and blood vessel problems. It combines three blood-pressure medicines and is generally used when more than one medicine is needed.

How does it work?
Telmisartan relaxes blood vessels, chlorthalidone helps remove extra salt and water through urine, and metoprolol slows the heart rate and reduces the heart's workload. Together, they help lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with water and do not stop it suddenly, especially because it contains metoprolol. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber's instructions rather than taking extra medicine.

Common side effects
Dizziness, tiredness, headache, slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, increased urination, nausea, and changes in blood salt levels may occur.

Precautions
Regular monitoring of blood pressure, pulse, kidney function, and electrolytes may be needed. Rise slowly if dizziness occurs and maintain adequate fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised. Tell the doctor about diabetes, asthma or breathing problems, kidney or liver disease, gout, or a slow heartbeat. This medicine should not be used during pregnancy; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Do not stop treatment suddenly without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and other complications.

How does it work?
Telmisartan relaxes blood vessels by blocking the action of a substance that causes them to tighten. Cilnidipine relaxes the blood vessel walls through calcium-channel blocking, helping blood flow more easily and lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take this medicine exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet whole with water and do not stop it suddenly or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, ankle or foot swelling, palpitations and tiredness may occur. Contact a doctor if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
May cause dizziness, especially when standing up; rise slowly and avoid driving until the effect is known. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, low blood pressure, or high potassium levels. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Do not use during pregnancy; inform the doctor if pregnant or planning pregnancy. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially other blood-pressure medicines and anti-inflammatory painkillers.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and other complications.

How does it work?
Telmisartan relaxes and widens blood vessels, while chlorthalidone helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water. Together, they lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow with water. Do not stop treatment or take an extra dose without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, light-headedness, increased urination, headache, nausea, tiredness, and changes in blood salts such as low sodium or potassium may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision during pregnancy; telmisartan can seriously harm an unborn baby. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, low blood pressure, diabetes, high uric acid or gout, or electrolyte problems. Regular blood pressure, kidney-function and blood-salt checks may be needed. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Rise slowly if dizzy and seek medical help for fainting, severe weakness, swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Telmisartan 40 mg + hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It helps lower blood pressure and reduce the risk of related heart and blood vessel problems.

How does it work?
Telmisartan relaxes and widens blood vessels by blocking the action of a hormone that raises blood pressure. Hydrochlorothiazide helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water, which also lowers blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop it or change the dose without medical advice. Because it may increase urination, avoid taking it close to bedtime unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, increased urination, nausea, diarrhoea, and changes in blood salt or potassium levels may occur. Dizziness may be more noticeable when standing up.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, gout, diabetes, dehydration, or previous low sodium or potassium levels. Blood pressure, kidney function, and electrolytes may need monitoring. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Do not use during pregnancy; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Alcohol may worsen dizziness. Seek medical advice for severe dizziness, fainting, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to lower high blood pressure (hypertension). Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and other blood-vessel complications.

How does it work?
Telmisartan relaxes blood vessels by blocking the action of a hormone that raises blood pressure. Cilnidipine further relaxes the blood vessels, while chlorthalidone helps the body remove extra salt and water through urine.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and take it at the same time each day. Do not stop it or change the dose without medical advice. Since it may increase urination, follow the timing advised by the doctor.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, ankle or leg swelling, increased urination, and stomach upset may occur. Low blood pressure, dehydration, or changes in blood sodium or potassium can also occur.

Precautions
Monitor blood pressure regularly. Medical monitoring of kidney function, electrolytes and sometimes uric acid may be needed. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, gout, or frequent vomiting or diarrhoea. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Telmisartan should not be used during pregnancy; inform the doctor if pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if severe dizziness, fainting, marked weakness, or very little urine occurs.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin for certain inflamed skin infections involving fungi or bacteria. It should be used only when recommended by a doctor, as the steroid component can worsen some infections if used incorrectly.

How does it work?
Clobetasol reduces redness, swelling and itching. Miconazole treats fungal growth, while neomycin acts against certain bacteria.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and do not cover the area with a tight dressing unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, irritation, dryness or itching at the application site. Prolonged or improper use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Do not use on the face, groin, skin folds, broken skin or large areas unless specifically advised by a doctor. Avoid prolonged use, especially in children. Do not use for acne or untreated viral skin infections. Stop using it and seek medical advice if the infection worsens, a severe rash develops, or there is no improvement. Tell the doctor about any allergy to clobetasol, neomycin, miconazole or similar medicines.

What is it used for?
Teneligliptin is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
It belongs to a group of medicines called DPP-4 inhibitors. It helps the body release more insulin after meals and reduce the amount of glucose produced by the liver, helping lower blood sugar.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. It may generally be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, take it when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; do not take an extra dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and cold-like symptoms may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or sulfonylurea medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, a history of pancreatitis, heart failure, or allergies to diabetes medicines. Seek medical help for severe or persistent stomach pain, swelling of the face or breathing difficulty, or a severe blistering skin rash. Pregnancy and breastfeeding require medical advice. Monitor blood sugar regularly as advised.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Teneligliptin helps the body release more insulin after meals and reduces the release of sugar from the liver. Metformin also reduces sugar production by the liver and helps the body use insulin better.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, preferably with food. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole with water; do not crush, chew or split it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, bloating, indigestion, metallic taste and headache may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, severe infection, dehydration, heart failure, or heavy alcohol use. Medical advice is needed before surgery or an X-ray scan using iodinated contrast. Seek urgent medical help for severe weakness, unusual sleepiness, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting or severe abdominal pain, as these may indicate a serious reaction. Monitor blood sugar as advised.

What is it used for?
A cosmetic cream intended to improve the appearance of dull or uneven-looking skin and provide daily skin care. Its exact benefits depend on the ingredients, which are not provided.

How does it work?
The action cannot be confirmed without the ingredient list. It may moisturise the skin and contain ingredients intended to support a brighter-looking complexion.

For external use only. Apply to clean skin as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not apply to broken or irritated skin. Perform a patch test before regular use.

Possible skin irritation, redness, itching, dryness or burning, especially in sensitive skin.

Precautions
Stop use if significant irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Avoid contact with the eyes. Seek medical advice for persistent or severe skin reactions. Use sun protection during the day unless the product is specifically labelled as a sunscreen.

What is it used for?
This is an antioxidant nutritional supplement used to support the body's antioxidant defences and general wellness. It is not intended to treat a specific disease unless recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Glutathione, alpha-lipoic acid, grape seed extract, vitamin C and vitamin E help protect cells from oxidative stress by supporting the body's antioxidant systems.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include nausea, stomach discomfort, loose stools or headache.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking diabetes medicines or blood-thinning medicines. Tell the doctor before surgery. Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
This topical cosmetic cream is intended to improve the appearance of dull or uneven-looking skin and support a brighter-looking complexion.

How does it work?
Its effect depends on the ingredients, which have not been provided. The ingredients may help improve the appearance of uneven skin tone or dullness.

How to take/use it
Use on the skin only and follow the product label for application instructions. Avoid contact with the eyes and broken or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Ingredient information is not available, so common side effects cannot be reliably listed. Skin irritation, redness or an allergic reaction may occur with some skincare ingredients.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list before use, especially if there is sensitive skin or a history of allergies. Stop using it if significant irritation or rash develops and seek medical advice if symptoms persist.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin for certain bacterial and fungal skin infections that may be associated with redness, itching or inflammation. It should be used only when prescribed, as it is not suitable for every rash or skin infection.

How does it work?
Ciprofloxacin and metronidazole act against susceptible bacteria, while terbinafine treats fungal infections. Clobetasol is a potent corticosteroid that reduces redness, swelling and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the clean, dry affected area exactly as directed by a doctor. Wash hands before and after application, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and do not cover the area tightly unless advised.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, irritation, redness, dryness or itching at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or skin-colour changes.

Precautions
Use only on the prescribed area and for the prescribed duration. Clobetasol can worsen, hide or mask some infections when used inappropriately. Avoid use on the face, groin, skin folds, broken skin or large areas unless specifically advised. Do not use for acne or undiagnosed rashes. Stop and seek medical advice if the infection worsens, an allergic reaction occurs, or there is no improvement.

What is it used for?
Tranexamic acid is used to reduce excessive bleeding. It is commonly prescribed for heavy menstrual bleeding and may also be used for certain nosebleeds, dental or surgical bleeding, and bleeding after childbirth, as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It helps prevent blood clots from breaking down too quickly, allowing bleeding to slow or stop.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with water. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. The dose and duration depend on the cause of bleeding and medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, or stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any past or current blood clots, kidney disease, vision problems, or unexplained bleeding. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, painful leg swelling, or changes in vision. People using combined hormonal contraceptives should discuss the increased risk of blood clots with a doctor before use.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to reduce heavy menstrual bleeding and relieve period pain or cramps.

How does it work?
Tranexamic acid helps reduce bleeding by slowing the breakdown of blood clots. Mefenamic acid reduces the substances that cause menstrual cramps, pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor, preferably with or after food and with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, indigestion, stomach pain, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about a history of blood clots, kidney disease, stomach ulcers or bleeding, asthma or allergy to painkillers, or use of blood thinners. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathlessness, painful leg swelling, sudden vision changes, severe rash, or signs of stomach bleeding. Consult a doctor if bleeding is unusually heavy, irregular or continues despite treatment.

What is it used for?
Tranexamic acid injection is used by healthcare professionals to prevent or reduce excessive bleeding, including bleeding during or after surgery, after injury, during childbirth, or in some cases of heavy menstrual bleeding.

How does it work?
It helps keep blood clots from breaking down too quickly, allowing bleeding to stop more effectively.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and duration depend on the cause and severity of bleeding, kidney function, and the treatment plan. It should not be self-injected.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness, headache, and low blood pressure if injected too quickly. Rarely, blood clots, seizures, or vision changes may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of blood clots, kidney disease, seizures, blood in the urine, or problems with colour vision. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, painful leg swelling, seizures, or changes in vision. Use during pregnancy only when specifically recommended by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to help reduce swelling, discomfort and bruising associated with superficial vein problems, bruises, haematomas and minor soft-tissue injuries.

How does it work?
Heparin sodium helps reduce the formation of small clots and supports the clearance of local blood collections under the skin. Benzyl nicotinate increases local blood flow, which may help relieve swelling and discomfort.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected area as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Use only on intact skin. Wash hands after application and avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching or rash at the application site. Stop use if a severe allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
Do not apply to open wounds, infected skin or bleeding areas. Avoid use if allergic to heparin or any ingredient. Seek medical advice before use if there is a bleeding disorder, low platelet count or treatment with blood-thinning medicines. Sudden or severe limb swelling, pain, warmth or breathlessness requires urgent medical attention.

What is it used for?
This is a nutritional supplement that provides co-enzyme Q10, L-carnitine, lycopene and zinc. It is used to support normal energy production, antioxidant protection and general nutritional health.

How does it work?
Co-enzyme Q10 and L-carnitine are involved in energy production in cells. Lycopene and co-enzyme Q10 provide antioxidant support, while zinc supports normal immune function and other body processes.

Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. It may be taken with food if stomach upset occurs.

Nausea, stomach upset, abdominal discomfort or diarrhoea may occur. Zinc may cause an unpleasant taste or nausea, particularly when taken on an empty stomach.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or regular medicine use. Zinc can interact with some antibiotics and other medicines; separate doses only as advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Dermina Tinted+Sunscreen SPF 50 is used to protect exposed skin from harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays and help prevent sunburn and sun-related skin damage.

How does it work?
Its sunscreen filters reduce the amount of UV radiation reaching the skin, helping protect it from sun exposure.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply evenly and generously to exposed skin before sun exposure. Reapply after swimming, sweating or towelling, and as directed on the product label. Use additional sun protection such as shade, protective clothing and sunglasses.

Usually well tolerated. Mild stinging, redness, itching or skin irritation may occur, especially on sensitive skin.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes and mucous membranes. Do not apply to damaged or irritated skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use if severe irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Sunscreen does not provide complete protection from the sun; avoid prolonged sun exposure.

What is it used for?
This combination is generally used in skincare products to help hydrate the skin, support the skin barrier, improve the appearance of dull or uneven-looking skin, and provide antioxidant support.

How does it work?
Vitamin C provides antioxidant support and may help improve the appearance of uneven skin tone. Niacinamide supports the skin barrier, while hyaluronic acid helps attract and retain moisture in the skin.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label. Apply to clean skin and avoid contact with the eyes. Use sunscreen during the day when using products containing vitamin C.

Common side effects
Mild stinging, redness, dryness, itching, or skin irritation may occur, especially in sensitive skin.

Precautions
For external use only. Perform a patch test before wider application. Stop use if significant irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Avoid applying to broken or severely irritated skin and seek medical advice if symptoms persist.

What is it used for?
Tofacitinib is used to treat certain inflammatory autoimmune conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and ulcerative colitis, when prescribed by a specialist.

How does it work?
It blocks Janus kinase (JAK) enzymes involved in immune-system signalling. This helps reduce the inflammation and overactive immune response causing symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular monitoring may be needed during treatment.

Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver or kidney disease, and all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Used to protect the skin from harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays, helping reduce sunburn and sun-related skin damage. It is oil-free, provides a matte finish, is water resistant and is designed not to clog pores.

How does it work?
The sunscreen filters UV radiation before it reaches the skin. This helps reduce the effects of UVA and UVB exposure.

How to take/use it
Apply generously and evenly to all exposed skin before going outdoors. Reapply regularly, especially after swimming, sweating, towelling or prolonged sun exposure. Water-resistant sunscreen is not completely waterproof. Use with shade, protective clothing and sunglasses where possible.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, stinging or rash may occur, especially in sensitive skin.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes; rinse thoroughly with water if contact occurs. Stop use if irritation or rash develops. Do not rely only on sunscreen for protection, and avoid prolonged direct sun exposure. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Used to help protect the skin from sunburn and harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation during sun exposure.

How does it work?
Its sunscreen filters help reduce the amount of UV radiation reaching the skin. SPF 50 indicates high protection against UVB rays when used as directed.

How to take/use it
Apply evenly and generously to exposed skin before sun exposure. Reapply after swimming, sweating or towel drying, and as directed on the product label. Sunscreen should be used along with shade, protective clothing and avoiding strong midday sunlight.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching or stinging may occur, especially on sensitive skin.

What is it used for?
Isotretinoin is an oral prescription medicine used mainly to treat severe acne, including painful nodular or cystic acne that has not improved with other treatments.

How does it work?
It reduces oil production from the skin’s sebaceous glands, helps prevent blocked pores, and reduces acne-related inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the dermatologist. Swallow the capsule whole with water and do not crush or chew it. Do not share this medicine or change the dose without medical advice. Regular follow-up and blood tests may be needed.

Common side effects
Dry, cracked lips; dry skin; dry or irritated eyes; nose dryness or nosebleeds; headache; and muscle or joint aches. Blood tests may show increased liver enzymes or blood fats.

Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. It can cause serious birth defects; people who can become pregnant must follow the prescribed pregnancy-prevention and testing requirements. Tell the doctor about liver disease, high cholesterol or triglycerides, mood changes, or vision problems. Avoid vitamin A supplements and tetracycline antibiotics unless specifically approved by the doctor. Avoid blood donation during treatment and for the period advised after treatment. Seek medical help for severe headache, vision changes, severe abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or major mood changes.

What is it used for?
Used to protect exposed skin from the sun’s ultraviolet (UV) rays and help prevent sunburn and sun-related skin damage.

How does it work?
It forms a protective layer on the skin and contains sunscreen protection that helps reduce the amount of UV radiation reaching the skin.

How to take/use it
Apply evenly and generously to all exposed skin before sun exposure. Reapply after swimming, sweating or towelling, and follow the product label instructions. Sunscreen does not replace protective clothing, shade or avoiding strong midday sun.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching or a stinging sensation may occur. Eye irritation can occur if the product gets into the eyes.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes and broken or irritated skin. Stop use if a rash or significant irritation develops. Keep out of reach of children and follow the product label instructions.

What is it used for?
Lactulose is mainly used to relieve constipation by making stools softer and easier to pass. It may also be prescribed under medical supervision to help reduce high ammonia levels in people with certain liver conditions.

How does it work?
It draws water into the bowel, softening the stool and helping bowel movements. Gut bacteria break it down into substances that stimulate bowel movement.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Measure the liquid carefully using a proper measuring device. It may be taken alone or mixed with water or another suitable drink. Drink enough fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, stomach cramps, nausea and diarrhoea. These effects may be more likely if too much is taken.

Precautions
Do not use it without medical advice if there is severe or unexplained abdominal pain, suspected bowel blockage, or vomiting. Prolonged or severe diarrhoea can cause dehydration and electrolyte imbalance. People with diabetes or those following a low-sugar diet should ask a doctor or pharmacist before use, as some formulations contain sugars. Seek medical advice if constipation persists or worsens.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used for certain liver and bile-flow disorders. In selected patients, it is also used to dissolve cholesterol gallstones and help prevent some gallstones.

How does it work?
It makes bile less likely to form cholesterol deposits and helps improve the flow of bile. This may reduce the harmful effects of bile acids on liver cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the medicine with water. It is usually taken with food; follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, loose stools, abdominal discomfort, nausea and vomiting. Itching or worsening of existing itching may also occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, as liver function and the condition of the gallbladder or bile ducts may need monitoring. Tell the doctor about gallbladder inflammation, bile-duct blockage, severe liver disease or frequent abdominal pain. Antacids containing aluminium and some cholesterol-binding medicines can reduce its absorption, so ask about suitable spacing between medicines.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used under medical supervision to treat certain chronic liver and bile-flow conditions, including primary biliary cholangitis. It may also be used to dissolve certain small cholesterol gallstones when surgery is not suitable.

How does it work?
It improves the flow and composition of bile, helping reduce cholesterol buildup in bile. This can help protect liver cells and dissolve some cholesterol gallstones.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. Regular liver tests or scans may be needed during treatment.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea or loose stools, abdominal discomfort, nausea and indigestion. Itching may occur, especially in people being treated for liver disease.

Precautions

This supplement provides calcium and vitamin D3 to support normal bones and teeth and help meet calcium and vitamin D requirements. Cissus quadrangularis is a plant-based ingredient commonly included in bone-health supplements, but its specific benefits are not well established.

How does it work?
Calcium is needed for strong bones and teeth. Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium and supports normal bone health.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. If taking other medicines or supplements, seek advice about the appropriate timing.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include constipation, gas, nausea or stomach upset. Excessive calcium or vitamin D intake can cause more serious problems.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels, or an overactive parathyroid gland. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, including certain antibiotics and thyroid medicines; timing may need to be separated. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking other calcium or vitamin D products.

What is it used for?
Citicoline injection is used as supportive treatment during recovery from stroke and head injury, and may be prescribed for certain problems with memory or thinking. It should be used only for the condition diagnosed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Citicoline helps provide substances needed for the structure and function of brain-cell membranes. It may support the repair and functioning of nerve cells.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose, frequency and duration depend on the condition and should be followed exactly as prescribed.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, nausea, stomach upset, restlessness or difficulty sleeping may occur. Injection-site discomfort or allergic reactions can occur rarely.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to citicoline or other medicines. Inform the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding, or if taking levodopa or other medicines for Parkinson’s disease. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash.

What is it used for?
Citicoline may be prescribed to support recovery after a stroke and to help manage certain cognitive or neurological problems, such as memory and thinking difficulties.

How does it work?
Citicoline provides building blocks used to make phospholipids, which help maintain nerve-cell membranes. It also supports the production of acetylcholine, a chemical involved in memory and brain function.

How to take/use it
Use it exactly as directed by the doctor or according to the product label. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, stomach upset, diarrhoea, restlessness or difficulty sleeping may occur. Contact a doctor if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergies and all medicines being used, especially levodopa. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. This medicine should not replace urgent treatment for stroke symptoms.

What is it used for?
Clobazam is used with other medicines to help control certain types of seizures in epilepsy.

How does it work?
It is a benzodiazepine that increases the calming activity of GABA, a chemical messenger in the brain. This helps reduce abnormal electrical activity that can cause seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop it suddenly, as seizures or withdrawal symptoms may occur. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, tiredness, dizziness, poor coordination, slowed thinking, speech difficulties and memory problems may occur.

Precautions
Do not drink alcohol or use opioid pain medicines unless specifically advised by a doctor, as severe sleepiness and breathing problems may occur. Use only under medical supervision if there is a history of breathing problems, liver or kidney disease, depression, or medicine dependence. Seek urgent medical help for severe breathing difficulty, extreme drowsiness, unusual behaviour or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Clobazam is an anticonvulsant used with other medicines to help control seizures, including certain types of epilepsy.

How does it work?
It increases the calming effect of a natural chemical called GABA in the brain. This helps reduce excessive electrical activity that can cause seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop taking it suddenly, as seizures or withdrawal symptoms may occur; the dose usually needs to be reduced gradually under medical supervision.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, tiredness, dizziness, slowed reactions, poor coordination, weakness and difficulty speaking may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and do not drive or operate machinery until the effects are known. Clobazam may cause dependence and can lead to serious breathing problems when combined with opioids, alcohol or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Tell the doctor about breathing or liver problems, pregnancy, or a history of medicine or substance dependence. Seek urgent medical help for severe breathing difficulty, extreme sleepiness, unusual behaviour or a serious skin rash.

What is it used for?
Clomipramine is mainly used to treat obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), including unwanted thoughts and repetitive behaviours. It may also be prescribed for depression or panic disorder.

How does it work?
It increases the activity of certain chemical messengers in the brain, mainly serotonin and noradrenaline. This helps reduce obsessive thoughts, compulsive behaviours and related mood symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water, with or without food, and take it at the same time each day if possible. Do not stop it suddenly or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, constipation, sweating, nausea, dizziness, drowsiness, blurred vision, increased appetite or weight gain, and sexual difficulties may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is heart disease, an irregular heartbeat, glaucoma, seizures, difficulty passing urine, liver problems or bipolar disorder. Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving until its effects are known. Do not use with MAO inhibitor antidepressants, and tell the doctor about all other medicines being taken. Seek urgent medical help for suicidal thoughts, severe palpitations, fainting, seizures, extreme agitation, fever, muscle stiffness or confusion.

What is it used for?
Clomipramine 75 mg SR is mainly used to treat obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), including unwanted intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviours. It may also be prescribed for certain depressive or panic-related conditions.

How does it work?
It increases the activity of certain chemical messengers in the brain, mainly serotonin and noradrenaline. This can help reduce obsessive thoughts, compulsive behaviours and related mood or anxiety symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Take it at the same time each day and do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, sweating, drowsiness, dizziness, nausea, increased appetite or weight, sexual problems and a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
This is a prescription medicine. It may cause drowsiness or dizziness, so avoid driving until its effects are known and avoid alcohol. Tell the doctor about heart disease, seizures, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, bipolar disorder, liver problems or suicidal thoughts. Do not take it with MAO inhibitors or other medicines that increase serotonin unless specifically advised. Seek urgent medical help for severe palpitations, fainting, seizures, severe confusion or suicidal thoughts.

What is it used for?
This combination is generally used to treat mixed vaginal infections caused by bacteria and fungi, including bacterial vaginosis and vaginal thrush.

How does it work?
Clindamycin is an antibiotic that stops the growth of certain bacteria. Clotrimazole is an antifungal medicine that stops the growth of fungi such as Candida.

How to take/use it
Use it in the vagina exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before and after use, and do not swallow it. Do not use a different dose or continue treatment longer than advised.

Common side effects
Vaginal burning, itching, irritation, discomfort or increased discharge. Mild abdominal discomfort or nausea may also occur.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice, especially during pregnancy or breastfeeding. This medicine may weaken latex condoms or diaphragms during treatment and for a period afterwards; check the product instructions. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, severe irritation, rash, swelling or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
This combination is generally used as a dietary supplement to support memory and cognitive function. It should not be used as a proven treatment for dementia or other neurological conditions without medical advice.

How does it work?
Ginkgo biloba may support blood flow and has antioxidant properties. L-carnosine also has antioxidant activity, but the benefits of this combination may vary between individuals.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Indigestion, nausea, headache, dizziness or allergic skin reactions may occur.

Precautions
Ginkgo biloba may increase the risk of bleeding. Seek medical advice before use if taking blood thinners or antiplatelet medicines, if there is a bleeding disorder, a history of seizures, or before surgery. Consult a healthcare professional during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop use and seek medical help for unusual bleeding or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This combination is commonly used to improve poor appetite and support healthy weight gain. It should be used only when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Cyproheptadine blocks histamine and certain serotonin effects and may stimulate appetite. Tricholine citrate is included as part of the appetite-supporting combination.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a healthcare professional. Measure the liquid with an oral syringe or measuring cup, and do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, increased appetite, nausea and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Cyproheptadine may cause drowsiness; avoid alcohol and do not drive or operate machinery if affected. Tell the healthcare professional if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, asthma, liver or kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe sleepiness, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Diazepam is a prescription medicine used mainly for the short-term relief of severe anxiety. It may also be prescribed for muscle spasms, certain seizures, alcohol withdrawal symptoms, or to help relax a person before a medical procedure.

How does it work?
Diazepam increases the action of a calming chemical in the brain called GABA. This slows excessive brain activity and produces calming, muscle-relaxing and anticonvulsant effects.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. Do not take more than prescribed or stop it suddenly after regular use, as this may cause withdrawal symptoms.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, dizziness, weakness, confusion, reduced alertness and poor coordination may occur.

Precautions
Diazepam can cause dependence, especially with prolonged or frequent use. Avoid alcohol and do not combine it with opioid pain medicines or other sedatives unless specifically advised, as this can cause severe drowsiness and breathing problems. Do not drive or operate machinery if affected. Older adults and people with breathing problems, liver disease, sleep apnoea, depression or a history of substance dependence should use it only under medical supervision. Seek urgent medical help for very slow or difficult breathing, extreme sleepiness or unusual unresponsiveness.

What is it used for?
Diazepam is used to relieve severe anxiety, muscle spasms and symptoms of alcohol withdrawal. It may also be used to control certain seizures or to help with sedation before medical procedures, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Diazepam increases the action of a calming chemical messenger in the brain. This helps reduce anxiety, relax muscles and control abnormal electrical activity that can cause seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Do not change the dose, use it more often or continue it for longer than advised. Do not stop regular treatment suddenly without medical advice, as withdrawal symptoms may occur.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, tiredness, muscle weakness, poor coordination, confusion and blurred vision may occur.

Precautions
Diazepam can cause dependence, especially with prolonged or frequent use. Avoid alcohol and do not drive or operate machinery if drowsy or less alert. Combining it with opioid pain medicines, sleeping tablets or other sedatives can cause dangerous breathing problems. Seek urgent medical help for extreme sleepiness, slowed or difficult breathing, severe confusion or an allergic reaction. Tell the doctor about breathing problems, sleep apnoea, liver disease, pregnancy or a history of substance dependence.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary supplement to provide vitamins, minerals, Coenzyme Q10 and L-arginine when nutritional intake may be inadequate. It is not a replacement for a balanced diet or a treatment for a specific disease.

How does it work?
The vitamins and minerals support normal body functions. Coenzyme Q10 helps with energy production in cells, while L-arginine is used by the body to produce nitric oxide and other proteins.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Take with food if it causes stomach discomfort.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache or dizziness. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe or unusual symptoms occur.

Precautions
Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is kidney disease, liver disease, low blood pressure or a history of heart problems. Seek advice if taking blood-pressure medicines, nitrates, blood thinners such as warfarin, or other vitamin and mineral supplements. Avoid taking more than the recommended amount, as excessive vitamins or minerals may be harmful.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain and burning caused by acid-related irritation of the stomach or food pipe, and to protect and support healing of stomach or duodenal ulcers.

How does it work?
Sucralfate forms a protective coating over ulcers and irritated areas. Oxetacaine is a local anaesthetic that temporarily numbs the area to reduce pain.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with a suitable measuring device. Do not change the dose or treatment duration without medical advice. Sucralfate can affect the absorption of other medicines, so ask a doctor or pharmacist how to space them.

Common side effects
Constipation, dry mouth, nausea, indigestion or stomach discomfort. Temporary numbness of the mouth or throat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease or an allergy to any ingredient. Do not eat or drink very hot food or drinks while the mouth or throat feels numb. Seek medical help for vomiting blood, black stools, severe or persistent abdominal pain, difficulty swallowing or breathing. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat bacterial infections, including some infections of the ear, throat, chest, sinuses, urinary tract, skin and teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall. Potassium clavulanate helps amoxycillin work against bacteria that can otherwise resist it.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Swallow with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, other beta-lactam antibiotics or clavulanate. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, previous antibiotic-associated diarrhoea, or a past reaction to antibiotics. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, a severe rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose, and watery or itchy eyes.

How does it work?
Bilastine blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which can contribute to inflammation and nasal congestion.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the product label regarding timing with food or fruit juice, as these may reduce the absorption of bilastine. Do not use it to treat a sudden asthma attack.

Common side effects
Headache, drowsiness, dizziness, stomach pain, nausea, or sleep disturbances may occur.

Precautions
Montelukast may rarely cause mood or behaviour changes, nightmares, anxiety, depression, or suicidal thoughts; seek medical advice promptly if these occur. Tell the doctor about other medicines or medical conditions, especially kidney problems. Avoid driving or operating machinery if drowsiness or dizziness occurs.

What is it used for?
Triamcinolone injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation in conditions such as painful or swollen joints, severe allergies, and some skin or other inflammatory disorders. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and allergic or immune reactions.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a healthcare professional. Depending on the condition, it may be injected into a muscle, joint, or other affected area. Do not self-inject it. The dose and injection schedule depend on the condition being treated.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; increased blood sugar or blood pressure; mood or sleep changes; indigestion; and increased risk of infections. Repeated or prolonged treatment may cause additional steroid-related effects.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, infections, tuberculosis, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, or a history of mental health problems. Steroids may worsen or hide infections and may affect blood sugar. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken and before receiving vaccines. Seek medical help for signs of a serious infection, severe allergic reaction, vision changes, or unusual weakness.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat depression associated with anxiety, low energy, tension or physical symptoms related to stress. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Flupentixol helps regulate dopamine activity in the brain, while melitracen increases the activity of certain natural mood-regulating chemicals, including serotonin and noradrenaline.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice. Avoid alcohol unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, dizziness, headache, nausea, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, sweating or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about glaucoma, prostate or urination problems, seizures, heart disease, liver disease, bipolar disorder or a history of mania. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially antidepressants, medicines for mental health conditions and medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical help for severe restlessness, uncontrolled movements, high fever with muscle stiffness, fainting, or worsening depression or suicidal thoughts.

What is it used for?
Used to help manage diarrhoea, including diarrhoea associated with antibiotic use, and to support the balance of healthy microorganisms in the intestine.

How does it work?
It contains beneficial microorganisms that help restore the normal balance of intestinal flora. This may help reduce the duration or severity of some types of diarrhoea.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not mix with very hot liquids, as heat may reduce the activity of the microorganisms. Drink enough fluids during diarrhoea to help prevent dehydration.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort or constipation may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice for bloody diarrhoea, high fever, severe abdominal pain, signs of dehydration, or diarrhoea lasting more than a few days. Consult a healthcare professional before use if immunocompromised, seriously ill, hospitalised, or using antifungal medicines. Stop use and seek medical help if an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, urinary tract and respiratory system. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not skip doses or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion and headache. Mild skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to cefixime, cephalosporins or penicillin-type antibiotics, and about kidney problems. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea, especially if it contains blood. Use only when prescribed for a bacterial infection.

What is it used for?
It is a prescription antibiotic combination used to treat certain bacterial infections caused by susceptible bacteria. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefixime prevents bacteria from building their protective cell wall. Ofloxacin interferes with bacterial DNA replication. Together, they help stop the growth of susceptible bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Do not take antacids or mineral supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, iron or calcium at the same time; follow the product or doctor's instructions about spacing them.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and indigestion may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to cefixime, other cephalosporin or penicillin antibiotics, ofloxacin or related quinolone antibiotics. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash or breathing difficulty, tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, or unusual mood or nervous-system changes. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, seizures, tendon disorders, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all medicines being taken. Avoid self-medication and unnecessary antibiotic use.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary supplement to provide multivitamins, lycopene and antioxidant nutrients when dietary intake may be insufficient. It is not intended to treat or prevent a specific disease.

How does it work?
The vitamins support normal body functions. Lycopene and other antioxidants help protect cells from oxidative stress.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount, and avoid taking other multivitamin products unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, stomach upset, constipation or diarrhoea, especially when taken in excess.

Precautions
Check with a doctor or pharmacist before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or regular medicine use. Keep out of reach of children. Seek medical advice if side effects are severe or persistent.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain, swelling and stiffness associated with muscle, joint and soft-tissue conditions such as sprains, strains and arthritis.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling or warming sensation that may help relieve local discomfort.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected area as directed on the product label, and gently rub in if advised. Wash hands after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not cover tightly or apply near heat unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or a rash at the application site.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth, mucous membranes and broken or infected skin. Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other anti-inflammatory painkillers or any ingredient in the product. Stop use and seek medical help if severe skin reactions, facial swelling or breathing difficulty occur. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy, especially in the last three months, or if breastfeeding. Keep away from children.

What is it used for?
Memantine is used to help manage symptoms of moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease. It may help support memory, thinking and daily functioning, but it does not cure the disease.

How does it work?
It regulates the activity of glutamate, a chemical messenger in the brain. This may help protect nerve cells from excessive stimulation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food, and at the same time each day if possible. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, constipation, sleepiness, confusion and increased blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, seizures, or liver disease before use. Seek medical advice if severe dizziness, fainting, worsening confusion, hallucinations or seizures occur. Check with a doctor or pharmacist before taking other medicines, including products that may alter urine acidity.

What is it used for?
Memantine is used to help manage symptoms of moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease, such as problems with memory, thinking and daily activities. It may help slow the worsening of symptoms but does not cure Alzheimer's disease.

How does it work?
It regulates the activity of glutamate, a chemical messenger involved in learning and memory. This helps protect brain cells from excessive stimulation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food, and swallow it with water. Take it at the same time each day. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, constipation, sleepiness and confusion may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, epilepsy or a history of seizures, or heart problems. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially amantadine, ketamine, dextromethorphan or medicines that alter urine acidity. Seek medical advice if severe dizziness, fainting, seizures or marked confusion occurs.

What is it used for?
Used to moisturise and protect dry, rough or irritated skin. It helps relieve skin dryness and supports the skin's natural protective barrier.

How does it work?
White soft paraffin and shea butter form a protective layer that helps reduce moisture loss. Glycerin and other moisturising ingredients help attract and retain moisture in the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply gently to clean, dry affected skin according to the product label or a healthcare professional's advice. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, redness, itching or skin irritation may occur, especially on sensitive skin. Stop using it if irritation or an allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Do not use on skin that is infected, badly broken or severely inflamed unless advised by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, persistent or worsening.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of acidity, heartburn, indigestion, gas and bloating.

How does it work?
Aluminium and magnesium compounds neutralise excess stomach acid. Dimethicone helps combine gas bubbles, making them easier to pass and relieving bloating.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. If it is a suspension, shake well before use and measure with the provided measuring device. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Constipation or diarrhoea may occur. Nausea or stomach discomfort can occasionally occur.

Precautions
People with kidney disease should seek medical advice before use. Antacids can affect the absorption of some medicines; take them separately from other medicines as advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, persistent or frequently recurring.

What is it used for?
Clonazepam is used to help control certain seizure disorders and to treat panic disorder. It may also be prescribed for other conditions only under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It increases the activity of a calming chemical messenger in the brain called GABA. This reduces excessive brain activity and can help control seizures and panic symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Place the mouth-dissolving tablet on the tongue and allow it to dissolve. Do not change the dose or stop taking it suddenly, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms or seizures. Avoid taking more than prescribed.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, tiredness, poor coordination, slowed reactions, memory problems and difficulty concentrating.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and do not combine it with opioid pain medicines or other medicines that cause sleepiness unless specifically advised by a doctor, as breathing problems may occur. Do not drive or operate machinery until its effects are known. It can cause dependence, especially with prolonged use. Older adults and people with breathing problems, liver disease, depression or a history of substance misuse should use it only under medical advice. Seek urgent medical help for extreme sleepiness, confusion, unusual behaviour or slow or difficult breathing. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Clonazepam is a prescription medicine used to control certain seizures. It may also be prescribed for panic disorder and related severe anxiety, depending on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It increases the effect of a calming chemical messenger called GABA in the brain. This helps reduce excessive brain activity, seizures and panic symptoms.

Sleepiness, dizziness, tiredness, reduced coordination, slowed thinking and memory or concentration problems.

Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Clonazepam is used to control certain types of seizures and fits. It may also be prescribed for panic disorder and severe anxiety-related symptoms.

How does it work?
It increases the calming activity of a chemical messenger called GABA in the brain. This helps reduce excessive brain activity, anxiety and seizures.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to help manage sleep problems, such as difficulty falling asleep, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Melatonin helps regulate the body's sleep-wake cycle. Clonazepam increases calming activity in the brain, which can cause drowsiness and help promote sleep.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Do not take more than prescribed, and do not stop clonazepam suddenly without medical advice. Avoid driving or operating machinery after taking it.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, tiredness, headache, reduced alertness and poor coordination may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and other medicines that cause sleepiness unless advised by a doctor. Clonazepam may cause dependence with continued use. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, breathing problems, liver disease, or a history of medicine or substance dependence. Seek medical help for extreme sleepiness, confusion or slow or difficult breathing.

What is it used for?
This combination is used when prescribed for anxiety-related symptoms, including nervousness, trembling, palpitations and other physical symptoms of anxiety.

How does it work?
Clonazepam calms excessive activity in the brain and helps reduce anxiety. Propranolol blocks the effects of adrenaline, helping reduce physical symptoms such as a fast heartbeat and trembling.

How to take/use it

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and other medicines that cause sleepiness unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, fainting, extreme sleepiness or an unusually slow heartbeat.

What is it used for?

Lactulose is mainly used to relieve constipation by making stools softer and easier to pass. It may also be prescribed for certain liver-related conditions, such as hepatic encephalopathy, but this requires medical supervision.

How does it work?
It draws water into the bowel, which softens the stool and helps stimulate bowel movement. It is not absorbed significantly from the digestive tract.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the label or by the doctor. Measure the liquid with a proper measuring device, and drink enough fluids unless a doctor has advised otherwise. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, stomach cramps, nausea and diarrhoea. Excessive diarrhoea may lead to dehydration.

Precautions
Do not use it if there is a suspected bowel blockage or severe unexplained abdominal pain. Use it cautiously if there is diabetes or intolerance to certain sugars. Contact a doctor if constipation does not improve, or if severe diarrhoea, vomiting, dehydration or worsening abdominal pain occurs.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent and control nausea and vomiting during pregnancy. The folic acid component also helps meet folate requirements during pregnancy.

How does it work?
Doxylamine reduces nausea and vomiting by blocking histamine-related signals. Pyridoxine may help regulate pathways involved in nausea, while folic acid supports normal cell growth and development.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor and follow the instructions on the label. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Doxylamine may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth and constipation.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice during pregnancy. Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor before using other medicines that cause drowsiness, including sleeping tablets or sedatives. Seek medical attention if vomiting is severe or persistent, or if there are signs of dehydration.

What is it used for?
Donepezil is used to manage symptoms of Alzheimer’s disease, including memory loss and problems with thinking and daily activities. It may help symptoms but does not cure Alzheimer’s disease.

How does it work?
Donepezil increases the amount of acetylcholine, a chemical messenger involved in memory and thinking, in the brain. This may help improve or maintain cognitive function in some people.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Take it regularly, swallow it with water, and do not change the strength or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed or treatment is interrupted, ask a doctor or pharmacist what to do.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, tiredness, difficulty sleeping and muscle cramps.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about a history of slow heartbeat, fainting, stomach ulcers or bleeding, asthma or other breathing problems, seizures, or difficulty passing urine. Seek medical help for fainting, a very slow or irregular heartbeat, black stools, vomiting blood, severe breathing difficulty, or seizures. Inform the doctor before surgery or anaesthesia.

What is it used for?

Donepezil inhibits an enzyme that breaks down acetylcholine, a chemical messenger involved in memory and thinking. This may improve or maintain cognitive symptoms in some people.

What is it used for?

Donepezil increases the availability of acetylcholine, a chemical involved in memory and thinking. Memantine helps regulate excessive activity of another brain chemical called glutamate.

What is it used for?

Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, at the same time each day. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed or treatment is interrupted, ask the doctor or pharmacist for advice rather than taking extra medicine.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime proxetil is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall.

Take it exactly as prescribed and preferably with food. Swallow the tablet with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not take extra doses or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney disease or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, difficulty breathing, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?

Cefpodoxime stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall. Potassium clavulanate helps protect cefpodoxime from enzymes produced by some bacteria, improving its antibacterial action.

Take it only as prescribed. Cefpodoxime proxetil is generally better absorbed when taken with food. Take doses at evenly spaced times and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share or use leftover antibiotics.

Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporins, penicillins or related antibiotics. What is it used for?
This prescription combination is used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
Cefpodoxime damages the bacterial cell wall. Ofloxacin blocks enzymes bacteria need to copy and repair their DNA; together, they help stop bacterial growth.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, indigestion, headache, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about kidney disease, epilepsy or seizures, heart rhythm problems, tendon disorders, or previous allergy to antibiotics. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, swelling or breathing difficulty, severe rash, numbness or tingling, unusual muscle or tendon pain, or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice. Avoid driving if dizziness occurs.

What is it used for?
Duloxetine is used to treat depression and anxiety. It is also used for nerve pain, fibromyalgia and some types of long-lasting muscle or bone pain.

How does it work?
It increases the activity of serotonin and noradrenaline, chemical messengers that help regulate mood and how the body feels pain.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the medicine whole if it is a delayed-release capsule. Do not stop taking it suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, dry mouth, headache, dizziness, sleepiness or difficulty sleeping, constipation, increased sweating, reduced appetite and sexual problems.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, high blood pressure, glaucoma, bipolar disorder, seizures, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Duloxetine can interact with some antidepressants, pain medicines and other medicines that affect serotonin. Seek urgent medical help for severe agitation, confusion, fever, muscle stiffness, suicidal thoughts, unusual bleeding, severe allergic reactions or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Prochlorperazine 5 mg is mainly used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for dizziness or vertigo in some cases.

It blocks dopamine signals in areas of the brain involved in nausea and vomiting. This helps reduce nausea, vomiting and, in some cases, vertigo.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?

Vitamin E is a fat-soluble vitamin with antioxidant properties. It helps protect cells from damage caused by free radicals.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?

Acebrophylline helps relax the airways and loosen mucus. Montelukast reduces inflammation caused by leukotrienes, while desloratadine blocks histamine to relieve allergy symptoms.

Precautions

What is it used for?

Fexofenadine blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which can contribute to allergic inflammation and nasal congestion.

It stops fungi from making ergosterol, a substance they need to build and maintain their cell membranes. This helps stop the growth of the fungus.
