What is it used for?
Ginkgo biloba is a herbal supplement commonly used to support memory and cognitive function. Evidence for these benefits is mixed, and it should not be used as a substitute for medical treatment of dementia or other conditions.

How does it work?
Ginkgo biloba contains plant compounds with antioxidant activity and may affect blood flow. Its exact effects and clinical benefits are not fully established.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Different products may contain different strengths of ginkgo extract.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, stomach upset, nausea or diarrhoea. Ginkgo may also increase the risk of bruising or bleeding.

Precautions
Use cautiously or seek medical advice if taking blood thinners or antiplatelet medicines, including warfarin, aspirin or clopidogrel. Avoid before surgery unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice if there is unusual bleeding. People with seizure disorders, and those who are pregnant or breastfeeding, should consult a healthcare professional before use.

What is it used for?
Ginkgo biloba is a herbal supplement commonly used to support memory and cognitive function. It may also be used for age-related circulation problems, but benefits can vary.

How does it work?
Ginkgo biloba contains plant compounds with antioxidant effects and may help improve blood flow. Its exact benefits for memory and cognition are not fully established.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole; do not crush or chew it.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, stomach upset, nausea or diarrhoea. Allergic skin reactions may also occur.

Precautions
Ginkgo biloba may increase the risk of bleeding, especially with blood thinners or antiplatelet medicines such as warfarin, aspirin or clopidogrel. Seek medical advice before use if there is a bleeding disorder, epilepsy or a planned surgery. Avoid use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical help for unusual bleeding or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to support normal hair health, especially when the intake of nutrients such as biotin, niacinamide, minerals or amino acids is inadequate.

How does it work?
It provides nutrients involved in normal metabolism and the formation and maintenance of hair structures. Benefits may be limited if there is no nutritional deficiency.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Some people may experience nausea, stomach upset or headache. Stop use and seek medical advice if signs of an allergic reaction occur.

Precautions
Tell a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a known allergy to any ingredient. Biotin may interfere with some blood test results; inform healthcare professionals before having blood tests. Do not use as a substitute for a balanced diet.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used to improve bile flow and treat certain liver and bile-related conditions. It may be prescribed for some types of gallstones and chronic cholestatic liver diseases, including primary biliary cholangitis.

How does it work?
It improves the flow of bile and changes its composition, helping reduce the buildup of harmful bile acids. It can also gradually dissolve certain cholesterol-containing gallstones.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Take it regularly at the same time each day. Do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort or pain, nausea, vomiting, and constipation may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is blockage or inflammation of the bile ducts or gallbladder, or if the gallbladder is not functioning properly. Liver function tests and, for gallstones, periodic scans may be needed. Seek medical advice if severe or persistent abdominal pain, worsening jaundice, or severe diarrhoea occurs.

What is it used for?
This medicine is a combined oral contraceptive used to prevent pregnancy. It does not protect against sexually transmitted infections.

How does it work?
It prevents ovulation and makes it harder for sperm to enter the womb. It also changes the lining of the womb, reducing the chance of pregnancy.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions on the pack or package leaflet. Take it at the same time each day. If a dose is missed, follow the missed-dose instructions in the leaflet or ask a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, breast tenderness, mood changes, and irregular bleeding or spotting may occur, especially during the first few months.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy. Tell a doctor before use if there is a history of blood clots, stroke, heart disease, migraine with aura, uncontrolled high blood pressure, liver disease, or breast cancer. Smoking increases the risk of serious cardiovascular side effects, particularly in women over 35. Seek urgent medical help for sudden chest pain, breathlessness, coughing blood, severe headache, vision changes, or painful swelling in one leg.

What is it used for?
Itraconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, nails, mouth, and other parts of the body, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making ergosterol, a substance they need to build and maintain their cell membranes. This helps stop the growth of the fungus.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions on the pack. Do not change the dose or stop treatment early without medical advice. Tell the doctor about all other medicines being taken, as itraconazole can interact with many medicines.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, heart failure, pregnancy, or an allergy to antifungal medicines. Itraconazole can cause important medicine interactions. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, breathing difficulty, swelling of the legs, or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Itraconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, nails, mouth, and other parts of the body, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making ergosterol, a substance they need to build and maintain their cell membranes. This helps stop fungal growth.

How to take/use it
Take or use it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course. Do not change the dose or stop treatment early without medical advice. Follow the product label or doctor’s instructions about food and administration.

Nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart failure, pregnancy, or breastfeeding before use. Itraconazole can interact with many medicines, so share a complete list of medicines and supplements being taken. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe rash, breathing difficulty, swelling, or unusual shortness of breath.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain infections caused by both bacteria and parasites, especially infectious diarrhoea or dysentery, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin stops susceptible bacteria from multiplying. Ornidazole damages the genetic material of certain parasites and anaerobic bacteria, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it only in the dose and for the duration prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water and complete the course, even if symptoms improve. Do not self-medicate or share it with others. Avoid alcohol while taking it and as advised after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and a metallic or bitter taste may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney disease, seizures, nerve problems, or a history of tendon problems. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, confusion, allergic symptoms, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Antacids and mineral supplements may affect ofloxacin absorption, so take them separately as advised by the doctor.

What is it used for?
Lacosamide is used to treat epilepsy, particularly seizures that start in one part of the brain (focal-onset seizures). It may be used alone or with other anti-seizure medicines, as prescribed.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by affecting voltage-gated sodium channels in nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment suddenly, as seizures may worsen. If a dose is missed or too much is taken, seek medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, nausea, vomiting, sleepiness, tiredness, blurred or double vision, and problems with balance or coordination.

Precautions
It may cause dizziness, sleepiness or blurred vision; avoid driving or using machinery until its effects are known. Tell the doctor about heart rhythm problems, fainting, kidney or liver disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic symptoms, or thoughts of self-harm. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Lacosamide is used to treat epilepsy, particularly focal-onset (partial-onset) seizures. It may be used alone or with other seizure medicines, as prescribed.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by affecting voltage-gated sodium channels, which helps control seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop taking it suddenly, as this may worsen seizures. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber’s instructions.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, sleepiness, nausea, double vision, blurred vision, tiredness and problems with balance or coordination.

Precautions
Use with caution if there is a history of heart rhythm problems or fainting, as lacosamide can affect heart conduction. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Seek medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic symptoms, or worsening mood or suicidal thoughts.

What is it used for?
Levocetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. It may cause drowsiness in some people, so avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, and dizziness.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful with driving if drowsy. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for signs of a severe allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or throat or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Levocetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching. It is also used for hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, and dry mouth.

Precautions
This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid or limit alcohol, as it may increase sleepiness. Seek medical advice if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding, or before giving it to a child. Get urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips or throat, or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Used to help control asthma and other breathing symptoms, particularly when associated with allergies. It may also relieve allergic rhinitis symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose and nasal blockage.

How does it work?
Acebrophylline helps relax the airways and clear mucus. Montelukast reduces leukotriene-related airway inflammation, while desloratadine blocks histamine to relieve allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. This medicine is not intended for immediate relief of a sudden asthma attack.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach upset, dry mouth, dizziness, tiredness or drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical help for severe breathing difficulty or an asthma attack. Inform the doctor about liver disease, heart rhythm problems, seizures, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop the medicine and seek medical advice for unusual mood or behaviour changes, depression or suicidal thoughts. Avoid driving or alcohol if dizziness or drowsiness occurs.

What is it used for?
Used mainly to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose, and watery or itchy eyes.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, a substance that causes allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which can contribute to allergic inflammation and breathing-related symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended. If it causes drowsiness, avoid driving or operating machinery.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, headache, tiredness, dry mouth, stomach discomfort, and nausea.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is kidney disease. Montelukast may rarely cause mood or behaviour changes, disturbing dreams, depression, or suicidal thoughts; seek medical help promptly if these occur. This medicine is not intended to treat a sudden asthma attack.

What is it used for?
Levofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin and other tissues. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking enzymes they need to copy and repair their DNA, which stops the infection from growing.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food, and swallow with water. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional tells otherwise. Keep antacids and supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc separate from this medicine as advised by a pharmacist or doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and difficulty sleeping.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice. Seek urgent medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, severe or persistent diarrhoea, a fast or irregular heartbeat, or signs of a serious allergic reaction. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney problems, seizures, heart rhythm problems or previous tendon problems. Avoid driving if dizzy or otherwise affected.

What is it used for?
Levofloxacin is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin and other parts of the body. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops bacteria from making the enzymes needed to grow and multiply, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection. Swallow the tablet with water and complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise. Keep antacids and mineral supplements containing iron, zinc, calcium or magnesium at least 2 hours before or after this medicine.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and difficulty sleeping.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, a severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash, breathing difficulty or an irregular heartbeat. Avoid strenuous exercise if tendon pain develops. Tell the prescriber about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, seizures, diabetes, myasthenia gravis or previous tendon problems, and about all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Linezolid is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, including pneumonia, complicated skin and soft-tissue infections, and infections caused by resistant Gram-positive bacteria such as vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE). It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and survive.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them for another illness.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and changes in taste may occur. Prolonged treatment may affect blood cell counts.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about all medicines being used, especially antidepressants or other serotonergic medicines, and medicines known as MAO inhibitors, because serious interactions may occur. Medical monitoring may be needed during treatment, particularly if it lasts more than 2 weeks. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, unusual bruising or bleeding, vision changes, numbness or tingling, severe weakness, or repeated vomiting. Use only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Lorazepam is mainly used for the short-term treatment of severe anxiety. It may also be prescribed for short-term sleep problems related to anxiety, certain seizures, or before medical procedures.

How does it work?
It increases the effect of a calming chemical in the brain called GABA. This helps reduce anxiety and causes relaxation and drowsiness.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and for the duration advised by the doctor. Swallow with water. Do not stop it suddenly, especially after regular use, as withdrawal symptoms may occur.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, tiredness, weakness, reduced alertness, poor coordination and memory problems.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and other medicines that cause drowsiness unless approved by a doctor. Do not drive or operate machinery if sleepy or less alert. Lorazepam can cause dependence, especially with prolonged use or higher doses. Use only under medical supervision if there are breathing problems, sleep apnoea, liver disease, pregnancy or a history of substance misuse. Seek urgent medical help for severe breathing difficulty, extreme sleepiness, confusion or unusual behaviour.

What is it used for?
Lorazepam injection is used under medical supervision for the short-term relief of severe anxiety, calming or sedation before certain procedures, and the emergency treatment of prolonged seizures. It may also be used in some cases of severe alcohol withdrawal.

How does it work?
It increases the effect of a calming chemical messenger in the brain called GABA. This slows excessive brain activity and produces calming, sedative and anticonvulsant effects.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and method of administration depend on the condition being treated and the patient's response. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, weakness, confusion, unsteadiness, blurred vision and pain or irritation at the injection site. Slow or shallow breathing and low blood pressure can occur, especially with higher doses or other sedative medicines.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and inform the doctor about opioid painkillers, sleeping medicines or other sedatives, as combining them can cause severe drowsiness and breathing problems. Use with caution in older adults and people with breathing problems, sleep apnoea, severe liver disease or a history of alcohol or medicine dependence. Lorazepam can cause dependence and withdrawal symptoms if used repeatedly or stopped suddenly. Do not drive or operate machinery after receiving it until fully alert. Seek urgent medical help for extreme sleepiness, confusion or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Lorazepam is used for the short-term relief of severe anxiety and anxiety-related sleep problems. It may also be used in hospitals for certain seizures or before medical procedures, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It increases the effect of a calming chemical in the brain called GABA. This helps reduce anxiety and causes relaxation and drowsiness.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and do not take more or use it for longer than advised. Do not stop suddenly after regular use, as withdrawal symptoms may occur. Avoid alcohol and do not drive or operate machinery if drowsy or less alert.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, tiredness, weakness, poor coordination, confusion and memory problems. Long-term or repeated use can lead to dependence.

Precautions
Lorazepam can cause serious breathing problems when combined with opioid pain medicines, alcohol or other sedatives. Use only under medical supervision if there is breathing difficulty, sleep apnoea, liver disease, a history of substance dependence, or in older adults. Seek urgent medical help for very slow or difficult breathing, extreme sleepiness, severe confusion or unusual behaviour.

What is it used for?

It enhances the action of a natural calming chemical in the brain called GABA. This reduces excessive brain activity and produces calming, relaxing and sedative effects.

Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more or use it for longer than prescribed. Do not stop it suddenly, especially after regular use, as withdrawal symptoms can occur.

Older adults and people with breathing problems, liver disease, depression or a history of substance misuse should consult a doctor before use. Seek urgent medical help for extreme sleepiness, confusion or slow or difficult breathing.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is an anti-seizure medicine used to prevent and control epileptic seizures.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain that can trigger seizures. Its main action is linked to binding with a brain protein involved in the release of chemical signals between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop taking it suddenly, as seizures may worsen.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, nausea, and mood or behaviour changes such as irritability or agitation.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe mood or behaviour changes, thoughts of self-harm, a serious rash, swelling of the face or throat, or breathing difficulty. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam syrup is used to prevent and control seizures in epilepsy. It may be used alone or with other medicines, depending on the type of seizure.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by binding to a brain protein involved in the release of chemical signals between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device, and do not use a household spoon. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop it suddenly, as seizures may worsen.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, weakness, reduced appetite, and irritability or other mood changes.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe mood or behaviour changes, thoughts of self-harm, a serious skin rash, swelling of the face or throat, or breathing difficulty. Avoid driving or using machinery until its effects are known.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is an anti-seizure medicine used to help prevent and control certain types of epileptic seizures, including focal seizures and some generalized seizures.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by binding to a brain protein involved in the release of chemical signals between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, and swallow the tablet with water. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop taking it suddenly, as seizures may worsen.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea, and changes in mood or behaviour such as irritability or aggression.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice promptly for severe mood or behaviour changes, depression, thoughts of self-harm, a serious rash, swelling, or breathing difficulty. Avoid driving or operating machinery if sleepy or dizzy.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is an anti-seizure medicine used to prevent and control seizures in epilepsy.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by acting on a brain protein involved in the release of chemical signals between nerve cells.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam injection is used to prevent and control seizures in people with epilepsy, especially when medicine cannot be taken by mouth.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by changing the release of chemical signals between nerve cells.

This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type of seizures, kidney function and medical condition. Do not self-administer it or stop treatment suddenly.

Sleepiness, dizziness, weakness, headache, nausea, and irritability or other mood changes may occur.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is used to treat epilepsy and help prevent different types of seizures. It may be used alone or together with other anti-seizure medicines.

It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by binding to a brain protein involved in the release of chemical signals. This helps prevent seizures.

What is it used for?
Luliconazole cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch. It helps relieve symptoms such as itching, redness and scaling caused by these infections.

How does it work?
It stops the growth of fungi by blocking the production of ergosterol, an essential part of the fungal cell membrane.

For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin as directed by the doctor or product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are the treated area. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose.

Mild application-site irritation, redness, itching, burning, dryness or stinging may occur.

Precautions
Do not apply to the eyes, mouth or broken skin unless advised by a doctor. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs. Consult a doctor if the infection worsens or does not improve as expected.

What is it used for?
Lamotrigine is used to control certain types of seizures in epilepsy. It may also be prescribed to help prevent episodes of depression or mania in bipolar disorder.

How does it work?
It helps reduce excessive electrical activity in the brain by affecting sodium channels and the release of certain chemical messengers.

Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Follow the product instructions for swallowing, chewing or dispersing the tablet. Do not stop treatment suddenly, as seizures may worsen. What is it used for?
Lamotrigine is used to control certain types of seizures in epilepsy. It is also used to help prevent mood episodes in bipolar disorder, as prescribed by a specialist.

How does it work?
It helps stabilise electrical activity in the brain by reducing excessive nerve signalling. This helps prevent seizures and may help stabilise mood.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. The dispersible tablet may be taken as directed in the package instructions, with or without food. Do not stop treatment suddenly. If a dose is missed or the tablet is difficult to use, follow the prescribed instructions or ask a pharmacist.

Headache, dizziness, drowsiness, nausea, vomiting, blurred or double vision, tremor, sleep problems and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical help for a rash, blistering or peeling skin, mouth sores, facial swelling, fever or unusual bruising, especially during the first weeks or after a dose increase. Do not drive or operate machinery until the effects on alertness and vision are known.

What is it used for?
Lamotrigine SR is used to control certain types of seizures in epilepsy. It may also be prescribed to help prevent mood episodes in bipolar disorder.

How does it work?
It reduces excessive electrical activity in the brain by blocking sodium channels and lowering the release of certain excitatory chemicals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Swallow the SR tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop treatment suddenly, as seizures may worsen. If a dose is missed or treatment has been interrupted, follow the doctor’s advice before restarting.

Headache, dizziness, sleepiness, nausea, vomiting, blurred or double vision, and lack of coordination may occur.

Do not change the dose or stop it without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn, indigestion and bloating or discomfort caused by excess gas.

How does it work?
Magaldrate neutralises excess stomach acid. Simethicone helps gas bubbles combine and pass more easily, reducing bloating and gas-related discomfort.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with the supplied measuring device. Do not take it at the same time as other medicines; ask a pharmacist about the appropriate gap between medicines.

Common side effects
Constipation or diarrhoea, nausea, and stomach discomfort may occur. Simethicone is generally well tolerated.

Precautions
People with kidney disease should consult a healthcare professional before use. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, keep returning, or do not improve. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking other medicines.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat depression accompanied by anxiety, tension, or related physical complaints. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Flupentixol helps regulate chemical signals in the brain involved in mood and motivation. Melitracen increases the activity of certain mood-related chemicals, including serotonin and noradrenaline.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food, and swallow it with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, constipation, nausea, dizziness, headache, blurred vision, restlessness, sleep disturbance, increased sweating, or palpitations may occur.

Precautions
This is a prescription medicine. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness and other side effects. Tell the doctor about heart problems, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, seizures, bipolar disorder, liver problems, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Inform the doctor about all other medicines, especially antidepressants, medicines affecting the heart rhythm, and MAO inhibitors. Seek medical help for severe restlessness, unusual muscle movements, fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, or worsening depression or suicidal thoughts.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactive immune responses in conditions such as severe allergies, asthma and other inflammatory or autoimmune conditions. It should be used only for the condition prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces inflammation and suppresses excessive activity of the immune system, helping relieve swelling, redness, pain and allergic symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food to reduce stomach irritation. Do not stop treatment suddenly without medical advice, especially if it has been used for several days or longer.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, swelling due to fluid retention, and increased blood sugar or blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, infections or a history of mental health problems. This medicine can reduce resistance to infections; avoid close contact with people who have contagious infections and ask a doctor before receiving vaccines, especially live vaccines. Seek medical help for signs of a serious infection, severe mood or behaviour changes, black stools, vision changes or severe allergic symptoms.

What is it used for?
Methylcobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 used to prevent or treat vitamin B12 deficiency. It may help support healthy red blood cell formation and normal nerve function.

How does it work?
Vitamin B12 is needed for the production of red blood cells, DNA, and the normal functioning of nerves.

How to take/use it
Use it exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, headache, or skin rash may occur. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as swelling or difficulty breathing.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to methylcobalamin, vitamin B12, or cobalt. Unexplained anaemia, numbness, or tingling should be evaluated by a doctor rather than treated without advice. Tell the doctor about other medicines and medical conditions.

What is it used for?
This is a nutritional supplement that provides vitamin B12, folic acid, vitamin B6 and vitamin D3, along with alpha-lipoic acid. It may be used to support nerve function and help prevent or correct deficiencies of these nutrients when advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
The vitamins support normal nerve function, red blood cell formation, bone health and energy metabolism. Alpha-lipoic acid acts as an antioxidant and also supports nerve metabolism.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Tell the healthcare professional about all supplements and medicines being used.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include nausea, stomach upset, headache or skin rash. Stop use and seek medical advice if a severe allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
People with diabetes should use it only with medical advice, as alpha-lipoic acid may affect blood sugar levels. Consult a healthcare professional during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is thyroid disease or any long-term medical condition. Seek advice before use with regular medicines or other vitamin supplements to avoid excessive intake.

What is it used for?
Used to support nerve health and help manage symptoms of peripheral neuropathy, such as tingling, numbness, burning or prickling sensations.

How does it work?
Alpha lipoic acid provides antioxidant support, while the B vitamins help support normal nerve function and energy production.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, vomiting, headache or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
People with diabetes should monitor their blood sugar, as alpha lipoic acid may lower it. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking medicines for diabetes or thyroid problems. Stop use and seek medical help if a severe allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
This medicine is a nutritional supplement that provides lysine and B vitamins. It may be used when dietary intake is inadequate or when supplementation is recommended for a deficiency.

How does it work?
It supplies lysine, an essential amino acid, and B vitamins that support protein metabolism, energy production and normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Measure the liquid with a proper measuring device and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort or loose stools may occur. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction, such as rash, swelling or breathing difficulty, occur.

Precautions
Check the ingredients before use if there is a known allergy to any component. Tell a healthcare professional about other supplements or medicines being used, especially before prolonged use or in pregnancy or breastfeeding. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
This medicine provides vitamins B12, B3 and B6. It is used to prevent or treat deficiencies of these vitamins and to support normal nerve function and energy metabolism.

How does it work?
These B vitamins help the body maintain healthy nerves, form blood cells and release energy from food. Replacing low vitamin levels may help correct symptoms related to deficiency.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as advised by a doctor or as directed on the product label. Swallow with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Do not use it for a prolonged period without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, headache, skin rash or itching may occur. Bright yellow urine can occur with B-vitamin products and is usually harmless.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to any ingredient. Long-term or excessive intake of vitamin B6 can cause nerve problems, such as tingling or numbness. Seek medical advice if these symptoms develop. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking levodopa or other long-term medicines.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat calcium and vitamin D deficiency and to support strong bones. It may also provide zinc and vitamin B12 when supplementation is needed.

How does it work?
Calcium helps maintain bones, muscles and nerves. Calcitriol and vitamin D help the body absorb calcium, while zinc and vitamin B12 support normal body functions.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as directed by the doctor or as stated on the label. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid taking additional calcium or vitamin D supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort or bloating may occur. Excess calcium may cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness or confusion.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, or high calcium or vitamin D levels. Medical monitoring may be needed during treatment with calcitriol. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, including thyroid medicines, iron and certain antibiotics; ask a pharmacist about suitable spacing. Seek medical help for severe nausea, vomiting, marked weakness, confusion or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
This supplement provides alpha lipoic acid and B vitamins to support normal nerve function and nutritional health. It may be recommended as part of care for tingling, numbness or other nerve-related symptoms, depending on the cause.

How does it work?
Alpha lipoic acid has antioxidant activity. Thiamine, pyridoxine, folic acid and cyanocobalamin help support nerve function, energy metabolism and the formation of healthy blood cells.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, vomiting, headache or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Use under medical advice if there is diabetes, as alpha lipoic acid may affect blood sugar. Tell a healthcare professional about all medicines and supplements being taken. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
It is a vitamin B supplement used to prevent or treat deficiencies of methylcobalamin (vitamin B12), nicotinamide (vitamin B3) and pyridoxine (vitamin B6). These vitamins help support normal nerve function, red blood cell formation and energy metabolism.

How does it work?
It provides B vitamins needed for nerve health, red blood cell production and normal energy processes in the body.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid taking other vitamin B6-containing supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Prolonged or excessive intake of vitamin B6 can cause or worsen numbness, tingling or nerve damage. Seek medical advice if these symptoms develop. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is liver or kidney disease. Stop use and seek help for signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Propranolol may be prescribed for high blood pressure, fast or irregular heartbeat, angina, prevention of migraine attacks, tremors, and some physical symptoms of anxiety. The exact use depends on the doctor's advice.

How does it work?
It is a beta-blocker that slows the heart rate and reduces the force of the heartbeat. This can lower blood pressure and reduce symptoms such as palpitations and shaking.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with water. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice, as this may worsen heart problems.

Common side effects
Tiredness, dizziness, cold hands or feet, slow heartbeat, sleep disturbances, nausea, or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma or wheezing, a slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart failure, diabetes, or poor circulation. Propranolol may hide some warning signs of low blood sugar. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, fainting, or an unusually slow heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Propranolol 20 mg is a beta-blocker used for several conditions, including high blood pressure, certain heart rhythm problems, angina and other heart-related conditions. It may also be prescribed to prevent migraine attacks and to reduce physical symptoms such as a fast heartbeat or trembling.

How does it work?
It blocks the effects of stress hormones on the heart and blood vessels. This slows the heart rate, reduces the heart's workload and can help control blood pressure and some physical symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with water, and try to take it at the same time each day. Do not stop it suddenly, as this may worsen heart problems. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the prescriber or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Tiredness, dizziness, slow heartbeat, cold hands or feet, sleep problems and nausea may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma or wheezing, a slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart failure, circulation problems or diabetes. Propranolol can hide some warning signs of low blood sugar. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, fainting or an unusually slow heartbeat. Check before using it with other medicines, especially those affecting blood pressure or heart rate.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to help prevent migraine headaches and reduce how often they occur. It is not usually intended for immediate relief during a migraine attack.

How does it work?
Propranolol reduces the effects of certain stress signals on the heart and blood vessels, while flunarizine helps reduce changes in brain blood-vessel activity linked with migraine. Together, they help prevent migraine episodes.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Do not stop it suddenly, especially because it contains propranolol. It may take time to reduce the frequency of migraines and should not be used to treat an acute attack unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Tiredness, dizziness, slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, cold hands or feet, sleep problems, increased appetite and weight gain. Flunarizine may rarely cause depression or movement-related symptoms.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma or wheezing, a slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart-rhythm or circulation problems, diabetes, depression, Parkinson’s disease or other movement disorders. Avoid driving if dizzy or unusually tired. Seek medical advice for breathing difficulty, fainting, a very slow heartbeat, severe mood changes or uncontrolled movements.

What is it used for?
Used to help prevent migraine headaches and reduce how often they occur. It is not usually used for immediate relief during a migraine attack.

How does it work?
Propranolol helps reduce the effects of certain stress signals on the heart and blood vessels. Flunarizine helps reduce changes in blood vessel activity and nerve sensitivity involved in migraine.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Do not stop it suddenly, especially because it contains propranolol. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber's instructions and do not take an extra dose unless advised.

Common side effects
Tiredness, dizziness, drowsiness, slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, cold hands or feet, increased appetite and weight gain. Mood changes or movement problems can occur with flunarizine.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma or breathing difficulty, a slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart rhythm problems, diabetes, depression, Parkinson's disease or other movement problems. Propranolol may hide some warning signs of low blood sugar. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, fainting, a very slow heartbeat, severe mood changes or unusual movements. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This combination is used as prescribed to help prevent migraine headaches. It may also help reduce anxiety symptoms associated with migraine in some patients.

How does it work?
Propranolol helps reduce the overactivity of certain nerve and heart signals involved in migraine prevention. Alprazolam has a calming effect by enhancing the action of a chemical messenger in the brain.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not change the dose or stop it suddenly. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, tiredness, weakness, slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, nausea and reduced alertness.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol because it can increase drowsiness. Alprazolam may cause dependence if used regularly or for a long time. Do not stop this medicine suddenly without medical advice. Tell the doctor about asthma or breathing problems, a slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, diabetes, liver or kidney problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. What is it used for?
Propranolol is used to lower high blood pressure and manage certain heart rhythm problems, chest pain and other heart conditions. It may also be prescribed to prevent migraine attacks and reduce some physical symptoms of anxiety or overactive thyroid, depending on medical advice.

How does it work?
It is a beta-blocker that reduces the effects of adrenaline on the heart. This slows the heart rate, lowers blood pressure and reduces the heart's workload.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop taking it suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Tiredness, dizziness, slow heartbeat, cold hands or feet, sleep problems or vivid dreams, nausea and weakness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma or wheezing, a very slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart failure, diabetes, or circulation problems. Propranolol can hide some warning signs of low blood sugar. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, fainting, very slow heartbeat or worsening chest pain. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Modafinil is used to improve excessive daytime sleepiness caused by narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnoea, or shift work sleep disorder. In obstructive sleep apnoea, it is used along with the prescribed treatment for the condition and does not replace devices such as CPAP.

How does it work?
Modafinil promotes wakefulness by affecting certain chemical messengers in the brain. Its exact mechanism is not fully understood.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. It is usually taken in the morning, or before a work shift when prescribed for shift work sleep disorder. Do not change the dose or timing without medical advice. Avoid taking it close to bedtime unless specifically instructed.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, nervousness, anxiety, dizziness, dry mouth and difficulty sleeping.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart problems, high blood pressure, liver or kidney disease, mental health conditions, or a history of drug dependence. Modafinil may reduce the effectiveness of some hormonal contraceptives, so additional contraception may be needed during treatment and for the period advised by a doctor after stopping it. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Stop taking it and seek urgent medical help for a severe skin rash, swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, chest pain, or severe mood or behaviour changes.

What is it used for?
Modafinil 200 mg is used to improve excessive daytime sleepiness caused by narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnoea, or shift work sleep disorder. It helps increase wakefulness but does not replace adequate sleep or treat the underlying cause of sleep apnoea.

How does it work?
It acts on the brain to promote wakefulness and reduce excessive sleepiness. Its exact mechanism is not fully understood.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. It is usually taken at a time that helps prevent sleepiness during the day or during a work shift. Avoid taking it close to bedtime, and do not change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, nervousness or anxiety, difficulty sleeping, dizziness, dry mouth and stomach upset.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart problems, high blood pressure, liver or kidney disease, mental health conditions, or a history of drug dependence. Modafinil can interact with several medicines, including hormonal contraceptives, and may reduce their effectiveness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Stop taking it and seek urgent medical help for a severe skin rash, facial swelling, breathing difficulty, chest pain, or unusual mental or behavioural changes. Discuss its use during pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor.

What is it used for?
Used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ears, sinuses, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes that can make some bacteria resistant to it.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor. Take it with a meal and swallow it with water. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share this medicine or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and skin rash. Oral or vaginal thrush may also occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, clavulanate or related antibiotics. Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease or previous antibiotic-related jaundice. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, a severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotics can promote resistance.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve migraine headaches and associated nausea or vomiting.

How does it work?
Naproxen reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Domperidone helps control nausea and supports movement of food through the stomach.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow with water, preferably with or after food, to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised.

Indigestion, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, dizziness, headache, dry mouth or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Avoid if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney or liver disease, or allergy to aspirin or other NSAID painkillers, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Inform the doctor if taking blood thinners or other painkillers. Domperidone may rarely affect heart rhythm; seek medical help for fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting or severe dizziness. Avoid during pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks, unless prescribed.

What is it used for?
Used for the short-term relief of migraine headache and associated nausea or vomiting.

How does it work?
Naproxen reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Domperidone helps control nausea and vomiting and supports movement of the stomach.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow with water, preferably with or after food, to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, dry mouth or stomach cramps.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, allergy to naproxen or other NSAID painkillers, or severe kidney, liver or heart disease, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, chest pain, fainting or a fast or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Flunarizine 10 mg is mainly used to help prevent migraine attacks. It may also be prescribed for certain types of dizziness or vertigo.

How does it work?
It reduces abnormal activity in the brain and helps prevent changes that can trigger migraine. It also has an effect on the balance centres involved in some types of dizziness.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually on a regular schedule for prevention. Swallow it with water. It is not intended for immediate relief of an ongoing migraine attack. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, increased appetite, weight gain and stomach discomfort may occur. Some people may experience low mood or movement-related symptoms.

Precautions
Do not use it without medical advice if there is a history of depression, Parkinson’s disease or other movement disorders. Avoid driving or alcohol if it causes drowsiness. Seek medical advice if low mood, tremors, stiffness or unusual movements develop.

What is it used for?
Flunarizine is mainly used to help prevent migraine attacks. It may also be prescribed to manage vertigo or dizziness caused by balance-related inner-ear disorders. It is not usually used to provide immediate relief during an ongoing migraine attack.

How does it work?
It helps reduce the activity of calcium channels in nerve cells, which can lower the tendency for migraine attacks and reduce abnormal signals involved in vertigo.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day. Swallow with water. Do not take more than prescribed or stop treatment without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Norethisterone is a progesterone-like hormone used to treat heavy or painful periods, irregular menstrual bleeding and endometriosis. It may also be prescribed to delay a period.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone progesterone and changes the lining of the womb, helping regulate menstrual bleeding. Its effect depends on the condition being treated.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, and swallow with water. The dose and duration vary according to the reason for treatment. Do not change or stop it without medical advice. It is not a reliable contraceptive.

Nausea, headache, breast tenderness, bloating, mood changes, spotting or other changes in menstrual bleeding.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about previous blood clots, liver disease, unexplained vaginal bleeding, breast or other hormone-sensitive cancer, or severe migraine. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, coughing blood, or painful swelling in a leg.

What is it used for?
Olanzapine is used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, including manic episodes and helping prevent their recurrence. It may also be used with other medicines for certain treatment-resistant depression cases, only when prescribed by a specialist.

How does it work?
It helps balance certain chemical messengers in the brain, mainly dopamine and serotonin. This can reduce symptoms such as hallucinations, confused thinking, severe mood changes and agitation.

Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. For the mouth-dissolving tablet, place it on the tongue and allow it to dissolve before swallowing. Do not stop taking it suddenly without medical advice. Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving until its effects are known.

Sleepiness, dizziness, increased appetite, weight gain, constipation, dry mouth, tiredness and swelling of the hands or feet. It may also increase blood sugar and cholesterol levels.

Tell the doctor about diabetes, high cholesterol, obesity, liver disease, seizures, heart problems or a history of stroke. Blood sugar, cholesterol and weight may need monitoring. Older adults with dementia-related psychosis have an increased risk of serious side effects; olanzapine is not approved for this use. Seek urgent medical help for severe muscle stiffness, high fever, confusion, uncontrolled movements or fainting.

What is it used for?
Paroxetine is used to treat depression and several anxiety-related conditions, such as panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder and generalised anxiety disorder.

How does it work?
It is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI). It increases the availability of serotonin in the brain, which can help improve mood and reduce anxiety symptoms.

Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole with water; do not crush, chew or split it. Do not stop treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

Tell the doctor about bipolar disorder, epilepsy, liver or kidney problems, bleeding disorders, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not take it with MAO inhibitors or certain other medicines unless specifically advised. Seek medical help for suicidal thoughts, severe agitation, unusual bleeding, a seizure, or symptoms such as high fever, confusion, muscle stiffness and fast heartbeat. What is it used for?

What is it used for?

It increases the availability of serotonin, a natural chemical messenger in the brain that helps regulate mood and anxiety.

What is it used for?

Paroxetine increases the activity of serotonin, a chemical messenger that helps regulate mood and anxiety. Clonazepam enhances the calming effects of GABA in the brain, helping reduce anxiety.

What is it used for?

It blocks a stomach enzyme that produces acid, thereby reducing acidity and allowing acid-related irritation to heal.

Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is generally taken before food, as directed by the doctor.

Precautions

Itching, redness, burning, stinging, tingling or skin irritation may occur, and itching can continue for some time after treatment.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes and broken or severely irritated skin. Seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or signs of an allergic reaction occur. Consult a doctor before use in infants, during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Close household contacts may also need evaluation or treatment.

What is it used for?
Permethrin 1% soap is used on the skin to help treat certain external parasite infestations, such as lice. Use it only for the condition stated on the product label or as advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Permethrin acts on the nervous system of certain parasites, helping to kill them. It works on the skin and is not intended for internal use.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use the soap exactly as directed on the pack or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and wash hands after use. Do not use more often or for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Temporary itching, burning, stinging, redness, dryness or irritation of the skin may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to permethrin or any ingredient in the product. Avoid applying to the eyes, mouth or severely irritated or broken skin. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or other signs of an allergic reaction occur. If the infestation persists or returns, consult a healthcare professional rather than repeating treatment without advice.

What is it used for?
Sertraline is used to treat depression and several anxiety-related conditions, including panic disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), social anxiety disorder and premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD).

How does it work?
It is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI). It increases the availability of serotonin in the brain, which can help improve mood and reduce anxiety and unwanted thoughts.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Do not stop taking it suddenly; the dose usually needs to be reduced gradually under medical supervision.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, dry mouth, tiredness, difficulty sleeping and sexual problems may occur. These effects may improve as the body adjusts.

Precautions
Do not use sertraline with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) or certain other medicines unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about bipolar disorder, epilepsy, liver problems, bleeding disorders, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all medicines being taken. Seek urgent medical help for suicidal thoughts, severe agitation, unusual mood elevation, seizures, severe allergic reactions or symptoms such as fever, confusion, sweating and muscle stiffness.

What is it used for?

Do not use sertraline with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) or certain other medicines unless specifically advised. What is it used for?

How does it work?
It increases the activity of serotonin, a chemical messenger in the brain that helps regulate mood and anxiety.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow with water. Do not stop treatment suddenly without medical advice, even if feeling better.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron 4 mg MD Tablet is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including those related to chemotherapy, radiotherapy or surgery.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals in the body that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Place the tablet on the tongue and allow it to dissolve before swallowing. Do not take more than the recommended amount. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, dizziness and tiredness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of irregular heartbeat, heart rhythm problems, low potassium or magnesium levels, liver disease, or allergy to ondansetron. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or serotonin levels. What is it used for?
Ondansetron injection is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including those related to chemotherapy, radiotherapy or surgery.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals in the body that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or other trained healthcare professional. The dose and timing depend on the cause of nausea or vomiting and should be decided by the prescriber. Do not self-inject.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any heart rhythm problem, liver disease or allergy to ondansetron. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, breathing difficulty or swelling of the face or throat.

What is it used for?
Baclofen is used to relieve muscle stiffness, tightness and spasms (spasticity), especially when caused by conditions affecting the brain or spinal cord, such as multiple sclerosis or spinal cord disorders.

How does it work?
It acts on nerve signals in the spinal cord to reduce the excessive activity that causes muscle spasms and stiffness.

How to take/use it
Take this medicine by mouth exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop taking it suddenly unless advised by a doctor, as this may cause withdrawal symptoms or worsening spasms.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, weakness, tiredness, nausea and confusion may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery, as baclofen can cause drowsiness or dizziness. Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, epilepsy, breathing difficulty, or a history of mental health problems. Seek medical help for severe weakness, breathing difficulty, extreme sleepiness or confusion.

Baclofen is used to reduce muscle stiffness, spasms and tightness (spasticity), especially when related to conditions affecting the brain, spinal cord or nerves.

It acts on GABA-B receptors in the nervous system to reduce the nerve signals that cause excessive muscle tightening and spasms.

Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery, as baclofen can cause sleepiness or dizziness. Seek medical help for severe weakness, breathing difficulty, hallucinations or seizures.

Avoid alcohol and be careful with other medicines that cause sleepiness. Do not drive or operate machinery if affected. What is it used for?
Meropenem with tazobactam is an injectable antibiotic used under medical supervision to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections that may be caused by bacteria resistant to some other antibiotics.

How does it work?
Meropenem kills bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Tazobactam helps protect meropenem from certain bacterial enzymes that can reduce its effect.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection or infusion by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and medical advice. Complete the prescribed course unless the healthcare professional advises otherwise.

Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, headache, rash, and pain or redness at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Inform the healthcare professional about any allergy to meropenem, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics.
