Tell the healthcare professional about all medicines being used, especially valproic acid or valproate.

What is it used for?
Thiamine (vitamin B1) is used to prevent or treat thiamine deficiency, including deficiency-related conditions such as beriberi. It may be recommended when the body needs extra vitamin B1 due to poor nutrition or certain medical conditions.

How does it work?
Thiamine is converted into an active form that helps the body use carbohydrates for energy and supports normal nerve and muscle function.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or as stated on the product label. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort or diarrhoea may occur. Allergic reactions are uncommon.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to thiamine or vitamin products. Seek urgent medical help for rash, swelling, breathing difficulty or other signs of a severe allergic reaction. If deficiency is suspected due to poor diet or an underlying illness, medical advice is recommended.

What is it used for?
Thiamine (vitamin B1) injection is used to prevent or treat vitamin B1 deficiency. It may be used when a rapid effect is needed or when thiamine cannot be taken or absorbed properly by mouth.

How does it work?
Thiamine helps the body convert carbohydrates into energy and supports normal nerve and heart function.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or other healthcare professional. The dose and duration depend on the severity of the deficiency and the medical condition. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; nausea or sweating may occur.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about any previous allergy to thiamine or injectable medicines. Rarely, serious allergic reactions can occur after injection. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial or throat swelling, severe rash, dizziness or fainting.

What is it used for?
Etizolam 0.25 mg is used for the short-term treatment of anxiety and, in some cases, anxiety-related sleeping problems. It should be used only when prescribed, as it can cause dependence.

How does it work?
It increases the activity of a calming chemical messenger in the brain, helping reduce anxiety and promote relaxation and sleepiness.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow it with water. Do not change the dose or stop it suddenly without medical advice. Avoid using it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, tiredness, reduced alertness, poor coordination, confusion and memory problems may occur.

Precautions
Do not drink alcohol or take opioids or other medicines that cause sleepiness unless advised by a doctor, as this may dangerously slow breathing. Do not drive or operate machinery if affected. Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is a history of dependence, breathing problems, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for extreme sleepiness, confusion or slow or difficult breathing.

What is it used for?
Etizolam is used for the short-term treatment of anxiety and anxiety-related symptoms. It may also be prescribed for short-term insomnia (difficulty sleeping) when anxiety is contributing to the problem.

How does it work?
It enhances the effect of a calming chemical messenger in the brain called GABA. This helps reduce anxiety and promotes relaxation and sleepiness.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor and for the prescribed duration. Swallow it with water. Do not take more than prescribed or stop suddenly after regular use without medical advice.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, tiredness, reduced alertness, poor coordination, confusion and memory problems.

Precautions
Etizolam can cause dependence and withdrawal, especially with prolonged or regular use. Avoid alcohol and do not combine it with opioid pain medicines or other sedatives unless specifically advised by a doctor. Do not drive or operate machinery if drowsy or less alert. Older adults and people with breathing problems, liver or kidney disease, a history of substance misuse, or depression should use it only under medical supervision. Seek urgent medical help for extreme sleepiness, slow or difficult breathing, severe confusion or unusual behaviour.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for the short-term treatment of anxiety symptoms, including physical symptoms such as a fast heartbeat, trembling and sweating, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Etizolam calms excessive activity in the brain, helping reduce anxiety and promote relaxation. Propranolol reduces the effects of stress hormones on the heart and blood vessels, helping control symptoms such as a fast heartbeat and trembling.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Do not take extra doses or use it for longer than advised. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice, as etizolam may cause withdrawal symptoms.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, tiredness, weakness, slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, cold hands or feet and nausea.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and other medicines that cause sleepiness unless approved by a doctor. Do not drive or operate machinery if drowsy or dizzy. Tell the doctor before use if there is asthma, a slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart block, diabetes, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Etizolam can cause dependence with regular or prolonged use. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, fainting, extreme sleepiness or an unusually slow heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Tofisopam is used to relieve anxiety and related tension or nervousness. It is available only on prescription.

How does it work?
Its exact mechanism is not fully understood. It affects brain signalling involved in anxiety and helps reduce anxiety symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with water. Do not change the dose, take it more often, or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, dry mouth, headache, dizziness, stomach discomfort, restlessness, and sleep disturbances may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor before using other medicines that cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Tell the doctor if pregnant, breastfeeding, or if there are liver or kidney problems. Seek medical help for severe allergic reactions, unusual confusion, or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Tofisopam is used to relieve symptoms of anxiety, such as excessive worry, nervousness and tension.

How does it work?
It acts on brain pathways involved in anxiety to help reduce excessive nervousness and tension. It is an atypical benzodiazepine medicine and may cause less sedation than some other medicines in this group.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. Do not take more than recommended or stop it suddenly without medical advice. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea or other stomach upset, dry mouth, restlessness, irritability and sleep disturbance may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol unless a doctor advises otherwise. Tell the doctor about liver or kidney problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken, especially medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical help for severe allergic reactions, unusual agitation or worsening symptoms.

What is it used for?
Tolperisone 150 mg is a muscle relaxant used to relieve painful muscle spasms, stiffness and increased muscle tightness in certain muscle and nerve-related conditions.

How does it work?
It reduces excessive nerve signals that cause muscle tightening, helping muscles relax and easing spasms and stiffness.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, muscle weakness, nausea, stomach discomfort and low blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Stop taking it and seek urgent medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur, such as rash, severe itching, swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty or fainting. Tell the doctor about any previous medicine allergy, and seek medical advice before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or if there are kidney or liver problems.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve painful muscle spasms, inflammation and pain in musculoskeletal conditions such as back pain, neck pain, and muscle or joint pain.

How does it work?
Tolperisone helps reduce excessive muscle tightness and spasms. Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow it with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness, headache and weakness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if allergic to tolperisone, diclofenac, aspirin or other NSAIDs. Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or use of blood thinners. Avoid during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed, especially during the last three months. Stop using it and seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin rash, black stools, or vomiting blood.

What is it used for?
Topiramate is mainly used to control certain types of seizures in epilepsy. It is also used to help prevent migraine headaches; it is not used to stop a migraine that has already started.

How does it work?
It reduces excessive electrical activity in the brain and helps balance certain brain signals, which can prevent seizures and reduce the frequency of migraines.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food, and swallow the tablet whole unless instructed otherwise. Drink plenty of fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not stop taking it suddenly, as seizures may worsen.

Common side effects
Tingling in the hands or feet, sleepiness, dizziness, tiredness, nausea, reduced appetite, weight loss, taste changes, and difficulty with concentration or memory.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, kidney stones, glaucoma, breathing problems, or mood changes before use. Avoid overheating and dehydration, especially in hot weather. Seek urgent medical help for sudden eye pain or blurred vision, severe confusion, fast breathing, inability to sweat, or thoughts of self-harm. Topiramate may harm an unborn baby, so pregnancy or plans for pregnancy must be discussed with a doctor. Do not drive or operate machinery until its effects are known.

What is it used for?
Topiramate 25 mg is used to control certain types of seizures in epilepsy. It is also used to help prevent migraine attacks; it is not meant for immediate relief of a migraine once it has started.

How does it work?
It reduces excessive electrical activity in the brain, helping to prevent seizures and migraine attacks.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. It may be taken with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Tingling in the hands or feet, reduced appetite, weight loss, drowsiness, dizziness, tiredness, nausea, and difficulty with concentration or memory.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, a history of kidney stones, glaucoma, or metabolic acidosis. Drink adequate fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised. Seek urgent medical help for sudden eye pain or blurred vision, severe drowsiness, confusion, reduced sweating with high body temperature, or unusual mood changes. Pregnancy requires special medical advice because topiramate may harm an unborn baby.

What is it used for?
Topiramate 50 mg is used to control certain types of seizures in epilepsy. It is also used to help prevent migraine headaches. It does not usually treat a migraine after it has already started.

How does it work?
It reduces excessive electrical activity in the brain and affects certain chemical signals involved in seizures and migraine.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food and should be swallowed with water. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice. Drink enough fluids unless a doctor has advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Tingling in the hands or feet, sleepiness, dizziness, tiredness, nausea, diarrhoea, reduced appetite, weight loss, changed taste and difficulty concentrating or finding words.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve moderate to severe pain when a combination of tramadol and paracetamol is prescribed.

How does it work?
Tramadol acts on opioid receptors and also affects certain brain chemicals involved in pain signals. Paracetamol reduces pain signalling in the central nervous system.

Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Do not take more than prescribed or combine it with other medicines containing tramadol or paracetamol unless advised by a healthcare professional. Avoid alcohol, and do not drive or operate machinery if feeling sleepy or dizzy.

Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, sleepiness, constipation, dry mouth and headache.

Use only under medical advice if there are breathing problems, liver or kidney disease, epilepsy, a history of drug or alcohol dependence, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about antidepressants, sleeping medicines, sedatives or other pain medicines, as serious interactions may occur. Seek urgent medical help for slow or difficult breathing, extreme sleepiness, seizures, severe allergic reaction or confusion.

What is it used for?
Isotretinoin is used to treat severe acne, especially acne that has not improved with other treatments. It should be used only under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It reduces oil production in the skin and helps prevent blocked pores. It also reduces inflammation associated with acne.

Take exactly as prescribed, usually with food, and swallow the capsule whole with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular check-ups and blood tests may be needed.

Avoid vitamin A supplements unless advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about liver disease, high blood fats, mental health concerns, or medicines being taken. Seek medical help for severe headache or vision changes, severe abdominal pain, marked mood changes, or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Isotretinoin 20 mg is a prescription medicine used mainly to treat severe acne, especially acne that has not improved with other treatments. It should be used only under a dermatologist’s supervision.

It reduces the activity of the skin’s oil glands, decreases oil production and helps prevent blocked pores. It also reduces inflammation associated with acne.

Take it exactly as prescribed by the dermatologist, usually with food, and swallow the capsule whole with water. Do not change the dose, stop treatment, or share this medicine without medical advice.

Seek medical help for severe headache or vision changes, major mood changes, severe abdominal pain, or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Levosulpiride is used to relieve symptoms of slow or disturbed digestion, such as indigestion, bloating, fullness, nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for reflux-related symptoms.

How does it work?
It blocks certain dopamine receptors and improves movement of the upper digestive tract, helping the stomach empty more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the recommended timing in relation to meals, and do not take it for longer than advised. Do not drive or operate machinery if it causes drowsiness or dizziness.

Drowsiness, dizziness, headache, nausea, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea or constipation. Increased prolactin levels may cause breast tenderness, menstrual changes or milk discharge.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?
Tadalafil 10 mg is mainly used to treat erectile dysfunction (difficulty getting or keeping an erection) in adult men. It helps achieve an erection only when there is sexual stimulation.

It increases blood flow to the penis by relaxing blood vessels, helping an erection occur during sexual stimulation.

Drowsiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, nausea and next-day reduced alertness or coordination. Memory problems and unusual sleep-related behaviours can also occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and other medicines that cause sleepiness unless advised by a doctor. Do not drive or operate machinery if drowsy or not fully alert the next day. Zolpidem can cause dependence, particularly with prolonged use. Seek medical help immediately for sleep-walking, sleep-driving, breathing problems, severe confusion or unusual behaviour. Older adults and people with breathing problems, liver disease, depression or a history of substance misuse should use it only with medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used for the short-term treatment of insomnia, including difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.

How does it work?
Zolpidem enhances the action of calming signals in the brain to help induce sleep. Melatonin helps regulate the body's sleep-wake cycle and may support more natural sleep.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor, usually at or just before bedtime. Take it only when able to get a full night's sleep. Do not take more than prescribed or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, nausea, and next-day drowsiness or reduced alertness.

Precautions
Do not drink alcohol or combine with other sleep medicines or sedatives unless advised by a doctor. Avoid driving or operating machinery after taking it and the next day if drowsy or less alert. Zolpidem may rarely cause sleepwalking or other activities while not fully awake; stop use and seek medical advice if this occurs. Long-term or frequent use may cause dependence. Seek medical advice if sleep problems continue or worsen.

What is it used for?
Used for the short-term treatment of insomnia, including difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.

How does it work?
Zolpidem calms brain activity through GABA-A receptors to help induce sleep. Melatonin helps regulate the body's sleep-wake cycle.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, usually at bedtime when able to sleep for a full night. Do not take an extra dose during the same night. Avoid driving or activities requiring alertness after taking it.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, next-day drowsiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, nausea, and memory or concentration problems.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor before using other sleeping medicines, sedatives, opioids, or medicines that cause drowsiness. Use only for the prescribed duration because zolpidem may cause dependence or misuse. Seek medical help for unusual sleep behaviours, such as sleepwalking or doing activities while not fully awake, breathing problems, severe confusion, or an allergic reaction. Older adults and people with breathing, liver, or mental health problems should consult a doctor before use.

What is it used for?
Zolpidem extended-release is used for the short-term treatment of insomnia, especially difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.

How does it work?
It increases the activity of certain calming chemicals in the brain, helping reduce brain activity and promote sleep.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, immediately before going to bed, when able to sleep for 7–8 hours. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole; do not crush, chew or split it. Do not take it with or immediately after a meal unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, reduced alertness, memory problems and nausea may occur. Next-day sleepiness or impaired coordination is possible.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and other medicines that cause sleepiness unless specifically approved by a doctor. Do not drive or operate machinery until fully alert the next day. Seek medical help if sleepwalking, sleep-driving, unusual behaviour, breathing difficulty, severe confusion or an allergic reaction occurs. Use only as prescribed because prolonged or improper use may cause dependence. Older adults and people with breathing problems, liver disease, depression or a history of substance misuse should consult a doctor before use.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 200 mg tablets are used to treat certain serious fungal infections when other suitable antifungal treatments are not available, suitable or tolerated. They should only be used under medical supervision because of the risk of serious liver damage.

How does it work?
It blocks the production of ergosterol, an essential component of the fungal cell membrane. This weakens the membrane and stops fungal growth.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor and swallow the tablet with water. Do not self-medicate or change the dose, frequency or treatment duration. Tell the doctor about all other medicines being taken.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache and itching may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and inform the doctor about any liver disease. Seek medical help promptly for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe weakness, persistent nausea or abdominal pain. Ketoconazole has many important medicine interactions and may affect heart rhythm and adrenal hormone production; it is not suitable for everyone.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membranes, helping to clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use it only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Apply/use it on the affected area as instructed, and wash hands before and after use. Avoid swallowing it and keep it away from the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild burning, itching, redness, irritation, dryness or stinging at the application site.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes and broken skin. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs, or if the infection does not improve as expected.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% soap is used on the skin to treat fungal infections, such as ringworm and other superficial fungal skin infections. Use it only for the condition advised by a doctor or stated on the product label.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole stops fungi from making ergosterol, an essential part of their cell membrane. This helps control and clear the fungal infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Wet the affected skin, apply the soap to form a lather, and rinse well. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Use as directed on the label or by a doctor; do not use it more often or for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, burning, itching, dryness or redness may occur where it is applied.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole or any ingredient in the product. Avoid contact with the eyes and broken or severely irritated skin. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs. Consult a doctor if the infection does not improve or worsens.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain, swelling and inflammation in conditions such as muscle, joint and arthritis-related pain. It may also help reduce fever.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and reduce fever through a complementary action.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a healthcare professional. Swallow with water, preferably after food, to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or anti-inflammatory painkillers unless advised.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to aceclofenac, paracetamol, aspirin or other anti-inflammatory painkillers. Tell the healthcare professional about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney, liver or heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or pregnancy, especially the last three months. Avoid excessive alcohol. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin reactions, breathing difficulty or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Acebrophylline 100 mg is used to help manage breathing problems caused by asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including wheezing, chest tightness and excess mucus. It helps improve airflow but is not usually intended for immediate relief of a sudden breathing attack.

How does it work?
It helps relax and widen the airways and reduces airway inflammation. It also helps thin and loosen mucus, making it easier to clear.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Do not stop regular treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and palpitations may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about heart disease, high blood pressure, irregular heartbeat, seizures, thyroid problems, liver disease or kidney disease. Tell the doctor about all other medicines being taken, as interactions may occur. Seek medical help for severe or worsening breathing difficulty, marked palpitations, persistent vomiting or seizures. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Acyclovir is an antiviral medicine used to treat herpes virus infections, including genital herpes, cold sores, shingles and chickenpox. It helps reduce the severity and duration of outbreaks but does not permanently remove the virus from the body.

How does it work?
It blocks the herpes virus from making new copies of itself, helping control the infection and allowing the body to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Drink plenty of fluids unless a doctor has advised otherwise. Do not take extra doses if a dose is missed; follow the prescribed instructions.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, dehydration, or an allergy to acyclovir or valacyclovir, as the dose may need adjustment. Older adults may need extra monitoring. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for reduced urination, severe confusion, unusual tiredness, or a serious skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Acyclovir eye ointment is used to treat herpes simplex infection of the eye, including herpes-related inflammation of the cornea.

How does it work?
It is an antiviral medicine that becomes active in infected cells and stops the herpes virus from multiplying.

How to take/use it
Use it in the affected eye exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before and after use, and avoid touching the eye or eyelashes with the ointment tube tip. Vision may be blurred briefly after application. Do not wear contact lenses unless advised by an eye specialist.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, burning, irritation or blurred vision after application.

Precautions
For eye use only. Do not use if allergic to acyclovir or related antiviral medicines. Seek medical advice if eye pain, redness or vision problems worsen, or if signs of an allergic reaction occur. Use only under medical supervision for a suspected herpes eye infection.

What is it used for?
Acyclovir is an antiviral medicine used to treat herpes simplex infections, including cold sores and genital herpes. It may also be prescribed for shingles and chickenpox.

How does it work?
It blocks the ability of herpes viruses to multiply, helping reduce the severity and duration of the infection. It does not remove the virus permanently from the body.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. It can usually be taken with or without food. Drink plenty of fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Starting treatment early is generally more helpful.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or an allergy to acyclovir or valacyclovir. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney problems. Seek medical advice for confusion, hallucinations, severe weakness, or a serious skin reaction. Avoid sexual contact during genital herpes outbreaks; acyclovir does not reliably prevent spreading the infection.

What is it used for?
Disulfiram is used as part of a supervised treatment plan for alcohol dependence. It helps support abstinence by causing an unpleasant reaction if alcohol is consumed.

How does it work?
It blocks the breakdown of alcohol in the body, causing acetaldehyde to build up. This can lead to flushing, headache, nausea, vomiting, palpitations and other unpleasant symptoms after drinking alcohol.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and under medical supervision. Do not consume alcohol while taking disulfiram, and avoid alcohol-containing products such as some cough syrups, mouthwashes, sauces and personal-care products. Follow the prescriber’s advice about alcohol avoidance after stopping treatment.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, headache, tiredness, nausea, vomiting, metallic or garlic-like taste, bad breath and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not start disulfiram without medical advice or if alcohol may still be present in the body. Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart disease, diabetes, epilepsy, mental-health conditions or pregnancy. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe weakness, abdominal pain, numbness, tingling or mental changes. Many medicines and products may interact with disulfiram, so provide a complete medication list to the doctor or pharmacist.

What is it used for?
Disodium Hydrogen Citrate is used as a urinary alkaliser to reduce burning or discomfort while passing urine. It may also help make urine less acidic, which can support the management or prevention of certain uric acid kidney stones.

How does it work?
It is converted in the body into alkaline substances, making the urine less acidic. This can help reduce irritation caused by acidic urine and may help dissolve or prevent some uric acid stones.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed by the doctor or product label. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Maintain adequate fluid intake unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, or bloating may occur.

Precautions
Use only with medical advice if there is kidney disease, heart failure, high blood pressure, swelling, or a sodium-restricted diet, as it contains sodium. Seek medical advice for persistent urinary burning, fever, back pain, blood in the urine, or difficulty passing urine. Do not self-treat suspected kidney stones or urinary infection.

What is it used for?
The supplied ingredient list does not confirm a specific medical indication or dosage form. Avoid use if allergic to any ingredient. Stop using it if significant irritation, swelling, rash, or breathing difficulty occurs and seek medical help. Keep out of the reach of children. What is it used for?
Alpha ketoanalogues with essential amino acids are used in people with chronic kidney disease who are following a controlled low-protein diet. They help provide essential amino acids while reducing the amount of nitrogen waste produced by protein breakdown.

How does it work?
The ketoanalogue components are converted by the body into essential amino acids using nitrogen already present in the body. This supports nutrition while limiting the production of waste products that the kidneys need to remove.

How to take/use it
Use only under medical supervision and as part of the prescribed kidney-friendly, low-protein diet. Take it with meals and follow the product label or doctor’s instructions for the exact dose and duration. Do not change the diet or dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, vomiting or diarrhoea may occur. Products containing calcium may rarely cause increased blood calcium levels, which can lead to constipation, nausea, excessive thirst or frequent urination.

Precautions
Regular medical monitoring is needed, including kidney function and blood calcium levels. Inform the doctor about calcium disorders, kidney stones or medicines containing calcium. Seek medical advice if symptoms of high calcium levels occur. In advanced kidney disease, use only under the supervision of a nephrologist or other qualified healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Amikacin injection is a strong antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, especially those caused by certain bacteria that may not respond to other antibiotics. It is usually given in a hospital or under close medical supervision.

How does it work?
It stops bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents them from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Amikacin is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule are decided by the doctor based on the infection, body weight and kidney function. Do not self-inject or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea, vomiting, headache and weakness may occur. Kidney problems and hearing or balance problems are important serious side effects that require prompt medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Kidney function and sometimes hearing may need monitoring during treatment. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially those that can affect the kidneys, hearing or muscles. Seek medical help for reduced urine, ringing in the ears, hearing loss, dizziness, breathing difficulty or severe weakness.

What is it used for?
Amiodarone is used to treat and prevent serious irregular heart rhythms (arrhythmias), including fast or uneven heartbeats. It is usually prescribed when other treatments are not suitable or have not worked.

How does it work?
It helps control abnormal heart rhythms by slowing and stabilising the electrical signals in the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food as advised. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice, even if the heartbeat feels normal.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, constipation, loss of appetite, tiredness, dizziness, tremors and increased sensitivity to sunlight may occur.

Precautions
Regular medical checks may be needed for the heart, thyroid, liver, lungs and eyes during treatment. Tell the doctor about thyroid, lung, liver or heart problems, and about all other medicines being taken, as amiodarone has important drug interactions. Avoid grapefruit unless the doctor advises otherwise, use sun protection, and seek medical advice for new or worsening breathlessness, persistent cough, fainting, severe heartbeat changes, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or vision changes. Inform the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Amiodarone is used to treat and prevent certain serious abnormal heart rhythms, including fast or irregular heartbeats. It is usually prescribed when other treatments are not suitable or have not worked.

How does it work?
It slows and stabilises the electrical signals in the heart, helping the heart beat more regularly.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop taking it suddenly unless advised by a doctor. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice unless the prescriber says they are safe.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, constipation, tiredness, dizziness, and increased sensitivity to sunlight may occur. Bluish-grey skin discolouration or vision changes can occur with longer-term use.

Precautions
Regular medical monitoring may be needed, including heart, thyroid, liver, lung, and eye checks. Tell the doctor about existing thyroid, liver, lung, or heart problems and all other medicines being taken, as amiodarone has many important drug interactions. Seek medical advice urgently for worsening breathlessness, persistent cough, fainting, a very slow heartbeat, yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe skin reaction, or new vision problems. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Amlodipine 5 mg is used to treat high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed to prevent chest pain caused by angina. It helps reduce the risk of complications from high blood pressure, such as heart attack and stroke.

How does it work?
Amlodipine is a calcium-channel blocker. It relaxes and widens the blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily and reducing the workload on the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food and should be swallowed with water. Do not stop taking it without medical advice. It is not intended to relieve sudden chest pain.

Common side effects
Ankle or foot swelling, headache, dizziness, flushing, tiredness, palpitations, nausea and stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about low blood pressure, liver disease, heart problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Rise slowly if dizziness occurs. Seek urgent medical help for severe dizziness, fainting, swelling of the face or throat, or worsening or new chest pain.

What is it used for?
Amlodipine is used mainly to treat high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed to help prevent chest pain caused by angina.

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens the blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily. This lowers blood pressure and reduces the workload on the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow it with water and do not stop it without medical advice. If it is being used for angina, it is not intended to relieve a sudden chest-pain attack.

Common side effects
Ankle or foot swelling, headache, dizziness, flushing, tiredness, palpitations, nausea and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is very low blood pressure, liver disease or a heart condition. Dizziness may occur, especially when starting treatment; take care when driving or standing up. Inform the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for severe dizziness, fainting, worsening chest pain or signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It may also help prevent chest pain due to angina when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Amlodipine relaxes and widens blood vessels. Atenolol slows the heart rate and reduces the heart’s workload, helping lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, with or without food, preferably at the same time each day. Do not stop it suddenly, especially because of atenolol. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, ankle swelling, tiredness, slow heartbeat, cold hands or feet, and nausea.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is a slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, asthma or other breathing problems, heart conduction problems, heart failure, diabetes, or kidney disease. Monitor for excessive dizziness or fainting. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not stop treatment suddenly.

What is it used for?
This is an injectable antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxicillin kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps amoxicillin work against bacteria that can otherwise resist it.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a doctor or nurse, usually by injection into a vein. The dose, timing and treatment duration depend on the infection and must be decided by the prescriber. Do not self-inject or stop treatment early unless advised.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash and pain or redness at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxicillin, clavulanate or similar antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease and any previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Contact a doctor for severe or persistent diarrhoea, including diarrhoea with blood.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, sinuses, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, and teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against a wider range of infections.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor. Take doses with a meal or snack to reduce stomach upset, and complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not share this antibiotic or use leftover medicine.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur. Thrush can also occur. Seek medical advice if diarrhoea is severe or persistent.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, clavulanic acid or related antibiotics. Tell the doctor about previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, kidney disease, or any history of severe allergy. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or blistering or peeling skin.

What is it used for?
Amoxicillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ears, sinuses, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxicillin kills susceptible bacteria by damaging their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps prevent some bacteria from making enzymes that can stop amoxicillin from working.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Swallow with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not take leftover antibiotics or share them with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and oral or vaginal thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there is a known serious allergy to penicillin, amoxicillin, clavulanic acid or related cephalosporin antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, glandular fever, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, a severe skin rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ears, sinuses, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps protect amoxycillin from bacterial resistance, allowing it to work against a wider range of bacteria.

Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, and any medicines being taken. Seek medical attention for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Herbal toothpaste is used for routine cleaning of the teeth and gums as part of daily oral hygiene. It helps remove food particles and plaque during brushing.

How does it work?
It helps clean the teeth and gums through brushing and the cleansing action of its ingredients. The exact benefits depend on the herbs and other ingredients in the product.

How to take/use it
Use for brushing the teeth as directed on the product label. Do not swallow. Rinse the mouth after brushing.

Common side effects
Mild mouth irritation or an allergic reaction may occur in sensitive people. Stop using it if irritation develops.

Precautions
Do not swallow the toothpaste. Children should use it under adult supervision. Check the ingredients if there is a known allergy or sensitivity. Seek dental advice for persistent tooth pain, bleeding gums or other ongoing oral problems.

What is it used for?
Chlorhexidine mouthwash is used to reduce harmful bacteria in the mouth and help manage plaque and gum inflammation (gingivitis). It may be recommended after some dental procedures or when usual brushing is difficult.

How does it work?
It is an antiseptic that kills or reduces bacteria in the mouth. It also attaches to the surfaces inside the mouth, allowing its antibacterial effect to last for some time.

How to take/use it
Use it only as directed by a dentist or doctor. Rinse the mouth with the measured amount, then spit it out. Do not swallow the mouthwash. Do not dilute it unless specifically instructed. Avoid eating or drinking immediately after use if advised by the dentist.

Common side effects
Temporary staining of the teeth or tongue, altered taste, mouth irritation, dryness, or increased tartar may occur, especially with continued use.

Precautions
Do not swallow. Stop using it and seek medical help if swelling, rash, breathing difficulty, or other signs of an allergic reaction occur. Use for the recommended period only, as prolonged use can increase staining and taste changes. Keep away from children. Continue regular dental cleaning unless advised otherwise.

What is it used for?
This medicine is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

What is it used for?
Apixaban is an anticoagulant used to prevent blood clots and reduce the risk of stroke in people with certain irregular heart rhythms. It is also used to treat deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), and to help prevent these clots from returning. It may also be used to prevent clots after certain hip or knee replacement surgeries.

How does it work?
Apixaban blocks factor Xa, a substance needed for blood clot formation. This reduces the blood's ability to form harmful clots.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, with or without food. Do not stop or change the dose without medical advice, as this may increase the risk of clots. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber's instructions.

Common side effects
Easy bruising, nosebleeds, bleeding from the gums, heavier menstrual bleeding, nausea, and anaemia. Any unusual or prolonged bleeding requires medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of bleeding, stomach ulcers, kidney or liver problems, or planned surgery or dental treatment. Avoid starting aspirin, painkillers such as ibuprofen, or other blood-thinning medicines unless advised by a doctor. Seek urgent medical help for severe or uncontrollable bleeding, blood in the urine or stools, vomiting blood, severe headache, or an injury to the head.

What is it used for?
Apixaban is an anticoagulant (blood thinner) used to prevent and treat harmful blood clots. It may be prescribed to reduce the risk of stroke in certain people with an irregular heartbeat, and to treat or prevent deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE).

How does it work?
