This medicine is usually given as an injection into a vein or muscle by a healthcare professional. Use it only as prescribed and complete the recommended treatment unless the prescriber advises otherwise. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash, itching, and pain or redness at the injection site may occur. Changes in liver tests or blood counts can also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to penicillin, cephalosporin, or other antibiotics, and about liver disease, kidney disease, or bleeding problems. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, unusual bleeding, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Avoid alcohol during treatment unless the doctor says it is safe, as cefoperazone may cause an unpleasant reaction with alcohol.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime sodium injection is an antibiotic used to treat a range of serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin, abdomen, bones and joints. It may also be used to help prevent infection during certain surgeries. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a doctor or nurse as an injection into a vein or muscle. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and medical advice. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, rash, and pain or inflammation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any allergy to cefuroxime, cephalosporin antibiotics, penicillins or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney disease. Seek medical attention for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Contact a doctor if severe or persistent diarrhoea develops during or after treatment. Use only as prescribed and complete the advised course.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime is an antibiotic used to treat a range of bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, chest, urinary tract and skin, when prescribed by a healthcare professional. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall, which stops the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow oral tablets with water; taking cefuroxime tablets after food may improve absorption. Do not share this antibiotic or use leftover doses.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, cephalosporins or other beta-lactam antibiotics unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related severe diarrhoea, or any history of serious medicine allergies. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime sodium is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by susceptible bacteria, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin, abdomen, bones and joints. It may also be used to prevent infections during some surgeries, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It is a cephalosporin antibiotic that kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and medical advice. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Pain or inflammation at the injection site, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, other cephalosporins or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, previous antibiotic-related severe diarrhoea, or a history of serious allergies. Seek medical attention for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a widespread skin reaction. Use only when prescribed, as antibiotics do not treat viral infections.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, lungs, urinary tract and skin, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefuroxime kills bacteria by interfering with their cell-wall formation. Clavulanic acid helps protect cefuroxime from enzymes made by some bacteria, improving its action.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Take each dose with or after food if directed on the product label or by the prescriber. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, headache and skin rash may occur. Mild fungal infections such as oral or vaginal thrush are also possible.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin-type antibiotics, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin reaction. Contact a doctor for severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Cetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching or hives on the skin.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. It may be taken with or without food and should be swallowed with water. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness or sleepiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, and nausea may occur.

Precautions
Cetirizine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid or limit alcohol. Consult a healthcare professional if there is kidney disease, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat.

What is it used for?
Cetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching or hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance released during allergic reactions. This helps reduce itching, sneezing, runny nose and other allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water; it may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, nausea and dizziness.

Precautions
Cetirizine may cause drowsiness in some people; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known. Avoid or limit alcohol, as it may increase sleepiness. Seek medical advice if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or before giving it to a child. Get medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold and flu symptoms such as fever, headache, body aches, blocked nose, sneezing and a runny nose.

How does it work?
Paracetamol reduces fever and pain. Phenylephrine helps relieve nasal congestion, while diphenhydramine reduces sneezing and a runny nose; caffeine may help support the pain-relieving effect.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or other cold and flu ingredients. Do not exceed the recommended amount or duration.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, blurred vision, difficulty sleeping, nervousness, or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol. Ask a doctor before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, an enlarged prostate or difficulty passing urine. Seek medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not use with other paracetamol-containing medicines or sedating antihistamines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Chlorthalidone is mainly used to lower high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed to reduce swelling caused by excess fluid retention.

How does it work?
It is a thiazide-like diuretic, often called a water tablet. It helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water from the body, which lowers blood pressure and reduces fluid buildup.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Follow the dose and schedule on the prescription, and do not stop it without medical advice. It may increase urination, so taking it earlier in the day may be helpful if advised by the prescriber. Regular blood pressure and blood tests may be needed.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, headache, nausea, weakness, dehydration, and changes in blood salt or potassium levels. It may also increase uric acid and trigger gout in some people.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, gout, diabetes, low blood sodium or potassium, or an allergy to sulfonamide medicines. Seek medical advice for severe dizziness, fainting, muscle cramps, unusual weakness, confusion, or signs of dehydration. Discuss its use during pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor.

What is it used for?
Chlorthalidone is mainly used to treat high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed to reduce excess fluid retention (swelling) in certain conditions.

How does it work?
It is a thiazide-like diuretic, or water tablet. It helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water from the body, which lowers blood pressure and reduces fluid buildup.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may increase urination, so taking it earlier in the day can help avoid frequent urination at night. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, headache, nausea, weakness, and low levels of potassium or sodium in the blood. It may also increase uric acid or blood sugar levels.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is kidney or liver disease, gout, diabetes, dehydration, or a history of low potassium or sodium. Drink fluids as advised and rise slowly if feeling dizzy. Regular blood pressure and blood tests may be needed. Seek medical advice for severe weakness, confusion, fainting, muscle cramps, or an irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve pain, inflammation and swelling, especially in muscle, joint and bone-related conditions. It may also be prescribed after injuries or procedures when pain and swelling are present.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation, while paracetamol helps relieve pain and fever. Trypsin and chymotrypsin are enzymes that may help reduce inflammation and swelling.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to any ingredient. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase the risk of liver or stomach problems. Use during pregnancy, especially the last three months, only on medical advice. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, facial swelling or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve pain, inflammation and swelling associated with muscle, joint and soft-tissue injuries and other painful inflammatory conditions, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Trypsin, bromelain and rutoside may help support the reduction of swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by the doctor. Swallow the enteric-coated tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more or use it for longer than prescribed.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if allergic to diclofenac, other painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin, or any ingredient in the tablet. Tell the doctor about a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems, or bleeding disorders. Inform the doctor if taking blood thinners, other painkillers or medicines that increase bleeding risk. Avoid use during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, chest pain or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Trypsin-Chymotrypsin is used to help reduce swelling, inflammation and discomfort associated with injuries, soft-tissue inflammation and recovery after surgery. Use it only for the condition prescribed by the doctor.

How does it work?
It contains enzymes that help break down proteins involved in inflammation and swelling, which may support recovery of injured or inflamed tissues.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Do not change the dose or duration, and do not use it for a different condition without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea or loose motions, and skin rash may occur. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a bleeding disorder, an upcoming surgery, or use of blood-thinning medicines. Inform the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding, or if there has previously been an allergy to this medicine or similar enzymes.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve pain, swelling and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and soft-tissue conditions, sprains, injuries and arthritis. It may also be prescribed for short-term pain after certain procedures.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Trypsin, bromelain and rutoside may help reduce inflammation and swelling.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Swallow the enteric-coated tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is an allergy to diclofenac, aspirin or other painkillers, or a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding unless specifically advised. Inform the doctor about heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems, asthma, bleeding disorders, or use of blood thinners. Do not combine it with other diclofenac-containing or NSAID painkillers without medical advice. Avoid during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless prescribed. Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin rash.

What is it used for?
Cilnidipine 10 mg is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It helps lower blood pressure and reduces the risk of complications related to uncontrolled hypertension.

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens the blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily. This lowers the pressure inside the blood vessels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, palpitations, and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur.

Precautions
Use cautiously if there is very low blood pressure or significant liver or kidney disease. Rise slowly if dizziness occurs. Inform the doctor if pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice for fainting, severe dizziness, or troublesome swelling.

What is it used for?
Cilnidipine 5 mg is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It helps lower blood pressure and reduces the strain on the heart and blood vessels.

How does it work?
It blocks calcium channels in the blood vessel walls, helping the blood vessels relax and widen. This improves blood flow and lowers blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, preferably at the same time each day. Do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, palpitations, tiredness, and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice, especially if there is low blood pressure, heart disease, or liver or kidney problems. Rise slowly if dizziness occurs. Seek medical help for severe dizziness, fainting, or swelling. Tell the doctor if pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It may help lower the risk of complications related to persistently high blood pressure when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Cilnidipine relaxes and widens blood vessels, while metoprolol slows the heart rate and reduces the heart’s workload. Together, they help lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, tiredness, headache, slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, flushing, and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially with asthma or breathing problems, a very slow heartbeat, heart block, heart failure, diabetes, or liver disease. Metoprolol may hide some warning signs of low blood sugar. Rise slowly if dizzy, and seek medical help for fainting, severe breathing difficulty, or a very slow heartbeat. Tell the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding and about all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and other complications.

How does it work?
Cilnidipine relaxes and widens blood vessels, while telmisartan blocks a hormone that causes blood vessels to tighten. Together, they help lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food, and swallow it with water. Take it regularly and do not stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, tiredness, low blood pressure and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur. Contact a doctor if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, low blood pressure, or high potassium levels. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor. This medicine should not be used during pregnancy; seek medical advice if pregnancy occurs. Rise slowly if dizziness occurs, and have blood pressure, kidney function and potassium monitored as advised.

What is it used for?
Cilostazol is used to improve walking distance and reduce leg pain caused by intermittent claudication, a symptom of reduced blood flow to the legs in peripheral arterial disease.

How does it work?
It widens blood vessels and reduces the stickiness of platelets, helping improve blood flow to the legs.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the prescribed timing and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, abnormal stools, dizziness, palpitations and fast heartbeat.

Precautions
Do not use it if there is heart failure or a history of serious bleeding. Inform the doctor about heart rhythm problems, low blood pressure, liver or kidney disease, bleeding disorders, or any planned surgery. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially blood thinners and antiplatelet medicines. Seek medical help for severe or persistent headache, chest pain, fainting, unusual bleeding or a fast or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Cilostazol is used to improve walking ability and reduce leg pain caused by intermittent claudication, a condition in which narrowed leg arteries reduce blood flow during walking.

How does it work?
It widens blood vessels and reduces the tendency of platelets to stick together, helping improve blood flow to the legs.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. It is usually taken on an empty stomach, either at least 30 minutes before or 2 hours after meals. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, abnormal stools, dizziness, palpitations, and a fast heartbeat.

Precautions
Do not use cilostazol if there is heart failure or active bleeding. Inform the doctor about heart rhythm problems, recent heart attack or chest pain, bleeding disorders, kidney or liver disease, and all other medicines being taken. Seek medical help for severe or persistent headache, fainting, chest pain, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Cetirizine syrup is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching or hives on the skin.

How does it work?
Cetirizine is an antihistamine. It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions, thereby reducing allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device rather than a household spoon. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, and stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Cetirizine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase sleepiness. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
Citicoline is used to support brain function and recovery after conditions such as stroke or head injury. It may also be prescribed for problems with memory, attention or other cognitive functions.

How does it work?
Citicoline helps provide building blocks for nerve-cell membranes and supports the production of certain brain chemicals involved in memory and nerve signalling.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or as stated on the product label. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice. If it is an oral tablet or capsule, swallow it with water.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include headache, dizziness, nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, restlessness or difficulty sleeping.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, allergies and all other medicines being used. Medical advice is important if there is a history of significant blood-pressure or heart-rate problems. Seek medical advice if side effects are severe or persistent.

What is it used for?
Citicoline is used under medical supervision to support brain function, including cognitive problems and recovery after conditions such as stroke or head injury.

How does it work?
Citicoline helps provide materials needed for nerve-cell membranes and may support the function of certain brain chemicals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed or as directed on the product label. Do not change the dose or treatment duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, stomach upset, diarrhoea, restlessness or difficulty sleeping may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergies and all medicines being used. Medical advice is especially important during pregnancy or breastfeeding, in children, or when taking medicines for Parkinson’s disease. Seek urgent care for sudden weakness, speech difficulty or other new stroke symptoms.

What is it used for?
Citicoline 500 mg + Piracetam 800 mg is used under medical supervision to support brain function and help manage cognitive problems such as difficulties with memory, attention or thinking. It may also be prescribed during recovery from certain brain conditions, including stroke, when considered appropriate by a doctor.

How does it work?
Citicoline helps support the production of important components of nerve-cell membranes and brain chemical activity. Piracetam may help support communication and function between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow it with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, nervousness, restlessness, dizziness and difficulty sleeping may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, a history of bleeding, brain haemorrhage, or if taking blood thinners or other medicines that increase bleeding risk. Older adults may need kidney-function monitoring. Seek medical advice if unusual bleeding, severe headache, confusion or an allergic reaction occurs. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only if specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Clarithromycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the chest, throat, sinuses, ears and skin. It may also be used with other medicines to treat Helicobacter pylori infection linked to stomach ulcers. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, indigestion, headache and an altered or bitter taste.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to clarithromycin or other macrolide antibiotics, liver or kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, or a history of severe diarrhoea after antibiotics. Clarithromycin can interact with several medicines, so provide a complete list of medicines being taken. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, a fast or irregular heartbeat, or signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used to soften and help remove excess earwax (ear cerumen) that may cause blockage or reduced hearing.

How does it work?
The ingredients help soften and loosen hardened earwax. Benzocaine may provide a local numbing effect to reduce minor discomfort.

How to take/use it
Use in the ear only and follow the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions. Do not insert cotton buds or other objects into the ear. Do not swallow.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, burning, itching, irritation or discomfort in the ear. Stop use if signs of an allergic reaction occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there is ear pain, discharge, bleeding, a suspected or known perforated eardrum, ear tubes, or a current ear infection unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice if blockage or hearing problems persist. Use in children only on professional advice.

What is it used for?
Clindamycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the skin, teeth, bones, joints, lungs and other body tissues. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Do not skip doses or stop treatment early unless advised by a healthcare professional. If it is an oral medicine, swallow it with a full glass of water.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and diarrhoea may occur. Skin rash can also occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to clindamycin or lincomycin. Tell the doctor if there is a history of colitis or other bowel disease. Contact a doctor promptly for severe, persistent or watery/bloody diarrhoea, even during or after treatment, as this may indicate a serious bowel infection. Seek urgent help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Clindamycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections affecting the skin, teeth, bones, lungs and other parts of the body. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not share this medicine with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to clindamycin or lincomycin. Seek medical help for severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea during treatment or even several weeks afterwards, as this may indicate a serious bowel infection. Tell the doctor about previous bowel disease or liver problems. Seek urgent help for swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Clindamycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, including infections of the skin and soft tissues, bones and joints, teeth, lungs, and other areas. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Use clindamycin exactly as prescribed. The method of use depends on the product form and may be by mouth or injection. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about any previous allergy to clindamycin or lincomycin, or any history of colitis or severe diarrhoea after antibiotics. Contact a healthcare professional promptly if severe, persistent, or bloody diarrhoea develops during or after treatment. Seek urgent help for signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
This combination is used on the skin to treat acne, including pimples, blackheads and whiteheads.

How does it work?
Adapalene helps prevent blocked pores and supports normal skin cell turnover. Clindamycin reduces acne-causing bacteria and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use only on the skin and apply exactly as prescribed or directed on the product label. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry acne-prone skin. Avoid the eyes, lips, inside of the nose and broken or irritated skin. Wash hands after use.

Common side effects
Dryness, redness, peeling, burning, stinging, itching and increased sensitivity to sunlight may occur, especially when treatment is started.

Precautions
Avoid unnecessary sun exposure and use suitable sun protection. Do not use with other irritating acne products unless advised by a healthcare professional. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically approved by a doctor. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation or persistent diarrhoea develops.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat acne, including inflamed pimples and spots.

How does it work?
Clindamycin helps reduce acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Nicotinamide helps reduce skin inflammation and may help control excess oil.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry acne-affected skin as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Avoid the eyes, lips, mouth and broken skin, and wash hands after applying. Do not use more than recommended.

Common side effects
Skin dryness, redness, burning, itching, irritation or peeling at the application site.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes and other sensitive areas. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Seek medical advice if persistent or severe diarrhoea develops during treatment. Use only on the affected skin and as prescribed.

What is it used for?
Clobazam is mainly used with other medicines to help control seizures in epilepsy. It may also be prescribed for other conditions only when specifically advised by a doctor.

How does it work?
It enhances the calming action of GABA, a chemical messenger in the brain, helping to reduce excessive brain activity that can cause seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, and swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop it suddenly or change the dose without medical advice, as this may worsen seizures or cause withdrawal symptoms.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, tiredness, dizziness, poor coordination, slowed thinking, slurred speech, and memory problems may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful with driving or operating machinery because this medicine can cause sleepiness and reduced alertness. Tell the doctor if there is breathing difficulty, sleep apnoea, liver or kidney disease, pregnancy, or a history of medicine or substance dependence. Combining it with opioid pain medicines or other sedatives can cause severe drowsiness and breathing problems. Long-term use may cause dependence.

What is it used for?
Clobazam 5 mg is used mainly as an add-on treatment to help control certain types of epileptic seizures. It is usually prescribed by a specialist as part of an overall seizure-management plan.

How does it work?
Clobazam belongs to the benzodiazepine group. It increases the calming activity of a chemical messenger in the brain, helping reduce abnormal electrical activity that can cause seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment suddenly, as this may worsen seizures or cause withdrawal symptoms. Avoid alcohol and do not take more than prescribed.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, tiredness, reduced alertness, poor coordination, slurred speech and difficulty with memory or concentration may occur.

Precautions
Clobazam can cause dependence and withdrawal symptoms, especially with prolonged use. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Tell the doctor about breathing problems, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and any use of opioids, sleeping medicines or other sedatives, as combined use can cause excessive sedation and breathing difficulties. What is it used for?
This medicine is used on the skin to reduce redness, swelling, itching and inflammation in steroid-responsive skin conditions with thick, scaly or rough skin, such as psoriasis and some types of eczema.

How does it work?
Clobetasol is a very strong corticosteroid that reduces skin inflammation and itching. Salicylic acid softens and removes thick, scaly skin and may help the medicine penetrate better.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Wash hands after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not cover the area with a bandage or dressing unless advised by a doctor.

Mild burning, stinging, irritation, dryness, peeling or redness may occur. Prolonged or excessive use can cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Use only on the affected areas and only for the period advised. Do not use on the face, groin, underarms, broken skin or infected skin unless specifically directed. Avoid large areas of skin and use in children only under medical advice. Stop and seek medical advice if the condition worsens, signs of infection develop, or severe irritation occurs.

What is it used for?
Clopidogrel is an antiplatelet medicine used to help prevent harmful blood clots. It is commonly prescribed after a heart attack, stroke, certain heart procedures such as stent placement, or in some conditions affecting the blood vessels.

How does it work?
It makes blood platelets less likely to stick together and form clots. This helps reduce the risk of blocked blood vessels affecting the heart or brain.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not stop taking it without medical advice, especially after a stent or heart event. Tell the doctor or dentist before any surgery or dental procedure.

Common side effects
Easy bruising, bleeding that takes longer to stop, nosebleeds, indigestion, stomach pain, or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unexplained bleeding, black stools, blood in urine or vomit, or sudden severe headache or weakness. Inform the doctor about any bleeding disorder, stomach ulcer, liver disease, allergy to clopidogrel, or use of blood thinners, aspirin, or painkillers such as ibuprofen. Do not start other medicines or supplements without medical advice.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to help prevent harmful blood clots and reduce the risk of heart attack or stroke, especially in people with certain heart conditions or after procedures such as coronary stent placement. It is usually prescribed for a specific period by a doctor.

How does it work?
Clopidogrel and aspirin are antiplatelet medicines. They reduce the ability of platelets in the blood to stick together and form clots.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Swallow with water and do not stop taking it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions

Avoid starting painkillers such as ibuprofen or other blood-thinning medicines unless advised. Seek urgent medical help for severe or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, blood in urine, or sudden weakness or difficulty speaking.

Precautions

It damages the outer covering of fungal cells, stopping the fungus from growing and helping clear the infection.

Precautions

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, sinuses, chest, urinary tract and skin. It does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria and helps clear the infection.

Take it only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the prescribed dose and duration, and complete the full course even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with food if advised or if it causes stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporins or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as swelling or breathing difficulty.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with or just before a meal. Do not skip meals after taking it, and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Low blood sugar, nausea, stomach discomfort, increased appetite, and weight gain. Low blood sugar may cause sweating, shaking, dizziness, hunger, or confusion.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially with kidney or liver problems, in older adults, or if meals are irregular. Avoid excessive alcohol, as it can increase the risk of low blood sugar. Monitor blood sugar as advised. Seek urgent help for severe or persistent low blood sugar, fainting, or confusion.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when one medicine alone is not enough.

How does it work?
Glibenclamide helps the pancreas release more insulin. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with meals, to reduce stomach upset and help prevent low blood sugar. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular blood sugar monitoring may be advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, loss of appetite and a metallic taste may occur. Low blood sugar can cause sweating, shakiness, dizziness, hunger or confusion. Weight gain may also occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially if there are kidney or liver problems, dehydration, severe infection or heavy alcohol use. The risk of low blood sugar is higher with missed meals, excessive exercise or alcohol. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent weakness, breathing difficulty, unusual sleepiness or vomiting. Inform the doctor before surgery or certain scans using contrast dye, and if pregnant or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes.

How does it work?
Dapagliflozin helps the kidneys remove excess glucose through urine. Linagliptin helps the body release more insulin and reduce glucagon when blood sugar is high.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, genital fungal infections, urinary tract infections, dehydration, dizziness, and symptoms of a cold or blocked nose may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or sulfonylurea medicines.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about kidney problems, low blood pressure, repeated urinary or genital infections, or medicines used for diabetes. Drink adequate fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised. Seek urgent medical help for nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, difficulty breathing, or confusion, as these may indicate diabetic ketoacidosis. Discuss its use before surgery, prolonged fasting, pregnancy, or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes.

Dapagliflozin helps the kidneys remove excess glucose through urine. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin better.

Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food to reduce stomach upset. Drink enough fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, increased urination, genital fungal infections and urinary tract infections. Low blood sugar may occur, especially when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, recurrent genital or urinary infections, or heavy alcohol use. Seek urgent medical help for severe weakness, vomiting, stomach pain, breathing difficulty, confusion, or unusual tiredness, as these may indicate a serious reaction. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, recurrent urinary or genital infections, or heavy alcohol use. What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It may be prescribed when blood sugar is not adequately controlled with other treatment.

How does it work?
Dapagliflozin helps the kidneys remove excess glucose through urine. Vildagliptin increases the body's natural insulin response after meals and reduces the release of hormones that raise blood sugar.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food unless the prescriber gives different instructions. Swallow the tablet with water, and do not change or stop treatment without medical advice. Do not take a double dose if a dose is missed.

Common side effects
Increased urination, thirst, dizziness, dehydration, nausea, urinary tract infections, and genital fungal infections may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Drink adequate fluids unless advised otherwise. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, repeated urinary or genital infections, pancreatitis, or low blood pressure. Seek urgent medical help for severe dehydration, persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, difficulty breathing, confusion, or unusual tiredness. This medicine is not generally used for type 1 diabetes. Inform the doctor before major surgery, prolonged fasting, or if pregnant or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Dapagliflozin is used to help control blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is also prescribed for some adults with heart failure or chronic kidney disease, as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove extra glucose and sodium from the body through urine. This lowers blood sugar and may reduce strain on the heart and kidneys.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water, with or without food. Drink enough fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not stop it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Passing urine more often, increased thirst, dizziness, dehydration, urinary tract infections, and genital fungal infections. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, low blood pressure, repeated urinary or genital infections, or planned surgery. Seek urgent medical help for severe nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, difficulty breathing, or confusion, as these may indicate diabetic ketoacidosis. It is generally not used for type 1 diabetes unless specifically directed by a specialist. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Dapagliflozin is mainly used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It may also be prescribed for certain adults with heart failure or chronic kidney disease, as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove excess glucose from the blood through the urine. This can also reduce fluid build-up in some people with heart or kidney conditions.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet whole, with or without food. Drink enough fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Passing urine more often, increased thirst, dizziness, dehydration, urinary tract infection, and fungal infections of the genitals. Low blood sugar may occur, especially when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, dehydration, recurrent urinary or genital infections, or use of insulin or other diabetes medicines. Seek urgent medical help for severe nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, breathing difficulty, or confusion, as these may indicate diabetic ketoacidosis even if blood sugar is not very high. It may need to be temporarily stopped during prolonged fasting, severe illness, or before surgery—follow medical advice.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid used under specialist supervision for certain conditions involving bone loss, including osteoporosis. It may also be used in selected cases of anaemia or advanced breast cancer, only when specifically prescribed.

How does it work?
It acts like an androgen hormone and helps increase protein production. This may support bone formation and tissue rebuilding, but its effects and risks require medical monitoring.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection, usually by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the condition and must be decided by the prescriber. Do not self-inject or use it for bodybuilding.

Common side effects
Acne, oily skin, swelling due to fluid retention, changes in sex drive, mood changes, menstrual irregularities, increased facial or body hair, and changes in cholesterol levels may occur.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a specialist. Tell the doctor about liver, kidney, heart, prostate or hormone-sensitive breast conditions. It should be used cautiously in children and adolescents because it can affect growth and sexual development. Medical monitoring may include blood counts, liver function, cholesterol and hormone-related checks.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid mainly used as an additional treatment for osteoporosis, a condition in which bones become weak and fragile. It may also be used in some cases of anaemia related to kidney disease, only when specifically prescribed by a specialist.

How does it work?
It is a synthetic form of an androgen hormone. It promotes protein building and may support bone formation and red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as a deep injection into a muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the medical condition and must be decided by the prescriber. Do not self-inject or use it for bodybuilding.

Common side effects
Acne or oily skin, swelling due to fluid retention, changes in sexual desire, menstrual irregularities, increased facial or body hair, voice changes, injection-site pain, and changes in cholesterol levels may occur. In men, breast enlargement or reduced sperm production may occur.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Inform the doctor about liver, kidney, heart, prostate or breast disease, or high cholesterol. Women should report voice deepening, increased facial hair, or menstrual changes promptly, as some effects may be irreversible. Children and adolescents require specialist supervision because it can affect growth and puberty. Regular medical check-ups may be needed during treatment.

What is it used for?
Deflazacort is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and control overactive immune reactions in conditions such as severe allergies, asthma, autoimmune disorders and other inflammatory conditions. It may also be prescribed for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

How does it work?
It acts like natural steroid hormones made by the body. It reduces inflammation and suppresses excessive immune activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with water. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach discomfort. Do not stop it suddenly, especially after prolonged use; the dose may need to be reduced gradually under medical supervision.

Common side effects
Increased appetite, weight gain, indigestion, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, acne, increased blood sugar and increased susceptibility to infections may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, liver or kidney problems, or any current infection. Avoid close contact with people who have contagious infections and check before receiving vaccines. Long-term use requires medical monitoring. Seek medical advice for signs of infection, vision changes or severe mood changes.

What is it used for?
Deflazacort is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and control an overactive immune response in conditions such as autoimmune disorders, severe allergies and other inflammatory illnesses. The exact reason for use depends on the condition being treated.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor, especially if it has been used for a longer period.

Common side effects
Increased appetite, indigestion, weight gain, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, acne and swelling may occur, particularly with higher doses or longer treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, osteoporosis, stomach ulcers, glaucoma, liver or kidney problems, or any current infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body's ability to fight infections; seek medical advice after exposure to chickenpox or measles. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically approved by a doctor. Long-term treatment may require monitoring and should not be stopped suddenly.

What is it used for?
Deflazacort is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactive immune responses in conditions such as allergic, inflammatory and autoimmune disorders. It should be used only for the condition prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and helps suppress an overactive immune response.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Do not stop it suddenly, especially after prolonged use, unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Increased appetite, weight gain, indigestion, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, raised blood sugar and increased risk of infections.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, liver or kidney problems, or any current infection. Avoid close contact with people who have contagious infections and check before receiving vaccines. Long-term treatment requires medical monitoring.

What is it used for?
Used to help relieve and prevent breathing difficulties caused by asthma and other long-term airway conditions such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It helps open the airways but is not usually used for immediate relief of a sudden breathing attack.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them open and making breathing easier.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Do not take extra doses or change the dose without medical advice. Take it at the same time each day if advised, and avoid excessive caffeine unless the doctor recommends otherwise.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, shakiness and a fast or irregular heartbeat.

Precautions
This medicine has a narrow safety margin, so regular medical monitoring may be needed. Inform the doctor about heart or liver disease, seizures, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, as many medicines can affect its safety. Smoking changes how it works; inform the doctor if smoking is started or stopped. Seek urgent medical help for severe vomiting, marked palpitations, confusion, seizures or worsening breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Etophylline + theophylline is a bronchodilator used to help relieve breathing difficulty, wheezing and chest tightness in conditions such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It should be used only as prescribed.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them open and making breathing easier.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Do not crush or chew it unless the product instructions specifically allow this. It is not usually intended to provide immediate relief during a sudden severe breathing attack unless directed by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, headache, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, shakiness and fast or pounding heartbeat.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about heart disease, high blood pressure, seizures, overactive thyroid, liver disease or persistent fever. Avoid excessive caffeine, as it may worsen side effects. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially other breathing medicines, antibiotics and seizure medicines. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent vomiting, very fast or irregular heartbeat, severe agitation or seizures.

What is it used for?
Etophylline and theophylline are bronchodilators used to help prevent and control breathing problems such as wheezing, chest tightness and breathlessness in asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). They are generally not intended for immediate relief of a sudden breathing attack.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them open and making breathing easier.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not take more than recommended, as theophylline can cause side effects at high levels. Take it consistently in relation to food, and do not change or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, shakiness and fast or irregular heartbeat.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, as theophylline has a narrow safety range and may require monitoring. Tell the doctor about heart disease, high blood pressure, seizures, liver disease, stomach ulcers or thyroid problems. Avoid excessive caffeine, and inform the doctor about all medicines being taken because several medicines can interact with theophylline. Seek urgent medical help for persistent vomiting, severe palpitations, marked shakiness or seizures.

What is it used for?
Etophylline and theophylline are bronchodilators used to help relieve breathing difficulties, wheezing and chest tightness in conditions such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). They are not usually used as the only treatment for a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping to widen them and improve airflow to the lungs.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Do not take more than the prescribed amount, as theophylline requires careful dosing. Do not stop regular treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, headache, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, tremors and fast or irregular heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, seizures, liver disease, stomach ulcer or an overactive thyroid. Tell the doctor about all medicines being used, as many medicines can interact with theophylline. Seek urgent medical help for severe vomiting, persistent fast or irregular heartbeat, seizures or worsening breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
This topical medicine is used for certain skin infections involving fungi or bacteria, especially when redness, itching and inflammation are also present. It should be used only when prescribed, as it contains a strong corticosteroid.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole and tolnaftate act against fungi, while neomycin and iodochlorhydroxyquinoline act against certain bacteria and other microorganisms. Clobetasol reduces skin inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before and after use, unless treating the hands. Avoid the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not cover the area with a tight bandage unless directed by a doctor. Do not use for longer than prescribed.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice because clobetasol is a potent steroid. Do not use on the face, groin, skin folds, broken skin or large areas unless specifically directed. Stop and seek medical advice if the rash worsens, spreads or develops swelling or severe irritation. Avoid use if there is a known allergy to any ingredient, including neomycin. Do not use for suspected viral skin infections unless prescribed.

What is it used for?
Dexlansoprazole is used to treat acid reflux (GERD), relieve heartburn, and help heal irritation or damage to the food pipe caused by stomach acid.

How does it work?
It reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach by blocking acid-producing proton pumps.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the modified-release capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It may generally be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, stomach pain or discomfort, nausea, gas, and constipation.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, osteoporosis, low magnesium or vitamin B12 levels, or allergies to acid-reducing medicines. Long-term use may require medical monitoring and can increase the risk of certain infections, low magnesium or vitamin B12, and bone fractures. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, or persistent diarrhoea. Inform the doctor about all other medicines being taken, as interactions are possible.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, swelling and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint, bone or soft-tissue conditions, injuries, and some dental or post-procedure pain. Use only as prescribed.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Serratiopeptidase is an enzyme used to help reduce swelling associated with inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow it with water. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless advised. Do not take it for longer than recommended or combine it with other diclofenac or NSAID painkillers unless a doctor advises.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness, headache and skin rash.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin or other NSAID painkillers. Inform the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, kidney, liver or heart disease, high blood pressure, or bleeding problems. Tell the doctor if taking blood thinners, steroids or other painkillers. Avoid during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed, particularly during the last three months. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Dydrogesterone is a progesterone-like medicine used to treat conditions caused by low progesterone, such as irregular or painful periods, endometriosis, abnormal uterine bleeding and absence of periods. It may also be prescribed to support fertility treatment or certain pregnancy-related progesterone deficiencies, as decided by a doctor.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone progesterone. It helps regulate the menstrual cycle and supports the lining of the uterus.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, as the dose and schedule depend on the condition being treated. Swallow the tablet with water and try to take it at the same time each day. Do not stop treatment or change the schedule without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache or migraine, nausea, stomach discomfort, breast tenderness, mood changes and changes in menstrual bleeding or spotting may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about unexplained vaginal bleeding, liver disease, migraine, depression or a history of hormone-sensitive conditions before taking it. Seek medical advice if bleeding is unusual or persistent. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only when specifically advised by a doctor. Seek urgent help for signs of an allergic reaction, such as facial swelling or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Dydrogesterone is used to supplement the hormone progesterone. It may be prescribed for progesterone-related menstrual problems such as irregular or painful periods and endometriosis, and in some fertility or pregnancy-related situations.

How does it work?
It acts like the body’s natural progesterone. This helps regulate the lining of the uterus and support a normal menstrual cycle when progesterone levels are insufficient.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor, at the recommended times and for the prescribed duration. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache or migraine, nausea, abdominal pain, breast tenderness, changes in menstrual bleeding, and mood changes may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about unexplained vaginal bleeding, liver disease, or any allergy to dydrogesterone. Seek medical advice for yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe abdominal pain, or an allergic reaction. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only as directed by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Diltiazem is used to lower high blood pressure, prevent or relieve chest pain due to angina, and control certain abnormal heart rhythms or a fast heartbeat.

How does it work?
It relaxes blood vessels and slows the heart rate, helping the heart pump with less effort and improving blood flow.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day. Take with or without food consistently. Do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless specifically instructed.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, constipation, nausea, tiredness, ankle or leg swelling, and a slow heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is low blood pressure, a slow heartbeat, heart block, heart failure, or liver or kidney disease. Tell the doctor about all medicines being used, especially beta-blockers, digoxin, and other heart or blood-pressure medicines. Avoid grapefruit or grapefruit juice unless a doctor or pharmacist confirms it is safe. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, severe dizziness, breathing difficulty, or a very slow or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Diltiazem is used to treat high blood pressure, prevent chest pain caused by angina, and control certain abnormal heart rhythms. The specific use depends on the prescription.

How does it work?
It relaxes blood vessels, helping lower blood pressure and improve blood flow to the heart. It can also slow the heart rate and help regulate abnormal heart rhythms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice. Take it consistently as directed, and follow any instructions specific to the formulation supplied.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, flushing, tiredness, constipation, nausea, ankle swelling, and a slow heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor if there is low blood pressure, a slow or irregular heartbeat, heart failure, or liver or kidney disease. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, especially beta-blockers, digoxin, and other medicines for blood pressure or heart rhythm. Avoid driving if dizzy. Seek medical help for fainting, severe breathing difficulty, marked swelling, or an unusually slow heartbeat. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Drotaverine is used to relieve painful spasms or cramps in the smooth muscles of the stomach and intestines, such as abdominal cramps. It may also be used for spasmodic menstrual, urinary or biliary pain when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It relaxes the smooth muscles in internal organs, helping reduce spasms and cramp-like pain.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water, with or without food. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, nausea, constipation, low blood pressure or palpitations may occur. Allergic reactions are uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Use only with medical advice if there is low blood pressure or severe liver, kidney or heart disease. Tell the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding. Avoid driving if dizzy. Seek medical attention for severe, persistent or unexplained abdominal pain, especially with vomiting, fever or blood in the stool.

What is it used for?
Drotaverine is used to relieve painful cramps and spasms caused by tightening of smooth muscles, especially stomach and intestinal cramps. It may also be used for spasms of the urinary or biliary tract and period-related cramps, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It relaxes smooth muscles in the stomach, intestines and other organs, helping reduce spasms and cramp-like pain.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. The dose and duration depend on the condition being treated.

Common side effects
Nausea, constipation, headache, dizziness, palpitations and low blood pressure may occur. Allergic reactions are uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice if there is low blood pressure or serious liver, kidney or heart disease. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness occurs. Seek medical help for severe allergy symptoms, fainting or a fast heartbeat. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Drotaverine injection is used to relieve painful cramps and spasms caused by tightening of smooth muscles, such as stomach or intestinal cramps, biliary spasms, urinary tract spasms and menstrual cramps.

How does it work?
It relaxes the smooth muscles in organs such as the intestine, bile ducts and urinary tract, helping to reduce spasms and cramp-like pain.

How to take/use it
This injection should be given only by a doctor or other trained healthcare professional. The dose and method of administration depend on the condition and should be decided by the prescriber. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, nausea, palpitations, low blood pressure and allergic reactions may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is low blood pressure or severe liver, kidney or heart disease. Seek immediate medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe dizziness or fainting. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding and all other medicines being used.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve painful menstrual cramps and other pain caused by smooth-muscle spasms, such as spasmodic abdominal pain.

How does it work?
Drotaverine relaxes the muscles responsible for spasms. Mefenamic acid reduces the production of prostaglandins, which contribute to pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Take it with or after food and swallow with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac or aspirin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache.

Precautions
Avoid or seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, NSAID-sensitive asthma, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Consult a doctor during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop use and seek urgent medical help for severe stomach pain, black stools, vomiting blood, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Drotaverine is used to relieve painful muscle spasms and cramps, especially in the stomach and intestines. It may also be prescribed for spasms of the bile or urinary tract and for menstrual cramps.

How does it work?
It relaxes the smooth muscles of internal organs, helping reduce spasms and cramp-like pain.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. If this is an oral liquid, measure each dose with a proper measuring device rather than a household spoon. Do not use more or for longer than recommended.

Precautions

Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness occurs. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, fainting, or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Divalproex sodium extended-release is mainly used to control seizures in epilepsy. It may also be prescribed for bipolar disorder or to prevent migraine attacks, as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It helps calm excessive electrical activity in the brain by increasing the effects of a natural calming chemical and affecting nerve-cell activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Precautions

Medical monitoring may be required.

What is it used for?
Divalproex ER is mainly used to control seizures in epilepsy. It may also be prescribed to help control episodes of mania in bipolar disorder and to prevent migraine headaches.

How does it work?
It helps calm excessive electrical activity in the brain by increasing the effects of certain natural calming chemicals and affecting nerve-cell activity.
