Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole with water; do not crush, chew or break it. Do not stop treatment suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, sleepiness, dizziness, tremor, weight gain and hair thinning or hair loss.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. It can cause serious liver problems, pancreatitis and changes in blood-cell or platelet counts; seek urgent medical help for severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, yellowing of the skin or eyes, unusual bruising or bleeding, or extreme drowsiness. It may cause serious harm to an unborn baby, so pregnancy or plans for pregnancy must be discussed with a doctor. Tell the doctor about liver disease, bleeding problems and all other medicines. Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy.

What is it used for?
Domperidone is used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also help improve symptoms related to slow movement of the upper digestive system, such as bloating or a feeling of fullness, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals involved in nausea and vomiting and helps increase movement of food through the upper digestive system.

How to take/use it
Take this tablet only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. It is generally taken before food, but follow the instructions on the prescription or pack.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, headache, abdominal cramps, diarrhoea, and breast tenderness or breast milk production due to increased prolactin levels.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is a heart rhythm problem, heart disease, significant liver disease, or low potassium or magnesium levels. It should not be used if there may be a blockage or bleeding in the stomach or intestine. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or interact with domperidone. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, a rapid or irregular heartbeat, or seizures.

What is it used for?
Donepezil is used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer’s disease, such as memory loss, confusion and difficulty with thinking. It may help manage symptoms but does not cure the disease.

How does it work?
It increases the level of acetylcholine, a chemical messenger involved in memory and thinking, by slowing its breakdown in the brain.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, preferably at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop treatment or change the way it is taken without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, trouble sleeping, tiredness and muscle cramps.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a slow or irregular heartbeat, fainting, asthma or other breathing problems, stomach ulcers or bleeding, seizures, or difficulty passing urine. Seek medical help for fainting, very slow heartbeat, black stools, vomiting blood, or severe breathing difficulty. Tell the doctor or dentist before surgery, especially if anaesthesia is planned.

What is it used for?
Donepezil is used to help manage symptoms of Alzheimer’s disease, including memory loss, confusion and problems with thinking. It may help maintain daily functioning but does not cure the disease.

How does it work?
It increases the amount of acetylcholine, a chemical messenger involved in memory and thinking, in the brain by slowing its breakdown.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually by mouth. It may be taken with or without food. Take it at the same time each day and do not stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed or treatment is interrupted, consult a doctor before restarting.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, weight loss, stomach discomfort, dizziness, headache, tiredness, muscle cramps and sleep problems.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about slow or irregular heartbeat, fainting, stomach ulcers or bleeding, asthma or chronic lung disease, seizures, urinary problems, or planned surgery. Seek medical help for fainting, severe or persistent vomiting, black stools, chest symptoms, or a very slow heartbeat. Older adults may be more prone to dizziness and falls.

What is it used for?
Used to manage symptoms of moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease dementia. It may help support memory, thinking and daily functioning, but it does not cure the disease.

How does it work?
Donepezil increases the availability of acetylcholine, a chemical involved in memory and thinking. Memantine helps protect brain cells from the effects of excessive glutamate activity.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor, at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, dizziness, headache, sleep problems, constipation and tiredness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart rhythm problems, a slow heartbeat or fainting, asthma or chronic breathing problems, seizures, stomach ulcers or bleeding, urinary blockage, or kidney disease. Use caution with other medicines that affect heart rate or brain function. Seek medical help for fainting, severe vomiting, black stools, breathing difficulty or a seizure.

What is it used for?
Dorzolamide and timolol eye drops are used to reduce raised pressure inside the eye in conditions such as open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension. Lowering eye pressure helps protect the optic nerve and reduce the risk of vision loss.

How does it work?
Dorzolamide reduces the formation of fluid inside the eye, while timolol also lowers fluid production. Together, they help reduce pressure in the eye.

How to take/use it
Use only in the affected eye(s) and exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before use and avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or any surface. Remove contact lenses before applying the drops and follow the product instructions about when to replace them. Do not stop treatment without medical advice. Temporary blurred vision may occur, so avoid driving until vision is clear.

Common side effects
Temporary burning or stinging, blurred vision, watery or dry eyes, eye irritation, a bitter taste, headache, tiredness, dizziness, or a slow heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor before use if there is asthma or chronic breathing disease, a slow heartbeat, heart block, heart failure, low blood pressure, diabetes, kidney disease, or an allergy to dorzolamide, timolol, or sulfonamide medicines. Timolol can affect breathing and heart rate even when used as eye drops. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, fainting, severe dizziness, marked slowing of the heartbeat, or swelling of the face or eyes.

What is it used for?
Doxycycline is an antibiotic used to treat a range of bacterial infections. Lactic acid bacillus is included to help support healthy gut bacteria during antibiotic treatment. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Doxycycline stops susceptible bacteria from making proteins needed for their growth. Lactic acid bacillus is a probiotic that helps maintain the balance of beneficial bacteria in the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor and complete the prescribed course. Swallow with plenty of water while sitting or standing, and do not lie down immediately after taking it. Avoid taking it at the same time as antacids or mineral supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, calcium or iron; ask a doctor or pharmacist about suitable spacing.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort, headache and increased sensitivity to sunlight. Mild bloating may occur due to the probiotic.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to tetracycline antibiotics, pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver problems or a history of swallowing or food-pipe problems. Use in children under 8 years is generally avoided unless specifically prescribed. Limit strong sunlight and use sun protection. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, difficulty swallowing, severe headache, vision changes or signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Doxycycline injection is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection and should be decided by the prescriber. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, increased sensitivity to sunlight, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to doxycycline or other tetracycline antibiotics. Avoid unnecessary exposure to sunlight and use sun protection. Tell the doctor if pregnant, planning pregnancy, breastfeeding, or if the patient is a child. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash, breathing difficulty, or severe injection-site reactions.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve nausea and vomiting during pregnancy, commonly called morning sickness.

How does it work?
Doxylamine is an antihistamine that helps reduce nausea and vomiting. Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) and folic acid provide vitamins important during pregnancy.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the prescribed timing and instructions, and do not take more than recommended. Do not stop or change the treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, constipation and tiredness.

Precautions
This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving, alcohol and other medicines that cause sleepiness unless advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, breathing problems, liver or kidney disease, or use of sedative medicines. Seek medical advice if vomiting is severe or there are signs of dehydration.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to help prevent and relieve nausea and vomiting during pregnancy. It also provides folic acid, which supports normal cell growth and fetal development.

How does it work?
Doxylamine is an antihistamine that helps reduce nausea and vomiting. Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) helps support processes involved in controlling pregnancy-related nausea, while folic acid provides nutritional support during pregnancy.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the instructions on the label and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Do not take additional doxylamine, vitamin B6 or folic acid products unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth and constipation may occur.

Precautions
This medicine may cause sleepiness or reduced alertness. Avoid driving, alcohol and other medicines that cause drowsiness until its effects are known. Tell the doctor about other medicines being taken, especially sleeping tablets, sedatives or other antihistamines. Seek medical advice if vomiting is severe or fluids cannot be kept down.

What is it used for?
Doxofylline is a bronchodilator used to help relieve and prevent breathing problems caused by asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including wheezing and shortness of breath.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them widen so that air can flow more easily.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. It is not intended to provide immediate relief during a sudden severe breathing attack; use the prescribed rescue inhaler when needed.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, difficulty sleeping, restlessness, tremor and fast or irregular heartbeat.

Precautions
Tell the doctor before use if there is a history of heart disease, irregular heartbeat, high blood pressure, seizures, overactive thyroid, or liver or kidney problems. Avoid taking other medicines containing theophylline or similar bronchodilators unless advised by a doctor. Limit excessive caffeine, and seek medical help for severe vomiting, chest pain, fainting or a very fast or irregular heartbeat. Tell the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of dry cough, blocked nose, runny nose and sneezing associated with common cold or allergy symptoms.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps suppress the cough reflex. Phenylephrine reduces nasal swelling, while chlorpheniramine (CPM) helps relieve histamine-related symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and check other cold or cough medicines to avoid duplicate ingredients.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, headache, nervousness, increased blood pressure or a fast heartbeat.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if affected. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, prostate or urination problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not use with MAO inhibitors, and check with a doctor or pharmacist before combining with antidepressants or other medicines that affect serotonin.

What is it used for?
Sildenafil 100 mg is used to treat erectile dysfunction (difficulty getting or keeping an erection firm enough for sexual activity) in adult men. It does not increase sexual desire and works only when there is sexual stimulation.

How does it work?
It helps relax blood vessels in the penis, increasing blood flow during sexual stimulation and helping produce an erection.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Do not take more than prescribed or use it more often than directed. It is not suitable for everyone; follow the prescribed instructions carefully.

Common side effects
Headache, facial flushing, indigestion, blocked or runny nose, dizziness, and visual changes such as blurred vision or altered colour vision.

Precautions
Do not use with nitrate medicines for chest pain or riociguat, as this can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure. Tell the doctor about heart disease, low blood pressure, recent stroke or heart attack, liver or kidney problems, or if taking alpha-blockers or other medicines for erectile dysfunction. Seek urgent medical help for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, sudden loss of vision or hearing, chest pain, or severe dizziness.

What is it used for?
Duloxetine is used to treat depression and anxiety, and certain types of nerve pain, including pain related to diabetic nerve damage. The exact reason for use depends on the prescriber's advice.

How does it work?
It increases the activity of serotonin and noradrenaline, natural chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood and reduce the perception of pain.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the gastro-resistant capsule whole with water; do not crush, chew or open it. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, dry mouth, constipation, headache, dizziness, sleepiness, reduced appetite, increased sweating and sexual problems may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney problems, glaucoma, seizures, bipolar disorder, bleeding problems or pregnancy. Avoid heavy alcohol use. Do not use it with monoamine oxidase inhibitors, and inform the doctor about all other medicines, especially antidepressants and other medicines affecting serotonin. Seek urgent help for severe allergic symptoms, unusual bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe agitation, fever, muscle stiffness or thoughts of self-harm.

What is it used for?
Duloxetine is a prescription medicine used to treat depression and generalised anxiety disorder. It is also used for some types of nerve pain, including diabetic nerve pain, and certain long-lasting muscle or bone pain conditions.

How does it work?
It increases the activity of serotonin and noradrenaline, natural chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood and reduce the perception of pain.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the delayed-release capsule whole with water. Do not crush or chew it. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, dry mouth, headache, dizziness, sleepiness or difficulty sleeping, constipation, reduced appetite, increased sweating and sexual problems.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, glaucoma, bipolar disorder, seizures, bleeding problems, high blood pressure or pregnancy. Avoid heavy alcohol use. Duloxetine can interact with antidepressants, MAO inhibitors, blood thinners and other medicines that affect serotonin. Seek urgent medical help for suicidal thoughts, severe agitation, unusual bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or symptoms such as fever, confusion, muscle stiffness and diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve and prevent narrowing of the airways in breathing conditions such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It helps reduce wheezing, breathlessness and chest tightness.

How does it work?
Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles around the airways. Ipratropium reduces tightening of the airways, helping air flow more freely.

How to take/use it
Use only by inhalation with the prescribed device and follow the instructions provided by the doctor or device leaflet. Do not change the dose or frequency without medical advice. If breathing suddenly worsens or does not improve, seek urgent medical help.

Common side effects
Shakiness, nervousness, headache, fast heartbeat or palpitations, dry mouth, throat irritation and cough.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, glaucoma, prostate or urinary problems, diabetes, thyroid disease, or a history of medicine allergies. Avoid getting the medicine into the eyes. Seek medical help if severe eye pain, blurred vision, difficulty passing urine, allergic reactions or worsening breathing occurs.

What is it used for?
This nebuliser solution helps relieve bronchospasm, wheezing and breathing difficulty in conditions such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It relaxes narrowed airway muscles to make breathing easier.

How does it work?
Levosalbutamol and ipratropium are bronchodilators. They relax the muscles around the airways through different actions, helping open the air passages.

How to take/use it
Use only by nebulisation and exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the nebuliser device instructions carefully. Do not swallow or inject the solution, and do not change the dose or frequency without medical advice.

Common side effects
Trembling, nervousness, headache, dry mouth, throat irritation, cough, dizziness, nausea and fast or pounding heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, high blood pressure, glaucoma, thyroid problems, diabetes or difficulty passing urine, including prostate problems. Avoid getting the mist in the eyes. Seek urgent medical help for severe or worsening breathing difficulty, chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, swelling or an allergic reaction. If breathing suddenly worsens after use, stop and seek medical advice immediately.

What is it used for?
Dutasteride is used to treat an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia, or BPH). It can help improve urinary symptoms such as difficulty starting urination, weak urine flow and frequent or urgent urination, and may reduce the risk of urinary retention.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme that converts testosterone into dihydrotestosterone (DHT). Lower DHT levels help shrink the enlarged prostate and improve urine flow.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole; do not chew or open it. Take it regularly and do not stop without medical advice.

Common side effects
Reduced sex drive, difficulty getting or maintaining an erection, ejaculation problems, breast tenderness or enlargement, and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease or any history of prostate problems. Dutasteride lowers PSA blood-test levels, so inform the doctor before prostate screening. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should not handle leaking capsules, as the medicine may harm a male baby. Do not donate blood during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose. Seek medical advice for breast lumps or nipple discharge.

What is it used for?
Eberconazole 1% cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch, skin candidiasis and pityriasis versicolor.

How does it work?
It is an antifungal medicine that damages the fungal cell membrane, stopping the growth of fungi on the skin.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected and surrounding skin exactly as directed by the doctor or product instructions. Wash and dry the area before application, wash hands after use, and use it for the prescribed course. For external use only; avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes.

Common side effects
Mild burning, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation or an allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to eberconazole or similar antifungal medicines. Avoid applying to the eyes, mouth, broken skin or inside the vagina unless specifically prescribed. Keep the affected area clean and dry, and do not share towels or clothing. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve with treatment.

What is it used for?
Saccharomyces boulardii is a probiotic used to help manage diarrhoea, including diarrhoea associated with antibiotic use. It may also help restore the balance of helpful microorganisms in the intestine.

How does it work?
It is a beneficial yeast that helps support the normal balance of microorganisms in the gut and may reduce the effects of some harmful organisms that contribute to diarrhoea.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow with water; avoid mixing it with very hot liquids. Do not use it as a substitute for oral rehydration during diarrhoea.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort, or constipation may occur.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if immunocompromised, seriously ill, or fitted with a central venous catheter, as rare serious fungal infections have been reported. Avoid use if allergic to Saccharomyces boulardii or other yeasts. Seek medical care for severe diarrhoea, blood in the stool, high fever, signs of dehydration, or diarrhoea that does not improve.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cough and related cold or allergy symptoms. It may help loosen mucus, soothe throat irritation and reduce allergy-related symptoms.

How does it work?
Diphenhydramine helps reduce allergy symptoms and can suppress coughing. Ammonium chloride and sodium citrate help loosen mucus, while menthol provides a cooling, soothing effect in the throat.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Measure liquid doses carefully if supplied as a syrup. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea or stomach upset may occur.

Precautions
Diphenhydramine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol after taking it. Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use in young children, older adults, pregnancy, breastfeeding, glaucoma, breathing problems or difficulty passing urine. Avoid combining it with other medicines that cause sleepiness unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat scabies, an itchy skin infestation caused by mites. It may also be used for certain lice infestations when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Gamma benzene hexachloride (lindane) kills mites and lice. Cetrimide is an antiseptic that helps reduce germs on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist, and do not use more often or for longer than advised. Avoid the eyes, mouth, inside of the nose and other sensitive areas. Wash hands after applying, unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Skin irritation, burning, redness, dryness or increased itching may occur. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, dizziness, unusual drowsiness, muscle twitching or seizures occur.

Precautions
Do not use on broken, inflamed or extensively irritated skin unless advised by a doctor. Use only under medical advice in children, older adults, pregnancy, breastfeeding or people with a history of seizures. Avoid repeated or excessive use, as lindane can be toxic. Keep away from children and do not swallow.

What is it used for?
Used to support healthy gut bacteria and overall digestive health. It may also help maintain gut balance when it has been disturbed, such as after antibiotic use.

How does it work?
Probiotics provide beneficial live microorganisms, while prebiotics provide nourishment for helpful bacteria already present in the gut. Together, they support a balanced gut environment.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Follow any storage instructions on the pack, as some products may require refrigeration.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort, constipation or loose stools may occur, usually temporarily.

Precautions
Ask a doctor before use if seriously ill, immunocompromised, or if the product is intended for a premature or seriously ill infant. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe or persistent symptoms occur.

What is it used for?
Prebiotics and probiotics are used to support the balance of beneficial bacteria in the gut and promote digestive health. They may also help support gut health during or after antibiotic treatment, depending on the specific product and probiotic strain.

How does it work?
Probiotics provide live beneficial microorganisms, while prebiotics are fibres that help nourish these microorganisms in the gut.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If taking antibiotics, ask a pharmacist whether the product should be taken at a different time.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort, constipation or loose stools may occur, especially when starting treatment.

Precautions
Ask a doctor before use if there is a weakened immune system, serious illness or a severe underlying medical condition. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe or persistent symptoms occur. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to provide zinc and support healthy gut function with prebiotics and probiotics.

How does it work?
Zinc supports normal immune function and other essential body processes. Probiotics add beneficial microorganisms to the gut, while prebiotics help support their growth.

How to take/use it
Prepare and take the dry suspension exactly as directed on the product label or by the healthcare professional. Do not guess the dose or duration. Use the supplied measuring device if provided.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, stomach discomfort, vomiting, gas or bloating. Zinc may cause an unpleasant or metallic taste, especially at higher amounts.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Avoid taking more than the recommended amount, as excess zinc can be harmful. If taking antibiotics or other regular medicines, ask a doctor or pharmacist about possible interactions. People with severely weakened immunity should seek medical advice before using probiotic products.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, headache, toothache, muscle pain and pain associated with colds.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever. Ibuprofen reduces pain, fever and inflammation by blocking the production of substances involved in these symptoms.

How to take/use it
Use only the dose and schedule directed on the product label or by a doctor, based on age and weight. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or ibuprofen unless advised by a healthcare professional. Use the measuring device supplied with the product if it is a liquid.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ibuprofen, paracetamol, aspirin or other anti-inflammatory medicines. Seek medical advice before use in children with dehydration, asthma triggered by painkillers, stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver problems. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially the later months, unless prescribed. Stop use and seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, vomiting blood or black stools.

What is it used for?
Used for the short-term relief of mild to moderate pain and reduction of fever.

How does it work?
Ibuprofen reduces the production of substances that cause pain, swelling and fever. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or ibuprofen unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to ibuprofen, paracetamol, aspirin or other similar medicines. Seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, heart disease, dehydration, or use of blood thinners. Ibuprofen should generally be avoided during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Stop use and seek help for signs of stomach bleeding, severe allergic reaction or a serious skin rash.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of mild to moderate pain, such as headache, toothache, muscle or body pain, menstrual pain, and pain associated with inflammation. It can also help reduce fever.

How does it work?
Ibuprofen reduces the production of substances that cause pain, swelling and fever. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and reduce fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the package or by a doctor. Take with or after food and swallow with water if it causes stomach upset. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol, ibuprofen or other NSAIDs.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, heartburn, dizziness or headache. Skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid or seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart problems, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to ibuprofen, paracetamol or other NSAIDs. Avoid excessive alcohol. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months, or if taking blood thinners or other regular medicines. Stop and seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, breathing difficulty or a serious skin rash.

What is it used for?
This supplement provides calcium, phosphorus, zinc and vitamin D3 to support healthy bones and teeth and help prevent or correct nutritional deficiencies. It may be used when dietary intake is inadequate or when supplementation is recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Calcium and phosphorus are important minerals for bones and teeth. Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium and phosphorus, while zinc supports normal growth, tissue repair and immune function.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Tell a doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines and supplements being taken.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, constipation or diarrhoea may occur. Excessive use can cause high calcium levels, which may lead to marked thirst, frequent urination, weakness or vomiting.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels or other mineral-balance problems. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, so ask a pharmacist about suitable spacing from other medicines. Avoid taking additional calcium or vitamin D supplements unless advised.

What is it used for?
Provides calcium, magnesium, vitamin D3 and zinc to supplement dietary intake. Calcium and vitamin D support normal bone health.

How does it work?
These nutrients support normal bone mineralisation and several normal body functions.

How to take/use it
Use as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
May cause stomach discomfort or constipation in some people.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, or use of other mineral supplements or medicines.

What is it used for?
Used to supplement calcium and vitamin D when dietary intake is insufficient, and to support healthy bones and teeth.

How does it work?
Calcium provides the mineral needed for bones, teeth and normal muscle and nerve function. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Calcium carbonate is usually best taken with food. Do not take more than recommended or combine with other calcium or vitamin D supplements unless advised.

Common side effects
Constipation, gas, bloating, nausea or stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, or high calcium levels. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, including iron supplements, thyroid medicines and certain antibiotics; these may need to be taken at different times as advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
This supplement provides calcium, vitamin D3, magnesium and zinc to help meet nutritional needs and support healthy bones and teeth. It may be used to help prevent or correct calcium and vitamin D deficiency, as advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Calcium and vitamin D3 support bone and tooth strength; vitamin D3 also helps the body absorb calcium. Magnesium and zinc support normal muscle, nerve and bone function.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional, with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount. If stomach upset occurs, taking it with food may help.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach upset, abdominal discomfort, bloating or diarrhoea may occur. Excessive use may increase the risk of high calcium levels or kidney stones.

Constipation, stomach discomfort, bloating, nausea, or vomiting may occur. Excess calcium may cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness, or confusion.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high blood calcium, or other calcium or vitamin D supplements are being used. Vitamin K2 may interact with warfarin and similar blood thinners. Seek medical advice if symptoms of excess calcium occur, and keep the medicine out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or correct vitamin and mineral deficiencies and support nutritional health when dietary intake is inadequate. The zinc in it also supports normal immune function and wound healing.

How does it work?
It supplies essential vitamins and minerals needed for normal body functions. Zinc contributes to immune function, growth and tissue repair.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, constipation or diarrhoea, and an unpleasant or metallic taste may occur.

Precautions
Check the ingredients if there is an allergy to any vitamin, mineral or other component. Avoid taking it with other multivitamin or zinc-containing products unless advised by a healthcare professional. Inform a doctor or pharmacist about other medicines being taken, as minerals may affect the absorption of some medicines. Seek advice before use in pregnancy, breastfeeding, or kidney or liver disease.

What is it used for?
This is a nutritional supplement that provides vitamins, minerals, omega-3 fatty acids, lycopene, methylcobalamin, vitamin D3 and coenzyme Q10. It is used to help meet nutritional requirements and support general health when dietary intake is inadequate.

How does it work?
Its vitamins and minerals support normal body functions such as energy production, nerve function and bone health. Omega-3 fatty acids, lycopene and coenzyme Q10 have antioxidant or nutritional roles in the body.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset.

Common side effects
Some people may experience nausea, stomach upset, loose stools or a fishy aftertaste. Stop use and seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction.

Precautions
Inform a healthcare professional before use if taking blood thinners or other regular medicines, or if there is a bleeding disorder, fish or seafood allergy, kidney disease or high calcium levels. Avoid taking additional vitamin or mineral supplements without advice, particularly those containing vitamin D. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary supplement to provide vitamins, minerals, lycopene and other antioxidants when dietary intake may be insufficient. It is not intended to treat a specific disease unless advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
The vitamins and minerals support normal body functions, while lycopene and other antioxidants help protect cells from oxidative stress.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount or combine it with other multivitamin supplements unless advised.

Common side effects
May cause stomach discomfort, nausea, constipation or diarrhoea in some people.

Precautions
Check the ingredients for allergies. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, in children, or if there is a medical condition or regular medicine use. Avoid taking more than the recommended amount, as excessive intake of some vitamins and minerals can be harmful.

What is it used for?
Used to supplement the diet and help prevent or correct vitamin and mineral deficiencies, including inadequate zinc intake, when dietary intake is insufficient or a deficiency has been identified.

How does it work?
It provides essential vitamins and minerals needed for normal energy production, growth, immunity and other body functions.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device, and do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid taking other multivitamin or mineral products unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, constipation or diarrhoea may occur. A metallic taste may occur because of zinc.

Precautions
Check the ingredients if there is an allergy to any vitamin, mineral or other ingredient. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or with kidney or liver disease. Keep out of reach of children; accidental overdose of some vitamins or minerals can be serious.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary supplement to provide essential vitamins, minerals and antioxidant nutrients, with ginseng, for general nutritional support and wellness.

How does it work?
The vitamins and minerals support normal body functions, while antioxidant nutrients help protect cells from oxidative damage. Ginseng is an herbal ingredient traditionally used as a general tonic.

How to take/use it
Swallow the softgel with water and take it only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount or take it along with other multivitamin products unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or headache. Ginseng may cause difficulty sleeping in some people. Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is diabetes, a bleeding disorder, or liver or kidney disease. Ask about possible interactions if taking blood thinners, diabetes medicines or other regular medicines. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Aceclofenac 100 mg + paracetamol 325 mg is used to relieve pain and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor, preferably with or after food, and swallow with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid excessive alcohol. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin reactions, breathing difficulty or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Use during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, only if specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Used for the short-term relief of pain and reduction of fever.

How does it work?
Mefenamic acid reduces the production of substances that cause pain, swelling and fever. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Take with or after food to reduce stomach discomfort. Do not take more than the recommended amount, or combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol or mefenamic acid unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to mefenamic acid, paracetamol, aspirin or other painkillers. Seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, heart problems, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid alcohol, and seek urgent help for severe stomach pain, vomiting blood, black stools, breathing difficulty, swelling or a serious skin reaction.

What is it used for?
This skin medicine is used for short-term treatment of inflamed, itchy and thickened or scaly skin conditions, such as psoriasis and some forms of eczema or dermatitis, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Clobetasol reduces skin inflammation, redness and itching. Salicylic acid softens and removes thick, scaly skin, helping the medicine reach the affected area.

How to take/use it
Use only on the skin and apply as directed by the doctor. Apply a thin layer to the affected area and wash hands after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not use more often, for longer, or over larger areas than advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, irritation, dryness or peeling may occur. Prolonged or excessive use can cause thinning of the skin, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not apply to broken, infected or acne-prone skin unless advised by a doctor. Avoid covering the treated area with airtight dressings unless specifically instructed. Do not use on the face, groin or skin folds without medical advice. Seek medical advice if the condition worsens or does not improve. Children, pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should use it only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
This digestive enzyme combination is used to help digest food and relieve indigestion, heaviness or fullness after meals, and bloating related to poor digestion.

How does it work?
Diastase helps break down starches, while pepsin helps digest proteins. Together, they support the normal digestion of food.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Mild nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating, loose stools or constipation may occur. Allergic reactions are uncommon.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to diastase, pepsin or any ingredient in the product. Seek medical advice for persistent or recurrent indigestion, severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, blood in the stool or unexplained weight loss. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This digestive enzyme combination is used to support the digestion of carbohydrates and proteins and may help relieve indigestion or digestive discomfort when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Alpha-amylase helps break down carbohydrates, while pepsin helps break down proteins during digestion.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Stomach discomfort, nausea, or changes in bowel movements may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, persistent, or associated with repeated vomiting, severe abdominal pain, or blood in the stool. Stop use and seek urgent help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
Propranolol is used to lower high blood pressure and manage certain heart-related problems, such as a fast or irregular heartbeat and angina. It may also be prescribed for migraine prevention, tremors, or physical symptoms of anxiety, depending on the doctor's advice.

How does it work?
It is a beta-blocker that slows the heartbeat and reduces the force with which the heart pumps. This helps lower blood pressure and reduces the heart's workload.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow it with water. Take it consistently at the same time each day. Do not stop it suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Tiredness, dizziness, light-headedness, slow heartbeat, cold hands or feet, sleep disturbances, or nausea.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma or wheezing, a very slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart failure, circulation problems, diabetes, or liver or kidney disease. Propranolol can hide some warning signs of low blood sugar. Seek medical advice for breathing difficulty, fainting, or an unusually slow heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Propranolol is a beta-blocker used for high blood pressure, certain heart rhythm problems and other heart-related conditions. It may also be prescribed to prevent migraine attacks, control physical symptoms of anxiety, or reduce tremors, depending on medical advice.

How does it work?
It slows the heart rate and reduces the force with which the heart pumps. This lowers the workload on the heart and can reduce some physical symptoms such as a fast heartbeat and tremor.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Take doses at the same time each day and follow the instructions on the prescription or package. Do not stop treatment suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Tiredness, dizziness, cold hands or feet, slow heartbeat, sleep disturbances and nausea may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor before use if there is asthma or wheezing, a very slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart failure, diabetes or circulation problems. Propranolol can mask some warning signs of low blood sugar. Avoid stopping it suddenly, and seek medical advice if breathing difficulty, fainting or an unusually slow heartbeat occurs.

What is it used for?
Bimatoprost and timolol eye drops are used to lower raised pressure inside the eye in open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension. Lowering eye pressure helps protect the optic nerve and reduce the risk of vision loss.

How does it work?
Timolol reduces the production of fluid inside the eye. Bimatoprost increases the drainage of this fluid, helping lower eye pressure.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the ophthalmologist. Wash hands, avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or other surfaces, and close the eye gently after applying the drop. Remove contact lenses before use and reinsert them only as directed. If using other eye drops, separate them as advised by the doctor. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Eye redness, irritation, itching, dryness, watering, temporary blurred vision, headache, and increased eyelash growth. Darkening of the skin around the eye or the iris may occur with bimatoprost.

Precautions
Tell the doctor before use if there is asthma or other breathing disease, a slow heartbeat, heart block, heart failure, low blood pressure, diabetes, or other eye disease. Timolol may rarely affect breathing or heart rate and may mask some signs of low blood sugar. Inform the doctor about all medicines and other eye drops being used. Avoid driving until blurred vision clears. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, fainting, severe dizziness, or a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve symptoms of osteoarthritis, such as joint pain, stiffness and difficulty moving, especially in the knees and other joints.

How does it work?
Diacerein helps reduce inflammation-related activity in osteoarthritis. Glucosamine and MSM may support joint cartilage and help relieve joint discomfort.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow with water and follow the prescribed instructions. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, loose stools, stomach pain, nausea, indigestion, headache and yellow or reddish-brown urine may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about liver or kidney disease, inflammatory bowel problems, persistent diarrhoea, diabetes, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if severe or prolonged diarrhoea occurs. Tell the doctor if taking warfarin or other regular medicines, and report any signs of allergy.

What is it used for?
Allopurinol is used to lower high uric acid levels and prevent gout attacks, including the formation of uric acid kidney stones in some patients. It helps prevent future attacks but does not provide quick relief from pain during an acute gout attack.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called xanthine oxidase, reducing the body’s production of uric acid.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, regularly, and preferably after food with plenty of water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. It may take time to reduce gout attacks, and attacks can sometimes occur when treatment is first started.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Stop taking it and seek urgent medical help if a rash, blistering, peeling skin, mouth sores, facial swelling or breathing difficulty develops. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, and provide a complete list of medicines, especially azathioprine or mercaptopurine. Do not start, stop or change treatment without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Allopurinol is used to lower high uric acid levels and prevent gout attacks. It may also be prescribed to prevent uric acid kidney stones or uric acid build-up during some cancer treatments.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme involved in making uric acid. This lowers uric acid levels in the blood and urine over time.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually regularly even when feeling well. Swallow with plenty of water, preferably after food, and do not stop it without medical advice. It does not provide immediate relief during a gout attack.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach upset, and headache may occur. A skin rash can occur and should be reported promptly.

Precautions
Stop taking it and seek urgent medical help if a rash, blistering, peeling skin, mouth sores, facial swelling, or breathing difficulty develops. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines, especially azathioprine, mercaptopurine, or certain blood thinners. Drink adequate fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for temporary relief of a blocked or runny nose, sneezing and other nasal symptoms caused by the common cold or allergies.

How does it work?
Phenylephrine helps reduce swelling in the nasal passages and relieve congestion. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that reduces sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not take it with other cold, allergy or decongestant medicines containing similar ingredients. Avoid alcohol and do not drive if it causes drowsiness.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, nervousness, headache, nausea or palpitations may occur.

Precautions
Use medical advice if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, prostate or urinary problems, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek advice before giving it to children. Stop use and seek medical help for severe palpitations, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This combination is used in oral care products to help relieve tooth sensitivity and support protection against tooth decay and plaque buildup.

How does it work?
Potassium nitrate helps reduce the sensitivity of nerves in the teeth. Sodium monofluorophosphate strengthens tooth enamel and helps prevent cavities, while triclosan helps reduce plaque-forming bacteria.

How to take/use it
Use it for brushing only, following the directions on the product label or as advised by a dentist. Spit out after brushing and do not swallow. Do not use more often than directed.

Common side effects
Some people may experience mild mouth irritation, burning, or changes in taste. Stop using it if significant irritation or an allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
Do not swallow. Keep out of reach of young children. Avoid use if allergic to any ingredient. Consult a dentist if tooth sensitivity continues, worsens, or is associated with pain, swelling, or a damaged tooth.

What is it used for?
Enalapril is mainly used to treat high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed to help manage heart failure.

How does it work?
It is an ACE inhibitor that relaxes and widens blood vessels. This lowers blood pressure and reduces the workload on the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Do not stop taking it or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea and a dry, persistent cough may occur. Dizziness may be more noticeable when starting treatment or increasing the dose.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, high potassium levels, dehydration, or a previous serious swelling or allergic reaction to an ACE inhibitor. Enalapril should not be used during pregnancy and may harm the unborn baby. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Enalapril is mainly used to treat high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed for heart failure and certain heart-related conditions.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of a substance that narrows blood vessels. This helps the blood vessels relax, lowering blood pressure and reducing the workload on the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber’s instructions rather than taking an extra dose.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea and a dry, persistent cough may occur. Dizziness can be more noticeable when starting treatment or when standing up.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, dehydration, low blood pressure, high potassium levels or previous swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat with similar medicines. Regular blood pressure, kidney function and potassium monitoring may be needed. Seek urgent help for swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing, fainting or severe dizziness.

What is it used for?
This is a nutritional supplement containing vitamin E, wheat germ oil and omega-3 fatty acids. It is used to help supplement the diet when intake of these nutrients is inadequate. It is not a substitute for a balanced diet or prescribed treatment.

How does it work?
Vitamin E provides antioxidant activity, while omega-3 fatty acids provide essential dietary fats. Wheat germ oil is a natural source of vitamin E and other fats.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow the capsule with water, preferably with food. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, nausea, loose stools, or fishy-tasting burps may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if signs of an allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional before use if taking blood thinners or antiplatelet medicines, if there is a bleeding disorder, or before surgery, as high doses may increase bleeding risk. Avoid use if allergic to any ingredient, including fish or wheat-derived ingredients where applicable. Ask a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or when giving it to children.

What is it used for?
This product is used as a vitamin E supplement when additional vitamin E is needed. It is not intended to treat a specific disease unless advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, helping protect body cells from oxidative damage. The effects of aloe vera depend on how the product is formulated and used.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Check the product instructions to confirm whether it is meant to be taken by mouth or applied to the skin.

Common side effects
Possible side effects may include stomach upset, nausea or diarrhoea when taken by mouth, or skin irritation when applied to the skin.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to vitamin E, aloe vera or any ingredient. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, if taking blood-thinning medicines, or if a bleeding disorder or other medical condition is present. Stop use and seek advice if significant irritation or other unusual symptoms occur.

What is it used for?
This medicine is a nutritional supplement containing vitamin E and L-carnitine. It is used to provide antioxidant support and support normal energy production in the body.

How does it work?
Vitamin E helps protect cells from damage caused by free radicals. L-carnitine helps transport fatty acids into cells for energy production.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Take with food if it causes stomach discomfort.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, abdominal cramps, or a fish-like body odour may occur.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use if taking blood thinners, having a bleeding disorder, or before surgery. People with a seizure disorder, kidney disease, or those who are pregnant or breastfeeding should seek medical advice before taking it. Stop use and seek medical help for unusual bleeding or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This supplement provides vitamin E, lycopene and vitamin C to help meet nutritional needs and provide antioxidant nutrients. It is not intended to treat a specific disease unless advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Vitamin E, lycopene and vitamin C act as antioxidants, helping protect cells from oxidative damage.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Taking it with food may improve tolerance and absorption.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Some people may experience nausea, stomach upset or loose stools.

Precautions
Use cautiously if taking blood thinners or antiplatelet medicines, or if there is a bleeding disorder, because high-dose vitamin E may increase bleeding risk. Inform a healthcare professional before surgery. Seek medical advice during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or if there is an existing medical condition. Stop use and seek advice if an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
This combination is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes.

How does it work?
Empagliflozin helps the kidneys remove excess glucose through urine. Linagliptin helps the body release more insulin after meals and reduces the release of glucose from the liver.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole and maintain adequate fluid intake unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not change or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, genital yeast infections, urinary tract infections, thirst, dehydration, dizziness, and symptoms of low blood sugar—especially when used with insulin or sulfonylureas. Nasal congestion or a cough may also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, low blood pressure, frequent infections, pancreatitis, or heart problems. Seek urgent medical help for nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, or difficulty breathing, as these may indicate diabetic ketoacidosis even if blood sugar is not very high. Report severe genital infection, allergic reactions, or persistent severe abdominal pain. Extra medical advice may be needed during serious illness, prolonged fasting, dehydration, or before surgery. Discuss use during pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor.

What is it used for?
Empagliflozin + linagliptin is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Empagliflozin helps the kidneys remove excess glucose through urine. Linagliptin increases the effect of natural hormones that help the body release insulin after meals and reduce glucose production.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Maintain adequate fluid intake unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction.

Common side effects
Increased urination, thirst, urinary tract infections, genital fungal infections, and low blood sugar—especially when used with insulin or sulfonylurea medicines. Nausea or stomach discomfort may also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, frequent urinary or genital infections, dehydration, or a history of pancreatitis. Seek urgent medical help for severe nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, breathing difficulty, or confusion, as these may indicate ketoacidosis. Report severe genital pain or swelling, allergic reactions, or persistent severe abdominal pain. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Empagliflozin is mainly used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It may also be prescribed to reduce the risk of worsening heart failure or kidney disease in some adults.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove excess glucose from the blood through the urine. This lowers blood sugar and can also reduce excess fluid in the body.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Drink enough fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not stop or change the medicine without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, thirst, dehydration, dizziness, urinary tract infection, and genital fungal infection. Low blood sugar may occur, especially when used with insulin or some other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, low blood pressure, dehydration, or recurrent urinary or genital infections. Seek urgent medical help for severe nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, or fast breathing, as these may indicate diabetic ketoacidosis even if blood sugar is not very high. The medicine may need to be stopped temporarily during serious illness, prolonged fasting, or before surgery, only as advised by a doctor. Discuss its use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Empagliflozin helps the kidneys remove excess sugar through urine. Metformin reduces sugar production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, preferably with food. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole; do not crush, split or chew it. Maintain adequate fluid intake unless a doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, increased urination, thirst, urinary tract infections and genital fungal infections. Low blood sugar may occur, especially when used with insulin or sulfonylureas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, recurrent urinary or genital infections, heart failure, or heavy alcohol use. Seek urgent medical help for severe weakness, vomiting, stomach pain, breathing difficulty, confusion, or unusual drowsiness, as these may indicate lactic acidosis or ketoacidosis. The medicine may need to be stopped temporarily during prolonged fasting, severe illness, dehydration or around surgery, only on medical advice. Kidney function should be checked regularly.

What is it used for?
Empagliflozin + metformin is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes.

How does it work?
Metformin reduces the amount of glucose made by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin. Empagliflozin helps the kidneys remove extra glucose from the body through urine.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole; do not crush, chew or split it. Drink enough fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, increased urination, thirst, genital fungal infections and urinary tract infections may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, recurrent urinary or genital infections, heart failure, or a planned surgery or procedure. Seek urgent medical help for severe weakness, vomiting, stomach pain, difficulty breathing, confusion, or very little urine. This medicine may need to be stopped temporarily during serious illness, prolonged fasting or before some procedures. Avoid excessive alcohol and tell the doctor before receiving contrast dye. Seek medical advice if pregnant or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Empagliflozin helps the kidneys remove excess glucose through urine. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with food to reduce stomach upset. Take it at the same time each day and do not stop it without medical advice. Maintain adequate fluid intake unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, reduced appetite, increased urination, urinary tract infections and genital fungal infections. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Kidney function should be checked before and during treatment.
