Contact a doctor for signs of dehydration, urinary infection or genital infection. Tell the doctor before surgery, prolonged fasting, severe illness, or if pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid excessive alcohol and follow the prescribed diabetes monitoring plan.

What is it used for?
Bacillus clausii spore suspension is a probiotic used to help restore the natural balance of healthy bacteria in the intestine, especially during or after diarrhoea or antibiotic treatment.

How does it work?
It provides beneficial bacterial spores that can help support the normal balance of microorganisms in the gut.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Complete medical advice is needed to determine the appropriate dose and duration.

Common side effects
Mild stomach discomfort, gas, bloating or nausea may occur. Allergic reactions are rare.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to Bacillus clausii or any ingredient. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, high fever or signs of dehydration. People with severely weakened immunity or those with a central venous catheter should use it only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Pheniramine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, itching, watery eyes and skin hives.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance released during allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than recommended. Avoid using other medicines that cause drowsiness unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation and difficulty passing urine.

Precautions
It may cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol until its effects are known. Seek medical advice before use if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, prostate problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Older adults and children may be more sensitive to its effects.

What is it used for?
Eplerenone is used to treat high blood pressure and certain types of heart failure, including heart failure after a heart attack. It may help reduce strain on the heart and lower the risk of further heart-related problems.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of aldosterone, a hormone that makes the body retain salt and water. This helps reduce fluid and pressure on the heart and blood vessels, but can increase potassium levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular blood tests may be needed to check potassium levels and kidney function.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, diarrhoea, low blood pressure, increased potassium levels and changes in kidney function.

Precautions
Do not use potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, high potassium levels, or if taking blood-pressure medicines, diuretics or medicines that interact with eplerenone. Seek medical advice for muscle weakness, an irregular heartbeat or severe dizziness. Potassium and kidney function should be monitored during treatment.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to reduce excess fluid retention (swelling or oedema), especially in people with heart failure. By removing extra salt and water, it can help reduce the workload on the heart and improve symptoms such as swelling and breathlessness.

How does it work?
Torsemide helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water through urine. Eplerenone blocks the effect of aldosterone, a hormone that can cause salt and water retention, while helping protect the heart in certain heart conditions.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. It may increase urination, so follow the timing advised by the doctor. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular blood tests may be needed.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, headache, dehydration, low blood pressure, changes in blood potassium or sodium levels, and changes in kidney function.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Potassium and kidney function should be monitored, as eplerenone can cause dangerously high potassium levels and torsemide can cause dehydration or electrolyte changes. Avoid potassium supplements and potassium-containing salt substitutes unless specifically advised. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, low blood pressure, dehydration, or all other medicines being taken. Seek medical help for severe weakness, fainting, irregular heartbeat, or very little urine.

What is it used for?
Phenytoin is mainly used to prevent and control certain types of seizures (epilepsy). It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain.

How does it work?
It reduces the spread of excessive electrical signals in the brain by blocking certain sodium channels in nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, as this may trigger seizures. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber's instructions and do not take an extra dose unless advised. Regular blood tests may be needed to check the medicine level and monitor safety.

Common side effects
Dizziness, drowsiness, unsteadiness, nausea, vomiting, headache, blurred vision and gum swelling or overgrowth may occur.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical advice for a skin rash, blistering, peeling skin, facial swelling, breathing difficulty, unusual bruising, severe tiredness or yellowing of the eyes or skin. Phenytoin has many medicine interactions; inform the doctor about all medicines, including contraceptive pills and supplements. Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, pregnancy or plans for pregnancy. Maintain good oral hygiene and attend recommended check-ups and blood tests. Avoid stopping it suddenly or taking alcohol unless the doctor advises it is safe.

What is it used for?
Escitalopram is used to treat depression and anxiety disorders, including generalised anxiety disorder, panic disorder, social anxiety and obsessive-compulsive disorder, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI). It increases the availability of serotonin, a chemical messenger that helps regulate mood and anxiety.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop treatment suddenly; the dose should usually be reduced gradually under medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, dry mouth, sweating, trouble sleeping, sleepiness, dizziness and sexual problems may occur. These effects may improve as the body adjusts.

Precautions
Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs), and inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially other antidepressants or medicines affecting serotonin. Seek medical help for worsening depression, suicidal thoughts, severe agitation, confusion, fever, muscle stiffness or unusual bleeding. Tell the doctor if there is a history of bipolar disorder, seizures, liver problems or glaucoma. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, and avoid stopping it suddenly.

What is it used for?
Escitalopram is an antidepressant used mainly to treat depression and anxiety disorders, including generalised anxiety, panic disorder and social anxiety. It may also be prescribed for obsessive-compulsive disorder.

How does it work?
It increases the availability of serotonin, a chemical messenger in the brain that helps regulate mood and anxiety. Its benefits may take several weeks to become noticeable.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day, with or without food. Do not stop taking it suddenly; the dose should be reduced gradually only under medical supervision.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, dry mouth, increased sweating, sleepiness or difficulty sleeping, dizziness and sexual problems may occur. These effects may improve as the body adjusts.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about bipolar disorder, seizures, liver or kidney problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or any history of suicidal thoughts. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs), and inform the doctor about all other medicines, especially those affecting serotonin or increasing bleeding risk. Seek urgent medical help for severe agitation, confusion, fever, muscle stiffness, unusual bleeding, a severe allergic reaction or worsening suicidal thoughts. Do not stop suddenly, and avoid alcohol if it increases drowsiness.

What is it used for?
Esomeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), and acid-related stomach or intestinal ulcers. It may also be used with antibiotics for certain stomach infections when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It is a proton pump inhibitor that blocks the release of acid in the stomach. This helps relieve heartburn and allows acid-damaged tissues to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is commonly taken before food, as directed by the doctor.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation, and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially clopidogrel, warfarin, digoxin, phenytoin, or methotrexate. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss, or persistent symptoms. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Esomeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid. It helps treat acidity, heartburn and acid reflux, and may also be used for acid-related stomach ulcers as prescribed.

How does it work?
It is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that blocks the final step of acid production in the stomach, reducing irritation and allowing acid-related problems to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably before food. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if long-term treatment is planned. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or persistent symptoms. Esomeprazole can interact with some medicines, including certain blood thinners and medicines used to treat HIV; provide a complete list of medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux (GERD). The domperidone component may also help with nausea, vomiting and uncomfortable fullness associated with upper digestive problems.

How does it work?
Esomeprazole reduces the production of acid in the stomach. Domperidone helps improve movement of the upper digestive tract and may reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the instructions on the label and do not take more or use it for longer than advised. Do not stop regular treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, abdominal pain, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation and dry mouth may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of heart rhythm problems, fainting, heart disease, liver disease, stomach or intestinal bleeding, or electrolyte imbalance. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or interact with domperidone or esomeprazole. Seek medical help for fast or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting. Consult a doctor during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux, including reflux-related indigestion, bloating or stomach discomfort.

How does it work?
Esomeprazole reduces the production of stomach acid. Itopride helps improve stomach movement and emptying, which may reduce fullness, bloating and indigestion.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed timing in relation to meals.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to any of its ingredients. Tell the doctor about other medicines, especially clopidogrel or blood thinners. Seek medical advice for black stools, vomiting blood, difficulty swallowing, persistent vomiting or unexplained weight loss. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or for prolonged treatment.

What is it used for?
Used to treat acidity, acid reflux and heartburn, especially when these symptoms are associated with indigestion, nausea or slow stomach emptying.

How does it work?
Esomeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Levosulpride helps improve movement of the upper digestive tract and supports stomach emptying.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the sustained-release capsule/tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed timing in relation to meals.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, dizziness or drowsiness. Levosulpride may rarely cause restlessness, tremors or breast-related hormonal changes.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, heart rhythm problems, seizure disorders, movement disorders, intestinal blockage or gastrointestinal bleeding. Inform the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding, or if taking medicines that affect heart rhythm, brain function or hormone levels. Seek medical advice for persistent vomiting, black stools, vomiting blood, difficulty swallowing or unexplained weight loss.

What is it used for?
Hydroxyzine is mainly used to relieve itching and other symptoms caused by allergies. It may also be prescribed for short-term anxiety or to cause drowsiness before a medical procedure.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions, helping reduce itching and allergy symptoms. It can also have a calming and sedating effect.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Measure the liquid with an oral syringe or the supplied measuring device, not a household spoon. Shake the bottle well before use. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, headache and constipation may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and activities requiring alertness, such as driving, until its effects are known. Tell the doctor about glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, breathing problems, heart rhythm problems, liver or kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe drowsiness, fainting, palpitations or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Hydroxyzine is mainly used to relieve itching and other symptoms caused by allergies, including hives. In some cases, a doctor may prescribe it for short-term anxiety or to cause drowsiness before a procedure.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions, helping reduce itching and allergy symptoms. It can also have a sedating effect, which may cause drowsiness.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Measure the liquid with an oral syringe or measuring spoon, not a household spoon. Do not take more than prescribed. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation and headache.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor before using other medicines that cause drowsiness. Use only with medical advice if there is a history of heart rhythm problems, glaucoma, difficulty urinating, breathing problems, or in older adults. Tell the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, severe palpitations or a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Hydroxyzine is an antihistamine used to relieve itching and other symptoms caused by allergies or allergic skin conditions. It may also be prescribed for short-term anxiety or to help cause drowsiness before a medical procedure.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions. It can also have a calming and drowsy effect.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation and headache.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor before using it with sleeping medicines, sedatives or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice before use if there is a heart rhythm problem, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, liver or kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, breathing difficulty or severe allergic reactions.

What is it used for?
Ethamsylate is used to help reduce excessive bleeding, including heavy menstrual bleeding and bleeding from small blood vessels. It may also be used around surgery when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It helps strengthen small blood vessels and improves the sticking of platelets, which supports the formation of a blood clot and helps reduce bleeding.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the recommended dose and duration, and do not stop or change treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, headache, skin rash or other allergic reactions may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice for unexplained, very heavy or persistent bleeding, as its underlying cause needs to be assessed. Do not use it if previously allergic to ethamsylate. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, or any history of blood-clotting problems before use. Seek urgent care for signs of a severe allergic reaction or unusual clotting symptoms.

What is it used for?
Ethamsylate is used to help control certain types of bleeding, including heavy menstrual bleeding and bleeding from small blood vessels. It should be used only when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It helps improve the strength of small blood vessels and supports the formation of an initial platelet plug, which may help reduce bleeding.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, with water. Do not change the dose or duration, or use it to treat unexplained bleeding without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, headache, skin rash or other allergic reactions may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice for heavy, prolonged or unexplained bleeding, as its cause should be assessed. Do not use if allergic to ethamsylate. Inform the doctor about any history of blood-clotting problems or acute porphyria. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash.

What is it used for?
Ethamsylate injection is used by healthcare professionals to help prevent or control certain types of bleeding, including heavy menstrual bleeding and bleeding during or after surgery.

How does it work?
It helps strengthen small blood vessels and supports the formation of an initial platelet plug, which can reduce capillary bleeding.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection into a vein or muscle by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the cause and severity of bleeding. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, skin rash or itching, and low blood pressure if injected too quickly may occur.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about any allergy to ethamsylate or previous reactions to injections. The cause of unusual or heavy bleeding should be assessed by a doctor. Seek urgent medical care for severe, persistent or unexplained bleeding. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Etodolac is used to relieve pain and reduce inflammation, especially in osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and other muscle or joint conditions.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. Taking it with or after food and a full glass of water may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more than prescribed or combine it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and heartburn.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to NSAIDs. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin rash. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed, particularly from 20 weeks onwards and during the last trimester. Older adults and people taking blood thinners, steroids or other medicines that increase bleeding risk should use it only under medical advice.

What is it used for?
Etoricoxib is used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness caused by arthritis and other painful joint or muscle conditions. It may also be prescribed for certain short-term painful conditions, as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation. It selectively blocks an enzyme called COX-2.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet whole with water, with or without food. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, swelling of the legs or feet, and increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about high blood pressure, heart disease, previous stroke, stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, or an allergy to painkillers. It may increase the risk of heart attack or stroke, especially with higher doses or prolonged use. Avoid taking it with other anti-inflammatory painkillers unless advised. Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed, and seek medical advice if severe skin rash, breathing difficulty, chest pain, black stools or marked swelling occurs.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain and inflammation, especially pain related to joints, muscles and other musculoskeletal conditions.

How does it work?
Etoricoxib reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor, with or without food. Do not take additional paracetamol-containing medicines or other anti-inflammatory painkillers unless advised by a doctor. Do not exceed the prescribed amount.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach discomfort, nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, swelling of the feet or legs, and increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about heart disease, previous heart attack or stroke, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, kidney or liver problems, or asthma triggered by painkillers. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised. Avoid excessive alcohol and check with a doctor before use with blood thinners, blood-pressure medicines or other painkillers. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, black stools, severe allergic reactions, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, swelling, stiffness and painful muscle spasms associated with musculoskeletal conditions, such as joint or muscle problems.

How does it work?
Etoricoxib reduces substances in the body that cause pain and inflammation. Thiocolchicoside helps relax tight or spasming muscles.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the recommended dose and treatment duration, and do not take more than prescribed. Do not continue treatment or combine it with other painkillers without medical advice.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness or drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor. Inform the doctor about high blood pressure, heart disease, previous heart attack or stroke, stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver problems, or a history of seizures. Etoricoxib may increase blood pressure and heart-related risks. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizzy or drowsy. Seek medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, black stools, severe skin rash or swelling.

What is it used for?
Carboxymethylcellulose eye drops are used to relieve dry, burning or irritated eyes by acting as artificial tears.

How does it work?
It forms a lubricating layer over the eye surface and helps retain moisture, providing temporary relief from dryness and irritation.

How to take/use it
Wash hands before use and apply the drops as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface. If wearing contact lenses, remove them before use unless the product instructions say otherwise.

Common side effects
Temporary blurred vision, mild stinging, burning or irritation may occur after application.

Precautions
Do not use if the solution is cloudy or the container is damaged. Seek medical advice if eye pain, marked redness, vision changes or persistent irritation occurs. Avoid contaminating the dropper tip and do not share the bottle.

What is it used for?
Ezetimibe 10 mg is used to lower high cholesterol, especially LDL (bad) cholesterol. It may be used alone or together with a statin when cholesterol is not adequately controlled.

How does it work?
It reduces the absorption of cholesterol from the small intestine, helping lower the amount of cholesterol in the blood.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Take it regularly and do not stop treatment without medical advice. If also taking a bile-acid binding medicine, follow the advised time gap between the medicines.

Common side effects
Headache, stomach pain, diarrhoea, tiredness, muscle pain and joint pain may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. If taking it with a statin, liver problems and muscle injury are possible; seek medical advice for severe muscle pain, weakness, dark urine, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or unusual tiredness. Regular cholesterol and liver tests may be recommended.

What is it used for?
This herbal oral-care preparation is used to support everyday oral hygiene and help freshen the breath.

How does it work?
Its aromatic oils provide a cooling, fresh taste and may help reduce unpleasant mouth odour. Glycerin helps retain moisture, while aloe may provide a soothing effect.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label. If intended as a mouth rinse, rinse and spit out; do not swallow. Follow the label for the amount and frequency of use.

Common side effects
Temporary mouth irritation, burning, taste changes or allergic reactions may occur.

Precautions
Do not swallow. Stop use if mouth irritation, swelling or rash develops. Avoid use if allergic to any ingredient. Children should use it only under adult supervision and according to the label.

What is it used for?
Papaya extract with vitamin C is a dietary supplement used to provide vitamin C and papaya-derived nutrients. The supplied information does not establish a specific disease or condition that it treats.

How does it work?
Vitamin C acts as an antioxidant and supports normal collagen formation and immune function. The effects of papaya extract depend on the specific extract and its strength.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause stomach discomfort, nausea or loose motions. Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
Check the label for the complete ingredient list. Avoid use if allergic to papaya or any ingredient. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or if taking regular medicines or managing a medical condition.

What is it used for?
Faropenem 200 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the respiratory tract, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall, helping to clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the prescribed dose and duration, swallow the tablet with water, and complete the full course even if symptoms improve. Do not share antibiotics or use leftover medicine.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur. Seek medical advice if diarrhoea is severe or persistent.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to faropenem or other beta-lactam antibiotics such as penicillins, cephalosporins or carbapenems. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Faropenem is an antibiotic used to treat susceptible bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall, helping to clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there is a known allergy to faropenem or other beta-lactam antibiotics unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, allergies, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or a serious skin rash.

What is it used for?
Febuxostat is used to lower high uric acid levels in people with gout. It helps prevent the build-up of uric acid crystals that can cause gout attacks and joint problems.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called xanthine oxidase, reducing the body's production of uric acid.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Gout attacks may occur more often when treatment is first started; continue the medicine unless the prescriber advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Gout flare-ups, nausea, joint pain, skin rash, and changes in liver function tests may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, stroke, liver disease, kidney disease, or any previous allergy to this medicine. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or a severe skin rash. Liver tests may be needed during treatment. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially azathioprine, mercaptopurine, or theophylline.

What is it used for?
Febuxostat is used for the long-term treatment of gout in adults with high uric acid levels. It lowers uric acid to help prevent gout attacks and the buildup of urate crystals. It does not provide immediate relief from pain during an acute gout attack.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called xanthine oxidase, which reduces the production of uric acid in the body.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop treatment without medical advice, even if symptoms improve. Continue any separate medicine prescribed for an acute gout attack as directed.

Common side effects
Nausea, joint pain, rash, diarrhoea, and abnormal liver function tests may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, stroke, liver or kidney problems, or a previous reaction to febuxostat. Seek urgent medical help for a severe or blistering rash, swelling of the face, difficulty breathing, chest pain, or sudden weakness. Febuxostat can interact with azathioprine, mercaptopurine, and some other medicines. Liver tests and uric acid monitoring may be needed. Discuss its use during pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor.

What is it used for?
Fenofibrate is used with a healthy diet and lifestyle changes to lower high triglyceride levels and improve abnormal cholesterol levels in the blood.

How does it work?
It helps the body break down and remove triglycerides and other fats from the blood, helping improve the balance of blood lipids.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions on the product label. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Continue the recommended diet and exercise plan.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, and increased liver enzyme levels may occur. Muscle pain or weakness can also occur and should not be ignored.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, gallbladder problems, or a history of muscle disorders. Seek medical advice promptly for unexplained muscle pain or weakness, severe stomach pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or dark urine. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially statins or blood thinners. It is generally avoided during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Fenofibrate is used with diet and lifestyle changes to treat high levels of triglycerides and cholesterol in the blood, helping reduce the risk of complications from abnormal blood fats.

How does it work?
It helps the liver process and remove certain fats from the blood. It mainly lowers triglycerides and may increase protective HDL cholesterol.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the prolonged-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Continue the recommended diet and exercise plan, and attend blood tests as advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, and changes in liver blood tests may occur. Muscle pain or weakness can occur and should be reported promptly.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about liver, kidney, or gallbladder disease, or a history of muscle problems. Seek medical advice promptly for severe muscle pain or weakness, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe abdominal pain. The risk of muscle problems may increase when used with statins. Inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Iron sucrose is an intravenous iron medicine used to treat iron-deficiency anaemia, especially when oral iron is not suitable, not effective, or iron replacement is needed under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It supplies iron, which the body uses to make haemoglobin and red blood cells. This helps restore iron levels and improve anaemia.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein as an injection or infusion by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule are decided by the doctor based on iron levels and medical condition. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, dizziness, changes in blood pressure, muscle cramps, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous reaction to intravenous iron, iron overload, liver disease, or other medical conditions. Serious allergic reactions can occur, so the patient should be monitored during and for a period after administration. Use only when prescribed and keep follow-up blood tests as advised.

What is it used for?
Ferric carboxymaltose injection is used to treat iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anaemia, especially when oral iron is not suitable, has not worked well, or iron levels need to be restored quickly.

How does it work?
It provides iron that the body uses to make haemoglobin and red blood cells. This helps replenish low iron stores and improve anaemia.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given only by a healthcare professional as an intravenous injection or infusion. The dose and number of treatments depend on iron levels, body weight and medical condition. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, dizziness, flushing, temporary increase in blood pressure, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur. Low phosphate levels can also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous reaction to injectable iron, iron overload, liver problems, or ongoing infection. Serious allergic reactions can rarely occur, so monitoring is required during and after administration. Avoid contact with the skin because leakage outside the vein may cause long-lasting brown discolouration. Repeated or high-dose treatment may require phosphate monitoring.

What is it used for?
Used to provide iron and help prevent or treat iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anaemia. The exact use depends on the product formulation and individual needs.

How does it work?
Iron is needed to make haemoglobin, the substance in red blood cells that carries oxygen around the body. Replacing low iron can support healthy red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional, as the strength and dose vary between Ayurvedic products. Shake well before use and measure with the supplied measuring device. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and dark-coloured stools may occur.

Precautions
Keep out of reach of children, as iron overdose can be dangerous. Do not combine with other iron products unless advised. Seek medical advice if anaemia has not been diagnosed, or if there is a history of iron overload. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or with other medicines.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron and folic acid deficiency, including deficiency-related anaemia, when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Iron helps the body make haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood. Folic acid supports the production of healthy red blood cells.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Swallow with water. If it causes stomach upset, it may be taken with food. Avoid taking it at the same time as tea, coffee, milk, calcium supplements or antacids unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, diarrhoea and dark or black stools.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is iron overload, a history of serious blood disorders or an unexplained anaemia. Folic acid may mask vitamin B12 deficiency. Keep out of reach of children, as an iron overdose can be dangerous. Inform the doctor about other medicines and supplements being taken.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron and folic acid deficiency, including iron-deficiency anaemia and anaemia related to low folate levels.

How does it work?
Iron helps the body make haemoglobin and red blood cells. Folic acid supports the formation of healthy red blood cells and other body cells.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed or as directed on the product label. Swallow with water. If it causes stomach upset, taking it with food may help. Avoid taking it at the same time as tea, coffee, milk, calcium supplements or antacids, as these may reduce iron absorption.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, diarrhoea and dark-coloured stools.

Precautions
Do not take more than recommended; iron overdose can be dangerous, especially in children. Tell the doctor if there is a history of iron overload, vitamin B12 deficiency or another cause of anaemia. Iron and folic acid can interact with some medicines, including antacids, calcium supplements, thyroid medicines and certain antibiotics; medical advice may be needed about timing. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Ayurvedic iron syrup is used to prevent or treat iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anaemia, which may cause tiredness, weakness or pale skin. It should be used when iron supplementation is appropriate.

How does it work?
It supplies iron needed by the body to make haemoglobin, the substance in red blood cells that carries oxygen.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and dark-coloured stools may occur.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is iron overload or an iron-storage disorder. Keep out of reach of children, as an overdose can be dangerous. Tell a healthcare professional about other medicines or supplements being taken, as iron may interact with some of them.

What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It may also be used to relieve itching and hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor, with water. Avoid taking it with fruit juices such as apple, orange or grapefruit juice, as they may reduce its effect. Antacids containing aluminium or magnesium should be taken separately as advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, dizziness or mild tiredness may occur. Fexofenadine usually causes little drowsiness, but some people may still feel sleepy.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or sleepiness occurs. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, unusual or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or as stated on the product label, with water. Avoid taking it with fruit juice, as this may reduce its absorption. If using aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids, ask a pharmacist about separating them from fexofenadine.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, dizziness, and tiredness may occur.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This medicine is mainly used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and itchy or watery eyes.

How does it work?
Fexofenadine blocks histamine, a chemical that causes allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, substances involved in allergic inflammation and nasal swelling.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed or directed on the label. Swallow with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid taking it with fruit juice unless advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, dizziness, or tiredness may occur.

Precautions
Montelukast may rarely cause mood or behaviour changes, sleep problems, anxiety, depression, or suicidal thoughts; report these symptoms promptly. This medicine is not a rescue treatment for a sudden asthma attack. Seek medical advice if pregnant, breastfeeding, or if there is a known allergy to either ingredient. Ask a pharmacist before taking aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids, as they may affect fexofenadine absorption.

What is it used for?
Trimetazidine is used as an add-on treatment to relieve symptoms of stable angina (chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart) when other anti-anginal medicines are not enough or are not suitable. It is not used to treat a sudden angina attack.

How does it work?
It helps heart muscle cells use energy more efficiently when the heart has a reduced oxygen supply. This can help reduce angina symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not change or stop treatment without medical advice. This extended-release medicine should not be used for immediate relief of sudden chest pain; seek urgent medical help for new, worsening or persistent chest pain.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, stomach pain, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, weakness, and skin rash or itching may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, Parkinson’s disease, tremors, stiffness, slow movements or other movement disorders. Older adults and people with reduced kidney function may need special medical supervision. Stop the medicine and seek medical advice if new tremors, unusual movements or marked difficulty walking develop. Use only under medical supervision; it is not suitable for acute angina or unstable heart-related chest pain.

What is it used for?
Trimetazidine is used with other medicines to help prevent symptoms of stable angina, such as chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart. It is not intended to treat a sudden angina attack.

How does it work?
It helps heart cells use energy more efficiently when the blood supply is reduced, which may improve the heart’s ability to cope with low oxygen.

How to take/use it
Take this modified-release tablet exactly as prescribed, usually with food. Swallow it whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, stomach discomfort, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, indigestion and weakness may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it to relieve sudden chest pain; seek urgent medical help for an angina attack. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, Parkinson’s disease, tremors or movement disorders, especially if older. Report new or worsening shaking, stiffness, slowed movement or unsteady walking. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Flunarizine is mainly used to prevent migraine attacks. It may also be prescribed to help manage vertigo (a spinning or dizzy sensation) caused by vestibular disorders. It is not usually used to treat a migraine attack after it has started.

How does it work?
It helps reduce the abnormal activity of calcium channels in nerve cells and can reduce the sensitivity of the balance centres in the inner ear. This helps prevent migraine and reduce vertigo in some people.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment without medical advice. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect on alertness is known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, increased appetite, weight gain, constipation, nausea and stomach discomfort may occur. Mood changes, depression or abnormal movements can occur and need medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the doctor before using it if there is a history of depression, Parkinson’s disease or other movement disorders. It may cause sleepiness; avoid alcohol and be careful with driving. Older adults may be more prone to movement-related side effects. Seek medical advice if depression, unusual movements, stiffness or severe drowsiness develops.

What is it used for?
Flunarizine is mainly used to help prevent migraine attacks. It may also be prescribed for certain vertigo or balance problems. It does not usually provide immediate relief during an ongoing migraine attack.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of calcium channels in nerve cells and helps decrease the abnormal nerve activity involved in migraine. It may also reduce overactivity in the balance system of the inner ear.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Take it regularly for the prescribed period, and do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect on alertness is known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, increased appetite, weight gain, tiredness, nausea, constipation and low mood or depression. Movement-related symptoms such as stiffness, tremors or unusual movements can occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of depression, Parkinson’s disease or other movement disorders. Avoid alcohol and use caution with other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice promptly for persistent low mood, tremors, stiffness or unusual movements. Older adults may be more sensitive to movement-related side effects.

What is it used for?
Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation. Depending on the formulation, it may be used for allergic rhinitis (nasal allergies) or asthma. The supplied information does not identify the formulation, so the exact use cannot be confirmed.

How does it work?
It reduces inflammation and swelling in the affected airways or nasal passages, helping relieve related symptoms.

How to take/use it
Use only in the form and manner prescribed by the doctor or stated on the product label. Follow the instructions for the specific nasal spray or inhaler, and do not change the amount or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Side effects depend on the formulation. Nasal use may cause nasal dryness, irritation, nosebleeds or headache. Inhaled use may cause sore throat, hoarseness or oral thrush.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about existing infections, glaucoma, cataracts or other long-term steroid use. If inhaled, rinse the mouth after use to help reduce the risk of oral thrush. Seek medical advice for persistent nosebleeds, vision changes, worsening breathing or signs of infection.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as blocked or runny nose, sneezing, and itchy nose. It may help with allergy symptoms caused by pollen, dust, or other allergens.

How does it work?
Fluticasone reduces inflammation inside the nose, while azelastine blocks the effects of histamine, a chemical involved in allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Use only in the nose and exactly as prescribed. Follow the product instructions for correct spray technique, and avoid spraying into the eyes or swallowing the medicine. Do not share the nasal spray with others.

Common side effects
Nosebleed, nasal dryness or irritation, sneezing, headache, unpleasant taste, and a bitter taste in the mouth.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about nasal injury, recent nasal surgery, nasal infection, glaucoma, cataracts, or long-term use of steroid medicines. Seek medical advice if there is persistent nose irritation or bleeding, blurred vision, or signs of an allergic reaction. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Folic Acid 5 mg is used to prevent or treat folate deficiency and folate-deficiency anaemia. It may also be prescribed during pregnancy, particularly when a higher-strength supplement is medically advised, to help reduce the risk of neural tube defects in the baby.

How does it work?
Folic acid provides folate, a vitamin needed for making DNA and healthy red blood cells. This helps correct or prevent problems caused by folate deficiency.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water; it may usually be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or treatment duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, bloating, gas, reduced appetite or a mild skin rash may occur. Serious allergic reactions are rare.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any vitamin B12 deficiency or unexplained anaemia, as folic acid can improve anaemia while allowing nerve damage from B12 deficiency to progress. Inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding and all medicines being used, especially medicines for epilepsy or methotrexate. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
Used topically to moisturise and soften dry, rough or scaly skin. It may also help improve thickened skin conditions, such as rough bumps, when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Lactic acid helps attract moisture into the skin and gently removes excess dead skin cells, making the skin softer and smoother.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin as directed by the product label or healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and broken or irritated skin. Wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Mild stinging, burning, redness, itching or irritation may occur, especially on sensitive or damaged skin.

Precautions
Avoid applying to broken, infected or severely irritated skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Keep away from the eyes and do not swallow.

What is it used for?
Used for long-term control and prevention of symptoms such as wheezing, breathlessness and coughing in asthma. It may also be prescribed for maintenance treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in some patients.

How does it work?
Budesonide reduces inflammation and swelling in the airways. Formoterol relaxes the airway muscles and helps keep the airways open for easier breathing.

How to take/use it
Use by oral inhalation exactly as prescribed, with the correct inhaler technique. Shake and use the inhaler as directed for the device, and rinse the mouth with water after use without swallowing. Do not stop regular treatment suddenly. Use a separate quick-relief inhaler for sudden breathing difficulty unless a doctor has specifically prescribed this inhaler as part of a reliever plan.

Common side effects
Mouth or throat irritation, hoarseness, oral thrush, headache, tremor, muscle cramps, fast heartbeat or palpitations, and cough may occur.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical help if breathing suddenly worsens or does not improve with the prescribed reliever. Inform the doctor about heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, thyroid problems, low potassium, glaucoma, or current infections. Regular mouth rinsing helps reduce the risk of oral thrush. Do not use more often than prescribed, and report persistent palpitations, severe tremor or vision changes.

What is it used for?
Used regularly to control asthma symptoms and prevent breathing problems. It may also be prescribed for other long-term obstructive airway conditions, such as COPD. It is not intended for immediate relief of a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
Budesonide reduces swelling and inflammation in the airways. Formoterol relaxes the airway muscles and keeps the airways open for longer.

How to take/use it
Use only with a nebulizer and exactly as prescribed. Do not swallow or inject the suspension. Use it regularly even when breathing is normal, unless the prescriber advises otherwise. Rinse the mouth with water after use and spit it out. Do not stop treatment suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Hoarseness, throat irritation, cough, headache, oral fungal infection (thrush), tremor, fast heartbeat or palpitations, and muscle cramps may occur.

Precautions
This medicine does not replace a quick-relief inhaler for sudden breathing difficulty. Seek urgent medical help if breathing suddenly worsens or does not improve with the prescribed rescue medicine. Inform the doctor about heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, thyroid problems, low potassium, or recurrent infections. Avoid using other formoterol-containing medicines unless specifically advised. Rinse the mouth after each treatment and report persistent white patches or soreness in the mouth.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, airways, urinary tract and other areas, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming a protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Reconstitute the powder only as directed on the label or by the pharmacist, using the supplied water if provided. Shake the suspension well before each use and take only the prescribed amount and for the prescribed duration. Complete the course unless the prescriber advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to cefixime, cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, previous antibiotic-associated severe diarrhoea, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin rash or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotics can promote resistance.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by interfering with the formation of their cell walls.

How to take/use it
It is given by injection by a healthcare professional. The dose and duration depend on the infection and patient.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, rash, pain at the injection site and changes in blood test results may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about penicillin or cephalosporin allergy, kidney or liver problems, and other medicines. Use only when prescribed.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone is an antibiotic injection used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin, abdomen, blood, bones and joints. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by preventing them from making the protective cell wall they need to survive.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and must be decided by the prescriber. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise.

Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; rash; and changes in blood test results.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to ceftriaxone, cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, or gallbladder problems. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or a severe skin rash. It should be used in newborn babies only under specialist medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood, bones and joints. It is not effective against viral infections such as colds or flu.

It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. Use it only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Cefixime and azithromycin are antibiotics that stop susceptible bacteria from growing. The added LB (usually a probiotic) may help support healthy gut bacteria during antibiotic treatment.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Take with water and do not share or reuse leftover antibiotics. If a dose is missed, follow the prescribed instructions; do not take extra doses without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea and headache may occur. Mild skin rash can also occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there is a known allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporins, penicillins or azithromycin. Inform the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, heart rhythm problems, or a history of antibiotic-associated diarrhoea. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or irregular heartbeat. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, including heart-rhythm medicines and antacids.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, chest, urinary tract and skin, when prescribed by a healthcare professional. It does not treat viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

Cefixime kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps protect cefixime from enzymes produced by some resistant bacteria.

Take it exactly as prescribed, at evenly spaced times if directed, and complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Do not share this medicine or use leftover antibiotics.

What is it used for?

It stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria and helps clear the infection.

Take it exactly as prescribed, at regular times, and complete the full course even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

It stops susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria and helps clear the infection.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain bacterial infections when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work for viral infections such as common colds or flu.

Cefixime damages the bacterial cell wall, while ofloxacin blocks enzymes bacteria need to grow and multiply. Together, they help kill or stop the growth of susceptible bacteria.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone with sulbactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

What is it used for?
Frusemide is used to remove excess fluid from the body, helping reduce swelling caused by conditions such as heart failure or some kidney and liver problems. It may also be prescribed to help control high blood pressure.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water from the body through urine. This reduces fluid build-up and may lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. It may increase urination, so follow the timing instructions given by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Increased urination, thirst, dizziness, headache, nausea, low blood pressure and dehydration. Changes in body salts, such as low potassium, may also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, low blood pressure, dehydration, diabetes, gout or an existing electrolyte imbalance. Rise slowly if feeling dizzy. Seek medical advice for severe weakness, fainting, confusion, very dry mouth or markedly reduced urine. Regular blood tests may be needed to monitor kidney function and body salts.

What is it used for?
Frusemide injection is used to remove excess fluid from the body, such as swelling caused by heart, kidney or liver problems. It may also be used in emergencies, such as fluid build-up in the lungs, under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water from the body, increasing urine production and reducing fluid build-up.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or nurse, usually in a hospital or clinic. The dose and speed of administration depend on the medical condition and must be decided by the healthcare professional. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, low blood pressure, dehydration, weakness, nausea and changes in body salts such as potassium or sodium.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, low blood pressure, diabetes, gout or existing electrolyte problems. Medical monitoring of blood pressure, kidney function and body salts may be needed. Seek urgent medical attention for severe dizziness, fainting, confusion, muscle weakness or hearing changes.

What is it used for?
This cream is used for bacterial skin infections that are accompanied by redness, swelling, itching or inflammation, including infected eczema or dermatitis.

How does it work?
Fusidic acid is an antibiotic that stops the growth of susceptible bacteria. Beclomethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces skin inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless treating the hands. Avoid covering the area tightly unless advised. For external use only.

Common side effects

What is it used for?

It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, helping to clear the infection.

It stops fungi from making an essential substance needed for their growth, helping clear the infection.

What is it used for?

It blocks the production of an essential part of the fungal cell membrane, stopping the growth and spread of the fungus.
