Itraconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, nails, mouth, and other parts of the body, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential component of their cell membrane, which prevents their growth and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course. Swallow the medicine whole and follow the product label or doctor's instructions regarding food. Do not stop treatment early or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart failure, pregnancy, or breastfeeding before use. Itraconazole can interact with many medicines, including some medicines for heart problems, cholesterol, allergies, and anxiety; provide a complete list of medicines being taken. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe rash, breathing difficulty, swelling, or sudden weight gain.

What is it used for?
Ivabradine is used to lower an elevated heart rate in certain people with chronic stable angina (heart-related chest pain) or chronic heart failure. It is prescribed when reducing the heart rate may help improve symptoms and heart function.

How does it work?
It selectively slows the heart’s natural pacemaker, reducing the heart rate without directly reducing the strength of heart contractions.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with food. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular heart-rate monitoring may be recommended.

Common side effects
Temporary brightness or flashing lights in the field of vision, slow heartbeat, dizziness, headache, tiredness and raised blood pressure. Irregular heartbeat, including atrial fibrillation, may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about a slow or irregular heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart rhythm or conduction problems, liver disease, or if a pacemaker is present. Seek medical advice for fainting, severe dizziness, worsening chest pain or a very slow heartbeat. Avoid grapefruit and inform the doctor about all medicines, especially those affecting heart rhythm or ivabradine levels. Ivabradine is generally not used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Sitagliptin helps the body release more insulin after meals and reduces signals that raise blood sugar. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet whole unless advised otherwise. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber’s instructions and do not double the next dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, gas, vomiting, headache and a reduced appetite may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, heart failure, pancreatitis, heavy alcohol use, or if an operation or contrast-dye scan is planned. Kidney function may need checking before and during treatment. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, breathing difficulty, extreme weakness, or unusual sleepiness. Monitor blood sugar as advised.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Sitagliptin helps the body release insulin when blood sugar is high and reduces the release of hormones that raise blood sugar. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin better.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, usually with food to reduce stomach upset. Take it at the same time each day and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber’s instructions and do not double the next dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, indigestion, headache, and a metallic taste may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or sulfonylurea medicines.

Precautions
Kidney function should be checked regularly, as the dose may need adjustment. Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, heavy alcohol use, heart failure, or planned surgery or contrast-dye tests. Seek medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, extreme weakness, breathing difficulty, or unusual sleepiness, as these may indicate serious reactions. Report symptoms of low blood sugar such as sweating, shaking, dizziness, or confusion.

What is it used for?
Kayam Churn is an Ayurvedic herbal laxative used to relieve constipation and help make bowel movements easier.

How does it work?
Its laxative ingredients help stimulate bowel movement and support the passage of stool through the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by an Ayurvedic doctor. Use with adequate water and do not use for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Abdominal cramps, loose stools, diarrhoea, nausea or bloating may occur, especially if too much is taken.

Precautions
Avoid prolonged or frequent use unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, vomiting, blood in the stool, or suspected intestinal blockage. Use cautiously in children, older adults, and people with dehydration or electrolyte problems. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before use.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin or scalp to treat fungal infections and related fungal irritation. It may also help control dandruff when the product is intended for scalp use.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole stops the growth of fungi. Cetrimide is an antiseptic that helps reduce microorganisms on the treated area.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply or use on the affected area exactly as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole, cetrimide or any ingredient. Avoid applying to the eyes or severely broken skin. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs, or if the condition does not improve. Do not swallow.

What is it used for?
Ketorolac tromethamine is used for the short-term relief of moderate to severe acute pain, such as pain after surgery. It is not intended for long-term pain treatment.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that contribute to pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and for the shortest time advised by the doctor. Swallow with water; taking it with food may help reduce stomach discomfort. Do not take more than prescribed or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac or aspirin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Stomach pain or discomfort, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness and diarrhoea.

Precautions
May cause stomach ulcers or bleeding and can affect kidney function. Avoid it or seek medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney disease, heart failure, uncontrolled high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to NSAIDs. Avoid during pregnancy unless specifically advised, especially from 20 weeks onward and during the third trimester. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, swelling or reduced urination.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% is an antifungal medicine used in topical preparations to treat fungal infections of the skin and scalp. Some preparations are also used for dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, helping to clear the infection and reduce related symptoms.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Apply to the affected skin or scalp as instructed. Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth, and wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
For external use only unless specifically prescribed otherwise. Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole or any ingredient. Avoid contact with the eyes; rinse well with water if contact occurs. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction develops, or if the condition does not improve.

What is it used for?
Used to treat dandruff and fungal-related scalp conditions such as seborrhoeic dermatitis, which can cause itching, flaking and scaling.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole and zinc pyrithione help control the growth of fungi on the skin and scalp, reducing flaking and irritation.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use on the affected area exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes and rinse well with water if contact occurs.

Common side effects
Mild skin or scalp irritation, itching, burning, dryness or redness may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole, zinc pyrithione or any ingredient. Avoid use on severely broken or irritated skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops, or if symptoms do not improve.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% shampoo is used to treat dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis, and certain fungal skin infections such as pityriasis versicolor.

How does it work?
It is an antifungal medicine that stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, helping control fungal growth and related scaling or itching.

How to take/use it
Use on the scalp or affected skin exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Wet the area, apply the shampoo, gently lather and rinse thoroughly. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not swallow it.

Common side effects
Mild burning, itching, irritation, dryness or redness at the application site. Changes in hair texture or colour may occasionally occur.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid the eyes and broken or severely irritated skin; rinse well with water if it gets into the eyes. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Labetalol is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It may also be used under medical supervision when blood pressure is dangerously high, including during pregnancy.

How does it work?
It blocks certain effects of adrenaline on the heart and blood vessels. This slows the heartbeat and relaxes blood vessels, helping to lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or immediately after food, and at the same time each day. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, tiredness, nausea, headache, and a slow heartbeat may occur. These effects may be more noticeable when starting treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma or other breathing disease, a slow heartbeat, heart block, heart failure, diabetes, or liver disease. Labetalol may mask some warning signs of low blood sugar. Rise slowly if feeling dizzy, and seek medical advice for fainting, breathing difficulty, swelling, or an unusually slow heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Lactulose is mainly used to relieve constipation by making stools softer and easier to pass. It may also be prescribed by a doctor to help reduce high ammonia levels in people with certain liver conditions.

How does it work?
It draws water into the bowel, softening the stool and helping bowel movements. In liver disease, it also helps reduce the absorption of ammonia from the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. It may be taken alone or mixed with water or juice. Drink adequate fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, stomach cramps, nausea and diarrhoea. Excessive diarrhoea may cause dehydration or loss of body salts.

Precautions
Do not use it without medical advice if there is severe or unexplained abdominal pain, vomiting, suspected bowel blockage or a serious bowel condition. Use with caution if diabetes is present, as some formulations contain sugars. Seek medical advice if diarrhoea is severe or persistent, or if constipation does not improve.

What is it used for?
Lactulose is mainly used to relieve constipation by making stools softer and easier to pass. It may also be prescribed for some people with liver disease to help reduce the absorption of ammonia, but this use requires medical supervision.

How does it work?
It draws water into the bowel, softening the stool and helping bowel movements. In liver disease, it also helps reduce ammonia absorption from the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as directed on the package or by the prescriber. Measure the product carefully and drink adequate fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended without medical advice.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, stomach cramps, nausea and diarrhoea, especially if too much is taken.

Precautions
Do not use it without medical advice if there is severe or unexplained abdominal pain, vomiting, suspected bowel blockage or a sudden change in bowel habits. Prolonged or severe diarrhoea may cause dehydration or disturbed body salts. People with diabetes should ask a doctor or pharmacist before use, as some products may contain sugars. Seek medical advice if constipation does not improve or keeps returning.

What is it used for?
Lactic acid bacilli are probiotic bacteria used to help restore the normal balance of bacteria in the intestine. They may support recovery from diarrhoea, including diarrhoea associated with antibiotic use.

How does it work?
It adds beneficial bacteria to the intestine and helps support a healthy balance of gut microorganisms.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not use more or for longer than recommended. If taking antibiotics, follow the advice of a healthcare professional about when to take this product.

Common side effects
Mild gas, bloating or stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, high fever, dehydration or severe abdominal pain. People with severely weakened immunity or serious underlying illness should use probiotics only after medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve constipation by making stools softer and easier to pass.

How does it work?
Lactulose draws water into the bowel, softening the stool and helping bowel movements. Fructo-oligosaccharides and polydextrose act as dietary fibres that support bowel function.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. It may be taken with water or mixed with a suitable drink. Drink adequate fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal cramps, nausea and diarrhoea, especially if too much is taken.

Precautions
Do not use if there is suspected bowel blockage or severe unexplained abdominal pain. Consult a doctor if constipation persists, or if there is vomiting, blood in the stool or marked abdominal swelling. People with diabetes or those requiring long-term use should seek medical advice, as prolonged or excessive use may cause fluid or electrolyte imbalance.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve constipation by softening stools and making them easier to pass.

How does it work?
Lactitol draws water into the bowel to soften stools. Ispaghula husk absorbs water and increases stool bulk, helping promote bowel movement.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Mix with sufficient water and drink promptly; do not take the powder dry. Drink plenty of fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised. Keep other oral medicines separate as advised by a pharmacist or doctor.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort or cramps, nausea, and diarrhoea, especially when starting treatment or if too much is taken.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is severe or unexplained abdominal pain, vomiting, suspected intestinal blockage, or difficulty swallowing. Stop and seek medical advice if constipation persists, worsens, or there is blood in the stool. Ensure adequate fluid intake to reduce the risk of blockage from the fibre component.

What is it used for?
Lansoprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be prescribed for stomach or duodenal ulcers and other acid-related conditions.

How does it work?
It is a proton pump inhibitor that reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. This helps relieve symptoms and allows acid-related irritation or ulcers to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by the doctor or stated on the label. Place the orally disintegrating tablet on the tongue and allow it to dissolve before swallowing. It is usually taken before food; follow the prescribed instructions. Do not chew or crush it.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking other medicines. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or persistent symptoms. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor, as it may affect vitamin B12, magnesium or bone health and may increase the risk of certain infections.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of constipation and to help make hard stools easier to pass.

How does it work?
Liquid paraffin lubricates the stool and bowel, milk of magnesia draws water into the bowel, and sodium picosulfate stimulates bowel movement.

How to take/use it
Shake the suspension well before use. Measure it with the supplied measuring device and take it exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Drink adequate fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised. Do not use it regularly or for a prolonged period without medical advice.

Common side effects
Abdominal cramps, bloating, nausea, loose stools or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, vomiting, suspected bowel blockage, or rectal bleeding. Stop and seek medical advice if constipation persists or if severe diarrhoea, weakness or signs of dehydration occur. Frequent or prolonged use can disturb body salts and may make the bowel dependent on laxatives. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, in children, or if there is kidney disease or other significant illness.

What is it used for?
Levocetirizine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching. It may also be used for hives (urticaria) and related skin itching.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, and stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
It may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid or limit alcohol, as it may increase sleepiness. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
Leflunomide is used to treat rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis. It helps reduce joint pain, swelling and stiffness and may slow damage to the joints.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of certain immune cells involved in inflammation. This helps control the abnormal immune response that causes joint inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment without medical advice. Regular blood tests may be needed to check the liver and blood cell counts.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, headache, skin rash, hair loss and increased liver enzyme levels may occur. It can also increase the risk of infections.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy, and discuss pregnancy planning with a doctor because it may harm an unborn baby. Tell the doctor about liver disease, high blood pressure, blood disorders, immune-system problems or ongoing infections. Avoid or limit alcohol and do not start new medicines without medical advice. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe rash, breathing difficulty, persistent cough, fever or unusual bruising.

What is it used for?
Leflunomide is used to treat rheumatoid arthritis and psoriatic arthritis. It helps reduce joint pain, swelling and stiffness, and may slow worsening of the disease.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of certain immune cells that cause inflammation in the joints. This helps control inflammation and autoimmune-related joint damage.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, with or without food, and swallow the tablet with water. Take it regularly and do not stop treatment without medical advice. Regular blood tests may be needed during treatment.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach upset, headache, hair loss, skin rash, increased blood pressure and abnormal liver test results may occur. It can also increase the risk of infections.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a specialist. Women who could become pregnant should use reliable contraception. Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, high blood pressure, infections, blood disorders or nerve problems. Liver function and blood counts should be monitored. Avoid excessive alcohol and do not receive live vaccines unless advised. Seek medical advice promptly for yellowing of the skin, severe rash, breathing problems, persistent infection or unusual bleeding.

What is it used for?
Letrozole is mainly used to treat certain types of breast cancer in women after menopause. It may also be prescribed by a specialist to help induce ovulation in some fertility treatments.

How does it work?
Letrozole lowers the body’s production of oestrogen. This can slow or stop the growth of some breast cancer cells and may help trigger ovulation in fertility treatment.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water and take it at the same time each day. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Hot flushes, sweating, tiredness, headache, dizziness, nausea, joint or muscle pain, increased cholesterol, and thinning or weakening of the bones may occur.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically directed by a specialist; it can harm an unborn baby. It is generally not used for breast cancer treatment before menopause unless prescribed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about liver or kidney problems, osteoporosis, or a history of fractures. Long-term treatment may require bone-health monitoring. Seek medical advice if severe dizziness, unusual bone pain, or symptoms of a fracture occur.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is an anti-seizure medicine used to prevent and control epileptic seizures. It may be used alone or with other seizure medicines, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain, which can prevent seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Do not stop it suddenly, even if feeling better, as this may trigger seizures. If a dose is missed, follow the advice provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, weakness, reduced appetite, and mood or behaviour changes such as irritability or agitation.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or any history of depression or other mental-health problems. Seek medical help for severe mood changes, unusual aggression, depression, thoughts of self-harm, serious rash, swelling, or breathing difficulty. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known, and avoid alcohol unless approved by the doctor.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is an anti-seizure medicine used to prevent and control epileptic seizures, including focal seizures and some generalised seizures. It may be used alone or with other seizure medicines, as prescribed.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain that can trigger seizures. Its exact action is not fully understood, but it affects a brain protein involved in the release of chemical signals between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day. It may usually be taken with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop taking it suddenly, as this may worsen seizures. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea, and irritability or other mood changes may occur.

Precautions
Report severe irritability, aggression, depression, unusual behaviour, or thoughts of self-harm promptly. Use cautiously in people with kidney problems, as the dose may need adjustment. Avoid driving or operating machinery until the effects are known. Seek urgent medical help for a serious rash, swelling, breathing difficulty, or other signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is an anti-seizure medicine used to prevent and control epileptic seizures, including focal seizures and some generalized seizures. It may be used alone or together with other seizure medicines, as prescribed.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by regulating the release of chemical signals between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop treatment or change the dose suddenly, as this may worsen seizures. If a dose is missed, follow the advice provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, nausea, irritability, agitation, or mood changes may occur.

Precautions
It may cause sleepiness or dizziness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Inform the doctor about kidney problems, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe rash, swelling, breathing difficulty, unusual aggression, depression, suicidal thoughts, or worsening seizures. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is used to prevent and control seizures in epilepsy. It may be used alone or together with other anti-seizure medicines, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by regulating the release of certain chemical signals between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop taking it suddenly, as seizures may worsen. If a dose is missed, follow the doctor’s or pharmacist’s advice.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, weakness, nausea, and irritability or other mood changes.

Precautions
It may cause sleepiness or dizziness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Report severe mood or behaviour changes, depression, thoughts of self-harm, unusual aggression, or allergic reactions promptly. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is used to control seizures in people with epilepsy. It may help reduce different types of seizures, including focal and generalised seizures, as prescribed by the doctor.

How does it work?
It helps calm excessive electrical activity in the brain and reduces the likelihood of seizures. Its exact action is not fully understood, but it acts partly by binding to a protein involved in the release of chemical signals between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day. The tablet may usually be taken with or without food and should be swallowed with water. Do not stop treatment suddenly, as this may worsen seizures. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, weakness, nausea, and irritability or other mood changes may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, depression, or previous mood or behaviour changes. Seek medical help for severe rash, swelling, breathing difficulty, unusual aggression, severe depression, or thoughts of self-harm. Avoid driving or operating machinery until the effects are known. Do not stop levetiracetam suddenly without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam injection is used to prevent and control epileptic seizures. It may be given in hospital when levetiracetam tablets or oral liquid cannot be taken.

How does it work?
It reduces abnormal electrical activity in the brain that can cause seizures, helping to prevent them.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type of seizures, age, kidney function and medical condition. Do not stop treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea, and irritability or other mood or behaviour changes may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, previous allergies to levetiracetam, or a history of depression or other mental health problems. Report severe mood or behaviour changes, aggression, confusion, hallucinations, or thoughts of self-harm promptly. Seek urgent help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Levocetirizine syrup is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin allergies such as hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce itching, sneezing, runny nose and other allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device, and do not use a household spoon. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache and dry mouth may occur.

Precautions
It may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known. Avoid or limit alcohol, as it may increase sleepiness. Consult a doctor before use in children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is kidney disease. Seek medical advice if allergy symptoms are severe or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Levocetirizine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching. It may also be used for hives (urticaria) and related skin itching.

How does it work?
It is an antihistamine that blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, and dizziness.

Precautions
It may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known. Avoid alcohol because it may increase sleepiness. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve breathing difficulty, wheezing and chest tightness caused by narrowing of the airways in conditions such as asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It helps open the airways and improve airflow.

How does it work?
Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles around the airways, while ipratropium reduces airway muscle tightening. Together, they help widen the airways and make breathing easier.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed and follow the instructions for the inhaler or other device provided. Use the correct technique, do not exceed the prescribed amount, and seek medical advice if breathing problems worsen or do not improve.

Common side effects
Shakiness, nervousness, headache, dry mouth, throat irritation, cough, nausea, muscle cramps, fast heartbeat or palpitations.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, glaucoma, prostate or urinary problems, diabetes, or thyroid disease. Avoid getting the medicine into the eyes. Seek urgent medical help for severe worsening of breathing, chest pain, severe palpitations, eye pain or blurred vision, or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Levosalbutamol is a bronchodilator used to relieve breathing difficulty, wheezing and chest tightness caused by narrowed airways in conditions such as asthma and other breathing disorders.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them open and making it easier to breathe.

How to take/use it
Use it only as prescribed by the doctor and follow the instructions for the prescribed inhalation device. Do not change the dose or frequency, and do not swallow a product intended for inhalation.

Common side effects
Shakiness or tremor, nervousness, headache, dizziness, fast heartbeat, palpitations and muscle cramps may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, thyroid problems or low potassium levels. Seek medical help if breathing suddenly worsens, the heartbeat becomes very fast or irregular, or severe chest pain occurs. Do not use more often than prescribed.

What is it used for?
Levosulpride is used to relieve indigestion symptoms such as bloating, early fullness, nausea and upper-abdominal discomfort, especially when these are related to slow movement of food through the stomach.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals involved in nausea and helps improve movement of the stomach and upper digestive tract, allowing food to pass more normally.

What is it used for?
Linezolid is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, including some infections of the lungs, skin and soft tissues, and infections caused by resistant Gram-positive bacteria. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and survive.

Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not share it or use leftover antibiotics.

What is it used for?

It forms a protective layer over the lips that helps lock in moisture and protect them from drying out.

Precautions
This medicine may cause dizziness, especially when starting treatment; rise slowly and avoid driving if affected. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, pregnancy, or plans to become pregnant. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor. Regular monitoring of blood pressure, kidney function, and blood potassium may be recommended.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) when treatment with one medicine alone is not enough. Lowering blood pressure helps reduce the risk of related heart and blood vessel problems.

How does it work?
Losartan relaxes blood vessels by blocking the action of angiotensin II, a substance that can raise blood pressure. Hydrochlorothiazide helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water, which also lowers blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food; swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, increased urination, low blood pressure, and changes in blood potassium or other body salts may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, gout, diabetes, or previous high or low potassium levels. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. This medicine should not be used during pregnancy; contact a doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially other blood-pressure medicines, diuretics, anti-inflammatory painkillers such as ibuprofen, or lithium. Rise slowly if dizziness occurs, and seek medical help for severe weakness, fainting, swelling, or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Luliconazole 1% is a topical antifungal used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin exactly as directed by the doctor or product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. For external use only.

Common side effects
Mild application-site irritation, redness, itching, burning or dryness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not apply to broken or severely irritated skin unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens, does not improve, or causes severe irritation. Use only for the diagnosed skin infection.

What is it used for?
Luliconazole 1% is used on the skin to treat fungal infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, helping to clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin as directed by the doctor or product instructions. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose.

Common side effects
Mild application-site irritation, redness, itching, burning or stinging may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to luliconazole or any of its ingredients. Avoid applying to the eyes, mouth, vagina or broken skin unless specifically advised. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Complete the recommended treatment and seek medical advice if the infection does not improve.

What is it used for?
Luliconazole 1% is a topical antifungal used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch. It helps relieve infection-related itching, redness and scaling.

How does it work?
It stops the growth of fungi by interfering with the production of ergosterol, a substance fungi need to maintain their cell membranes.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the clean, dry affected skin exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. For external use only; avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild application-site irritation, redness, itching, burning or dryness may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to luliconazole or any ingredient in the product. Avoid applying to the eyes, mouth, open wounds or severely irritated skin. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops, or if the infection does not improve as expected.

What is it used for?
This is a multivitamin and mineral supplement used to help provide nutritional support when the diet may not provide enough vitamins, minerals, omega-3 fatty acids and other nutrients. It is not intended to treat a specific disease unless advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Its vitamins, minerals and other nutrients support normal body functions, including energy metabolism, nerve function, immunity and general nutritional health.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount or combine it with other multivitamin products without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, indigestion, loose stools or a fishy aftertaste may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
Check the ingredients if there is an allergy to fish, seafood or any component of the product. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, before surgery, or if taking blood-thinning medicines or other supplements. Excessive use of vitamins, especially fat-soluble vitamins, can be harmful.

What is it used for?
This supplement helps provide vitamins, minerals and lycopene when dietary intake is inadequate. It supports normal immune function and general nutritional health, but it is not a treatment for a specific disease.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamin A, vitamins C and E, zinc, selenium and lycopene. These nutrients support normal body functions and help protect cells from oxidative stress.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow with water; taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not exceed the recommended amount or combine it with other supplements containing the same nutrients unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or loose stools may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if unusual or severe symptoms develop.

Precautions
Inform a doctor or pharmacist if pregnant, planning pregnancy, breastfeeding, or if there is liver disease or another medical condition, particularly because the product contains vitamin A. Check with a healthcare professional before use with other vitamin or mineral supplements. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Magnesium glycinate is a dietary supplement used to provide magnesium and help prevent or correct low magnesium levels. Magnesium is needed for normal nerve, muscle and bone function.

How does it work?
It supplies magnesium, an essential mineral involved in nerve signalling, muscle contraction and many normal body processes. Glycinate is magnesium bound to glycine.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label. Do not assume that 2000 mg of magnesium glycinate equals 2000 mg of elemental magnesium. Take with water, and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, abdominal cramps or diarrhoea may occur, especially with excessive intake.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, as magnesium can accumulate. Ask a doctor or pharmacist about use with antibiotics, thyroid medicines or medicines for osteoporosis, as magnesium may reduce their absorption and may need to be taken separately. Seek medical advice if supplementation is being used to treat suspected magnesium deficiency.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain, swelling and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions. It may also help reduce fever.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and lower fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Take it with or after food and swallow with water. Do not take more than the prescribed amount, or combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol or painkillers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac or aspirin unless advised.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to painkillers. Avoid alcohol and other paracetamol-containing products. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe rash, breathing difficulty or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Use during pregnancy, especially late pregnancy, only if specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and swelling, especially in muscle, joint and other musculoskeletal conditions. It may also help reduce pain associated with injury or after certain procedures, when prescribed.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and fever, while serratiopeptidase may help reduce swelling.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food if it causes stomach discomfort. Do not take additional paracetamol- or anti-inflammatory-containing medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache. Skin rash or other allergic reactions may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or bleeding problems. Avoid excess alcohol. Do not use during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe rash, breathing difficulty, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Mebeverine is used to relieve painful intestinal cramps and spasms, especially symptoms associated with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), such as abdominal pain, bloating and bowel discomfort.

How does it work?
It directly relaxes the muscles of the intestine, helping to reduce spasms and cramping without significantly affecting normal bowel movement.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed or as directed on the package. Swallow the tablet with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Seek medical advice if symptoms are new, severe or do not improve.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon. Possible effects include indigestion, heartburn, dizziness, headache, nausea, constipation or diarrhoea. Allergic reactions such as rash, itching or swelling can rarely occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if allergic to mebeverine or any of its ingredients. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or in children. Seek medical advice for blood in the stool, unexplained weight loss, fever, vomiting, severe abdominal pain or persistent bowel changes. Stop use and seek urgent help if swelling of the face or throat or difficulty breathing occurs.

What is it used for?
Mebeverine 200 Retard is used to relieve painful cramps, spasms and discomfort in the intestines, especially in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and other bowel conditions involving spasms.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles of the intestine and helps reduce painful spasms. It generally works without stopping the normal movement of the bowel.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by the doctor or as stated on the package. Swallow the retard capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon. Possible effects include allergic skin reactions such as rash, itching or hives. Rarely, swelling of the face, lips or throat or breathing difficulty may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to mebeverine or any of its ingredients. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice for new, severe or persistent abdominal pain, vomiting, blood in the stool, unexplained weight loss, or changes in bowel habits. Stop taking it and seek urgent help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
Medroxyprogesterone 10 mg is a progesterone-like hormone used to treat irregular or absent menstrual periods and abnormal uterine bleeding caused by hormonal imbalance. It may also be prescribed for conditions such as endometriosis or to protect the lining of the uterus during some hormone replacement treatments.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone progesterone. It helps regulate the menstrual cycle and controls the growth and shedding of the uterine lining.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Take it at the same time each day if instructed. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions on the prescription or ask a pharmacist.

Common side effects
Irregular bleeding or spotting, changes in menstrual flow, headache, nausea, breast tenderness, bloating, mood changes and weight changes.

Precautions
Do not use it during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor before use if there is unexplained vaginal bleeding, liver disease, a history of blood clots or stroke, breast cancer, or significant depression. Seek urgent medical help for sudden chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, vision changes, or painful swelling in a leg.

What is it used for?
Metformin 500 mg is mainly used to control high blood sugar in people with type 2 diabetes. It may be used alone or with other diabetes medicines, along with a suitable diet and exercise plan.

How does it work?
It reduces the amount of glucose made by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively. It usually does not cause low blood sugar when used alone.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain or discomfort, gas, reduced appetite, and a metallic taste. These effects may improve as the body adjusts.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there are kidney or liver problems, severe infection, dehydration, heavy alcohol use, or plans for an X-ray or scan using injected contrast dye. Seek urgent medical help for severe weakness, breathing difficulty, unusual sleepiness, or persistent vomiting. Long-term use may reduce vitamin B12 levels, so monitoring may be advised.

What is it used for?
Mefenamic acid is used for short-term relief of mild to moderate pain, including period pain. It may also help reduce fever.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, inflammation and fever.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food and with water. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest recommended time. Do not take it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Stomach pain or indigestion, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Avoid or seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAIDs. It may increase the risk of stomach bleeding, especially with blood thinners, steroids or alcohol. Avoid during pregnancy, particularly after 20 weeks, unless specifically prescribed. Stop and seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin rash.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain and fever, including body aches and pain associated with inflammation.

How does it work?
Mefenamic acid reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow with water, preferably after food. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or other painkillers unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty or swelling of the face or lips.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if allergic to mefenamic acid, paracetamol or similar painkillers. Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, kidney or liver disease, heart problems, or regular alcohol use. Avoid during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, unless specifically prescribed. Do not combine with other paracetamol-containing products or NSAID painkillers without medical advice.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of mild to moderate pain and fever, including pain associated with inflammation such as muscle, joint, dental or menstrual pain.

How does it work?
Mefenamic acid reduces the production of substances that cause pain, swelling and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different mechanism.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor or pharmacist. Take it with or after food and swallow with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or other anti-inflammatory painkillers unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation, dizziness or headache.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to mefenamic acid, paracetamol, aspirin or other anti-inflammatory painkillers. Seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, heart disease or high blood pressure. Avoid alcohol. This medicine may not be suitable during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months, or while breastfeeding unless prescribed. Stop and seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve crampy pain, including painful menstrual cramps and spasmodic abdominal pain.

How does it work?
Mefenamic acid reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Dicyclomine relaxes spasms in the muscles of the stomach and intestines, helping reduce cramping.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food to reduce stomach upset. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, diarrhoea or constipation, dizziness, drowsiness, dry mouth and blurred vision may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is a history of allergy to mefenamic acid, dicyclomine, aspirin or other NSAIDs. Use cautiously with stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver problems, asthma, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, or bowel blockage. Avoid combining it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor. It should generally be avoided in the last three months of pregnancy. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty or facial swelling.

What is it used for?
Melatonin is used for certain sleep problems, such as difficulty falling asleep or disruption of the sleep-wake cycle.

How does it work?
It is a hormone that helps regulate the body's sleep-wake timing.

How to take/use it
Use only at the time and dose advised by a healthcare professional or stated on the approved label. Do not take extra doses.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, headache, dizziness and nausea may occur.

Precautions
May cause sleepiness; avoid driving if affected. Check with a healthcare professional before use with other sedatives, during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Memantine is used to help manage symptoms of moderate to severe Alzheimer’s disease, such as problems with memory, thinking and daily activities. It may help slow worsening of symptoms but does not cure Alzheimer’s disease.

How does it work?
It regulates the activity of a brain chemical called glutamate. This may help protect brain cells from excessive stimulation and support memory and thinking.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice. If a dose is missed, do not take an extra dose unless advised.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, constipation, sleepiness, confusion, tiredness, vomiting and problems with balance may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, seizures, or difficulty passing urine. Seek advice before using other medicines, especially those that affect kidney function or urine acidity. Dizziness or sleepiness may affect activities such as driving. Medical supervision is important, particularly for older adults.

What is it used for?
Memantine is used to help manage symptoms of moderate to severe Alzheimer’s disease, such as problems with memory, thinking and daily activities. It may help slow worsening of symptoms but does not cure Alzheimer’s disease.

How does it work?
Memantine blocks excessive activity of a brain chemical called glutamate. This may help protect nerve cells and support memory and thinking.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. It may be taken with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water, and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, constipation, sleepiness, confusion and increased blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, seizures, or bladder and urinary-tract problems. Memantine may cause dizziness or sleepiness, so take care when driving or using machinery. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially amantadine, ketamine, dextromethorphan or medicines that make the urine alkaline.

What is it used for?
Meropenem is a strong antibiotic used in hospitals to treat serious infections caused by susceptible bacteria, including infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin, blood, and brain. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by preventing them from making the protective cell wall they need to survive.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Use it only as prescribed and do not stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea or vomiting, headache, rash, and pain or inflammation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to meropenem, penicillins, cephalosporins, or other antibiotics. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney disease. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, seizures, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Tell the doctor if taking valproate or other regular medicines.

What is it used for?
Meropenem is a prescription antibiotic used in hospitals to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin, blood, and brain. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Meropenem is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose, timing, and treatment length depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea or vomiting, headache, rash, and pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to meropenem, penicillins, cephalosporins, or other antibiotics; kidney problems; or a history of seizures. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, seizures, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Tell the doctor if taking valproate or other medicines, as interactions may occur. Use only when prescribed and complete the prescribed course.

What is it used for?
This injection is used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, and other parts of the body. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Meropenem kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps meropenem work against some bacteria that can otherwise resist certain antibiotics.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Complete the prescribed course unless the treating doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, headache, rash, and pain or inflammation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to meropenem, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics, kidney disease, seizures, or previous severe diarrhoea after antibiotic use. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, seizures, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Use only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Mesalamine is used to treat ulcerative colitis, a condition that causes inflammation in the large intestine. It helps reduce symptoms such as diarrhoea, abdominal pain and blood in the stool, and may help maintain remission.

How does it work?
Mesalamine acts locally in the lining of the intestine to reduce inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions on the product label. Swallow the tablet as directed; do not crush or chew it unless specifically advised. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, abdominal pain, indigestion and diarrhoea.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, stomach or intestinal problems, or allergy to mesalamine, aspirin or other salicylates. Medical monitoring may be needed during treatment. Seek urgent medical help for severe rash, breathing difficulty, chest pain, worsening bloody diarrhoea, severe abdominal pain or markedly reduced urine.

What is it used for?
Mesalamine 1200 mg used rectally helps reduce inflammation in the rectum and lower bowel caused by ulcerative colitis, including ulcerative proctitis.

How does it work?
It acts mainly on the lining of the bowel to reduce the release of substances that cause inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use rectally only, exactly as prescribed and according to the product instructions. Do not swallow it. Wash hands before and after use, and complete the prescribed treatment unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Headache, abdominal pain or cramps, nausea, diarrhoea, gas, and rectal discomfort or irritation may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to mesalamine, aspirin, or other salicylates, and about kidney or liver disease. Medical monitoring may be needed during treatment. Seek urgent medical help for severe rash, breathing difficulty, severe abdominal pain, worsening bloody diarrhoea, or markedly reduced urine.

What is it used for?
Metformin 1000 mg SR is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in people with type 2 diabetes. It may also be prescribed for other conditions only when specifically advised by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the amount of glucose made by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively, lowering blood sugar levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with or after food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush, chew or split it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, gas, indigestion, reduced appetite and a metallic taste may occur, especially when treatment is started. Long-term use may reduce vitamin B12 levels.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems, severe infection, dehydration, heart failure or heavy alcohol use. Kidney function should be checked during treatment. Metformin may need to be stopped temporarily before certain scans using injectable contrast dye or during serious illness, as advised by a doctor. Seek urgent medical help for severe weakness, unusual sleepiness, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting or severe abdominal pain.

What is it used for?
Metformin 500 SR is used to help control high blood sugar in people with type 2 diabetes. It may be used alone or with other diabetes medicines, along with a healthy diet and regular physical activity.

How does it work?
It reduces the amount of glucose made by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively, lowering blood sugar levels.

What is it used for?
Methylcobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 used to prevent or treat vitamin B12 deficiency. It may help manage deficiency-related megaloblastic anaemia and nerve problems.

How does it work?
It replaces vitamin B12 needed for healthy red blood cell formation and normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. The dose and duration depend on the severity and cause of vitamin B12 deficiency. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, headache, or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to vitamin B12, methylcobalamin, or cobalt. Seek medical help for swelling, breathing difficulty, or a severe rash. Vitamin B12 deficiency may require tests to identify and treat its underlying cause.

What is it used for?
Methylcobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 used to prevent or treat vitamin B12 deficiency. It may help correct B12-related anaemia and nerve problems.

How does it work?
Vitamin B12 is needed for the formation of healthy red blood cells and for normal nerve function. Methylcobalamin helps support these processes when vitamin B12 levels are low.

How to take/use it
Use it exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. The dose and treatment duration depend on the reason for use and the product form. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, headache, or skin rash may occur. Seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to methylcobalamin, vitamin B12, or cobalt. Medical advice is important before use for unexplained anaemia, persistent tiredness, or nerve symptoms, as the underlying cause may need evaluation. Inform the doctor about other medicines and any existing medical conditions.

What is it used for?
Methylcobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 used to prevent or treat vitamin B12 deficiency. It may help support the formation of healthy red blood cells and normal nerve function.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamin B12, which the body needs for red blood cell production, DNA formation and healthy nerves.

How to take/use it
Take or use it exactly as directed by a doctor or as stated on the product label. Do not use more than the recommended amount. The dose and duration depend on the severity and cause of vitamin B12 deficiency.

Common side effects
It is usually well tolerated. Nausea, diarrhoea, headache, skin rash or itching may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to methylcobalamin, vitamin B12 or cobalt. Seek medical advice if symptoms do not improve or if vitamin B12 deficiency has not been confirmed.
