What is it used for?
Methylcobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 used to prevent or treat vitamin B12 deficiency. B12 deficiency can cause certain types of anaemia and nerve-related symptoms such as tingling or numbness.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamin B12, which supports the formation of healthy red blood cells and helps maintain normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take or use it exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not change the dose or treatment duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
It is usually well tolerated. Nausea, diarrhoea, headache, or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a previous allergic reaction to methylcobalamin, vitamin B12, or its ingredients. Seek medical advice for persistent tingling, numbness, weakness, or symptoms of anaemia, as the underlying cause may need evaluation. Tell the doctor about any other medicines or supplements being used.

What is it used for?
This nutritional supplement helps provide vitamins, minerals and antioxidant nutrients that support normal nerve function, energy metabolism and bone health. It may be used when dietary intake of these nutrients is inadequate or when supplementation is recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Its ingredients supply nutrients involved in nerve function, blood-cell formation, energy production and bone maintenance. Alpha-lipoic acid also provides antioxidant activity.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not start or continue it for a prolonged period without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea or constipation may occur. Rarely, allergic reactions may develop.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use if there is diabetes, kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Chromium and alpha-lipoic acid may affect blood sugar and may require monitoring when used with diabetes medicines. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, including iron, thyroid medicines and certain antibiotics; separate their use as advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
This supplement provides L-carnitine, vitamin B12 (methylcobalamin) and folic acid to help meet nutritional needs and support normal nerve function, red blood cell formation and energy metabolism. It may be used when supplementation is recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
L-carnitine helps transport fatty acids for energy production. Vitamin B12 and folic acid support DNA formation, healthy blood cells and normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. The duration of use depends on the reason for supplementation.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea or abdominal discomfort may occur. L-carnitine may sometimes cause a fish-like body odour.

Precautions
Inform a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, a history of seizures, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek advice if taking blood thinners such as warfarin or other regular medicines. Stop use and seek medical help if an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
This supplement provides vitamin B12, vitamin B6, folic acid, vitamin D3 and alpha-lipoic acid. It is used to help prevent or correct nutritional deficiencies and support normal nerve function when supplementation is advised.

How does it work?
The vitamins help support nerve, blood-cell, bone and general body functions. Alpha-lipoic acid acts as an antioxidant and supports normal nerve metabolism.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount or combine it with other supplements containing the same vitamins unless advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache or skin rash may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if symptoms are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Inform a healthcare professional if there is diabetes, pregnancy, breastfeeding, thyroid disease, or kidney or liver problems. Alpha-lipoic acid may lower blood sugar and may require caution with diabetes medicines. Prolonged or excessive vitamin B6 intake can cause tingling or numbness. Check with a healthcare professional before use with other vitamin supplements or medicines.

What is it used for?
This combination is commonly used to support nerve health and help manage symptoms of peripheral neuropathy, such as tingling, numbness, burning or nerve discomfort. It may also be prescribed when these nutrients are deficient.

How does it work?
Methylcobalamin, folic acid and pyridoxine support normal nerve function and blood-cell formation. Alpha-lipoic acid acts as an antioxidant and may help protect nerves from oxidative stress.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet or capsule with water and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, headache or skin rash may occur. Stop taking it and seek medical advice if signs of a serious allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to these ingredients. People with diabetes should monitor blood sugar, as alpha-lipoic acid may affect glucose levels, especially when used with diabetes medicines. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking other medicines or supplements.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when one medicine alone is not enough.

How does it work?
Glimepiride helps the pancreas release more insulin. Metformin reduces sugar production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin, while voglibose slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates after meals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with or just before meals. Swallow the tablet whole and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Follow the recommended diet and exercise plan, and monitor blood sugar as advised.

Common side effects
Low blood sugar, nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, bloating and gas may occur. Low blood sugar may cause sweating, shakiness, dizziness, hunger or weakness.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Take extra care if there is kidney or liver disease, reduced food intake, heavy alcohol use, or a history of low blood sugar. Seek medical help for severe or persistent weakness, breathing difficulty, unusual sleepiness, or severe vomiting. Inform the doctor before surgery, serious illness, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and before any scan using an injected contrast dye.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone sodium succinate injection is used to quickly reduce severe inflammation and overactive immune reactions in conditions such as severe allergies, asthma flare-ups, and autoimmune or other inflammatory disorders. The exact reason for treatment depends on the patient's condition and is decided by a doctor.

How does it work?
It is a corticosteroid that suppresses inflammation and reduces excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and response to treatment.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar, increased blood pressure, indigestion, fluid retention, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, and pain or redness at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health conditions, liver or kidney problems, or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body's ability to fight infections and may mask infection symptoms. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically advised. If used for a longer period, it should not be stopped suddenly without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactivity of the immune system. It may be prescribed for inflammatory and autoimmune conditions, severe allergies, arthritis, and certain skin or breathing problems.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune reactions.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, preferably with food to reduce stomach irritation. Do not stop treatment suddenly, especially if it has been used for a longer period; the dose may need to be reduced gradually by a doctor.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, swelling due to fluid retention, and increased blood sugar or blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health problems, or any infection. Methylprednisolone can reduce resistance to infection and may mask infection symptoms. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically advised by a doctor. Seek medical advice for signs of infection or severe mood changes.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone succinate injection is used for the short-term treatment of severe inflammation and overactive immune or allergic reactions. It may be prescribed for serious inflammatory, autoimmune, allergic or respiratory conditions when a corticosteroid injection is needed.

How does it work?
It is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation and suppresses excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a doctor or nurse by injection. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the condition and response to treatment. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar or blood pressure, stomach upset, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, increased appetite, fluid retention and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health problems or any current infection. Corticosteroids can reduce resistance to infection and may mask infection symptoms. Avoid live vaccines unless advised by a doctor. Do not stop prolonged treatment suddenly without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and an overactive immune response. It may be prescribed for inflammatory, allergic, autoimmune, skin, joint, respiratory, or other medical conditions, depending on the doctor's assessment.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food or milk to reduce stomach irritation. Do not stop it suddenly, especially after prolonged treatment; the dose may need to be reduced gradually under medical supervision.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, fluid retention, increased blood sugar, and increased blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions, eye problems, or any infection. Methylprednisolone can weaken immunity and may hide signs of infection. Avoid contact with people who have contagious infections and check with the doctor before receiving vaccines, especially live vaccines. Seek medical advice for severe mood changes, vision problems, swelling, or signs of infection.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and suppress overactive immune responses. It may be prescribed for conditions such as severe allergies, asthma flare-ups, arthritis and autoimmune disorders.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and allergic or immune reactions.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with food or milk to reduce stomach upset. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition. Do not stop treatment suddenly without medical advice, especially after prolonged use.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, fluid retention, increased blood sugar and increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health conditions or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body's ability to fight infections; avoid close contact with people who have contagious infections and seek medical advice for fever or other signs of infection. Ask the doctor before receiving vaccines. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Metoclopramide 10 mg is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for certain stomach-emptying problems, such as delayed stomach emptying.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals in the brain that trigger nausea and vomiting. It also helps food move more quickly from the stomach into the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the prescribed dose and timing, and do not use it for longer than recommended. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, restlessness, headache, dizziness and diarrhoea.

Precautions
Do not take it without medical advice if there is stomach or intestinal blockage or bleeding, epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, or a history of involuntary muscle movements caused by medicines. Avoid alcohol because it may increase drowsiness. Seek urgent medical help for uncontrolled movements, muscle stiffness, severe restlessness or unusual facial or tongue movements.

What is it used for?
Metoprolol succinate extended-release is used to treat high blood pressure and certain heart conditions, such as angina (chest pain), fast or irregular heartbeat, and heart failure. The exact use depends on the condition prescribed by the doctor.

How does it work?
It is a beta-blocker that slows the heart rate and reduces the force of the heartbeat. This lowers blood pressure and reduces the heart’s workload.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Tiredness, dizziness, slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, cold hands or feet, nausea, and shortness of breath may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is a very slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, asthma or other breathing problems, diabetes, poor circulation, or heart failure. It may mask some warning signs of low blood sugar. Rise slowly if dizzy, and seek medical advice for fainting, worsening breathing difficulty, swelling, or a very slow heartbeat. Do not stop treatment suddenly.

What is it used for?
Metoprolol extended-release is commonly prescribed to lower high blood pressure and help manage certain heart conditions, including a fast or irregular heartbeat, angina, and heart failure. The exact use depends on the doctor's prescription.

How does it work?
It is a beta-blocker that slows the heart rate and reduces the force of the heartbeat. This lowers blood pressure and reduces the heart's workload.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole; do not crush or chew it. Take it consistently with or without food, as directed. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Tiredness, dizziness, slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, cold hands or feet, nausea, and headache.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about asthma or other breathing problems, a very slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart block, heart failure, diabetes, or circulation problems. It may hide some warning signs of low blood sugar. Avoid driving if dizzy. Do not stop treatment suddenly, as this may worsen heart problems. Tell the doctor about all other medicines being taken, and seek advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Metoprolol extended release is used to lower high blood pressure and help manage certain heart conditions, including fast or irregular heartbeat, angina (heart-related chest pain), and some cases of heart failure. The exact use depends on the doctor's prescription.

How does it work?
It is a beta-blocker that slows the heart rate and reduces the force of the heartbeat. This lowers the heart's workload and can help reduce blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop treatment suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Tiredness, dizziness, slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, cold hands or feet, nausea, and sleep problems may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma or other breathing disease, diabetes, a very slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, circulation problems, heart failure, or liver disease. Metoprolol may hide some warning signs of low blood sugar. Avoid driving if dizzy. Seek medical help for fainting, severe breathing difficulty, or a very slow or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Metoprolol 50 mg + amlodipine 5 mg is used to lower high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed for certain heart-related conditions, such as angina, when considered appropriate by a doctor.

How does it work?
Metoprolol slows the heart rate and reduces the heart's workload. Amlodipine relaxes and widens the blood vessels, helping blood flow more easily and lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop it suddenly without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber's instructions.

Common side effects
Dizziness, tiredness, headache, slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, flushing, nausea and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is a slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart block, heart failure, asthma or other breathing problems. People with diabetes should monitor blood sugar carefully because metoprolol may hide some warning signs of low blood sugar. Rise slowly if dizzy, avoid driving until the effects are known, and inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding or other medicines being used.

What is it used for?
Miconazole 2% is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections. The exact infection and body area treated depend on the product formulation, so use it only for the condition stated on the label or advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It damages the fungal cell membrane, stopping the growth and survival of the fungus.

How to take/use it
Use the product exactly as directed on its label or by a healthcare professional. Follow the instructions for the specific formulation and affected body area. Do not use more often or for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or rash at the application site may occur.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or a worsening rash occurs. Check with a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if the infection does not improve. Do not use if allergic to miconazole or similar antifungal medicines.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat fungal infections that are inflamed, itchy, or irritated. It should be used only for the condition advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

How does it work?
Miconazole stops the growth of fungi. Fluocinolone reduces inflammation, redness, and itching.

How to take/use it
For external skin use only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth, and inside of the vagina. Do not cover the area with a tight dressing unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation, or dryness at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Use only on the affected skin and do not use for longer than prescribed. Do not apply to the face, groin, skin folds, broken skin, or in children unless specifically advised. Avoid self-treating undiagnosed rashes, as the steroid may mask or worsen some infections. Stop and seek medical advice if the infection worsens, spreads, or causes severe irritation.

What is it used for?
Topical minoxidil is used to help treat certain types of hair loss, commonly pattern hair loss.

How does it work?
It helps support hair growth by prolonging the hair-growth phase and increasing activity around hair follicles.

How to take/use it
Apply only to the scalp and exactly as directed on the product label or by a dermatologist. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Scalp irritation, itching, dryness and unwanted hair growth may occur.

Precautions
For external use only. Stop and seek medical advice for chest pain, rapid heartbeat, faintness or swelling. Keep away from children.

What is it used for?
This topical combination is generally used for certain types of pattern hair loss. Confirm the intended use and suitability with a dermatologist.

How does it work?
Minoxidil supports the hair-growth phase. Finasteride reduces conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT), which contributes to pattern hair loss.

How to take/use it
Use on the scalp only as prescribed. Avoid contact with the face, eyes and other people.

Common side effects
Scalp irritation, itching, dryness and unwanted hair growth may occur. Finasteride may cause sexual or other hormonal side effects.

Precautions
Finasteride can harm a developing male foetus; pregnant people should not handle leaking product. Use under dermatology supervision.

What is it used for?
Used to help treat pattern hair loss by slowing hair thinning and supporting hair regrowth on the scalp. It is generally intended for adult men unless specifically prescribed otherwise.

How does it work?
Minoxidil helps stimulate hair follicles and prolongs the hair-growth phase. Finasteride reduces the effect of DHT, a hormone involved in pattern hair loss.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or as stated on the product label. Apply to the scalp as instructed, avoid contact with the eyes and broken or irritated skin, and wash hands after use. Do not apply more than recommended.

Common side effects
Scalp itching, dryness, redness, irritation or flaking; unwanted hair growth on the face or other areas. Sexual side effects or mood changes may occur with finasteride.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor; pregnant women should not handle leaking product. Keep away from children and avoid contact with the eyes. Stop use and seek medical advice for severe scalp irritation, chest pain, fast heartbeat, dizziness, swelling, sexual problems or significant mood changes. Consult a doctor before use if there is heart disease or other significant medical illness.

What is it used for?
Mirabegron is used to treat symptoms of overactive bladder, such as urgency, frequent urination and urge-related leakage.

How does it work?
It relaxes the bladder muscle, allowing the bladder to store more urine.

How to take/use it
Swallow the prolonged-release tablet whole as prescribed. Do not crush or chew it.

Common side effects
Increased blood pressure, headache, urinary tract infection and fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Blood pressure should be monitored. Tell the doctor about urinary retention, kidney or liver problems and other medicines.

What is it used for?
A moisturising lotion intended to help hydrate dry skin. The exact formulation is not supplied.

How does it work?
Moisturisers help reduce water loss from the skin and improve skin softness.

How to take/use it
Apply to the skin as directed on the label; avoid contact with eyes.

Common side effects
Some people may experience irritation or an allergic skin reaction.

Precautions
Check the full ingredient list, especially if there is a known skin sensitivity. Stop use if significant irritation develops.

What is it used for?
Used to moisturise dry or rough skin and help relieve skin dryness and tightness.

How does it work?
It helps hydrate the outer layer of the skin and supports the skin barrier, reducing moisture loss.

How to take/use it
Apply to clean, dry skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Use externally only and avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild stinging, redness, itching or skin irritation may occur, especially on sensitive skin.

Precautions
Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops. Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Avoid applying to infected or seriously damaged skin unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Mometasone 0.1% is a topical corticosteroid used to reduce redness, swelling, itching and irritation in inflammatory skin conditions such as eczema and dermatitis. It may also be prescribed for other steroid-responsive skin conditions.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances in the skin that cause inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid covering the area with a tight dressing unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, dryness or irritation may occur. Prolonged or improper use can cause skin thinning, stretch marks, changes in skin colour or worsening of a skin infection.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and broken skin. Do not use on the face, groin, armpits or on infected skin unless specifically advised by a doctor. Use in children, on large skin areas or for prolonged periods only under medical supervision. Seek medical advice if the condition worsens, spreads or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Used for inflamed skin conditions, such as infected eczema or dermatitis, where there is also a bacterial skin infection. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Mometasone reduces skin inflammation, redness and itching. Fusidic acid is an antibiotic that helps control susceptible bacterial infections on the skin.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before and after application, unless the hands are being treated. For external use only; avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not cover the area with a dressing unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, irritation, dryness or redness at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Do not use on untreated fungal or viral skin infections, acne or rosacea unless specifically advised. Avoid prolonged use and use on the face, skin folds, groin or in children unless directed by a doctor. Stop use and seek medical advice if the skin infection worsens, spreads or does not improve. Avoid using more than prescribed, as fusidic acid resistance and steroid-related skin problems may occur.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to help prevent and control breathing symptoms in asthma and other obstructive airway conditions, such as wheezing, chest tightness and difficulty breathing. It may also help with allergy-related nasal symptoms. It is not used for immediate relief during a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
Montelukast blocks substances that cause airway inflammation and narrowing. Acebrophylline helps relax the airways and loosen mucus, making breathing easier.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Use it regularly as directed, even when symptoms are controlled. Keep a quick-relief inhaler available if prescribed.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, dizziness and vomiting may occur. Palpitations or a fast heartbeat can occur less commonly.

Precautions
This medicine does not treat a sudden asthma attack. Seek medical help for severe or worsening breathing difficulty. Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart rhythm problems, seizure disorders or other medicines being used. Montelukast may rarely cause mood or behaviour changes, sleep problems or suicidal thoughts; report these promptly. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness occurs.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergies such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, nasal itching, and itchy or watery eyes. It may also be prescribed as an add-on treatment for asthma, but it does not relieve a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, chemicals that can cause airway and nasal inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Do not use it as a rescue medicine for sudden breathing difficulty.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, headache, tiredness, dry mouth, stomach pain, or nausea.

Precautions
Drowsiness may occur; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Contact a doctor promptly if unusual mood or behaviour changes, nightmares, agitation, depression, or thoughts of self-harm occur. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for sudden or severe breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, nasal itching and watery or itchy eyes.

How does it work?
Montelukast blocks substances that contribute to allergy-related inflammation, while levocetirizine blocks histamine, which causes allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Regular use should follow the prescriber's instructions.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, stomach discomfort or nausea may occur.

Precautions
This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known, and avoid alcohol. Seek medical advice if unusual changes in mood or behaviour, disturbed sleep, depression or suicidal thoughts occur. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. It is not intended for immediate relief of a sudden asthma attack.

What is it used for?
Chlorhexidine mouthwash is an antiseptic used to reduce harmful bacteria in the mouth and help manage plaque and gum inflammation (gingivitis). It may also be recommended after some dental procedures.

How does it work?
It kills or reduces many bacteria in the mouth by damaging their cell membranes and remains active on oral surfaces for some time.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a dentist. Rinse the mouth with the recommended amount and spit it out; do not swallow. Do not mix it with other mouthwashes unless advised.

Common side effects
Temporary staining of the teeth or tongue, altered taste, mouth irritation, dryness, or increased tartar may occur.

Precautions
Do not swallow. Chlorhexidine mouthwash is generally intended for short-term use unless a dentist advises otherwise. Toothpaste may reduce its action, so follow the product instructions regarding the timing of brushing and rinsing. Stop use and seek urgent medical help if swelling, breathing difficulty, or other signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
Used to treat bacterial eye infections when there is also redness and inflammation. It should be used only when prescribed by an eye-care professional.

How does it work?
Moxifloxacin is an antibiotic that stops the growth of bacteria. Loteprednol is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation, redness and swelling in the eye.

How to take/use it
Use in the affected eye(s) exactly as prescribed. Shake the bottle well if it is a suspension, and wash hands before use. Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface. Remove contact lenses before use and restart them only as advised. If using other eye drops, leave an appropriate gap between them.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging or burning, eye irritation, blurred vision, watering, or increased sensitivity to light may occur. Prolonged use may increase eye pressure or delay healing.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice, especially if the eye infection may be viral or fungal, as steroids can worsen or mask these infections. Tell the doctor about glaucoma, eye surgery, or other eye problems. Seek medical advice if pain, redness, swelling, vision changes or the infection worsens. Avoid driving until temporary blurred vision clears.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ear, nose, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor and complete the full course, even if feeling better. It may be taken with or without food; take it with water. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to amoxycillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, or a severe skin rash. Contact a doctor for severe or persistent diarrhoea, especially during or after treatment. Tell the doctor about kidney problems and all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Amoxicillin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ears, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from making their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the capsule with water; it may generally be taken with or without food. Do not share leftover antibiotics or skip doses.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to amoxicillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, glandular fever (mononucleosis), pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Moxifloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the lungs, sinuses, skin and abdomen. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking enzymes needed for bacterial DNA replication and repair.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water, with or without food, if this is the prescribed form. Do not take it together with antacids or supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, iron, calcium or zinc; ask a pharmacist or doctor about suitable spacing.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and vomiting may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, palpitations, fainting, rash or breathing difficulty. Tell the doctor about heart rhythm problems, tendon disorders, seizures, myasthenia gravis, diabetes, aortic aneurysm risk, kidney or liver problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all medicines being taken. Avoid driving if dizzy or affected. Use only when prescribed, because unnecessary antibiotic use can cause resistance.

What is it used for?
This combination is generally used for bacterial eye infections that are accompanied by inflammation. It should be used only when prescribed by an eye-care professional.

How does it work?
Moxifloxacin is an antibiotic that stops the growth of susceptible bacteria. Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces eye inflammation, redness and swelling.

How to take/use it
Use in the affected eye(s) exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before use and do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface. Do not use it for longer than prescribed. If symptoms do not improve or worsen, seek medical advice.

Common side effects
Temporary burning or stinging, eye irritation, redness, blurred vision or discomfort may occur after use.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, as the steroid component may worsen some viral or fungal eye infections, delay healing or increase eye pressure. Tell the doctor about glaucoma, an eye injury or recent eye surgery. Remove contact lenses before use and ask when they can be worn again. Seek urgent care for severe eye pain, worsening vision, marked swelling or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Moxifloxacin 0.5% eye drops are used to treat bacterial eye infections, such as bacterial conjunctivitis. They do not treat viral or fungal eye infections.

How does it work?
Moxifloxacin is an antibiotic that stops susceptible bacteria from multiplying, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use in the affected eye(s) exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before use, avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or any surface, and complete the prescribed course. Do not use it in the mouth or swallow it. Remove contact lenses before use unless advised otherwise by a doctor.

Common side effects
Temporary eye irritation, stinging, redness, discomfort, itching or blurred vision may occur after application.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to moxifloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics. Seek medical help for severe eye pain, swelling, rash, breathing difficulty, worsening symptoms or vision changes. Use only under medical advice in children, during pregnancy or while breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This eye medicine is commonly used after eye surgery, such as cataract surgery, to help prevent or treat bacterial eye infection and reduce inflammation and discomfort.

How does it work?
Moxifloxacin is an antibiotic that stops the growth of bacteria. Ketorolac is an anti-inflammatory medicine that helps reduce pain, redness and swelling in the eye.

How to take/use it
Use only in the eye and exactly as prescribed by the eye specialist. Wash hands before use, do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or other surfaces, and keep the container closed after use. Do not wear contact lenses unless specifically advised.

Common side effects
Temporary burning or stinging, eye irritation, redness, itching, dry eye or blurred vision may occur after application.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to moxifloxacin, ketorolac or similar medicines. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent eye pain, worsening redness, reduced vision, marked swelling or unusual discharge. Tell the eye specialist about corneal problems, diabetes, bleeding disorders, previous eye surgery or use of steroid eye drops. Do not use for longer than prescribed.

What is it used for?
Montelukast is used to help prevent and control asthma symptoms, including symptoms triggered by exercise. It may also help relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, a blocked or runny nose, and itchy nose. It is not a rescue medicine for a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
It blocks leukotrienes, substances involved in airway swelling, tightening and allergy symptoms. This helps keep the airways more open and reduces inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Do not take extra doses, and do not use it instead of a prescribed rescue inhaler during a sudden asthma attack. Continue other asthma medicines unless the prescriber advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Headache, stomach pain, nausea and diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Stop the medicine and seek medical advice promptly if there are significant mood or behaviour changes, unusual dreams, sleep problems, anxiety, depression or thoughts of self-harm. Tell the prescriber about any previous mental health problems, allergies or liver disease. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used mainly to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It may also be prescribed as part of treatment to help prevent asthma symptoms, but it does not provide quick relief during an asthma attack.

How does it work?
Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, chemicals that contribute to allergy and airway inflammation. Levocetirizine blocks histamine, which helps reduce common allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor, at the recommended time, and do not take more than directed. Use it regularly if prescribed for prevention. Do not use it as a substitute for a fast-acting rescue inhaler.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or tiredness, headache, dry mouth, nausea, and stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Levocetirizine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or alcohol until its effect is known. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, liver disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if unusual mood or behaviour changes, nightmares, anxiety, depression, or suicidal thoughts occur. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty or swelling of the face, lips, or throat.

What is it used for?
Used mainly to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itching, and watery eyes.

How does it work?
Montelukast blocks substances called leukotrienes that contribute to allergy-related inflammation. Levocetirizine blocks histamine, reducing allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Swallow with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. This medicine is not a rescue treatment for a sudden asthma attack.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, headache, tiredness, dry mouth, nausea, and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Avoid driving or operating machinery if drowsy, and avoid alcohol as it may increase sleepiness. Inform the doctor about kidney disease or other medicines being taken. Stop the medicine and seek medical advice if unusual mood or behaviour changes, disturbing dreams, agitation, depression, or suicidal thoughts occur.

What is it used for?
Acetylcysteine is a mucolytic used to loosen thick, sticky mucus in the airways, making phlegm easier to cough up. It may be used for chesty or productive coughs associated with respiratory conditions.

How does it work?
It breaks down the structure of thick mucus, reducing its stickiness and making it easier to clear from the airways.

How to take/use it
Dissolve the effervescent tablet completely in a glass of water and drink it immediately. Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not swallow the tablet whole.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, skin rash and indigestion may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to acetylcysteine. Use with caution if there is asthma or a history of stomach ulcers. Avoid taking it with cough-suppressant medicines unless advised by a doctor, as these may prevent mucus from being cleared. Seek medical advice if breathing difficulty, wheezing or a severe allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
