What is it used for?
This medicine is used for asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), bronchitis and other breathing conditions with thick mucus and narrowed airways. It helps loosen mucus and makes breathing easier.

How does it work?
Acetylcysteine breaks down and loosens thick mucus in the airways. Acebrophylline helps relax the airway muscles and improve airflow.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the instructions on the label and do not change the dose or duration yourself. Take with water and do not stop treatment without medical advice. This medicine is not meant to provide immediate relief during a sudden severe breathing attack unless specifically advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and palpitations may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to acetylcysteine, acebrophylline or similar medicines. Inform the doctor if there is heart disease or an irregular heartbeat, low blood pressure, liver or kidney disease, stomach ulcer, seizure disorder, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for severe breathing difficulty, facial or throat swelling, or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
The exact use of this combination cannot be reliably determined from the ingredient names alone. It should be used only for the condition and duration recommended by a doctor or pharmacist.

How does it work?
Acetylcysteine can help reduce oxidative stress and may loosen mucus. Pyridoxamine is a form of vitamin B6. The combined therapeutic effect depends on the specific product and condition being treated.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache or skin rash.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma, a history of stomach ulcers, liver or kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if a rash, breathing difficulty or severe vomiting occurs. Avoid prolonged or unnecessary use of vitamin B6-containing products unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
The supplied ingredients do not reliably identify the approved use of this specific combination. Acetysetine may refer to acetylcysteine, which is used in some medicines to loosen mucus and in hospitals for paracetamol overdose; however, this product should not be assumed to be for either use without checking its pack or a pharmacist's advice.

How does it work?
If Acetysetine is acetylcysteine, it can help loosen thick mucus and supports the body's antioxidant glutathione system. Taurine is an amino-acid-like nutrient, but the purpose of this combination cannot be confirmed from the generic information alone.

How to take/use it
Use only according to the product label or the prescriber's instructions. Do not use it to treat paracetamol overdose; that requires urgent medical care and a specific treatment regimen.

Common side effects
If the product contains acetylcysteine, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort or rash may occur. The side effects of this specific combination cannot be confirmed from the information provided.

Precautions
Check the pack or ask a pharmacist before use if there is asthma, a history of stomach ulcer, medicine allergy, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Do not rely on this product for suspected paracetamol overdose.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful acidity, heartburn and acid-related indigestion. It may also help relieve burning or discomfort associated with stomach irritation.

How does it work?
Aluminium hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide neutralise excess stomach acid. Oxetacaine is a local anaesthetic that helps reduce pain and burning in the stomach or food pipe.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with the supplied measuring device. Do not take it for a prolonged period without medical advice.

Common side effects
Constipation or loose stools, nausea, stomach discomfort, and changes in bowel movements may occur. Temporary numbness of the mouth or throat is possible.

Precautions
Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if there is kidney disease, persistent or severe stomach pain, repeated vomiting, difficulty swallowing, black stools or vomiting blood. Antacids can affect the absorption of other medicines; separate this product from other medicines as advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or keep returning.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary supplement to provide vitamins, minerals, antioxidant nutrients and ginseng when dietary intake may be inadequate. It is not intended to treat a specific disease unless advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
The vitamins and minerals support normal body functions, while antioxidant nutrients help protect cells from oxidative damage. Ginseng is a herbal ingredient traditionally used as a general supplement.

How to take/use it
Take the soft gel exactly as directed on the product label. Swallow it whole with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Avoid taking other multivitamin or mineral supplements at the same time unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include nausea, stomach upset, headache, or difficulty sleeping. Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is diabetes, a bleeding disorder, or any ongoing medical condition. Ginseng may interact with some medicines, including blood thinners and diabetes medicines. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Mupirocin 2% is a topical antibiotic used to treat bacterial skin infections, including impetigo and infected minor cuts, wounds or scratches.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins needed for their growth and survival.

How to take/use it
Use only on the skin and apply as directed by the doctor or product label. Clean and dry the affected area before use, wash hands before and after applying it, and avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose unless specifically prescribed for that use. Do not share the medicine or cover the area unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or rash where it is applied.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to mupirocin or any ingredient. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a widespread rash develops. Avoid prolonged or repeated use unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve as expected.

What is it used for?
Mupirocin 2% is a topical antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial skin infections, such as impetigo and infected minor cuts or wounds.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents them from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only on the skin and apply exactly as prescribed. Clean and dry the affected area before application. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose unless specifically prescribed for that use. Wash hands before and after applying it, unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation where it is applied. Allergic rash can occur rarely.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to mupirocin or any ingredient. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or a widespread rash occurs. Do not use for longer than directed, as prolonged use may allow other organisms to grow. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve.

What is it used for?
A multivitamin injection may be used to provide vitamins when oral supplementation is unsuitable or when clinically indicated. The exact formulation is not supplied.

How does it work?
It provides vitamins required for normal metabolic and body functions; the specific action depends on the ingredients.

How to take/use it
Must be administered by a healthcare professional according to the prescribed formulation and dose.

Common side effects
Depend on the ingredients and route; injection-site reactions or allergic reactions may occur.

Precautions
Confirm the complete vitamin composition and route. Use only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Naproxen is used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness caused by muscle or joint problems, arthritis and other inflammatory conditions. It may also be prescribed for short-term pain, such as period pain or gout attacks.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or just after food and a full glass of water. Swallow the tablet whole unless advised otherwise. Do not take more than prescribed or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless a doctor advises it.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, headache, dizziness and drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest pain, breathing difficulty or a severe skin rash. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed, especially after 20 weeks and in the last trimester. Check with a doctor before use with blood thinners, steroids, aspirin or other medicines that can irritate the stomach or affect the kidneys.

What is it used for?
Naproxen is used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness in conditions affecting the muscles and joints, including arthritis. It may also be prescribed for other short-term painful conditions, such as menstrual pain.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine (NSAID). It reduces the production of chemicals in the body that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food and with a full glass of water. Do not take more than recommended or combine it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea or constipation, headache, dizziness and drowsiness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAIDs. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised, especially from 20 weeks onwards and during the last trimester. Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, chest pain or a serious skin rash. Tell the doctor about blood thinners, steroids, aspirin, other painkillers, medicines for blood pressure, lithium or methotrexate.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve migraine headaches and associated nausea or vomiting.

How does it work?
Naproxen reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Domperidone helps control nausea and vomiting and supports movement of the stomach.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow with water, preferably with or after food, and do not exceed the recommended dose. Do not use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, heartburn, dizziness, headache, or dry mouth. Naproxen may rarely cause stomach ulcers or bleeding.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is an allergy to naproxen, aspirin, or other NSAIDs, or a history of stomach ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding. Tell the doctor about kidney, liver, heart, or blood-pressure problems, asthma triggered by painkillers, or heart-rhythm problems. Domperidone may affect heart rhythm and can interact with some medicines. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless specifically prescribed. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, fainting, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Nebivolol is used mainly to treat high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed for certain heart conditions, including some cases of heart failure, under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It is a beta-blocker that slows the heart rate and reduces the force of the heartbeat, helping lower blood pressure. It may also help blood vessels relax.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day, with or without food. Do not stop taking it suddenly without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the prescriber or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, tiredness, nausea, diarrhoea, and a slow heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma or breathing difficulty, a slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart block, diabetes, circulation problems, or liver disease. Nebivolol may mask some warning signs of low blood sugar. Seek medical advice for severe dizziness, fainting, breathing difficulty, swelling, or an unusually slow heartbeat. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
This herbal juice is used as a supportive product for blood sugar management in people with diabetes. It should not replace prescribed diabetes medicines, a balanced diet, exercise or regular blood sugar monitoring.

How does it work?
Neem, karela, jamun and giloy are traditionally used in herbal medicine for blood sugar support. Their effects can vary, and they are not a substitute for proven diabetes treatment.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount. People taking diabetes medicines should monitor their blood sugar regularly and consult a healthcare professional before use.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, stomach discomfort or loose motions. It may also contribute to low blood sugar, especially when used with diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use if pregnant or breastfeeding, if there is liver disease, or if taking medicines for diabetes. Stop use and seek medical advice if symptoms of low blood sugar occur, such as sweating, shaking, dizziness or confusion. Do not stop prescribed diabetes treatment without medical advice.

What is it used for?
The specific use cannot be determined from the ingredient information alone. Neem extract and aloe vera extract are used in different products, including topical skin preparations and oral herbal products. Check the product label or a healthcare professional for the intended use.

How does it work?
The effects depend on the formulation and route of use. Aloe vera may soothe and moisturise skin, while neem may have antimicrobial properties, but the product-specific action cannot be confirmed from the supplied information.

How to take/use it
Use only according to the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions. Do not use it orally or apply it to the skin unless the product is specifically intended for that route.

Common side effects
Possible effects include skin irritation, redness, itching or allergic reactions, especially after topical use. Other side effects depend on the formulation.

Precautions
Check the ingredients for allergies. For topical products, test a small area first and stop use if irritation occurs. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not apply to broken skin unless advised. Seek professional advice before use in children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if the product is intended for oral use.

What is it used for?
Nepafenac eye suspension is used to reduce eye pain and inflammation after cataract surgery. Use it only for the eye condition and duration prescribed by the eye specialist.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine that reduces the production of chemicals responsible for pain and inflammation in the eye.

How to take/use it
Shake the bottle well before use. Put the prescribed number of drops into the affected eye(s), following the eye specialist’s instructions. Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface. Close the bottle after use and do not wear contact lenses unless advised by the eye specialist.

Common side effects
Temporary burning or stinging, eye irritation, redness, itching, watering, eye pain or blurred vision may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to nepafenac, aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines. Use with caution if there is a history of bleeding problems, corneal disease, dry eyes or previous eye surgery. Do not use it for longer than prescribed, as prolonged use may delay healing or affect the cornea. Seek medical attention for severe eye pain, worsening redness, discharge, marked vision changes or persistent irritation.

What is it used for?
Vitamin B Complex with B12 is used to prevent or treat B-vitamin deficiencies and to support normal energy metabolism, nerve function and red blood cell formation. It is not a substitute for treatment of a specific medical condition unless advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
B vitamins act as nutrients and coenzymes that help the body use food for energy and support the normal function of nerves and blood cells. Vitamin B12 is especially important for healthy nerve function and red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If it is being used to treat a confirmed deficiency, follow the prescribed treatment plan.

Common side effects
Mild nausea, stomach discomfort or headache may occur. Urine may become bright yellow with some B-vitamin products; this is usually harmless.

Precautions
Check with a healthcare professional before use if pregnant, breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or use of other medicines. Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Seek medical advice if symptoms of vitamin deficiency continue or worsen.

What is it used for?
Nicorandil is used to help prevent and reduce chest pain caused by stable angina, a heart condition in which the heart muscle does not receive enough oxygen-rich blood.

How does it work?
It widens the blood vessels, helping improve blood flow to the heart and reducing the workload on the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, at the same times each day. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop it suddenly without medical advice. It is generally used for prevention and is not a replacement for prescribed emergency treatment for sudden chest pain.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, weakness, flushing, nausea and vomiting. Mouth ulcers may also occur.

Precautions
It may lower blood pressure and cause dizziness, especially when standing up. Do not use it with medicines for erectile dysfunction, such as sildenafil or tadalafil, or with riociguat, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about any persistent or unusual ulcers, including ulcers in the mouth, stomach, intestines, skin or eyes. Seek urgent medical help for severe or worsening chest pain, fainting or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Nicoumalone is an anticoagulant used to prevent and treat harmful blood clots. It may be prescribed for conditions such as irregular heartbeat, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism or artificial heart valves.

How does it work?
It reduces the action of vitamin K, which the body needs to make certain clotting proteins. This makes the blood less likely to form harmful clots.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Regular blood tests, usually INR tests, are needed to check its effect. Do not change the dose, stop treatment, or take a missed dose without medical advice. Keep vitamin K-rich foods reasonably consistent and inform the doctor about all medicines, supplements and herbal products.

Common side effects
Easy bruising, nosebleeds, bleeding from the gums, prolonged bleeding from cuts, heavier menstrual bleeding, nausea or stomach upset.

Precautions
Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, vomiting blood, black stools, blood in urine, severe headache or a serious injury. Tell the doctor before surgery or dental treatment, and if there is liver disease, a bleeding disorder, stomach ulcer or a recent injury. Many medicines, including some painkillers and antibiotics, can interact with nicoumalone. Avoid starting aspirin or other blood-thinning medicines unless prescribed. It is generally avoided during pregnancy unless specifically directed by a specialist.

What is it used for?
Nicorandil is used to prevent and reduce episodes of angina (heart-related chest pain) caused by reduced blood flow to the heart.

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens the blood vessels, helping improve blood flow to the heart and reducing the heart’s workload.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at regular times. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment suddenly without medical advice. Do not take an extra dose if one is missed; follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, flushing, weakness and low blood pressure may occur. Headaches are often more noticeable when treatment begins.

Precautions
Do not use with medicines for erectile dysfunction such as sildenafil, tadalafil or vardenafil, or with riociguat, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor if there is low blood pressure, heart disease or a history of stomach, intestinal, mouth or skin ulcers. Seek medical attention for persistent or unusual ulcers, severe dizziness or fainting.

What is it used for?
Nifedipine SR is used to treat high blood pressure and to help prevent or relieve angina (chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart).

How does it work?
It is a calcium-channel blocker that relaxes and widens blood vessels. This lowers blood pressure and improves blood flow to the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the SR tablet whole with water; do not crush, chew or break it. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, flushing, dizziness, palpitations, constipation, and swelling of the ankles or feet.

Precautions
It may cause dizziness, especially when starting treatment; take care when driving or standing up. Tell the doctor about low blood pressure, heart problems, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid grapefruit or grapefruit juice unless advised otherwise. Seek urgent medical help for severe dizziness, fainting, worsening chest pain or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain parasitic worm infections, including some intestinal worm infections. It should be used only for the infection diagnosed or suspected by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Albendazole damages the worms' ability to use nutrients and survive. Ivermectin affects the nervous system of susceptible parasites, helping to paralyse and eliminate them.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with the provided measuring device. Do not change the dose or stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver disease or a history of allergy to either medicine. Avoid self-medication, especially in children. Seek medical help for severe rash, breathing difficulty, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or persistent vomiting.

What is it used for?
Nimesulide 100 mg is used for short-term relief of pain, swelling and fever, including pain related to muscles, joints or arthritis. It should be used only as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine (NSAID) that reduces the production of substances involved in pain, swelling and fever.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food. Do not use it for longer than advised, and do not take more than the prescribed amount. Avoid taking it with other painkillers or anti-inflammatory medicines unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is liver disease, stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney or heart disease, or an allergy to NSAID painkillers. Avoid alcohol. Stop taking it and seek medical help if yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, unusual tiredness, severe stomach pain, black stools, breathing difficulty or facial swelling occurs. Tell the doctor if pregnant, breastfeeding, or taking other medicines.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for short-term relief of common cold symptoms such as fever, headache, body aches, blocked or runny nose, sneezing and nasal congestion.

How does it work?
Paracetamol and nimesulide help reduce fever and pain. Phenylephrine helps relieve nasal congestion, while CPM (chlorpheniramine) helps reduce runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended, and do not combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol, nimesulide, phenylephrine or chlorpheniramine. Avoid alcohol and use caution when driving if drowsiness occurs.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, stomach upset, headache, palpitations or a rise in blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor if there is liver or kidney disease, stomach ulcer, high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, prostate problems or alcohol use. Avoid use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised. Stop and seek medical advice for severe skin reactions, breathing difficulty, persistent vomiting, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe abdominal pain.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and fever, such as body pain, muscle or joint pain, dental pain, headache and period pain.

How does it work?
Nimesulide reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor, preferably with or after food, and swallow with water. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or painkillers such as NSAIDs unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is liver disease, severe kidney disease, stomach ulcer or previous allergy to painkillers, unless specifically prescribed. Avoid alcohol. Stop taking it and seek medical help if yellowing of the eyes or skin, dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual bleeding, rash or breathing difficulty occurs. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and fever, such as body pain, muscle or joint pain, dental pain and other painful conditions as directed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Nimesulide helps reduce inflammation and pain, while paracetamol helps relieve pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed or according to the package instructions. It is usually taken with or after food to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol, nimesulide or similar painkillers unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or skin rash.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is liver disease, severe kidney disease, stomach ulcer or bleeding, or an allergy to painkillers, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Avoid alcohol because of the risk of liver damage. Seek medical advice for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual bleeding or an allergic reaction. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should use it only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Nitrofurantoin is an antibiotic used mainly to treat bacterial urinary tract infections (UTIs), including bladder infections. It does not treat viral infections.

How does it work?
It damages essential parts of susceptible bacteria, stopping them from growing and surviving in the urinary tract.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Taking it with food or milk may help reduce stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, diarrhoea, headache, and stomach discomfort may occur. Urine may become dark yellow or brown, which is usually harmless.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, liver disease, lung disease, anaemia, G6PD deficiency, or a history of nerve problems. Nitrofurantoin may not be suitable near the end of pregnancy or for some newborns. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, persistent cough, yellowing of the skin or eyes, numbness or tingling, severe diarrhoea, or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Norfloxacin is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, especially urinary tract infections and some bacterial intestinal infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the enzymes needed for their growth and multiplication, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water and follow the product or prescriber’s instructions about food. Keep it separate from antacids and mineral supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc, as these can reduce absorption. Do not self-medicate.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and altered taste may occur.

Precautions
Stop taking it and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nervous-system changes, rash, breathing difficulty or other signs of a serious allergic reaction. Use only on medical advice during pregnancy, breastfeeding, in children, or if there is a history of tendon problems, seizures, heart-rhythm problems or kidney disease. Avoid unnecessary strenuous exercise during treatment and shortly afterwards. It may increase sensitivity to sunlight.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat certain infectious diarrhoea and loose motions caused by susceptible bacteria or intestinal parasites. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Norfloxacin stops susceptible bacteria from multiplying. Tinidazole damages the DNA of certain bacteria and intestinal parasites, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water and do not self-medicate or share this medicine. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 3 days after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and a metallic or bitter taste.

Precautions
Avoid use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, tendon disorders, nerve problems, heart rhythm problems, or allergies to quinolone antibiotics. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash, breathing difficulty, or palpitations. Keep well hydrated during diarrhoea and follow medical advice regarding other medicines and supplements, especially antacids or mineral supplements.

What is it used for?
Oxymetazoline nasal spray is a decongestant used for short-term relief of a blocked nose. The stated strength and paediatric suitability should be verified.

How does it work?
It narrows swollen blood vessels in the nasal passages, reducing congestion.

How to take/use it
Use only the age-appropriate product and dose stated on the label or prescribed. Do not use for longer than directed, as congestion can worsen with prolonged use.

Common side effects
Nasal dryness, irritation, sneezing or burning may occur.

Precautions
Confirm the concentration and age range before use in a child. Seek advice for children with underlying conditions or if symptoms persist.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to help prevent or treat minor bacterial infections in cuts, scrapes and minor burns.

How does it work?
It contains three antibiotics that work together to stop the growth of many bacteria on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after use. Do not use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Mild irritation, redness, itching or rash at the application site. Allergic skin reactions can occur, especially with neomycin.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not apply to large, deep or serious wounds, or extensive areas of skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a worsening rash occurs. Seek medical care for spreading redness, increasing pain, pus or fever. Do not use if allergic to any of its ingredients.

What is it used for?
Long-acting nitroglycerin is used to help prevent episodes of angina (chest pain due to reduced blood flow to the heart).

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens blood vessels, reducing the workload on the heart.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed. Controlled-release products must be taken according to their specific instructions and should not be crushed or altered unless the product information allows it.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, flushing and low blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Never combine with sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil or riociguat. It is for prevention, not immediate relief of an acute chest-pain attack. Seek urgent care for new or severe chest pain.

What is it used for?
Nitroglycerin controlled-release medicine is used to prevent and reduce episodes of angina (chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart). It is not intended to provide quick relief during a sudden angina attack.

How does it work?
It widens the blood vessels, helping more blood reach the heart and reducing the heart’s workload and oxygen demand.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the controlled-release form whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. For sudden or worsening chest pain, seek urgent medical care and use any prescribed fast-acting angina medicine as directed.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, flushing, weakness, nausea, and low blood pressure may occur. A fast heartbeat or fainting can also occur, especially if blood pressure falls.

Precautions
Do not use with sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil, or other medicines for erectile dysfunction, or with riociguat, unless specifically approved by a doctor, as this can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure. Use caution with low blood pressure, dehydration, anaemia, or heart conditions. Avoid alcohol if it worsens dizziness or low blood pressure. Rise slowly and seek urgent help for severe or worsening chest pain, fainting, or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 200 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the urinary tract, respiratory system, skin and other tissues, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the enzymes they need to grow and multiply, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with a full glass of water, and complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or mineral supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, calcium, iron or zinc; follow the separation advice provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and sleep disturbance.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, seizures, heart rhythm problems, tendon disorders, diabetes or nerve problems, and all medicines being taken. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe diarrhoea, or signs of a serious allergic reaction. Avoid unnecessary strong sunlight. It is generally avoided during pregnancy, breastfeeding and in children unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 200 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the urinary tract, lungs, skin, or other body areas. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin stops bacteria from making and repairing their genetic material, which prevents the bacteria from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water and do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, iron, calcium, or zinc; follow the advised time gap. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, and difficulty sleeping may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, a severe rash, breathing difficulty, or persistent watery or bloody diarrhoea. Use only on medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding, in children, older adults, or people with kidney disease, seizures, heart rhythm problems, or myasthenia gravis. Avoid unnecessary intense exercise during treatment and tell the doctor about all medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 200 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as urinary tract, respiratory, skin and other infections when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops bacteria from making the enzymes they need to grow and survive, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with water, and complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc; follow the timing advice provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, headache, dizziness and difficulty sleeping.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ofloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nervous-system changes, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only on medical advice during pregnancy, breastfeeding, childhood, or in people with kidney disease, seizures, heart-rhythm problems or myasthenia gravis. Avoid driving if dizzy or if vision or alertness is affected.

What is it used for?
Olanzapine is a prescription medicine used to treat schizophrenia and episodes of bipolar disorder.

How does it work?
It acts on dopamine and serotonin receptors in the brain to help regulate mood, thinking and behaviour.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed. The MD formulation is designed to dissolve in the mouth; follow the pack instructions.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, weight gain, increased appetite, dizziness and constipation may occur.

Precautions
May affect blood sugar, cholesterol and weight. Avoid alcohol and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Olanzapine is an antipsychotic medicine used to treat schizophrenia and episodes of mania associated with bipolar disorder. It may also be used to help prevent further mood episodes in bipolar disorder, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It helps balance certain chemical messengers in the brain, especially dopamine and serotonin. This can reduce symptoms such as hallucinations, unusual thoughts, agitation and severe mood changes.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor, at the recommended time, with or without food. Do not stop it suddenly or change the dose without medical advice. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, increased appetite, weight gain, dry mouth, constipation, dizziness, restlessness and swelling of the hands or feet. It may also increase blood sugar and cholesterol levels.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high cholesterol, heart disease, seizures, liver problems or a history of stroke. Weight, blood sugar and cholesterol may need monitoring. Avoid alcohol because it can worsen sleepiness and dizziness. Older adults with dementia-related psychosis have an increased risk of serious side effects and death with this medicine. Seek urgent medical help for severe muscle stiffness with fever, uncontrolled movements, fainting or signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Olmesartan 20 mg + amlodipine 5 mg is used to lower high blood pressure (hypertension). Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and other blood pressure-related complications.

How does it work?
Olmesartan relaxes blood vessels by blocking the action of a hormone that narrows them. Amlodipine also relaxes and widens blood vessels, helping blood flow more easily and lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop it without medical advice, even if feeling well. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, flushing, palpitations, nausea and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur. Contact a doctor if these effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, dehydration, low blood pressure, or a history of swelling of the face or throat with blood-pressure medicines. Regular monitoring of blood pressure and kidney function may be advised. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically directed by a doctor, and inform the doctor about all other medicines, including potassium supplements and painkillers such as ibuprofen. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips or tongue or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Olmesartan 20 mg is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It helps lower the risk of complications caused by uncontrolled blood pressure.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of angiotensin II, a substance that narrows blood vessels. This relaxes the blood vessels and helps lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Do not stop taking it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, nausea, diarrhoea and tiredness may occur. Contact a doctor if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, or use of potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes. It may cause dizziness, especially when starting treatment. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Regular blood pressure, kidney function and potassium monitoring may be recommended.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to lower high blood pressure (hypertension). Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of complications such as heart attack and stroke.

How does it work?
Olmesartan blocks the action of a hormone that narrows blood vessels. Amlodipine relaxes and widens blood vessels, helping blood flow more easily and lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop it or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, flushing, and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur. Low blood pressure can also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, or heart problems. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing. This medicine should not be used during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Olmesartan 40 mg with hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension), helping reduce the risk of related heart and blood vessel problems.

How does it work?
Olmesartan relaxes and widens blood vessels by blocking the action of angiotensin II. Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic that helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water from the body, lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop treatment without medical advice. Regular blood pressure checks and blood tests may be recommended.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, increased urination, nausea, and changes in blood potassium or sodium levels may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, diabetes, gout, or previous reactions to similar medicines. Avoid becoming dehydrated, especially during vomiting, diarrhoea, or excessive sweating. This medicine should not be used during pregnancy; seek medical advice immediately if pregnancy occurs. Report severe dizziness, fainting, swelling of the face or throat, or very little urine promptly.

What is it used for?
Olmisartan 40 mg is used to treat high blood pressure. Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and kidney problems.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of a substance called angiotensin II, which normally narrows blood vessels. This helps the blood vessels relax and lowers blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Swallow with water and do not stop it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, nausea and diarrhoea may occur. Contact a doctor if side effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, or medicines and supplements that increase potassium. Blood pressure, kidney function and potassium levels may need monitoring. Do not use during pregnancy; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips or throat or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to lower high blood pressure (hypertension). Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of complications such as heart attack and stroke.

How does it work?
Olmesartan relaxes and widens blood vessels, helping blood flow more easily. Chlorthalidone helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water from the body, reducing the pressure inside the blood vessels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular blood pressure checks and blood tests may be needed to monitor kidney function and blood salts.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, increased urination, nausea, dehydration, and changes in blood salts such as low sodium or potassium may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, diabetes, gout, or previous low sodium or potassium levels. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. This medicine should not be used during pregnancy, especially after the first trimester, unless specifically directed by a doctor. Seek medical advice for severe dizziness, fainting, marked weakness, muscle cramps, or swelling of the face or throat.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension), especially when treatment with more than one blood-pressure medicine is needed.

How does it work?
Olmesartan relaxes blood vessels, while amlodipine widens them to improve blood flow. Hydrochlorothiazide helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water, lowering the amount of fluid in the body and reducing blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may usually be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, ankle or foot swelling, increased urination, nausea, and mild stomach upset.

Precautions
Monitor blood pressure regularly. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, gout, diabetes, or low sodium or potassium levels. Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically advised; olmesartan can harm an unborn baby. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless recommended by a doctor. Blood tests may be needed to check kidney function and electrolyte levels. Seek urgent help for severe dizziness, fainting, or swelling of the face, lips, or tongue.

What is it used for?
Olopatadine 0.1% eye drops are used to relieve itching, redness and watering caused by allergic conjunctivitis, also called eye allergy.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions, and helps reduce the release of allergy-causing substances in the eye.

How to take/use it
Use in the eyes exactly as directed on the product label or by the doctor. Wash hands before use and do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface. Remove contact lenses before use and follow the product instructions about when to put them back in. If using other eye drops, ask a healthcare professional about the suitable time gap.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging or burning, eye irritation, dry eyes, blurred vision or headache may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to olopatadine or any ingredient. Avoid wearing contact lenses if the eyes are irritated and follow the product instructions carefully. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, there is eye pain or vision change, or symptoms do not improve. Do not drive until temporary blurred vision clears.

What is it used for?
Used as eye drops to relieve itching, redness, watering and inflammation caused by allergic conjunctivitis (eye allergy).

How does it work?
Olopatadine blocks the action of histamine, which causes eye-allergy symptoms. Ketorolac is an anti-inflammatory medicine that helps reduce inflammation and discomfort in the eye.

How to take/use it
Use only in the eyes and exactly as directed by the doctor or product label. Wash hands before use, avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or other surfaces, and remove contact lenses before applying. Follow the product instructions about when to put lenses back in.

Common side effects
Temporary burning or stinging, eye irritation, redness, watery eyes, blurred vision or headache may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to olopatadine, ketorolac, aspirin or other NSAID painkillers. Avoid driving or operating machinery until temporary blurred vision clears. Seek medical advice for severe eye pain, vision changes, worsening redness, eye injury or symptoms that do not improve. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Omeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be prescribed for certain stomach or intestinal ulcers and other acid-related conditions.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of acid in the stomach by blocking the stomach’s acid-producing proton pumps.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by the doctor or stated on the label. Swallow the enteric-coated pellets with water; do not crush or chew them. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation and gas may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about allergies, pregnancy or breastfeeding, liver disease, or other medicines being taken. Long-term or repeated use should be medically supervised. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or persistent symptoms.

What is it used for?
Omeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be prescribed for stomach or duodenal ulcers and other acid-related conditions.

How does it work?
It blocks the acid-producing pumps in the stomach, reducing the amount of acid made and helping irritated tissues heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. It is usually taken before food and should be swallowed whole with water; do not crush or chew the capsule or tablet. Do not stop long-term treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, gas, diarrhoea or constipation, and vomiting.

Precautions
Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss, persistent vomiting or severe abdominal pain. Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken, especially blood thinners, certain HIV medicines, methotrexate or medicines affected by stomach acidity. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor because it may affect magnesium, vitamin B12 or bone health.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat acid reflux, heartburn and other acidity-related digestive symptoms. Domperidone may also help relieve associated nausea, vomiting or a feeling of fullness when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Omeprazole reduces the production of stomach acid. Domperidone helps improve movement of food through the stomach and can reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor or as directed on the label. Swallow the enteric-coated pellets whole with water; do not crush or chew them. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, gas, diarrhoea, constipation and dry mouth may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is a history of heart rhythm problems, fainting, significant liver disease, gastrointestinal bleeding or blockage. Domperidone can rarely cause serious heart rhythm disturbances and may interact with some medicines, including certain antibiotics, antifungals and medicines affecting heart rhythm. Seek urgent medical help for palpitations, fainting or severe dizziness. Consult a doctor if symptoms persist or recur frequently, or before prolonged use.

What is it used for?
This supplement helps provide omega-3 fatty acids (EPA and DHA), flaxseed and vitamins A, D, E and K as part of the daily diet. The supplied information does not establish a specific disease treatment use.

How does it work?
Omega-3 fatty acids and flaxseed provide essential nutrients involved in normal body functions. Vitamins A, D, E and K support functions such as vision, immunity, bones, antioxidant protection and normal blood clotting.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach discomfort. Do not combine with other vitamin A, D, E or K supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Fishy aftertaste or burps, nausea, indigestion, stomach discomfort or loose stools may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to fish or any ingredient. Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if taking blood thinners or other medicines that affect blood clotting, or before surgery. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding because the product contains vitamin A. Tell a healthcare professional about all supplements being used.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including nausea and vomiting related to medical treatments or surgery.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals in the body that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. The dose and treatment duration depend on the cause of nausea or vomiting and the product form. Do not take more than prescribed.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, dizziness and tiredness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart rhythm problems, low potassium or magnesium levels, liver disease, or medicines being taken. Ondansetron may affect heart rhythm and may rarely cause serotonin syndrome with some medicines. Seek medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic symptoms, or unusual agitation, sweating, fever or muscle stiffness.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including nausea and vomiting related to certain medical treatments or after surgery.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the instructions for the specific form supplied, and do not take more or use it more often than directed.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, dizziness and tiredness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of abnormal heart rhythm, long QT syndrome, low potassium or magnesium levels, liver disease, or allergy to ondansetron. Seek medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic symptoms, or unusual muscle stiffness and agitation. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or serotonin levels.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including nausea and vomiting related to medical treatments or surgery.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals in the body that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Use it exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. It may usually be taken with or without food. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, tiredness, dizziness, or flushing may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of heart rhythm problems, low potassium or magnesium levels, liver disease, or an allergy to ondansetron. It may affect heart rhythm and can rarely cause serious irregular heartbeat. Seek medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, swelling, breathing difficulty, or severe restlessness, sweating, fever, muscle stiffness, or confusion. Tell the doctor about all medicines being used, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or serotonin levels.

What is it used for?
This product is a nutritional supplement used to provide riboflavin, folic acid and niacinamide when dietary intake is inadequate or vitamin supplementation is recommended. Lactic acid bacillius is included to support normal intestinal flora.

How does it work?
The B vitamins and folic acid support normal energy production, red blood cell formation and nervous-system function. Lactic acid bacillius helps maintain a healthy balance of bacteria in the intestine.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, gas, bloating or loose stools may occur. Riboflavin may harmlessly turn urine yellow-orange.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is liver disease. Prolonged use of folic acid can mask vitamin B12 deficiency; seek medical advice if anemia, numbness or persistent tiredness is present.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation from mouth ulcers, sore gums and other minor painful conditions inside the mouth.

How does it work?
Choline salicylate helps reduce pain and inflammation. Lignocaine is a local anaesthetic that temporarily numbs the affected area.

How to take/use it
Apply a small amount to the affected area as directed on the product label or by a pharmacist. Do not swallow deliberately, and avoid eating or drinking while the area is numb.

Common side effects
Temporary numbness, altered taste, mild burning or irritation at the application site. Stop use and seek medical help if swelling, rash or breathing difficulty develops.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to salicylates such as aspirin, lignocaine or any ingredient. Use in children only with medical advice. Avoid applying to large areas, using more often than recommended, or prolonged use without professional advice. Take care to avoid biting the numb area.

What is it used for?
Cefadroxil is an antibiotic used to treat infections caused by susceptible bacteria, such as certain infections of the throat, skin, urinary tract and other areas. Lactic acid bacillus is included to help support healthy gut bacteria during antibiotic treatment. It will not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefadroxil kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Lactic acid bacillus is a beneficial bacterium that helps maintain the natural balance of microorganisms in the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and mild skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to cefadroxil, other cephalosporin antibiotics or penicillin-type antibiotics. Inform the doctor if there is kidney disease. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, or signs of a serious allergy such as facial swelling, breathing difficulty or a widespread rash. Use only when prescribed, and do not use it for viral infections.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, skin, urinary tract and respiratory tract, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work for viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefadroxil is a cephalosporin antibiotic that kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. The added lactic acid bacillus may help support the balance of beneficial bacteria in the gut.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water; it may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain or indigestion may occur. Skin rash or other allergic reactions can occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefadroxil, other cephalosporins or penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, previous antibiotic-associated diarrhoea, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to support joint, cartilage and connective-tissue health. It may be used as part of supportive care for osteoarthritis-related joint discomfort, but it is not a replacement for prescribed treatment.

How does it work?
Chondroitin, collagen peptides and hyaluronate are components associated with cartilage and connective tissue. Vitamin C supports normal collagen formation, while L-arginine is an amino acid involved in normal body functions.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If the label does not provide directions, consult a pharmacist or doctor.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating or diarrhoea. Stop use and seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction, such as rash, swelling or breathing difficulty.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, before surgery, or if taking blood thinners, blood-pressure medicines or nitrate medicines. Use cautiously if there is a known allergy to any ingredient or a history of significant medical conditions. Seek medical advice for persistent or worsening joint pain, swelling or stiffness.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary supplement to support joint health and mobility. It may help reduce mild joint discomfort and stiffness.

How does it work?
Glucosamine and collagen peptides provide components involved in cartilage and connective-tissue support. Vitamin C helps normal collagen formation, while boswellia contains compounds with anti-inflammatory activity.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach discomfort.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, nausea, bloating, heartburn or diarrhoea may occur. Allergic reactions are possible, especially if glucosamine is derived from shellfish.

Precautions
Check the ingredients if allergic to shellfish. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, with diabetes, a bleeding disorder, or when taking warfarin or other blood-thinning medicines. Stop use and seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Oseltamivir is an antiviral medicine used to treat or help prevent influenza (flu) when prescribed.

How does it work?
It blocks a viral enzyme needed for the release of new influenza viruses from infected cells.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course. It works best when started early after symptoms begin.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting and headache may occur.

Precautions
Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney problems. It does not replace annual influenza vaccination.

What is it used for?
Vicks Inhaler is used for temporary relief of a blocked or stuffy nose, commonly associated with a cold.

How does it work?
It releases aromatic vapours that produce a cooling sensation in the nose and may temporarily make breathing feel easier.

How to take/use it
Use by inhalation through the nostrils as directed on the product pack. Do not swallow it or apply it inside the nose unless specifically instructed.

Common side effects
Temporary nasal irritation, sneezing, or watery eyes may occur.

Precautions
For inhalation use only. Avoid contact with the eyes and stop use if significant irritation occurs. Keep out of reach of children. Seek medical advice for severe breathing difficulty or nasal blockage that does not improve.

What is it used for?
Oxymetazoline nasal spray provides short-term relief from a blocked or stuffy nose caused by the common cold, allergies or sinus congestion.

How does it work?
It narrows swollen blood vessels inside the nose, helping reduce swelling and improve airflow.

How to take/use it
Use in the nose only and follow the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions. Do not use it more often or for longer than recommended, as prolonged use can make nasal congestion worse. Do not share the spray with others.

Common side effects
Nasal dryness, burning or irritation, sneezing, headache, and throat irritation may occur. Fast heartbeat or increased blood pressure can occur rarely.

Precautions
Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, glaucoma or prostate enlargement. Seek advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking monoamine oxidase inhibitors or certain antidepressants. Stop and seek medical advice if symptoms worsen, persist, or if severe palpitations occur.

What is it used for?
Oxymetazoline paediatric nasal spray is used for short-term relief of a blocked or stuffy nose caused by colds, allergies or sinus congestion.

How does it work?
It narrows swollen blood vessels inside the nose, helping reduce swelling and improve airflow.

How to take/use it
For nasal use only. Clear the nose gently and use the spray exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Use only in the child and age group specified on the pack. Do not share the spray, and do not use it for longer than recommended, as this may worsen nasal blockage.

Common side effects
Nasal dryness, burning or irritation, sneezing, headache, and temporary worsening of congestion after the effect wears off may occur.

Precautions
Use only the recommended paediatric product and follow the stated directions carefully. Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if the child has high blood pressure, heart disease, thyroid problems, diabetes, glaucoma, or is taking other medicines. Stop use and seek medical advice if symptoms worsen, do not improve, or unusual effects such as a fast heartbeat occur.

What is it used for?
This combined oral contraceptive is used to prevent pregnancy when taken correctly. It may also help make menstrual bleeding more regular and reduce period pain in some people. It does not protect against sexually transmitted infections.

How does it work?
Levonorgestrel and ethinylestradiol prevent ovulation and make cervical mucus thicker, making it harder for sperm to reach an egg. They also change the lining of the womb.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and follow the order and instructions in the pack leaflet. Take it at the same time each day. If a tablet is missed, or vomiting or severe diarrhoea occurs, follow the missed-tablet instructions or ask a pharmacist or doctor for advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, breast tenderness, mood changes, and changes in menstrual bleeding or spotting may occur, especially during the first few months.

Precautions
Do not use or start this medicine without medical advice if there is a history of blood clots, stroke, heart disease, migraine with aura, uncontrolled high blood pressure, serious liver disease, or breast cancer. Smoking increases the risk of serious cardiovascular side effects, particularly in people over 35 years. Seek urgent medical help for sudden chest pain, breathlessness, coughing blood, severe headache, vision changes, or painful swelling in one leg. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines, as some can reduce contraceptive effectiveness.

What is it used for?
Oxcarbazepine 300 mg is mainly used to control seizures in epilepsy, including focal (partial) seizures. It is usually taken regularly as prescribed to help prevent seizures.

How does it work?
It reduces abnormal electrical activity in the brain by affecting sodium channels in nerve cells, helping to prevent seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop taking it suddenly, as this may worsen seizures. If a dose is missed, follow the advice provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, tiredness, headache, nausea, vomiting, blurred or double vision, difficulty with coordination, and shaking may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney, liver or heart problems, low blood sodium, or an allergy to oxcarbazepine or carbamazepine. Seek medical help for severe rash, swelling of the face or throat, unusual confusion, severe weakness, worsening seizures, or thoughts of self-harm. Oxcarbazepine may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. Discuss pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor before using it. Avoid driving or alcohol until its effects are known.

What is it used for?
This is a dietary supplement used to provide vitamins, minerals, ginseng, lycopene and other antioxidant nutrients when dietary intake may be inadequate. It is intended for general nutritional support and is not a treatment for a specific disease.

How does it work?
It supplies essential vitamins and minerals needed for normal body functions. Ginseng, lycopene and other antioxidants help support the body's natural protection against oxidative stress.

How to take/use it
Swallow the softgel whole with water and use it only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, nausea, headache, or difficulty sleeping may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list if there is an allergy to any component. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is diabetes, a bleeding disorder, or a planned surgery. Seek medical advice if taking blood thinners or other regular medicines, as ginseng may interact with some medicines.

What is it used for?
This is a dietary supplement used to provide vitamins, minerals, omega-3 fatty acids and plant-based ingredients such as ginseng, ginkgo, garlic, ginger and green tea extract. It may help supplement nutritional intake but is not intended to treat or cure a specific disease.

How does it work?
Its vitamins and minerals support normal body functions, while the other ingredients provide various nutritional compounds. The exact effects depend on the amount of each ingredient in the product.

Take only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended serving. Swallow the softgel with water; taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset.

Precautions
Check with a doctor or pharmacist before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition. Seek advice before taking it with blood thinners, antiplatelet medicines, diabetes or blood-pressure medicines, or before surgery, because several ingredients may interact with these treatments. Do not use it as a replacement for a balanced diet or prescribed treatment.

What is it used for?
Used to treat bacterial infections of the eye that are accompanied by redness, swelling or other inflammation. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin is an antibiotic that stops the growth of susceptible bacteria. Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces eye inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use in the affected eye(s) exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before use and do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or other surfaces. Do not use more often or for longer than directed. Avoid wearing contact lenses unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Temporary burning or stinging, eye irritation, watering and blurred vision may occur after use.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially in children or people with glaucoma or other eye problems. Do not use for undiagnosed red eye or suspected viral or fungal infection. Prolonged or repeated use may increase eye pressure, delay healing or cause another infection. Seek medical advice for worsening pain, vision changes, severe irritation or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This combination is generally used, when prescribed, to treat certain bacterial or parasitic intestinal infections causing diarrhoea, dysentery, abdominal discomfort and gas or bloating.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin and metronidazole act against susceptible bacteria and parasites in the intestine. Simethicone helps break up gas bubbles and may relieve bloating and discomfort.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Take the prescribed amount at the recommended times and complete the course, even if symptoms improve. Do not self-medicate or use leftover antibiotics.

Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, metallic taste and gas may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to quinolone antibiotics or metronidazole, liver or kidney problems, seizure disorders, nerve problems, or a history of tendon problems. Avoid alcohol during treatment with metronidazole and for at least 48 hours after the last dose. Seek medical advice for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Pregnant or breastfeeding patients should use it only on medical advice. Keep a gap from antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc if advised by the doctor or pharmacist.

What is it used for?
Used to treat certain mixed bacterial and protozoal infections of the digestive tract, including infectious diarrhoea and dysentery. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin stops susceptible bacteria from multiplying. Ornidazole damages the genetic material of certain parasites and anaerobic bacteria, helping clear the infection.

Take exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course. Swallow with water and do not take antacids or mineral supplements at the same time unless advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not self-medicate for diarrhoea.

Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and a metallic or unpleasant taste.

Precautions
Avoid if allergic to ofloxacin, other quinolone antibiotics, or ornidazole. Seek medical advice for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, confusion, or seizures. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver or kidney problems, seizures, or previous tendon problems. Avoid alcohol during treatment and follow the prescriber’s advice after the last dose. Use only under medical supervision in children and older adults.
