What is it used for?
Dr. Ortho Type Pain Oil is used for temporary relief of minor muscle and joint aches and pains.

It is applied to the skin over the painful area and is intended to provide local soothing relief. The exact action cannot be confirmed because the ingredients are not provided.

Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Serratiopeptidase is an enzyme that may help reduce inflammatory swelling.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve pain and reduce inflammation, including pain affecting the muscles, joints, bones or other parts of the body. It may also help reduce fever.

Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?
Pancreatin is used as pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy when the pancreas does not produce enough digestive enzymes. It helps the body digest fats, proteins and carbohydrates, including in conditions such as chronic pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis or after pancreatic surgery.

How does it work?
It contains digestive enzymes that break down fats, proteins and carbohydrates in food, helping the body absorb nutrients.

Take it with or during meals and snacks, exactly as prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions for the correct dose.

Precautions

What is it used for?
Pancreatin is used to replace digestive enzymes when the pancreas does not make enough of them. It helps the body digest fats, proteins and carbohydrates, and may reduce symptoms such as greasy stools, bloating and poor digestion caused by pancreatic enzyme deficiency.

How does it work?
It contains digestive enzymes, including lipase, amylase and protease. These enzymes help break down fats, carbohydrates and proteins in food so they can be absorbed.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed or directed on the product label. It is generally taken during or immediately after meals and snacks. Swallow the dosage form as directed; do not crush or chew enteric-coated preparations unless specifically advised.

Abdominal pain, bloating, nausea, constipation or diarrhoea may occur. Mouth irritation can occur if the medicine is chewed.

What is it used for?
Pantoprazole 40 mg is used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), and stomach or intestinal ulcers.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of acid in the stomach by blocking acid-producing pumps in the stomach lining.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is commonly taken before food, but follow the instructions on the label or from the doctor.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, vomiting, constipation, or gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to pantoprazole or similar medicines, liver disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice for persistent symptoms, difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, or unexplained weight loss. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor, as it may affect vitamin B12 or magnesium levels and bone health.

What is it used for?
Pantoprazole 40 mg reduces excess stomach acid. It is commonly used for acidity, heartburn, acid reflux and related stomach or intestinal ulcers, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It blocks the stomach’s acid-producing proton pumps, reducing the amount of acid released into the stomach.

What is it used for?

Pantoprazole reduces stomach acid. Domperidone helps stomach contents move forward and reduces nausea.

Take as prescribed. Swallow the capsule or dosage form as directed; do not crush modified-release pellets.

What is it used for?

Clobetasol reduces redness, swelling and itching. Miconazole treats fungal infections, while neomycin treats certain bacterial infections.

Pantoprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Levosulpride helps improve movement of the upper digestive tract, which may help relieve reflux and indigestion symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If it is supplied as a sustained-release formulation, swallow it whole; do not crush or chew it unless advised.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, drowsiness, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal discomfort or bloating may occur. Levosulpride may rarely cause breast tenderness or unexpected milk production.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about liver disease, epilepsy, movement disorders, hormone-related conditions, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice for persistent vomiting, black stools, vomiting blood, difficulty swallowing or unexplained weight loss. Avoid driving or alcohol if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor.

What is it used for?
This combination may be prescribed to manage acidity/reflux symptoms together with nausea or vomiting. The exact approved indication for this fixed combination is not provided.

How does it work?
Pantoprazole reduces stomach acid. Ondansetron blocks serotonin signals involved in triggering nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed; follow the product-specific instructions.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, diarrhoea or abdominal discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Ondansetron can affect heart rhythm in some people. Tell the doctor about heart-rhythm problems, electrolyte imbalance and other medicines.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 125 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, headache, toothache and muscle pain.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain and fever, helping lower temperature and relieve discomfort.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it more often than advised. Check other medicines being taken, as some may also contain paracetamol.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when used as directed. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to paracetamol. Ask a healthcare professional before use if there is liver disease, regular alcohol use or poor nutrition. Avoid taking it with other paracetamol-containing medicines. Seek urgent medical help after an overdose, even if feeling well.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 500 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, body pain, toothache, muscle aches and menstrual pain.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances involved in pain and fever, helping to lower body temperature and relieve discomfort.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth with water, exactly as directed on the package or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it with other medicines containing paracetamol.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid or seek medical advice before use if there is liver disease, regular heavy alcohol use or an allergy to paracetamol. Check other medicines to prevent accidental overdose. Too much paracetamol can cause serious liver damage. Seek urgent medical help after taking more than recommended, even if feeling well. Stop and seek help for severe rash, swelling or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 650 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, body pain, toothache and muscle aches.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of chemicals involved in pain and helps lower raised body temperature.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth with water, exactly as directed on the pack or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when taken as recommended. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to paracetamol. Seek medical advice before use if there is liver disease, kidney disease, regular heavy alcohol use or poor nutrition. Avoid taking other paracetamol-containing products at the same time. Get urgent medical help after an overdose, even if feeling well, as serious liver damage may occur.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 250 mg is used to relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, toothache, body pain and muscle aches. It also helps reduce fever.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of certain chemicals in the brain that cause pain and helps lower raised body temperature.

How to take/use it
Take or give it exactly as directed on the package or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol, and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Paracetamol is usually well tolerated when used correctly. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is liver disease, regular alcohol use, or allergy to paracetamol. Taking too much can cause serious liver damage, even if there are no immediate symptoms. Seek urgent medical help after an overdose or if severe skin rash, swelling or breathing difficulty occurs.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol is used to relieve mild to moderate pain and reduce fever.

How does it work?
It acts mainly in the central nervous system to reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Do not combine with other paracetamol-containing products or exceed the recommended daily amount.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated at recommended doses; allergic reactions can occur rarely.

Precautions
Overdose can cause serious liver damage. Seek urgent medical help if too much is taken. Ask a healthcare professional before use with liver disease or heavy alcohol use.

What is it used for?
Permethrin 5% is a skin treatment used mainly to treat scabies, a mite infestation that causes intense itching and a rash. It should be used only for the condition it has been prescribed or recommended for.

How does it work?
It kills scabies mites and their eggs by affecting their nervous system. It acts mainly on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated. Do not use more often or for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Temporary itching, redness, burning, stinging, tingling or mild skin irritation may occur. Itching can continue for some time after scabies has been treated.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes and mucous membranes, and rinse well with water if contact occurs. Do not apply to severely irritated or broken skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Seek medical advice before use in young children, during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Treating close household or sexual contacts and washing recently used clothes, towels and bedding may be advised to help prevent reinfection.

What is it used for?
Pregabalin is mainly used to relieve nerve pain, such as burning, shooting or tingling pain caused by diabetes, shingles or other nerve damage. It may also be prescribed with other medicines for certain seizures and, in some cases, anxiety.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of certain pain and excitatory signals in the nervous system by acting on calcium channels in nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the capsule whole with water. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop it suddenly; the dose should be reduced gradually under medical supervision.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, blurred vision, headache, dry mouth, constipation, tiredness, difficulty concentrating, increased appetite, weight gain and swelling of the hands or feet.

Precautions
Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase sleepiness and dizziness. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, breathing problems, heart failure, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Pregabalin can cause dependence or misuse in some people. Seek urgent medical help for severe breathing difficulty, facial or throat swelling, a serious rash, or thoughts of self-harm. Extra caution is needed with opioid painkillers or other medicines that cause drowsiness.

What is it used for?
Pregabalin is mainly used to relieve nerve pain caused by conditions such as diabetes, shingles or nerve injury. It is also used with other medicines to help control certain partial seizures.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of certain chemical signals in the nervous system, helping to calm overactive nerve activity and reduce nerve pain or seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the capsule whole with water. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop taking it suddenly without medical advice, as the dose may need to be reduced gradually.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, blurred vision, dry mouth, swelling of the hands or feet, increased appetite and weight gain.

Precautions
Avoid driving or operating machinery until the effects are known. Avoid alcohol, as it can increase sleepiness and dizziness. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, breathing problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or use of opioids or other sedative medicines. Seek urgent medical help for facial or throat swelling, difficulty breathing, severe rash or thoughts of self-harm. Pregabalin may cause dependence in some people and should be used only as prescribed.

What is it used for?
Pregabalin is mainly used to treat nerve pain, such as pain caused by diabetes, shingles or nerve injury. It may also be used with other medicines to help control certain partial seizures.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of chemical signals in the nervous system that cause nerve pain and seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food, and swallow the capsule whole with water. Do not stop it suddenly; the dose usually needs to be reduced gradually under medical guidance. Avoid driving or using machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, blurred or double vision, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, constipation, swelling of the hands or feet, increased appetite and weight gain.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, breathing problems, heart failure, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Pregabalin may cause dependence or withdrawal symptoms if stopped suddenly. Avoid alcohol and use caution with opioid painkillers or other sedatives, as excessive sleepiness and breathing problems may occur. Seek urgent help for facial or throat swelling, severe breathing difficulty, or thoughts of self-harm.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve nerve pain (neuropathic pain), including pain caused by irritated or damaged nerves. It may be prescribed for conditions such as diabetic nerve pain, only when recommended by a doctor.

How does it work?
Pregabalin reduces the release of pain-signalling substances in the nervous system. Duloxetine increases certain brain chemicals that help reduce abnormal pain signals.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, with or without food, and swallow the tablet whole. Do not stop treatment suddenly; the dose may need to be reduced gradually under medical supervision.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, tiredness, nausea, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, increased appetite, weight gain, or swelling of the legs or feet.

Precautions
Avoid driving or operating machinery until the effects are known, and avoid alcohol because sleepiness and dizziness may worsen. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems, glaucoma, seizures, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Seek medical help for severe mood changes, suicidal thoughts, facial or throat swelling, breathing difficulty, or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve neuropathic pain, which is pain caused by irritated or damaged nerves. It may be used for nerve pain related to diabetes or other nerve conditions.

How does it work?
Pregabalin reduces abnormal pain signals in the nerves. Methylcobalamin, vitamin B6, folic acid and benfotiamine provide vitamins that support normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, with or without food. Swallow it with water and do not stop it suddenly without medical advice, as pregabalin may need to be reduced gradually.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, blurred vision, dry mouth, constipation, nausea, swelling of the hands or feet and weight gain may occur.

Precautions
Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid or limit alcohol, as it may increase sleepiness and dizziness. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or a history of drug dependence. Seek medical help for severe swelling, breathing difficulty, serious allergic symptoms or unusual mood changes or suicidal thoughts.

What is it used for?
This medicine is mainly used to relieve nerve pain (neuropathic pain), including pain linked with diabetes, nerve injury or other nerve conditions.

How does it work?
Pregabalin reduces excessive nerve signals that cause pain. Mecobalamin, a form of vitamin B12, supports normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, at the recommended time and dose. It may be taken with or without food. Swallow the tablet/capsule whole and do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, blurred vision, dry mouth, constipation, swelling of the hands or feet, increased appetite and weight gain.

Precautions
Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid or limit alcohol, as it may increase sleepiness and dizziness. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, breathing problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or a history of medicine dependence. Seek urgent help for facial or throat swelling, breathing difficulty or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This combination is mainly used to relieve neuropathic (nerve-related) pain, which may feel like burning, tingling, shooting or electric-shock-like pain.

How does it work?
Pregabalin and nortriptyline reduce abnormal pain signals in the nerves. Methylcobalamin, a form of vitamin B12, supports normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor and follow the prescribed schedule. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving until its effects are known. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, nausea, increased appetite, weight gain and swelling of the hands or feet.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful with driving or machinery because of possible drowsiness or dizziness. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, heart problems, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, depression or thoughts of self-harm. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for severe allergy, breathing difficulty or marked swelling.

What is it used for?
This prescription combination is used to relieve nerve pain (neuropathic pain), including pain caused by nerve damage. It is not usually intended for ordinary short-term pain such as a minor injury.

How does it work?
Pregabalin helps reduce abnormal nerve signals involved in pain. Nortriptyline changes the activity of certain brain chemicals, helping reduce the transmission of pain signals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food as directed. Do not change the dose or stop it suddenly without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the prescriber or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, tiredness, blurred vision, dry mouth, constipation, nausea, swelling of the feet or ankles, and weight gain.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful driving or operating machinery until the effect is known. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, heart problems, depression, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe allergic swelling, breathing difficulty, extreme sleepiness, or unusual mood changes or thoughts of self-harm. Do not take it with other sedating medicines unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve nerve pain caused by nerve damage (neuropathic pain), including pain linked with diabetic peripheral neuropathy.

How does it work?
Pregabalin reduces abnormal pain signals in the nerves. Methylcobalamin, alpha-lipoic acid, pyridoxine and folic acid support nerve function and may help protect damaged nerves.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not change the dose or stop it suddenly, as this may cause withdrawal symptoms or worsening pain. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, blurred vision, tiredness, dry mouth, constipation, swelling of the hands or feet, increased appetite and weight gain.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid alcohol and use caution with sleeping tablets, opioid painkillers or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Tell the doctor if there is a history of drug dependence, breathing problems or diabetes. Seek urgent medical help for severe allergy, breathing difficulty, extreme sleepiness or thoughts of self-harm.

What is it used for?
Calcium acetate is used to control high phosphate levels in people with severe chronic kidney disease, including those receiving dialysis.

How does it work?
It binds phosphate from food in the digestive tract, reducing the amount absorbed into the blood.

How to take/use it
Take with meals exactly as prescribed. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular blood tests may be needed to monitor phosphate and calcium levels.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and loss of appetite. Too much calcium may cause unusual thirst, weakness, confusion or irregular heartbeat.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about high calcium levels, kidney or heart problems, or use of calcium supplements or calcium-containing antacids. Calcium acetate can affect the absorption of some medicines, including iron, thyroid medicines and certain antibiotics; take other medicines only as directed. Seek medical advice if severe constipation, vomiting, confusion or abnormal heartbeat occurs.

What is it used for?
Sodium picosulphate is a stimulant laxative used for short-term relief of constipation and to help empty the bowel when specifically prescribed before certain medical procedures.

How does it work?
It stimulates the muscles of the large intestine and increases water in the bowel, helping soften stools and promote bowel movement.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the package or by a doctor, with water. Drink adequate fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Do not use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Abdominal cramps, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, nausea and vomiting. Excessive diarrhoea may cause dehydration or changes in body salts.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is severe or unexplained abdominal pain, vomiting, suspected bowel blockage, or severe dehydration. Avoid prolonged or frequent use, as it may disturb body salts. Seek medical advice if constipation persists, or if blood appears in the stool. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals, children, and people with kidney or heart problems should seek medical advice before use.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve symptoms of piles (haemorrhoids), such as pain, itching, swelling and irritation around the anus.

How does it work?
Lignocaine helps numb pain, while hydrocortisone reduces inflammation and itching. Calcium dobesilate helps reduce swelling, and zinc helps protect irritated skin.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the package or by a doctor. If it is a rectal preparation, clean and gently dry the area before use, and wash hands before and after application. Do not use more often or for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, irritation, itching or redness at the application site. Stop using it and seek medical advice if these symptoms are severe or if a rash or swelling develops.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Avoid prolonged or excessive use of hydrocortisone-containing products, as this may thin the skin or worsen an infection. Seek medical advice for heavy or unexplained rectal bleeding, severe pain, or symptoms that do not improve. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Pioglitazone is used to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes, along with a suitable diet and exercise. It may be used alone or with other diabetes medicines.

How does it work?
It helps the body's cells respond better to insulin, allowing more sugar to move from the blood into the cells. This helps lower blood sugar levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Take it regularly and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Continue the recommended diet, exercise and blood sugar monitoring.

Common side effects
Weight gain, swelling of the ankles or legs, headache, muscle aches and symptoms of an upper respiratory infection may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when it is taken with certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart failure, liver disease, bladder cancer or blood in the urine before using it. Seek medical help for sudden weight gain, increasing swelling or breathing difficulty, as these may indicate fluid retention or heart problems. Liver function may need monitoring. Pioglitazone may increase the risk of bone fractures and is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis. Inform the doctor if pregnant, planning pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Pioglitazone is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It may be used alone or with other diabetes medicines. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
It improves the body's sensitivity to insulin, helping cells use sugar from the blood more effectively. This helps lower blood sugar levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. It may be taken with or without food. Continue the recommended diet, exercise and blood sugar monitoring, and do not stop it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Weight gain, swelling of the ankles or legs, headache, muscle pain and symptoms of low blood sugar when used with other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor before use if there is heart failure, liver disease, bladder cancer or blood in the urine, or a history of bone fractures. Pioglitazone can cause fluid retention and may worsen heart failure; seek medical help for breathlessness, rapid weight gain or severe swelling. Liver tests and blood sugar monitoring may be needed. Discuss use during pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor.

What is it used for?
Piperacillin and tazobactam is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues. It is usually given in a hospital or clinic.

How does it work?
Piperacillin kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Tazobactam helps protect piperacillin from enzymes that can make some bacteria resistant to it.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Complete the prescribed course unless the treating doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, headache, rash and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, other beta-lactam antibiotics or any ingredient. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, bleeding or blood disorders, or other medicines being taken. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or unusual bleeding. Unnecessary use can promote antibiotic resistance.

What is it used for?
Piperacillin with tazobactam is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues. It is usually used in hospitals and does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Piperacillin kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall. Tazobactam helps protect piperacillin from bacterial enzymes that can make some bacteria resistant to it.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by intravenous infusion by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Complete the prescribed course unless the treating doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, headache, skin rash and pain or redness at the injection site may occur. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, piperacillin, tazobactam or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, bleeding or blood disorders, seizures, or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Kidney function and blood tests may be monitored during treatment. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or blistering.

What is it used for?
Piracetam is mainly used under specialist supervision to help reduce involuntary muscle jerks (cortical myoclonus). Its use depends on the underlying condition and medical assessment.

How does it work?
Its exact action is not fully understood. It is thought to affect the function of nerve-cell membranes and communication between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and kidney function. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice, especially when it is being used for myoclonus.

Common side effects
Nervousness, irritability, anxiety, headache, sleeplessness, drowsiness, nausea, stomach discomfort and weight gain may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, a history of bleeding, a bleeding disorder, or use of blood-thinning medicines. Medical advice is needed before surgery. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for unusual bleeding, severe confusion or worsening involuntary movements.

What is it used for?
Piracetam is mainly used, under specialist supervision, to help control cortical myoclonus—repeated, involuntary muscle jerking caused by a brain or nerve disorder.

How does it work?
Its exact action is not fully understood. It may help regulate the function of nerve-cell membranes and communication between brain cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, at the recommended times. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice, especially when it is being used for myoclonus. Drink enough water unless fluid restriction has been advised.

Common side effects
Nervousness, restlessness, irritability, sleep problems, headache, dizziness, nausea, stomach discomfort and diarrhoea.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, a history of bleeding or haemorrhagic stroke, or use of blood-thinning medicines. Medical advice is needed before surgery. Avoid use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically prescribed. Seek medical help for unusual bleeding, severe weakness or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Piracetam is mainly used to help control cortical myoclonus, a condition causing sudden, involuntary muscle jerks. It should be used only under medical supervision.

How does it work?
Its exact mechanism is not fully understood. It is believed to influence nerve-cell membrane function and communication between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, especially when it is being used for myoclonus.

Common side effects
Nervousness, irritability, anxiety, difficulty sleeping, drowsiness, headache, nausea, stomach discomfort or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about kidney disease, a history of brain bleeding, bleeding problems, or planned surgery. Extra caution may be needed if taking blood thinners or medicines that affect bleeding. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only if specifically advised by a doctor. Seek medical help if unusual bleeding or worsening involuntary movements occur.

What is it used for?
Piroxicam is an anti-inflammatory painkiller used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness in conditions such as osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. It is generally used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the product label. Do not use more than recommended or for longer than advised. The dose and route depend on the product form; if it is an injection, it should be given by a healthcare professional. Do not combine it with other anti-inflammatory painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding, severe kidney or liver disease, heart failure, or an allergy to aspirin or other NSAIDs, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about asthma, high blood pressure, heart disease, blood-clotting problems, or use of blood thinners, steroids or other painkillers. It may increase the risk of stomach bleeding, kidney problems and cardiovascular events. Avoid during pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks and in the last trimester, unless prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, chest pain or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Piroxicam is used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness in inflammatory joint conditions such as osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. It may also be prescribed for other painful muscle or joint conditions.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that reduces the production of substances responsible for pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, usually with or after food and with water, to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more than prescribed or combine it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and skin rash.

Precautions
Avoid or use only with medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to NSAIDs. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin rash. It may increase the risk of stomach bleeding, kidney problems and heart-related events, especially with long-term use or in older adults. Avoid during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed, particularly from 20 weeks onward and during the last trimester. Tell the doctor about blood thinners, steroids or other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Carica papaya leaf extract is a herbal supplement commonly marketed to support platelet counts, particularly during dengue. Evidence for this use is limited, and it should not replace medical assessment or treatment for dengue, bleeding, or low platelet counts.

How does it work?
Its proposed effects on platelet production and inflammation are not fully established. The exact way it may affect platelet counts is still uncertain.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not use it as a substitute for prescribed treatment or urgent care.

Common side effects
Possible effects include nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, or an allergic reaction. Product-specific side effects may vary.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, before surgery, or if taking blood-thinning medicines. Seek urgent medical care for bleeding, severe weakness, persistent vomiting, or suspected dengue. Stop use and seek help if an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Carica papaya leaf extract is a herbal supplement traditionally used during dengue to support platelet counts. It is not proven to treat dengue or replace medical care and monitoring.

How does it work?
Its exact action is not well established. Some compounds in papaya leaves may influence platelet production, but the evidence is limited.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not use it as a substitute for fluids, blood tests or prescribed dengue treatment.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, stomach discomfort or loose stools. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Avoid use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless advised by a healthcare professional. Do not use if allergic to papaya or latex. Seek urgent medical care for bleeding, severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, breathing difficulty or worsening dengue symptoms.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or correct deficiency of B vitamins, including vitamin B12. B vitamins support normal energy metabolism, red blood cell formation and nerve function.

How does it work?
B vitamins act as essential helpers in the body's chemical processes, including energy production. Vitamin B12 also supports healthy red blood cells and normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause mild nausea or stomach upset. Bright yellow urine can occur with some B-vitamin supplements and is usually harmless.

Precautions
Check the ingredients if there is a known allergy. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or regular medication use. Seek medical advice if symptoms of vitamin deficiency continue or worsen.

What is it used for?
This combination is commonly used to help prevent the formation or recurrence of certain kidney stones, particularly calcium oxalate stones. Its exact use should be confirmed by a doctor based on urine and kidney test results.

How does it work?
Potassium citrate makes the urine less acidic and citrate can help reduce the formation of some crystals. Magnesium citrate and vitamin B6 may also support the reduction of oxalate-related stone formation.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Take with sufficient water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, vomiting or abdominal bloating may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, high blood potassium, heart disease, dehydration or reduced urine output. Inform the doctor about medicines used for blood pressure or fluid retention, especially potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics, ACE inhibitors or ARBs. Stop use and seek medical help for severe weakness, palpitations or persistent vomiting.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat certain local infections caused by bacteria and protozoa, commonly vaginal infections. The exact use depends on the product formulation and the diagnosis.

How does it work?
Povidone-iodine releases iodine, which acts as an antiseptic against many germs. Ornidazole acts against certain anaerobic bacteria and protozoa that can cause infection.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the package or by a healthcare professional, and follow the prescribed route of use. Do not swallow or apply it to the eyes unless specifically instructed. Do not use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Local burning, itching, irritation or discomfort may occur. Nausea, headache, dizziness or a metallic taste may occur with ornidazole.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to povidone-iodine, iodine or ornidazole. Ask a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is thyroid disease. Avoid prolonged or repeated use of povidone-iodine unless medically advised. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, rash or other allergic symptoms occur.

What is it used for?
Povidone-iodine 2% mouthwash is an antiseptic used to reduce germs in the mouth and throat and support oral hygiene.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or inactivates many types of bacteria, viruses and fungi.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a dentist or doctor. Rinse or gargle as instructed, then spit it out. Do not swallow. Do not dilute unless specifically advised.

Common side effects
Unpleasant taste, temporary mouth or throat irritation, and temporary staining or discoloration of the mouth or teeth may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to povidone-iodine or iodine. Avoid swallowing it. Seek medical advice before use in children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is thyroid disease. Avoid prolonged or repeated use unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek help for swelling, breathing difficulty or other signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine solution is a topical antiseptic used to disinfect the skin and help prevent infection in minor cuts, grazes, wounds and burns. It may also be used to prepare the skin before certain medical procedures.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or reduces many types of bacteria, viruses and fungi on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean the affected area, apply the solution as directed by a doctor or pharmacist, and allow it to dry. Do not swallow it or use it in the eyes, mouth or other body openings.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, dryness or itching may occur. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe irritation or an allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to povidone iodine or iodine-containing products. Do not use repeatedly over large areas, for prolonged periods, or on deep or serious wounds unless advised by a healthcare professional. Use with medical advice if there is thyroid disease, kidney disease, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine 5% is used as an antiseptic to help clean minor cuts, grazes and other superficial skin wounds and reduce the risk of infection.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or inactivates many types of germs on the skin, including bacteria, viruses and fungi.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean the affected area and apply the product as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not swallow it.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, dryness or itching may occur. Allergic reactions are uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to povidone iodine or iodine-containing products. Avoid prolonged or repeated use over large areas, deep wounds or severe burns unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice if irritation worsens, an allergic reaction develops, or the wound does not improve.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine cleansing scrub is an antiseptic used to clean the skin and reduce germs before surgery, injections, or other medical procedures. It may also be used for cleansing minor cuts and wounds when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or reduces many types of germs on the skin, including bacteria, viruses and fungi.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use on the skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and rinse thoroughly if it gets into the eyes.

Common side effects
Skin irritation, redness, dryness or itching may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if a severe rash, swelling or breathing difficulty develops.

Precautions
Do not swallow. Avoid using on large areas, deep wounds or severe burns unless advised by a healthcare professional. Do not use if allergic to povidone iodine. Seek medical advice before prolonged or repeated use, especially in people with thyroid problems, pregnant or breastfeeding women, and infants. Keep away from the eyes and mucous membranes.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine 10% solution is a topical antiseptic used to clean and help prevent infection in minor cuts, wounds, grazes and burns. It may also be used to disinfect the skin before certain medical procedures, as directed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or inactivates many types of germs on the skin, including bacteria, fungi and some viruses.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a small amount to the affected, cleaned skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Allow the area to dry. Do not swallow it or use it inside the body unless specifically prescribed.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, dryness or itching may occur. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling or breathing difficulty develops.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes. Do not use if allergic to povidone iodine or any ingredient. Avoid applying repeatedly to large areas, deep wounds or severe burns unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice for deep, infected or non-healing wounds. People with thyroid disorders, those who are pregnant or breastfeeding, and infants should ask a healthcare professional before extensive or repeated use.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine 5% solution is a topical antiseptic used to help prevent infection in minor cuts, wounds, grazes and burns. Use it only for the purpose stated on the product label or advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or helps control a broad range of bacteria, viruses and fungi on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean the affected area and apply the solution as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not use on deep or serious wounds without medical advice.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, skin irritation, redness, dryness or itching may occur. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to povidone iodine or other iodine-containing products. Avoid prolonged or extensive use, especially in people with thyroid disease, kidney problems, or those taking lithium, unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical care for deep wounds, severe burns, animal bites or wounds showing signs of infection.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine 5% solution is a topical antiseptic used to help prevent infection in minor cuts, grazes, superficial wounds and burns, and to disinfect skin when directed. Use only for the purpose and area stated on the product label.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or inhibits many bacteria, viruses and fungi on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to clean, affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not swallow, and avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Temporary skin irritation, redness, dryness or itching. Rarely, an allergic skin reaction may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to povidone iodine or other iodine-containing products. Avoid use on large areas, deep or serious wounds, or for prolonged periods unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice for severe irritation, worsening symptoms or signs of infection. Keep away from children and do not use in the eyes unless specifically labelled for ophthalmic use. Ask a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in people with thyroid disease.

What is it used for?
Prazosin is used to lower high blood pressure (hypertension). It may be prescribed for other conditions only when specifically directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It blocks alpha-1 receptors in blood vessels, causing them to relax and widen. This reduces resistance to blood flow and lowers blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole with water; do not crush, chew or break it. Stand up slowly, especially when starting treatment or after a dose change. Do not stop it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, light-headedness, headache, drowsiness, weakness, nausea and palpitations may occur, particularly when starting treatment.

Precautions
The medicine can cause a sudden fall in blood pressure or fainting, especially after the first dose or when standing up. Avoid driving or alcohol until its effects are known. Tell the doctor about other blood-pressure medicines or erectile-dysfunction medicines, as the combination may cause excessive low blood pressure. Inform the doctor before cataract surgery and seek medical advice for severe dizziness, fainting or a fast heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Prazosin extended-release is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It may be used alone or with other blood pressure medicines as prescribed.

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens blood vessels by blocking alpha-1 receptors. This helps blood flow more easily and lowers blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole with water; do not crush, chew or split it. Do not stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, light-headedness, headache, drowsiness, weakness, nausea and palpitations may occur, especially when starting treatment or increasing the dose.

Precautions
It can cause a sudden fall in blood pressure or fainting, particularly after the first dose or when standing up. Rise slowly and avoid driving or operating machinery if dizzy or drowsy. Alcohol and medicines for erectile dysfunction may worsen low blood pressure. Tell the doctor before cataract surgery and report fainting, severe dizziness or a fast heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Prednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and control overactive immune reactions in conditions such as allergies, asthma, skin problems, and inflammatory or autoimmune disorders. Its use depends on the condition being treated and should be determined by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the body's production of substances that cause inflammation and helps suppress excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. It is usually taken by mouth with food to reduce stomach irritation. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor, especially if it has been used for a prolonged period.

Common side effects
Increased appetite, indigestion, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, fluid retention, and increased blood sugar may occur. The risk of side effects increases with higher doses or longer treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health problems, or any current infection. Prednisolone can reduce resistance to infection and may affect blood sugar and blood pressure. Avoid close contact with people who have contagious infections and check before receiving vaccines. Long-term treatment requires medical monitoring.

What is it used for?
Prednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactive immune reactions in conditions such as severe allergies, asthma, skin problems, joint inflammation and autoimmune disorders. It should be used only for the condition and duration prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces inflammation and suppresses an overactive immune response.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food, and swallow with water. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition. Do not stop it suddenly, especially after prolonged treatment, unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, fluid retention, increased blood sugar and increased susceptibility to infections may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, liver or kidney problems, or any current infection. Avoid close contact with people who have infections and check before receiving vaccines. Seek medical advice if signs of infection, severe stomach pain or major mood changes occur.

What is it used for?
This combipack is prescribed to medically terminate an early intrauterine pregnancy. It should be used only after assessment by a qualified healthcare professional and is not suitable for an ectopic pregnancy.

How does it work?
Mifepristone blocks progesterone, a hormone needed to maintain pregnancy. Misoprostol softens the cervix and causes uterine contractions to help expel the pregnancy.

How to take/use it
Use the tablets exactly as prescribed, including the correct order and timing. Do not self-use this medicine or change the regimen without medical advice. A follow-up check is needed to confirm that the pregnancy has ended completely.

Common side effects
Abdominal cramps, vaginal bleeding, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, chills and temporary fever may occur.

Precautions
Do not use without medical assessment to rule out ectopic pregnancy and confirm the pregnancy stage. Tell the healthcare professional about bleeding disorders, use of blood thinners, long-term corticosteroid treatment, adrenal problems, allergies, or an intrauterine device. Seek urgent medical care for very heavy or prolonged bleeding, severe or one-sided abdominal pain, fainting, persistent fever, severe weakness, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve neuropathic pain, which is pain caused by damaged or irritated nerves. It may be prescribed for conditions such as diabetic nerve pain, nerve pain after shingles, or other nerve-related pain. It is not a routine painkiller for ordinary aches.

How does it work?
Pregabalin reduces the release of pain-signalling chemicals in the nervous system, helping calm overactive nerves. Mecobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 that supports normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Swallow the capsule with water. Do not stop it suddenly unless advised by a doctor, as the dose may need to be reduced gradually. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, blurred vision, tiredness, dry mouth, swelling of the hands or feet, increased appetite and weight gain. Mecobalamin may occasionally cause nausea or stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, breathing problems, heart failure, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney disease. Avoid alcohol and inform the doctor about sleeping medicines, opioid painkillers or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek urgent medical help for facial or throat swelling, breathing difficulty, severe rash, or unusual mood or behaviour changes.

What is it used for?
Norethisterone acetate is a progestogen used to manage certain menstrual problems, such as heavy or irregular menstrual bleeding, and conditions such as endometriosis. The exact use depends on the prescription.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone progesterone. It helps control the growth and shedding of the womb lining and can reduce abnormal bleeding and hormone-related symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, at the same time each day. Swallow the controlled-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, breast tenderness, bloating, mood changes, acne and irregular vaginal bleeding or spotting.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about a history of blood clots, stroke, liver disease, unexplained vaginal bleeding, migraine or hormone-sensitive cancer. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, coughing blood, or painful swelling in a leg. This medicine is not a reliable contraceptive unless specifically advised.

What is it used for?
Norethisterone acetate is a hormonal medicine used mainly to treat endometriosis, a condition in which tissue similar to the womb lining grows outside the womb. It can help reduce related pelvic pain and abnormal bleeding.

How does it work?
It is a progestogen, a hormone similar to natural progesterone. It suppresses the growth and activity of endometriosis-related tissue and helps control the menstrual cycle.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the controlled-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, breast tenderness, bloating, mood changes, acne, weight changes and irregular vaginal bleeding or spotting.

Precautions
Do not use it during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about unexplained vaginal bleeding, liver disease, a history of blood clots, breast cancer or other hormone-sensitive cancer, migraine, or significant depression. Seek urgent medical help for sudden chest pain, breathing difficulty, coughing blood, severe headache, vision changes, or painful swelling in an arm or leg. This medicine is not a contraceptive unless specifically advised otherwise.

What is it used for?
Norethisterone is a progestogen hormone medicine used to treat heavy or painful periods, irregular menstrual bleeding and endometriosis. It may also be prescribed to delay a period.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone progesterone and helps control changes in the womb lining and menstrual cycle.

How to take/use it
Take the tablets exactly as prescribed, at the recommended times, and swallow them with water. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. It is not a reliable contraceptive.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, breast tenderness, bloating, mood changes and spotting or changes in menstrual bleeding.

Precautions
Do not take it if pregnant unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor before use if there is a history of blood clots, liver disease, unexplained vaginal bleeding, migraine or hormone-sensitive cancer. Seek urgent medical help for sudden chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, vision changes or painful swelling in a leg.

What is it used for?
Evening primrose oil is a dietary supplement commonly used by some people for symptoms linked with premenstrual syndrome (PMS), cyclical breast tenderness and other women's health concerns. Its benefits may vary, and it should not replace medical assessment for persistent or severe symptoms.

How does it work?
It contains gamma-linolenic acid (GLA), an omega-6 fatty acid involved in the production of substances that help regulate inflammation and other body processes. The effectiveness of evening primrose oil for these uses is not certain.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Swallow the softgel with water; do not use it if the pack is damaged or expired.

Common side effects
Mild stomach upset, nausea, loose stools or headache may occur.

Precautions
Check with a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, if there is a seizure disorder or bleeding problem, or when taking blood-thinning medicines. Seek medical advice before surgery. Stop use and seek advice if an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Evening primrose oil is commonly used as a dietary supplement for premenstrual symptoms, including breast tenderness. Evidence of benefit is limited, and it should not replace medical treatment for persistent or severe symptoms.

How does it work?
It contains gamma-linolenic acid, a fatty acid that the body uses to make signalling substances involved in inflammation. Its exact benefit for premenstrual symptoms is uncertain.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause stomach discomfort, nausea, loose stools or headache.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, before surgery, or if there is a bleeding disorder, epilepsy or a history of seizures. Consult a healthcare professional if taking blood-thinning medicines or other regular medicines.

What is it used for?
Progesterone Sustained Release 200mg is used when the body needs additional progesterone. Depending on the doctor's advice, it may be prescribed for irregular menstrual periods, progesterone support during fertility treatment or pregnancy, or with oestrogen therapy during menopause to help protect the uterine lining.

How does it work?
Progesterone is a natural female hormone. It helps regulate the menstrual cycle and prepares and maintains the lining of the uterus.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the sustained-release tablet/capsule whole with water; do not crush, chew or open it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, headache, nausea, bloating, breast tenderness and changes in vaginal bleeding or menstrual periods.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about liver disease, a history of blood clots, unexplained vaginal bleeding, breast or reproductive-organ cancer, or allergy to progesterone. It may cause drowsiness or dizziness, so take care when driving or operating machinery. Seek medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, chest pain, breathing difficulty, severe headache or leg swelling.

What is it used for?
Progesterone is a female hormone medicine used when progesterone supplementation is needed. Depending on the prescription, it may be used as part of menopausal hormone therapy or to support fertility and early pregnancy. The exact use depends on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It replaces or supplements the natural hormone progesterone. Progesterone helps regulate the menstrual cycle and prepares and maintains the lining of the uterus.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed. Follow the product instructions for swallowing the sustained-release formulation; do not crush or chew it unless specifically advised. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, headache, nausea, bloating, breast tenderness, mood changes and irregular vaginal bleeding may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about unexplained vaginal bleeding, liver disease, a history of blood clots or stroke, breast or reproductive-organ cancer, or allergies to progesterone. Drowsiness or dizziness may occur, so take care while driving or operating machinery. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, one-sided leg swelling, sudden severe headache, vision changes or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Protein powder is used to supplement dietary protein when food intake is insufficient. It may support muscle maintenance and growth as part of a balanced diet and regular exercise.

How does it work?
It provides protein and amino acids that the body uses to build and repair muscles and other tissues.

How to take/use it
Mix and use according to the product label, usually with water, milk or another suitable drink. Do not exceed the recommended serving. Protein powder should supplement, not replace, a balanced diet unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Some people may experience bloating, gas, nausea, stomach discomfort or diarrhoea. Reactions may depend on the protein source and other ingredients.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list for milk, soy, egg or other allergens. People with kidney disease or other medical conditions should seek medical advice before using protein supplements. Those with lactose intolerance should check whether the product contains lactose. Stop use and seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) is used to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency. It helps the body absorb calcium and supports healthy bones and muscles.

How does it work?
It increases the body’s vitamin D levels, helping improve calcium and phosphate absorption. These nutrients are important for maintaining strong bones and normal muscle function.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor or as directed on the product label. Do not take extra vitamin D or calcium supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, headache, weakness, increased thirst or frequent urination may occur, particularly with excessive use.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or conditions such as sarcoidosis. Avoid taking other high-dose vitamin D or calcium products without medical advice. Seek medical advice if symptoms such as persistent nausea, vomiting, unusual thirst, frequent urination, or confusion occur.

What is it used for?
Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) is used to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency. It helps the body absorb calcium and supports healthy bones and muscles.

How does it work?
It increases vitamin D levels in the body, helping improve calcium absorption and maintain bone strength.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the instructions on the product label, and do not take this high-strength product more often than recommended. Do not take other vitamin D or calcium supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated when used as prescribed. Excessive vitamin D may cause nausea, vomiting, constipation, stomach discomfort, unusual thirst, frequent urination or weakness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or conditions such as sarcoidosis. Seek medical advice if symptoms of excess calcium occur. Medical supervision may be needed if taking calcium supplements, other vitamin D products, digoxin or thiazide diuretics.

What is it used for?
Quetiapine is an antipsychotic medicine used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. It may also be prescribed with other medicines for certain depressive conditions, depending on the doctor's advice.

How does it work?
It helps balance the effects of certain chemical messengers in the brain, mainly dopamine and serotonin. This can help reduce disturbances in thinking, mood and behaviour.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect on alertness is known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, increased appetite and weight gain may occur. Blurred vision or a drop in blood pressure on standing can also occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol because it can increase sleepiness and dizziness. Tell the doctor about diabetes, heart problems, liver disease, seizures, or a history of low blood pressure. Blood sugar, cholesterol and weight may need monitoring. Older adults with dementia-related psychosis may have an increased risk of serious effects. Seek urgent medical help for severe muscle stiffness, high fever, confusion, uncontrolled movements or fainting.

What is it used for?
Quetiapine is a prescription antipsychotic medicine used mainly to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. It may also be used with other medicines for certain depressive symptoms, only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It helps balance chemical signals in the brain, particularly dopamine and serotonin. This can help reduce hallucinations, disturbed thoughts, severe mood changes and related symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop it suddenly without medical advice. Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if it causes sleepiness or dizziness.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, dry mouth, constipation, increased appetite, weight gain and tiredness.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about diabetes, heart disease, low blood pressure, seizures, liver problems or a history of stroke. Seek medical help for severe muscle stiffness, high fever, fainting, uncontrolled movements or thoughts of self-harm. Older adults with dementia-related psychosis may have an increased risk of serious complications with this medicine.

What is it used for?
Quetiapine is a prescription medicine used to treat certain mental health conditions, including schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.

How does it work?
It helps balance certain chemical messengers in the brain, including dopamine and serotonin, which can improve mood, thinking and behaviour.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, increased appetite and weight gain may occur.

Precautions
It may cause drowsiness or dizziness; avoid driving until its effects are known and avoid alcohol. Rise slowly to reduce light-headedness. Inform the doctor about diabetes, heart problems, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if severe muscle stiffness, high fever, unusual movements or fainting occur.

What is it used for?
Rabeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD) and stomach or duodenal ulcers. It may also be used with antibiotics to help treat Helicobacter pylori infection, when prescribed.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of stomach acid by blocking the acid-producing pumps in the stomach lining.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed timing and treatment duration, and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain and gas may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, allergies to acid-reducing medicines, or other medicines being taken. Prolonged use may require medical monitoring. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash, swelling, difficulty breathing, black stools or vomiting blood.

What is it used for?
Used to treat acidity and acid reflux (GERD), including heartburn and regurgitation. It may also help relieve nausea or vomiting associated with these digestive symptoms.

How does it work?
Rabeprazole reduces the production of stomach acid. Domperidone helps improve movement of the stomach and upper digestive tract and reduces nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the product label and do not change the dose or duration without medical advice. Swallow the medicine as directed; do not crush or chew it unless specifically advised.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain, nausea, dry mouth and dizziness. Domperidone may occasionally cause breast tenderness or increased prolactin levels.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, irregular heartbeat, liver disease, electrolyte problems or a history of fainting. Domperidone can rarely affect heart rhythm and may interact with some medicines, including certain antibiotics, antifungals and heart medicines. Seek urgent medical help for palpitations, fainting or severe dizziness. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat acid reflux, heartburn and gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD). It may also help relieve associated indigestion, bloating and a feeling of fullness.

How does it work?
Rabeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Levosulpride helps improve movement of the stomach and intestines, which can support the passage of stomach contents and reduce reflux-related symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the sustained-release tablet or capsule whole with water; do not crush, chew or open it. Follow the timing instructions provided by the doctor or product label.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain, dizziness, drowsiness and tiredness may occur. Levosulpride may occasionally cause breast tenderness or menstrual changes.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about pregnancy or breastfeeding, liver or kidney problems, epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, intestinal blockage or bleeding, or a history of hormone-related breast problems. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizzy or drowsy. Seek medical advice for unusual muscle movements, severe abdominal pain, vomiting blood or black stools. Do not use for prolonged periods unless medically advised.

What is it used for?
Racecadotril 100 is used to help treat acute diarrhoea in adults, along with oral rehydration fluids. It helps reduce excessive loss of water and salts from the intestines.

How does it work?
It reduces excessive secretion of water and electrolytes into the intestine, helping to lessen loose motions. It does not replace the need for oral rehydration.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Continue drinking oral rehydration solution and other recommended fluids. Do not use it as a replacement for rehydration treatment or for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, constipation and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice if diarrhoea is severe, lasts more than a short period, or is associated with blood in the stool, fever or signs of dehydration. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop it and seek urgent help if swelling of the face, lips or tongue, breathing difficulty, or a severe skin reaction occurs. People taking ACE inhibitor blood-pressure medicines should consult a doctor before use because of a possible increased risk of swelling reactions.

What is it used for?
Ranolazine extended-release tablets are used to help prevent and reduce symptoms of chronic stable angina, such as chest pain or discomfort caused by reduced blood flow to the heart. It is not used to treat a sudden angina attack.

How does it work?
It helps the heart use energy more efficiently and reduces changes in heart muscle cells that can contribute to angina symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole with water; do not crush, chew or break it. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.
