This medicine may interact with several medicines, including some blood-pressure medicines and painkillers, so provide a complete list of medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Prochlorperazine is used to treat nausea and vomiting and, in some cases, vertigo. The exact indication depends on the prescription.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine receptors involved in nausea and vomiting pathways in the brain.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth and blurred vision may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving if drowsy. Seek medical advice for muscle stiffness, unusual movements, fever or severe confusion. Use caution in older adults.

What is it used for?
Cinnarizine is used to prevent and relieve vertigo (a spinning or balance sensation), dizziness, nausea and vomiting related to inner-ear problems. It can also help prevent motion sickness.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of the balance centre in the inner ear and blocks certain signals that can cause dizziness, nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth with water, exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach discomfort. Do not drive or operate machinery until its effect is known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dry mouth, stomach discomfort, indigestion and weight gain may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol because it may increase drowsiness. Use cautiously in older adults, as confusion or movement-related side effects may occur. People with Parkinson’s disease should use it only on medical advice. Seek medical advice if dizziness is severe, new or persistent.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve vertigo (a spinning or whirling sensation) and the nausea or vomiting associated with it.

How does it work?
Cinnarizine helps reduce abnormal signals from the inner ear that can cause dizziness. Domperidone helps control nausea and vomiting by improving movement in the upper digestive system.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid self-treatment for prolonged or recurring dizziness.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, dry mouth, headache, stomach discomfort, abdominal cramps or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol if affected. Tell the doctor about heart rhythm problems, heart disease, liver or kidney problems, Parkinson’s disease, or use of medicines that can affect heart rhythm. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Domperidone should be used at the lowest effective dose and for the shortest duration advised.

What is it used for?
Used to help treat stomach and duodenal ulcers, gastritis and other acid-related stomach problems. It can also help relieve burning or pain caused by irritation of the stomach lining.

How does it work?
Sucralfate forms a protective coating over ulcers and irritated areas, helping shield them from stomach acid. Oxetacaine is a local anaesthetic that helps reduce pain and burning in the affected area.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Sucralfate is usually taken on an empty stomach or before meals when directed. Keep a suitable gap from other medicines if advised, as it may affect their absorption. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, indigestion, dry mouth and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, difficulty swallowing, or an allergy to either ingredient. Inform the doctor about all other medicines being taken, as sucralfate can reduce the absorption of some medicines. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not continue treatment for persistent or worsening stomach pain without medical review.

What is it used for?
Sucralfate is mainly used to treat and help heal ulcers in the stomach and duodenum. It protects the damaged area from stomach acid and digestive enzymes.

How does it work?
It forms a protective coating over ulcers and irritated areas of the stomach or intestine. This barrier helps protect them while they heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually on an empty stomach. Follow the product label or doctor’s instructions, and take other medicines at a different time if advised, as sucralfate can affect their absorption. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Constipation, dry mouth, nausea, indigestion, or stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Sucralfate can interfere with the absorption of other medicines, so provide a complete list of medicines being taken. Use antacids only as advised and keep them separate from sucralfate. Seek medical advice for persistent or worsening stomach pain, vomiting blood, or black stools.

What is it used for?
Sulfasalazine is used to reduce inflammation in inflammatory bowel disease, especially ulcerative colitis, and in inflammatory arthritis such as rheumatoid arthritis.

How does it work?
It is broken down in the bowel into components that help reduce inflammation. This can relieve inflammation in the intestine and joints.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, usually with plenty of water. Swallow the gastro-resistant tablet whole; do not crush or chew it. Take it consistently and complete the prescribed treatment. Regular blood, liver and kidney tests may be needed.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain or indigestion, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, loss of appetite and skin rash. Urine or other body fluids may become yellow-orange.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to sulfonamide medicines or aspirin/salicylates, liver or kidney disease, blood disorders, or porphyria. Seek medical help for severe rash, fever, sore throat, unusual bruising or bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or reduced urine. Do not stop treatment without medical advice. Men should discuss fertility concerns, as a reversible reduction in sperm count can occur.

What is it used for?
Sulfasalazine is used to reduce inflammation in inflammatory bowel diseases such as ulcerative colitis and, in some cases, Crohn’s disease. It is also used to treat inflammatory arthritis, including rheumatoid arthritis.

How does it work?
It reduces inflammation in the bowel and joints. In the bowel, it is broken down into active substances that help control inflammation; its exact action in arthritis is not fully understood.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the gastro-resistant tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Take it regularly and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, loss of appetite, headache, dizziness and skin rash may occur. Urine or skin may develop an orange-yellow discolouration.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to sulfonamides, salicylates or aspirin, and about liver or kidney problems, blood disorders, or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency. Regular blood, liver and kidney tests may be needed. Seek urgent medical help for severe rash, fever, sore throat, unusual bruising or bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Magnesium Elemental 200mg is used as a magnesium supplement to prevent or treat low magnesium levels when dietary intake is insufficient or supplementation is recommended.

How does it work?
Magnesium is an essential mineral that supports normal nerve and muscle function, energy production, and bone health.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow with water. Do not take more than recommended. The stated 200mg refers to the amount of elemental magnesium.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, loose stools, nausea, stomach discomfort, or abdominal cramps may occur, especially with higher amounts.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease. Magnesium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, including certain antibiotics, thyroid medicines, and medicines for osteoporosis; separate doses as advised. Seek medical advice if side effects are severe or persistent.

What is it used for?
Used as an eye lubricant to temporarily relieve dryness, burning, irritation and discomfort caused by dry eyes or exposure to wind, sun and similar conditions.

How does it work?
Polyethylene glycol and propylene glycol help lubricate the surface of the eye and reduce dryness and irritation.

How to take/use it
For use in the eyes only. Use as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface. Close the container properly after use.

Common side effects
Temporary blurred vision, mild stinging, burning or irritation after application.

Precautions
Do not use if the solution is discoloured or the container is damaged. Stop use and seek medical advice if eye pain, vision changes, worsening irritation or persistent symptoms occur. Do not share the product with others.

What is it used for?
Tacrolimus 0.03% ointment is used to treat moderate to severe eczema (atopic dermatitis), especially when other topical treatments are not suitable or have not worked well.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of certain immune cells in the skin, helping to reduce inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Use it only on the affected areas, wash hands before and after application, and avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not cover the area with tight or airtight dressings unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Burning, warmth, stinging, itching or redness at the application site, usually during the first few days. Increased sensitivity to sunlight may also occur.

Precautions
Use only on eczema-affected skin and do not apply to infected skin unless advised by a doctor. Avoid excessive sunlight, sunbeds and ultraviolet treatment; use sun protection. Tell the doctor if swollen glands, a skin infection or worsening symptoms develop. Avoid use in children under 2 years unless specifically prescribed. Do not use continuously for longer than recommended or without medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Tacrolimus 0.1% ointment is used to treat moderate to severe eczema (atopic dermatitis), especially when other topical treatments are not suitable or have not worked well.

How does it work?
It reduces overactivity of the immune response in the skin, helping to reduce inflammation, itching and eczema symptoms.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before and after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Do not cover the treated area with airtight or tight dressings unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, warmth, redness or itching where the ointment is applied. These effects are often temporary.

Precautions
Avoid unnecessary exposure to sunlight, tanning beds and ultraviolet treatment; use protective clothing and sunscreen as advised. Do not apply to infected skin unless directed by a doctor. Avoid using it in people with a weakened immune system unless prescribed by a specialist. Seek medical advice if skin infection develops or symptoms worsen. Use only for the prescribed period and as directed.

What is it used for?
Tamsulosin is used to relieve urinary symptoms caused by an enlarged prostate, such as difficulty starting urination, weak or interrupted urine flow, frequent urination, and an urgent need to urinate.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the prostate and the opening of the bladder. This helps urine flow more easily.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with water and do not crush or chew it. Take it consistently as directed by the doctor. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, runny or blocked nose, weakness, and changes in ejaculation may occur.

Precautions
It may cause dizziness or a drop in blood pressure, especially when standing up; rise slowly and avoid driving if affected. Inform the doctor before cataract or glaucoma surgery, as this medicine can affect the eye during surgery. Tell the doctor about any allergy, severe dizziness, or fainting. Seek medical help for a prolonged or painful erection.

What is it used for?
Tamsulosin is used to relieve urinary symptoms caused by an enlarged prostate, such as difficulty starting urination, weak urine flow, frequent urination and a feeling that the bladder has not emptied fully.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles in the prostate and at the opening of the bladder. This helps urine flow more easily.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the product label or prescriber's instructions about when to take it and take it consistently as directed.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, runny or blocked nose, and ejaculation problems may occur. Dizziness may be more noticeable when standing up.

Precautions
Rise slowly from sitting or lying down to reduce the risk of dizziness or fainting. Avoid driving or operating machinery if affected. Tell the doctor before cataract or glaucoma surgery, as tamsulosin can affect the eye during surgery. Seek medical help for severe allergic symptoms or fainting.

What is it used for?
Used in adult men to treat symptoms of an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia, or BPH), such as difficulty starting urination, weak urine flow, frequent urination and incomplete bladder emptying.

How does it work?
Tamsulosin relaxes the muscles around the prostate and bladder outlet to improve urine flow. Dutasteride lowers the hormone that contributes to prostate growth and may gradually reduce prostate size.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, reduced sex drive, difficulty getting or maintaining an erection, ejaculation problems or reduced semen, and breast tenderness or enlargement.

Precautions
This medicine may cause dizziness or a drop in blood pressure when standing; rise slowly and avoid driving if affected. Tell the doctor before cataract surgery. Dutasteride can reduce PSA blood-test results, so inform healthcare professionals that it is being taken. Pregnant women or women who may become pregnant should not handle leaking capsules. Seek medical advice for severe allergy, fainting, or inability to pass urine.

What is it used for?
Teicoplanin is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections caused by susceptible Gram-positive bacteria, including infections of the skin and soft tissues, bones and joints, lungs, blood, or heart valves. It is usually used in hospitals or under specialist supervision.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from multiplying.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, body weight, kidney function, and response to treatment. Do not self-administer or stop treatment early.

Common side effects
Injection-site pain or redness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, rash, itching, and fever may occur. More serious reactions can include allergic reactions, kidney problems, hearing changes, or changes in blood-cell counts.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing problems, blood disorders, or any previous allergy to teicoplanin, vancomycin, or other medicines. Kidney function, blood counts, and sometimes hearing may need monitoring, especially during prolonged treatment or in people with kidney problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, blistering, or persistent severe diarrhoea. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only if specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Teicoplanin is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections caused by susceptible Gram-positive bacteria, including certain skin and soft-tissue, bone and joint, bloodstream, heart-valve and urinary infections. It may also be used for infections caused by bacteria such as MRSA when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making their protective cell wall, which kills or prevents the growth of the bacteria.

How to take/use it
Teicoplanin is given as an injection or infusion by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Complete the prescribed course and do not self-administer it.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site, skin rash or itching, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache and fever may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any allergy to teicoplanin or similar antibiotics, kidney disease, hearing problems or blood disorders. Kidney function, blood counts and hearing may need monitoring during treatment, especially with prolonged use or high doses. Seek urgent medical attention for severe rash, breathing difficulty, severe diarrhoea, unusual bleeding or reduced urination. Tell the doctor if pregnant, breastfeeding or taking other medicines that may affect the kidneys or hearing.

What is it used for?
Telmisartan 20 mg is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of serious problems such as stroke and heart disease.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of angiotensin II, a substance that narrows blood vessels. This helps the blood vessels relax and lowers blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber's instructions and do not take a double dose.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, back pain, diarrhoea, and tiredness may occur. Dizziness may be more noticeable when standing up.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, or high potassium levels. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for severe dizziness, fainting, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of a hormone called angiotensin II, which normally narrows blood vessels. This helps the blood vessels relax and lowers blood pressure.

What is it used for?
Telmisartan 40 mg is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It may also be prescribed to help reduce the risk of certain cardiovascular problems in some high-risk adults.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of angiotensin II, a substance that tightens blood vessels. This helps the blood vessels relax and lowers blood pressure.

Take it exactly as prescribed, usually at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet with water; it can generally be taken with or without food. Do not stop it without medical advice.

Do not use during pregnancy, especially after the first trimester, unless specifically advised by a doctor. What is it used for?
Telmisartan 40 mg is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It may also be prescribed to help reduce the risk of certain heart and blood vessel problems in some high-risk adults.

It blocks the action of angiotensin II, a substance that narrows blood vessels and raises blood pressure. This helps the blood vessels relax and lowers blood pressure.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
Telmisartan blocks the action of a substance that tightens blood vessels. Amlodipine relaxes and widens the blood vessels, helping blood flow more easily and lowering blood pressure.

Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop taking it or change the dose without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Dizziness, headache, tiredness, flushing, palpitations, and swelling of the ankles or feet may occur.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
Telmisartan relaxes blood vessels by blocking the action of a hormone that causes them to narrow. Hydrochlorothiazide helps the kidneys remove excess salt and water through urine, which also lowers blood pressure.

Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, diabetes, gout, or any electrolyte problem. Avoid use during pregnancy; contact a doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Controlling blood pressure helps reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke and other blood vessel problems.

How does it work?
Telmisartan relaxes and widens blood vessels by blocking the action of a hormone that raises blood pressure. Amlodipine also relaxes blood vessels, helping the heart pump blood more easily and lowering blood pressure.

This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It helps lower the risk of complications caused by uncontrolled blood pressure.

Telmisartan blocks the action of a substance that narrows blood vessels, helping them relax. Metoprolol slows the heart rate and reduces the heart's workload, which lowers blood pressure.

What is it used for?
Teneligliptin is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It may be used alone or with other diabetes medicines as prescribed.

It is a DPP-4 inhibitor that helps the body release more insulin when blood sugar is high and reduces the release of hormones that raise blood sugar.

Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Take it at the same time each day if possible. Do not stop it or take an extra dose without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach discomfort and symptoms of low blood sugar, especially when taken with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

What is it used for?
