How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food, and swallow it with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Continue the recommended diet, exercise and blood sugar monitoring.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, vomiting, loss of appetite, headache and symptoms of low blood sugar such as sweating, shakiness or dizziness.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems, heart failure, heavy alcohol use, pancreatitis, or any planned surgery or contrast-dye scan. Seek medical help for severe or persistent vomiting, abdominal pain, breathing difficulty, unusual weakness or yellowing of the skin. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice. Kidney function may need monitoring.

What is it used for?
Teneligliptin + Metformin SR is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes.

How does it work?
Teneligliptin helps the body release more insulin after meals and reduces the release of hormones that raise blood sugar. Metformin reduces sugar production by the liver and helps the body use insulin better.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole; do not crush, chew or split it. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, indigestion, loss of appetite, headache and a metallic taste may occur. Low blood sugar is possible, especially when used with other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about kidney or liver disease, heart failure, heavy alcohol use, or a history of pancreatitis. Seek medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, breathing difficulty, unusual weakness or severe vomiting. Kidney function may need monitoring, and metformin may require temporary interruption around some contrast-dye tests. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken and during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Terbinafine 250 mg is used to treat fungal infections of the nails and certain fungal infections of the skin, such as athlete’s foot, ringworm and jock itch. It is usually prescribed when treatment by mouth is needed.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making ergosterol, an essential part of their cell membranes. This causes the fungus to stop growing and die.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not take an extra dose if a dose is missed; follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, indigestion, skin rash and changes in taste or smell may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Liver function tests may be needed, especially during longer treatment. Stop taking it and seek medical help if yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent nausea, severe rash, facial swelling or breathing difficulty occurs. Report significant or persistent changes in taste or smell, or unusual tiredness, to the doctor.

What is it used for?
Monosulfiram 5% Soap is used on the skin to treat scabies, a contagious infestation caused by tiny mites.

How does it work?
It acts as a scabicide, helping to kill scabies mites on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use the soap exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and wash hands after use. Do not use on broken or severely irritated skin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Skin irritation, redness, burning, itching, dryness or rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid swallowing the soap. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic rash develops. Keep away from children. Scabies can spread through close contact, so household members may also need medical assessment.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to help relieve bruising, swelling and discomfort from minor soft-tissue injuries, and to support treatment of superficial inflammation or clotting in veins, such as superficial thrombophlebitis. It is not a treatment for deep vein thrombosis.

How does it work?
Heparin helps reduce clot formation in superficial tissues and veins. Benzyl nicotinate increases local blood flow, which may help reduce congestion and support absorption of bruising.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, intact skin as directed by a doctor or the product label. Gently spread it without vigorous massage, especially over a painful or inflamed vein. Do not apply to open wounds, broken or infected skin, eyes or mucous membranes. Wash hands after use.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site. Stop using it if severe irritation or an allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to heparin or any ingredient. Avoid use on open wounds or bleeding skin. Seek medical advice before use if there is a bleeding disorder, low platelet count, or use of blood-thinning medicines. Seek urgent medical care for sudden leg swelling, severe pain, chest pain or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Thyroxine is used as thyroid hormone replacement to treat an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism). It replaces the hormone that the thyroid gland does not produce in sufficient amounts.

How does it work?
It supplies synthetic thyroid hormone, helping restore normal thyroid hormone levels and support the body's metabolism and energy functions.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually on an empty stomach with water. Take it at the same time each day and do not stop or change the dose without medical advice. Keep calcium, iron, antacids and some other medicines separate from thyroxine as advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Regular blood tests may be needed to adjust treatment.

Common side effects
Side effects are more likely if the dose is too high and may include palpitations, fast heartbeat, trembling, nervousness, sweating, difficulty sleeping, headache, diarrhoea and weight loss.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, diabetes, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice for chest pain, severe or persistent palpitations, or marked shortness of breath. Do not use thyroxine for weight loss. Many medicines and supplements can affect its absorption, so provide a complete medicine list to the doctor or pharmacist.

What is it used for?
Thyroxine sodium is used as thyroid hormone replacement to treat an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism). It may also be prescribed to help prevent the thyroid from becoming underactive after certain thyroid treatments.

How does it work?
It supplies a synthetic form of thyroxine (T4), a hormone normally produced by the thyroid gland. The body converts it into active thyroid hormone to help regulate metabolism and other body functions.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually consistently at the same time each day. It is commonly taken on an empty stomach with water, but follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist. Do not change the strength or stop treatment without medical advice. Calcium, iron and some antacids can reduce its absorption, so they may need to be taken separately.

Common side effects
Side effects are more likely if the dose is too high and may include palpitations, fast heartbeat, nervousness, tremors, sweating, difficulty sleeping, headache, diarrhoea and unexplained weight loss.

Precautions
Regular blood tests are needed to check thyroid hormone levels and adjust treatment. Tell the doctor about heart disease, diabetes, adrenal problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice for chest pain, severe palpitations or breathlessness. Do not use thyroxine for weight loss. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines, especially calcium, iron, antacids and medicines affecting the heart or blood clotting.

What is it used for?
Thyroxine 50 mcg is used as thyroid hormone replacement to treat an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism). It may also be prescribed for other thyroid conditions under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It provides levothyroxine, a synthetic form of the thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4), helping restore normal thyroid hormone levels and body functions.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Swallow with water on an empty stomach, usually before breakfast, and take it consistently at the same time each day. Keep calcium, iron and antacid products at least 4 hours apart unless advised otherwise. Regular blood tests may be needed.

Common side effects
When the dose is too high, symptoms may include fast or irregular heartbeat, nervousness, tremors, sweating, difficulty sleeping, headache, diarrhoea and weight loss.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, diabetes, adrenal problems or pregnancy. Seek medical advice for chest pain, severe or irregular heartbeat, marked shaking or breathlessness. Many medicines and supplements can affect absorption, so inform the doctor or pharmacist about all products being used.

What is it used for?
Thyroxine 75 mcg is used to replace the thyroid hormone that the body lacks, mainly in people with an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism). It may also be prescribed for certain other thyroid conditions under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It supplies a synthetic form of thyroxine, a hormone normally produced by the thyroid gland. This helps restore normal body functions affected by low thyroid hormone levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually once daily on an empty stomach, consistently at the same time. It is commonly taken 30–60 minutes before breakfast with water. Keep calcium, iron, and antacid medicines separate from thyroxine by the interval advised by the doctor or pharmacist. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular blood tests may be needed.

Common side effects
When the dose is higher than needed, possible effects include palpitations, tremor, nervousness, difficulty sleeping, increased sweating, headache, diarrhoea, and weight loss.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, diabetes, or a history of thyroid problems. Seek medical advice for chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, or severe breathlessness. The dose often needs monitoring during pregnancy. Thyroxine should not be used for weight loss unless specifically prescribed for a thyroid condition.

What is it used for?
Ticagrelor is an antiplatelet medicine used with prescribed treatment to reduce the risk of blood clots, heart attack and stroke in people with acute coronary syndrome or a previous heart attack.

How does it work?
It prevents blood platelets from sticking together and forming harmful clots in the blood vessels.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with the accompanying medicines advised by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Bleeding or bruising more easily, nosebleeds, shortness of breath, headache, dizziness and nausea.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any bleeding disorder, previous bleeding in the brain, liver problems, planned surgery or dental treatment. Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood or severe breathing difficulty. Do not take other medicines that increase bleeding risk unless approved by the doctor.

What is it used for?
Tobramycin is an antibiotic used to treat infections caused by susceptible bacteria. The exact infection and method of use depend on the product form and the prescriber's instructions.

How does it work?
It stops bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents them from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only in the form and by the route prescribed. Follow the label or doctor's instructions carefully, and do not change the amount or stop treatment early without medical advice. Do not use it for viral or fungal infections unless specifically advised.

Common side effects
Side effects depend on the product form. Local irritation, redness, itching or discomfort may occur with topical use. Other side effects can occur with medicines absorbed into the body.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to tobramycin or other aminoglycoside antibiotics. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens, does not improve, or if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur, such as swelling, breathing difficulty or widespread rash.

What is it used for?
Tobramycin 0.3% w/v is an antibacterial eye medicine used to treat bacterial eye infections, such as bacterial conjunctivitis. It does not treat viral or fungal eye infections.

How does it work?
It kills or stops the growth of bacteria that cause eye infections.

How to take/use it
Use it in the affected eye(s) exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before use and do not let the dropper tip touch the eye or any surface. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Remove contact lenses before use and follow the product instructions about when to replace them.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, burning, irritation, redness, itching or blurred vision may occur after use.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to tobramycin or other aminoglycoside antibiotics. Stop using it and seek medical help if there is severe swelling, rash, breathing difficulty or worsening eye pain and redness. Seek medical advice if symptoms do not improve or vision becomes affected.

What is it used for?
Tofacitinib is used to treat autoimmune inflammatory conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and ulcerative colitis, usually when other treatments have not worked well or are not suitable.

How does it work?
It blocks Janus kinase (JAK) enzymes involved in immune-system signalling. This helps reduce the inflammation and abnormal immune activity causing symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, with or without food. Swallow the tablet as directed and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Regular blood tests and medical check-ups may be needed.

Common side effects
Upper respiratory infections, headache, diarrhoea, nausea, acne and increased cholesterol levels may occur.

Precautions
Tofacitinib can increase the risk of serious infections, including tuberculosis, shingles and other infections. Inform the doctor about any infection, tuberculosis or hepatitis history, cancer, heart disease or blood clots. Seek medical help for fever, persistent cough, painful skin rash, chest pain or sudden breathing difficulty. Avoid live vaccines and tell the doctor about all medicines being taken. Blood counts, liver function and cholesterol may need monitoring.

What is it used for?
Tolperisone is a muscle relaxant used to relieve painful muscle stiffness, spasms and tightness, including those related to musculoskeletal conditions.

How does it work?
It reduces excessive nerve signals that cause muscles to tighten, helping relax stiff or spasming muscles.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably after food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, muscle weakness, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to tolperisone or similar medicines. Stop taking it and seek urgent medical help if signs of an allergy occur, such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty or severe dizziness. Use only with medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding, and inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems or myasthenia gravis. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizzy or weak.

What is it used for?
Tolvaptan is used under medical supervision to treat low blood sodium levels (hyponatraemia) and, in selected patients, to slow the worsening of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). The exact use depends on the doctor's prescription.

How does it work?
It blocks the effect of vasopressin, a hormone that makes the kidneys retain water. This helps the kidneys remove excess water while retaining sodium and, in ADPKD, may slow the growth of kidney cysts.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Do not change the dose, limit or increase fluid intake, or stop treatment without medical advice. Treatment for low sodium may need to be started and monitored in a hospital, and regular blood tests may be required.

Common side effects
Thirst, increased urination, dry mouth, dizziness, headache, nausea, tiredness and dehydration. Changes in liver tests may occur, particularly during long-term treatment.

Precautions
This medicine requires medical monitoring. Seek medical advice for severe thirst, very little urine, marked dizziness, confusion, or symptoms of liver problems such as unusual tiredness, loss of appetite, nausea, dark urine, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or pain in the upper right abdomen. Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease and all other medicines. Avoid alcohol if it worsens dizziness or dehydration. It should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to remove excess fluid from the body, helping reduce swelling (oedema) that may occur with heart, liver or kidney conditions. It may also be prescribed for high blood pressure when considered appropriate by a doctor.

How does it work?
Torsemide helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water through urine. Amiloride also increases fluid removal while helping reduce potassium loss caused by some diuretics.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, with water. Take it at the same time each day and do not change the dose or stop it without medical advice. Because it increases urination, follow the prescribed timing and avoid taking extra doses.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, headache, nausea, weakness, dehydration and low blood pressure. Changes in blood potassium or other body salts may also occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially with kidney or liver disease, low blood pressure, dehydration, diabetes or gout. Blood pressure, kidney function and blood electrolyte levels may need monitoring. Do not use potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical advice for severe weakness, fainting, irregular heartbeat, very little urine or signs of dehydration.

What is it used for?
Torsemide is a diuretic used to remove excess fluid from the body. It is commonly used for swelling (oedema) related to heart failure and may also be prescribed for fluid retention associated with kidney or liver problems. It can also help lower high blood pressure.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water through urine, reducing fluid buildup and helping lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. It may increase urination, so follow the timing advised by the doctor. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, headache, low blood pressure, dehydration, nausea, and changes in blood salt levels such as low potassium or sodium.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially with kidney or liver disease, low blood pressure, dehydration, gout, or diabetes. Blood pressure, kidney function, and electrolyte levels may need monitoring. Seek medical advice for severe dizziness, fainting, unusual weakness, muscle cramps, or very little urine. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, particularly other diuretics, blood-pressure medicines, lithium, or regular painkillers such as ibuprofen.

What is it used for?
Torsemide 20 mg is a diuretic (“water tablet”) used to remove excess fluid from the body. It is commonly used for swelling caused by heart, kidney or liver problems, and may also be prescribed to help control high blood pressure.

How does it work?
It helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water through urine. This reduces fluid buildup and can lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. It is generally taken earlier in the day because it increases urination. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, headache, low blood pressure, dehydration, weakness, and changes in body salts such as low potassium or sodium.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially with kidney or liver disease, low blood pressure, dehydration, diabetes, gout, or an electrolyte imbalance. Drink fluids as advised by the prescriber. Rise slowly if dizzy. Medical monitoring of blood pressure, kidney function and electrolytes may be needed. Seek medical help for severe weakness, fainting, confusion, very little urine, or an irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
This combination helps remove excess fluid from the body and is commonly used for swelling or fluid buildup related to heart, liver, or kidney conditions. It may also be prescribed to help control high blood pressure.

How does it work?
Torsemide helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water through urine. Spironolactone also removes excess fluid while helping reduce the loss of potassium.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. It may increase urination, so follow the prescriber's instructions about timing. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, low blood pressure, dehydration, nausea, weakness, headache, and changes in blood potassium or sodium levels. Spironolactone may cause breast tenderness or enlargement.

Precautions
Regular monitoring of blood pressure, kidney function, and blood electrolytes may be needed. Use only under medical supervision if there is kidney disease, liver disease, dehydration, or low blood pressure. Avoid potassium supplements and potassium-containing salt substitutes unless specifically advised. Seek medical help for severe weakness, confusion, fainting, irregular heartbeat, or very little urination.

What is it used for?
This medicine helps remove excess salt and water from the body and is used to reduce swelling (oedema), especially when related to heart, liver or kidney conditions. It may also be prescribed for high blood pressure in some patients.

How does it work?
Torsemide increases the removal of salt and water through urine. Spironolactone also removes excess fluid while helping to prevent excessive potassium loss.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. As it increases urination, avoid taking it close to bedtime unless advised. Do not change the dose or stop it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, low blood pressure, dehydration, weakness, nausea, and changes in blood potassium or sodium levels. Spironolactone may cause breast tenderness or enlargement and menstrual changes.

Precautions
Regular monitoring of blood pressure, kidney function and blood potassium may be needed. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, or low blood pressure. Avoid potassium supplements and potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. Seek medical help for severe weakness, fainting, confusion, very low urine output, or irregular heartbeat. Discuss use during pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor.

What is it used for?
Tranexamic acid is used to reduce or prevent excessive bleeding. It is commonly prescribed for heavy menstrual bleeding and may also be used for certain other bleeding problems under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It helps keep blood clots from breaking down too quickly, which helps control bleeding.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. The dose and treatment duration depend on the reason for use.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor before use if there is a history of blood clots, kidney disease, seizures, vision problems or unexplained irregular bleeding. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, leg swelling or pain, sudden weakness, or changes in vision. Use during pregnancy or with hormonal contraceptives only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Tranexamic acid injection is used to prevent or reduce excessive bleeding, including bleeding during or after surgery, childbirth, injury, dental procedures, or heavy menstrual bleeding. It is given when treatment by injection is considered necessary.

How does it work?
It helps prevent blood clots from breaking down too quickly. This supports the body in stopping bleeding.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or nurse, usually into a vein. The dose and treatment duration depend on the cause and severity of bleeding, kidney function, and medical condition. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and low blood pressure if the injection is given too quickly.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of blood clots, kidney disease, seizures, or problems with colour vision. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, painful swelling in a leg, seizures, or changes in vision. It may not be suitable in some conditions involving abnormal blood clotting and should be used only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to reduce heavy menstrual bleeding and relieve period pain.

How does it work?
Tranexamic acid helps prevent the breakdown of blood clots, reducing menstrual blood loss. Mefenamic acid reduces the substances that cause pain, inflammation and menstrual cramps.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. It is generally taken during menstrual bleeding and should be swallowed with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more than the prescribed amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, indigestion, stomach pain, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about a history of blood clots, kidney disease, stomach ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding. Avoid use if allergic to mefenamic acid, tranexamic acid or similar medicines. Do not combine with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin unless advised by a doctor. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, leg swelling or vision changes.

What is it used for?
Triamcinolone acetonide is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactive immune or allergic reactions. Its exact use depends on the prescribed formulation and may include inflammatory skin, joint, or other medical conditions.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and allergic or immune reactions.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The route of use depends on the formulation; it may be given by injection or used on the skin. Do not self-inject, apply, or use it in another way unless specifically instructed.

Common side effects
Side effects depend on the route and duration of treatment. They may include pain or irritation at the application or injection site, increased blood sugar, increased blood pressure, stomach upset, mood or sleep changes, and thinning of the skin with prolonged use.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, infections, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, or a history of mental health problems. Corticosteroids can reduce resistance to infection and may mask infection symptoms. Do not stop prolonged treatment suddenly unless advised. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Linagliptin 5 mg is used to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes, along with a suitable diet and exercise. It may be used alone or with other diabetes medicines.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called DPP-4, which helps the body release more insulin after meals and reduce excess glucagon. This helps lower blood sugar levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. It may be taken with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not take an extra dose if a dose is missed; follow the doctor’s instructions.

Common side effects
Nasopharyngitis (runny or blocked nose and sore throat), cough, diarrhoea, headache and low blood sugar, especially when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis. Tell the doctor about any previous pancreatitis, allergies to linagliptin, or severe kidney or liver problems. Seek medical advice for severe, persistent abdominal pain, serious allergic symptoms, severe joint pain or blistering skin. Low blood sugar may occur when used with insulin or sulfonylureas; the doctor may need to adjust those medicines.

What is it used for?
This combination is used with diet and exercise to help control blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes.

How does it work?
Linagliptin helps increase insulin release when blood sugar is high and reduces glucagon. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and improves insulin sensitivity.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with meals if directed. Do not stop diabetes treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach discomfort and reduced appetite may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems and alcohol use. Seek urgent help for unusual weakness, breathing difficulty or severe illness, which may indicate a rare serious reaction.

What is it used for?
Amitriptyline is prescribed for depression and, often at lower strengths, for nerve pain and prevention of recurring migraine. The exact use depends on the doctor's prescription.

How does it work?
It changes the activity of certain chemical messengers in the brain, including serotonin and noradrenaline. This can improve mood and reduce the way the nervous system processes pain.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow it with water. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop treatment suddenly without medical advice. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, increased sweating, weight gain and difficulty passing urine.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease or irregular heartbeat, glaucoma, difficulty urinating, seizures, liver problems, bipolar disorder, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid alcohol and check before using other medicines, especially antidepressants, sedatives or medicines that affect heart rhythm. Seek urgent medical help for severe allergic reactions, fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe eye pain, or thoughts of self-harm.

What is it used for?
Amitriptyline is used to treat depression. At lower doses, it is also commonly prescribed for nerve-related pain and to help prevent migraine attacks.

How does it work?
It increases the activity of certain chemical messengers in the brain, which can improve mood and reduce abnormal pain signals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with water, and do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or using machinery until its effect is known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, sweating, nausea and weight gain.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, irregular heartbeat, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, seizures, liver problems or bipolar disorder. Avoid alcohol and check before using other medicines, especially sleeping medicines, antidepressants or medicines that affect heart rhythm. Seek urgent help for severe allergic reactions, fainting, abnormal heartbeat, severe confusion or thoughts of self-harm. Keep this medicine safely away from children, as overdose can be dangerous.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary supplement to provide ginseng, vitamins, minerals and antioxidant ingredients when dietary intake may be insufficient. It supports normal body functions and general nutritional wellness; it is not a treatment for a specific disease.

How does it work?
The vitamins and minerals provide nutrients needed for normal body processes. The antioxidant ingredients help protect cells from oxidative damage, while ginseng is a herbal supplement ingredient.

How to take/use it
Swallow the softgel exactly as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount or use it as a replacement for a balanced diet.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, stomach upset, headache, or difficulty sleeping. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Check with a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is diabetes, a bleeding disorder, or kidney or liver disease. Seek medical advice if taking blood thinners, diabetes medicines, or other regular medicines, as ginseng and some vitamins or minerals may interact with them. Avoid taking other multivitamin products at the same time unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Flavoxate is used to relieve urinary symptoms caused by bladder or urinary-tract spasms, such as frequent urination, urgency, painful urination and bladder discomfort. It may be prescribed for conditions such as cystitis or irritation related to urinary procedures, but it does not treat a urinary infection itself.

How does it work?
It relaxes the smooth muscles of the bladder and urinary tract, helping reduce unwanted bladder contractions and urinary urgency.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Continue any antibiotic or other treatment prescribed for an underlying urinary infection.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, blurred vision, headache, dizziness and drowsiness.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine or suspected urinary retention, or blockage of the stomach or intestines. Dizziness, drowsiness or blurred vision may occur; avoid driving or operating machinery until the effects are known. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice for fever, blood in the urine, severe pain or worsening urinary symptoms.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat bacterial urinary tract infections (UTIs) and help relieve bladder-related symptoms such as frequent urination, urgency and painful bladder spasms.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin kills bacteria that cause the infection. Flavoxate relaxes the muscles of the bladder and helps reduce spasms, urgency and frequency.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water and do not take it with antacids or mineral supplements unless advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, dizziness, headache, dry mouth, constipation and blurred vision may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ofloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics. Seek medical advice for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe diarrhoea, palpitations or serious mood or nervous-system changes. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney disease, seizures, heart-rhythm problems or previous tendon disorders. Avoid driving if dizzy or if vision is blurred.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used to treat certain liver and bile-flow disorders, including primary biliary cholangitis. It may also be prescribed to dissolve certain cholesterol gallstones when appropriate.

How does it work?
It improves the flow and composition of bile, helping reduce the buildup of harmful bile acids and cholesterol in the liver and gallbladder.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with food or as directed by the doctor. Swallow with water and do not stop treatment or change the dose without medical advice. Regular liver tests may be needed.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort or pain, nausea, and indigestion may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is blockage of the bile ducts, acute gallbladder inflammation, or severe liver disease. Tell the doctor about other medicines being taken, especially antacids or cholesterol-binding medicines. Seek medical advice if severe abdominal pain, persistent diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes occurs.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used to dissolve certain cholesterol gallstones and to improve bile flow in some long-term liver conditions, such as primary biliary cholangitis. It does not work for every type of gallstone.

How does it work?
It changes the composition of bile, helping reduce cholesterol buildup and improve the flow of bile through the liver and bile ducts.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the capsule or tablet with water and follow the medicine label regarding food. Treatment may require regular liver tests and may continue for a long period; do not stop it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, abdominal pain or discomfort, nausea, and indigestion may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about gallbladder or bile-duct blockage, severe abdominal pain, jaundice, or other liver problems. Regular liver-function monitoring may be needed. Seek medical advice if side effects are severe or persistent, or if a rash or breathing difficulty develops.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used to improve bile flow in certain liver and bile-related conditions. It may also be prescribed to dissolve certain cholesterol gallstones when suitable.

How does it work?
It makes bile less harmful to liver cells and improves the flow of bile. It can also reduce the cholesterol content of bile, helping dissolve some cholesterol gallstones.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with water. Swallow the sustained-release medicine whole; do not crush or chew it unless advised. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort or pain, nausea, vomiting, and constipation may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is severe liver disease, blockage of the bile ducts, gallbladder inflammation, or calcified gallstones. Liver function may need monitoring during treatment. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other medicines, particularly aluminium-containing antacids or medicines that bind bile acids. Seek medical advice if severe or persistent abdominal pain or diarrhoea occurs.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used to treat certain cholestatic liver diseases, including primary biliary cholangitis, and may be prescribed to help dissolve some cholesterol gallstones.

How does it work?
It improves the flow and composition of bile and reduces the amount of cholesterol in bile. This can help protect liver cells and gradually dissolve suitable cholesterol gallstones.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the sustained-release medicine whole; do not crush or chew it. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated and require medical supervision.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, loose stools, abdominal discomfort, nausea, or indigestion. Itching may occur in some people.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Regular liver-function tests may be needed. Tell the doctor about gallbladder or bile-duct blockage, acute gallbladder inflammation, liver disease, pregnancy, or other medicines being taken. It does not dissolve all types of gallstones.

What is it used for?
This medicine is mainly used to prevent and control seizures in epilepsy. It may also be prescribed for bipolar disorder or to prevent migraine headaches, depending on the doctor's advice.

How does it work?
It helps reduce excessive electrical activity in the brain by increasing the effect of calming chemical signals, helping to prevent seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Swallow the controlled-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop treatment suddenly, even if feeling well. If it causes stomach upset, taking it with food may help.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, sleepiness, dizziness, tremors, increased appetite or weight gain, and hair thinning or hair loss.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically directed by a specialist, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Tell the doctor about liver disease, pancreatitis, bleeding problems, or any other medicines being used. Regular blood and liver tests may be needed. Seek urgent medical help for severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, yellowing of the skin or eyes, unusual bruising or bleeding, or marked confusion. Avoid driving if drowsy or dizzy, and do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Sodium valproate is mainly used to control and prevent seizures in epilepsy. It may also be prescribed for certain mood disorders or migraine prevention, but its use depends on the doctor's assessment.

How does it work?
It reduces excessive electrical activity in the brain and helps stabilise nerve signals, helping to prevent seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. This controlled-release tablet should be swallowed whole with water and should not be crushed or chewed. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, sleepiness, dizziness, tremor, increased appetite or weight gain, and hair thinning or changes in hair texture.

Precautions
Valproate can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Women and girls who could become pregnant should discuss effective pregnancy prevention and pregnancy risks with a doctor before using it. Tell the doctor about liver disease, pancreatitis, bleeding or blood disorders, or kidney problems. Seek medical help for severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, yellowing of the skin or eyes, unusual bruising, or worsening drowsiness. Avoid alcohol and do not drive if dizzy or sleepy. Do not stop treatment suddenly.

What is it used for?
Sodium valproate with valproic acid is mainly used to control seizures in epilepsy. It may also be prescribed for bipolar disorder or to prevent migraine attacks, depending on the doctor's advice.

How does it work?
It increases the activity of calming chemical signals in the brain and helps reduce abnormal electrical activity that can cause seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. Swallow the controlled-release tablet whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop taking it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, drowsiness, dizziness, tremor, weight gain and hair thinning or hair loss may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a specialist, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Tell the doctor about liver disease, pancreatitis, bleeding problems or a low platelet count. Seek urgent medical help for severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, yellowing of the skin or eyes, unusual bruising or bleeding, severe rash, or worsening mood or suicidal thoughts. Avoid alcohol and tell the doctor about all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Sacubitril 49 mg and valsartan 51 mg is used to treat certain types of long-term heart failure, particularly heart failure with reduced pumping strength. It helps reduce the risk of worsening heart failure and hospitalisation when prescribed as part of an appropriate treatment plan.

How does it work?
Sacubitril helps increase substances that relax blood vessels and reduce fluid buildup. Valsartan blocks the effects of angiotensin II, helping blood vessels relax and reducing strain on the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, at the same times each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop it without medical advice. Regular checks of blood pressure, kidney function and blood potassium may be needed.

Common side effects
Low blood pressure, dizziness, increased blood potassium, changes in kidney function and cough may occur.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy; contact a doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing, as these may indicate angioedema. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, low blood pressure, high potassium, or previous angioedema. Do not take it with an ACE inhibitor; a suitable gap is required when switching between these medicines. Check with a doctor before using potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes or medicines that may affect kidney function.

What is it used for?
Sacubitril and valsartan are used together to treat certain types of long-term heart failure. They help reduce strain on the heart and may lower the risk of hospitalisation due to worsening heart failure.

How does it work?
Sacubitril helps increase substances that relax blood vessels and reduce salt and fluid buildup. Valsartan blocks a hormone that narrows blood vessels and increases the workload on the heart.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually at the same times each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment without medical advice. Do not take it together with an ACE inhibitor; a suitable gap is needed when changing from an ACE inhibitor to this medicine.

Common side effects
Dizziness, low blood pressure, cough, increased potassium levels, and changes in kidney function may occur.

Precautions
This medicine may cause serious swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; seek urgent medical help if this occurs. It must not be used during pregnancy. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, high potassium levels, low blood pressure, or dehydration. Regular monitoring of blood pressure, kidney function, and potassium may be needed. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Venlafaxine is a prescription antidepressant used mainly to treat depression. It is also used for some anxiety disorders, including generalised anxiety disorder, social anxiety disorder and panic disorder.

How does it work?
It increases the levels of serotonin and noradrenaline in the brain, which helps regulate mood and anxiety.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with food and at about the same time each day. This prolonged-release capsule should be swallowed whole; do not crush, chew or open it. Do not stop taking it suddenly, as the dose usually needs to be reduced gradually under medical supervision.

Common side effects
Nausea, dry mouth, sweating, headache, dizziness, constipation, sleep problems, tiredness, reduced appetite and sexual difficulties may occur. Blood pressure may increase.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about high blood pressure, heart problems, seizures, glaucoma, liver or kidney disease, bipolar disorder, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for suicidal thoughts, severe agitation, unusually elevated mood, seizures, severe allergic reactions or symptoms of serotonin syndrome such as fever, confusion, muscle stiffness or fast heartbeat. Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor before taking other medicines, especially antidepressants, migraine medicines, blood thinners or anti-inflammatory painkillers.

What is it used for?
Venlafaxine prolonged-release capsules are prescription antidepressants used mainly to treat depression. They are also used for certain anxiety disorders, including generalised anxiety, social anxiety and panic disorder.

How does it work?
It increases the activity of serotonin and noradrenaline, chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood and anxiety.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with food and at the same time each day. Swallow the prolonged-release capsule whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop treatment suddenly, as this may cause withdrawal symptoms.

Common side effects
Nausea, dry mouth, sweating, headache, dizziness, constipation, reduced appetite, sleep problems and sexual difficulties may occur. Blood pressure can increase in some people.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about bipolar disorder, seizures, glaucoma, liver or kidney problems, high blood pressure, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for severe agitation, fever, confusion, muscle stiffness or diarrhoea, which may indicate serotonin syndrome. Report worsening depression, unusual mood changes or thoughts of self-harm immediately. Avoid alcohol and use caution when driving until the effects are known. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, especially MAO inhibitors and other antidepressants.

What is it used for?
Venlafaxine is a prescription medicine used mainly to treat depression and anxiety disorders.

How does it work?
It helps increase the activity of serotonin and noradrenaline, chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood and anxiety.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with food and at about the same time each day. Swallow the prolonged-release capsule whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop treatment suddenly, as withdrawal symptoms may occur.

Common side effects
Nausea, dry mouth, sweating, headache, dizziness, constipation, sleep problems, reduced appetite and sexual difficulties. It may also increase blood pressure.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about high blood pressure, heart problems, glaucoma, seizures, liver or kidney disease, bipolar disorder, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not use it with MAO inhibitors or certain other medicines without medical advice, as serious interactions can occur. Seek urgent help for suicidal thoughts, severe agitation, unusual mood elevation, or symptoms such as fever, confusion, muscle stiffness or a fast heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Micronized Purified Flavonoid Fraction is used to relieve symptoms of piles (haemorrhoids), such as pain, swelling, bleeding and discomfort. It may also be used for symptoms related to poor venous circulation, such as heavy, aching or swollen legs, when prescribed.

How does it work?
It helps improve the tone of veins and reduce excessive leakage from small blood vessels. This can support blood flow back from the affected area and reduce swelling and discomfort.

How to take/use it
Take it with food and swallow it with water, exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Digestive upset, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, headache, dizziness, skin rash or itching.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to this medicine or its ingredients. Seek medical advice for heavy or persistent bleeding, severe pain, or symptoms that do not improve. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop use and seek urgent help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur, such as facial swelling or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Betahistine is used to reduce vertigo (a spinning sensation) associated with Ménière’s disease. It may also help relieve related symptoms such as ringing in the ears (tinnitus) and hearing difficulty.

How does it work?
It acts on histamine receptors and is thought to improve blood flow and pressure regulation in the inner ear, helping reduce vertigo symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, indigestion, stomach discomfort or bloating.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to betahistine or if diagnosed with pheochromocytoma, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor if there is asthma or a history of stomach ulcers. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen or new hearing problems occur.

What is it used for?
Betahistine is mainly used to help relieve symptoms of Ménière’s disease and other inner-ear balance problems, including episodes of vertigo (spinning sensation), ringing in the ears and sometimes hearing difficulty.

How does it work?
It acts on histamine receptors and may help improve blood flow and pressure regulation in the inner ear, reducing balance-related symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food if it causes stomach discomfort. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach discomfort, bloating and headache. These are often mild and may improve when taken with food.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma, a current or past stomach ulcer, or pheochromocytoma. Avoid use if allergic to betahistine or any of its ingredients. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Sildenafil 100 mg is used to treat erectile dysfunction (difficulty getting or keeping an erection firm enough for sexual activity) in adult men.

How does it work?
It helps relax the blood vessels in the penis and increases blood flow during sexual stimulation, making an erection easier to achieve and maintain. It does not cause an erection without sexual stimulation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually before sexual activity. Do not take more than one dose in 24 hours. It may work more slowly after a heavy or high-fat meal. Do not use it with other erectile dysfunction medicines unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Headache, facial flushing, indigestion, blocked nose, dizziness and visual changes such as blurred or altered colour vision.

Precautions
Do not take sildenafil with nitrate medicines for chest pain or with riociguat, as this can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure. Seek medical advice before use if there is heart disease, low blood pressure, recent stroke or heart attack, or if taking alpha-blockers. Seek urgent medical help for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, sudden vision or hearing loss, chest pain, or severe dizziness. Avoid excessive alcohol.

What is it used for?
Vildagliptin is used to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes, usually along with diet, exercise and sometimes other diabetes medicines.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme called DPP-4, helping the body release more insulin when blood sugar is high and reduce the release of glucagon. This helps lower blood sugar levels.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow it with water. It may generally be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber's instructions and do not take an extra dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, dizziness, headache, constipation, and symptoms of a cold such as a sore throat or blocked nose may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when it is taken with certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver, kidney, heart or pancreatic problems before use. Liver function may need monitoring. Seek medical help for severe, persistent abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. This medicine is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

What is it used for?
Vildagliptin 50 mg + metformin 1000 mg is used with diet and exercise to control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Vildagliptin helps the body release insulin when blood sugar is high and reduces the release of glucagon. Metformin reduces sugar production by the liver and helps the body use insulin better.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with or after food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet with water and do not crush or chew it unless advised. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, loss of appetite, headache and dizziness may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, heart failure, heavy alcohol use, or a history of pancreatitis. Seek medical help for severe or persistent stomach pain, repeated vomiting, unusual weakness, breathing difficulty or extreme drowsiness. Kidney function may need monitoring, and long-term metformin use can reduce vitamin B12 levels. Inform the doctor before surgery, serious illness, dehydration or an X-ray scan using injected contrast dye.

What is it used for?
Vildagliptin + metformin is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Vildagliptin helps the body release more insulin when blood sugar is high and reduces excess sugar release after meals. Metformin reduces sugar production by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with or after food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet whole and do not stop treatment without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber's instructions rather than taking extra medicine.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, vomiting, headache, dizziness, or a metallic taste may occur. Low blood sugar is more likely when used with insulin or certain other diabetes medicines.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, heart failure, heavy alcohol use, or a history of pancreatitis before starting treatment. Kidney and liver function may need monitoring. Seek medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, unusual weakness, breathing difficulty, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Avoid excessive alcohol. Metformin may reduce vitamin B12 levels during long-term use. This medicine is not suitable for some people with severe kidney impairment or serious liver disease.

What is it used for?
Vitamin AD oil provides vitamins A and D. It is generally used to prevent or treat deficiency when supplementation is advised. The exact use depends on whether the product is meant for oral or topical use; check the product label.

How does it work?
Vitamin A supports normal vision, skin and immune function. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and supports healthy bones and muscles.

How to take/use it
Use only by the route and in the amount directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take or apply more than recommended.

Common side effects
Side effects depend on the route and amount used. Excessive oral use may cause nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness or dry skin.

Precautions
Do not use with other vitamin A or vitamin D products unless advised by a healthcare professional. Avoid excessive use, as these vitamins can build up in the body. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy, in children, or with liver or kidney disease. Do not swallow a product labelled for external use.

What is it used for?
Vitamin AD oil provides vitamins A and D when supplementation is recommended or prescribed. The supplied information does not confirm whether this product is intended for oral use or application to the skin, so its intended use should be checked on the product label.

How does it work?
Vitamin A supports normal vision, skin and immune function. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and supports healthy bones and muscles.

How to take/use it
Use only by the route and in the amount stated on the product label or advised by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount, and do not take or apply it if the intended route is unclear.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when used as directed. Excessive intake may cause nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, dry skin or constipation.

Precautions
Avoid combining it with other vitamin A or vitamin D supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy, in children, or with liver disease, kidney disease, high calcium levels or medicines affecting calcium or vitamin levels. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Vitamin A&D softgels are used to prevent or treat vitamin A or vitamin D deficiency when recommended by a healthcare professional. Vitamin A supports normal vision, skin and immune function, while vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and supports healthy bones.

How does it work?
They supply vitamins A and D that the body needs for vision, immunity, skin health, calcium absorption and bone health.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and check before using other supplements containing vitamins A or D.

Common side effects
Excessive intake may cause nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, headache or dizziness. Long-term or high-dose use can cause vitamin toxicity.

Precautions
Do not exceed the recommended dose. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy, especially because excess vitamin A may harm the unborn baby. Seek advice if there is kidney or liver disease, high calcium levels, or use of other vitamin A or D products. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Voglibose is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in people with type 2 diabetes, especially the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How does it work?
It slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates in the intestine. This helps reduce the increase in blood sugar after eating.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually immediately before a meal. Follow the prescribed dose and timing, and do not change or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort, loose stools or diarrhoea, and nausea may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is kidney or liver disease, or a history of intestinal or digestive problems. Low blood sugar may occur when voglibose is used with insulin or other diabetes medicines. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, vomiting, or diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Voglibose 0.3 mg is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in people with type 2 diabetes, especially the rise in blood sugar after meals.

How does it work?
It slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates in the intestine. This helps reduce the rise in blood sugar after eating.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually immediately before a meal. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. If a meal is skipped, follow the prescriber's instructions.

Common side effects
Gas, bloating, abdominal discomfort or pain, diarrhoea, constipation, nausea and indigestion.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is a blockage or serious disease of the intestine, or significant kidney or liver problems. The risk of low blood sugar may increase when used with insulin or other diabetes medicines. If low blood sugar occurs while using voglibose, use glucose or dextrose rather than table sugar (sucrose), as sucrose may work more slowly. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal symptoms.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It helps reduce blood glucose levels and improve diabetes control.

How does it work?
Glimepiride helps the pancreas release more insulin. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin, while voglibose slows the digestion and absorption of carbohydrates after meals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually with food. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. Follow the recommended diet, exercise plan and blood-glucose monitoring schedule.

Common side effects
Low blood sugar, nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, gas, bloating and loss of appetite. Low blood sugar may cause sweating, shaking, dizziness, hunger or weakness.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is kidney or liver disease, heart failure, heavy alcohol use or a history of severe low blood sugar. Avoid skipping meals, as this may increase the risk of low blood sugar. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent weakness, breathing difficulty, unusual sleepiness or severe abdominal symptoms. Tell the doctor before surgery, certain scans using contrast dye, or if pregnant or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Vonoprazan reduces excess stomach acid and is used for acid reflux (GERD), heartburn, erosive oesophagitis and other acid-related stomach conditions. It may also be prescribed with antibiotics for certain Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infections.

How does it work?
It blocks the final step involved in stomach-acid production, providing strong and long-lasting acid suppression.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, constipation, nausea, stomach pain, gas and headache may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being used. Seek medical advice for persistent symptoms, unexplained weight loss, difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood or black stools. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Diclofenac sodium is used to relieve pain and reduce swelling and inflammation in conditions such as arthritis, muscle pain, joint pain, and other painful musculoskeletal conditions.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain, swelling, and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food, to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more than prescribed or combine it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and heartburn.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to NSAIDs. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, chest pain, or swelling. Avoid use during the last three months of pregnancy; ask a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Diclofenac may interact with blood thinners and some blood pressure medicines.

What is it used for?
Diclofenac sodium is used to relieve pain, swelling and inflammation in conditions such as arthritis, muscle or joint injuries, and other painful conditions. Use it only for the condition and duration prescribed.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use the prescribed form and strength exactly as directed by a doctor. If it is an oral medicine, take it with or after food and water to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more than prescribed or combine it with other diclofenac or NSAID medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAIDs. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin rash. Avoid use during the last three months of pregnancy and ask a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially blood thinners, steroids, other NSAIDs, diuretics and medicines for blood pressure or kidney problems.

What is it used for?
Diclofenac sodium is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine used to relieve pain, swelling and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use it only as prescribed and follow the directions for the prescribed form and route. Do not use more than recommended. If it is an oral medicine, taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach irritation.

Common side effects
