What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat low calcium and vitamin D levels and to support bone health.

How does it work?
Calcium provides the mineral needed for strong bones and teeth. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and supports normal bone health.

How to take/use it
Take as directed on the label or by a doctor. Calcium carbonate is usually best taken with food. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Ask a doctor or pharmacist about the timing if taking other medicines or supplements.

Common side effects
Constipation, gas, bloating, nausea or stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Tell a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels or parathyroid disease. Avoid taking additional calcium or vitamin D supplements unless advised. Seek medical advice if persistent nausea, vomiting, unusual thirst, frequent urination or worsening constipation occurs.

What is it used for?
Used to help prevent or treat calcium and vitamin D deficiency and support strong bones. It may be recommended when the body needs extra calcium, calcitriol (an active form of vitamin D) and zinc.

How does it work?
Calcitriol helps the body absorb calcium from the intestine. Calcium supports bone strength, while zinc supports normal body functions and tissue health.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by the doctor or pharmacist, preferably with food and water unless advised otherwise. Do not take additional calcium or vitamin D supplements without medical advice.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort or bloating. Excess calcium or vitamin D may cause unusual thirst, frequent urination, vomiting, weakness or confusion.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels, or parathyroid disease. Medical advice is important before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Some medicines, including thyroid medicines, iron supplements and certain antibiotics, may need to be taken separately.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat low calcium and vitamin D levels and to support bone health. It may be recommended when the body needs extra calcium, active vitamin D and zinc.

How does it work?
Calcitriol is an active form of vitamin D that helps the body absorb calcium. Calcium supports bones and teeth, while zinc supports normal body functions.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed or directed on the product label. Calcium carbonate is generally best taken with food. Swallow with water and do not take more than recommended. Do not use additional calcium or vitamin D supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort or bloating may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones or high calcium levels. Calcium levels may need monitoring during treatment. Seek medical advice for severe nausea, vomiting, unusual thirst, frequent urination, weakness or confusion, as these may indicate excess calcium. Calcium can interact with some medicines, so inform the doctor or pharmacist about all medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Used to supplement calcium and support calcium absorption and bone health, especially when calcium or active vitamin D supplementation is needed.

How does it work?
Calcium provides the mineral needed for strong bones and normal muscle and nerve function. Calcitriol helps the body absorb calcium, while vitamin K2 supports the normal use of calcium in bone.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the capsule with water, preferably with food. Do not take more than recommended or use it with other calcium or vitamin D products unless advised.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating or abdominal pain. Excess calcium may cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness or vomiting.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels or parathyroid disease. Medical monitoring may be needed during prolonged use. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, including iron, thyroid medicines and certain antibiotics; separate doses as advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat certain fungal infections, especially when there is significant inflammation or a suspected bacterial infection alongside it.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole damages the fungal cell membrane. Beclomethasone reduces redness, swelling and itching, while neomycin acts against susceptible bacteria.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, itching, irritation, redness, dryness or skin peeling at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning or colour changes.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not apply to large areas, open wounds or under airtight dressings unless advised by a doctor. Avoid self-use on the face, groin or skin folds, as the steroid may cause harm with prolonged use. Stop use and seek medical advice if the infection worsens, severe irritation develops, or there is no improvement. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only after medical advice.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole 1% is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch and fungal skin infections caused by Candida.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, helping to clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For use on the skin only. Apply to clean, dry affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, burning, stinging or itching may occur at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use on the eyes or swallow it. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, an allergic reaction or worsening symptoms occur. Seek medical advice if the infection does not improve or keeps returning.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole vaginal cream is used to treat vaginal fungal infections, commonly known as vaginal thrush or yeast infection. It can help relieve symptoms such as itching, soreness and abnormal discharge caused by the infection.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole is an antifungal medicine. It damages the fungal cell membrane, which stops the fungus from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For vaginal use only. Wash hands before and after use. Use the applicator to insert the cream into the vagina exactly as directed on the pack or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not swallow it. Avoid getting it in the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild burning, irritation, itching or discomfort in the vagina may occur after application.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to clotrimazole or any ingredient. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially before using the applicator. Seek medical advice if symptoms do not improve, keep returning, or occur with fever, lower abdominal pain, foul-smelling discharge, sores or unusual bleeding. The cream may reduce the effectiveness of latex condoms or diaphragms during treatment and for a short time afterwards; check the product instructions.

What is it used for?
Nifedipine extended-release is mainly used to lower high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed to help prevent chest pain caused by angina.

How does it work?
It relaxes and widens blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily and reducing the workload on the heart.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole with water; do not crush, chew or break it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, flushing, dizziness, ankle or leg swelling, constipation, nausea and a fast or pounding heartbeat.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is low blood pressure, heart disease or liver disease. Grapefruit and grapefruit juice may interact with nifedipine and should be avoided unless a doctor or pharmacist advises otherwise. Seek medical help for severe dizziness, fainting, worsening chest pain, breathing difficulty or swelling of the face or throat.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of blocked nose and nasal congestion associated with the common cold.

How does it work?
Its aromatic ingredients release vapours that provide a cooling sensation and may make nasal breathing feel easier. They mainly provide symptomatic relief and do not cure the underlying infection.

How to take/use it
The dosage form and route are not provided. Use only as directed on the product label. Do not swallow unless the label specifically states that it is for oral use. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Nose, throat or eye irritation, headache, nausea, or skin irritation. Allergic reactions may occur.

Precautions
Keep out of reach of children; camphor-containing products can be harmful if swallowed. Do not apply to the eyes or broken skin. Stop use and seek medical help if breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash occurs. People with asthma or sensitivity to strong vapours should use it cautiously.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold symptoms such as fever, body aches, blocked or stuffy nose, runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and body aches. Phenylephrine helps relieve nasal congestion, while chlorpheniramine reduces allergy-like symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Measure the liquid with the supplied measuring device. Do not take with other medicines containing paracetamol.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea and stomach discomfort. Some people may experience a fast heartbeat or increased blood pressure.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery if affected. Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine or an overactive thyroid. Avoid alcohol. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve dry cough and associated cold or allergy symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan suppresses the cough reflex. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that helps reduce allergy-related symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Measure the liquid with the supplied measuring device. Do not take more than recommended, and do not use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea and stomach upset may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors, and check with a doctor before using it with antidepressants or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice before use in children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, breathing difficulty or a persistent cough. Seek urgent help for severe breathing problems, confusion or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold and flu symptoms such as blocked or runny nose, sneezing, headache, body aches and fever.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and relieve pain. Phenylephrine helps reduce nasal congestion, while chlorpheniramine helps relieve sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the package label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or other cold and flu ingredients. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, blurred vision, increased blood pressure or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, prostate or urinary problems. Ask a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, breathing difficulty, an allergic reaction or symptoms that worsen or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve common cold symptoms such as fever, body aches, blocked or stuffy nose, and a runny nose.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and pain. Phenylephrine helps relieve nasal congestion, while chlorpheniramine reduces runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Measure the liquid with a proper measuring device. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or other cold-and-flu ingredients.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, or stomach discomfort may occur. Phenylephrine may cause palpitations or a temporary increase in blood pressure.

Precautions
May cause sleepiness; avoid driving and alcohol if affected. Ask a doctor before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, prostate or urination problems, or if taking antidepressants or other regular medicines. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat certain bacterial infections when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefixime stops bacteria from forming their protective cell wall. Ofloxacin stops bacteria from multiplying by interfering with their DNA. Together, they help control susceptible bacterial infections.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Do not self-medicate or share this medicine. Avoid taking it at the same time as antacids or mineral supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, iron or calcium unless advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and mild skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about allergies to cephalosporins, penicillins or quinolone antibiotics, kidney disease, seizures, heart rhythm problems, tendon problems or myasthenia gravis. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, swelling or breathing difficulty, tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, or an irregular heartbeat. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used to treat certain bacterial infections when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
Cefixime prevents bacteria from forming their protective cell wall. Ofloxacin interferes with bacterial enzymes needed for growth and multiplication.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if feeling better. Do not skip doses or share this medicine. Follow the product label or doctor’s instructions regarding food and other medicines.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, indigestion, headache, dizziness, or vomiting.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to cefixime, other cephalosporins, or quinolone antibiotics. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash or breathing difficulty, numbness or tingling, unusual mood or nerve symptoms, or tendon pain or swelling. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, seizures, or a history of tendon disorders. Avoid unnecessary exposure to strong sunlight and discuss other medicines with a doctor or pharmacist.

What is it used for?
Cefixime oral suspension is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, airways, urinary tract and other areas, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefixime is a cephalosporin antibiotic. It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Shake the suspension well before each use and measure it with an accurate measuring device. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. If it is supplied as a powder, prepare it only as directed on the label or by a pharmacist.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, vomiting, indigestion and headache. Mild skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to cefixime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin-type antibiotics, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash or persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Use only for a prescribed bacterial infection and do not share or save leftover medicine.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, ears, airways, urinary tract and other areas, when caused by susceptible bacteria. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming a protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. If this is an oral suspension, shake the bottle well before each use and measure the dose with an appropriate measuring device. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not use leftover antibiotics or share them with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion and headache. Mild skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making their protective cell wall, which helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. If supplied as a powder, prepare it with water exactly as directed on the label or by the pharmacist. Shake the suspension well before each use and measure each dose with an oral syringe or measuring spoon. Complete the prescribed course unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, vomiting and indigestion. Mild rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to cefixime or other cephalosporin antibiotics. Tell the doctor about any previous serious reaction to penicillin or other antibiotics, or kidney problems. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a widespread rash.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, blood, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, bones and joints, and meningitis. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Ceftriaxone is given as an injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; rash; and changes in blood test results.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to ceftriaxone, other cephalosporin antibiotics, or penicillin. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or a widespread or blistering rash. Use only under medical supervision, especially in newborn babies or people with liver or kidney problems.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone with sulbactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, as prescribed by a doctor. It is not effective against viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps ceftriaxone work against some bacteria that can otherwise resist certain antibiotics.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a doctor or nurse as an injection into a vein or muscle. The dose and duration depend on the type and severity of infection, so it should be used only as prescribed. Do not self-inject or stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain or redness at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, rash, and headache may occur. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or a widespread rash.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to ceftriaxone, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or other antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems, gallbladder problems, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Use only under medical supervision, especially in newborns or seriously ill patients.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone with tazobactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Tazobactam blocks certain bacterial enzymes that can make ceftriaxone less effective.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection. Use it only as prescribed and complete the recommended course.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, skin rash and changes in liver test results may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, other cephalosporins, penicillins or other antibiotics, and about liver, kidney or gallbladder problems. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash. This medicine should be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding only when advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the throat, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. If instructed to disperse the tablet, mix it with water as directed and take it immediately. Do not share leftover antibiotics with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion, headache and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Inform the prescriber about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the respiratory tract, urinary tract, skin and other areas. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions for the correct dose, route and duration. Use the supplied diluent and do not prepare or administer the medicine unless instructed to do so. Complete the prescribed course unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, indigestion and headache. Mild skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there is a history of serious allergy to cefpodoxime, cephalosporins or other beta-lactam antibiotics, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Antibiotics should not be used without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, sinuses, ears, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming a protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Take the tablet with food and swallow it with water. Do not take extra doses if one is missed; follow the advice of a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, as dose adjustment may be needed. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash. Use antibiotics only when prescribed.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, lungs, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed and follow the product label for preparation and storage. Shake the liquid well if instructed. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve, unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and headache. Skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the healthcare professional about kidney problems, as dose adjustment may be needed. Seek medical help for facial swelling, breathing difficulty, a severe rash or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only when prescribed.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime Proxetil + Clavulanic Acid is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefpodoxime kills susceptible bacteria by interfering with their cell-wall formation. Clavulanic acid helps protect cefpodoxime from enzymes produced by some bacteria, improving its activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Complete the full course, even if symptoms improve, and do not share it with others. If a dose is missed, follow the prescribed instructions rather than taking extra medicine.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain or discomfort, indigestion, and headache. Skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any allergy to cefpodoxime, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics, and about kidney problems. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea, especially if it contains blood. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can cause resistance.

What is it used for?
This medicine is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional; it does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefpodoxime stops bacteria from forming their protective cell wall. Potassium clavulanate helps protect cefpodoxime from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against them.

How to take/use it
Use only in the dose and for the duration prescribed. If supplied as a liquid suspension, prepare and store it exactly as directed, shake well before use, and measure each dose with an accurate measuring device. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, cephalosporins, penicillins or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Tell the healthcare professional about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Cefoperazone with sulbactam is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefoperazone stops susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall. Sulbactam blocks enzymes that can make some bacteria resistant to cefoperazone, helping the antibiotic work more effectively.

How to take/use it
This medicine is usually given as an injection by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and should be decided by a healthcare professional. Complete the prescribed course unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur. Changes in blood tests, including liver or blood-count results, are also possible.

Precautions
Inform the healthcare professional about any previous allergy to cephalosporins, penicillins, or other antibiotics. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Tell the doctor about liver disease, bleeding problems, or medicines that affect bleeding. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for the period advised by the doctor, as cefoperazone may cause an unpleasant reaction with alcohol.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime axetil is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, sinuses, ears, chest, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from making their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably after food, and swallow the tablet whole with water. Complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not take it without medical advice or share it with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to cefuroxime, penicillins or other antibiotics. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, or a severe skin rash. Antacids and medicines that reduce stomach acid may affect its absorption; inform the doctor or pharmacist about all medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime axetil is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, chest, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably after food, and swallow the tablet whole with water. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share this medicine or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort and headache may occur. Taking it after food may help reduce stomach upset.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about any previous antibiotic allergy and about other medicines, especially antacids or medicines that reduce stomach acid. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime axetil is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, sinuses, ears, lungs, urinary tract and skin, when the bacteria are sensitive to it. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, preferably after food, and complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics or skip doses. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, other cephalosporins or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin reaction. Contact a doctor if diarrhoea is severe, persistent or contains blood, as this may occur during or after antibiotic treatment. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, pregnancy, breastfeeding or other medicines being used.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime axetil with potassium clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, chest, urinary tract and skin. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefuroxime kills bacteria by interfering with the formation of their protective cell wall. Potassium clavulanate helps cefuroxime work against bacteria that can otherwise resist some antibiotics.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably after food, and complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not skip doses or share this medicine with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, penicillins, cephalosporins or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea or any history of severe allergy. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, a severe skin rash or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Trypsin and chymotrypsin help reduce inflammation, swelling and discomfort associated with injuries, surgery and some muscle or joint conditions.

How does it work?
These enzymes help break down proteins involved in inflammation and tissue swelling, which may support recovery after injury or surgery.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor. Swallow the enteric-coated tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea or other digestive upset may occur. Allergic reactions such as rash are uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a bleeding disorder, a stomach ulcer, liver or kidney disease, or if blood-thinning medicines are being taken. Inform the doctor before surgery. Seek medical help for unusual bleeding, severe stomach pain, swelling of the face or difficulty breathing. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Ciprofloxacin is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some urinary, gastrointestinal, skin, bone and joint, and respiratory infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking enzymes they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Do not self-medicate or stop treatment early without medical advice. The dose, treatment duration and route depend on the infection and the product. If taken by mouth, follow advice about separating it from antacids, iron, calcium or other mineral supplements.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and rash may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Seek urgent medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe weakness, serious mood or nervous-system changes, severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney problems, heart-rhythm problems, seizures or medicines being used. Ciprofloxacin interacts with several medicines, including tizanidine.

What is it used for?
Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the urinary tract, respiratory system, skin, bones, joints and digestive system. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking enzymes they need to copy and repair their genetic material.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with plenty of water. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing calcium, iron, magnesium or zinc; follow the timing instructions provided by a doctor or pharmacist. Avoid taking it with milk or yoghurt alone.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, allergic reaction, unusual muscle weakness, numbness or tingling, mood or nerve changes, or pain or swelling in a tendon. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, myasthenia gravis, or use of other medicines. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can cause resistance.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ears, sinuses, throat, lungs, skin, urinary tract and teeth. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by interfering with their cell wall. Clavulanate helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes that can make some bacteria resistant to it.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not share it or take extra doses to make up for a missed dose.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, clavulanate or related antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems and any previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver reaction. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotics can contribute to resistance.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat acne, including pimples and inflamed acne lesions.

How does it work?
Clindamycin helps reduce acne-causing bacteria and inflammation. Nicotinamide (niacinamide) also helps reduce skin inflammation.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Wash hands after applying.

Common side effects
Dryness, redness, burning, itching, irritation, peeling or stinging at the application site.

Precautions
For external use only. Do not apply to broken or severely irritated skin. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe skin irritation or persistent or severe diarrhoea develops. Inform a doctor if there is a history of bowel inflammation or antibiotic-associated diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
This is a medicated cleansing soap for washing the skin and supporting everyday skin hygiene. The supplied information does not establish treatment for a specific skin condition or infection.

How does it work?
Soap and cleansing agents help remove dirt, oil and microorganisms from the skin surface. Triclosan has antibacterial activity, while allantoin may help soothe the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Wet the skin, apply the soap, work into a lather and rinse thoroughly. Use according to the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not swallow.

Common side effects
Skin dryness, irritation, redness, itching or allergic rash may occur, especially in sensitive skin.

Precautions
Stop using it if significant irritation or a rash develops. Avoid use on the eyes and take care not to use on severely damaged skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice if skin symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin for inflamed, itchy and thick, scaly skin conditions such as eczema, dermatitis or psoriasis, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Clobetasol reduces skin inflammation, redness and itching. Salicylic acid softens and helps remove thick scales, allowing the medicine to work better.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Wash hands after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not cover the treated area with a bandage unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, irritation, dryness or redness at the application site. Prolonged or excessive use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Do not use on the face, groin, underarms, broken skin or infected skin unless specifically advised. Avoid prolonged or extensive use, especially in children. Seek medical advice if the condition worsens, shows signs of infection, or does not improve. Stop use and seek urgent help for severe swelling, rash or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to reduce inflammation, redness, itching and thick scaling in conditions such as eczema, psoriasis and other steroid-responsive scaly skin conditions. Use only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Clobetasol is a potent corticosteroid that reduces skin inflammation and itching. Salicylic acid softens and removes thick scales, helping the medicine penetrate the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the affected skin exactly as directed by the doctor. Avoid applying it to the eyes, face, groin, underarms, broken skin or infected skin unless specifically advised. Do not cover the treated area tightly unless instructed.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, irritation, dryness or redness at the application site. Prolonged or excessive use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Do not use for longer or over larger areas than prescribed. Avoid contact with the eyes and wash hands after application. Tell the doctor if the condition worsens or shows signs of infection, such as increasing pain, swelling, pus or spreading redness. Extra caution is needed in children and when used on the face or on large areas of skin.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve abdominal pain and cramps caused by spasms of the stomach or intestines.

How does it work?
Dicyclomine relaxes spasms in the muscles of the stomach and intestines. Paracetamol helps reduce pain.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, constipation, nausea, dizziness, drowsiness, blurred vision or stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is liver disease, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, bowel blockage, severe ulcerative colitis or myasthenia gravis. Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving if dizzy, drowsy or experiencing blurred vision. Seek medical advice if abdominal pain is severe, persistent or unexplained, or if an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid injection used under specialist supervision for certain cases of osteoporosis and some types of anemia, including anemia related to kidney disease. It may also be used for other conditions involving loss of body tissue when specifically prescribed.

How does it work?
It acts like an anabolic androgen hormone, helping increase protein production and support muscle and bone tissue. It can also stimulate red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as a deep injection into a muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and injection schedule depend on the condition being treated and must be decided by the prescriber. Do not self-inject or use it for bodybuilding.

Common side effects
Acne, oily skin, fluid retention, changes in mood or sex drive, injection-site pain, and changes in menstrual periods. Women may develop increased facial or body hair, a deeper voice, or other masculinising effects.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about prostate or breast cancer, liver, kidney or heart disease, high calcium levels, or a history of blood clots. Children and adolescents require specialist monitoring because this medicine can affect growth and puberty. Seek medical advice for yellowing of the skin, severe swelling, breathing difficulty, unusual bleeding, or significant voice or body changes.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate injection is an anabolic steroid used under medical supervision to help manage osteoporosis and certain types of anaemia, including anaemia associated with kidney disease. Its use depends on the medical condition being treated.

How does it work?
It acts like a modified male hormone and promotes protein production, muscle and bone tissue formation, and red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as a deep injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the condition and response to treatment. Do not self-inject or use it for bodybuilding.

Common side effects
Acne, oily skin, swelling due to fluid retention, changes in mood or sexual desire, injection-site pain, and changes in menstrual periods. Women may develop increased facial or body hair, a deeper voice, or other male-pattern changes.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a specialist. Tell the doctor about liver, kidney, heart or prostate disease, or a history of breast or prostate cancer. Regular medical checks may be needed for blood counts, liver function, cholesterol and prostate health. Seek medical advice for yellowing of the skin, severe swelling, breathing difficulty, unusual bleeding, or voice changes.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid used under specialist supervision for certain conditions involving bone or muscle loss, including some cases of osteoporosis. It may also be used for selected types of anaemia or severe tissue wasting, depending on the doctor's assessment.

How does it work?
It is a synthetic hormone related to testosterone. It promotes protein production and can support bone formation, muscle tissue maintenance and red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as a deep intramuscular injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and injection schedule depend on the condition being treated; do not self-inject or use it for bodybuilding.

Common side effects
Injection-site pain, acne or oily skin, fluid retention, changes in mood or sex drive, changes in cholesterol levels, and menstrual changes. Women may develop increased facial hair, a deeper voice or other signs of masculinisation.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell the doctor about prostate or breast cancer, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high cholesterol, or a history of blood clots. Children require specialist supervision because it may affect growth. Regular medical monitoring of blood counts, liver function, cholesterol and, where appropriate, the prostate may be needed. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin, severe swelling, chest pain, breathlessness or unusual bleeding.

What is it used for?
Deflazacort is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and suppress an overactive immune response in conditions such as certain autoimmune, allergic and inflammatory disorders. It may also be prescribed for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The exact use depends on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It acts like natural steroid hormones made by the body, reducing inflammation and decreasing immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, especially after prolonged use. Follow the instructions on the prescription or medicine label.

Common side effects
Increased appetite, weight gain, indigestion, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, acne and increased blood sugar. Corticosteroids may also increase the risk of infections.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, eye problems, liver or kidney disease, or any current infection. Avoid close contact with people who have contagious infections and ask the doctor before receiving vaccines. Seek medical help for signs of a serious infection, severe mood changes, vision changes or allergic reactions.

What is it used for?
Dexamethasone injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce severe inflammation and allergic or immune reactions. It may also be prescribed for other conditions requiring strong steroid treatment, only under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and excessive immune reactions.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose, injection route and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. Do not self-inject or use it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar, stomach upset, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, increased appetite, fluid retention and pain or redness at the injection site. Steroids may also increase the risk of infections.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions or any current infection. Avoid contact with people who have contagious infections and inform the doctor if signs of infection develop. Long-term treatment should not be stopped suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Dexamethasone injection is a strong corticosteroid used to reduce severe inflammation and suppress an overactive immune response. It may be prescribed for certain allergic, inflammatory, autoimmune or other serious conditions; the exact use depends on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It acts like natural steroid hormones and reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and immune reactions.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a doctor or nurse as an injection. The dose, route and duration depend on the condition and response to treatment. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar, indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, fluid retention and increased risk of infection may occur, especially with higher doses or longer treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health problems or any current infection. Dexamethasone may hide signs of infection and may affect blood sugar. Avoid live vaccines unless advised by a doctor. After prolonged treatment, it should not be stopped suddenly. Seek medical help for severe infection symptoms, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or severe mood changes.

What is it used for?
Diclofenac sodium 50 mg is used to relieve pain and reduce inflammation in conditions such as muscle and joint pain, arthritis, sprains, and other painful inflammatory conditions.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling, and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow the tablet with water. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or combine it with other diclofenac or NSAID medicines unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and gas.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems. Avoid use during the last three months of pregnancy unless specifically advised. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest pain, breathing difficulty, or facial swelling.

What is it used for?
Diclofenac sodium is used to relieve pain and reduce inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The correct route, dose and treatment duration depend on the product form and medical condition. Follow the label or healthcare professional's instructions, and do not use more than recommended.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or asthma triggered by painkillers. Tell the doctor about blood thinners or other medicines being taken. Avoid use in the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, chest pain or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Cinnarizine is used to prevent and relieve motion sickness and to help manage vertigo, dizziness and related balance problems caused by inner-ear disorders.

How does it work?
It reduces the excessive activity of the balance centre in the inner ear and has an antihistamine effect, helping to reduce dizziness, nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Swallow with water, preferably after food if it causes stomach upset. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dry mouth, stomach discomfort, indigestion and weight gain may occur.

Precautions
It may cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol until its effects are known. Use only with medical advice if there is Parkinson’s disease, as it may worsen symptoms. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if dizziness is severe, persistent or associated with fainting, weakness, severe headache or other unusual symptoms.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve abdominal cramps and pain caused by spasms in the digestive tract.

How does it work?
Dicyclomine relaxes the muscles of the intestine, helping to reduce spasms and cramps. Paracetamol helps relieve pain.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol at the same time.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, dizziness, drowsiness, blurred vision, nausea and constipation.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is liver disease, regular alcohol use, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, prostate problems or suspected intestinal blockage. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizzy, drowsy or experiencing blurred vision. Seek medical advice for severe, persistent or unexplained abdominal pain, especially with vomiting, fever or blood in the stool.

What is it used for?
Drotaverine is used to relieve painful spasms or cramps in smooth muscles, especially in the stomach and intestines. It may also be used for spasms of the bile ducts, urinary tract or uterus when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It relaxes smooth muscles, helping reduce spasms and cramp-like pain.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or healthcare professional. If this is an injectable medicine, it should be administered by a trained healthcare professional. Do not self-administer unless specifically instructed.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, nausea, constipation, palpitations and low blood pressure may occur. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to drotaverine, low blood pressure, or severe liver, kidney or heart disease. Seek medical help for severe dizziness, fainting, breathing difficulty or swelling of the face or throat. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Drotaverine injection is used to relieve painful cramps caused by spasms of smooth muscles, such as stomach or intestinal cramps, biliary or urinary tract spasms, and menstrual cramps.

How does it work?
It relaxes the smooth muscles in internal organs, helping reduce spasms and cramping pain.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or nurse. The dose, route and frequency depend on the condition and should be decided by a healthcare professional. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, nausea, palpitations, low blood pressure and injection-site discomfort may occur. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially if there is low blood pressure or severe liver, kidney or heart disease. Tell the doctor about any medicine allergies and if pregnant or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary protein supplement to help increase daily protein intake and support muscle maintenance, growth and recovery when combined with a balanced diet.

How does it work?
It provides protein and amino acids that the body uses to build and repair muscles and other tissues.

How to take/use it
Mix and consume as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended serving. Use with a balanced diet and adequate fluids.

Common side effects
Some people may experience bloating, gas, nausea or stomach discomfort, depending on the ingredients and individual tolerance.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list for allergens, including milk, soy, nuts or other ingredients. Avoid it if allergic to any ingredient. People with kidney disease or other medical conditions should seek medical advice before using a high-protein supplement. Sugar-free products may contain sweeteners that can cause digestive discomfort in some people.

What is it used for?
Dydrogesterone is a progesterone-like medicine used for conditions related to low progesterone, such as irregular or painful periods, endometriosis, abnormal uterine bleeding, and some fertility or pregnancy-support treatments. It may also be used with oestrogen in hormone replacement therapy, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It acts similarly to the natural hormone progesterone. This helps regulate the lining of the uterus and support the menstrual cycle or pregnancy when progesterone support is needed.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. Swallow the tablet with water and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache or migraine, nausea, breast tenderness, stomach discomfort, and changes in menstrual bleeding or spotting.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, unexplained vaginal bleeding, or a history of hormone-sensitive cancers. Seek medical advice for heavy or unusual bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe headache, or allergic symptoms. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Metoclopramide is used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for slow stomach emptying and related digestive movement problems.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals involved in nausea and vomiting. It also helps the stomach empty more quickly by increasing movement in the upper digestive tract.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. Avoid driving or operating machinery if it causes drowsiness or restlessness.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, restlessness, headache, diarrhoea and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, depression, a history of involuntary muscle movements, stomach or intestinal blockage or bleeding, or kidney or liver problems. Avoid alcohol and check before using it with sedatives, antipsychotics or other medicines that affect movement. Seek urgent medical help for unusual muscle movements, severe restlessness, facial or neck spasms, confusion or seizures. Prolonged use can cause serious movement disorders and should be avoided unless specifically advised.

What is it used for?
Metoclopramide is used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed to help food move through the stomach and upper digestive tract in certain conditions.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals in the brain that can trigger nausea and vomiting. It also increases movement of the upper digestive tract, helping the stomach empty more quickly.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. The dose and duration depend on the condition being treated. Do not take it for longer than recommended, and avoid driving or operating machinery if it causes drowsiness or restlessness.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, dizziness, restlessness, headache and diarrhoea. Unusual muscle spasms, stiffness, shaking or uncontrolled movements can occur and require prompt medical attention.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is stomach or intestinal blockage, bleeding or perforation, epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, or a history of involuntary muscle movements caused by medicines. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness. Seek urgent medical help for severe muscle stiffness, abnormal movements, confusion or fever. Prolonged or repeated use can cause serious movement disorders.

What is it used for?
Metoclopramide is used to prevent or treat nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for slow stomach emptying and related digestive symptoms.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals in the vomiting centre of the brain, helping control nausea and vomiting. It also increases movement of the upper digestive tract and helps the stomach empty more quickly.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually before meals if directed. Swallow with water and do not take it for longer than recommended. Do not drive or operate machinery if it causes drowsiness or dizziness.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, dizziness, restlessness, headache and diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice, especially in children, older adults, or people with Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, depression, kidney problems or a history of involuntary movements. Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor or pharmacist before combining it with medicines that cause drowsiness. Stop using it and seek urgent medical help for uncontrolled movements, muscle stiffness, severe restlessness or unusual facial or tongue movements. It should not be used if there is suspected stomach or intestinal blockage, bleeding or perforation.

What is it used for?
Prochlorperazine is used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for dizziness or vertigo and nausea associated with migraine.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals in the brain that can trigger nausea and vomiting. It also reduces abnormal signals involved in dizziness and vertigo.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. Place the mouth-dissolving tablet on the tongue and allow it to dissolve. Do not take more than prescribed. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision and restlessness may occur. Some people may develop muscle stiffness, tremors or other abnormal movements.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol, as it can increase drowsiness. Seek medical help for severe muscle stiffness, uncontrolled movements, high fever, confusion, fainting or an irregular heartbeat. Tell the doctor before use if there is Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, glaucoma, prostate problems, liver disease or a history of heart rhythm problems.

What is it used for?
Ethamsylate is used to help control or prevent certain types of bleeding, including heavy menstrual bleeding and bleeding from small blood vessels, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It helps strengthen small blood vessels and supports the formation of an initial platelet plug, which can reduce bleeding.

What is it used for?

It helps strengthen small blood vessels and improves the ability of platelets to form a plug at the site of bleeding, which can help reduce blood loss.

Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or duration without medical advice. Do not take extra doses to control sudden or heavy bleeding.
