Used for temporary relief of muscle and joint pain, including pain from sprains, strains and mild sports injuries.

How does it work?
Diclofenac and methyl salicylate help reduce pain and inflammation. Menthol provides a cooling sensation that may help soothe the painful area.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the painful area as directed on the product label and wash hands after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not swallow.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth, broken or infected skin. Do not cover the treated area with a tight bandage or apply heat over it. Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other painkillers or any ingredient in the product. Stop use and seek medical help if severe skin reactions, swelling or breathing difficulty occur. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially in the last three months, or if applying to large areas or for a prolonged period.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of local muscle and joint pain, including pain from sprains, strains and other minor soft-tissue injuries.

How does it work?
Diclofenac helps reduce pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling or warming sensation that may further help relieve local discomfort.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the painful area and gently rub in, following the product label or a healthcare professional’s advice. Wash hands after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not apply to broken or infected skin, or cover with a tight bandage.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe skin irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or a widespread rash occurs. Do not swallow. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months, or on large areas of skin or for prolonged use.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation in muscles, joints and soft tissues, such as sprains, strains and aches associated with arthritis.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling and warming sensation that can help relieve local pain.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the painful area and gently massage as directed on the product label. Wash hands after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not use more often or for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site.

Precautions
For external use only. Do not apply to broken, infected or irritated skin, or near the eyes, mouth or other mucous membranes. Do not cover with a tight bandage or apply external heat. Avoid use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other painkillers or salicylates. Stop use and seek medical help if severe skin rash, facial swelling, wheezing or breathing difficulty occurs. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months, or if applying to large areas or for prolonged use.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, such as sprains, strains and arthritis-related pain.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Methyl salicylate and menthol provide additional soothing and cooling relief in the applied area.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the painful area and gently rub in, following the instructions on the product label. Wash hands after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin, or cover tightly with a dressing.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, rash or burning at the application site. Stop using it if a severe skin reaction occurs.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other NSAID painkillers, salicylates or any ingredient in the product. Avoid heating pads and direct sunlight on the treated area. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks, or while breastfeeding. Stop use and seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a widespread rash.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve painful muscle and joint conditions, especially when muscle spasm, swelling or inflammation is present.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces pain and inflammation, while paracetamol helps relieve pain. Chlorzoxazone acts centrally to help relax painful muscle spasms.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more than prescribed. Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if it causes dizziness or drowsiness. Do not take it with other paracetamol-containing medicines or painkillers such as diclofenac or other NSAIDs unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, heartburn, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness and drowsiness.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to NSAIDs. Avoid during pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks and in the last trimester, unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe abdominal pain.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and muscle spasms, such as those associated with muscle or joint injuries and other painful musculoskeletal conditions.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain, while chlorzoxazone relaxes painful muscle spasms.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more than the prescribed dose or combine it with other medicines containing diclofenac or paracetamol. Avoid alcohol and do not drive if drowsy or dizzy.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and drowsiness.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or regular alcohol use. Avoid during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, unless prescribed. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, breathing difficulty, swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve painful muscle spasms and musculoskeletal pain, such as back pain, sprains and strains, and other painful muscle or joint conditions.

How does it work?
Diclofenac and paracetamol help reduce pain, while chlorzoxazone helps relax painful, tight muscles. Diclofenac also reduces inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor. Avoid driving if it causes dizziness or drowsiness.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness, drowsiness and headache. Liver enzyme changes may also occur.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or asthma triggered by painkillers. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase the risk of liver problems and drowsiness. Inform the doctor if pregnant, especially during the last three months, breastfeeding, or taking blood thinners or other painkillers. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin reactions, yellowing of the eyes or skin, or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain and inflammation, including body aches, muscle or joint pain, dental pain and pain with fever, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache.

Precautions
Use only after medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or pregnancy—especially the last 3 months. Avoid or limit alcohol. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and swelling, such as muscle or joint pain, dental pain, or pain after an injury or procedure.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and fever, while serratiopeptidase is used to help reduce inflammation and swelling.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist, preferably with or after food, and swallow it with water. Do not take it with other medicines containing diclofenac or paracetamol unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, indigestion, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache may occur. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

Precautions
Use only after medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or a bleeding disorder. Tell the doctor if taking blood thinners or other painkillers. Avoid excessive alcohol. Do not use during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, including pain from sprains, strains and arthritis.

How does it work?
Diclofenac helps reduce pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling or warming sensation that can help relieve local muscle and joint discomfort.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the painful area and gently massage as directed on the product label. Wash hands after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin, or cover with tight bandages or heat.

Common side effects
Skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin or other painkillers of the NSAID group. Stop use if severe skin irritation, swelling or breathing difficulty occurs. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months, or if using on large areas or for a prolonged period.

What is it used for?
Sildenafil 100 mg is used to treat erectile dysfunction (difficulty getting or keeping an erection firm enough for sexual activity).

How does it work?
It increases blood flow to the penis during sexual stimulation, helping produce an erection. It does not increase sexual desire and will not work without sexual stimulation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, usually before planned sexual activity. Swallow with water and do not take more than prescribed. Follow the product label or medical advice for timing and use.

Common side effects
Headache, flushing, indigestion, blocked or stuffy nose, dizziness and temporary visual changes.

Precautions
Do not use with nitrate medicines for chest pain or with riociguat, as this can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure. Seek medical advice before use if there is serious heart disease, low blood pressure, recent stroke or heart attack, or if taking alpha-blockers or other medicines for erectile dysfunction. Get urgent medical help for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, sudden loss of vision or hearing, or chest pain during sexual activity.

What is it used for?
Sildenafil is mainly used to treat erectile dysfunction (difficulty getting or keeping an erection firm enough for sexual activity).

How does it work?
It increases blood flow to the penis by relaxing blood vessels. It works only with sexual stimulation and does not increase sexual desire.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Swallow with water. Do not take more than prescribed or use it with other medicines for erectile dysfunction.

Common side effects
Headache, flushing, indigestion, blocked or runny nose, dizziness, and changes in vision.

Precautions
Do not use sildenafil with nitrate medicines for chest pain or with riociguat, as this can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure. Seek medical help for chest pain, sudden loss of vision or hearing, or an erection lasting more than 4 hours. Tell a doctor about heart problems, low blood pressure, or use of alpha-blockers before taking it.

What is it used for?
This combination is used in adult men to treat erectile dysfunction (difficulty getting or keeping an erection) and premature ejaculation.

How does it work?
Sildenafil improves blood flow to the penis when there is sexual stimulation, helping achieve and maintain an erection. Dapoxetine affects serotonin activity and can help delay ejaculation.

How to take/use it
Take only in the dose and at the time prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take it more often than prescribed. It does not increase sexual desire and works only with sexual stimulation. Avoid excessive alcohol.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, flushing, indigestion, blocked nose, nausea, diarrhoea, dry mouth and visual changes may occur.

Precautions
Do not use with nitrate medicines for chest pain or riociguat, as this can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure. Tell the doctor about heart disease, low blood pressure, fainting, liver problems, or medicines for blood pressure, depression or other mental health conditions. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, fainting, sudden loss of vision or hearing, or an erection lasting more than 4 hours.

What is it used for?
Metronidazole is used to treat certain bacterial infections, especially infections caused by bacteria that grow without oxygen. It is also used for some parasitic infections, including amoebiasis, giardiasis and trichomoniasis, and for conditions such as bacterial vaginosis and some dental infections.

How does it work?
It damages the DNA of susceptible bacteria and parasites, stopping them from growing and surviving. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Do not use leftover medicine or share it with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, and a metallic taste in the mouth. Urine may become darker temporarily.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol while taking metronidazole and for at least 48 hours after the last dose. Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, a history of nerve problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if medicines such as warfarin are being used. Seek medical help for severe rash, numbness or tingling, seizures, confusion, or severe diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Used to make urine less acidic and relieve burning or discomfort during urination. It may also be used as supportive treatment in some kidney stone conditions. It does not treat a bacterial urinary infection by itself.

How does it work?
Disodium hydrogen citrate is converted into bicarbonate in the body, which helps reduce acidity and makes the urine more alkaline.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Measure the liquid carefully using a proper measuring device. Do not use more or for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, bloating or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Use only with medical advice if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease, swelling, or a sodium-restricted diet, as this medicine contains sodium. Seek medical advice for fever, back or side pain, blood in the urine, or urinary symptoms that do not improve, as these may require treatment for an underlying infection or other condition.

What is it used for?
Used as a topical antiseptic to cleanse minor cuts, grazes and wounds and help reduce the risk of infection.

How does it work?
Chlorhexidine and cetrimide kill or reduce the growth of many bacteria and other microorganisms on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply or use it on the affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, ears and mouth, and do not swallow it.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, burning or itching. Allergic reactions may rarely occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to chlorhexidine, cetrimide or any of its ingredients. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or other signs of a serious allergic reaction occur. Seek medical advice for deep, heavily bleeding or seriously infected wounds.

What is it used for?
Used as an antiseptic to clean and disinfect the skin, including minor cuts, wounds and superficial skin injuries. It helps reduce germs on the skin.

How does it work?
Chlorhexidine and cetrimide kill or reduce many bacteria and other germs by damaging their outer membranes.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use on the affected skin exactly as directed on the product label. Avoid swallowing and wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, burning, redness, irritation or dryness of the skin may occur.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the ears. Do not use if allergic to chlorhexidine, cetrimide or similar antiseptics. Do not apply to deep or extensive wounds, serious burns or large areas unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs.

What is it used for?
Used to treat uncomplicated malaria, especially malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum. It is not suitable for severe malaria, which requires urgent hospital treatment.

How does it work?
Arteether and lumefantrine act together to kill malaria parasites in the blood. They reduce the parasites responsible for causing malaria symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor and complete the full treatment course. Taking it with food or milk may improve absorption. Do not use it to prevent malaria or take extra doses if a dose is missed without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, loss of appetite and palpitations may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart problems, fainting, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or medicines such as rifampicin, carbamazepine or phenytoin. Seek urgent medical help for severe vomiting, fainting, an unusually fast or irregular heartbeat, seizures, confusion or worsening malaria symptoms.

What is it used for?
Used to support digestion and relieve symptoms such as indigestion, stomach heaviness, bloating and gas.

How does it work?
Alpha-amylase and papain are digestive enzymes that help break down carbohydrates and proteins. Dill, anise and caraway oils may help reduce intestinal gas and digestive discomfort.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Use the measuring device provided and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause mild stomach discomfort, nausea or loose stools. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, persistent or associated with vomiting, severe abdominal pain or blood in the stool. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding or in young children.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to help reduce inflammation and swelling associated with soft-tissue injuries, inflammation and recovery after some procedures. Its exact use depends on the prescriber's advice.

How does it work?
Papain and alpha amylase are enzymes that help break down proteins and other substances involved in inflammatory swelling, which may help the body clear swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as directed by the doctor or as stated on the product label. Measure the liquid with the supplied measuring device and do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea. Allergic reactions such as rash or itching may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to papain, alpha amylase or any ingredient in the product. Tell the doctor if there is a bleeding disorder or if blood-thinning medicines are being used. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used to help relieve breathing difficulty and wheezing caused by asthma and other obstructive airway conditions, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It helps open the airways and improve airflow.

How does it work?
Etophylline and theophylline relax the muscles around the airways, helping them widen. This makes breathing easier.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the medicine with water and do not take more or more often than advised. Avoid changing the dose or stopping treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, headache, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, trembling and fast or irregular heartbeat.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially with heart disease, high blood pressure, seizures, thyroid problems, liver disease or stomach ulcers. Avoid excessive caffeine, as it may worsen side effects. Seek medical help for severe vomiting, marked palpitations, seizures or worsening breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used to relax narrowed airways and relieve breathing difficulty caused by bronchospasm, such as in asthma and other obstructive airway conditions.

How does it work?
It contains theophylline, a bronchodilator that relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them open and making breathing easier.

How to take/use it
This is an injectable medicine and should be given only by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. Do not inject it yourself. Use it only in the dose and manner prescribed.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, tremors and fast or irregular heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart disease, irregular heartbeat, high blood pressure, seizures, liver disease or fever. Theophylline can interact with several medicines, so provide a complete list of medicines being used. Seek urgent medical help for severe vomiting, marked restlessness, seizures, or a very fast or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat deficiencies of B-group vitamins and to support nutritional needs when dietary intake is inadequate. It may also support normal energy metabolism, nerve function and red blood cell formation.

How does it work?
The B vitamins help the body release energy from food and support the nervous system and blood cell production. Lysine is an essential amino acid needed for protein synthesis.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Shake the bottle well before use and measure the syrup with a proper measuring device. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort or diarrhoea may occur. Allergic reactions are uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Check the ingredients before use if there is a history of allergy to any component. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or use of other vitamin supplements. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, ears, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
It is a cephalosporin antibiotic that stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall, causing the bacteria to die.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Disperse the tablet in water as directed on the product label and drink it immediately. Do not share leftover antibiotics with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and headache. Mild rash may also occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, cephalosporins or other beta-lactam antibiotics, unless advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, or any medicine being taken. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe skin reactions, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime proxetil is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ear, throat, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by the doctor. Shake the suspension well before each use and measure it with an oral syringe or measuring spoon. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not use leftover medicine or share it with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and headache may occur. Skin rash can also occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Use in children only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and suppress an overactive immune response in conditions such as autoimmune disorders, severe allergies, and other inflammatory illnesses. The exact use depends on the condition being treated.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and allergic or immune reactions.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food or milk to reduce stomach irritation. Do not stop it suddenly, especially after prolonged treatment; the dose may need to be reduced gradually under medical supervision.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, fluid retention, and increases in blood sugar or blood pressure.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health conditions, or any infection. Corticosteroids can weaken the immune system and may hide signs of infection. Avoid live vaccines unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for severe infection symptoms, vision changes, severe mood changes, black stools, or unusual swelling.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactivity of the immune system in conditions such as severe allergies, asthma, arthritis and other inflammatory or immune-related disorders. Its exact use depends on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow with water. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, especially if it has been used for a prolonged period.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, fluid retention and increased blood sugar may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions or any infection. This medicine can increase the risk of infections or hide their symptoms. Avoid close contact with people who have contagious infections and check with the doctor before receiving vaccines. Seek medical help for signs of a serious infection, severe allergic reaction or major mood changes.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactive immune reactions in conditions such as severe allergies, asthma, arthritis, and other inflammatory or autoimmune disorders. It should be used only for the condition prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of the immune system and lowers the release of substances that cause inflammation, swelling, redness and allergic symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food to reduce stomach upset. Do not stop it suddenly, especially after prolonged use; the dose may need to be reduced gradually under medical supervision.

Common side effects
Indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, increased blood sugar and increased blood pressure may occur. The risk of side effects increases with higher doses or longer treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health conditions or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce resistance to infection and may mask infection symptoms. Avoid contact with people who have contagious infections and check with a doctor before receiving vaccines. Seek medical help for signs of serious infection, severe mood changes, vision problems or black stools.

What is it used for?
Hydroxyzine is used to relieve itching and other symptoms caused by allergies or skin conditions. It may also be prescribed for short-term relief of anxiety and tension.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergic symptoms such as itching. It can also have a calming and sedating effect.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, headache, blurred vision and tiredness.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor before using it with sleeping tablets, sedatives or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice before use if there is heart disease, an irregular heartbeat, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic reaction or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Hydroxyzine is an antihistamine used to relieve itching caused by allergies and skin conditions. It may also be prescribed for short-term relief of anxiety.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions and itching. It can also reduce activity in the brain, which may cause a calming and drowsy effect.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, headache and constipation.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor before using it with sleeping tablets, sedatives or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Use cautiously if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, heart-rhythm problems, liver or kidney disease, or in older adults. Seek medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe confusion or difficulty breathing. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used topically to help relieve symptoms associated with cough and cold, such as nasal or chest discomfort.

How does it work?
It may provide soothing local effects and aromatic vapours that can help ease cough-and-cold discomfort. The exact action depends on the Ayurvedic ingredients in the product.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply or use it only as directed on the product label. Do not apply near the eyes, inside the nose or mouth, or on broken or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Skin irritation, redness, burning or an allergic skin reaction may occur.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes and mucous membranes, and do not swallow. Stop use if irritation or rash develops. Seek medical advice if cough or cold symptoms are severe, persistent, or associated with breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cough and cold symptoms through topical application.

How does it work?
Its topical ingredients may provide a soothing or warming sensation that helps relieve cough and cold discomfort. The exact action depends on the ingredients in the product.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the recommended area exactly as directed on the product label. Do not swallow, and avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Skin irritation, redness, itching or an allergic rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not apply to broken, irritated or sensitive skin. Stop use if significant irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Keep out of reach of children and seek medical advice if swallowed. Check the label for age-specific warnings before use in children.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of indigestion, acidity, stomach discomfort and gas-related bloating. It may also help relieve mild digestive discomfort caused by trapped gas.

How does it work?
Sarjikakshara helps neutralise excess stomach acid. Dill, anise and peppermint oils have carminative properties that may help ease intestinal spasms and the feeling of gas.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount or use it for a prolonged period without medical advice.

Common side effects
Mild nausea, belching, stomach discomfort or bloating may occur. Stop use if an allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Check with a healthcare professional before use in children, especially infants, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek advice before use in people with kidney or heart disease, high blood pressure, or when following a low-sodium diet. Seek medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, blood in the stool or symptoms that do not improve.

What is it used for?
Belladonna plaster is used for temporary relief of local muscle and joint aches, including some rheumatic or nerve-related pain.

How does it work?
It releases belladonna extract through the skin. Belladonna contains substances that can reduce nerve-related pain and muscle spasm in the treated area.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply the plaster to clean, dry, unbroken skin as directed on the product pack or by a healthcare professional. Do not apply it to the eyes, mouth, wounds or irritated skin. Wash hands after applying or removing it.

Common side effects
Skin redness, itching, irritation or a rash at the application site. Stop use if severe irritation occurs.

Precautions
Do not use on broken skin or over large areas. Avoid contact with the eyes and mucous membranes. Belladonna can rarely cause dry mouth, blurred vision, dizziness, fast heartbeat or confusion if absorbed in excess; remove the plaster and seek medical help if these occur. Keep away from children and do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat scabies and lice infestations. The cetrimide component also provides antiseptic action.

How does it work?
Gamma benzene hexachloride kills scabies mites and lice by affecting their nervous system. Cetrimide helps reduce germs on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid the eyes, mouth, mucous membranes and broken or inflamed skin. Wash hands after use unless the hands are the treated area. Do not swallow.

Common side effects
Skin irritation, burning, itching, redness or dryness may occur. Stop use and seek medical help for severe irritation, dizziness, tremors, confusion or seizures.

Precautions
Use only when specifically advised, as excessive use or application to large areas can cause serious toxicity. Avoid use in infants and young children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or in people with a history of seizures unless prescribed by a healthcare professional. Keep away from children and avoid contact with the eyes.

What is it used for?
A compressor nebulizer is used to deliver prescribed liquid medicines into the lungs as a fine mist. It may be used to help manage breathing conditions such as asthma and other respiratory illnesses, when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
The compressor pushes air through the liquid medicine, changing it into a mist that can be inhaled through a mask or mouthpiece.

How to take/use it
Use only the medicine and amount prescribed by a healthcare professional. Add the medicine to the nebulizer cup, attach the tubing and mask or mouthpiece, and breathe in the mist as directed. Sit upright during treatment. Clean and dry the nebulizer parts after each use according to the product instructions, and do not share the device.

Common side effects
The nebulizer itself usually does not cause side effects. The inhaled medicine may cause effects such as throat irritation, coughing, shakiness or a fast heartbeat, depending on the medicine used.

Precautions
Use the device only as instructed and do not use unprescribed solutions or oils. Keep the equipment clean to reduce the risk of infection. Seek urgent medical help if breathing difficulty becomes severe, symptoms suddenly worsen, or the prescribed treatment does not provide relief.

What is it used for?
Neem soap is used for cleansing the skin and removing dirt, oil and sweat. It may be used as part of a routine skin-care regimen.

How does it work?
Soap cleans the skin by helping loosen oil, dirt and other substances so they can be rinsed away. The neem ingredient does not establish a specific medical treatment use from the information provided.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Wet the skin, apply the soap to form a lather, rinse thoroughly and dry gently. Avoid contact with the eyes.

Common side effects
Skin dryness, irritation, redness or itching may occur, especially in sensitive skin.

Precautions
Stop using it if significant irritation, rash or swelling develops. Avoid use on broken or severely irritated skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Keep away from the eyes and do not swallow.

What is it used for?
Sodium chloride 0.9% is an isotonic saline solution. Depending on the product and route, it may be used by healthcare professionals to replace fluids and sodium, or for rinsing/irrigating areas such as the nose, eyes or wounds. The exact use depends on the product label.

How does it work?
It contains sodium and chloride in a concentration similar to body fluids. This helps replace fluid and electrolytes or gently rinse affected areas.

How to take/use it
Use only by the route and for the purpose stated on the product label or advised by a healthcare professional. Injectable products should be given only by trained healthcare professionals and must not be self-injected.

Common side effects
Side effects depend on how it is used. Mild irritation may occur with rinsing products. When given by injection, swelling or fluid overload may occur.

Precautions
Do not use an injectable product without medical supervision. Extra care is needed in people with heart failure, kidney problems or a tendency to retain fluid. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, marked swelling or worsening symptoms.

What is it used for?
Oral rehydration solution is used to prevent or treat dehydration caused by diarrhoea, loose motions, vomiting or excessive fluid loss. It replaces water and essential salts lost from the body.

How does it work?
It contains water, electrolytes and glucose. These help the intestines absorb fluid and salts, restoring the body's fluid and electrolyte balance.

How to take/use it
Drink it as directed on the label, taking small, frequent sips. It is ready to drink, so do not dilute it unless the product instructions say otherwise. Use the product within the recommended period after opening.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting or mild stomach discomfort may occur, especially if it is consumed too quickly.

Precautions
Seek medical care for severe or persistent diarrhoea or vomiting, blood in the stool, very little urination, extreme weakness, confusion or signs of severe dehydration. People with kidney disease, heart failure or conditions requiring fluid or salt restriction should seek medical advice before use. This solution does not treat the underlying cause of diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Oral rehydration solution helps prevent and treat dehydration caused by diarrhoea, vomiting, or excessive fluid loss. It replaces water and essential salts lost from the body.

How does it work?
It contains water, salts and glucose. The glucose and salts help the intestine absorb fluids more effectively.

How to take/use it
Drink by mouth in small, frequent sips. Use the ready-to-drink solution as supplied and follow the product label or healthcare professional’s advice. Do not add extra water or other ingredients unless instructed.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, bloating or mild stomach discomfort may occur, especially if taken too quickly.

Precautions
Seek medical help for severe dehydration, persistent vomiting, very little or no urination, blood in the stool, worsening symptoms or inability to drink. People with kidney disease, heart failure, or conditions requiring fluid or salt restriction should seek medical advice before use.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat dehydration caused by diarrhoea, vomiting, or excessive fluid loss by replacing lost water and salts.

How does it work?
It contains water, salts, and glucose. These help the body absorb fluids and restore the balance of water and electrolytes.

How to take/use it
Drink as directed on the product label. Take small, frequent sips, especially if feeling nauseous. Do not dilute or mix with other drinks unless the label instructs otherwise. Once opened, follow the storage and use instructions on the pack.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, or mild bloating may occur, particularly if consumed too quickly.

Precautions
Seek medical help if there are signs of severe dehydration, such as very little urine, extreme weakness, confusion, or drowsiness. Medical advice is also needed for persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, blood in the stool, high fever, or if the person cannot drink. People with kidney disease, heart failure, or conditions requiring fluid or salt restriction should consult a doctor before use.

What is it used for?
Used mainly to relieve menstrual cramps and abdominal pain caused by muscle spasms.

How does it work?
Mefenamic acid reduces the chemicals that cause pain and inflammation. Dicyclomine relaxes intestinal and abdominal muscles to reduce spasms and cramping.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, preferably with or after food and with water. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Avoid taking other painkillers containing NSAIDs unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness, dry mouth and blurred vision.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to mefenamic acid, other NSAIDs or dicyclomine. Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, glaucoma, or difficulty passing urine. It may not be suitable during pregnancy, especially from 20 weeks onwards and in the last trimester. Seek urgent medical help for severe stomach pain, black stools, vomiting blood, breathing difficulty or facial swelling.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to help treat superficial bacterial skin infections and infected minor wounds, cuts, abrasions or burns, as directed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It contains three antibacterial ingredients that work in different ways to stop the growth of bacteria and help control infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean and gently dry the affected area, then apply the powder as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not apply it to the eyes or mouth, and avoid breathing in the powder. Wash hands after use.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, redness, itching or skin irritation. Allergic skin reactions such as rash or swelling may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to neomycin, bacitracin, sulfonamides or any ingredient in the product. Avoid prolonged use or applying it over large areas unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe rash, swelling, breathing difficulty or worsening infection occurs.

What is it used for?
This supplement helps provide vitamins, minerals and ginseng to support general nutritional health, especially when dietary intake may be inadequate. It is not a substitute for a balanced diet.

How does it work?
Vitamins and minerals support normal body functions such as energy production, immunity and metabolism. Ginseng is an herbal ingredient traditionally used as a general tonic, but its benefits may vary.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow the softgel with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Avoid taking other multivitamin products at the same time unless advised.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include nausea, stomach discomfort, headache, difficulty sleeping or allergic reactions.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is diabetes, high blood pressure, kidney or liver disease. Consult a healthcare professional if taking blood thinners, diabetes medicines or other regular medicines. Stop use and seek medical help if a severe allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Cetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin allergies such as hives.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance released during an allergic reaction. This helps reduce itching, sneezing, runny nose and other allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take this tablet exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow it with water; it may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness or sleepiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, nausea and dizziness.

Precautions
It may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase sleepiness. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty or a severe rash.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with mucus (phlegm), especially when it occurs with allergy-related symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose or an itchy nose and throat.

How does it work?
Ambroxol helps loosen and thin mucus, making it easier to clear. Cetirizine is an antihistamine that reduces allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the label or by a doctor. Swallow with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid driving or operating machinery if drowsiness occurs.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dry mouth, headache, nausea, stomach upset or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid alcohol and be cautious with other medicines that cause drowsiness. Stop use and seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, a severe rash or worsening symptoms.

What is it used for?
Levocetirizine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It is also used to relieve itching and hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Swallow the tablet with water, with or without food, as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, and dry mouth.

Precautions
This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid or limit alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or a history of difficulty passing urine. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Cetirizine oral solution is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It is an antihistamine that blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce itching, swelling, sneezing and watery discharge.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Measure the liquid with the supplied measuring device, and do not take more than recommended. It may cause drowsiness in some people.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or tiredness, headache, dry mouth, nausea and dizziness.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Consult a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical help urgently for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Bacillus clausii is a probiotic used to help restore the natural balance of beneficial bacteria in the intestines, including during or after diarrhoea or other disturbances of gut flora.

How does it work?
It provides beneficial bacterial spores that can reach the intestine and help support the normal balance of gut bacteria.

How to take/use it
For oral use only. Take the suspension exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not mix it with hot liquids. Do not use a vial if it is damaged or the contents look unusual.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Occasional gas, bloating, nausea or stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if the person has a severely weakened immune system, is seriously ill or has a central venous catheter. Stop use and seek urgent medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur. Medical advice is needed for severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or signs of dehydration.

What is it used for?
Ketorolac is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine used for short-term relief of moderate to severe acute pain, such as pain after surgery or injury. It is not intended for long-term or mild pain relief.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, with a glass of water. Taking it with food may reduce stomach upset. Use the lowest effective amount for the shortest prescribed period. Do not take it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac, naproxen or aspirin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Stomach pain or discomfort, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney disease, or allergy to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Tell the doctor about heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma, dehydration, bleeding disorders, or use of blood thinners. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, chest pain or markedly reduced urination. It should generally be avoided in pregnancy, especially from 20 weeks onwards and during the third trimester, unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Ketorolac injection is used for the short-term relief of moderate to severe acute pain, such as pain after surgery. It is not intended for long-term pain treatment.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of prostaglandins, substances involved in pain, inflammation and fever. This helps reduce pain and swelling.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or nurse. Use it only as prescribed and do not take it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac or aspirin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Stomach pain or indigestion, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness and drowsiness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, dehydration, or allergy to aspirin or other NSAIDs. It may increase the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney problems. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or very little urine. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised, especially after 20 weeks and in the last trimester.

What is it used for?
Ketorolac is used for short-term relief of moderate to severe acute pain, such as pain after surgery or injury. It is not intended for long-term or chronic pain relief.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed, with a full glass of water. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not take it for longer than prescribed or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac or aspirin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Stomach pain or discomfort, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness and diarrhoea.

Precautions
Avoid use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney disease, or allergy to aspirin or other NSAIDs, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Use caution with heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma, dehydration or blood-thinning medicines. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or reduced urination. Avoid during pregnancy, especially from 20 weeks onwards, unless prescribed by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Triamcinolone acetonide injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and swelling in conditions such as painful or inflamed joints, allergic disorders, and other inflammatory conditions. The exact use depends on the condition and the injection site.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and allergic reactions. It also suppresses some immune responses.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The route and injection site depend on the condition being treated. It should not be self-injected.

Common side effects
Pain or irritation at the injection site, increased blood sugar, indigestion, mood or sleep changes, and increased risk of infections may occur. Repeated or prolonged use can cause additional corticosteroid-related effects.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma, osteoporosis, stomach ulcers, infections, or any other medical condition. Corticosteroids may worsen or hide infections and can affect blood sugar. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, and all medicines being used. Seek medical help for signs of a serious infection, severe allergic reaction, or vision changes.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin. Depending on the product form, it may also be used for dandruff or seborrhoeic dermatitis.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, helping to control and clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only on the affected area and follow the instructions on the product label or those given by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not swallow it.

Common side effects
Application-site burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation.

Precautions
For external use only. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Consult a healthcare professional if the infection worsens or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin and scalp, including conditions such as dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis when prescribed or labelled for these uses.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making ergosterol, an essential part of their cell membrane. This helps stop the growth of the fungus.

How to take/use it
Use it only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. If it is a topical preparation, use it on the affected skin or scalp as directed and avoid contact with the eyes. Do not use more often or for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
For external use only if supplied as a topical preparation. Avoid contact with the eyes and broken skin. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs. Tell a doctor if the infection does not improve or gets worse.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% is a topical antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin or scalp, including dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis when prescribed or recommended for these conditions.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making ergosterol, a substance they need to maintain their cell membranes. This helps control and clear the fungal infection.

How to take/use it
Use only on the skin or scalp, as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes and wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated. Do not swallow.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole or any ingredient. Avoid applying to the eyes, mouth or severely damaged skin. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs.

What is it used for?
Ketorolac injection is used for the short-term relief of moderate to severe acute pain, usually when an injection is needed.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a healthcare professional as an injection. Use it only as prescribed and for the shortest duration advised. Do not take other NSAID painkillers, such as ibuprofen or diclofenac, unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain or indigestion, headache, dizziness, and pain or irritation at the injection site.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney disease, bleeding problems, heart disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAIDs. It may increase the risk of stomach bleeding, kidney problems and allergic reactions. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or very little urine. It is generally avoided during pregnancy, especially in the later months, unless specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat fungal infections accompanied by redness, itching or inflammation, such as ringworm and similar fungal rashes.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole stops the growth of fungi. Beclomethasone reduces redness, swelling and itching caused by skin inflammation.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the affected skin exactly as prescribed, usually after cleaning and drying the area. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Do not cover the area tightly unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, irritation, dryness or redness at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Use only for the condition diagnosed by a healthcare professional, as the steroid may mask or worsen some infections. Do not use for longer than recommended. Avoid applying to large areas, broken skin, the face, skin folds or the genital area unless advised. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens, spreads or does not improve. Children, pregnant or breastfeeding women should use it only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
This topical medicine is used to treat fungal infections of the skin. It may help relieve symptoms such as itching, redness and scaling caused by fungal infection.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole stops the growth of fungi by damaging their cell membranes. Cetrimide acts as an antiseptic and helps reduce microorganisms on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the affected area as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Keep the area clean and dry, and wash hands before and after use. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole, cetrimide or any ingredient. Avoid applying to the eyes or severely damaged skin. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or worsening symptoms occur.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to help treat fungal skin infections.

How does it work?
Ketoconazole is an antifungal medicine that stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, helping control the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use on the affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes and rinse well with water if this happens. Do not swallow.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, dryness or burning may occur. Tea tree oil fragrance may also cause irritation or an allergic skin reaction in sensitive people.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ketoconazole, tea tree oil or any ingredient. Avoid applying to the eyes, mouth, mucous membranes or severely broken skin. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or worsening symptoms occur.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cough, blocked or stuffy nose, runny nose and sneezing associated with common cold and similar upper-airway conditions.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps reduce the urge to cough. Phenylephrine helps relieve nasal blockage, while chlorpheniramine reduces runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Measure the liquid carefully using a suitable measuring device. Do not take it with other cough, cold or allergy medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, nervousness, headache and difficulty sleeping. Phenylephrine may cause palpitations or a temporary increase in blood pressure.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if drowsy or less alert. Seek medical advice before use in people with high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid problems, prostate or urinary difficulties, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines, or within 14 days of stopping them, unless advised by a doctor. Keep out of reach of children and seek medical advice for young children. Seek medical help if breathing difficulty occurs or the cough persists or worsens.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough, particularly cough associated with mucus and cold symptoms.

How does it work?
Ammonium chloride and sodium citrate help loosen and clear mucus. Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine that reduces histamine-related symptoms and may also help soothe cough.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Use the supplied measuring device rather than a household spoon, and do not take more than recommended. This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea or stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and other medicines that cause drowsiness unless advised by a healthcare professional. Check with a healthcare professional before use in young children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, breathing problems, or significant liver or kidney disease. Seek medical advice if the cough is severe, lasts more than a few days, or is accompanied by breathing difficulty, chest pain or high fever.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough, including cough associated with colds. It may help loosen mucus and reduce the urge to cough.

How does it work?
Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine that can reduce cough and allergy-related symptoms. Ammonium chloride helps loosen mucus, while sodium citrate supports mucus clearance.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Measure the liquid with a proper measuring device. Do not take more than recommended. Diphenhydramine may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known.

Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea or stomach discomfort.

Use cautiously in older adults and in people with glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, breathing problems or other conditions affected by drowsiness. What is it used for?
Used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, itching, watery eyes and hives. Diphenhydramine may also cause drowsiness and is sometimes used short-term to help with sleep, only when recommended on the product label or by a healthcare professional.

Used for temporary relief of cough, blocked nose, runny nose and sneezing associated with the common cold.

Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines, and check with a healthcare professional before combining it with antidepressants or other medicines.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cough, blocked nose, runny nose and sneezing associated with common cold and similar upper-respiratory symptoms.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps suppress the cough reflex. Phenylephrine reduces nasal swelling, while chlorpheniramine helps relieve runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Shake the bottle well and measure the liquid with the supplied measuring device. Do not take it with other cough, cold or allergy medicines containing similar ingredients.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea and stomach upset. Palpitations or a rise in blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness—avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Seek medical advice before use in high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, breathing problems or difficulty passing urine. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines or within 14 days of stopping them. Consult a doctor before giving it to children, and seek medical help if the cough is severe, persistent or associated with breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cough, blocked or stuffy nose, runny nose and sneezing associated with cold symptoms.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps suppress coughing. Phenylephrine reduces nasal congestion, while chlorpheniramine helps relieve runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other cough, cold or allergy medicines without medical advice.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, nervousness or difficulty sleeping. Phenylephrine may cause a fast heartbeat or increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery, as drowsiness or dizziness may occur. Consult a doctor before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, prostate or urinary problems, or if taking antidepressants or other regular medicines. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen, last several days, or the cough is severe or persistent.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for temporary relief of cough and cold symptoms, including dry cough, blocked or stuffy nose, and runny nose.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan suppresses the cough reflex. Phenylephrine helps reduce nasal congestion, while chlorpheniramine helps relieve runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Measure the liquid with a proper measuring device. Do not take more than recommended, and avoid using other cough, cold or allergy medicines at the same time unless advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, stomach upset, restlessness or difficulty sleeping. Phenylephrine may cause a fast heartbeat or a rise in blood pressure.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy. Ask a doctor before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, prostate problems or liver disease.
