What is it used for?
Used to relieve dry cough and associated cold or allergy symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Levodropropizine helps reduce the cough reflex. Chlorpheniramine blocks histamine, helping relieve symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed by the doctor or according to the product label. Use a measuring cup or oral syringe to measure the liquid accurately, and do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea or stomach discomfort.

Precautions
This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Check with a doctor before use with sleeping medicines, sedatives or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice for breathing difficulty, worsening symptoms or a cough that does not improve. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding or in young children.

What is it used for?
Used to loosen and clear thick mucus and relieve cough associated with narrowed airways or wheezing in respiratory conditions.

How does it work?
Ambroxol helps thin mucus, while guaiphenesin helps loosen and expel phlegm. Levosalbutamol relaxes the airway muscles, helping improve airflow.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed by a doctor or the product label. Use a measuring device for the liquid and do not exceed the recommended amount. Shake well before use if indicated on the label.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, tremor, muscle cramps, fast heartbeat or palpitations may occur.

Precautions
Use cautiously in people with heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, seizures or sensitivity to bronchodilator medicines. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, or signs of an allergic reaction. Consult a doctor if the cough worsens or does not improve.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve wet or productive cough with thick mucus and wheezing or breathing difficulty caused by narrowed airways in respiratory conditions.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus, making it easier to cough up. Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles of the airways to help improve breathing.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Measure the liquid with a proper measuring device and do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not combine it with other cough or breathing medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, shakiness, nervousness, muscle cramps or fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid or a history of seizures. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, chest pain, worsening breathing difficulty, or signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with mucus and chest congestion, especially when airway narrowing causes wheezing or breathing difficulty.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus so it can be coughed up more easily. Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles of the airways to help improve breathing.

How to take/use it
Shake well before use and measure with a medicine cup or oral syringe. Take only the dose and for the duration recommended by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not exceed the recommended dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach upset, headache, trembling, muscle cramps, fast heartbeat or palpitations.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, glaucoma or a history of seizures. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, or an allergic reaction. Consult a doctor if the cough persists or worsens.

What is it used for?
Used to help restore healthy bacteria in the intestine and support recovery from diarrhoea or loose motions, including diarrhoea that may occur after antibiotic use.

How does it work?
It supplies beneficial lactic acid-producing bacteria that help support the normal balance of microorganisms in the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not mix with very hot drinks or food. Drink plenty of fluids if experiencing loose motions.

Common side effects
Mild gas, bloating or stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, high fever, signs of dehydration or severe abdominal pain. People with severely weakened immunity or serious illness should use probiotics only after medical advice.

What is it used for?
Levofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops bacteria from making and repairing their genetic material, which kills the bacteria and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc; follow the recommended time gap advised by the prescriber or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and sleep disturbance.

Precautions
Tell the prescriber about kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, tendon disorders, seizures, nerve problems or a history of reactions to quinolone antibiotics. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, irregular heartbeat, severe allergic symptoms or unusual mood or nerve-related changes. Use during pregnancy, breastfeeding or in children only when specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Levofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin and other parts of the body. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking enzymes they need to copy and repair their genetic material.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Antacids and supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc can reduce its absorption, so ask a doctor or pharmacist how to separate them from this medicine.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and difficulty sleeping.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, heart rhythm problems, seizures, tendon problems, nerve problems, myasthenia gravis, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or burning sensations, severe or persistent diarrhoea, serious rash or breathing difficulty, or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Avoid unnecessary strenuous exercise if tendon pain occurs.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain bacterial and protozoal infections, including some intestinal infections that cause diarrhoea or dysentery. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Levofloxacin kills susceptible bacteria by blocking enzymes needed for their growth. Ornidazole damages the genetic material of certain protozoa and anaerobic bacteria, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet whole with water. Keep antacids and supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc at least 2 hours apart from this medicine. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 3 days after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and a metallic or unpleasant taste.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to levofloxacin, other quinolone antibiotics or ornidazole. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, seizures, heart rhythm problems, tendon problems, or nerve disorders, and if pregnant or breastfeeding. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, confusion, rash, breathing difficulty or an irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Linezolid is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, including some infections of the lungs, skin and soft tissues, and infections caused by resistant bacteria. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not share it or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache and a change in taste may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially antidepressants, opioid pain medicines or other medicines that affect serotonin or blood pressure. Blood tests may be needed during treatment, particularly if treatment continues for more than a short period. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, unusual bruising or bleeding, vision changes, numbness or tingling, or severe weakness.

What is it used for?
Linezolid is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by certain Gram-positive bacteria, including some types of pneumonia, skin and soft-tissue infections, and infections caused by vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus (VRE). It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not take more or for longer than advised. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and changes in taste.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially antidepressants or other medicines that affect serotonin, and medicines used for high blood pressure. Linezolid may affect blood counts, especially during longer treatment, so monitoring may be advised. Seek medical help for unusual bruising or bleeding, severe diarrhoea, repeated vomiting, numbness or tingling, vision changes, severe weakness, or confusion. Avoid large amounts of mature or aged foods unless advised otherwise.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of mild to moderate pain and inflammation, especially muscle, joint and other musculoskeletal pain.

How does it work?
Lornoxicam reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take other medicines containing paracetamol or NSAIDs unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and drowsiness.

Precautions
Avoid or seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or use of blood thinners. Avoid alcohol and do not exceed the prescribed dose, as excess paracetamol can seriously damage the liver. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, breathing difficulty, or severe skin reactions. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
This syrup is a nutritional supplement used to help prevent or correct vitamin and mineral deficiencies and support general nutritional needs when the diet is inadequate. Lycopene provides an antioxidant nutrient. It is not a treatment for a specific disease unless prescribed for that purpose.

How does it work?
The vitamins and minerals support normal body functions, including energy production, immunity and tissue maintenance. Lycopene acts as an antioxidant.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Use the measuring device provided and do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not use it as a substitute for a balanced diet.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, constipation or diarrhoea may occur. Some formulations may also cause temporary changes in stool or urine colour.

Precautions
Check the ingredients if there is an allergy or sensitivity to any component. Avoid taking other multivitamin or mineral supplements at the same time unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or in people with kidney or liver disease or other long-term medical conditions. Keep out of reach of children; accidental overdose of some vitamins or minerals can be harmful.

What is it used for?
Levocetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take the tablet exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow it with water; it may generally be taken with or without food. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness or sleepiness, tiredness, headache, and dry mouth.

Precautions
Drowsiness may occur; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase sleepiness. People with kidney problems, or those who are pregnant or breastfeeding, should seek medical advice before use. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Methylcobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 used to prevent or treat vitamin B12 deficiency. Vitamin B12 deficiency can contribute to certain types of anaemia and nerve-related symptoms such as tingling or numbness.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamin B12, which is needed for healthy red blood cell formation and normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Use it only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. The appropriate treatment depends on the cause and severity of vitamin B12 deficiency.

Common side effects
It is generally well tolerated. Nausea, diarrhoea, headache or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to methylcobalamin or any ingredient in the product. Seek medical advice if symptoms such as persistent tiredness, numbness or tingling continue, as the underlying cause may need evaluation. People with significant anaemia or nerve symptoms should use it under medical guidance.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat deficiencies of vitamin B12, vitamin B6 and niacinamide. These vitamins help support normal nerve function, red blood cell formation and energy metabolism.

How does it work?
It replenishes important B vitamins needed for healthy nerves, blood cells and normal energy production.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as directed by the doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Swallow with water.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset or headache may occur.

Precautions
This product contains a high dose of vitamin B6. Prolonged or excessive use may cause nerve problems such as tingling, numbness or burning sensations; stop use and seek medical advice if these occur. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is liver or kidney disease. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Methylcobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 used to prevent or treat vitamin B12 deficiency. Vitamin B12 deficiency can lead to megaloblastic anaemia and nerve-related symptoms such as tingling or numbness.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamin B12, which the body needs to make healthy red blood cells and maintain normal nerve function.

Take or use it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. The dose and duration depend on the severity and cause of vitamin B12 deficiency and the product form.

Nausea, diarrhoea, headache or skin rash may occur. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as facial swelling or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
This combination provides vitamins and alpha-lipoic acid to support normal nerve function and help prevent or correct nutritional deficiencies. It may be used as a nutritional supplement for symptoms such as tingling or numbness when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Methylcobalamin, folic acid and pyridoxine help support healthy nerve function and blood-cell formation. Alpha-lipoic acid provides antioxidant support, while vitamin D supports normal muscle and bone function.

Use only in the amount and for the duration recommended on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other vitamin supplements without medical advice.

Nausea, stomach discomfort, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache or skin rash may occur. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

Tell a healthcare professional about all medicines and supplements being used. People taking diabetes medicines should seek advice before use because alpha-lipoic acid may affect blood sugar. What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat deficiencies of vitamin B12, vitamin B6 and nicotinamide. It may also be used when these deficiencies contribute to nerve-related symptoms or certain blood-related problems.

How does it work?
It replenishes important B vitamins needed for normal nerve function, red blood cell formation and energy metabolism.

How to take/use it
This is an injectable medicine and should be given by a healthcare professional. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the medical condition and should be followed as prescribed. Do not self-inject.

Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site, nausea, headache or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to vitamin B12, vitamin B6, nicotinamide or similar injections. Use only under medical supervision, especially if repeated doses are needed, as prolonged high-dose vitamin B6 may affect the nerves. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash after the injection.

What is it used for?
Used when prescribed for vitamin B-group deficiency and related nerve problems, including symptoms such as tingling or numbness.

How does it work?
It replenishes methylcobalamin (vitamin B12), vitamin B6 and nicotinamide, which support normal nerve function and blood-cell formation.

How to take/use it
This is an injection and should be given by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the medical condition and should be followed exactly as prescribed.

Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; nausea, headache or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to vitamin B12, vitamin B6, nicotinamide or injection ingredients. This combination is used as nutritional support for nerve health and to supplement vitamins involved in normal nerve function and blood-cell formation. Methylcobalamin, pyridoxine and folic acid support normal nerve function and red blood cell formation. Alpha lipoic acid is an antioxidant involved in energy metabolism and may help protect cells from oxidative stress.

What is it used for?
Mefloquine is used to prevent and treat malaria, a serious infection spread by mosquito bites.

It kills the malaria parasite in the blood by interfering with processes the parasite needs to survive.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor. The dose and schedule depend on whether it is being used for prevention or treatment. Take it with food and plenty of water, and complete the prescribed course. Do not self-medicate or use it for unexplained fever.

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, dizziness, headache, sleep disturbance, vivid dreams and tiredness.

Amoxycillin kills bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against a wider range of bacteria.

Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems and any previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, a severe skin rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Meropenem is a strong antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by susceptible bacteria, such as infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, blood, or brain. It does not work against viral infections.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall, helping stop the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
Meropenem is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse, usually in a hospital or healthcare setting. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function, and medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea or vomiting, headache, rash, and pain, redness or swelling at the injection site.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about allergies to meropenem, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics, kidney problems, seizures, or nervous-system disorders. Tell the doctor about all medicines being used, especially valproate. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, facial swelling, breathing difficulty, seizures, or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Methylergometrine maleate is used after childbirth or certain pregnancy-related procedures to help the uterus contract and control or prevent heavy bleeding caused by poor uterine contraction.

How does it work?
It increases the strength of uterine contractions, helping the uterus tighten and reduce bleeding.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor, usually after childbirth or a pregnancy-related procedure. Do not use it during pregnancy unless specifically directed by a specialist. Do not self-medicate for heavy bleeding; seek urgent medical care.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, abdominal cramps and increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is high blood pressure, pre-eclampsia or eclampsia, heart or blood-vessel disease, or a history of stroke. Seek urgent medical help for severe headache, chest pain, breathing difficulty, seizures, or very heavy or persistent bleeding.

What is it used for?
Mefenamic acid is used for short-term relief of mild to moderate pain, including menstrual cramps and other body pain.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, preferably with or after food and with water. Use the lowest effective amount for the shortest time advised. Do not take it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen, naproxen or aspirin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Stomach pain or indigestion, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, dizziness and headache.

Precautions
Avoid or seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to NSAID medicines. Inform the doctor if taking blood thinners or other medicines. Avoid during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed, especially from 20 weeks onwards and in the last 3 months. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin rash.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of mild to moderate pain and fever.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever. Mefenamic acid is an anti-inflammatory medicine that reduces substances involved in pain, swelling and fever.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Shake the bottle well and measure the liquid with the supplied measuring device. Do not take more than prescribed or use it with other medicines containing paracetamol or mefenamic acid/other NSAIDs.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, indigestion or dizziness.

Precautions
Use cautiously in children with dehydration, stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver problems, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAIDs. Avoid use with other paracetamol-containing or NSAID medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, vomiting blood or black stools.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve occasional constipation and make stools easier to pass.

How does it work?
Milk of magnesia draws water into the bowel to soften the stool and promote bowel movement. Liquid paraffin lubricates the stool and bowel, helping it pass more easily.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended or use it for a prolonged period without medical advice. Drink adequate fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised.

Common side effects
Loose stools or diarrhoea, abdominal cramps, bloating, nausea and stomach discomfort. Liquid paraffin may occasionally cause oily leakage from the rectum.

Precautions
Do not use it for severe or persistent abdominal pain, vomiting, or suspected bowel blockage unless advised by a doctor. Ask a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, difficulty swallowing, or ongoing constipation. Avoid prolonged or frequent use without medical advice, as it may cause fluid or electrolyte problems and reduce absorption of some nutrients or medicines. Seek medical advice if constipation does not improve or if there is blood in the stool.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of constipation and to help make stools softer and easier to pass.

How does it work?
Milk of magnesia draws water into the bowel, liquid paraffin lubricates and softens the stool, and sodium picosulphate stimulates bowel movement.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Measure the liquid carefully, do not exceed the recommended amount, and drink adequate fluids unless otherwise advised. Do not use it for a prolonged period without medical advice.

Common side effects
Abdominal cramps, loose stools or diarrhoea, nausea, bloating and increased bowel movements.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if there is severe or unexplained abdominal pain, vomiting, suspected bowel blockage or rectal bleeding. Use cautiously in kidney disease or if dehydrated. Stop and seek medical advice if constipation continues, diarrhoea is severe, or there is weakness, dizziness or reduced urination.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve mild to moderate pain and reduce fever.

How does it work?
Mefenamic acid reduces the production of substances that cause pain, inflammation and fever. Paracetamol also helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth only as directed by a doctor or the product label. Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with an accurate measuring device. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or another NSAID painkiller unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Stomach pain, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Use in children only according to medical advice or the recommended age and weight-based instructions. Avoid or seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to NSAIDs. Avoid use during the last three months of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin rash, black stools, vomiting blood, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine is used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve heartburn, acid indigestion and symptoms of acid reflux (GERD). It may also be prescribed for treating or preventing stomach and intestinal ulcers.

How does it work?
It blocks H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the amount of acid produced. This helps relieve acid-related symptoms and allows ulcers to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or return frequently.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, constipation or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if other medicines are being taken. Seek urgent medical help for vomiting blood, black stools, severe stomach pain, difficulty swallowing, or unexplained weight loss. Ranitidine use or availability may be restricted in some countries because of safety concerns about impurities; use it only when advised by a qualified healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine injection is used to reduce excess stomach acid in conditions such as acidity, heartburn, stomach ulcers and acid reflux. It may be used when medicine cannot be taken by mouth.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine H2 receptors in the stomach, which reduces the production of stomach acid.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or nurse. It should not be self-administered. The dose and duration depend on the condition and should be decided by the treating doctor.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea or constipation, and pain or irritation at the injection site.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, a history of acute porphyria, allergies, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being used. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, severe rash, confusion, or an irregular heartbeat. Persistent or unexplained stomach symptoms should be medically assessed.

What is it used for?
Used to help control asthma and other obstructive airway conditions, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), by reducing airway narrowing, breathing difficulty and mucus-related symptoms. It is not intended to provide immediate relief during a sudden breathing attack.

How does it work?
Montelukast blocks substances that cause airway inflammation and narrowing. Acebrophylline helps relax the airways and improve mucus clearance, making breathing easier.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Use it regularly as directed and do not take an extra dose if one is missed without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, dizziness, tremor or palpitations.

Precautions
This medicine is not a substitute for a rescue inhaler during an acute asthma or breathing attack. Inform the doctor about liver, kidney, heart or seizure problems, peptic ulcers, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Seek medical advice promptly for worsening breathing, severe palpitations, allergic reactions, or mood or behaviour changes such as agitation, depression or suicidal thoughts.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for allergy-related nose and airway symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and cough with thick mucus. It may be prescribed when allergy symptoms occur along with mucus in the airways.

How does it work?
Montelukast reduces allergy-related airway inflammation, while levocetirizine blocks histamine to relieve allergy symptoms. Ambroxol helps thin and loosen mucus so it can be cleared more easily.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised. This medicine is not a rescue treatment for a sudden asthma or breathing attack.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, headache, dry mouth, nausea, stomach discomfort, indigestion or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Drowsiness may occur; avoid driving or alcohol if affected. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being used. Seek medical advice promptly for mood or behaviour changes, unusual thoughts, severe rash, facial swelling or difficulty breathing. Do not use it to treat a sudden asthma attack.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis (hay fever), such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and itchy or watery eyes.

How does it work?
Fexofenadine blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, chemicals that can contribute to inflammation and nasal allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed and swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not take it with apple, orange or grapefruit juice, as these may reduce fexofenadine absorption. Avoid taking aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids close to this medicine unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, nausea, tiredness, dry mouth and stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Montelukast has been linked to mood or behaviour changes, unusual dreams, sleep problems, anxiety, depression and suicidal thoughts. Seek medical advice promptly if any such changes occur. This medicine is not intended for sudden asthma attacks. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and any other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis (hay fever), such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, nose or throat itching, and watery or itchy eyes. It may also be prescribed as an add-on treatment for asthma in some patients.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which can contribute to nasal swelling and breathing-related symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet whole with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. This medicine does not relieve a sudden asthma or breathing attack.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, headache, dry mouth, tiredness, abdominal pain, nausea, or sore throat may occur.

Precautions
Drowsiness may occur; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known. Contact a doctor promptly if there are unusual mood or behaviour changes, sleep problems, agitation, depression, or thoughts of self-harm. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Do not stop prescribed asthma treatment without medical advice.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, nasal itching and itchy or watery eyes.

How does it work?
Montelukast blocks substances called leukotrienes that contribute to allergy-related inflammation. Levocetirizine blocks histamine, another substance responsible for allergy symptoms.

Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed. Swallow the film-coated tablet whole with water. Do not take more than recommended. This medicine is not meant to provide immediate relief during a sudden asthma attack.

Avoid alcohol and be careful with driving or operating machinery until the effect on alertness is known. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or a history of mental health problems. Contact the doctor promptly if unusual mood or behaviour changes, nightmares, sleep problems, anxiety, depression or thoughts of self-harm occur. Seek urgent medical help for signs of a severe allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

Montelukast blocks substances involved in allergy-related inflammation. Levocetirizine is an antihistamine that reduces allergy symptoms such as sneezing, itching and a runny nose.

Precautions

What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis, such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It may also be prescribed as an add-on treatment for some people with asthma, but it does not relieve a sudden asthma attack.

How does it work?
Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, chemicals that contribute to allergy and airway inflammation. Levocetirizine is an antihistamine that reduces allergy symptoms such as sneezing, itching and a runny nose.

Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Shake the bottle well before use and measure the liquid with the supplied measuring device. Do not take more than the prescribed amount. Follow the prescribed schedule and duration.

Sleepiness or tiredness, headache, dry mouth, stomach pain or discomfort, and nausea may occur.

Precautions
Levocetirizine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or alcohol until its effects are known. Tell the doctor about kidney disease or any previous allergy to this medicine. What is it used for?
Used to relieve symptoms of allergies such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose or throat, and watery or itchy eyes. It may also be prescribed as an add-on treatment for certain breathing problems related to asthma, but it does not provide quick relief during an asthma attack.

Montelukast blocks chemicals involved in airway inflammation and allergy symptoms. Levocetirizine is an antihistamine that reduces the effects of histamine, helping relieve common allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by the doctor. Measure the liquid with the provided measuring device and do not exceed the prescribed amount. Do not use it as a rescue medicine for sudden breathing difficulty.

Precautions

Seek medical advice if there are mood or behaviour changes, unusual dreams, agitation, or thoughts of self-harm. Seek urgent help for severe breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Moxifloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops bacteria from making the genetic material they need to grow and survive.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water, with or without food. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc; ask a pharmacist about suitable spacing.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice. Seek urgent medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, fainting or a fast/irregular heartbeat, or signs of a serious allergic reaction. Tell the doctor about heart-rhythm problems, tendon disorders, nerve problems, myasthenia gravis, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all medicines being used.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the ear, throat, chest, skin, urinary tract and teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not share leftover antibiotics with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to amoxycillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, or a severe skin reaction. Contact a doctor if diarrhoea is severe or persistent. Use only under medical advice, especially during pregnancy, breastfeeding or if there is kidney disease.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with potassium clavulanate is a prescription antibiotic used to treat a range of bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, sinuses, lungs, skin, urinary tract or teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Potassium clavulanate helps protect amoxycillin from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against more bacterial strains.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with a meal, and complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not share it or use leftover antibiotics.

Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach discomfort, headache, skin rash and fungal infections such as oral or vaginal thrush.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to amoxycillin, penicillins, cephalosporins or similar antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems, previous antibiotic-related jaundice or colitis, or glandular fever. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, a severe blistering rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin is an antibiotic used to treat infections caused by susceptible bacteria. It does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of acidity, heartburn and acid-related stomach discomfort or pain.

Aluminium hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide neutralise excess stomach acid. Oxetacaine helps reduce the sensation of pain by locally numbing the stomach lining.

Use by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Ask a pharmacist about spacing it from other medicines, as antacids can affect their absorption.

Constipation, loose stools or diarrhoea, nausea, and stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease or an allergy to any ingredient. Seek medical advice for persistent or worsening symptoms, difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood or black stools. Do not use for prolonged periods without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Prochlorperazine is mainly used to control nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for severe dizziness or vertigo.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals in areas of the brain that trigger nausea and vomiting. It also reduces abnormal signals involved in vertigo.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more than directed. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or using machinery until its effects are known. Avoid alcohol.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision and headache. It may also cause restlessness, muscle stiffness or tremors.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, glaucoma, prostate or urinary problems, liver disease, heart rhythm problems, or a history of involuntary movements. Seek urgent medical help for severe muscle stiffness, high fever, confusion, fainting, or uncontrolled movements.

What is it used for?
This topical antibiotic combination is used to help prevent or treat bacterial infection in minor cuts, scrapes, and other small skin wounds.

How does it work?
Neomycin, polymyxin B, and bacitracin work together to stop the growth of susceptible bacteria on the skin.

Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not use it for longer than recommended.

Skin irritation, redness, itching, or rash. Neomycin may cause allergic skin reactions in some people.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth, and inside of the nose. Do not apply to large areas, deep wounds, serious burns, or animal bites unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe rash, swelling, breathing difficulty, worsening infection, or no improvement occurs.

Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

Indigestion, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache may occur.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, urinary tract and respiratory system. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

It should generally be avoided during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Piroxicam is an anti-inflammatory painkiller used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness in conditions such as arthritis and other muscle or joint problems.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Follow the instructions on the label. If directed, disperse the tablet in water before taking it. Taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and skin rash.

Precautions

Do not take it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised. Tell the doctor about kidney, liver, heart or blood-pressure problems, or if taking blood thinners. Avoid use during the last 3 months of pregnancy. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Piroxicam is used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness caused by inflammatory joint conditions such as osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that reduces the production of substances responsible for pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed and follow the instructions for the supplied formulation. Do not use more than recommended or for longer than advised. Do not combine it with other NSAIDs, such as ibuprofen or diclofenac, unless directed by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and skin rash.

Precautions

What is it used for?
Piroxicam is used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness caused by arthritis and other painful muscle, joint or bone conditions. It may also be prescribed for short-term treatment of acute painful inflammation, such as gout.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Dissolve the dispersible tablet as directed on the label or by the pharmacist, and do not take more than the prescribed amount. Taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not use it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and skin rash.

Precautions
Piroxicam can cause stomach ulcers or bleeding, especially with prolonged use. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash. Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAIDs. It may not be suitable during pregnancy, particularly after 20 weeks and in the last 3 months. Avoid alcohol and inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially blood thinners, steroids, aspirin or other NSAIDs.

What is it used for?
Used to help prevent and relieve nausea and vomiting during pregnancy.

How does it work?
Doxylamine is an antihistamine with anti-nausea effects. Pyridoxine is vitamin B6; together, they help reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed or as directed on the product label. Do not take more than recommended. This medicine may cause drowsiness, so follow instructions about driving and other activities requiring alertness.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth and constipation.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor or pharmacist before using other medicines that cause drowsiness. Use caution when driving. Seek medical advice if vomiting is severe, persistent or accompanied by signs of dehydration. Tell the doctor if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine or any allergy to its ingredients.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent and control nausea and vomiting during pregnancy. It should be used under medical advice.

How does it work?
Doxylamine helps reduce nausea signals in the brain. Pyridoxine (vitamin B6) also helps relieve pregnancy-related nausea, while folic acid supports normal folate needs.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Follow the dose and schedule on the label, and do not take more than recommended. Doxylamine may cause sleepiness, so avoid driving until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth and constipation.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and check with a doctor or pharmacist before using other medicines that cause drowsiness. Inform the doctor about glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, or other medical conditions. Seek medical advice if vomiting is severe or there are signs of dehydration, such as very little urine, extreme weakness or dizziness.

What is it used for?
Norethisterone is a progestogen used to manage menstrual problems such as heavy, painful or irregular periods. It may also be prescribed for endometriosis or to delay a period.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone progesterone. It changes the lining of the womb and helps control menstrual bleeding; its effects depend on the treatment schedule and reason for use.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and at the same time each day, with water. The dose and treatment duration vary depending on the condition being treated. It is not a contraceptive.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, breast tenderness, bloating, mood changes, and spotting or irregular bleeding may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor if there is a history of blood clots, liver disease, unexplained vaginal bleeding, migraine, or hormone-sensitive cancer. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, coughing blood, severe headache, vision changes, or painful swelling in a leg.

What is it used for?
Protein powder is used to supplement dietary protein when protein intake from food may be insufficient. Protein supports muscle maintenance, growth and repair, but this product is not a treatment for a specific disease.

How does it work?
It provides protein and amino acids that the body uses to build and repair tissues and maintain muscle.

How to take/use it
Mix and consume only as directed on the product label. The exact serving size and mixing instructions depend on the formulation. Do not use it as a complete substitute for a balanced diet.

Common side effects
Bloating, gas, stomach discomfort, nausea or loose motions may occur, especially if taken in large amounts or if the product contains ingredients that are not well tolerated.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list for milk, soy or other allergens. People with kidney or liver disease, milk-protein allergy or lactose intolerance should seek medical advice before use. Pregnant or breastfeeding women, children and people following a medically restricted diet should consult a healthcare professional before taking it.

What is it used for?
A protein supplement used to help increase daily protein intake and support muscle maintenance and recovery when used with a balanced diet and suitable physical activity.

How does it work?
It provides protein, which is broken down into amino acids used by the body to build and repair muscles and other tissues.

How to take/use it
Mix and use according to the instructions on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended serving. Use as part of a balanced diet and drink adequate fluids.

Common side effects
May cause bloating, gas, nausea, stomach discomfort or loose motions in some people. Allergic reactions may occur in people sensitive to an ingredient.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list if there is an allergy or intolerance to milk, soy or other ingredients. People with kidney or liver disease, or those who are pregnant or breastfeeding, should seek medical advice before use. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary protein supplement to help increase daily protein intake and support general nutrition and muscle maintenance.

How does it work?
It provides protein, which is broken down into amino acids used by the body for maintaining and repairing muscles and other tissues.

How to take/use it
Mix and consume as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended serving. Use the provided scoop, if included, and prepare with the liquid specified on the label.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list for allergens before use, especially if there is a known food allergy or intolerance. People with kidney disease or other medical conditions should seek medical advice before using protein supplements. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
Protein powder is used to supplement daily protein intake. It may support muscle maintenance and recovery when combined with a balanced diet and appropriate physical activity.

How does it work?
It provides protein, which is broken down into amino acids used for maintaining and repairing body tissues.

Mix and use only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended serving. It should supplement, not replace, a balanced diet.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list for milk, soy or other allergens. Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, a known food allergy, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if protein-restricted diets are advised. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
Used to supplement dietary protein when the daily diet does not provide enough. Protein supports muscle maintenance, growth and general nutritional needs.

How does it work?
It provides protein, which is broken down into amino acids used by the body to build and repair tissues.

How to take/use it
Mix and consume as directed on the product packaging. Do not exceed the recommended serving. Use as part of a balanced diet and adequate fluid intake.

Common side effects
Bloating, gas, stomach discomfort, nausea or loose motions may occur in some people. Allergic reactions may occur if the product contains an ingredient that causes sensitivity.

Precautions
Check the ingredient list for milk, soy or other allergens. People with kidney or liver disease, or those who are pregnant or breastfeeding, should seek medical advice before use. Stop use and seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Rabeprazole injection reduces excess stomach acid. It is used for acid-related conditions such as heartburn, gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and stomach or duodenal ulcers, particularly when oral treatment is not suitable.

How does it work?
It is a proton pump inhibitor that blocks the final step of acid production in the stomach, thereby reducing acidity and allowing irritation or ulcers to heal.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. It should not be self-administered. The dose and duration depend on the condition being treated and the healthcare professional’s advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, constipation, and gas may occur. Injection-site discomfort may also occur.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about any allergy to rabeprazole or other acid-reducing medicines, liver problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and other medicines being taken. Seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction, severe or persistent diarrhoea, or unusual weakness or muscle cramps, especially during prolonged treatment.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine reduces excess stomach acid and is used for acidity, heartburn, acid reflux, and stomach or duodenal ulcers.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the amount of acid produced.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take it for longer than recommended without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, constipation, or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Seek medical advice for persistent or recurrent symptoms, difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss, or severe stomach pain. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease and other medicines being taken. Ranitidine products have been withdrawn or restricted in some countries due to contamination concerns; use only if approved and advised by a healthcare professional locally.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine injection is used to reduce excess stomach acid in conditions such as acidity, heartburn, gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and stomach or duodenal ulcers. It is generally used when treatment by injection is needed and must be prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the production of stomach acid.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or other trained healthcare professional. The dose and duration depend on the condition and kidney function; do not self-administer it.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, dizziness, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about kidney or liver disease, a history of acute porphyria, allergies, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice for persistent stomach pain, vomiting blood, black stools, difficulty swallowing, or unexplained weight loss. Ranitidine has been withdrawn or restricted in some countries because of concerns about a possible impurity; use it only when specifically prescribed and approved for use locally.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine reduces excess stomach acid. It is used for heartburn, acid indigestion, acid reflux and stomach or intestinal ulcers.

How does it work?
It blocks H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the production of stomach acid.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Follow the prescribed dose and duration, and do not continue self-treatment if symptoms persist or return frequently.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, unexplained weight loss, difficulty swallowing, vomiting, black stools or persistent stomach pain. Seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction. Ranitidine availability and recommendations vary by country; use only a locally approved product as advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine injection reduces excess stomach acid. It may be used for acid reflux and heartburn, stomach or intestinal ulcers, and other acid-related conditions when an injection is needed.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine-2 (H2) receptors in the stomach, reducing the production of stomach acid.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or nurse, usually when treatment by mouth is not suitable. Do not self-inject. The dose and duration depend on the condition and kidney function.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, abdominal discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and pain or irritation at the injection site.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, a history of acute porphyria, allergies to ranitidine or similar medicines, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being used. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, confusion, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

Serratiopeptidase is used to help reduce inflammation, swelling and discomfort associated with injuries, surgery and some painful inflammatory conditions. It may also help loosen thick mucus in certain conditions.

How does it work?
It is a proteolytic enzyme that is thought to break down proteins involved in inflammation, which may help reduce swelling and support the removal of inflammatory fluid.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet whole with water and follow the instructions on the product label. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Use cautiously if there is a bleeding disorder, a stomach ulcer, or if taking blood-thinning medicines. Inform the doctor before surgery. Seek medical help for unusual bleeding, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty or a serious skin reaction. Consult a doctor during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and swelling in muscle and joint conditions, including pain after injuries or procedures.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Serratiopeptidase is an enzyme that may help reduce inflammatory swelling.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take it with other diclofenac or NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Stomach pain or discomfort, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache.

Precautions
Avoid use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, allergy to diclofenac or other NSAIDs, or severe kidney, liver or heart disease unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor if taking blood thinners or medicines that may increase bleeding risk. Avoid during pregnancy, especially from 20 weeks onwards and in the third trimester, unless prescribed. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin reaction.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and swelling, especially in muscle, joint and other painful inflammatory conditions. Use it only for the condition advised by a doctor.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation, while paracetamol helps relieve pain. Serratiopeptidase may help reduce swelling associated with inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow it with water. Do not take additional paracetamol, diclofenac or other painkillers from the same group unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache. Serratiopeptidase-containing medicines may also increase the risk of bleeding in some people.

Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Ayurvedic pain relief oil is used for temporary relief of minor muscle and joint aches, stiffness and discomfort.

How does it work?
It is applied to the skin and massaged over the affected area. Its herbal ingredients may provide a soothing and warming effect, but the exact action depends on the ingredients in the product.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the affected area as directed on the product label and massage gently. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching or rash may occur in sensitive people.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Stop use if irritation or an allergic reaction occurs. Seek medical advice if pain is severe, follows an injury, or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Used as a toothpaste for relief of sensitive teeth and for daily protection against tooth decay, plaque and gum problems.

How does it work?
Potassium nitrate helps reduce the sensitivity of tooth nerves. Sodium monofluorophosphate strengthens tooth enamel and helps prevent cavities, while triclosan helps reduce bacteria and plaque.

How to take/use it
Use for brushing according to the product label. Brush thoroughly and spit out after use. Do not swallow. Children should use it only with adult supervision.

Mild mouth irritation, burning, dryness or an altered taste may occur in some people.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to any ingredient. Stop using it and seek dental advice if irritation develops or sensitivity persists or worsens. Do not swallow. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
Terbutaline relaxes the muscles of the airways to help breathing. Bromhexine and guaiphenesin thin and loosen mucus, making it easier to cough out.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device and do not use a household spoon. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Shakiness, nervousness, headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, or an allergic reaction. Consult a doctor if the cough worsens or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Fradiomycin sulphate is a topical antibacterial used to treat or prevent bacterial infections of the skin, including infected minor cuts, wounds and burns.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents their growth.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to the affected area as directed by a doctor or the product label. Clean and dry the area first, and wash hands before and after use. Do not apply in the eyes or swallow it.

Common side effects
Skin irritation, redness, itching or rash. Allergic contact dermatitis may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to fradiomycin, neomycin or similar aminoglycoside antibiotics. Avoid prolonged use or applying to large areas, deep wounds or severely damaged skin unless advised by a doctor. Stop use and seek medical advice if the infection worsens or a severe rash or swelling develops.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and discomfort from mouth ulcers, sore gums and minor irritation inside the mouth.

How does it work?
Choline salicylate helps reduce pain and inflammation. Lignocaine locally numbs the area, while benzalkonium chloride helps limit the growth of some germs.

How to take/use it
For use in the mouth only. Apply or use exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not swallow it or use more than recommended. Avoid eating or drinking very hot foods and drinks while the area is numb.

Common side effects
Temporary numbness, mild burning or stinging, and irritation at the application site. Stop using it and seek medical help if swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to choline salicylate, aspirin, other salicylates or lignocaine. Use cautiously in children and only with appropriate medical advice. Avoid prolonged or excessive use and seek medical advice if symptoms persist, worsen or keep returning.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole is used to treat fungal infections of the skin, such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch.

How does it work?
It is an antifungal medicine that damages the protective outer layer of fungal cells, helping stop the growth of the fungus.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply to clean, dry, affected skin as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to clotrimazole or any ingredient. Avoid applying to the eyes or broken skin. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or a rash develops. Consult a doctor if the infection worsens or does not improve with treatment.

What is it used for?

The vitamins support energy production, healthy blood cells and normal body functions. Lactobacillus helps support the balance of beneficial bacteria in the intestines.

Take it only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating or changes in bowel movements may occur. Riboflavin may harmlessly turn urine bright yellow.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any vitamin supplements or medicines being taken. Folic acid may mask some signs of vitamin B12 deficiency. Seek medical advice before using it if pregnant, breastfeeding, allergic to any ingredient or severely immunocompromised.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful abdominal cramps and spasms, including intestinal colicky pain. It may also be prescribed for other types of spasmodic pain when advised by a doctor.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces pain and inflammation. Dicyclomine relaxes spasming muscles in the intestine, helping to relieve cramps.

Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food, and do not exceed the recommended dose or duration. Do not take other diclofenac or similar painkillers unless advised.

Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Lidocaine 10% spray is a local anaesthetic used to temporarily numb the skin or mucous membranes and reduce sensation or pain. The exact area and purpose depend on the product instructions or medical advice.

How does it work?
It temporarily blocks pain signals from the nerves in the area where it is applied, causing reduced sensation or numbness.

How to take/use it
Use only on the area and in the amount directed on the label or by a doctor. Do not spray into the eyes or inhale the spray. Avoid eating or drinking until normal sensation returns after use on the mouth or throat, as numbness can increase the risk of choking or burns.

Common side effects
Temporary numbness, tingling, mild burning, redness or irritation at the application site. Drowsiness or dizziness may occur, especially if too much is absorbed.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to lidocaine or similar local anaesthetics. Do not apply large amounts, use repeatedly, or apply to large, broken or inflamed areas unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek urgent medical help for severe dizziness, ringing in the ears, blurred vision, tremors, seizures, breathing difficulty, or an irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain and discomfort caused by acid-related stomach conditions, such as gastritis, peptic ulcers and heartburn.

How does it work?
Sucralfate forms a protective coating over irritated or ulcerated areas in the stomach and intestine. Oxetacaine is a local anaesthetic that helps reduce pain in the affected area.

Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with a proper measuring device. Take it exactly as prescribed. Sucralfate can affect the absorption of other medicines, so ask a doctor or pharmacist about separating this medicine from other medicines.

Constipation, dry mouth, nausea, dizziness or temporary numbness in the mouth or throat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease or an allergy to either ingredient. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for vomiting blood, black stools, severe stomach pain or symptoms that do not improve.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain and discomfort from acidity, heartburn, gastritis and peptic ulcers. It helps protect irritated areas in the stomach and food pipe while oxetacaine provides local relief from pain.

How does it work?
Sucralfate forms a protective coating over ulcers and irritated lining in the stomach and food pipe. Oxetacaine is a local anaesthetic that helps reduce pain in the affected area.

How to take/use it
Shake the bottle well before use and measure the medicine with a proper measuring device. Take it exactly as prescribed. Sucralfate may affect the absorption of other medicines, so inform the doctor or pharmacist about all medicines being taken and follow their advice on spacing doses.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, indigestion, dry mouth and stomach discomfort. Temporary numbness of the mouth or throat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease or an allergy to sucralfate, oxetacaine or any ingredient. Do not eat or drink very hot food or liquids if the mouth or throat feels numb. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist, worsen or there is vomiting blood, black stools or severe abdominal pain.

What is it used for?
Sucralfate is used to treat and protect ulcers in the stomach or upper intestine. It may also be prescribed for other acid-related digestive problems.

How does it work?
It forms a protective coating over damaged areas of the stomach and intestine, helping shield them from acid and digestive enzymes so they can heal.

How to take/use it
Shake the suspension well before use. Take it on an empty stomach exactly as prescribed, usually before meals and at bedtime. Do not take other medicines at the same time unless advised, as sucralfate can affect their absorption.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, dry mouth and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, difficulty swallowing, or pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if severe or persistent stomach pain, vomiting blood, or black stools occur.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to treat scabies and may also be used for lice infestations, as directed by a doctor or the product label.

How does it work?
Monosulfiram acts against the mites or lice that cause these infestations, helping to eliminate them from the skin or hair.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Use the soap exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas, and wash hands after use. Do not use more often or for longer than recommended.

Skin irritation, redness, burning, dryness or itching may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation or an allergic rash develops.

Precautions
Do not swallow or apply to the eyes, mucous membranes or severely broken skin. Keep out of reach of children. Use in children, during pregnancy or while breastfeeding only after medical advice. Seek medical help if accidentally swallowed or if symptoms do not improve after treatment.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
Heparin helps reduce clotting in small superficial blood vessels. Benzyl nicotinate widens small blood vessels and may produce a temporary warming or reddening sensation.

Mild skin redness, warmth, itching, burning or irritation at the application site. Local bruising or bleeding may rarely occur.

What is it used for?
Used for the short-term treatment of moderate to severe pain when a combination of tramadol and paracetamol is appropriate.

How does it work?
Tramadol acts on the central nervous system to reduce the sensation of pain. Paracetamol also reduces pain signals, providing additional pain relief.

Take only as prescribed by a doctor and swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not take more than prescribed or use it with other medicines containing paracetamol or tramadol. Do not stop or continue treatment longer than advised without medical guidance.
