It is usually well tolerated. Nausea, diarrhoea, headache or skin reactions may occur occasionally.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional about any allergy to vitamin B12 or cobalt. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing. Vitamin B12 deficiency with anaemia or nerve symptoms should be medically assessed.

What is it used for?
Citicoline is used to support brain function and may be prescribed during recovery from stroke or head injury, and for certain problems with memory or thinking. Its exact use depends on the medical condition and the prescriber’s advice.

How does it work?
Citicoline helps provide building blocks used to maintain nerve-cell membranes and support the production of certain brain chemicals. This may help support brain-cell function.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, or difficulty sleeping may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergies and all other medicines being used. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only if advised by a doctor. Seek medical advice if side effects are severe or persistent.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat calcium and vitamin D deficiency and to support bone health. It may be prescribed when the body needs extra calcium and active vitamin D, such as in some bone disorders.

How does it work?
Calcium helps maintain strong bones, teeth, muscles and nerves. Calcitriol, an active form of vitamin D, helps the body absorb calcium, while zinc supports normal body functions.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the capsule with water, preferably with food unless advised otherwise. Do not take additional calcium or vitamin D supplements without medical advice.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort, vomiting or diarrhoea may occur. Zinc may sometimes cause stomach upset.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice, especially if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels or a history of vitamin D excess. Seek medical advice for persistent nausea, vomiting, severe constipation, unusual thirst, frequent urination, weakness or confusion, as these may indicate high calcium levels. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about other medicines, as calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines when taken together.

What is it used for?
Used to provide calcium, calcitriol (active vitamin D), vitamin K2, magnesium, vitamin B12 and methylfolate to support bone health and help prevent or correct related nutritional deficiencies. It should be used as advised by a healthcare professional, especially because it contains calcitriol.

How does it work?
Calcium and magnesium provide minerals needed for bones and muscles. Calcitriol helps the body absorb calcium, while vitamin K2 and the B vitamins support normal bone and blood-cell functions.

How to take/use it
Take only in the dose and for the duration recommended on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than recommended or combine it with other calcium or vitamin D products unless advised.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort or vomiting may occur. Excess calcium may cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness or confusion.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high blood calcium, or a history of vitamin D-related disorders. Seek medical advice if symptoms of excess calcium occur. Discuss its use with a healthcare professional if taking digoxin, thiazide diuretics, or other calcium or vitamin D products.

What is it used for?
Calcium gluconate is used to treat or prevent low calcium levels in the body. Injectable calcium gluconate may be used in hospitals for urgent treatment of severe low calcium and certain medical emergencies.

How does it work?
It supplies calcium, which is needed for healthy bones and teeth, normal muscle movement, nerve function and heart activity.

How to take/use it
Use it only as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Oral forms should be taken as directed. Injectable calcium gluconate must be given by a trained healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Oral forms may cause constipation, stomach discomfort, nausea or diarrhoea. Injection-site irritation may occur with injectable forms. Rapid or incorrectly administered injections can cause serious heart-related effects.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones or high calcium levels. Inform the doctor or pharmacist about other medicines, especially thyroid medicine, iron supplements and certain antibiotics, as calcium can affect their absorption. Seek urgent medical help for irregular heartbeat, severe weakness, confusion or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to provide calcium, vitamin D3 and vitamin B12. Calcium and vitamin D3 support normal bones and teeth, while vitamin B12 supports normal nerve function and red blood cell formation.

How does it work?
Calcium provides the mineral needed for bones and teeth. Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium, while vitamin B12 supports blood-cell and nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort or bloating, particularly with calcium supplements.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones or high calcium levels. Avoid taking more than the recommended amount. Seek medical advice if unusual symptoms occur.

What is it used for?
Used to supplement calcium and vitamin D3 when dietary intake is insufficient, helping support healthy bones and teeth and prevent or correct deficiencies.

How does it work?
Calcium provides an essential mineral needed for bones, teeth, muscles and nerves. Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium from the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If taking other medicines, ask a pharmacist or doctor whether they should be taken separately.

Common side effects
Constipation, gas, bloating, nausea or stomach discomfort may occur, especially with higher amounts.

Precautions
Ask a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, or high calcium or vitamin D levels. Calcium can affect the absorption of some medicines, including iron supplements, thyroid medicines and certain antibiotics; seek medical advice about suitable timing. Avoid taking multiple calcium or vitamin D products unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
It is used to treat fungal infections of the skin and relieve associated itching, burning and local discomfort.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole stops the growth of fungi. Lignocaine is a local anaesthetic that temporarily numbs the area and helps reduce discomfort.

How to take/use it
Use only on the affected area and exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Clean and dry the area before application. Wash hands before and after use, unless treating the hands. Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, redness, irritation or itching at the application site.

Precautions
For external use unless specifically directed otherwise. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or other signs of an allergic reaction occur, or if the infection does not improve. Do not use on broken skin or near the eyes unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold symptoms such as fever, headache or body aches, blocked or runny nose, sneezing and watery eyes.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and pain. Chlorpheniramine helps reduce allergy-like symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose, while phenylephrine helps relieve nasal blockage.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it with other medicines containing paracetamol or similar cold-relief ingredients.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea and mild stomach discomfort. Some people may experience a fast heartbeat or restlessness.

Precautions
Chlorpheniramine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or alcohol if affected. Ask a doctor before use in people with high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, urinary problems, liver disease or thyroid problems. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, worsen or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold symptoms such as fever, body aches, blocked or runny nose, sneezing and related nasal congestion.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and relieve pain. Chlorpheniramine helps reduce allergy-related symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose, while phenylephrine helps relieve nasal congestion.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or additional cold and flu ingredients. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea and stomach discomfort. It may sometimes cause palpitations or a rise in blood pressure.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery because it may cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, prostate or urinary problems, liver disease, or use of antidepressants such as monoamine oxidase inhibitors. Consult a doctor if symptoms are severe, worsen or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cold and flu symptoms such as fever, headache, body aches, blocked nose, runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Paracetamol reduces fever and pain. Phenylephrine helps relieve nasal blockage, while diphenhydramine reduces runny nose and sneezing; caffeine may enhance the pain-relieving effect of paracetamol.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and avoid using it with other medicines containing paracetamol, diphenhydramine or decongestants.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, blurred vision, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, increased blood pressure or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Diphenhydramine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, prostate or urination problems, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, allergic reactions or symptoms that worsen or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Used for bacterial eye infections accompanied by inflammation, redness or swelling. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Chloramphenicol stops the growth of susceptible bacteria. Dexamethasone reduces inflammation, redness and swelling in the affected eye.

How to take/use it
Use in the affected eye exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before use, avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or any surface, and complete the prescribed course. Do not wear contact lenses unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, irritation, watering or blurred vision after application. Prolonged use may increase eye pressure or cause other eye problems.

Precautions
Do not use for untreated viral or fungal eye infections unless specifically advised. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen, vision changes, severe eye pain or an allergic reaction occurs. Long-term or repeated use should be medically supervised. Avoid driving until temporary blurred vision clears.

What is it used for?
Chloramphenicol palmitate is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, usually when other suitable antibiotics cannot be used. It should only be used under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents them from growing and multiplying.

How to take/use it
Take it only in the dose and for the duration prescribed by the doctor. Do not skip doses, stop early, or use it for viral infections such as colds or flu.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Chloramphenicol can rarely cause serious blood disorders, including bone marrow suppression. Seek urgent medical help for unusual bruising or bleeding, persistent fever, sore throat, severe weakness, or pale skin. Tell the doctor about any blood disorder, liver disease, or previous reaction to chloramphenicol. It should not be self-used and may require blood monitoring during treatment. Newborn babies and young infants require special medical caution.

What is it used for?
Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It may also help relieve some cold-related runny-nose symptoms.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce symptoms such as itching, sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the package or by a healthcare professional. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation and difficulty passing urine.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and other medicines that cause drowsiness unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek advice before use if there is glaucoma, prostate enlargement, difficulty passing urine, breathing problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe drowsiness, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Ciprofloxacin + dexamethasone is used to treat certain bacterial infections of the eye or ear that also involve inflammation. The exact use depends on the product formulation and should be confirmed on the label or by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic that stops the growth of susceptible bacteria. Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation, swelling and irritation.

How to take/use it
Use only in the eye or ear specified on the product label and exactly as prescribed. Do not use it in another body part, share it with others, or continue it longer than advised. Avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye, ear or other surfaces.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, burning, irritation, itching or discomfort may occur at the application site. Temporary blurred vision may occur with eye preparations.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ciprofloxacin, other quinolone antibiotics, dexamethasone or any ingredient. This medicine is not suitable for all viral or fungal infections. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen, do not improve, or if severe pain, swelling, rash, breathing difficulty or vision changes occur. Contact lens wearers should follow the product instructions; eye lenses may need to be removed before use.

What is it used for?
This prescription combination is generally used as drops for certain bacterial infections of the eye or ear that are accompanied by inflammation. The exact use depends on the prescribed formulation and diagnosis.

How does it work?
Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic that stops the growth of susceptible bacteria. Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation, redness and swelling.

How to take/use it
Use only in the eye or ear and only as directed by a doctor. Follow the prescribed number of drops and treatment duration. Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye, ear or other surfaces. Do not use leftover drops for a new infection.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, burning, itching or irritation at the application site may occur. Eye or ear discomfort can also occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ciprofloxacin, other quinolone antibiotics, dexamethasone or similar medicines. Use only for the condition prescribed, as steroid-containing drops may worsen some viral or fungal infections or mask signs of infection. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen, vision or hearing changes occur, or there is severe pain, swelling or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some urinary, intestinal, respiratory, skin and other infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills or stops the growth of bacteria by blocking enzymes they need to copy and repair their DNA.

How to take/use it
Use it only as prescribed and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Take with plenty of water. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing calcium, iron, magnesium or zinc; follow the prescribed spacing instructions. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, vomiting, headache, dizziness and skin rash.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies, pregnancy or breastfeeding, kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, seizures, tendon problems or myasthenia gravis. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, palpitations, or a serious allergic reaction. Avoid unnecessary intense exercise if tendon pain develops.

What is it used for?
This prescription combination is used to treat certain bacterial and parasitic infections of the digestive tract that may cause infectious diarrhoea or dysentery. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Ciprofloxacin stops susceptible bacteria from multiplying. Tinidazole damages the DNA of certain parasites and anaerobic bacteria, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Do not take it together with antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc; ask a pharmacist about the appropriate time gap. Avoid alcohol while taking it and for 3 days after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and a metallic taste.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney problems, seizures, heart rhythm problems, tendon disorders or previous reactions to quinolone antibiotics. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe or bloody diarrhoea, rash, breathing difficulty or other serious symptoms. Do not self-medicate or use it for ordinary non-infectious diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Ciprofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some urinary tract, respiratory, gastrointestinal, skin, bone and joint infections. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking enzymes they need to copy and repair their DNA.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with plenty of water. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc; follow a pharmacist or doctor’s advice about spacing them. Avoid taking it with dairy products alone.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is a history of tendon problems, seizures, nerve problems, heart rhythm problems, kidney disease, or if pregnant or breastfeeding. Stop taking it and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, serious rash, breathing difficulty, fainting or unusual mental or nerve-related symptoms. Avoid unnecessary strenuous exercise during treatment and shortly afterwards because of the risk of tendon injury.

What is it used for?
Cetirizine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching or hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than the recommended amount. It may cause drowsiness in some people.

Common side effects
Drowsiness or tiredness, headache, dry mouth, nausea, and dizziness.

Precautions
Avoid driving or using machinery until its effects are known. Avoid or limit alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness. Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding, or if taking other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek urgent help for swelling of the face, lips or throat, or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole dusting powder is used on the skin to treat fungal infections such as athlete’s foot, ringworm, jock itch and some yeast infections. It can also help keep affected skin dry.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an important part of their cell membrane, which helps control and clear the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, completely dry affected skin and use it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after use. Avoid inhaling the powder and keep it away from the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or stinging may occur where it is applied.

Precautions
Do not use on broken or severely irritated skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs, or if the infection worsens or does not improve. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not swallow.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole dusting powder is used to treat fungal skin infections such as athlete’s foot, ringworm and jock itch. It may also help keep affected skin dry.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Apply the powder to clean, completely dry affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after use. Avoid inhaling the powder and do not apply it to the eyes or mouth.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, burning, stinging, redness or itching may occur at the application site.

Precautions
For external use only. Keep away from the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, an allergic reaction or worsening symptoms occur. Seek medical advice if the infection does not improve with treatment.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of dry cough and associated cold or allergy symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan reduces the cough reflex in the brain. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that helps relieve allergy-related symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take/use only as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and use the measuring device provided for liquid formulations. Do not use with other medicines containing dextromethorphan or chlorpheniramine unless advised.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea and constipation may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Consult a healthcare professional before use in children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is glaucoma, breathing difficulty, prostate or urinary problems, or liver disease. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines or within 14 days of stopping them. Seek medical advice if the cough lasts, worsens, or is associated with high fever, breathing difficulty or excessive mucus.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for temporary relief of common cold symptoms such as blocked or runny nose, sneezing, fever and body aches.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and body aches. Chlorpheniramine reduces allergy-like symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose, while phenylephrine helps relieve nasal blockage.

How to take/use it
Use only in the dose and manner stated on the product label or prescribed by a doctor. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol. Do not use it for longer than recommended without medical advice.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dry mouth, dizziness, nausea, restlessness, nervousness or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Drowsiness may affect driving or operating machinery; avoid alcohol. Consult a doctor before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease or difficulty passing urine. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen, persist, or breathing difficulty occurs.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold symptoms such as blocked or runny nose, sneezing, headache, body aches and fever.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and relieve pain. Chlorpheniramine helps reduce sneezing and a runny nose, while phenylephrine helps relieve nasal blockage.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the package or by a healthcare professional. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol. Avoid alcohol and do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea and stomach discomfort. Phenylephrine may sometimes cause restlessness, palpitations or increased blood pressure.

Precautions
It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery if affected. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine or an enlarged prostate. Avoid taking it with alcohol or certain antidepressants, including MAO inhibitors. Seek medical help for severe or persistent symptoms, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, muscle or joint pain, headache, toothache and menstrual pain. It can also help reduce fever and inflammation.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever. Ibuprofen reduces substances in the body that cause pain, inflammation and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the package or by a doctor. Take with or after food and swallow with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it with other medicines containing paracetamol or ibuprofen unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, heartburn, dizziness or headache.

Precautions
Avoid use or seek medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, severe heart problems, or allergy to ibuprofen, aspirin or other painkillers. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially from 20 weeks onwards, or while taking blood thinners, steroids or other painkillers. Avoid excessive alcohol. Stop use and seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty or swelling of the face or throat.

What is it used for?
Vitamin B-complex is used to prevent or treat deficiency of B vitamins. It supports normal energy metabolism, nerve function and red blood cell production.

How does it work?
It supplies several B vitamins that help the body convert food into energy and support the normal functioning of the nervous system and blood cells.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset.

Common side effects
Mild nausea, stomach upset or headache may occur. Bright yellow urine can occur and is usually harmless.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional if pregnant, breastfeeding, or if there is kidney or liver disease. Avoid taking more than the recommended amount, especially for long periods, because excessive vitamin B6 can cause nerve problems. Seek medical advice if unusual numbness, tingling or weakness develops.

What is it used for?
Used to improve appetite in people with poor appetite or inadequate food intake, and may help support weight gain when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Cyproheptadine can increase appetite by blocking certain histamine and serotonin effects in the body. Tricholine citrate is included as a nutritional support ingredient.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, increased appetite, nausea and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Cyproheptadine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Use only under medical advice in children, older adults, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and in people with glaucoma, urinary retention, asthma or liver problems. Seek medical help for severe sleepiness, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used to help improve appetite and support weight gain in people with poor appetite or inadequate food intake, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Cyproheptadine can increase appetite by blocking certain histamine and serotonin effects in the body. Tricholine citrate provides choline, a nutrient involved in normal fat metabolism.

How to take/use it
Take only in the dose and for the duration prescribed by the doctor. Do not take more than recommended. If it causes drowsiness, avoid driving or operating machinery.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, increased appetite, nausea and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Cyproheptadine may cause sleepiness, which can worsen with alcohol or other sedating medicines. Seek medical advice before use if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, asthma, liver disease or pregnancy. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to help improve appetite in people with poor appetite or inadequate food intake. It may be prescribed when appetite loss is contributing to low body weight or poor nutrition.

How does it work?
Cyproheptadine blocks certain histamine and serotonin effects and can stimulate appetite. Tricholine citrate and sorbitol are included as supporting ingredients in the formulation.

How to take/use it
Take only in the dose and for the duration prescribed by the doctor. Measure the liquid with the supplied measuring device and do not use a household spoon. Do not use it for weight gain without medical advice.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, increased appetite, weight gain, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea or abdominal cramps.

Precautions
Cyproheptadine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Tell the doctor about glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, asthma, liver disease or other medical conditions. Use in children, during pregnancy or while breastfeeding only on medical advice. Seek medical help for severe drowsiness, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to help improve poor appetite and support increased food intake. It may be prescribed for people with reduced appetite or inadequate nutritional intake.

How does it work?
Cyproheptadine blocks certain histamine and serotonin effects and can stimulate appetite. Tricholine citrate provides choline, a nutrient involved in normal fat metabolism.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Follow the prescribed dose and duration, and do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, nausea, and increased appetite or weight gain.

Precautions
Cyproheptadine may cause drowsiness; avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, or other ongoing medical conditions. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Cyproheptadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, itching, watery eyes and hives. It may also be prescribed by a doctor to help stimulate appetite in some people.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions, and helps reduce allergy symptoms. It can also affect serotonin pathways, which may increase appetite.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. It may cause sleepiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, increased appetite and weight gain.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and other medicines that cause drowsiness unless advised by a doctor. Use cautiously if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, asthma, liver or kidney disease, or in older adults. It is generally not used in infants below 2 years unless specifically prescribed. Seek medical help for severe drowsiness, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used for certain bacterial eye infections that are accompanied by redness, swelling or inflammation. It should be used only when prescribed, as the steroid component is not suitable for every eye infection.

How does it work?
Chloramphenicol kills susceptible bacteria. Dexamethasone reduces inflammation, redness and swelling in the affected eye.

How to take/use it
Use only in the eye and exactly as directed by a doctor. Do not touch the dropper or applicator tip to the eye or any surface. Do not wear contact lenses unless advised by an eye specialist. The exact dose and treatment duration depend on the product and condition.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, irritation or blurred vision after application. Prolonged or repeated use may increase eye pressure or delay healing.

Precautions
Do not use for an undiagnosed red eye or suspected viral or fungal infection unless advised by an eye specialist. Tell the doctor about glaucoma, eye injury, or recent eye surgery. Seek medical help for worsening pain, vision changes, severe swelling, or an allergic reaction. Prolonged or repeated use should be monitored by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Dexamethasone injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce severe inflammation and overactive immune or allergic reactions. Its exact use depends on the condition being treated and must be decided by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a healthcare professional as an injection. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the condition and medical response. Do not self-inject or use it without medical supervision.

Common side effects

What is it used for?

Wrap it evenly around the affected area, starting below the injured area and moving upward. It should feel snug but not tight. What is it used for?

The tape has a pressure-sensitive adhesive that sticks to the skin and holds dressings or medical materials in place.

Apply to clean, dry skin after placing the dressing or gauze. Press gently to secure it, without wrapping it tightly. Change or remove it as directed for the dressing being used, and remove gently to reduce skin injury.

Redness, itching, irritation, discomfort or skin damage when the tape is removed. Allergic skin reactions may occur.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron-deficiency anaemia and nutritional anaemia caused by low levels of iron, vitamin B12 or folic acid.

How does it work?
It provides iron needed to make haemoglobin, along with vitamin B12 and folic acid needed for healthy red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended. Iron may be taken with food if it causes stomach discomfort. Avoid taking it at the same time as tea, coffee, milk or antacids unless advised otherwise.

Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea. Dark or black stools may occur with iron supplements.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if the cause of anaemia is unknown or if there is iron overload. What is it used for?
This medicine is used to stimulate appetite in people with poor appetite and may help support weight gain when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Cyproheptadine blocks histamine and serotonin activity and can increase appetite. Tricholine citrate is included as a nutritional component in the combination.

How to take/use it
Take it only in the dose and for the duration prescribed by the doctor. Do not use it on your own solely to gain weight.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea and constipation may occur.

Precautions
Cyproheptadine may cause sleepiness; avoid driving and alcohol if affected. Tell the doctor about glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, asthma, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if severe sleepiness, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Hydrocortisone sodium succinate injection is a corticosteroid used in hospitals and emergencies to reduce severe inflammation or allergic reactions. It may also be used to replace the body’s cortisol when the adrenal glands are not producing enough.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone cortisol. It reduces inflammation and suppresses an overactive immune response, while helping replace cortisol when it is deficient.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and response to treatment. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include increased blood sugar, increased blood pressure, fluid retention, stomach upset, mood or sleep changes, and increased risk of infection. Side effects may be more likely with higher doses or prolonged treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions, or any current infection. Corticosteroids can mask signs of infection and may worsen some infections. Seek medical help for severe allergic reactions, serious infection symptoms, vision changes, or severe mood changes. Do not stop prolonged corticosteroid treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?

Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever. Ibuprofen reduces the production of substances that cause pain, swelling and fever.

Shake the bottle well before use. Measure the suspension with the supplied measuring device and take it exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Taking it with food or milk may help reduce stomach upset. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or ibuprofen unless advised by a doctor.

Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach pain or discomfort, diarrhoea, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to ibuprofen, paracetamol, aspirin or other NSAIDs. Seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, heart problems, dehydration, or pregnancy—especially during the last 3 months. Avoid combining with other paracetamol- or ibuprofen-containing medicines. Stop use and seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, a severe skin rash, vomiting blood, black stools, or severe stomach pain. Get medical advice if fever or pain persists or worsens.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?

It replaces potassium in the body. Potassium is needed for normal nerve, muscle and heart function.

Vitamin K helps the liver make clotting proteins needed to control bleeding.

What is it used for?

It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation.

Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than the recommended amount. It may cause drowsiness in some people.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, and sometimes stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery until the effect of the medicine is known. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for signs of a severe allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Levocetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Follow the advice of a doctor or pharmacist if treatment is needed for a child, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or for a longer period.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, and occasionally stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Levocetirizine may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or drinking alcohol until its effects are known. People with kidney disease may need medical advice before using it. Seek medical help for severe allergic symptoms or unusual swelling or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Labetalol is used to lower high blood pressure, including severe high blood pressure when rapid control may be needed under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It blocks certain signals that make the heart beat faster and blood vessels narrow. This slows the heartbeat and relaxes blood vessels, helping to reduce blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. The 5 mg strength may be given by a healthcare professional, depending on the prescribed product and treatment. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, tiredness, nausea, headache, slow heartbeat and low blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is asthma or wheezing, a slow heartbeat, heart failure, circulation problems, diabetes, liver disease or other heart conditions. It may cause dizziness, especially when standing up. Seek medical help for fainting, severe breathing difficulty, very slow heartbeat or swelling of the legs.

What is it used for?
Loperamide 2mg is used to relieve diarrhoea and reduce frequent, watery stools. It may also help control diarrhoea in some longer-term bowel conditions when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It slows the movement of food and fluids through the intestines, allowing more water to be absorbed and making stools less frequent and watery.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the package or by a doctor. Swallow with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Drink plenty of fluids to help prevent dehydration. Do not use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Constipation, nausea, stomach cramps, bloating, dry mouth, dizziness and headache.

Precautions
Do not use it for diarrhoea with blood in the stools, high fever, severe abdominal pain or a swollen abdomen unless advised by a doctor. Stop using it and seek medical help if diarrhoea worsens, signs of dehydration occur, severe constipation develops, or there is no improvement within 48 hours. It is not suitable for all children; follow the product instructions or medical advice. Avoid taking more than recommended, as excessive use can cause serious heart problems.

What is it used for?
This supplement provides lycopene, vitamins C and E, and trace minerals including zinc, selenium, copper, chromium and manganese. It is used to supplement the diet and support antioxidant protection and general nutritional wellness.

How does it work?
Its vitamins, minerals and lycopene help support normal body functions and antioxidant defences, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow the softgel with water, preferably with food. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Some people may experience nausea, stomach upset or diarrhoea. Allergic reactions are uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Do not use more than the recommended amount or combine it with other vitamin and mineral supplements without medical advice. Seek advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or regular use of medicines. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
The intended use cannot be confirmed from “Magnesium Sulphate 500mg” alone. Magnesium sulphate may be used in different formulations for magnesium replacement or other medical purposes; check the product label or prescription.

How does it work?
It provides magnesium, a mineral needed for normal muscle, nerve and body functions. Its effects vary depending on the formulation and intended use.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not determine the dose or route of use from the strength alone.

Common side effects
Depending on the formulation, oral use may cause diarrhoea, nausea or stomach cramps. Side effects may differ for injectable products.

Precautions
Check the formulation and intended use before taking or using it. Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, as excess magnesium can accumulate. Do not use without professional guidance if the product is intended for injection or another medical procedure.

What is it used for?
Magnesium sulphate 500 mg may be used for different purposes depending on its formulation and prescribed indication, such as treating magnesium deficiency or as a laxative. The exact use cannot be confirmed from the generic name alone.

How does it work?
It provides magnesium, a mineral needed for normal muscle, nerve and heart function. In some formulations, it also draws water into the bowel to help produce a bowel movement.

How to take/use it
Use only according to the product label or a healthcare professional’s instructions. The route, dose and treatment duration depend on the formulation and reason for use. Do not use an injectable form without medical supervision.

Common side effects
Oral use may cause diarrhoea, stomach cramps, nausea or vomiting. Side effects depend on the formulation and route of administration.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, as magnesium can build up in the body. Do not self-treat with this medicine when the formulation or intended use is unclear. Seek urgent medical help for weakness, confusion, breathing difficulty or an irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat deficiency of B vitamins, including vitamins B1, B6 and B12. These vitamins support normal nerve function, energy metabolism and red blood cell formation.

How does it work?
It replenishes important B vitamins and related nutrients that the body needs for normal nerve function, energy production and blood formation.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. The method of use depends on the product form; do not self-administer if it is an injectable product. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Mild nausea, stomach upset or headache may occur. Injectable products may cause pain, redness or swelling at the injection site.

Precautions
Tell the doctor or pharmacist about any allergy to these ingredients or previous reactions to vitamin injections. Prolonged or excessive use of vitamin B6 can cause nerve problems. Seek medical help for rash, breathing difficulty, severe dizziness or other signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to provide B-group vitamins and lysine when dietary intake may be inadequate or supplementation is recommended.

How does it work?
B vitamins help support energy metabolism, nerve function and normal blood-cell formation. Lysine is an essential amino acid needed for protein formation.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort or diarrhoea may occur. Sorbitol can have a laxative effect, especially in larger amounts.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to any ingredient. Excessive use may cause diarrhoea or abdominal cramps. People with diabetes or hereditary fructose intolerance should seek medical advice before use because it contains sorbitol.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to help prevent or correct deficiencies of certain B vitamins and support normal energy metabolism and protein nutrition. It should not be used as a substitute for a balanced diet.

How does it work?
The B vitamins help the body release energy from food and support normal nerve and blood-cell function. Lysine is an essential amino acid needed for protein production.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating or loose motions may occur. Sorbitol may have a laxative effect, especially in larger amounts.

Precautions
Check the ingredients before use if there is a known allergy. Avoid use in hereditary fructose intolerance because the product contains sorbitol. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in children unless recommended by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek help if an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Calcium with vitamin D3 is used to supplement calcium and vitamin D levels and support normal bone and teeth health. It may help prevent or treat deficiency when dietary intake is insufficient.

How does it work?
Calcium provides a mineral needed for strong bones and teeth, as well as normal muscle and nerve function. Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. If taking other medicines, ask a healthcare professional about the appropriate timing.

Common side effects
Constipation, gas, bloating, nausea or stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels or vitamin D disorders. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, including iron supplements, thyroid medicines and certain antibiotics; these may need to be taken at different times as advised. Seek medical advice if severe or persistent side effects occur.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of dry cough, sneezing and runny nose associated with the common cold or allergies.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan reduces the cough reflex. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that helps relieve allergy-related symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid using other cough-and-cold medicines containing similar ingredients unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea and constipation may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Do not use with or within 14 days of monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines. Seek medical advice before use if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, prostate enlargement, breathing problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, severe drowsiness or a persistent or worsening cough.

What is it used for?
Used to treat certain bacterial and parasitic infections of the digestive tract that can cause diarrhoea, loose motions or dysentery. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Norfloxacin kills susceptible bacteria, while tinidazole acts against certain parasites and other microorganisms that can cause intestinal infections.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course. Swallow with water. Avoid taking it with milk or dairy products, and keep antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium or magnesium separate as advised by a healthcare professional. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 3 days after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and a metallic taste.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to norfloxacin, tinidazole, other quinolone antibiotics or nitroimidazole medicines. Tell the healthcare professional about pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver or kidney problems, seizures, nerve disorders or a history of tendon problems. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for severe rash, breathing difficulty, tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Analgin 500 mg is used to relieve moderate to severe pain and reduce fever.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Swallow with water and do not take more than recommended. Do not use it for a prolonged period without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, dizziness, or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been an allergy to Analgin (metamizole) or similar painkillers. Use only with medical advice if there is a history of blood disorders, bone-marrow problems, liver or kidney disease, or asthma triggered by painkillers. Stop taking it and seek urgent medical help if there is difficulty breathing, facial swelling, a severe rash, persistent sore throat, fever, chills, or unusual infections, as serious allergic or blood-related reactions can occur. Consult a doctor during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Metronidazole is used to treat certain infections caused by anaerobic bacteria and parasites, including some infections of the stomach and intestines, teeth and gums, reproductive organs, and skin. It may also be used for bacterial vaginosis and certain sexually transmitted infections, as prescribed.

How does it work?
It damages the genetic material of susceptible bacteria and parasites, stopping them from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Do not drink alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, metallic taste and dark-coloured urine.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, nervous-system problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken, especially warfarin, lithium or disulfiram. Seek medical advice for numbness or tingling, seizures, severe diarrhoea, or signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Metronidazole suspension is used to treat certain infections caused by anaerobic bacteria and parasites, including some infections of the stomach, intestines and reproductive or urinary tract. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It enters susceptible bacteria and parasites and damages their genetic material, stopping them from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
Shake the suspension well before each use and measure it with the supplied measuring device. Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the course, even if symptoms improve. Do not take more or use it for longer than directed. Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and a metallic taste in the mouth. The urine may sometimes become darker.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, a blood disorder, a nervous-system disorder or pregnancy. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially warfarin or other blood thinners. Seek medical help for severe rash, numbness or tingling, seizures, confusion, or persistent severe diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Tranexamic acid injection is used to reduce or prevent excessive bleeding, including bleeding related to surgery, injury, childbirth or certain medical conditions. The exact use depends on the doctor's assessment.

How does it work?
It helps prevent blood clots from breaking down too quickly, which helps control bleeding.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection, usually into a vein, by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the reason for treatment and kidney function. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache may occur. Low blood pressure can occur if it is given too quickly.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of blood clots, kidney problems, seizures or vision problems. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, swelling or pain in a limb, seizures, or changes in vision. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only when advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Tranexamic acid injection is used to prevent or reduce excessive bleeding, including bleeding associated with surgery or other medical conditions. It is given only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It helps prevent the breakdown of blood clots, allowing clots to remain stable and reducing bleeding.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection, usually by a doctor or nurse. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the cause and severity of bleeding, kidney function and medical advice. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache may occur. Tell a healthcare professional about any visual changes.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of blood clots, kidney disease, seizures or vision problems. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, swelling or pain in a limb, severe headache, seizures or sudden changes in vision.

What is it used for?
Artesunate injection is used to treat severe malaria, including malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum. It is usually given in a hospital or healthcare setting.

How does it work?
It rapidly kills malaria parasites in the blood, helping to control the infection and reduce its complications.

How to take/use it
It is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on body weight, the severity of malaria and the prescribed treatment plan. A follow-up antimalarial treatment may be needed.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, injection-site discomfort and changes in blood counts may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to artesunate or other artemisinin medicines. Medical monitoring and blood tests may be needed because delayed breakdown of red blood cells can occur after treatment. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe weakness, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or dark urine.

What is it used for?
Artesunate injection is used for the emergency treatment of severe malaria, especially when the patient cannot take medicines by mouth. It is given in a hospital or healthcare facility.

How does it work?
It rapidly kills malaria parasites in the blood, helping to reduce the severity of the infection.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the severity of malaria and must be decided by the treating doctor. Once the patient can take medicines by mouth, additional antimalarial treatment may be needed as advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, fever, injection-site reactions and temporary changes in blood tests may occur.

Precautions
Severe malaria is a medical emergency and requires hospital care. Do not self-administer this injection. Medical monitoring is important because delayed destruction of red blood cells (haemolysis), anaemia, allergic reactions or liver-related problems can occur after treatment. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, unusual weakness, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine or worsening symptoms.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat deficiencies of vitamins A, D3 and B-group vitamins, and to support general nutritional health when dietary intake is insufficient.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamins needed for normal vision, bones, skin, nerve function and energy metabolism.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by the doctor or product label. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
May cause nausea, stomach upset or headache. These are more likely with excessive use.

Precautions
Do not combine with other vitamin A or vitamin D supplements unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy, especially if there may be a risk of excess vitamin A, or if there is liver or kidney disease. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
This vitamin B-complex supplement is used to help prevent or treat deficiencies of B vitamins and support normal energy metabolism, nerve function and blood cell formation.

How does it work?
It supplies several B vitamins that help the body convert food into energy and support the normal functioning of the nervous system and other body tissues.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
It is usually well tolerated. Mild nausea, stomach upset, headache or flushing may occur. Riboflavin may harmlessly make urine bright yellow.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is liver disease or another medical condition. Seek advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
This B-complex supplement is used to provide several B vitamins and to help prevent or treat B-vitamin deficiency. These vitamins support normal energy metabolism and nerve function.

How does it work?
It supplies B vitamins needed for the body's energy-producing processes, normal nerve function and other essential body functions.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount, especially if using other vitamin supplements.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Mild nausea or stomach upset may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Consult a healthcare professional before use if pregnant, breastfeeding, or taking other vitamin or mineral supplements. Seek advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for short-term relief of pain and inflammation. Cetirizine may also help relieve allergy symptoms, while magnesium trisilicate helps reduce excess stomach acid.

How does it work?
Diclofenac and paracetamol reduce pain, and diclofenac also reduces inflammation. Cetirizine blocks histamine to reduce allergy symptoms, while magnesium trisilicate neutralises stomach acid.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor or pharmacist. Take with or after food and swallow with water. Do not take more than recommended, or combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol, diclofenac or other NSAIDs unless advised.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea or constipation, dizziness, drowsiness and headache.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving if drowsy or dizzy. Tell a doctor before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to painkillers. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
This medicine is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the urinary tract, respiratory tract and skin. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It contains trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole, which work together to block the production of folic acid that bacteria need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with a full glass of water. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not use leftover antibiotics or share this medicine with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, diarrhoea, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to trimethoprim, sulfonamide medicines or any ingredient. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, blood disorders, folate deficiency, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for a severe or blistering rash, swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, unusual bruising, severe diarrhoea or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
This antibiotic is used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some urinary tract, respiratory, ear and intestinal infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It combines trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole to block two steps that bacteria need to make folic acid and grow.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Take with plenty of water. Do not share this medicine or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, diarrhoea, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to trimethoprim, sulfonamide medicines or this combination. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, folate deficiency, blood disorders, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being used. Seek urgent medical help for severe or blistering rash, swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, unusual bruising, severe diarrhoea or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) is used to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency and to support calcium absorption and healthy bones. This high-strength preparation should be used only when recommended by a doctor or pharmacist.

How does it work?
Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium and phosphate from the intestine. These minerals are important for maintaining strong bones and muscles.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take extra doses or combine it with other vitamin D or calcium supplements unless advised. Do not repeat high-strength doses without medical guidance.

Common side effects
Excess vitamin D can cause nausea, vomiting, constipation, stomach pain, weakness, excessive thirst or frequent urination.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or a condition that increases calcium levels. Seek medical advice if symptoms of excess calcium occur. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Triamcinolone acetonide is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation, redness and itching in conditions such as eczema, dermatitis and other inflammatory skin problems. Its use can vary depending on the formulation.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances in the body that cause inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
Use only the formulation, amount and duration advised by a doctor or stated on the label. If it is a skin preparation, apply it only to the affected area and wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not use more often or for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, irritation, dryness or redness at the application site. Prolonged or excessive use on the skin may cause skin thinning or other skin changes.

Precautions
For skin preparations, avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and broken skin unless specifically directed. Do not use on untreated skin infections unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical advice if the condition worsens, does not improve, or signs of infection develop. Children and people using it on the face or skin folds should use it only under medical advice.

What is it used for?
Dexamethasone injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce severe inflammation and overactive immune reactions. The exact condition and reason for use depend on the doctor's prescription.

How does it work?
It acts like natural corticosteroid hormones and reduces inflammation and immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a healthcare professional, usually by injection. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. Do not self-inject or use it without medical supervision.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar, stomach upset, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, increased appetite, fluid retention and increased risk of infections may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is diabetes, high blood pressure, a stomach ulcer, osteoporosis, an existing infection, or a history of mental-health problems. Corticosteroids can mask infection symptoms. Do not stop prolonged treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for signs of a serious infection, severe mood changes, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Dexamethasone injection is a corticosteroid used under medical supervision to reduce severe inflammation and suppress overactive immune or allergic reactions. Its use depends on the condition being treated.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and allergic reactions. It also suppresses excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or nurse. The dose and injection route depend on the medical condition and response to treatment. It should not be self-injected.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, increased blood sugar, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, increased appetite, fluid retention and increased risk of infections may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, infections or a history of mental health problems. Dexamethasone may mask signs of infection. Use only as prescribed, and do not stop prolonged treatment suddenly without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Dexamethasone injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce severe inflammation and allergic reactions, and to suppress an overactive immune response in various medical conditions. Its exact use depends on the condition being treated.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and allergic symptoms. It also lowers excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or nurse. The dose, injection route and treatment duration depend on the medical condition. Do not self-administer it.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar, stomach upset, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, increased appetite, fluid retention and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, mental health conditions, osteoporosis or any infection. Dexamethasone can reduce the body's ability to fight infections and may mask infection symptoms. Seek medical advice for signs of infection, severe mood changes, vision problems or severe stomach pain. If used repeatedly or for a prolonged period, it should not be stopped suddenly without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Gentamicin injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including certain infections of the blood, lungs, abdomen, urinary tract and other areas. It is usually used when treatment with an injectable antibiotic is needed.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by interfering with their ability to make essential proteins.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a healthcare professional, usually by injection into a muscle or through a vein. The dose and treatment length depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and other medicines being used. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea, dizziness and headache may occur. Serious effects can include reduced kidney function, ringing in the ears, hearing loss or problems with balance.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Kidney function and, when needed, hearing should be monitored during treatment. Seek medical help for reduced urination, swelling, severe dizziness, ringing in the ears, hearing changes, breathing difficulty or unusual muscle weakness. Other medicines that can affect the kidneys, hearing or muscles may increase the risk of side effects.

What is it used for?
Gentamicin injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections. It is usually given in hospitals or clinics when treatment with an injectable antibiotic is needed.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills the bacteria and helps control the infection.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a healthcare professional into a vein or muscle. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, body weight and kidney function. Do not self-inject or change the dose. Kidney function and, when needed, blood levels may be monitored during treatment.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea or vomiting may occur. Serious effects can include kidney problems, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, dizziness or balance problems.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, myasthenia gravis, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Extra monitoring may be needed in older adults. Seek medical help for reduced urine, swelling, unusual tiredness, ringing in the ears, hearing changes, severe dizziness or difficulty breathing. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially those that may affect the kidneys, hearing or muscles.

What is it used for?
Gentamicin injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections caused by bacteria that are sensitive to gentamicin. It may be used for certain infections of the blood, lungs, abdomen, urinary tract or other parts of the body, as decided by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from growing.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type of infection, body weight and kidney function. Kidney function and, when needed, medicine levels may be monitored during treatment.

Common side effects
Injection-site pain, nausea, vomiting, headache and dizziness may occur. Gentamicin can also seriously affect the kidneys or hearing, especially with prolonged treatment or higher doses.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy, or a muscle or nerve disorder. Inform the doctor about all medicines being used, especially other medicines that may affect the kidneys or hearing. Seek medical help for reduced urine, swelling, ringing in the ears, hearing loss, severe dizziness, unusual weakness or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Analgin (metamizole) is used for short-term relief of moderate to severe pain and for reducing fever.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances involved in pain and fever, helping relieve discomfort and lower body temperature.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth with water exactly as prescribed or as directed on the label. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised.

Nausea, stomach discomfort, dizziness, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to metamizole or similar pain medicines.
