What is it used for?
Norfloxacin + tinidazole is used to treat certain bacterial and parasitic infections of the stomach and intestines, including infectious diarrhoea and dysentery. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Norfloxacin kills susceptible bacteria, while tinidazole acts against certain parasites and bacteria that can cause intestinal infections.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Avoid taking it with milk or dairy products, and separate it from antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc as advised by a healthcare professional. Do not drink alcohol during treatment or for at least 72 hours after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and a metallic taste in the mouth.

Precautions
Do not use it without medical advice, especially during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is kidney or liver disease, a history of seizures, nerve problems or heart-rhythm problems. Stop taking it and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, allergic reactions, or severe or bloody diarrhoea. Avoid driving if dizzy or drowsy.

What is it used for?
Used to treat certain bacterial and protozoal infections of the stomach and intestines that may cause diarrhoea, loose motions or dysentery. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Norfloxacin stops susceptible bacteria from multiplying. Tinidazole damages the genetic material of certain parasites and anaerobic bacteria, helping to clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Avoid taking it with milk or dairy products, and ask a pharmacist about separating it from antacids or iron, calcium or zinc supplements. Do not use it for self-treatment of every episode of diarrhoea.

Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain or discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and a metallic taste in the mouth.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol during treatment and for 72 hours after the last dose. Tell the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding, under 18 years of age, or if there is kidney disease, a history of seizures, nerve problems or tendon disorders. What is it used for?
Vitamin B-complex supplements are used to prevent or treat deficiency of B vitamins. They support normal energy metabolism, nerve function and formation of healthy blood cells.

The B vitamins act as coenzymes that help the body release energy from food and support the normal function of the nervous system and blood cells.

Take or use it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Mild nausea or stomach upset may occur. Bright-yellow urine can occur with riboflavin and is usually harmless. Some formulations may cause flushing or headache.

Avoid long-term use of high doses, especially vitamin B6, unless medically advised, as it may cause nerve problems. Check with a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is kidney or liver disease or regular medicine use. What is it used for?
Vitamin B-complex is used to prevent or treat deficiency of B vitamins. It supports normal energy metabolism, nerve function and the formation of red blood cells.

How does it work?
The B vitamins act as coenzymes that help the body use carbohydrates, proteins and fats for energy. They also support normal nerve and blood-cell function.

Take it by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset or diarrhoea may occur. Riboflavin (vitamin B2) may harmlessly turn urine bright yellow.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional about any medical conditions, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and medicines or supplements being used. Avoid prolonged use of high doses unless advised by a healthcare professional, as some B vitamins can cause harm in excessive amounts.

What is it used for?
Chloroquine is mainly used to prevent and treat certain types of malaria. It may also be prescribed for some autoimmune conditions, such as lupus or rheumatoid arthritis, under specialist supervision.

How does it work?
It acts against malaria parasites by interfering with their ability to process haemoglobin inside red blood cells. It also reduces abnormal immune-system activity in some autoimmune conditions.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food or milk to reduce stomach upset. Do not change the dose, stop treatment early, or use it to treat malaria without medical advice, as chloroquine does not work against all malaria parasites.

Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, itching or skin rash, and temporary blurred vision.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about eye or retinal problems, psoriasis, hearing problems, liver or kidney disease, heart-rhythm problems, or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency. Long-term use may require regular eye examinations. Seek urgent medical help for severe vision changes, fainting, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe weakness, or signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone sodium injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce severe inflammation and overactive immune or allergic reactions. It may be used for conditions such as severe asthma or allergic reactions, autoimmune disorders, and other inflammatory illnesses when rapid treatment is needed.

How does it work?
It reduces inflammation and suppresses excessive immune-system activity, helping decrease swelling, redness, pain and allergic or inflammatory symptoms.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or other trained healthcare professional. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated and the response to treatment. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar or blood pressure, indigestion, fluid retention, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, headache and injection-site discomfort may occur. It can also increase the risk of infections.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health problems, eye disease or any current infection. Corticosteroids can mask infection symptoms and may worsen infections. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for severe allergic symptoms, signs of infection, vision changes or serious mood changes.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone sodium injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and an overactive immune response in conditions such as severe allergic, inflammatory, or autoimmune problems. The exact use depends on the medical condition and the doctor's prescription.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose, injection route and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar, increased blood pressure, indigestion, fluid retention, mood changes, sleep problems and increased risk of infections may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health problems, liver or kidney disease, or any current infection. Corticosteroids may mask infection symptoms and can interact with vaccines and other medicines. Do not stop treatment suddenly if it has been used for a prolonged period unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for signs of a serious infection, severe mood changes or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone sodium succinate injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce severe inflammation and suppress an overactive immune response. It may be used for severe allergic, inflammatory and autoimmune conditions, as well as certain other conditions requiring corticosteroid treatment.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and helps control an overactive immune response.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a healthcare professional. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the condition and response to treatment. Do not self-administer it.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar, increased blood pressure, fluid retention, stomach upset, difficulty sleeping, mood changes and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health problems or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body's ability to fight infections and may mask infection symptoms. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically advised. After prolonged treatment, it may need to be stopped gradually rather than suddenly. Seek medical help for signs of a serious infection, severe mood changes, vision problems or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of mild to moderate pain and fever.

Mefenamic acid and paracetamol reduce the production of substances involved in pain and fever. Mefenamic acid also helps reduce inflammation.

How to take/use it

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness, or headache.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if allergic to mefenamic acid, paracetamol, aspirin, or other painkillers. Consult a doctor before use if there is a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, or heart problems. Avoid alcohol. Seek medical help for severe stomach pain, black stools, vomiting blood, rash, breathing difficulty, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially in the last three months, or while breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of mild to moderate pain and fever, including general body pain and pain associated with inflammation.

How does it work?
Mefenamic acid reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label, preferably with or after food. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or mefenamic acid/other NSAIDs unless advised by a doctor.

Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache.

Mefenamic acid reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Dicyclomine relaxes spasms in the smooth muscles of the intestine and abdomen, helping to reduce cramping.

What is it used for?

It is a uterotonic medicine that makes the muscles of the uterus contract, helping reduce bleeding.

Use only on the advice of a doctor or midwife and exactly as prescribed. Follow the instructions for the specific product and route of administration. Do not use it during pregnancy before delivery unless specifically advised by a specialist.

Precautions

Avoid prolonged use unless specifically advised, as it can cause serious movement-related effects. Seek medical help for unusual muscle spasms, uncontrolled movements, severe restlessness or muscle stiffness.

How does it work?
It slowly releases iodine, which kills or inactivates many bacteria, viruses and fungi on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply or use it on the affected skin exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other body openings. Do not swallow.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, dryness, itching or a temporary stinging sensation. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling or breathing difficulty occurs.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to povidone iodine or iodine-containing products. Do not use repeatedly over large areas or for prolonged periods unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice before use in people with thyroid disorders, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or when treating deep, extensive or serious wounds.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine 7.5% is a topical antiseptic used to clean the skin and help reduce germs around minor cuts, grazes, wounds or before certain procedures.

How does it work?
It slowly releases iodine, which kills or reduces many types of bacteria, viruses and fungi on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply or use it on the affected skin as directed on the product label. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other body openings. Do not swallow it.

Temporary skin irritation, redness, dryness or itching may occur. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling or breathing difficulty develops.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to povidone iodine or iodine. Avoid prolonged use or applying it over large areas unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice for deep, extensive or infected wounds, or if the wound is not healing. Keep out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Sucralfate is used to treat and help heal stomach and duodenal ulcers. It may also be prescribed to protect the stomach lining in some conditions causing irritation or inflammation.

How does it work?
It forms a protective coating over ulcers and irritated areas in the stomach and intestine. This barrier helps protect them from stomach acid and digestive enzymes while healing occurs.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. It is usually taken on an empty stomach; follow the product label or prescriber's instructions. Sucralfate can affect the absorption of other medicines, so ask a doctor or pharmacist how to space it from other medicines.

Common side effects
Constipation, dry mouth, nausea and indigestion.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, as the medicine contains aluminium. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines being taken because sucralfate may reduce their absorption. Seek medical advice if symptoms continue or worsen.

What is it used for?
Carboxymethylcellulose sodium is used as an artificial tear to relieve dryness, irritation, burning and discomfort caused by dry eyes.

How does it work?
It forms a lubricating layer over the surface of the eye, helping keep it moist and reducing irritation.

How to take/use it
Use in the eyes exactly as directed on the product label or by an eye-care professional. Wash hands before use and avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or other surfaces. If using other eye medicines, ask a healthcare professional about the correct order of use.

Common side effects
Temporary blurred vision, mild stinging, irritation or redness may occur after use.

Precautions
Do not use if the product is discoloured or contaminated. Stop use and seek medical advice if eye pain, vision changes, worsening redness or irritation occurs, or if symptoms persist. Seek advice before use if there is an eye injury or infection.

What is it used for?
Etofylline + theophylline is a bronchodilator used to help prevent and relieve breathing difficulty, wheezing and chest tightness in conditions such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It is not usually intended for immediate relief of a sudden severe asthma attack unless specifically advised by a doctor.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping to widen them and make breathing easier.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow oral forms with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Do not stop regular treatment without medical advice. Avoid taking other theophylline-containing medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?
Etofylline + theophylline is used to help relieve breathing difficulty, wheezing and tightness of the airways in conditions such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them widen and making breathing easier.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day if advised. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid taking extra doses for sudden breathing difficulty; use the quick-relief inhaler prescribed for such episodes.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, headache, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, tremors and fast or irregular heartbeat.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially with heart disease, high blood pressure, seizures, thyroid problems, liver disease or stomach ulcers. Tell the doctor about all medicines being taken, as theophylline can interact with several medicines. Limit excessive caffeine, and seek medical help for severe vomiting, persistent palpitations, seizures or worsening breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used for eye inflammation when a bacterial eye infection is present or likely, such as certain cases of bacterial conjunctivitis. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Tobramycin is an antibiotic that fights susceptible bacteria. Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces eye inflammation, redness and swelling.

How to take/use it
Use in the affected eye(s) exactly as prescribed and follow the product instructions. Wash hands before use and avoid touching the dropper or tube tip to the eye or other surfaces. Do not wear contact lenses unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, irritation, itching, redness or blurred vision may occur after use. Prolonged use may increase pressure inside the eye or delay healing.

Precautions
Do not use for untreated viral or fungal eye infections unless specifically advised. Tell the prescriber about glaucoma, eye ulcers, recent eye surgery or other eye problems. Avoid prolonged or repeated use without medical supervision. Seek medical help for worsening pain, vision changes, severe swelling or an eye infection that does not improve.

What is it used for?
Metoclopramide is used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for conditions where the stomach empties slowly, such as diabetic gastroparesis.

How does it work?
It blocks certain chemical signals in the brain that trigger nausea and vomiting. It also helps food move more quickly through the upper digestive system.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Avoid alcohol if it makes you sleepy or dizzy.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, dizziness, restlessness, headache, diarrhoea and weakness.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice, usually for a short period, because prolonged or repeated use can cause involuntary movements. Seek medical help urgently for unusual muscle movements, muscle stiffness, severe restlessness or seizures. Tell the doctor before use if there is bowel blockage or bleeding, epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, depression, or if taking medicines that cause drowsiness or affect movement.

What is it used for?
Metoclopramide is used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for certain conditions where the stomach empties slowly.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals in the vomiting centre of the brain and helps food move more quickly through the upper digestive system.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and do not take more or use it for longer than advised. Swallow the tablet with water. Follow the prescribed timing and instructions carefully.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, tiredness, restlessness, headache and diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Avoid driving or operating machinery if sleepy or less alert, and avoid alcohol. Tell the doctor if there is bowel blockage or bleeding, epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, depression, or kidney or liver problems. Use only as prescribed, as prolonged use can cause abnormal movements. Seek urgent medical help for uncontrollable movements, severe muscle stiffness, high fever or confusion.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful abdominal cramps or colicky pain associated with muscle spasms. It may also be prescribed for other painful conditions involving spasms, as decided by a doctor.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces pain and inflammation. Dicyclomine relaxes spasms of the muscles in the intestine and other internal organs, helping relieve cramp-like pain.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not take it with other diclofenac or NSAID painkillers unless advised.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision or drowsiness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney, liver or heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, or bowel blockage. Use during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, only if prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Domperidone is used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also be used for symptoms related to slow movement of the stomach, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals involved in nausea and vomiting and helps improve movement of food through the upper digestive system.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist, and do not take more than recommended. Follow the instructions on the product label or prescription, including when to take it in relation to meals.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, headache, stomach cramps, diarrhoea, and increased breast tenderness or milk production may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart rhythm problems, heart disease, liver disease, or a history of fainting. Domperidone can rarely cause serious abnormal heart rhythms and may interact with some antibiotics, antifungals, and other medicines. Seek urgent medical help for a fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting, or seizures. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only after medical advice.

What is it used for?
Diclofenac injection is used for short-term relief of moderate to severe pain and inflammation, including pain affecting the muscles, joints and bones.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a healthcare professional, usually by injection. Do not self-inject. The dose, route and duration depend on the medical condition and must be decided by the prescriber.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems. Diclofenac may increase the risk of stomach bleeding and cardiovascular problems. Avoid taking it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor. It may not be suitable during pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks and in the last trimester. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic symptoms, chest pain or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve a dry cough along with cold or allergy symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan reduces the cough reflex in the brain. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that helps relieve runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the package or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended, and use a measuring device if it is a liquid. Avoid taking other cough, cold or allergy medicines at the same time unless advised.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea and constipation may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery, as this medicine may cause drowsiness. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors or within 14 days of stopping them; check with a doctor or pharmacist before use with antidepressants or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek advice before use if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, breathing problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not give to children unless the product is appropriate for their age and a healthcare professional confirms its use. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty or a persistent or worsening cough.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cough, especially dry cough, along with cold or allergy symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan reduces the urge to cough. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that helps relieve allergy-related symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take or use exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Avoid taking it with other cough-and-cold medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea and constipation may occur.

Precautions
This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) medicines or within 14 days of stopping them. Seek medical advice before use if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, breathing problems, liver disease, or if taking antidepressants or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical help for a severe or persistent cough, breathing difficulty, or allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This combination is generally used in eye or ear preparations to treat bacterial infections accompanied by redness, swelling or inflammation. The exact use depends on the product formulation and prescribed route.

How does it work?
Gentamicin is an antibiotic that kills susceptible bacteria. Dexamethasone is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation, redness and swelling.

How to take/use it
Use only in the eye or ear, and only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not use it by mouth or inject it. Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye, ear or other surfaces.

Common side effects
Temporary burning, stinging, irritation, itching or discomfort may occur. Eye preparations may briefly cause blurred vision.

Precautions
Do not use for unexplained redness or irritation without medical advice, as corticosteroids can worsen some viral or fungal infections and may delay healing. Seek medical advice if symptoms worsen, vision changes, severe pain or hearing problems develop. Do not use in an ear with a perforated eardrum unless specifically advised. Prolonged eye use may increase eye pressure and requires medical monitoring.

What is it used for?
Cetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, nausea, and dizziness.

Precautions
Cetirizine may cause drowsiness, which can be increased by alcohol or sedative medicines. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Cetirizine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching. It is also used to relieve hives (urticaria) and related skin itching.

How does it work?
It is an antihistamine that blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the package or by a doctor. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, nausea, or dizziness.

Precautions
Cetirizine may cause drowsiness in some people; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for signs of a severe allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or throat or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn, acid reflux and indigestion, especially when these symptoms are associated with nausea or vomiting.

How does it work?
Ranitidine reduces the production of stomach acid. Domperidone helps stomach contents move forward and helps control nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed or as directed on the pack. Swallow the tablet whole with water and follow the recommended timing. Do not take more than advised or use it for a longer period without medical guidance.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, dry mouth, stomach cramps, diarrhoea or constipation may occur. Domperidone can rarely cause a fast or irregular heartbeat.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of heart disease, irregular heartbeat, liver or kidney problems, or bleeding or blockage in the stomach or intestine. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that can affect heart rhythm. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, severe dizziness, or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Alpha amylase and papain are digestive enzymes used to support the digestion of carbohydrates and proteins. They may help relieve digestive discomfort such as indigestion, fullness or bloating when related to difficulty digesting food.

How does it work?
Alpha amylase helps break down starches and other carbohydrates. Papain helps break down proteins, supporting the normal digestive process.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Take with water and follow any instructions about taking it with meals.

Common side effects
Stomach discomfort, nausea, diarrhoea or constipation may occur. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to papaya, papain, alpha amylase or any ingredient in the product. Stop use and seek medical help if swelling, breathing difficulty or a severe rash occurs. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if symptoms are persistent or severe.

What is it used for?
Used as a digestive aid to help relieve indigestion, bloating and gas associated with digestion.

How does it work?
Alpha-amylase helps break down starches into smaller sugars. Dill, caraway and anise oils act as carminatives, which may help reduce intestinal gas and digestive discomfort.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, nausea, heartburn or loose motions may occur. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur, such as rash, swelling or breathing difficulty. Consult a healthcare professional if symptoms are severe, persistent or recurrent, or before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding or in young children.

What is it used for?
Used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and indigestion associated with stomach or intestinal cramps.

How does it work?
Ranitidine reduces the production of stomach acid. Dicyclomine relaxes the muscles of the intestine, helping to relieve abdominal cramps and spasms.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more or use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, constipation, diarrhoea, nausea and headache.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, prostate enlargement, myasthenia gravis, or kidney or liver disease. Dicyclomine may cause blurred vision or dizziness; avoid driving if affected. Seek medical help for severe or persistent abdominal pain, black stools, vomiting blood or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine is used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be prescribed for stomach or intestinal ulcers and other acid-related digestive conditions.

How does it work?
It blocks H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the production of stomach acid.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Swallow with water and do not take more or for longer than recommended. Check with a pharmacist before using it, as ranitidine availability and use may be restricted in some countries because of safety concerns.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, a history of stomach ulcers, or difficulty swallowing. Seek medical advice for persistent or severe symptoms, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or severe abdominal pain. Seek urgent help for swelling, breathing difficulty or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine reduces excess stomach acid. It has been used to relieve heartburn and acid reflux, and to treat stomach or duodenal ulcers and other acid-related conditions.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the production of stomach acid.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed or directed on the product label. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Ranitidine products have been withdrawn or restricted in many countries; confirm with a doctor or pharmacist that this product is appropriate before use.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, a history of porphyria, or other medicines being taken. Seek medical advice for persistent or worsening symptoms, difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss, or severe stomach pain. Avoid self-treating recurring acidity without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Acyclovir is an antiviral medicine used to treat herpes virus infections, including serious herpes simplex infections and chickenpox or shingles caused by the varicella-zoster virus.

How does it work?
It blocks the ability of the herpes virus to multiply, helping control the infection and reduce its severity.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection and kidney function. Do not stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, tiredness, and irritation or pain at the administration site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, dehydration, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or any other medicines being used. Drink adequate fluids unless a doctor has advised fluid restriction. Seek medical help for reduced urination, confusion, tremors, seizures, or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Acyclovir is used to treat herpes virus infections, including genital herpes, cold sores, shingles and chickenpox. It can reduce the severity and duration of symptoms but does not remove the virus from the body.

How does it work?
It blocks the ability of herpes viruses to make their genetic material, which slows the growth and spread of the virus.

How to take/use it
Use it only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. The dose, frequency, duration and route depend on the infection and the formulation. Drink plenty of fluids unless a doctor has advised otherwise, and complete the prescribed course.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and tiredness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or a weakened immune system. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney disease. Seek medical help for severe allergic reactions, confusion, seizures, very little urine or unusual bruising.

What is it used for?
Adrenaline is an emergency medicine used to treat severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) and, in hospital settings, cardiac arrest and other serious breathing or circulation problems. Its exact use depends on the prescribed product and medical condition.

How does it work?
It quickly stimulates the heart and blood vessels, helping improve blood pressure and blood flow. It also relaxes the airways and reduces swelling during a severe allergic reaction.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose, route and timing depend on the emergency and the product. Emergency medical care is required after use for a severe allergic reaction.

Common side effects
Fast or pounding heartbeat, shaking, anxiety or restlessness, headache, sweating, dizziness, nausea and vomiting.

Precautions
Use under medical supervision, especially in people with heart disease, high blood pressure, thyroid problems or diabetes. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, severe headache, fainting, irregular heartbeat or worsening breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Take or receive the medicine exactly as directed and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. The dose and route depend on the type and severity of the infection.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to ampicillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Contact a doctor for severe or persistent diarrhoea, especially during or after treatment. Tell the doctor about kidney problems and any other medicines being used.

What is it used for?
Ampicillin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by interfering with the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Take each dose with water and follow the product label or medical advice regarding food. Do not take an extra dose if one is missed without medical advice.

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a previous serious allergy to ampicillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, or a severe rash. Contact a doctor if diarrhoea is severe, persistent or bloody. Use only on medical advice, especially during pregnancy, breastfeeding or in people with kidney problems.

What is it used for?
Artesunate is an antimalarial medicine used mainly to treat severe malaria. It may also be used as part of a prescribed treatment regimen for malaria.

How does it work?
It damages malaria parasites in the blood, helping to clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The route and schedule depend on the formulation and severity of malaria; injectable artesunate must be given by a healthcare professional. Complete the full antimalarial treatment as directed.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, stomach discomfort and tiredness may occur.

Precautions
Malaria, especially severe malaria, requires urgent medical care. Seek medical attention for allergic symptoms, unusual tiredness, pale skin, dark urine, yellowing of the eyes or skin, or worsening symptoms, as delayed anaemia and other serious reactions can occur. Inform the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, liver problems or any previous reaction to antimalarial medicines.

What is it used for?
Artesunate is used to treat malaria, especially severe malaria that may require hospital treatment. It is usually followed by a complete course of another antimalarial medicine as prescribed.

How does it work?
It rapidly kills malaria-causing parasites in the blood, helping to reduce the infection and its symptoms.

How to take/use it
This medicine is usually given by injection by a trained healthcare professional. The dose, route and treatment schedule depend on the severity of malaria and must be decided by a doctor. Complete the recommended follow-up antimalarial treatment.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, fever and pain or reactions at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Seek urgent medical help for difficulty breathing, swelling, severe rash, fainting, unusual weakness, pale skin, dark urine or yellowing of the eyes or skin. Blood tests may be needed after treatment because delayed breakdown of red blood cells can rarely occur.

What is it used for?
Atracurium injection is used during general anaesthesia to relax the muscles and help doctors place a breathing tube during surgery. It may also be used to help control muscle movement while a patient is receiving mechanical ventilation. It does not cause unconsciousness or relieve pain by itself.

How does it work?
It temporarily blocks nerve signals to the muscles, including the muscles used for movement and breathing. The effect wears off after the medicine is stopped and the body breaks it down.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein only by trained healthcare professionals in a hospital. Breathing support and careful monitoring are required because it temporarily weakens or stops the breathing muscles. The dose and timing are decided by the anaesthetist.

Common side effects
Flushing, low blood pressure, fast heartbeat, wheezing or bronchospasm, skin rash and temporary muscle weakness may occur.

Precautions
It must not be self-administered. Tell the anaesthetist about any previous reaction to muscle-relaxing medicines, asthma or breathing problems, heart or blood-pressure problems, or neuromuscular disorders. Seek immediate medical attention for severe breathing difficulty, swelling, widespread rash or other signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Atropine 0.6 mg/ml injection is used by healthcare professionals in emergencies to treat a dangerously slow heartbeat. It may also be used to reduce excessive secretions before procedures and as part of treatment for certain poisonings, such as organophosphate poisoning.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of a chemical messenger called acetylcholine. This can increase the heart rate and reduce saliva, airway and other secretions.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or nurse. The dose, route and frequency depend on the condition being treated and the patient's response. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, blurred vision, enlarged pupils, sensitivity to light, flushing, fast heartbeat, constipation, difficulty passing urine and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is glaucoma, prostate enlargement, difficulty passing urine, bowel blockage, heart disease or high fever. Seek urgent medical help for severe palpitations, confusion, extreme agitation, breathing difficulty or inability to pass urine.

What is it used for?
Azithromycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the chest, throat, ears, skin and reproductive system. It does not work against viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making proteins needed for their growth and survival.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food unless the prescriber advises otherwise. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them for a future illness.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, vomiting and headache.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about an allergy to azithromycin or other macrolide antibiotics, liver disease, heart rhythm problems or a history of prolonged QT interval. Tell the doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines being taken. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, facial or throat swelling, difficulty breathing, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Aztreonam injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by certain Gram-negative bacteria, including some infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood and reproductive organs. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment length depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Use it only as prescribed.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea or vomiting; rash; headache; and changes in liver tests.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to aztreonam or other antibiotics, kidney or liver problems, or a history of antibiotic-associated diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Do not use it for viral infections.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall, which stops the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
Aztreonam is usually given by injection by a healthcare professional. Use it only as prescribed, and complete the recommended treatment even if symptoms improve. Do not self-administer unless specifically trained to do so.

Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, rash and headache.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to aztreonam, penicillin, cephalosporins or other antibiotics. Inform the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea, as these may indicate a serious reaction.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?
Aztreonam 500 mg is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by certain bacteria, especially Gram-negative bacteria. It may be used for infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood or reproductive organs, as determined by the doctor.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and medical advice. Do not self-inject or stop treatment early.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea or vomiting; skin rash; and headache.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to aztreonam or other antibiotics, and about kidney or liver problems. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Contact a doctor if severe or persistent diarrhoea develops during or after treatment, as this may indicate a serious intestinal infection.

What is it used for?
Betamethasone is a corticosteroid used on prescription to reduce inflammation and control overactive allergic or immune reactions. The exact condition it treats depends on the prescribed formulation and the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune responses.

How to take/use it
Use it only as prescribed. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the formulation and condition being treated. Do not change the dose or stop prolonged treatment suddenly without medical advice.

Possible side effects include indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, fluid retention, and increases in blood sugar or blood pressure.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health conditions, or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce resistance to infection and may mask infection symptoms. Seek medical advice for signs of infection, severe mood changes, vision problems, or serious allergic reactions.

What is it used for?
Alpha-Beta Arteether is an antimalarial injection used to treat malaria, especially severe or complicated malaria caused by Plasmodium parasites.

How does it work?
It forms active compounds that damage the malaria parasite and help clear it from the blood.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or other healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the severity of malaria and must be decided by the prescriber. Do not self-administer it.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, dizziness, headache and pain at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any allergy to arteether or other artemisinin medicines, pregnancy, or liver, kidney or heart problems. Malaria can become serious quickly; seek urgent medical care for worsening fever, confusion, breathing difficulty, seizures or extreme weakness. Complete the prescribed treatment and do not stop it without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) is used to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency and support healthy bones and muscles. It may be prescribed when vitamin D levels are low or when the body needs extra vitamin D.

How does it work?
It helps the body absorb calcium and phosphate from food, supporting bone mineralisation and normal muscle function.

How to take/use it
Use only in the dose and by the route prescribed by a doctor. This is a high-strength vitamin D product; do not repeat the dose or take other vitamin D supplements unless advised. The correct schedule depends on the patient's vitamin D level and treatment plan.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated when used as prescribed. Excessive vitamin D can cause nausea, vomiting, constipation, stomach pain, increased thirst or frequent urination.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or disorders that cause excess calcium. Avoid taking additional vitamin D or calcium products without medical advice. Seek medical help if severe nausea, vomiting, confusion, unusual weakness or excessive thirst occurs.

What is it used for?
Cerebroprotein is used under medical supervision for certain neurological conditions, such as recovery support after stroke or brain injury and some disorders affecting memory or thinking. The exact use depends on the diagnosis and the prescribing doctor's advice.

How does it work?
It contains small protein fragments and amino acids that may support nerve-cell function and recovery in the brain. Its exact benefits can vary depending on the neurological condition.

How to take/use it
Use only in the form, dose and schedule prescribed by the doctor. If supplied as an injection, it should be administered by a healthcare professional. Do not self-administer or change the treatment schedule.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include headache, dizziness, nausea, sweating, restlessness or confusion. Injection-site reactions may occur when given by injection.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about epilepsy or a history of seizures, severe kidney problems, allergies, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for a seizure, severe allergic reaction or marked confusion. Use only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Levocarnitine is used to prevent or treat low carnitine levels, including certain inherited metabolic conditions and carnitine deficiency associated with some kidney conditions or treatments. It should be used under medical advice.

How does it work?
Levocarnitine helps transport fatty acids into cells so they can be used to produce energy.

Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Measure the liquid with the supplied measuring device, and do not take more or for longer than advised. It may be taken with or after food if it causes stomach upset.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach cramps, diarrhoea and a fish-like body odour.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, a seizure disorder, diabetes, or use of warfarin. Seek medical advice if seizures worsen or if severe or persistent vomiting or diarrhoea occurs.

What is it used for?
Caspofungin injection is an antifungal medicine used to treat serious fungal infections, including invasive Candida infections and certain Aspergillus infections. It may also be used in some patients with persistent fever and suspected fungal infection, as decided by a specialist.

How does it work?
It blocks the production of an important part of the fungal cell wall, helping to stop the growth of fungi.

This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. It is intended for hospital or specialist use and should not be self-administered. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection.

Fever, chills, headache, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, rash, redness or pain at the injection site, and changes in liver enzyme levels may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to caspofungin or other antifungal medicines, liver disease, or pregnancy or breastfeeding. Liver function may need monitoring during treatment. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, as some medicines can affect caspofungin. Seek immediate medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or a severe infusion reaction.

What is it used for?
Cefepime is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by bacteria, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin, abdomen and bloodstream. What is it used for?
Cefoperazone with sulbactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin and soft tissues, bones and joints, and blood, when prescribed by a doctor.

It stops susceptible bacteria from making proteins needed for their growth and survival, helping control the infection.
