How does it work?
It is converted in the body to colistin, which damages the outer membrane of susceptible bacteria and kills them.

How to take/use it
This medicine is supplied as a dry powder that must be reconstituted before use. It should be prepared and administered by a healthcare professional, or used exactly as instructed if prescribed for home treatment. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the infection and kidney function. Do not use leftover or improperly prepared solution.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include nausea, diarrhoea, tingling or numbness, dizziness, weakness, and reactions at the injection site. Kidney problems and breathing difficulty or wheezing can occur, particularly with injectable or inhaled use.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, muscle or nerve disorders, breathing problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Kidney function and sometimes blood levels may need monitoring. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially those that may affect the kidneys or nervous system, or muscle-relaxing medicines. Seek urgent medical help for reduced urination, severe weakness, confusion, facial or throat swelling, or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Colistimethate injection is an antibiotic used in hospitals to treat serious bacterial infections caused by certain susceptible bacteria, including some infections that are resistant to other antibiotics.

How does it work?
It is converted in the body to colistin, which damages the outer membrane of certain bacteria and kills them.

How to take/use it
This injection is given by a doctor or nurse, usually into a vein. The dose is carefully selected according to the infection and kidney function. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Tingling or numbness, dizziness, weakness, nausea, diarrhoea, and injection-site reactions may occur. Kidney problems and breathing or muscle weakness can occur, particularly with higher doses or prolonged treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, muscle or nerve disorders, or any previous allergy to colistimethate or colistin. Kidney function may need monitoring during treatment. Seek urgent medical help for difficulty breathing, severe weakness, facial swelling, or a severe rash.

What is it used for?
Colistimethate injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by certain bacteria, especially difficult-to-treat Gram-negative infections such as those caused by Pseudomonas or Acinetobacter. It is generally used when other suitable antibiotics may not work.

How does it work?
It is converted in the body to colistin, which damages the outer membrane of susceptible bacteria and kills them.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection or infusion by a doctor or nurse in a hospital or healthcare setting. The dose and treatment duration depend on the infection, kidney function and response to treatment. Do not self-administer or skip doses.

Common side effects
Kidney problems, tingling or numbness, dizziness, weakness, muscle weakness, nausea and diarrhoea may occur. Serious allergic reactions and breathing or muscle problems can occur rarely.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, neuromuscular disorders, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being used. Kidney function and, when needed, nerve and muscle function should be monitored during treatment. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, severe weakness, facial swelling or a widespread rash.

What is it used for?
Dexamethasone injection is a prescription corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactive immune or allergic reactions in conditions selected by a doctor. The exact use depends on the patient's condition.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of chemicals and immune responses that cause inflammation, swelling and allergic reactions.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the condition and response to treatment. Do not self-inject or repeat it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar, indigestion, mood or sleep changes, increased appetite, fluid retention and increased risk of infections may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health problems or any current infection. Corticosteroids can mask or worsen infections. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically approved by the doctor. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe weakness or signs of a serious infection.

What is it used for?
Diclofenac injection is used for short-term relief of moderate to severe pain and inflammation, such as muscle, joint, or other acute pain. It is usually given when an injectable painkiller is needed.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
This injection must be administered by a healthcare professional. The dose, frequency and treatment duration should be decided by the prescriber. Do not self-inject or use it for longer than prescribed.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma or allergy to painkillers, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems. Avoid taking it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, chest pain or a severe skin rash. It should generally be avoided during the last three months of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful muscle spasms and pain in musculoskeletal conditions, such as back pain and other muscle or joint problems.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Thiocolchicoside helps relax painful muscle spasms.

How to take/use it
This injection should be given only by a healthcare professional. Do not self-inject. Use it only as prescribed.

Common side effects
Indigestion, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or drowsiness, and pain or irritation at the injection site.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid during pregnancy, especially the last three months, and do not use while breastfeeding unless specifically advised. Thiocolchicoside may increase the risk of seizures; inform the doctor about any history of seizures. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergy, breathing difficulty or severe skin reactions.

What is it used for?
This injection is generally used for short-term relief of painful abdominal cramps, spasms and colicky pain.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces pain and inflammation. Dicyclomine relaxes spasms in the muscles of the stomach and intestines, helping relieve cramp-like pain.

How to take/use it
This injection should be given only by a healthcare professional. Do not self-inject. The dose and duration should be decided by the prescriber.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea or constipation, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision and pain at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine or bowel blockage. Avoid use if allergic to diclofenac, dicyclomine or similar medicines. Diclofenac may increase the risk of stomach bleeding and is generally avoided during late pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Seek medical help for severe stomach pain, black stools, vomiting blood, breathing difficulty or facial swelling.

What is it used for?
Dicyclomine is used to relieve stomach and intestinal cramps or spasms, including symptoms associated with irritable bowel syndrome.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles of the stomach and intestines by reducing abnormal muscle spasms, helping to relieve cramping and pain.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. If supplied as an injection, it should be administered by a healthcare professional. Do not self-inject or use more than prescribed.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, dizziness, drowsiness, blurred vision, nausea, constipation and difficulty passing urine.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine or prostate enlargement, bowel blockage, severe ulcerative colitis, myasthenia gravis, or liver or kidney problems. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizzy or drowsy. Seek medical help for severe confusion, a fast heartbeat, inability to urinate, breathing difficulty or swelling of the face or throat.

What is it used for?
Dobutamine injection is used in hospitals for short-term treatment of severe heart failure, low blood flow from the heart, or cardiogenic shock. It helps the heart pump more strongly when urgent circulatory support is needed.

How does it work?
Dobutamine stimulates receptors in the heart, increasing the strength of heart contractions and improving blood flow. It may also affect heart rate and blood pressure.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein as a controlled infusion by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration are decided by the doctor based on the condition. Heart rhythm, blood pressure and other vital signs require close monitoring during treatment.

Common side effects
Increased heart rate, palpitations, abnormal heart rhythms, changes in blood pressure, headache, nausea and chest discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Use only under close medical supervision. Tell the doctor about heart rhythm problems, high blood pressure, reduced blood volume, or allergies to medicines. Seek urgent medical attention for severe chest pain, fainting, difficulty breathing or a fast or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Dopamine injection is used in hospitals to support blood pressure and heart function in severe low blood pressure, shock, or reduced blood flow to vital organs. It is given in emergency and critical-care situations under close medical supervision.

How does it work?
It stimulates specific receptors in the heart and blood vessels. This can increase the force of the heartbeat and help raise blood pressure and blood flow.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given only by intravenous infusion by a doctor or trained healthcare professional, usually after dilution and with continuous monitoring. The dose and infusion rate are adjusted according to the patient’s condition. It must not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, fast heartbeat, palpitations, irregular heartbeat, increased blood pressure and chest discomfort. Pain or tissue damage can occur if the medicine leaks outside the vein.

Precautions
Use only in a hospital or emergency-care setting. Blood pressure, heart rate, heart rhythm and the infusion site require close monitoring. Tell the doctor about heart rhythm problems, poor circulation, thyroid disease, or use of monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines. Seek immediate medical attention for severe chest pain, breathing difficulty, or a markedly irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Doripenem is an antibiotic used in hospitals to treat serious bacterial infections, especially complicated urinary tract and abdominal infections. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming the protective cell wall they need to survive.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function; follow the prescribed hospital treatment exactly.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, headache, rash, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to doripenem, other carbapenem antibiotics, penicillins or cephalosporins. Extra caution is needed in people with kidney problems or a history of seizures. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, seizures, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Doripenem can interact with some medicines, including valproic acid or sodium valproate.

What is it used for?
Doxofylline is a bronchodilator used to help relieve breathing difficulty, wheezing and chest tightness in asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It helps keep the airways open.

How does it work?
It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them widen and making breathing easier.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more or more often than directed. Do not stop regular asthma or COPD treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, difficulty sleeping, tremors, fast heartbeat and palpitations.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart problems, high blood pressure, seizures, liver or kidney disease, or pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe or worsening breathing difficulty, chest pain or a persistent fast heartbeat. Inform the doctor about all other medicines being taken, as some medicines may interact with doxofylline.

What is it used for?
Doxycycline is an antibiotic used to treat a range of bacterial infections, including certain infections of the skin, lungs, urinary tract and other body areas. It should be used only for infections confirmed or considered likely to be bacterial.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making proteins needed for their growth and survival, helping control the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course. Swallow with a full glass of water while sitting or standing, and avoid lying down immediately afterwards. Antacids and supplements containing iron, calcium or magnesium can reduce its absorption; ask a doctor or pharmacist how to space them apart.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach upset, indigestion and increased sensitivity to sunlight.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice during pregnancy, breastfeeding or in children, especially those under 8 years. Use sun protection and avoid excessive sunlight. Tell the doctor about allergies and any liver problems. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, difficulty swallowing, severe headache or vision changes, or signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Drotaverine injection is used to relieve painful spasms or cramps of smooth muscles, especially in the stomach and intestines. It may also be prescribed for spasms of the bile ducts or urinary tract.

How does it work?
It relaxes the smooth muscles in internal organs, helping reduce spasms and cramp-like pain.

How to take/use it
This injection should be given only by a doctor or other trained healthcare professional. The dose, route and frequency depend on the condition being treated; do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, nausea, palpitations, flushing or a fall in blood pressure may occur. Injection-site discomfort or allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about low blood pressure, severe liver, kidney or heart problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and any medicine allergies. Avoid driving if dizziness occurs. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, severe weakness, difficulty breathing, facial swelling or other signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Edaravone is mainly used to help slow the loss of physical function in adults with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a progressive disease affecting nerve cells that control muscles. In some countries and formulations, it is also used for acute ischemic stroke; the approved use depends on the product and local medical guidance.

How does it work?
Edaravone helps remove harmful free radicals and may reduce oxidative damage to nerve cells. This may help slow disease-related nerve and muscle deterioration in ALS.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a specialist. The route and schedule depend on the formulation; some forms are given by intravenous infusion by a healthcare professional, while others are taken by mouth. Follow the product-specific instructions and do not change or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Bruising, headache, difficulty walking, skin irritation or rash, and tiredness may occur. Side effects can vary with the formulation.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to edaravone or other ingredients, and about asthma or previous reactions to medicines or infusions. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, dizziness, or fainting, as these may indicate a serious allergic reaction. Medical supervision is required during treatment.

What is it used for?
Enoxaparin is an anticoagulant used to prevent and treat blood clots in the veins. It is commonly used after surgery, during hospital stays or periods of reduced movement, and in some heart-related conditions as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the blood’s ability to form clots by blocking clotting factor Xa. This helps prevent existing clots from getting larger and reduces the risk of new clots forming.

How to take/use it
This medicine is usually injected under the skin, often by a healthcare professional or after proper instruction. Use it exactly as prescribed. Do not inject it into a muscle, and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Bruising, pain or redness at the injection site, bleeding, and anaemia may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any bleeding disorder, low platelet count, kidney disease, stomach ulcer, recent surgery, or allergy to heparin. Inform the doctor before spinal or epidural procedures. Do not take aspirin, ibuprofen or other blood-thinning medicines unless advised. Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe headache, sudden weakness, or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Enoxaparin is an anticoagulant used to prevent and treat blood clots in the veins, such as deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). It is also used to reduce the risk of clots during hospitalisation or around certain surgeries.

How does it work?
It reduces the blood’s ability to form harmful clots by increasing the action of antithrombin, mainly against clotting factor Xa.

How to take/use it
This medicine is usually given as an injection under the skin, as prescribed. It should not be injected into a muscle. Follow the prescribed dose and schedule, do not stop it or change the dose without medical advice, and do not rub the injection site after use.

Common side effects
Bruising, pain or redness at the injection site, bleeding, and anaemia may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any bleeding disorder, stomach ulcer, kidney disease, liver disease, recent surgery, or planned surgery or dental procedure. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially other blood thinners, aspirin, ibuprofen, or similar painkillers. Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe headache, sudden weakness, or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Esomeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD) and related irritation of the food pipe. It may also be used for certain stomach ulcers and other acid-related conditions when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that blocks the release of acid in the stomach. This helps relieve acid-related symptoms and allows irritation or ulcers to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually before food. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies and all other medicines being taken, especially clopidogrel, warfarin, digoxin or medicines for HIV. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss, persistent vomiting or symptoms that do not improve. Long-term use should be taken only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Used to treat iron deficiency, including iron deficiency anaemia, when oral iron is not suitable, does not work well, or iron needs to be replaced quickly.

How does it work?
Ferric carboxymaltose supplies iron that the body uses to make haemoglobin and red blood cells. It also helps replenish the body's stored iron.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given only by a healthcare professional through a vein (intravenous injection or infusion). The dose and number of treatments depend on the severity of iron deficiency and the individual's iron needs. It must not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, dizziness, flushing, high blood pressure, and reactions at the injection site. Low phosphate levels may occur, especially with repeated treatment.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about any previous allergy to intravenous iron, iron overload, liver disease, or other medical conditions. The patient should be monitored during and shortly after administration because serious allergic reactions can rarely occur. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, fainting, or chest tightness.

What is it used for?
Fosfomycin is an antibacterial medicine used to treat certain bacterial infections. The exact infection it treats depends on the prescribed formulation and the doctor’s assessment. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking an early step needed to build their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. The route of use depends on the formulation; injectable fosfomycin must be given by a healthcare professional. Do not change the dose or stop treatment early unless advised by the doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach upset, headache, and injection-site discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to fosfomycin or other antibiotics, kidney problems, or a history of severe diarrhoea after antibiotic use. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash, swelling, breathing difficulty, or other signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by susceptible bacteria, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, abdomen, bones or joints, and blood. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection, kidney function and other medical factors. Complete the prescribed course unless the healthcare professional advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain or irritation at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash and temporary changes in liver blood tests may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there has been an allergy to cefuroxime, cephalosporins, penicillins or other antibiotics, or if there is kidney disease. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty or a severe skin reaction. Contact a doctor for severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, as this may occur during or after antibiotic treatment.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, bones and joints, abdomen, or blood. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Do not self-inject, and use it only as prescribed.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea or vomiting; and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics, or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, previous antibiotic-related severe diarrhoea, or any medicine being used. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
This antibiotic injection is used to treat certain bacterial infections. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor and is not effective against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefuroxime stops susceptible bacteria from forming their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps cefuroxime work against some bacteria that can resist certain antibiotics.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection by a doctor or nurse. The dose and duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and medical advice. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain or redness at the injection site, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to cefuroxime, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics, kidney problems, or a previous episode of severe antibiotic-associated diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Furosemide injection is used to remove excess fluid from the body (oedema), including fluid buildup related to heart failure, kidney disease or liver disease. It may also be used for urgent fluid buildup in the lungs and, in some cases, to help control high blood pressure.

How does it work?
It is a loop diuretic, or “water tablet” medicine. It helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water through the urine, reducing fluid buildup and sometimes lowering blood pressure.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein or muscle by a doctor or other trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the medical condition and response to treatment. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Increased urination, dizziness, low blood pressure, dehydration, weakness, nausea and changes in blood salts such as low potassium or sodium.

Precautions
Medical monitoring of blood pressure, kidney function, hydration and blood salts may be needed. Tell the healthcare professional about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, gout, diabetes, difficulty passing urine or hearing problems. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, severe weakness, confusion, very little urine or new hearing or ringing problems.

What is it used for?
Ganciclovir is an antiviral medicine used to treat serious cytomegalovirus (CMV) infections, especially in people with weakened immunity. It may also be used for CMV retinitis and, in some cases, to prevent CMV infection after an organ transplant.

How does it work?
It blocks the ability of CMV to make new copies of itself, helping control the infection.

How to take/use it
This 500 mg medicine is usually given by a healthcare professional, often into a vein. The exact dose and treatment duration depend on the infection, kidney function and blood test results. Do not self-administer or change the treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Low white blood cell, red blood cell or platelet counts; nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, headache and tiredness.

Precautions
Regular blood and kidney-function tests are usually needed. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, low blood counts, pregnancy, plans for pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for unusual bleeding, severe weakness, fever, signs of infection or a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Gentamicin injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, particularly those caused by certain Gram-negative bacteria. It is usually used in hospitals or under close medical supervision.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from multiplying.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a muscle or vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the infection, kidney function and other factors. Do not self-inject or use it without medical supervision.

Common side effects
Injection-site pain, nausea, headache and dizziness may occur. Serious effects can include kidney problems, ringing in the ears, hearing loss or balance problems.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, hearing or balance disorders, pregnancy, or dehydration. Kidney function and, when needed, blood levels and hearing may be monitored during treatment. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially those that can affect the kidneys, hearing or muscles. Seek medical help for reduced urination, severe dizziness, ringing in the ears, hearing changes, breathing difficulty or unusual muscle weakness.

What is it used for?
Glutathione 1200 mg is used as a dietary supplement to provide glutathione, a naturally occurring antioxidant in the body. It is not a substitute for treatment of a medical condition unless advised by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Glutathione helps neutralise reactive molecules and supports the body's normal antioxidant defences.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Some people may experience nausea, bloating, abdominal discomfort or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Check with a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking regular medicines. Do not use if allergic to any ingredient. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe or persistent side effects occur.

What is it used for?
Glutathione is used as an antioxidant supplement to support the body's natural antioxidant and cellular protection systems. It is not a replacement for treatment of any medical condition.

How does it work?
Glutathione is a naturally occurring antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative damage and supports normal detoxification processes in the body.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. The dosage form and route are not specified here; if it is an injectable product, it should be administered only by a qualified healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Side effects depend on the dosage form. Oral products may cause stomach upset, bloating, abdominal cramps or loose stools. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

Precautions
Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or allergy. Do not self-administer an injectable form. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or severe rash.

What is it used for?
Glutathione 600 mg is used as a glutathione supplement or medicine. The exact therapeutic use cannot be confirmed from the generic name alone and may depend on the product formulation and prescriber's advice.

How does it work?
Glutathione is a naturally occurring antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative damage.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. The dose, frequency and route cannot be determined from the supplied information.

Common side effects
Specific common side effects cannot be confirmed without knowing the product's formulation and route of use.

Precautions
Check the product instructions before use. Consult a healthcare professional during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is a medical condition or allergy. Seek medical help if an allergic reaction or other serious symptom occurs.

What is it used for?
L-Ornithine L-Aspartate injection is used to help lower high ammonia levels in the blood, especially in people with liver disease and hepatic encephalopathy. It may help improve symptoms such as confusion caused by this condition.

How does it work?
It helps the body convert ammonia into less harmful substances that can be removed through the urea cycle or used to make glutamine.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or nurse, usually into a vein. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and medical advice. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea or flatulence may occur. Allergic reactions are uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease or any previous allergy to this medicine. It should not be used in severe kidney impairment unless specifically advised by a specialist. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling or a severe rash.

What is it used for?
Heparin is an anticoagulant used to prevent and treat harmful blood clots, such as clots in the legs or lungs, and in some heart-related conditions. It is used under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It increases the action of antithrombin, a natural substance that slows the blood-clotting process. This helps prevent existing clots from getting larger and reduces the formation of new clots.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor or healthcare professional. The dose, route and duration depend on the condition and blood-clotting test results. Do not self-administer or change the dose. This medicine may require regular monitoring.

Common side effects
Bleeding, easy bruising, pain or irritation at the injection site, and reduced platelet counts. Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe headache or sudden weakness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any bleeding disorder, low platelet count, stomach ulcer, recent surgery, uncontrolled high blood pressure, liver or kidney problems, or previous reaction to heparin. Inform the doctor about all medicines being used, especially other blood thinners, aspirin and anti-inflammatory painkillers. Avoid activities that may cause injury and do not take extra medicines that increase bleeding risk unless advised.

What is it used for?
Heparin injection is an anticoagulant used to prevent or treat harmful blood clots in the veins or arteries. It may also be used during certain medical procedures to reduce clotting.

How does it work?
It strengthens the action of antithrombin, a natural substance in the body, and slows the blood-clotting process.

How to take/use it
This injection is given by a healthcare professional, usually under the skin or into a vein, as directed by the doctor. Do not self-inject or change the dose unless specifically instructed. Blood tests may be needed during treatment.

Common side effects
Bleeding, easy bruising, pain or redness at the injection site, and irritation. A fall in platelet count can occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any bleeding disorder, low platelet count, stomach ulcer, recent surgery, kidney or liver disease, or upcoming procedure. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially aspirin, ibuprofen, other blood thinners, and medicines that affect bleeding. Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, blood in urine, vomiting blood, severe headache, sudden weakness, or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Hydrocortisone injection is a corticosteroid used under medical supervision to reduce severe inflammation and allergic reactions. It may also be used when the body does not produce enough natural corticosteroid hormone, such as in adrenal insufficiency.

How does it work?
It acts like the body’s natural corticosteroid hormones. It reduces inflammation and dampens an overactive immune response.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or nurse into a vein or muscle. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated and the response to treatment. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, increased blood sugar, indigestion, mood changes, sleep problems, fluid retention and increased risk of infection may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions or any infection. Corticosteroids can mask infection symptoms. Do not stop prolonged treatment suddenly unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for severe allergic symptoms, signs of infection or major mood changes.

What is it used for?
Hydrocortisone injection is a corticosteroid used in hospitals for severe inflammation or allergic reactions and for replacing cortisol when the body does not produce enough, such as in adrenal insufficiency. Its use depends on the medical condition being treated.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone cortisol and reduces inflammation, swelling and overactive immune reactions. It also helps support the body during cortisol deficiency.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or nurse, usually into a vein or muscle. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the condition and response to treatment. Do not self-administer it.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar, increased blood pressure, fluid retention, stomach upset, headache, difficulty sleeping, mood changes and pain at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions, liver or kidney disease, or any infection. Hydrocortisone can reduce the body’s ability to fight infections and may mask infection symptoms. Long or repeated treatment should not be stopped suddenly unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Imipenem with cilastatin is a prescription injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, bones and joints, and blood. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Imipenem kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Cilastatin helps prevent imipenem from being broken down in the kidneys, allowing it to work effectively.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and other factors. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, rash, headache, injection-site pain or redness, and inflammation of the vein may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to imipenem, cilastatin, penicillins or other cephalosporin antibiotics; kidney disease; or a history of seizures. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, swelling or breathing difficulty, severe rash, confusion or seizures. This medicine can interact with valproate medicines.

What is it used for?
Imipenem with cilastatin is a prescription injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, bones and joints, and blood. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

Imipenem kills bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall. Cilastatin helps prevent imipenem from being broken down in the kidneys, allowing it to work effectively.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to imipenem, cilastatin, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics; kidney disease; seizures or other brain disorders; and any medicines being taken, especially valproate. What is it used for?
Used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections affecting the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, bones and joints, or blood. It is usually used in hospitals when injectable antibiotic treatment is needed.

How does it work?
Imipenem kills bacteria by preventing them from making their protective cell wall. Cilastatin helps stop imipenem from being broken down in the kidneys, allowing it to work effectively.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection or intravenous infusion by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, rash, redness or pain at the injection site, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any allergy to imipenem, cilastatin, penicillins, cephalosporins or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney disease. Tell the doctor about a history of seizures or nervous-system problems. Seek medical help for seizures, severe rash, breathing difficulty, or severe or persistent diarrhoea, especially during or after treatment.

What is it used for?
Iron sucrose is used to treat iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anaemia, especially when oral iron is not suitable, has not worked well, or iron replacement is needed under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It supplies iron that the body uses to make haemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and number of treatments depend on the severity of iron deficiency and the medical condition. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, dizziness, flushing, changes in blood pressure, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to iron injections, iron overload, liver disease, or other medical conditions. Blood pressure and allergic reactions should be monitored during and after administration. Seek immediate medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe dizziness, or fainting.

What is it used for?
Labetalol is mainly used to treat high blood pressure. It may also be used to control severely high blood pressure in hospital settings and high blood pressure during pregnancy, under medical supervision.

How does it work?
It blocks certain signals that make the heart beat faster and blood vessels tighten. This slows the heart rate and relaxes the blood vessels, helping lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day. It may be taken with or without food, but take it consistently the same way. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, tiredness, headache, nausea, cold hands or feet, and a slow heartbeat may occur. Dizziness may be more noticeable when standing up.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is asthma or other breathing disease, a slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, heart failure, diabetes, or liver disease. Labetalol can mask some warning signs of low blood sugar. Seek medical help for fainting, severe breathing difficulty, swelling, or an unusually slow heartbeat. If pregnant or breastfeeding, use it only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam oral solution is used to prevent and control seizures in people with epilepsy. It may be used alone or with other anti-seizure medicines, depending on the type of seizure.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain and lowers the likelihood of seizures. Its action is linked to regulating the release of chemical signals between nerve cells.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Measure each dose with the supplied measuring device, not a household spoon. Take it regularly and do not stop suddenly, as this may make seizures worse. If a dose is missed, follow the prescriber’s instructions.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, weakness, nausea and reduced appetite may occur. Irritability, agitation or other mood and behaviour changes can also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or any history of mood or behaviour problems. Avoid driving or operating machinery until the effect is known. Seek medical help for severe rash, swelling or breathing difficulty, or new or worsening depression, aggression, unusual behaviour or thoughts of self-harm. Medical advice is needed before stopping treatment.

What is it used for?
Levosulpiride oral solution is used for certain digestive problems such as indigestion, delayed stomach emptying, reflux-related symptoms, and nausea or vomiting. It may help relieve symptoms such as bloating, early fullness and upper abdominal discomfort when these are related to slow stomach movement.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine D2 receptors and helps improve movement of the stomach and upper digestive tract. This can support stomach emptying and reduce some nausea-related symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth only as prescribed by a doctor. Measure the liquid with an appropriate measuring device and follow the prescribed timing and duration. Do not take more or use it for longer than directed.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, headache, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea or constipation. Increased prolactin levels may cause breast tenderness, unexpected milk production or menstrual changes.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice. Avoid driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy, and avoid alcohol. Tell the doctor about Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, a history of abnormal involuntary movements, gastrointestinal bleeding or blockage, or hormone-sensitive conditions. Seek medical help for severe muscle stiffness, unusual movements, fainting, or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
L-Alanyl L-Glutamine is used as a source of glutamine and alanine in intravenous nutrition, especially when a person cannot meet nutritional needs through normal eating or requires additional nutritional support. It is used under medical supervision as part of a complete nutrition regimen.

How does it work?
It supplies glutamine and alanine, amino acids needed for protein production and normal metabolism. Glutamine also supports the cells of the intestines and immune system.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by intravenous infusion by a healthcare professional, usually after dilution and as part of parenteral nutrition. The dose and duration depend on nutritional needs and kidney and liver function; follow the prescribed hospital regimen.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, fever, chills, headache, and changes in liver function tests may occur. Irritation or inflammation of the vein can occur at the infusion site.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Kidney or liver problems, metabolic acidosis, or abnormal fluid and electrolyte levels require careful assessment and monitoring. Blood glucose, electrolytes, liver function, and kidney function may be monitored during treatment. Seek medical attention for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, or other signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Magnesium sulphate is used to treat or prevent low magnesium levels. In hospitals, it may also be used for specific serious conditions, such as preventing seizures related to pregnancy, under close medical supervision.

How does it work?
It supplies magnesium, an essential mineral that supports normal nerve, muscle and heart function. In higher medically supervised doses, it can reduce excessive nerve and muscle activity.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a healthcare professional. The route, dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and product formulation. Injectable magnesium sulphate should be administered by a healthcare professional with appropriate monitoring.

Common side effects
Flushing, warmth, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, drowsiness and low blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about kidney disease, heart problems or any other medicines being used. Medical monitoring may be needed because excessive magnesium can cause muscle weakness, slow breathing, low blood pressure or an abnormal heartbeat. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, severe weakness or fainting.

What is it used for?
Mephentermine is used for the short-term treatment of low blood pressure, especially during or after anaesthesia and in other hospital situations.

How does it work?
It stimulates the sympathetic nervous system, causing blood vessels to narrow and helping the heart pump more strongly. This raises blood pressure.

How to take/use it
This medicine is usually given as an injection by a doctor or nurse in a hospital or clinic. The dose and frequency are decided by the healthcare professional based on the patient’s condition. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, nervousness, tremors, palpitations and a fast or irregular heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, an irregular heartbeat, thyroid disease, diabetes or glaucoma. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, particularly antidepressants or other medicines that raise blood pressure. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, severe headache, difficulty breathing or a very fast or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Micafungin is an antifungal medicine used to treat serious Candida (yeast) infections, including infections of the blood and other internal organs. It may also be used for certain oesophageal fungal infections and to help prevent fungal infections in some high-risk patients, as prescribed by a specialist.

How does it work?
It blocks the production of an essential part of the fungal cell wall. This weakens the fungal cells and stops the infection from growing.

How to take/use it
Micafungin is given as a slow intravenous infusion by a doctor or nurse, usually in a hospital or clinic. The dose and treatment length depend on the type and severity of the infection. It should not be self-administered.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to micafungin or similar antifungal medicines, and about liver disease or other medicines being used. Liver function and blood tests may be needed during treatment. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or a severe reaction during or after the infusion.

What is it used for?

It stops susceptible bacteria from making proteins needed for their growth and survival.

Take it only as prescribed and complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise. Swallow with plenty of water. Follow medical advice about separating it from antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium or magnesium.

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and increased sensitivity to sunlight may occur.

Precautions

Seek medical help for severe headache or vision changes, a serious skin rash, breathing difficulty, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid used under specialist supervision for certain conditions involving bone loss or reduced red blood cell production. Its exact use depends on the patient's condition and local prescribing guidance.

How does it work?
It has anabolic and androgenic effects, helping increase protein production and support tissue and bone formation. It may also stimulate red blood cell production.
