It is a long-acting synthetic medicine related to testosterone. It can increase protein production and support bone formation and red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as a deep injection by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the condition being treated. Do not self-inject or use it without medical supervision.

Common side effects
Acne, oily skin, swelling or fluid retention, changes in mood or sex drive, injection-site pain, and changes in cholesterol. Women may experience increased facial or body hair, a deeper voice, or menstrual changes.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about prostate or breast cancer, liver, kidney or heart disease, high cholesterol, or a history of blood clots. Long-term or high-dose use can cause serious hormonal and liver-related problems. Seek medical advice for yellowing of the skin, severe swelling, chest pain, breathing difficulty, or unusual voice or hair changes.

What is it used for?
Nitroglycerin is mainly used to prevent or relieve angina, which is chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart.

How does it work?
It widens blood vessels, helping reduce the heart’s workload and improve blood flow to the heart muscle.

How to take/use it
Use only in the form and dose prescribed. Follow the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions, as directions vary by formulation. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, flushing, nausea and low blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
It may cause dizziness or fainting, especially when standing up. Avoid alcohol and do not use with medicines for erectile dysfunction such as sildenafil, tadalafil or vardenafil, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent chest pain, fainting or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Noradrenaline is used in hospitals to raise dangerously low blood pressure during severe shock or other emergency conditions, helping maintain blood flow to vital organs.

How does it work?
It narrows blood vessels and stimulates the heart, which increases blood pressure and supports circulation.

How to take/use it
This is a concentrated injection for use only in a hospital or intensive-care setting. It must be diluted and given through a vein by trained healthcare professionals using continuous monitoring. It is not for self-use.

Common side effects
High blood pressure, fast or irregular heartbeat, palpitations, headache, anxiety, tremor, nausea and reduced blood flow to the hands and feet.

Precautions
It requires close monitoring of blood pressure, heart rhythm and the injection site. Leakage outside the vein can cause serious tissue damage. The treating team should be informed about heart disease, circulation problems, low blood volume or use of antidepressants and other medicines.

What is it used for?
Omeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD) and stomach or duodenal ulcers. It may also be used with antibiotics for certain stomach infections or to help prevent ulcers caused by some pain medicines, when prescribed.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of stomach acid by blocking acid-producing pumps in the stomach. This helps relieve heartburn and allows acid-related irritation or ulcers to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually before a meal. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it unless specifically instructed. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, gas, diarrhoea or constipation.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is difficulty swallowing, unexplained weight loss, repeated vomiting, vomiting blood or black stools. Seek medical advice for persistent or worsening symptoms. Long-term use should be monitored, as it may rarely affect vitamin B12 or magnesium levels and bone health. Tell a doctor about other medicines being used, especially blood thinners or medicines for HIV or fungal infections.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including those related to surgery, chemotherapy or radiotherapy.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals that can trigger nausea and vomiting in the brain and digestive system.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more or use it for longer than directed. Follow the specific instructions for orally disintegrating tablets, if applicable.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, dizziness, tiredness and flushing may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of heart rhythm problems, low potassium or magnesium levels, liver disease, or an allergy to ondansetron. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or serotonin levels. Seek medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic symptoms, or unusual muscle stiffness, agitation or fever.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including nausea and vomiting related to surgery, chemotherapy or radiotherapy, when prescribed.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals in the body that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The route and instructions depend on the formulation. Do not self-administer an injectable formulation; it should be given by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, dizziness and tiredness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any heart rhythm problems, low potassium or magnesium levels, liver disease, or allergies to ondansetron. Inform the doctor about all medicines being used, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or serotonin levels. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, breathing difficulty, swelling, or signs of a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used to help control nausea and vomiting and reduce excess stomach acid, including acid-related stomach discomfort.

How does it work?
Ondansetron blocks signals that trigger nausea and vomiting. Ranitidine reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the advised dose and timing, and do not take more than recommended. Do not stop or continue treatment longer than advised without medical guidance.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, constipation, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach discomfort and tiredness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of heart rhythm problems, liver disease, stomach or intestinal blockage, or low levels of potassium or magnesium. Inform the doctor about all other medicines being taken, especially medicines that can affect heart rhythm. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe allergic reaction or persistent vomiting.

What is it used for?
Pantoprazole 40 mg is used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD) and stomach or duodenal ulcers. It may also be used with antibiotics to help treat Helicobacter pylori infection, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It blocks a stomach enzyme that produces acid, thereby reducing acidity and allowing irritated food pipes or ulcers to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is generally taken before a meal, according to medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, vomiting, constipation or gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, allergies, or other medicines being used. Long-term or repeated use should be monitored by a doctor. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or persistent symptoms.

What is it used for?
Phytomenadione (vitamin K1) injection is used to prevent or treat bleeding caused by vitamin K deficiency and certain problems with blood clotting. It may also be used to help reverse the effect of some anticoagulant medicines, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Vitamin K1 helps the liver produce proteins needed for normal blood clotting.

How to take/use it
This is an injection and must be given by a healthcare professional by the prescribed route. Do not self-inject or use it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; flushing or changes in taste may occur. Serious allergic reactions are rare but can occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to vitamin K or previous reaction to an injection. Inform the doctor if taking anticoagulants such as warfarin, as blood-clotting tests and medicine doses may need monitoring. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or dizziness after the injection.

What is it used for?
Piperacillin with tazobactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, and bloodstream. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Piperacillin kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall. Tazobactam helps protect piperacillin from enzymes produced by some bacteria that can make antibiotics ineffective.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and length of treatment depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function, and medical advice. Complete the prescribed course unless the treating doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, constipation, headache, rash, and pain, redness or swelling at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to penicillin, cephalosporin or other antibiotics. The dose may need adjustment in kidney disease. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, a severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Tell the doctor about other medicines and any history of bleeding or seizures.

What is it used for?
Piperacillin and tazobactam injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin and soft tissues, and bloodstream. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Piperacillin kills bacteria by interfering with the formation of their protective cell wall. Tazobactam helps protect piperacillin from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against a wider range of bacteria.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. It should be used exactly as prescribed, and the treatment course should not be stopped early unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, headache, skin rash, and pain or redness at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor before use if there is an allergy to penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics, kidney disease, or a history of antibiotic-related severe diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Kidney function and blood tests may be checked during prolonged treatment.

What is it used for?
Piperacillin with tazobactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues, and other parts of the body. It is given when treatment with a broad-spectrum antibiotic is needed.

How does it work?
Piperacillin kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall. Tazobactam helps protect piperacillin from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work against a wider range of infections.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. It is usually used in a hospital or medical setting. The dose and duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function; complete the prescribed course unless the treating doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, constipation, headache, rash, itching, and pain or irritation at the injection site. Blood tests may show changes in blood counts or liver or kidney function.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, other beta-lactam antibiotics, or any of its ingredients. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, bleeding or blood disorders, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, or allergies. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe skin rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Medical monitoring may be needed during treatment, especially with prolonged use or kidney problems.

What is it used for?
Potassium chloride is used to prevent or treat low potassium levels in the blood (hypokalaemia), when potassium replacement is needed.

How does it work?
It replenishes potassium, an essential mineral needed for normal nerve, muscle and heart function.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the prescribed route and instructions carefully. If supplied as a concentrated solution for injection, it must be diluted and administered by a healthcare professional; never inject or use it undiluted. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort or diarrhoea may occur. Injection-site pain or irritation can occur when given by injection. Too much potassium can cause weakness, tingling or an irregular heartbeat and requires urgent medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, high potassium levels, heart disease or adrenal gland problems. Medical monitoring may be needed during treatment. Inform the doctor about medicines such as ACE inhibitors, ARBs, potassium-sparing diuretics or other potassium supplements, as they can increase potassium levels.

What is it used for?
Hydroxyprogesterone injection is a prescription hormonal medicine used by specialist doctors for progesterone support during pregnancy, including in selected cases to help reduce the risk of preterm birth. It may also be prescribed for certain menstrual or uterine bleeding problems, depending on the doctor's assessment.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone progesterone. Progesterone helps support the lining of the uterus and maintain hormonal support during pregnancy.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection by a healthcare professional. The dose and injection schedule depend on the reason for treatment, so it should be used only as prescribed. Do not self-inject or change the schedule without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain, swelling or itching at the injection site, headache, dizziness, nausea, tiredness, breast tenderness and changes in vaginal bleeding or menstrual pattern.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of blood clots, liver disease, hormone-sensitive cancer, unexplained vaginal bleeding, depression or allergies to hormonal medicines. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, severe headache, vision changes, one-sided weakness or painful swelling in a leg.

What is it used for?
Hydroxyprogesterone injection is used under specialist supervision to provide progesterone support during pregnancy in selected cases, such as reducing the risk of pregnancy loss or premature birth when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone progesterone. It helps support the lining of the uterus and maintain the hormonal conditions needed for pregnancy.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection by a doctor or nurse. Do not self-inject. The dose and injection schedule depend on the reason for treatment and must be decided by the prescribing doctor.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site, headache, nausea, tiredness, dizziness and breast tenderness may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, especially during pregnancy. Tell the doctor about any history of blood clots, liver disease, hormone-sensitive cancer, unexplained vaginal bleeding or allergies to progest medicines. Seek urgent medical help for severe headache, vision changes, chest pain, breathing difficulty, leg swelling or unusual vaginal bleeding.

What is it used for?
Citicoline is used as part of treatment and recovery support after stroke or head injury. It may also be prescribed for certain problems involving memory, thinking or other brain functions, depending on the doctor's assessment.

How does it work?
Citicoline helps provide building blocks for nerve-cell membranes and supports brain-cell function. It may also influence certain chemical messengers involved in brain activity.

How to take/use it
This 2 mL injection should be given only by a healthcare professional, by the prescribed route and schedule. Do not self-inject or change the dose without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, nausea, stomach upset and difficulty sleeping may occur. Tell a healthcare professional if these effects are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any allergy to citicoline, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all medicines being used. Extra care may be needed with medicines used for Parkinson’s disease. Seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction or any sudden worsening of neurological symptoms.

What is it used for?
Citicoline is used as part of treatment to support brain function and recovery in certain neurological conditions, including stroke-related brain injury, head injury and some cognitive problems. Its use depends on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
Citicoline helps support the structure of nerve-cell membranes and the production of certain brain chemicals involved in nerve signalling.

How to take/use it
This 4 mL injection should be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose, route and duration depend on the condition being treated and the prescribed medical advice. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Headache, dizziness, nausea, stomach discomfort, restlessness or difficulty sleeping may occur. Most side effects are mild, but medical advice should be sought if they are severe or persistent.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to citicoline or other medicines. Inform the doctor if pregnant or breastfeeding, or if taking levodopa or other medicines for Parkinson’s disease. Seek urgent medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Metoclopramide injection is used to prevent or treat nausea and vomiting. It may also be used to help the stomach empty more quickly in certain digestive conditions.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals in the vomiting centre of the brain and helps movement of food through the upper digestive system.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection, usually by a doctor or nurse. Use it only as prescribed and do not self-inject. The dose and treatment duration depend on the medical condition and response to treatment.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, restlessness, headache, dizziness, diarrhoea and weakness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is bowel blockage or bleeding, epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, kidney or liver problems, or a history of involuntary movements. Avoid driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy. Seek urgent medical help for unusual muscle spasms, uncontrolled movements, severe restlessness, confusion, fever or muscle stiffness.

What is it used for?
Promethazine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as itching, rashes and runny nose. It may also be used to prevent or treat nausea and vomiting, including motion sickness, when prescribed.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions. It also acts on areas of the brain that trigger nausea and vomiting, and can cause drowsiness.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The dose, route and duration depend on the condition being treated. Do not self-inject; if this is an injectable product, it should be administered by a trained healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision and constipation may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if drowsy or less alert. Use cautiously if there is asthma or another breathing problem, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, epilepsy or severe liver disease. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, extreme sleepiness, confusion, fainting or a severe allergic reaction. Keep away from young children unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Polymyxin B is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections caused by susceptible bacteria, especially some Gram-negative infections. The exact use depends on the prescribed formulation and route of administration.

How does it work?
It damages the outer membrane of susceptible bacteria, causing the bacteria to die.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. The dose, treatment duration and method of administration depend on the infection and formulation. Injectable forms must be given by a healthcare professional; do not self-administer.

Common side effects
Kidney problems, tingling or numbness, dizziness, muscle weakness, and allergic reactions may occur. Side effects can be serious, particularly with injectable treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, neuromuscular disorders, or any previous allergy to polymyxins. Kidney function may need monitoring during treatment. Seek urgent medical help for reduced urination, severe weakness, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or a widespread rash.

What is it used for?
Propofol is an intravenous medicine used by healthcare professionals to start and maintain general anaesthesia during surgery. It may also be used to provide sedation for certain medical procedures and, in specialist settings, for patients receiving intensive care.

How does it work?
Propofol slows activity in the brain by enhancing the effect of a natural calming chemical called GABA. This produces sleep and loss of awareness; it does not provide pain relief on its own.

How to take/use it
Propofol is given into a vein by an anaesthetist or other trained healthcare professional in a hospital or clinical setting. Breathing, blood pressure, heart rate and oxygen levels must be closely monitored during use.

Common side effects
Pain or discomfort at the injection site, low blood pressure, slow or shallow breathing, temporary pauses in breathing, nausea, vomiting, dizziness and drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
It must only be administered where equipment and trained staff are available to support breathing and circulation. Tell the doctor about allergies, breathing problems, heart or blood-pressure problems, liver or kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all medicines being used. Do not drive, drink alcohol or make important decisions until the effects have fully worn off and medical advice permits it.

What is it used for?
Propofol is an intravenous anaesthetic used in hospitals to induce and maintain general anaesthesia during surgery. It may also be used to provide sedation for certain medical procedures or for patients receiving intensive care.

How does it work?
It acts on the brain to reduce activity and produce sleep-like unconsciousness and sedation. It also reduces awareness of pain and other sensations during anaesthesia.

How to take/use it
Propofol is given into a vein by a trained anaesthetist or other qualified healthcare professional. The dose is individually adjusted, and breathing, blood pressure, heart rate and oxygen levels must be closely monitored. It must not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Pain or burning at the injection site, low blood pressure, slowed or stopped breathing, slow heartbeat, nausea, vomiting, dizziness and confusion on waking.

Precautions
It should only be used where airway and breathing support equipment and trained medical staff are available. Extra care is needed in people with breathing or heart problems, low blood pressure, or allergies to propofol or its ingredients. Seek urgent medical attention for severe breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, or loss of consciousness that does not improve after the procedure.

What is it used for?
Cefotaxime injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood, bones and joints, and brain coverings. It is also used for some infections around surgery, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function, age and other medical factors. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, rash and changes in liver test results may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it without medical supervision. Tell the doctor about any allergy to cefotaxime, cephalosporins, penicillins or other antibiotics, and about kidney disease. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Contact a doctor if severe or persistent diarrhoea develops during or after treatment.

What is it used for?
Cefotaxime injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood, bones and joints, and brain coverings. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and duration depend on the type and severity of the infection. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise.

Pain or inflammation at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash and fever may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to cefotaxime, other cephalosporin or penicillin antibiotics, or a history of kidney or liver problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Cefotaxime injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin, abdomen, blood and other parts of the body. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, age and kidney function. Do not self-inject or stop treatment early unless advised by the healthcare professional.

Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea or vomiting; and skin rash.

What is it used for?
Cefotaxime with sulbactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin and soft tissues, or blood, when sensitive bacteria are involved. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefotaxime kills bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps cefotaxime work against bacteria that can resist some antibiotics.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Use it only as prescribed and complete the recommended course unless advised otherwise.

Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash or itching, and changes in liver test results may occur.

Do not use it without medical advice if there has been a serious allergy to cefotaxime, other cephalosporins, penicillins or related antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney disease, liver disease, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, or pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Octreotide is used to control excess growth hormone in acromegaly. It is also used to reduce severe diarrhoea and flushing caused by some hormone-producing tumours, and may be used in certain cases of bleeding from enlarged veins in the food pipe.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone somatostatin and reduces the release of several hormones and other substances in the body, including growth hormone and substances that increase intestinal secretions.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection under medical supervision or exactly as prescribed. The route, dose and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Injection-site pain, diarrhoea, abdominal pain or discomfort, nausea, vomiting, bloating, constipation, headache, dizziness, and gallstones or other gallbladder problems. Blood sugar changes and a slow heartbeat may also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is diabetes, gallbladder disease, thyroid problems, heart rhythm or heart-rate problems, or liver disease. What is it used for?

Octreotide acts like the natural hormone somatostatin. It reduces the release of growth hormone and several other hormones that can cause diarrhoea, flushing or other symptoms.

What is it used for?
Iohexol is a contrast medium used during certain X-rays, CT scans, angiograms and other imaging tests. It helps blood vessels, organs or body tissues show up more clearly on the images. It is used for diagnosis, not to treat a disease.

Iohexol contains iodine, which absorbs X-rays. This creates greater contrast between different tissues and makes the area being examined easier to see.

Iohexol is given by injection or through another route by a trained healthcare professional before or during the imaging test. It must not be self-administered. Follow the instructions provided by the radiology team, including any advice about fluids or eating and drinking.

A temporary warm or flushed feeling, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, or pain and discomfort at the injection site may occur. Most reactions are mild and short-lasting.

Precautions
Tell the doctor or radiology team about any previous reaction to contrast media, kidney problems, thyroid disease, asthma, allergies, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Inform them about all medicines being taken, especially medicines for diabetes or kidney-related conditions. Seek immediate medical help for difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, fainting, or other signs of a serious allergic reaction.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, previous allergy to ranitidine, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being used. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, confusion or an irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Carboxymethylcellulose eye drops are used to relieve dryness, irritation, burning and discomfort caused by dry eyes. They act as artificial tears.

How does it work?
It forms a lubricating layer over the surface of the eye, helping keep the eyes moist and reducing irritation.

How to take/use it
Use in the eyes exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before use and do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface. Do not use if the solution is cloudy or the seal is damaged.

Common side effects
Temporary blurred vision, mild stinging, burning or eye irritation may occur after use.

Precautions
Seek medical advice if eye pain, marked redness, discharge or vision changes occur, or if symptoms do not improve. People who wear contact lenses should check the product instructions before use. Stop using it and seek advice if irritation is severe or persistent.

What is it used for?
Teicoplanin is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections caused by Gram-positive bacteria, including infections of the skin and soft tissues, bones and joints, lungs, blood, and heart valves. It may also be used when infections are caused by bacteria such as MRSA, as decided by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from multiplying.

How to take/use it
Teicoplanin is given as an injection or infusion by a doctor or nurse, usually in a hospital or clinic. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function, and response to treatment. Complete the prescribed course and do not self-administer it.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; rash or itching; nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea; and headache. Changes in blood tests may also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing problems, or previous allergy to teicoplanin, vancomycin or similar antibiotics. Kidney function, blood counts, liver function and sometimes hearing may need monitoring, especially during prolonged treatment or in people with kidney problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, hearing changes, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Teicoplanin is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by certain Gram-positive bacteria, including infections of the blood, heart valves, bones, joints, skin and soft tissues. It is usually used in hospitals or under specialist medical supervision.

How does it work?
It prevents susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall, which stops them from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Teicoplanin is given as an injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and response to treatment. Complete the prescribed course unless the treating doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain or inflammation at the injection site, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, rash, itching and fever may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to teicoplanin or similar antibiotics, kidney problems, hearing problems or previous antibiotic-related reactions. Kidney function, blood counts and sometimes hearing may need monitoring, especially during prolonged treatment or in people with kidney problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, blistering or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Terlipressin is used in hospitals to treat serious complications of advanced liver disease, especially hepatorenal syndrome, a condition in which kidney function worsens. It may also be used to help control bleeding from enlarged veins in the food pipe (oesophageal varices).

How does it work?
It acts like vasopressin and narrows certain blood vessels, especially those supplying the digestive organs. This can increase blood pressure and improve blood flow to the kidneys, while also helping reduce bleeding from varices.

How to take/use it
Terlipressin is given by injection or infusion by a doctor or trained healthcare professional, usually in a hospital. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and response to treatment. It requires close monitoring.

Common side effects
Abdominal cramps, diarrhoea, headache, pale skin, increased blood pressure, slow or irregular heartbeat, low sodium levels, and breathing difficulty due to fluid in the lungs may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart or blood-vessel disease, high blood pressure, irregular heartbeat, breathing problems, kidney problems, or pregnancy. Blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen levels, fluid balance, and blood sodium levels may need monitoring. Seek urgent medical attention for chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, fainting, or a bluish or unusually pale appearance.

What is it used for?
Thiamine (vitamin B1) injection is used to prevent or treat vitamin B1 deficiency. It may be used when deficiency is severe or when thiamine cannot be taken or absorbed properly by mouth.

How does it work?
Thiamine is converted into an active form that helps the body produce energy from carbohydrates and supports normal nerve and heart function.

How to take/use it
This injection should be given by a healthcare professional. The dose, route and treatment duration depend on the severity of deficiency and the individual's medical condition.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or discomfort at the injection site; nausea or sweating may occur. Allergic reactions are uncommon but can be serious.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about any previous allergy to thiamine or this medicine. It should be administered under medical supervision because serious allergic reactions can rarely occur. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, widespread rash or severe dizziness after the injection.

What is it used for?
Thiopentone injection is mainly used in hospitals to induce general anaesthesia before surgery or other procedures. It may also be used by specialists to control certain severe seizures.

How does it work?
It is a fast-acting barbiturate that slows activity in the brain, causing unconsciousness and reducing brain activity.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given into a vein only by a trained doctor or anaesthetist. Breathing, blood pressure and heart rate must be closely monitored during and after use. It must not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, slow or shallow breathing, low blood pressure, nausea or vomiting, coughing, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about breathing problems, severe low blood pressure, liver or kidney disease, allergies, or a history of porphyria. Emergency medical support must be available because it can cause serious breathing or heart-related problems, allergic reactions, or prolonged unconsciousness.

What is it used for?
Ticarcillin with clavulanic acid is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin and soft tissues, bones or joints, and bloodstream, when caused by susceptible bacteria.

How does it work?
Ticarcillin kills bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid blocks certain bacterial enzymes that can otherwise make ticarcillin ineffective.

How to take/use it
This medicine is usually given into a vein by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function, and medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, skin rash, itching, and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, ticarcillin, clavulanic acid, or related antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, bleeding problems, or previous antibiotic-associated diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or unusual bleeding.

What is it used for?
Tigecycline is an injectable antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, including complicated skin and soft-tissue infections, complicated infections inside the abdomen, and some community-acquired bacterial pneumonias. It is used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Tigecycline is given as an intravenous infusion by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the infection and individual health factors. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, headache, and changes in liver enzyme levels.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to tigecycline or other tetracycline antibiotics, liver disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. It is generally avoided in children under 8 years unless specifically advised by a specialist because it may affect teeth and bone development. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, severe abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, rash, swelling, or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Tranexamic acid is used to reduce or control excessive bleeding. It may be prescribed for heavy menstrual bleeding or bleeding related to certain medical procedures, injuries or bleeding conditions.

How does it work?
It helps prevent blood clots from breaking down too quickly, which helps control bleeding.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor, with or without food, and swallow it with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and headache may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of blood clots, kidney disease, vision problems or irregular bleeding. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, coughing blood, leg swelling or pain, sudden weakness, or vision changes.

What is it used for?
Ulinastatin is a prescription injectable medicine used mainly in hospitals to help manage acute pancreatitis and certain severe inflammatory conditions, including severe sepsis, under specialist supervision.

How does it work?
It blocks enzymes called proteases, such as trypsin, that can contribute to tissue injury and inflammation. This may help reduce excessive inflammation in severe illness.

How to take/use it
It is given by injection into a vein by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition and response to treatment; do not self-administer it.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, injection-site discomfort, skin rash or itching, and changes in liver-test results may occur. Serious allergic reactions are uncommon but require urgent medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to ulinastatin or similar medicines, and about pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other medical conditions. It should be administered under medical supervision. Seek immediate help for breathing difficulty, facial or throat swelling, severe rash, dizziness, or fainting.

What is it used for?
Urokinase is used in hospitals to dissolve dangerous blood clots in blood vessels, such as clots causing pulmonary embolism or deep vein thrombosis. It may also be used to clear certain blocked medical catheters.

How does it work?
It activates plasminogen, a natural substance in the body, to form plasmin. Plasmin breaks down the fibrin framework of blood clots.

How to take/use it
This injection is given by a doctor or nurse in a hospital, usually into a vein or through a medical catheter. The dose and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated and must be decided by the treating doctor.

Common side effects
Bleeding, bruising, bleeding from injection sites, low blood pressure, fever, nausea and allergic reactions may occur.

Precautions
Urokinase can cause serious bleeding. Tell the doctor about any bleeding disorder, recent surgery or injury, previous stroke, uncontrolled high blood pressure, stomach ulcer or use of blood-thinning medicines. Seek immediate medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, severe headache, weakness, difficulty breathing or swelling of the face or throat.

What is it used for?
Vecuronium bromide injection is used during general anaesthesia to relax the muscles. It helps doctors place a breathing tube and keeps muscles relaxed during surgery or assisted breathing.

How does it work?
It temporarily blocks nerve signals to the skeletal muscles, causing muscle relaxation and paralysis. It does not provide pain relief or make a person unconscious.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection into a vein by an anaesthetist or other trained healthcare professional in a hospital. Breathing, oxygen levels and muscle function must be closely monitored, and breathing support must be available until its effects wear off.

Common side effects
Prolonged muscle weakness or paralysis, low blood pressure, flushing, changes in heart rate, breathing difficulty after the procedure, and allergic reactions may occur.

Precautions
It must only be used by trained healthcare professionals with equipment for assisted breathing and resuscitation. Tell the doctor about any previous reaction to muscle relaxants, neuromuscular disorders, liver or kidney problems, and all medicines being used. The patient must not try to move, eat or drink until muscle strength and swallowing have fully recovered.

What is it used for?
Vancomycin is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by certain bacteria, including some resistant infections. When given by mouth, it is used mainly for certain bacterial infections of the intestine, such as Clostridioides difficile infection.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from multiplying.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. The route depends on the formulation: injectable vancomycin is usually given into a vein by a healthcare professional, while oral vancomycin should be taken exactly as directed. Do not change the dose or stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, pain at the injection site, and redness, flushing or itching during infusion may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, hearing problems, previous reactions to vancomycin, or use of other medicines that may affect the kidneys or hearing. Medical monitoring may be needed during treatment. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, severe rash, swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, or reduced urination.

What is it used for?
Vancomycin is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by certain bacteria, including resistant bacterial infections. When taken by mouth, it is mainly used for certain infections of the intestine, such as Clostridioides difficile infection. The route of use depends on the product and prescription.

How does it work?
Vancomycin kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. Injectable vancomycin must be given by a healthcare professional. Oral vancomycin should be taken exactly as directed and should not be shared or stopped early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, or diarrhoea may occur. Injectable vancomycin can cause redness, flushing, itching, or a drop in blood pressure if given too quickly. Kidney problems and hearing problems are important but less common risks.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to vancomycin, kidney disease, hearing problems, or use of other medicines that may affect the kidneys or hearing. Medical monitoring may be needed during treatment. Seek urgent medical help for severe rash, breathing difficulty, severe or persistent diarrhoea, reduced urination, or ringing in the ears.

What is it used for?
Voriconazole is a prescription antifungal medicine used to treat serious fungal infections, including invasive aspergillosis and certain serious Candida and other fungal infections.

How does it work?
It blocks the production of ergosterol, an important part of the fungal cell membrane. This stops the fungi from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course. Voriconazole tablets are usually taken at least 1 hour before or 1 hour after food. Swallow the tablet whole and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Changes in vision or increased sensitivity to light, headache, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, rash, and changes in liver function tests.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, kidney disease, heart rhythm problems, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Voriconazole has many important medicine interactions, so provide a complete list of all medicines and supplements being taken. Avoid direct sunlight and use sun protection, as it can increase sensitivity to sunlight. Seek medical help for severe rash, breathing difficulty, yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe visual changes, or an irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone is an antibiotic injection used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin, abdomen, blood, bones and joints. It may also be used for meningitis and other infections when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming a protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Ceftriaxone is given as an injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, age and other health conditions. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; rash; and changes in liver test results.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillins or other cephalosporin antibiotics, and about liver, kidney or gallbladder problems. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or a severe skin rash. This medicine should be used in newborns only under specialist medical advice.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone injection is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as certain infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood, bones and joints, or brain. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, age, and other health conditions. Do not self-inject or stop treatment early unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Pain, swelling or redness at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; and skin rash.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, other cephalosporin antibiotics, or serious penicillin allergy. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. The doctor should be informed about liver or kidney problems and all other medicines being used. Ceftriaxone must be used carefully in newborns and should not be mixed with calcium-containing intravenous solutions in newborns.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall, which stops the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone with sulbactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone stops susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall. Sulbactam blocks certain bacterial enzymes that can make antibiotics ineffective, helping ceftriaxone work against some resistant bacteria.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a doctor or nurse as an injection into a vein or muscle. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and the patient's health. Complete the prescribed course and do not self-administer it.

Pain or discomfort at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillins, cephalosporins, or other antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver problems and any medicines being taken. This injection must be prepared and administered by healthcare professionals; special precautions are needed in newborns and with calcium-containing intravenous solutions.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone with sulbactam is a prescription antibiotic injection used to treat a range of bacterial infections. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps ceftriaxone work against certain bacteria that can resist some antibiotics.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, so it should be used only as prescribed. Complete the prescribed course unless advised otherwise by a healthcare professional.

Inform the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, a history of antibiotic-associated diarrhoea, or pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone with sulbactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills bacteria by preventing them from forming a protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps ceftriaxone work against some bacteria that can resist certain antibiotics.

This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone with tazobactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood and other body tissues, when prescribed by a doctor.

Ceftriaxone kills bacteria by stopping them from building their protective cell wall. Tazobactam helps protect ceftriaxone from certain enzymes made by bacteria, allowing it to work against some resistant bacteria.

What is it used for?
Ceftazidime and avibactam is an injectable antibiotic used in hospitals to treat serious bacterial infections, especially complicated urinary tract infections, complicated abdominal infections, hospital-acquired or ventilator-associated pneumonia, and certain infections caused by resistant Gram-negative bacteria.

Ceftazidime stops bacteria from building their protective cell wall. Avibactam blocks some bacterial enzymes that can otherwise break down ceftazidime, helping the antibiotic work against certain resistant bacteria.

This medicine is given into a vein by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. It should be used only as prescribed and the full treatment course should be completed.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftazidime, other cephalosporins, penicillins or other beta-lactam antibiotics. The dose may need adjustment in kidney disease. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, confusion or seizures. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

Ceftazidime is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin, abdomen, blood and brain. It may also be used for infections caused by certain bacteria such as Pseudomonas.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol Infusion is used for short-term relief of moderate pain and reduction of fever, especially when medicine cannot be taken by mouth or when an intravenous medicine is needed.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the body that contribute to pain and fever. It mainly acts in the brain and does not significantly reduce inflammation.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a healthcare professional. The prescribed amount and treatment duration depend on the patient's condition. Do not use other medicines containing paracetamol unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, and discomfort at the infusion site may occur. Serious allergic reactions and liver problems are uncommon but require urgent medical attention.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about liver disease, kidney problems, dehydration, poor nutrition, regular alcohol use, or allergy to paracetamol. Do not exceed the prescribed amount, as overdose can cause serious liver damage. Seek urgent help for a rash, swelling, breathing difficulty, severe weakness, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of painful muscle and joint conditions associated with inflammation and muscle spasms.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac and paracetamol help reduce pain and inflammation. Chlorzoxazone acts on the central nervous system to help relax painful muscle spasms.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more than the prescribed amount, or combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol or aceclofenac unless advised by a doctor. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving if affected.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness or drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart problems, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness and the risk of liver damage. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless specifically prescribed. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Acyclovir 5% ointment is used to treat herpes simplex infections of the skin, including cold sores and genital herpes sores.

How does it work?
It is an antiviral medicine that blocks the ability of the herpes virus to multiply, helping the sores heal.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin as directed by a doctor or the product label. Wash hands before and after use. Avoid applying it to the eyes, inside the mouth, or other areas unless specifically advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site.

Precautions
For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes. Do not pick or touch the sores unnecessarily, and wash hands regularly to reduce spreading the infection. Acyclovir does not remove the virus from the body or reliably prevent transmission. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens, does not improve, or if severe irritation or an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth. It does not work against viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from making a protective cell wall, which stops the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at evenly spaced times, with water. Complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. Do not take leftover antibiotics or share this medicine with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to amoxycillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, a severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin is an antibiotic used to treat infections caused by susceptible bacteria, such as certain infections of the ear, throat, chest, urinary tract and skin. It does not work for viral infections such as common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by interfering with the formation of their protective cell wall, helping to clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach upset. Do not share antibiotics or use leftover medicine.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a previous serious allergy to amoxycillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or a history of antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, a severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin is an antibiotic used to treat infections caused by bacteria, such as certain infections of the ear, throat, chest, skin, urinary tract and teeth. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the capsule with water. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a previous serious allergy to amoxycillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Seek medical help for difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, a severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Inform the doctor about kidney problems, pregnancy, breastfeeding or any other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, as prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall, helping to clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to amoxycillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related allergic reactions.

What is it used for?
Amoxicillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, sinuses, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxicillin kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps prevent certain bacteria from breaking down amoxicillin, making the antibiotic effective against some resistant bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with a meal to reduce stomach upset. Swallow with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share antibiotics or use leftover medicine.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take this medicine if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxicillin, clavulanic acid or related antibiotics. Inform the doctor about kidney or liver disease and any previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanate is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, sinuses, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanate helps amoxycillin remain effective against bacteria that can otherwise break it down.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed and follow the instructions on the label. Take each dose at the recommended time and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Taking it at the start of a meal may help reduce stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, other beta-lactam antibiotics or any of its ingredients. Tell the doctor about previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, kidney disease, glandular fever, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe skin rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Antibiotics should be used only when prescribed.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, ears, airways, urinary tract and other areas, when caused by bacteria sensitive to it. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not share this medicine or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, vomiting and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor if there is an allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or penicillin-type antibiotics, or if there is kidney disease. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, bloody stools, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, airways, urinary tract and other areas, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Disperse the tablet in water as directed on the pack or by the pharmacist, and take it immediately after it has dispersed. Do not share or reuse leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion and vomiting may occur. Mild rash or headache can also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or penicillin, or if there is kidney disease. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea, especially if it contains blood. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can lead to resistance.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, ears, airways and urinary tract. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion and headache. Mild skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to cefixime, penicillin or other cephalosporin antibiotics, kidney problems, or a history of severe diarrhoea after antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Used to treat bacterial infections caused by bacteria susceptible to cefixime and clavulanate. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefixime stops bacteria from building their protective cell wall. Potassium clavulanate blocks certain enzymes made by bacteria that can make them resistant to cefixime.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Follow the product label or prescriber's instructions, and do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion and headache. Skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Tell the prescriber about any allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporins or penicillin-type antibiotics, and about kidney or liver problems. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, a severe rash, persistent or bloody diarrhoea, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat certain bacterial infections when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
Cefixime damages the bacterial cell wall. Ofloxacin stops bacteria from copying their genetic material, helping to kill the bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Do not take antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc at the same time; follow the prescribed time gap. Do not share or reuse leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, indigestion, headache, dizziness and skin rash.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to penicillin, cephalosporins or quinolone antibiotics, kidney disease, seizures, tendon problems, heart rhythm problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for breathing difficulty, severe or persistent diarrhoea, tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe rash, or unusual palpitations. Use in children and older adults only when specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Metronidazole injection is used to treat serious infections caused by certain anaerobic bacteria and some parasites, including certain intestinal and genital infections. It may also be used to prevent certain infections around surgery when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It enters susceptible bacteria and parasites and damages their genetic material, stopping them from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection and should be decided by the treating doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, metallic taste and pain or irritation at the injection site.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose. Tell the doctor if there is liver disease, a history of seizures or nerve problems, or an allergy to metronidazole. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially warfarin. Seek medical help for severe rash, numbness or tingling, seizures, confusion, or severe diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, chest, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not skip doses or stop treatment early unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, cephalosporins or other penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime axetil is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, sinuses, ears, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and preferably after food, as this helps the body absorb it. Swallow the tablet whole with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, cephalosporins or other beta-lactam antibiotics unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin reaction. Contact a doctor if diarrhoea is severe, persistent or contains blood, as this may occur during or after antibiotic treatment. Tell the doctor about kidney problems and any medicines being taken, especially antacids or medicines that reduce stomach acid.

What is it used for?

How does it work?

How to take/use it
