What is it used for?
Bilastine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, usually with water. It should be taken on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after food or fruit juice. Do not take more than directed.

Common side effects
Headache, drowsiness, dizziness, tiredness and nausea may occur.

Precautions
Some people may feel drowsy or dizzy; avoid driving or operating machinery if affected. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there are kidney problems or other medicines being taken. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

What is it used for?
Bisacodyl 5 mg is a stimulant laxative used for short-term relief of occasional constipation. It may also be used to empty the bowel before certain medical procedures, when directed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It stimulates movement of the large intestine and helps increase water in the stool, making it easier to pass.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not chew or crush it. Do not use it for longer than recommended. Avoid taking it at the same time as milk or antacids.

Common side effects
Abdominal cramps, stomach discomfort, nausea and diarrhoea.

Precautions
Do not use it if there is severe abdominal pain, suspected intestinal blockage, severe dehydration, nausea or vomiting unless advised by a healthcare professional. Drink adequate fluids. Prolonged or frequent use may cause dehydration or changes in body salts. Seek medical advice if constipation continues, symptoms worsen, or there is blood in the stool.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone injection is an antibiotic used to treat a wide range of serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood, bones or joints. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall, which stops the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection. Use it only as prescribed and complete the recommended course.

Common side effects
Pain or swelling at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, other cephalosporins or penicillin antibiotics, and about kidney, liver or gallbladder problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or severe or bloody diarrhoea. It should be used in newborns and during pregnancy or breastfeeding only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone with sulbactam is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood and other body tissues, when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as cold or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps ceftriaxone work against certain bacteria that can otherwise resist some antibiotics.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and duration depend on the type and severity of infection and should be followed exactly as prescribed. Do not stop treatment early unless advised by the doctor.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, rash and headache may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillins, cephalosporins or other antibiotics, and about liver, kidney or gallbladder problems. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use only for a confirmed or strongly suspected bacterial infection and only as prescribed.

What is it used for?
This prescription injection is used to treat serious bacterial infections. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Tazobactam helps protect ceftriaxone from enzymes made by some bacteria, allowing it to work better.

Diarrhoea, nausea, rash, and pain or discomfort at the injection site may occur.

Use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in newborn babies only under medical supervision.

What is it used for?
Clobetasol propionate cream is a very strong steroid used for short-term treatment of severe, inflamed and itchy skin conditions such as eczema, dermatitis and psoriasis, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces inflammation, redness, swelling and itching by suppressing overactive immune reactions in the skin.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Use it only on the skin, wash hands after applying, and avoid contact with the eyes. Do not use it for longer or on larger areas than advised. Do not cover the treated area with a tight dressing unless instructed.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, itching, dryness or irritation at the application site. Prolonged or excessive use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks, changes in skin colour, or small visible blood vessels.

Precautions
Do not use on the face, groin, underarms, broken skin or infected skin unless specifically advised. Avoid use in children unless prescribed. Seek medical advice if the condition worsens, shows signs of infection, or does not improve. Stop and seek urgent help for severe irritation or an allergic reaction.

For external use only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed by the doctor. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not cover the area with a bandage unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, irritation, dryness or redness at the application site. Prolonged or inappropriate use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks, colour changes or increased hair growth.

Precautions
Use only on the affected skin and for the prescribed period. Avoid the eyes, mouth, face, broken skin and sensitive skin-fold areas unless specifically advised. Do not use for untreated viral skin infections or without medical advice. Stop using it and seek medical help if the rash worsens, spreads, or signs of a serious allergic reaction occur. Neomycin may cause skin allergy in some people.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to reduce redness, swelling, itching and thick, scaly patches in inflammatory skin conditions such as psoriasis and eczema, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Clobetasol is a strong corticosteroid that reduces skin inflammation and itching. Salicylic acid helps soften and remove thick, scaly skin so the medicine can work more effectively.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Wash hands after applying unless the hands are being treated. Do not cover the area with a bandage or dressing unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, itching, irritation, dryness or redness at the application site. Prolonged or excessive use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour.

Precautions
Use only on the affected skin and only for the period advised by a doctor. Avoid using it on the face, groin, underarms, skin folds, broken skin or infected skin unless specifically prescribed. Do not use for untreated fungal, bacterial or viral skin infections. Seek medical advice if the condition worsens, spreads or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch and other fungal rashes.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which prevents their growth and clears the infection.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after use. For external use only; avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to clotrimazole or any ingredient in the cream. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Consult a healthcare professional if the infection worsens or does not improve as expected.

How does it work?

Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after use. For external use only; avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Precautions

What is it used for?
This gel is used to treat acne, including pimples, blackheads and whiteheads.

How does it work?
Adapalene helps prevent blocked pores and reduces acne-related inflammation. Clindamycin is an antibiotic that helps reduce acne-causing bacteria and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry acne-affected skin and wash hands after use. Avoid contact with the eyes, lips, inside of the nose and other sensitive areas. Do not apply to cuts, broken or sunburned skin.

Common side effects
Dryness, redness, peeling, itching, burning or stinging at the application site. Skin may become more sensitive to sunlight.

Precautions
Use sunscreen and limit exposure to strong sunlight. Avoid using other irritating skin products unless advised by a healthcare professional. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe skin irritation or persistent, severe diarrhoea develops.

What is it used for?
Methylcobalamin injection is used to prevent or treat vitamin B12 deficiency. Vitamin B12 is important for healthy red blood cells and normal nerve function.

How does it work?
It supplies an active form of vitamin B12 that helps the body make red blood cells and supports the normal function of nerves.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection, usually by a healthcare professional. The dose, injection route and treatment schedule should be decided by the prescriber.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; nausea or headache may occur.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about any allergy to methylcobalamin, vitamin B12 or cobalt. Do not self-inject unless properly instructed. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash after the injection.

What is it used for?
Methylcobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 used to treat or prevent vitamin B12 deficiency. Vitamin B12 is important for healthy red blood cells and normal nerve function.

How does it work?
It supplies vitamin B12 needed for the formation of red blood cells and the maintenance of healthy nerves.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection, usually by a doctor or other healthcare professional. Use it only as prescribed and do not self-inject unless properly instructed.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; nausea, headache or skin rash.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about any allergy to vitamin B12, methylcobalamin or cobalt. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash after the injection.

What is it used for?
Deflazacort is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactivity of the immune system. It may be prescribed for certain inflammatory, allergic or autoimmune conditions, depending on the doctor's diagnosis.

How does it work?
It reduces the release of substances that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Take it with food if it causes stomach discomfort. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, especially after prolonged use, unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Increased appetite, indigestion, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, fluid retention and increased blood sugar may occur. The risk of side effects is higher with larger doses or longer treatment.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, liver or kidney problems, or any current infection. Deflazacort can reduce resistance to infection; avoid close contact with contagious illnesses and check with a doctor before receiving vaccines. Seek medical advice for signs of infection or severe mood changes. Long-term treatment should be medically monitored.

What is it used for?
Dexamethasone injection is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and control overactive allergic or immune reactions in conditions where an injectable treatment is needed. The specific reason for use depends on the patient's condition and must be decided by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and allergic or immune reactions.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose, frequency and treatment duration depend on the condition being treated. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Increased blood sugar, indigestion, mood or sleep changes, increased appetite, fluid retention and pain at the injection site may occur. It can also increase the risk of infections.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health problems or any current infection. Dexamethasone may hide signs of infection and can interact with other medicines. Seek medical help for severe allergic reactions, unusual weakness, vision changes or signs of infection.

What is it used for?
Dydrogesterone is a progesterone-like medicine used to treat conditions caused by low progesterone, such as irregular or painful periods, endometriosis and some menstrual problems. It may also be prescribed to support pregnancy or as part of hormone replacement treatment, only when directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It acts similarly to the natural hormone progesterone. This helps regulate the menstrual cycle and supports the lining of the uterus.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, breast tenderness, abdominal discomfort, spotting or changes in menstrual bleeding, and mood changes may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about liver disease, unexplained vaginal bleeding, depression, or any history of hormone-sensitive conditions. Seek medical advice for heavy or unusual bleeding, severe abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or signs of an allergic reaction. During pregnancy or breastfeeding, use only if prescribed.

What is it used for?
Amikacin injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, especially infections caused by certain Gram-negative bacteria. It is generally used in hospitals or under close medical supervision.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from growing.

How to take/use it
Amikacin injection is given into a vein or muscle by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration are decided by the doctor based on the infection, kidney function and body weight. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea and vomiting may occur. This medicine can also cause kidney problems, hearing loss, ringing in the ears or balance problems.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Inform the doctor about all medicines being used, especially other medicines that may affect the kidneys or hearing. Kidney function and, when needed, hearing should be monitored during treatment. Seek urgent medical help for reduced urination, swelling, severe dizziness, ringing in the ears or hearing changes.

What is it used for?
Amikacin injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including certain infections of the lungs, blood, abdomen, urinary tract and other parts of the body. It is usually used when other antibiotics may not be suitable or effective.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills the bacteria or prevents their growth.

How to take/use it
Amikacin is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a healthcare professional. The dose and treatment duration depend on the infection, kidney function, age and body weight. Do not self-inject or stop treatment early unless advised by the doctor.

Common side effects
Pain at the injection site, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and headache may occur. Serious effects can include kidney problems, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, dizziness or balance problems.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, or muscle-weakness disorders. Kidney function and, when needed, hearing should be monitored during treatment. Inform the doctor about all medicines being used, especially other antibiotics or medicines that may affect the kidneys or hearing. Seek medical help promptly for reduced urination, swelling, ringing in the ears, hearing changes, severe dizziness or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Esomeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be used to help heal acid-related irritation of the food pipe and stomach ulcers, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It blocks the acid-producing pump in the stomach, reducing the amount of acid released. This helps relieve acid reflux symptoms and allows irritated tissues to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by the doctor or on the label. It is usually taken before food. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not stop long-term treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, constipation and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies, liver problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Long-term use may rarely affect magnesium or vitamin B12 levels and may increase the risk of some infections or bone fractures. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or persistent symptoms.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux (GERD) symptoms. It may also help with associated nausea, vomiting or stomach fullness.

How does it work?
Esomeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps improve movement of the upper digestive tract and may reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, constipation, gas or dry mouth may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart rhythm problems, heart disease, liver disease, or low potassium or magnesium levels. Domperidone can rarely cause serious heart-rhythm problems, especially with higher doses or certain medicines. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, particularly those affecting heart rhythm. Seek medical help for fainting, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe or persistent diarrhoea, vomiting blood or black stools.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux symptoms. It may also help indigestion, bloating or discomfort related to slow movement of food through the stomach, when prescribed.

How does it work?
Esomeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Levosulpride helps improve movement of the stomach and upper digestive tract.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed timing in relation to meals, and do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, dizziness or drowsiness. Levosulpride may sometimes cause breast tenderness or menstrual changes.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, epilepsy, a history of stomach or intestinal blockage or bleeding, or hormone-sensitive conditions. Inform the doctor about all other medicines, especially those used for heart conditions or other stomach problems. Seek medical help for vomiting blood, black stools, severe abdominal pain, persistent diarrhoea, or unusual involuntary movements.

What is it used for?
Etoricoxib is used to reduce pain, swelling and stiffness in conditions such as osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and other joint-related inflammatory conditions. It may also be prescribed for short-term severe pain, including acute gout, when appropriate.

How does it work?
It is a selective COX-2 inhibitor that reduces the production of substances responsible for pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other painkillers from the NSAID group unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, headache, dizziness, swelling of the legs or feet, and increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, high blood pressure, heart disease, stroke, kidney disease, liver disease, or allergy to painkillers. It may increase the risk of heart attack or stroke, especially with higher doses or long-term use. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Seek medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, black stools, severe skin reactions, or swelling of the face or throat.

What is it used for?
Etoricoxib is used to reduce pain, swelling and stiffness caused by arthritis and other joint conditions. It may also be prescribed for short-term treatment of acute gout or other painful inflammatory conditions, as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation. It selectively blocks an enzyme called COX-2.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water; it can usually be taken with or without food. Do not take more than the prescribed dose or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac or naproxen unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, headache, dizziness, swelling of the feet or ankles, and increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure, stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed; it should not be used in late pregnancy. Seek medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, severe skin rash, black stools, or swelling of the face or throat.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain and reduce inflammation, including pain related to muscles, joints or arthritis. Paracetamol also helps reduce fever.

How does it work?
Etoricoxib reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and reduce fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, with or without food, and swallow with water. Do not take more than the recommended dose or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or anti-inflammatory painkillers unless advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach discomfort, nausea, headache, dizziness, swelling of the feet or legs, and increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems, or allergy to painkillers. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Seek medical help for chest pain, breathing difficulty, severe skin reactions, black stools, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of painful muscle spasms, muscle stiffness and inflammation associated with musculoskeletal conditions such as back or neck pain.

How does it work?
Thiocolchicoside helps relax tight muscles, while etoricoxib reduces pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Do not take it with other painkillers or anti-inflammatory medicines unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness or drowsiness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, high blood pressure, heart disease, a history of seizures, or an allergy to painkillers. Avoid use during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless specifically advised. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, severe stomach pain, black stools, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with phlegm, chest congestion and breathing difficulty caused by narrowed airways. It helps loosen mucus and makes it easier to cough out.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin thin and loosen mucus. Terbutaline relaxes the muscles of the airways to help improve breathing, while menthol provides a soothing effect.

How to take/use it
Take or use only as directed by the doctor or the product label. Do not take more than recommended, and use the measuring device provided if it is a liquid. Do not combine with other cough or cold medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach upset, headache, dizziness, nervousness, tremors or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, seizures or an allergy to any ingredient. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for severe palpitations, worsening breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used for relief of common cold symptoms such as blocked or runny nose, sneezing, fever and body aches.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and relieve aches. Chlorpheniramine reduces allergy-like symptoms such as runny nose and sneezing, while phenylephrine helps relieve nasal congestion.

How to take/use it
Shake the suspension well before use. Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor, using a proper measuring device. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or other cold and flu ingredients.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea and headache. Some people may experience palpitations or a rise in blood pressure.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol if affected. Consult a doctor before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not exceed the recommended amount, as excessive paracetamol can seriously damage the liver.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cough, blocked nose, runny nose and sneezing associated with the common cold.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps suppress coughing. Phenylephrine reduces nasal congestion, while chlorpheniramine helps relieve runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Do not take more than recommended or combine with other cough-and-cold medicines containing similar ingredients. Avoid alcohol while using it.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, nervousness and stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, prostate or urination problems, or if taking sedatives or antidepressants. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines or within 14 days of stopping them. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, severe palpitations or a persistent or worsening cough.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cough and cold symptoms, especially cough associated with allergy or upper respiratory irritation.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps reduce the urge to cough. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that reduces allergy symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than recommended or combine with other cough, cold or antihistamine medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea and constipation.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving, alcohol and activities requiring alertness until the effects are known. Seek medical advice before use if there is glaucoma, difficulty urinating, prostate enlargement, liver disease or breathing problems. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors, and check with a healthcare professional before using with antidepressants or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, severe allergic reaction or a persistent or worsening cough.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve wet or mucus-producing cough associated with narrowed airways, wheezing, or breathing difficulty. It helps loosen mucus and open the airways.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus, making it easier to cough out. Levosalbutamol relaxes the muscles around the airways to help improve breathing.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. If it is a liquid, measure each dose with the supplied measuring device.

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, tremor, muscle cramps, or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Use with medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, glaucoma, or a history of seizures. Seek medical help for severe or worsening breathing difficulty, chest pain, or a very fast or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It is also used to relieve itching and hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It is an antihistamine that blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water. Avoid taking it with apple, orange or grapefruit juice, as these may reduce its effect. Antacids containing aluminium or magnesium should generally be taken at least 2 hours apart.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, dizziness and tiredness may occur. Drowsiness is uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Tell a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips or throat, breathing difficulty, or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It is also used to relieve itching and hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance released during allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water. Avoid taking it with apple, orange or grapefruit juice, as these may reduce its effect. If using aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids, take them separately as advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, dizziness and tiredness may occur. Fexofenadine usually causes less drowsiness than some older antihistamines, but drowsiness can still occur in some people.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips or throat, breathing difficulty, or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve symptoms of allergic rhinitis (hay fever), such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy nose or throat, and itchy or watery eyes.

How does it work?
Fexofenadine blocks histamine, a substance involved in allergy symptoms. Montelukast blocks leukotrienes, which can also contribute to inflammation and nasal allergy symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed or directed on the label. Swallow the tablet with water. Avoid taking it with fruit juice, and ask a pharmacist about using aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, dizziness, tiredness, or sleep disturbance.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney problems and any other medicines being used. Montelukast may rarely cause mood or behaviour changes, unusual dreams, depression, or suicidal thoughts; seek medical help promptly if these occur. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, or a severe rash.

What is it used for?
Itraconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, nails, mouth, vagina and other parts of the body, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making ergosterol, a substance needed to maintain their cell membranes. This prevents the fungi from growing and spreading.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Itraconazole capsules are usually taken immediately after a full meal and should be swallowed whole with water. Do not stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart failure, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken, as itraconazole can interact with many medicines. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, swelling of the legs, shortness of breath, severe rash or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Itraconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, nails, mouth, and other parts of the body, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making ergosterol, a substance they need to build and maintain their cell membranes. This helps stop the growth and spread of the fungal infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Itraconazole capsules are generally taken immediately after a full meal and should be swallowed whole with water. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not take an extra dose if one is missed without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and skin rash.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart failure, pregnancy, or breastfeeding before use. Itraconazole can interact with many medicines, so provide a complete list of all medicines and supplements being taken. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, breathing difficulty, swelling of the legs, or a severe skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Ketorolac tromethamine is used for the short-term relief of moderate to severe acute pain, such as pain after surgery or injury. It is not usually meant for long-term or mild pain.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, preferably with food or milk and a full glass of water. Do not take it for longer than prescribed or combine it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Stomach pain or discomfort, indigestion, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness and drowsiness.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice, especially if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or bleeding problems. Avoid during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, swelling, chest pain or reduced urination.

What is it used for?
Levetiracetam is an anti-seizure medicine used to control epilepsy and prevent seizures, including certain focal seizures and some generalized seizures. It may be used alone or together with other anti-seizure medicines.

How does it work?
It helps reduce abnormal electrical activity in the brain by acting on a brain protein involved in the release of nerve signals. This helps prevent seizures.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same times each day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not stop taking it suddenly, as seizures may worsen; a doctor should reduce it gradually if stopping is needed.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, headache, tiredness, nausea, and irritability or other mood changes may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, depression, or other mental health concerns. Seek medical help for severe mood or behaviour changes, thoughts of self-harm, unusual rash or swelling, or difficulty breathing. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known, as it may cause drowsiness or dizziness.

What is it used for?
Levofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the lungs, sinuses, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking enzymes they need to copy and repair their DNA.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with plenty of water. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or products containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc; keep a gap of at least 2 hours before or after these products. Do not self-medicate with antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and difficulty sleeping.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, heart-rhythm problems, seizures, diabetes, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or previous tendon problems. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, an irregular heartbeat, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, or signs of a serious allergy. Avoid driving if dizzy or affected.

What is it used for?
Levofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as some infections of the lungs, sinuses, urinary tract, skin and other tissues. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking enzymes that bacteria need to copy and repair their genetic material.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed, with plenty of water. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional tells otherwise. Take it at least 2 hours before or after antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and difficulty sleeping.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice. Stop taking it and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nervous-system changes, a severe allergic reaction, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Tell the healthcare professional about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney disease, seizures, heart-rhythm problems, myasthenia gravis or previous tendon problems. Avoid unnecessary strong sunlight and use sun protection.

What is it used for?
Levofloxacin infusion is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary system, skin and other tissues. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops bacteria from making the DNA they need to grow and multiply, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection, kidney function and medical advice. It should not be self-administered.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, trouble sleeping and pain or redness at the injection site.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to levofloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics, kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, seizures, diabetes, or a history of tendon problems. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, confusion, palpitations, breathing difficulty or a serious skin reaction. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only if prescribed. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or visual problems occur.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used for certain liver and bile duct conditions, including primary biliary cholangitis. It may also be used to dissolve selected cholesterol gallstones when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It improves the flow and composition of bile, helping reduce the buildup of harmful bile acids in the liver. It can also reduce cholesterol in bile and help dissolve some cholesterol gallstones.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food if advised. Take it regularly and do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach discomfort, vomiting or constipation may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision, as liver function tests and other monitoring may be needed. Tell the doctor about gallbladder inflammation, blocked bile ducts, severe liver disease or frequent diarrhoea. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or worsening symptoms.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used for certain liver and bile-duct conditions, including primary biliary cholangitis and some types of cholesterol gallstones. It may also be prescribed to improve bile flow in selected cholestatic liver conditions.

How does it work?
It makes bile less harmful to liver cells, improves the flow of bile and can reduce the cholesterol content of bile. This may help dissolve certain cholesterol gallstones over time.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food if advised. Take it regularly and do not stop treatment without medical advice. Do not take antacids containing aluminium or medicines that bind bile acids at the same time unless advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, loose stools, stomach pain or discomfort, nausea and indigestion may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any liver or gallbladder disease, blocked bile ducts, or frequent diarrhoea. Seek medical advice if severe or persistent diarrhoea, worsening abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or an allergic reaction occurs. Regular medical check-ups and liver tests may be needed during treatment.

What is it used for?
Linezolid is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, including some infections of the lungs, skin and soft tissues caused by susceptible bacteria. It may also be used for infections caused by certain resistant Gram-positive bacteria, such as MRSA or VRE, when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Linezolid stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents them from growing and spreading.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not skip doses or use leftover antibiotics. Follow the doctor's instructions if a dose is missed.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and changes in taste may occur. Long or repeated treatment can affect blood cell counts.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about blood disorders, uncontrolled high blood pressure, thyroid problems, seizures, or kidney or liver disease. Linezolid can interact with antidepressants and other medicines that increase serotonin, as well as some medicines for migraine or congestion. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, unusual bruising or bleeding, vision changes, numbness or tingling, or symptoms such as agitation, sweating, fever, tremors or muscle stiffness.

What is it used for?
Luliconazole cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot and jock itch. It helps relieve symptoms such as itching, redness and scaling caused by these infections.

How does it work?
It blocks the production of an essential part of the fungal cell membrane, helping stop the growth of the fungus.

How to take/use it
For use on the skin only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid covering the area with a tight bandage unless advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, redness, itching, irritation or dryness at the application site.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose. Do not apply to broken skin unless advised by a doctor. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction occurs. Use it only for the prescribed skin condition and do not share the cream with others.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve mild to moderate pain and reduce fever. It may help with pain caused by inflammation.

How does it work?
Paracetamol reduces pain and fever. Mefenamic acid is an anti-inflammatory medicine that reduces substances responsible for pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. If it is a liquid, measure the dose with a proper measuring device. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or other anti-inflammatory painkillers unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or drowsiness.

Precautions
Use only after medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, or if taking blood thinners. Avoid during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, unless prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Meropenem is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including certain infections of the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, skin, blood and brain. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall, which stops the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
Meropenem is usually given into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and kidney function. Complete the prescribed course unless the prescriber advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea or vomiting, headache, rash, and pain, redness or swelling at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to meropenem, penicillin, cephalosporin or other antibiotics; kidney problems; or a history of seizures. The dose may need adjustment in kidney disease. Meropenem can interact with valproate medicines. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash or seizures.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and overactive immune responses in conditions such as severe allergies, asthma, inflammatory disorders and some autoimmune conditions. The exact use depends on the condition being treated.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances and immune reactions that cause inflammation, swelling, redness and allergic symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food or milk to reduce stomach irritation. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly without medical advice, especially after prolonged use.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, headache, mood changes, fluid retention, increased blood sugar and increased blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, glaucoma, mental health conditions or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce the body's ability to fight infections and may mask infection symptoms. Avoid live vaccines unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for signs of serious infection, severe mood changes, vision problems or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and calm an overactive immune response in conditions such as severe allergies, asthma, arthritis, autoimmune disorders and some skin conditions. The exact use depends on the condition being treated.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and suppresses excessive immune-system activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food to reduce stomach irritation. Do not change the dose or stop treatment suddenly, especially after longer use, unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, increased appetite, difficulty sleeping, mood changes, headache, fluid retention and increased blood sugar may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health problems or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce resistance to infection and may hide infection symptoms. Avoid close contact with people who have contagious illnesses and check with a doctor before receiving vaccines. Seek medical help for signs of serious infection, severe mood changes, vision problems or allergic reactions.

What is it used for?
Minoxidil 5% topical solution is used to help treat hereditary hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) by promoting hair growth on the scalp.

How does it work?
It may improve blood flow around hair follicles and help keep follicles in the active hair-growth phase. The exact way it works is not fully understood.

How to take/use it
Apply only to the scalp as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Use on a clean, dry scalp, wash hands after application, and avoid contact with the eyes or other areas of the body. Do not apply to broken, irritated or infected skin, and do not swallow it.

Common side effects
Scalp dryness, itching, redness or irritation; unwanted hair growth on the face or other areas; headache, dizziness or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
Do not use for sudden, patchy or unexplained hair loss without medical advice. Seek medical help for chest pain, fainting, severe dizziness, swelling, rapid heartbeat or severe scalp irritation. Consult a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is heart disease or low blood pressure.

What is it used for?
Used for pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia). It may help slow hair thinning and support hair regrowth on the scalp.

How does it work?
Minoxidil helps support the hair-growth phase of the hair cycle. Finasteride lowers the level of dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone involved in pattern hair loss, which may reduce further hair follicle miniaturisation.

How to take/use it
For external use on the scalp only. Apply exactly as directed by the doctor or product label, using it on a clean, dry scalp. Wash hands after application and avoid contact with the eyes, mouth, broken skin and other areas of the body. Do not swallow.

Common side effects
Scalp itching, dryness, redness or irritation; unwanted hair growth on the face or other body areas; headache or dizziness. Finasteride may also cause decreased sexual desire, erection or ejaculation problems, breast tenderness, or mood changes.

Precautions
Do not use on an irritated or infected scalp unless advised by a doctor. Seek medical help for chest pain, fainting, rapid heartbeat, swelling, severe dizziness or a severe allergic reaction. Pregnant or possibly pregnant women should not use this product or handle it if it may contact the skin, because of the finasteride content. Keep away from children and consult a doctor before use if there is heart disease, low blood pressure or sudden or patchy hair loss.

What is it used for?
Minoxidil 5% topical solution is used to help promote hair regrowth and reduce hair loss caused by hereditary pattern hair loss.

How does it work?
It helps improve blood flow around hair follicles and may prolong the hair-growth phase. The exact way it promotes hair growth is not fully understood.

How to take/use it
Apply only to the affected scalp areas as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Use on a dry scalp, avoid contact with the eyes and other body areas, and wash hands after application. Do not apply to irritated or damaged skin.

Common side effects
Scalp itching, dryness, redness or irritation. Unwanted hair growth on the face or other areas may occur.

Precautions
Do not use for sudden or patchy hair loss, or if the scalp is inflamed, infected or painful, unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop use and seek medical help if chest pain, rapid heartbeat, dizziness, fainting, swelling or severe scalp irritation occurs. Keep out of reach of children and avoid swallowing.

What is it used for?
Used on the scalp to help treat pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) and support hair regrowth.

How does it work?
Minoxidil helps stimulate hair follicles and support hair growth. Finasteride reduces the effect of DHT, a hormone linked to pattern hair loss.

How to take/use it
Apply to the scalp only as directed by the doctor or product label. Use on a clean, dry scalp, avoid contact with the eyes and other sensitive areas, and wash hands after application. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Scalp itching, dryness, redness, irritation or flaking; unwanted hair growth on the face or other areas. Some users may experience dizziness, headache, palpitations or sexual side effects.

Precautions
For external use only; do not swallow. Avoid use if allergic to any ingredient. Women who are pregnant, may become pregnant or are breastfeeding should not use this product unless specifically advised by a doctor, because finasteride may harm a developing male baby. Seek medical help for chest pain, fainting, fast or irregular heartbeat, sudden swelling or severe scalp irritation.

What is it used for?
Mupirocin cream is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial skin infections, such as impetigo and infected minor cuts, wounds or other skin injuries.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents them from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as prescribed. Clean and dry the area before use, and wash hands before and after applying it. For external use only; avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose unless specifically prescribed for that use.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to mupirocin or any ingredient. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe rash, swelling or breathing difficulty occurs. Avoid applying it over large areas or using it for longer than prescribed. Consult a doctor if the infection worsens or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Amoxycillin with clavulanic acid is an antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections, including infections of the ear, sinuses, throat, lungs, skin, urinary tract and teeth. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Amoxycillin kills susceptible bacteria by affecting their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps prevent some bacteria from resisting amoxycillin.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Taking it with a meal may help reduce stomach upset. Do not use leftover antibiotics or share this medicine with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, skin rash and thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin, amoxycillin, clavulanic acid or similar antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, previous antibiotic-related jaundice or liver problems, or a history of severe antibiotic-associated diarrhoea. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe skin rash, or persistent or bloody diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Norethisterone is a progestogen medicine used to treat heavy or painful periods, irregular bleeding and endometriosis. It may also be prescribed for temporarily delaying a period. The use depends on the doctor's advice.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural hormone progesterone and helps regulate the lining of the womb, which can control menstrual bleeding and related symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and at the same time each day, with water. The dose and treatment duration vary depending on the reason for use. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. It is not a contraceptive.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, breast tenderness, bloating, mood changes and spotting or other changes in menstrual bleeding may occur.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about a history of blood clots, liver disease, unexplained vaginal bleeding, migraine or hormone-sensitive cancer before use. Seek urgent medical help for sudden chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, vision changes, or painful swelling in a leg. Seek medical advice if yellowing of the skin or eyes develops.

What is it used for?
Sodium chloride intravenous solution (normal saline) is used in hospitals to replace fluids and salt in the body. It may also be used to dilute or deliver other medicines through a vein.

How does it work?
It contains sodium and chloride, which help restore fluid and electrolyte balance in the body.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given directly into a vein by a healthcare professional. The amount and rate depend on the patient's condition and must be decided by a doctor.

Common side effects
Fluid retention, swelling, irritation at the injection site, and changes in salt levels may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, kidney disease, high blood pressure, swelling, or a tendency to retain fluid. Medical monitoring may be needed during treatment, especially with large amounts or prolonged use.

What is it used for?
Used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It is also used in the treatment of stomach or intestinal ulcers and other acid-related conditions.

How does it work?
Omeprazole reduces the production of stomach acid by blocking the acid-producing pumps in the stomach lining.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or as stated on the package. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is commonly taken before food, as directed.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, gas, diarrhoea or constipation.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is liver disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding or allergy to omeprazole or similar medicines. Check with a doctor or pharmacist before use with other medicines, especially clopidogrel, warfarin, digoxin or medicines for HIV. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, persistent vomiting, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or persistent symptoms. Long-term use should be medically supervised.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux symptoms. It may also help when these symptoms are associated with nausea, bloating or slow movement of food through the stomach.

How does it work?
Omeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps improve movement of food through the upper digestive system and can reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the prescribed timing and swallow the medicine as directed. Do not take more than recommended or continue it longer than advised.

Common side effects
Headache, stomach pain or discomfort, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, bloating and dry mouth may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart disease, an irregular heartbeat or low potassium or magnesium levels. Domperidone may rarely cause serious heart-rhythm problems and should be used carefully with certain medicines that affect heart rhythm. Seek medical help for fainting, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe or persistent diarrhoea, vomiting blood or black stools. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Pantoprazole injection reduces excess stomach acid. It is used for acid reflux, heartburn and acid-related irritation or damage to the food pipe, especially when oral treatment is not suitable.

How does it work?
It blocks the stomach's acid-producing proton pumps, thereby reducing acid production.

How to take/use it
This injection is given into a vein by a healthcare professional. Use it only as prescribed and do not self-inject. The dose and duration depend on the condition being treated.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, gas and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to pantoprazole or similar medicines, liver disease, low vitamin B12 or magnesium levels, or osteoporosis. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, rash or swelling, breathing difficulty, muscle cramps, or irregular heartbeat. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor.

It reduces the production of acid in the stomach by blocking acid-producing pumps in the stomach lining.

Precautions

Inform the doctor about any allergy to penicillin, cephalosporin or other antibiotics, kidney disease, bleeding problems, or a history of severe antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Medical monitoring may be needed during treatment, especially in people with kidney problems. Seek urgent help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or persistent watery or bloody diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve neuropathic pain, such as burning, tingling, numbness or shooting pain caused by nerve damage. It may be prescribed for conditions such as diabetic nerve pain or nerve pain due to other causes.

How does it work?
Pregabalin and nortriptyline reduce the abnormal pain signals sent by damaged nerves. Methylcobalamin, a form of vitamin B12, supports normal nerve function.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food, and preferably at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not stop it suddenly without medical advice, as the dose may need to be reduced gradually.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, nausea, tiredness and weight gain may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery until the effects are known. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, heart problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent medical help for facial or throat swelling, breathing difficulty, severe rash, extreme mood changes or thoughts of self-harm.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to relieve neuropathic pain, which is caused by irritated or damaged nerves. It may help with burning, shooting, tingling or electric-shock-like pain.

How does it work?
Pregabalin reduces abnormal nerve signals involved in pain. Nortriptyline increases certain natural chemical messengers that help reduce pain signals.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water. Take it regularly and do not stop suddenly without medical advice, as the dose may need to be reduced gradually. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Dizziness, sleepiness, tiredness, blurred vision, dry mouth, constipation, nausea, increased appetite and weight gain.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol, as it can increase sleepiness and dizziness. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, heart problems, breathing problems, or use of opioid painkillers or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical help for severe breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe allergic reactions, or new or worsening suicidal thoughts.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 200 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from multiplying by blocking enzymes needed for their DNA production.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, iron or zinc; separate them as advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and sleep disturbance.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, or an allergic reaction. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, seizures, or previous tendon problems. Avoid driving if dizzy or affected by vision or concentration changes.

What is it used for?
Rabeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be prescribed for stomach or intestinal ulcers and other acid-related conditions.

How does it work?
It is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is commonly taken before food, but follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain and gas.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to rabeprazole or other acid-reducing medicines, pregnancy or breastfeeding, liver problems, and all other medicines being used. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or persistent symptoms. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for acidity, heartburn and acid reflux (GERD). It may also help relieve reflux-related nausea, vomiting or stomach discomfort.

How does it work?
Rabeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps improve the movement of food through the stomach and can help control nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the medicine with water and do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, stomach pain, nausea, dry mouth and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, or if taking medicines that can affect heart rhythm. Seek medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe diarrhoea, vomiting blood or black stools. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if it is needed for a prolonged period.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux, especially when these symptoms are associated with indigestion, bloating or slow stomach emptying.

How does it work?
Rabeprazole reduces the production of stomach acid. Levosulpride helps improve the movement of food through the stomach and may reduce reflux-related symptoms.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the timing advised by the doctor, often before a meal.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, constipation, stomach pain, dizziness, fatigue or drowsiness. Levosulpride may sometimes cause breast tenderness or menstrual changes.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, a history of movement disorders, or conditions affected by raised prolactin levels. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizzy or drowsy. Seek medical advice for persistent symptoms, black stools, vomiting blood, severe diarrhoea, or unusual involuntary movements.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine cream is a topical antiseptic used to help prevent infection in minor cuts, grazes, burns and other superficial wounds.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or reduces many bacteria, viruses and fungi on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth. Do not apply to deep or large wounds without medical advice.

Common side effects
Temporary skin irritation, redness, dryness or staining may occur. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation or an allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to iodine or povidone iodine. Avoid prolonged or repeated use, application over large areas, or use on deep wounds or severe burns unless advised by a healthcare professional. Ask a doctor before use if there is thyroid disease, lithium treatment, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if the wound becomes more painful, swollen, red or produces pus.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine 5% cream is a topical antiseptic used to help prevent or treat infection in minor cuts, grazes, burns and other superficial skin wounds.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or inactivates many types of bacteria and other microorganisms on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not use on deep wounds, serious burns or large areas without medical advice.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, dryness or temporary staining of the skin may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to povidone iodine or other iodine-containing products. Seek medical advice before use on large or deep wounds, for prolonged use, or if there is worsening redness, swelling, pain, pus or fever. Use with medical advice if there is thyroid disease, lithium treatment, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop use and seek urgent help if severe irritation, swelling or breathing difficulty occurs.

What is it used for?
Used on infected or infection-prone skin wounds, such as minor cuts, ulcers, burns or surgical wounds, to help treat or prevent bacterial infection.

How does it work?
Metronidazole acts against certain bacteria, especially those that grow without oxygen. Povidone iodine releases iodine that kills a wide range of germs on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean and gently dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use. Do not apply to the eyes or swallow it.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to metronidazole, povidone iodine or similar products. Use only on the affected area and avoid prolonged or extensive use unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice for deep, large, severely infected or non-healing wounds, or if there is increasing pain, redness, swelling or fever. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or if there is thyroid disease.

What is it used for?
This cream is generally used for the local treatment of certain mixed vaginal infections, including infections caused by bacteria or parasites. Use it only when recommended by a doctor or as directed on the product label.

How does it work?
Povidone iodine acts as an antiseptic against many germs. Ornidazole acts against certain bacteria and parasites that can cause infection.

How to take/use it
Use only by the route and in the amount directed by the doctor or product label. Do not swallow it or use it in the eyes. Complete the recommended treatment unless advised otherwise.

Common side effects
Mild burning, irritation, itching, redness or discomfort at the application site may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to povidone iodine, iodine or ornidazole. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is thyroid disease. Stop use and seek medical help for severe irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or worsening symptoms. Avoid prolonged or repeated use unless medically advised.

What is it used for?
Ondansetron is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting, including nausea and vomiting related to chemotherapy, radiotherapy or surgery.

How does it work?
It blocks serotonin signals in the body that can trigger nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed. Measure the syrup with an accurate measuring device. Do not take more or more often than advised.

Common side effects
Headache, constipation, diarrhoea, dizziness and tiredness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of heart rhythm problems, low potassium or magnesium levels, liver disease, or an allergy to ondansetron. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that affect heart rhythm or mood. Seek medical help for fainting, an irregular heartbeat, severe allergic reactions or unusual muscle stiffness and agitation.

It stops susceptible bacteria from making their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from growing.

What is it used for?

How does it work?
Cefpodoxime kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps cefpodoxime work against some bacteria that can otherwise resist it.
