What is it used for?
Sertaconazole cream is used to treat fungal skin infections such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch and certain yeast infections of the skin.

How does it work?
It prevents fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which stops their growth and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected, clean and dry skin as directed by the doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use. For external use only; avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, dryness or irritation at the application site may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to sertaconazole or similar antifungal medicines. Avoid applying to the eyes or inside the mouth. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs, or if the infection worsens or does not improve with treatment.

What is it used for?
Ketoconazole 2% cream is used to treat fungal infections of the skin, such as ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch, pityriasis versicolor and some yeast infections of the skin.

How does it work?
It is an antifungal medicine that stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane. This helps stop the fungal infection from growing and clears the infection.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to clean, dry, affected skin as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Wash hands before and after applying, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use in the eyes or on broken skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, rash or breathing difficulty occurs. Consult a healthcare professional if the infection worsens or does not improve as expected.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain, inflammation and muscle spasm in musculoskeletal conditions such as back pain, sprains and strains.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain, while chlorzoxazone acts as a muscle relaxant to reduce muscle spasm.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, preferably with or after food and with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Avoid taking other medicines containing diclofenac, paracetamol or similar painkillers unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and drowsiness.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if dizzy or drowsy. Use only under medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or during pregnancy. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to reduce heavy menstrual bleeding and relieve period pain or cramps.

How does it work?
Tranexamic acid helps prevent the breakdown of blood clots, reducing menstrual blood loss. Mefenamic acid reduces substances that cause pain, inflammation and menstrual cramps.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, usually during the menstrual period. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain or indigestion, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of blood clots, kidney disease, stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to NSAID painkillers. Avoid taking it with other NSAID painkillers unless advised. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, breathlessness, sudden leg swelling or pain, unusual vision changes, vomiting blood, or black stools.

What is it used for?
Azithromycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the chest, throat, skin, ears and genital tract. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making proteins needed for their growth and survival.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not skip doses or stop treatment early, even if symptoms improve. Do not share antibiotics or use leftover medicine. The dose and treatment duration depend on the infection and should be decided by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, vomiting and headache.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about allergies to azithromycin or other macrolide antibiotics, liver disease, heart rhythm problems or low levels of potassium or magnesium. Inform the doctor about all other medicines being taken. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, fainting, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat calcium and vitamin D deficiency and to support healthy bones and teeth. It may also be used as part of bone-health treatment when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Calcium provides the mineral needed for bones, teeth, muscles and nerves. Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) helps the body absorb calcium and supports bone mineralisation.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. If taking other medicines or supplements, check with a pharmacist about the appropriate timing.

Common side effects
Constipation, stomach discomfort, bloating, nausea or vomiting may occur. Excessive calcium intake can cause increased thirst or frequent urination.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels or vitamin D excess. Seek medical advice if severe stomach pain, persistent vomiting, confusion or unusual weakness occurs. Calcium can affect the absorption of some medicines, including certain antibiotics, thyroid medicines and iron supplements; ask a pharmacist about spacing doses.

What is it used for?
Cetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin allergies such as hives and itching.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth with water, exactly as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. It may cause drowsiness in some people; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, nausea, or dizziness.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and be careful with other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical advice if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Get urgent medical help for swelling of the face or throat, breathing difficulty, or a severe allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Cetirizine syrup is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin itching or hives.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Measure the syrup with the supplied measuring device. Do not take more than the recommended amount. It may cause drowsiness in some people.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, and nausea may occur.

Precautions
Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effect is known. Avoid alcohol, as it may increase drowsiness. Consult a doctor before use in kidney disease, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if taking other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction such as facial swelling, breathing difficulty, or severe rash.

What is it used for?
Trypsin and chymotrypsin tablets are used as prescribed to help reduce swelling and inflammation associated with injuries, surgery, or other soft-tissue conditions.

How does it work?
These are proteolytic enzymes that help break down proteins involved in inflammation and swelling, which may support recovery of injured tissues.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by the doctor or product label. Swallow the gastro-resistant tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Stomach upset, nausea, diarrhoea, or abdominal discomfort may occur. Skin rash or other allergic reactions can occur rarely.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a bleeding or clotting disorder, an active ulcer, an allergy to these enzymes, or if blood-thinning medicines are being used. Medical advice is recommended before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding and before planned surgery. Seek urgent medical help for unusual bleeding, severe rash, swelling, or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Norethisterone is used to manage heavy, painful or irregular periods and other menstrual problems. It may also be prescribed for endometriosis or to delay a period.

How does it work?
It is a synthetic form of the hormone progesterone. It helps control changes in the womb lining and regulate menstrual bleeding.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. This medicine is not a contraceptive.

Common side effects
Nausea, headache, breast tenderness, bloating, mood changes, and spotting or irregular bleeding may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if pregnant unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about unexplained vaginal bleeding, liver disease, a history of blood clots, migraine, or hormone-sensitive cancer. Seek urgent medical help for sudden chest pain, breathlessness, painful leg swelling, severe headache, vision changes, or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime axetil is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, chest, sinuses, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by interfering with the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and preferably after food. Swallow the tablet whole with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not skip doses or share this medicine with others.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or bloody diarrhoea. Use only on medical advice, as unnecessary antibiotic use can promote resistance.

What is it used for?
Cefuroxime is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections, including certain infections of the throat, sinuses, ears, chest, urinary tract, skin and soft tissues. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and preferably after food, as this helps its absorption. Swallow the tablet whole with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, headache, skin rash and fungal infections such as oral or vaginal thrush may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefuroxime, other cephalosporins or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, previous antibiotic-related severe diarrhoea, or allergies to antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe skin reactions or persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Medicines that reduce stomach acid may affect cefuroxime absorption; check with a doctor or pharmacist before using them together.

What is it used for?
This syrup is used to help improve appetite and may be prescribed for poor appetite or inadequate food intake. It should be used only when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Cyproheptadine blocks certain histamine and serotonin effects in the body and can increase appetite. The combination is intended to support appetite improvement.

How to take/use it
Take only in the dose and for the duration prescribed by the healthcare professional. Measure the syrup with an oral syringe or measuring cup. Do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, increased appetite, nausea and stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Cyproheptadine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Use cautiously in people with glaucoma, difficulty urinating or prostate problems. Inform the healthcare professional about other medicines being taken. Seek medical help for severe sleepiness, breathing difficulty or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This cream is used for fungal skin infections that cause inflammation and may also have a bacterial infection. It can help relieve redness, swelling and itching while treating the infection.

How does it work?
Clotrimazole treats fungal growth, while neomycin acts against certain bacteria. Beclomethasone reduces inflammation, redness and itching.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Clean and dry the area before application, and wash hands before and after use. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and broken skin. Do not cover the area tightly unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness, irritation or dryness at the application site. Allergic skin reactions may occur.

Precautions
Use only for the condition for which it was prescribed. Do not use for prolonged periods, on large areas, or on the face, groin or skin folds unless specifically advised. The steroid may mask or worsen some infections if used incorrectly. Stop use and seek medical advice if the infection worsens, spreads, or severe irritation or swelling develops.

What is it used for?
Clotrimazole 1% dusting powder is used to treat fungal infections of the skin, such as athlete’s foot, ringworm and fungal rashes in skin folds.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Apply the powder to clean, completely dry affected skin and nearby areas as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. For external use only. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, burning, stinging, redness, itching or rash may occur where it is applied.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Do not inhale the powder. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or other signs of an allergic reaction occur. Seek medical advice if the infection worsens or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid injection used for certain medical conditions involving loss of bone or body tissue, including some cases of osteoporosis. The exact use must be decided by a doctor based on the patient’s condition.

How does it work?
It is a synthetic substance related to testosterone. It can increase protein production in the body and may help support bone and muscle tissue.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the condition being treated. Do not self-inject or use it without medical supervision.

Common side effects
Acne, oily skin, swelling or fluid retention, changes in sexual desire, mood changes, and pain at the injection site. Women may develop increased facial hair, menstrual changes, or a deeper voice.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about liver, kidney, heart, prostate, or breast problems, diabetes, or high cholesterol. It may affect liver function and blood cholesterol. Seek medical advice for yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe swelling, chest pain, or breathing difficulty. This medicine may affect growth in children and should be used only under specialist supervision.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid used under medical supervision as an additional treatment for osteoporosis. In some cases, it may also be used for certain types of anaemia, such as anaemia associated with kidney disease.

How does it work?
It has anabolic effects that promote protein production and support the formation of body tissues and bones. It may also stimulate red blood cell production in selected patients.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection into a muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the condition being treated. Do not self-inject or use it without medical supervision.

Common side effects
Acne or oily skin, swelling due to fluid retention, changes in sex drive or mood, nausea, and changes in blood cholesterol. Women may experience irregular periods, increased facial or body hair, voice deepening, or hair loss.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about prostate or breast problems, liver, kidney or heart disease, diabetes, high cholesterol, or use of blood thinners. It should be used cautiously in children and adolescents because it can affect growth and puberty. Seek medical advice for yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe swelling, breathing difficulty, unusual bleeding, or significant voice changes.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with phlegm, chest congestion and breathing difficulty caused by narrowed airways, when prescribed.

How does it work?
Terbutaline helps relax the muscles around the airways. Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help loosen and thin mucus so it is easier to cough up, while menthol may soothe the throat.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Shake the bottle well and measure the syrup with a proper measuring device. Do not take more than recommended or combine it with other cough and cold medicines without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, tremors, nervousness or restlessness, and fast or pounding heartbeat.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Seek medical help for severe or worsening breathing difficulty, chest pain, or a persistent fast heartbeat. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice. This medicine should be used in children only as directed by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of dry cough and associated cold or allergy symptoms such as runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan helps reduce the cough reflex. Chlorpheniramine blocks histamine, helping relieve runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Use the provided measuring device and do not take more than recommended. Do not combine with other cough, cold or allergy medicines unless advised.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea or stomach upset.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Seek medical advice before use in young children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is glaucoma, difficulty urinating, liver disease or breathing problems. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors and check with a healthcare professional before use with antidepressants or other medicines that cause drowsiness. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, severe allergic reactions or a persistent or worsening cough.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve cough with mucus and associated cold or allergy symptoms, such as a blocked or runny nose and throat irritation.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine helps reduce allergy symptoms. Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus so it can be cleared more easily, while menthol helps soothe throat irritation.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Measure the syrup with a suitable measuring device and do not exceed the recommended amount. Shake well before use if advised on the label.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, stomach upset or headache may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol if affected. Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Consult a doctor if the cough worsens, lasts several days, or is accompanied by breathing difficulty, chest pain, high fever or blood in the mucus. Seek urgent help for signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
This syrup is used to relieve cough with mucus and related cold or allergy symptoms, such as a runny nose, sneezing and throat irritation.

How does it work?
Levocetirizine reduces allergy symptoms. Ambroxol and guaiphenesin help thin and loosen mucus so it can be coughed out, while menthol provides a soothing, cooling sensation.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Measure each dose with the supplied measuring device and do not exceed the recommended amount. Shake well before use if indicated on the label.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, stomach upset or headache may occur.

Precautions
Drowsiness may occur; avoid alcohol and be careful when driving or operating machinery. Seek medical advice if the cough lasts, worsens, or is associated with breathing difficulty, chest pain, high fever or blood in the mucus. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or in people with kidney disease. Stop use and seek urgent help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
This combination is used under medical supervision to medically end an early pregnancy inside the uterus. It is not suitable for an ectopic pregnancy (pregnancy outside the uterus).

How does it work?
Mifepristone blocks progesterone, a hormone needed to maintain pregnancy. Misoprostol softens the cervix and causes uterine contractions, leading to expulsion of the pregnancy.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a qualified healthcare professional. The two medicines must be taken in the specific sequence and at the time advised. Do not use this pack without medical assessment and access to follow-up care.

Common side effects
Abdominal cramps, vaginal bleeding, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, fever, chills and weakness may occur.

Precautions
Do not use without medical advice if an ectopic pregnancy is suspected, if there is an intrauterine device, severe anaemia, a bleeding disorder, use of blood thinners, long-term steroid treatment or allergy to either medicine. Seek urgent medical help for very heavy bleeding, severe or one-sided abdominal pain, fainting, worsening weakness, or fever that persists. Follow-up is important to confirm that the pregnancy has ended completely.

What is it used for?
Itraconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, nails, mouth, and other parts of the body, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making ergosterol, a substance they need to build and maintain their cell membranes. This helps stop fungal growth.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Itraconazole capsules are usually taken immediately after a full meal and should be swallowed whole with water. Do not change the dose or stop treatment early without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and skin rash.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart failure, pregnancy, or breastfeeding before use. Itraconazole can interact with many medicines, including some medicines for heart problems, cholesterol, acidity, and sleep; provide a complete list of medicines being taken. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, swelling, breathing difficulty, or a serious skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Itraconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, nails, mouth, and other parts of the body, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making ergosterol, an essential part of their cell membrane. This prevents the fungi from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the capsule whole. Itraconazole capsules are usually taken immediately after a full meal. Do not stop treatment early unless advised by a doctor, even if symptoms improve. Do not take extra doses if one is missed; follow the advice on the prescription or package.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart failure, pregnancy, or breastfeeding before use. Itraconazole can interact with many medicines, including some medicines for heart problems, cholesterol, acidity, and allergies; provide a complete list of medicines being taken. Seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, breathing difficulty, swelling of the legs, or a serious skin reaction.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 500 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, headache, toothache and period pain.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of chemicals in the brain that cause pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth with water, following the dose and directions on the label or as advised by a doctor. Do not take more than recommended or use it together with other medicines containing paracetamol.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when used as directed. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to paracetamol. Seek medical advice before use if there is liver disease, regular heavy alcohol use or malnutrition. Taking more than recommended can cause serious liver damage; seek urgent medical help after an overdose, even if feeling well.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 650 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, toothache, body aches and muscle pain.

How does it work?
It works mainly in the brain to reduce the production of substances that cause pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Swallow the tablet with water and follow the dose and timing advised by a doctor or stated on the package. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it with other medicines containing paracetamol.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when used correctly, but may include nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash.

Precautions
Use only with medical advice if there is liver disease, regular alcohol use or malnutrition. Avoid taking other paracetamol-containing products at the same time. Seek urgent medical help after an overdose or if severe skin rash, breathing difficulty, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or unusual bleeding occurs.

What is it used for?
Mometasone furoate cream is used to reduce redness, swelling and itching caused by inflammatory skin conditions such as eczema, dermatitis and psoriasis.

How does it work?
It is a topical corticosteroid that reduces inflammation and the skin reactions that cause redness and itching.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to the affected skin exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Use only on the skin. Avoid the eyes, face, groin, underarms and skin folds unless specifically advised. Wash hands after applying, unless the hands are being treated.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, irritation, dryness or itching at the application site. Prolonged or improper use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks, changes in skin colour or visible small blood vessels.

Precautions
Do not use on untreated skin infections, open wounds or broken skin unless advised by a doctor. Avoid covering the treated area with tight or airtight dressings unless instructed. Stop using it and seek medical advice if the skin condition worsens, signs of infection develop, or there is severe irritation. Avoid prolonged use, especially on the face and in children, unless prescribed.

What is it used for?
Aceclofenac is used to relieve pain and inflammation in conditions affecting the muscles, joints and bones, such as osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow the tablet with water. Do not take more than prescribed or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache.

Precautions
Avoid aceclofenac if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, allergy to aspirin or other NSAID painkillers, or NSAID-triggered asthma, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Inform the doctor about kidney, liver or heart disease, high blood pressure, or use of blood thinners. It should generally be avoided during the last 3 months of pregnancy. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin rash.

What is it used for?
Aceclofenac is used to relieve pain, swelling and stiffness in conditions such as osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and other muscle or joint problems.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food. Swallow the sustained-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache.

Precautions
Avoid taking it with other painkillers of the NSAID type unless advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or liver problems. Avoid use during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty, chest pain or swelling of the face or legs.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, including pain from sprains, strains and arthritis.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling and soothing effect on the affected area.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected area as directed on the product label or by a doctor, and gently rub in. Wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated. Do not use more often or for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site.

Precautions
Do not apply to broken, infected or irritated skin, or near the eyes, mouth or other sensitive areas. Avoid tight bandages and external heat over the treated area. Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other NSAIDs or salicylates. Stop use and seek medical help if severe rash, swelling or breathing difficulty occurs. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or on large areas of skin or for prolonged use.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for short-term relief of painful muscle and joint conditions, especially pain associated with muscle spasms, such as back pain and other musculoskeletal pain.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac and paracetamol help reduce pain and inflammation. Chlorzoxazone acts as a muscle relaxant to help relieve muscle spasm.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a healthcare professional. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or combine it with other paracetamol-containing medicines or painkillers unless advised.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy. Tell a healthcare professional before use if there is a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to painkillers. Avoid use during pregnancy unless specifically advised, especially in the later months. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, severe rash, black stools, vomiting blood or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve pain and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and bone-related conditions such as arthritis, sprains and other painful musculoskeletal problems.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow it with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol or pain-relieving NSAIDs unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional if there is a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to painkillers. Avoid or limit alcohol. Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe skin rash. Use during pregnancy only when specifically advised.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, including pain from sprains, strains and arthritis.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling and soothing effect on the affected area.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Spray on the affected area as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth, broken or irritated skin, and wash hands after use. Do not cover the area with a tight or airtight dressing unless advised.

Common side effects
Skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin or other NSAID painkillers, or if these medicines have caused asthma or skin reactions. Stop use and seek medical advice if severe skin irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or a widespread rash occurs. Avoid use during pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks, unless advised by a doctor. Do not apply with heat or near open flames, and avoid inhaling the spray.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, such as sprains, strains and arthritis-related pain.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling or warming sensation that may help relieve muscle and joint discomfort.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Spray on the affected area and use as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin, and wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other painkillers or any ingredient in the product. Avoid use on wounds, infected skin, near the eyes or with tight bandages or external heat. Stop use and seek medical help if severe skin reactions, breathing difficulty or swelling occur. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy, especially in the last 3 months, or while breastfeeding. Do not swallow or inhale the spray.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and swelling, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and fever, while serratiopeptidase may help reduce swelling.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Taking it after food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is an allergy to aceclofenac, paracetamol, other painkillers or NSAIDs. Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or pregnancy—especially the last three months. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or NSAIDs unless advised by a doctor. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Used as a digestive enzyme preparation to help break down proteins and carbohydrates and support digestion. It may be used for digestive discomfort related to inadequate digestion.

How does it work?
Pepsin helps digest proteins, while alpha-amylase helps break down carbohydrates into smaller components that the body can absorb more easily.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Measure the syrup with a suitable measuring device and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
May cause stomach discomfort, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea or allergic reactions in some people.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to pepsin, alpha-amylase or any ingredient in the product. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur. Consult a healthcare professional if digestive symptoms are severe, persistent or recurrent.

What is it used for?
Mupirocin ointment is a topical antibiotic used to treat bacterial skin infections, such as impetigo and infected cuts, wounds or other minor skin injuries.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, helping to clear the skin infection.

How to take/use it
For use on the skin only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer exactly as prescribed. Wash hands before and after applying it. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and inside of the nose unless specifically prescribed for that use. Do not share the ointment or cover the area tightly unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, itching, redness or irritation at the application site.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to mupirocin or any ingredient. Stop using it and seek medical advice if severe irritation, rash, swelling or difficulty breathing occurs. Consult a healthcare professional if the infection worsens or does not improve as expected. Use only for the prescribed skin infection; it does not treat fungal or viral infections.

What is it used for?
Tramadol injection is used to relieve moderate to severe pain when an injectable pain medicine is needed.

How does it work?
It acts on opioid receptors in the brain and spinal cord to reduce the feeling of pain. It also affects certain chemical messengers involved in pain signals.

How to take/use it
This injection must be given by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. Use only the prescribed amount and do not self-inject. Do not drive or operate machinery after receiving it until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, drowsiness, constipation, headache, sweating and dry mouth.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and tell the doctor about sleeping medicines, sedatives, antidepressants or other opioid medicines, as serious drowsiness, breathing problems or other interactions may occur. Inform the doctor if there is a history of breathing problems, seizures, liver or kidney disease, or medicine dependence. Tramadol can cause dependence and should be used only as prescribed. Seek urgent medical help for slow or difficult breathing, severe sleepiness, confusion, seizures or swelling of the face or throat.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to relieve moderate to severe pain when a stronger painkiller may be needed.

How does it work?
Tramadol and paracetamol work together in the brain and nervous system to reduce the sensation of pain. Tramadol is an opioid pain reliever, while paracetamol also helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Do not take more than the prescribed amount or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or tramadol unless a doctor approves. Do not drink alcohol while taking it, and avoid driving if it causes drowsiness or dizziness.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, constipation, dizziness, drowsiness, headache, dry mouth and stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Tramadol can cause dependence and may slow breathing, especially if taken in excess or with alcohol, sleeping medicines or other sedatives. Use only under medical advice if there is liver or kidney disease, breathing problems, a history of seizures, or a history of substance misuse. Seek urgent medical help for severe sleepiness, slow or difficult breathing, confusion, seizures, or signs of an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Pantoprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be prescribed for stomach or duodenal ulcers and other acid-related conditions.

How does it work?
It blocks the acid-producing pumps in the stomach, reducing the amount of acid made and helping relieve acid-related symptoms and support healing.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the gastro-resistant tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is generally taken before food, as directed by the prescriber.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, gas and constipation may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss or persistent symptoms. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor, as it may affect vitamin B12 or magnesium levels and bone health.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also help with nausea or vomiting associated with these digestive symptoms.

How does it work?
Pantoprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps food move through the stomach and can reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Follow the prescribed timing in relation to meals and do not take more than recommended.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, constipation, dizziness or dry mouth.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of heart rhythm problems, heart disease, liver disease or low potassium or magnesium levels. Domperidone can rarely cause serious heart rhythm problems, especially with higher doses or certain medicines. Seek medical help for fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting or severe dizziness. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially antibiotics, antifungals or medicines affecting heart rhythm.

What is it used for?
Used to reduce excess stomach acid and relieve acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also help with associated nausea, vomiting, bloating or indigestion when prescribed.

How does it work?
Pantoprazole reduces the production of acid in the stomach. Domperidone helps stomach contents move forward and can reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the enteric-coated tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is generally taken before meals when directed by a doctor.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, bloating, dry mouth or dizziness.

Precautions
Domperidone may affect heart rhythm. Tell the doctor about any heart disease, irregular heartbeat, fainting, liver disease or electrolyte imbalance, and about all other medicines being taken. Avoid self-treatment or prolonged use. Seek urgent medical help for a fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting, severe dizziness, vomiting blood or black stools.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and fever, such as body aches, muscle or joint pain, toothache and other painful conditions.

How does it work?
Nimesulide reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist, and do not take more or for longer than recommended. It is generally taken after food. Do not use it with other medicines containing paracetamol, nimesulide or similar painkillers unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is liver or kidney disease, stomach ulcer or bleeding, heart problems, or an allergy to painkillers. Avoid alcohol. Do not use during pregnancy, especially the last three months, unless prescribed. Stop taking it and seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, vomiting blood, black stools, breathing difficulty or a serious skin rash.

What is it used for?
Domperidone is used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also help stomach contents move through the digestive system when stomach emptying is delayed.

How does it work?
It blocks dopamine signals involved in nausea and vomiting and helps increase movement of the upper digestive tract.

How to take/use it
Shake the suspension well before use and measure it with the supplied measuring device. Take it exactly as prescribed, usually before meals. Do not use more than directed or for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, headache, abdominal cramps, diarrhoea, and sleepiness may occur.

Precautions
Domperidone can rarely cause serious heart-rhythm problems. Tell the doctor about any heart disease, irregular heartbeat, liver disease, or low potassium or magnesium levels, and about all medicines being taken. It may not be suitable with some antibiotics, antifungals, or medicines that affect heart rhythm. Stop using it and seek urgent medical help for a fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting, seizures, or severe dizziness.

What is it used for?
Micronised progesterone is a natural progesterone hormone. It may be used with oestrogen as part of hormone replacement therapy during menopause, or to support progesterone levels in some menstrual, fertility or pregnancy-related conditions when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It replaces or supplements progesterone in the body. When used with oestrogen during menopause, it helps protect the lining of the womb from excessive thickening.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Swallow the capsule whole with water and follow the prescribed timing and treatment schedule. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice. It may cause drowsiness, so caution may be needed when driving or operating machinery.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, headache, nausea, bloating, breast tenderness and changes in vaginal bleeding or menstrual periods.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about unexplained vaginal bleeding, liver disease, a history of blood clots, breast or reproductive-organ cancer, depression, migraine or allergies. Seek medical help for severe headache, chest pain, breathing difficulty, leg swelling, jaundice or unusual vaginal bleeding. This medicine is not a contraceptive unless specifically prescribed as part of a contraceptive regimen.

What is it used for?
Micronised progesterone is a form of the natural hormone progesterone. It is prescribed for progesterone deficiency, menstrual or uterine-lining problems, support during fertility treatment or early pregnancy, and with oestrogen hormone replacement therapy to protect the lining of the uterus. Its exact use depends on the doctor's prescription.

How does it work?
It replaces or supplements progesterone and helps regulate the menstrual cycle and prepare and maintain the lining of the uterus. When used with oestrogen therapy, it helps prevent excessive thickening of the uterine lining.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed and follow the directions for the route advised, as it may be taken by mouth or used vaginally for different conditions. Do not change the dose, timing or route without medical advice. If taken by mouth, it may cause drowsiness or dizziness, so use caution when driving.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, headache, nausea, bloating, breast tenderness and changes in menstrual bleeding or spotting.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about unexplained vaginal bleeding, liver disease, a history of blood clots, breast or reproductive-organ cancer, or allergies to progesterone. Seek urgent medical help for heavy bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe headache or vision changes, chest pain, breathing difficulty, or painful swelling in a leg. Use during pregnancy only as directed by a doctor; this medicine is not a contraceptive.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain worm and other parasitic infections, including intestinal worm infections. It should be used only for the infection diagnosed or suspected by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Albendazole damages the internal structures of worms, while ivermectin affects their nerve and muscle activity. Together, they help kill or paralyse certain parasites so the body can remove them.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with water. Follow the advised timing and treatment duration, and do not repeat or share the medicine without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and tiredness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding, other medicines or a history of allergic reactions. Use in children only on medical advice. Seek medical help for severe rash, breathing difficulty, yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe abdominal pain, confusion or seizures.

What is it used for?
Telmisartan 40 mg is used to treat high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed to help reduce the risk of certain cardiovascular problems in some high-risk adults.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of angiotensin II, a substance that narrows blood vessels. This relaxes the blood vessels and helps lower blood pressure.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food. Do not stop taking it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, diarrhoea, back pain and low blood pressure may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, dehydration, or high potassium levels. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised. It is not recommended during pregnancy, especially after the first trimester; seek medical advice if pregnancy occurs. Seek urgent help for severe dizziness, fainting, or swelling of the face, lips or throat.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) when treatment with one medicine alone is not enough. Lowering blood pressure helps reduce the risk of stroke and heart-related problems.

How does it work?
Telmisartan relaxes and widens blood vessels by blocking the action of a hormone that raises blood pressure. Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic that helps the kidneys remove extra salt and water from the body.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop taking it without medical advice. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, tiredness, increased urination, nausea, diarrhoea, and changes in blood electrolyte levels may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, dehydration, diabetes, gout, or any allergy to medicines. This medicine should not be used during pregnancy; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Regular blood pressure, kidney function, and electrolyte checks may be needed. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips or throat, difficulty breathing, fainting, or severe dizziness.

What is it used for?
This cream is used for certain inflamed skin infections involving fungi, sometimes with a suspected bacterial infection. It should be used only when prescribed or recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Miconazole stops the growth of fungi, while neomycin acts against some bacteria. Clobetasol is a strong corticosteroid that reduces redness, swelling and itching.

How to take/use it
Apply a thin layer to clean, dry affected skin exactly as directed by the doctor or product label. Wash hands before and after use, unless the hands are being treated. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not cover the area tightly unless advised.

Common side effects
Burning, stinging, irritation, dryness or redness at the application site. Prolonged or improper use may cause skin thinning, stretch marks or changes in skin colour. Neomycin may cause an allergic skin reaction.

Precautions
Clobetasol is a strong steroid; do not use it on large areas, the face, skin folds, groin or broken skin unless specifically advised. Do not use for longer than recommended. Avoid self-treatment of viral skin infections or undiagnosed rashes. Consult a doctor before use in children, during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Stop use and seek medical advice if the infection worsens, spreads, or severe irritation or swelling occurs.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood, bones and joints, and brain coverings. It may also be used before some surgeries to help prevent bacterial infections.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall, which stops the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain or swelling at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, rash, and changes in blood test results may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillin or other antibiotics. Seek medical help for severe rash, breathing difficulty, swelling, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use in newborn babies and in people with liver or kidney problems requires medical supervision. Do not take calcium-containing intravenous products at the same time unless specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by bacteria. The exact infection and treatment plan must be decided by a doctor.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by preventing them from forming a protective cell wall, which stops the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. Do not self-inject or stop treatment early unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Pain, swelling or redness at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; rash; and changes in blood test results.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillin or other cephalosporin antibiotics. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or a widespread rash. Use only when prescribed, as it does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone injection is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin, abdomen, blood, bones and joints, and brain coverings. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking the formation of their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of the infection, so it should be used only as prescribed. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; rash; and changes in liver function tests.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to ceftriaxone, other cephalosporin antibiotics, penicillins or other medicines. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or a widespread skin rash. Use in newborn babies, especially those with jaundice or who may need calcium-containing injections, requires special medical assessment.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the throat, ears, urinary tract and respiratory system. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Disperse the tablet in water before taking if instructed on the product label. It can generally be taken with or without food.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion and vomiting. Skin rash may also occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a widespread skin rash.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming a protective cell wall, which stops the infection from spreading.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the recommended times, and complete the full course even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food. Do not share it or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, indigestion and vomiting may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to cefixime, cephalosporins or penicillin-type antibiotics, or if there is kidney disease. Seek medical help for a severe allergic reaction or severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can lead to resistance.

What is it used for?
Cefixime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, airways and urinary tract. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making their protective cell wall, which kills the bacteria or prevents them from growing.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed. This dry syrup must be prepared with water as directed on the label or by a pharmacist. Shake the prepared suspension well before each dose and measure it with an oral syringe or measuring spoon. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, vomiting and indigestion. Mild rash may also occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to cefixime, other cephalosporin antibiotics or certain penicillin antibiotics. Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, a severe rash, or severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea. Use only for a confirmed or suspected bacterial infection as prescribed.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat certain bacterial infections when prescribed by a doctor. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefixime interferes with the formation of the bacterial cell wall. Ofloxacin blocks enzymes bacteria need to copy and repair their genetic material. Together, they stop the growth of susceptible bacteria.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with water and do not take it with antacids or mineral supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, calcium, iron or zinc at the same time; ask a doctor or pharmacist about suitable timing. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, indigestion, headache, dizziness and rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to cefixime, other cephalosporins, ofloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney disease, heart rhythm problems, seizures, tendon disorders or previous serious reactions to antibiotics. Stop taking it and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, breathing difficulty or a serious skin reaction.

What is it used for?
This prescription injection is used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin and soft tissues, blood, bones or joints. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ceftriaxone kills bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall. Sulbactam helps ceftriaxone work against some bacteria that can resist certain antibiotics.

How to take/use it
It is given by a doctor or nurse as an injection into a vein or muscle. The dose and duration depend on the type and severity of infection, age, and kidney or liver function. Complete the prescribed course unless the doctor advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Pain or swelling at the injection site, diarrhoea, nausea, rash and changes in blood tests may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to ceftriaxone, penicillins, cephalosporins or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, previous antibiotic-related diarrhoea, or allergies. Seek medical help urgently for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Omeprazole reduces excess stomach acid. It is used for acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), and some stomach or duodenal ulcers. It may also be used with other medicines to help treat certain stomach infections or prevent ulcers when prescribed.

How does it work?
Omeprazole blocks the stomach’s acid-producing pumps, reducing the amount of acid released into the stomach.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed by a doctor or as stated on the package. Swallow the enteric-coated capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew it. It is generally taken before food. Do not stop a prescribed course without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation, and gas.

Precautions
Tell a doctor about other medicines being taken, especially blood thinners, certain HIV medicines, or medicines requiring stomach acid for absorption. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, persistent vomiting, unexplained weight loss, vomiting blood, or black stools. Long-term or repeated use should be monitored by a doctor, as it may affect vitamin B12 or magnesium levels and bone health.

What is it used for?
Used to treat acidity, heartburn and acid reflux, especially when these symptoms are associated with nausea, vomiting or delayed stomach emptying.

How does it work?
Omeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps food move through the stomach and can reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually before food. Swallow the capsule whole with water; do not crush or chew the pellets. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, nausea, dry mouth and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heart disease, an irregular heartbeat, or a history of fainting. Avoid taking it with medicines that can affect heart rhythm unless specifically advised. Seek urgent medical help for a fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting, severe allergic reaction, or signs of stomach bleeding. Long-term use should be monitored by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Fluconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections, including vaginal yeast infections and certain other Candida or fungal infections. The exact use depends on the diagnosis.

How does it work?
It stops fungi from making an essential part of their cell membrane, which prevents the fungus from growing and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take extra doses or repeat treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea and skin rash.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is liver or kidney disease, an abnormal heart rhythm, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or an allergy to antifungal medicines. Fluconazole can interact with several medicines. Seek medical help for severe skin rash, swelling, breathing difficulty, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or unusual dark urine.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes when one medicine alone is not sufficient.

How does it work?
Glimepiride helps the pancreas release insulin. Pioglitazone improves the body's response to insulin, while metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and improves insulin sensitivity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or after food. Swallow the prolonged-release tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not skip meals, and do not take an extra dose if one is missed without medical advice.

Common side effects
Low blood sugar, nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, weight gain and swelling of the legs or ankles may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems, heart failure, swelling, bone fractures, or heavy alcohol use. Seek medical help for severe or persistent weakness, breathing difficulty, unusual sleepiness, severe stomach pain, or significant swelling. Monitor blood sugar as advised. Avoid driving if symptoms of low blood sugar occur.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and improves the body's response to insulin. Pioglitazone improves insulin sensitivity, while glimepiride helps the pancreas release more insulin.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and with food to reduce stomach upset. Swallow the extended-release tablet whole; do not crush, chew or split it. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Low blood sugar, nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, weight gain and swelling of the legs or feet.

Precautions
Watch for signs of low blood sugar such as sweating, shaking, dizziness, hunger or confusion. Tell the doctor about kidney, liver or heart problems, swelling, heavy alcohol use, or a history of bladder cancer. Seek urgent medical help for severe low blood sugar, severe weakness, breathing difficulty, unusual muscle pain, or marked swelling. Blood sugar, kidney and liver function may need regular monitoring.

What is it used for?
Used with diet and exercise to help control high blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not used to treat type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis.

How does it work?
Glimepiride helps the pancreas release more insulin. Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and helps the body use insulin more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with a meal, and swallow with water. Take it regularly and do not change the dose or stop it without medical advice. Blood sugar monitoring may be advised.

Common side effects
Low blood sugar, nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, gas and loss of appetite. Low blood sugar may cause sweating, shaking, dizziness, hunger or confusion.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision if there is kidney or liver disease, heavy alcohol use, or a history of severe low blood sugar. Do not skip meals after taking it. Avoid excessive alcohol. Seek urgent medical help for severe or persistent low blood sugar, unusual weakness, breathing difficulty or severe vomiting. Kidney function may need to be checked during treatment.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain and inflammation, such as musculoskeletal, joint or other acute pain. Paracetamol also helps reduce fever.

How does it work?
Paracetamol reduces pain and fever. Diclofenac is an anti-inflammatory medicine that reduces substances in the body responsible for pain, swelling and inflammation.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow the gastro-resistant tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Taking it with or after food may help reduce stomach irritation. Do not take other medicines containing paracetamol or diclofenac unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache. Diclofenac can sometimes cause stomach ulcers or bleeding, and paracetamol can affect the liver if too much is taken.

Precautions
Avoid or seek medical advice before use if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or use of blood thinners. Avoid other NSAID painkillers and excessive alcohol. Do not use during the last 3 months of pregnancy; seek medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic symptoms, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or severe skin reactions.

What is it used for?
Sildenafil is mainly used to treat erectile dysfunction (difficulty getting or keeping an erection firm enough for sexual activity). It may also be prescribed for pulmonary hypertension, but the dose and use differ.

How does it work?
It helps relax blood vessels and increases blood flow to the penis during sexual stimulation, helping produce an erection. It does not increase sexual desire and does not work without sexual stimulation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by a doctor. Do not take more than prescribed or use it more often than directed. It can be taken with or without food, but a heavy or high-fat meal may delay its effect. Do not use it with other medicines for erectile dysfunction unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Headache, flushing, indigestion, blocked or runny nose, dizziness, nausea, and temporary changes in vision.

Precautions
Do not use sildenafil with nitrate medicines for chest pain or with riociguat, as this can cause a dangerous fall in blood pressure. Tell the doctor about heart disease, low blood pressure, recent stroke or heart attack, liver or kidney problems, or use of alpha-blockers. Seek urgent medical help for an erection lasting more than 4 hours, sudden loss of vision or hearing, chest pain, or severe dizziness.

What is it used for?
Levofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, sinuses, urinary tract, skin and other parts of the body. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by blocking enzymes they need to copy and repair their genetic material.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water, with or without food. Take it at least 2 hours before or after antacids or supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, iron or zinc. Do not take more than prescribed.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and difficulty sleeping.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice. Tell the doctor about tendon problems, nerve disorders, seizures, heart rhythm problems, kidney disease, diabetes or a history of severe antibiotic reactions. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or behaviour changes, fainting, irregular heartbeat, severe or persistent diarrhoea, or signs of a serious allergic reaction. Avoid driving if dizzy or having vision problems.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 200 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops bacteria from making the genetic material they need to grow and survive, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc; ask a doctor or pharmacist about suitable spacing.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice. Stop taking it and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, a severe skin rash, breathing difficulty or persistent watery or bloody diarrhoea. Tell the doctor about kidney problems, seizures, heart-rhythm problems, tendon disorders, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
This combination is used to treat certain bacterial and protozoal infections, including some mixed infections of the intestines that may cause diarrhoea or dysentery. It should be used only when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin stops susceptible bacteria from multiplying. Ornidazole damages the genetic material of certain parasites and anaerobic bacteria, helping clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water. Do not self-medicate or use it for ordinary viral diarrhoea or colds. Avoid taking it together with antacids or mineral supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and a metallic or unpleasant taste may occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol during treatment and for the period advised after the last dose. Inform the healthcare professional if pregnant, breastfeeding, or if there is a history of seizures, nerve problems, tendon disorders, kidney disease or heart rhythm problems. Stop taking it and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, severe rash, breathing difficulty or other serious reactions.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. For a DT tablet, disperse it in water as directed on the product label and take it immediately. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not share or reuse leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporins or penicillin-type antibiotics, and about kidney disease. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe skin rash or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Use antibiotics only when prescribed.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, lungs, urinary tract and skin. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
