Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with food. Do not skip doses or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, headache and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to cefpodoxime, penicillins or other cephalosporin antibiotics, or if there is kidney disease. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
This antibiotic combination is used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Cefpodoxime kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming a protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid blocks certain bacterial enzymes that can otherwise reduce cefpodoxime's activity.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow the tablet with water; taking it with food may help absorption and reduce stomach upset. Do not share it or use leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion, headache, or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the prescriber about any previous allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or other antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea, especially if it contains blood. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney problems. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can contribute to resistance.

What is it used for?
Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, throat, sinuses, lungs, skin, or urinary tract, when the bacteria are susceptible to it. It does not work for viral infections such as common colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Reconstitute the dry suspension exactly as directed on the pack or by a pharmacist. Shake well before each use and measure each dose with an oral syringe or measuring spoon. Use it only as prescribed and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not use leftover antibiotic.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion, headache, and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if there has been a serious allergy to cefpodoxime, other cephalosporins, or certain penicillin-type antibiotics. Tell the doctor about kidney disease or previous antibiotic-associated diarrhoea. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Keep the reconstituted suspension and discard it according to the product label.

What is it used for?
Used to provide calcium, active vitamin D (calcitriol) and zinc. It may be prescribed to help prevent or treat calcium deficiency and support bone health when these nutrients are needed.

How does it work?
Calcium helps maintain strong bones and supports normal muscle and nerve function. Calcitriol helps the body absorb calcium, while zinc supports normal growth, tissue repair and immune function.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the soft gelatin capsule whole with water, preferably with food unless advised otherwise. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use additional calcium or vitamin D supplements without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, vomiting or diarrhoea may occur. Excess calcium can cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness or confusion.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, parathyroid disease or a history of vitamin D-related problems. Avoid taking other calcium, vitamin D or zinc products without advice. Seek medical help if severe vomiting, confusion, marked weakness, excessive thirst or frequent urination develops.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine ointment is an antiseptic used to help prevent infection in minor cuts, grazes, wounds and burns.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or reduces many types of bacteria, viruses and fungi on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not swallow it.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, dryness or itching may occur. Stop using it and seek medical help if signs of a serious allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to iodine or povidone iodine. Avoid prolonged or repeated use over large areas, deep wounds or severe burns unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice for deep, heavily bleeding or infected wounds, or if healing does not improve. Use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in people with thyroid problems only after medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used on infected or infection-prone skin wounds, cuts, abrasions and similar affected areas when advised by a healthcare professional. It helps control microorganisms that can cause wound infection.

How does it work?
Povidone iodine acts as a topical antiseptic against many microorganisms. Ornidazole helps act against certain anaerobic bacteria and other susceptible microorganisms.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean and dry the affected area, then apply a thin layer as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Do not apply more often or for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Mild burning, stinging, redness, itching or skin irritation may occur. Stop use and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling or an allergic reaction develops.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to povidone iodine, iodine or any ingredient. Avoid applying to large areas, deep wounds or severe burns unless specifically advised. Use medical advice before use in people with thyroid disorders, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or on young children. Seek medical care if the wound is deep, worsening, very painful, spreading redness or does not improve.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine solution is a topical antiseptic used to clean minor cuts, grazes, burns and other minor skin wounds, helping reduce germs and the risk of infection.

How does it work?
It slowly releases iodine, which destroys many types of bacteria, viruses and fungi on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean the affected area and apply the solution as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not swallow or use in the eyes, mouth or other internal areas unless specifically directed. Wash hands after use.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, dryness or itching may occur. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe irritation, swelling or difficulty breathing develops.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to povidone iodine or iodine. Do not use over large areas, deep or serious wounds, or for prolonged periods unless advised by a healthcare professional. Take advice before use in people with thyroid problems, those taking lithium, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, and in young children. Keep away from the eyes and out of reach of children.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine 5% solution is a topical antiseptic used to clean minor cuts, grazes, burns and other small wounds, helping reduce the risk of infection.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or reduces a wide range of bacteria, viruses and fungi on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean the affected area and apply the solution with clean cotton or gauze as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not swallow it or apply it to the eyes.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching or dryness may occur. Stop using it and seek medical help if severe irritation or signs of an allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to povidone iodine or iodine-containing products. Avoid prolonged or repeated use over large areas, particularly in people with thyroid problems, kidney problems or very young children, unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice for deep, extensive or seriously infected wounds.

What is it used for?
Povidone iodine 5% solution is a topical antiseptic used to clean minor cuts, grazes, superficial wounds and burns, and help reduce the risk of infection.

How does it work?
It releases iodine, which kills or inactivates many types of bacteria, viruses and fungi on the skin.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Clean the affected area and apply the solution as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Avoid contact with the eyes and do not swallow it.

Common side effects
Temporary stinging, skin irritation, redness, dryness or itching may occur. Stop use and seek medical advice if a severe rash, swelling or breathing difficulty develops.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to povidone iodine or other iodine-containing products. Avoid prolonged or repeated use over large areas, deep wounds or severe burns unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice before use in people with thyroid problems, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or in young infants. Seek medical care for deep, heavily contaminated or worsening wounds.

What is it used for?
This supplement is used to prevent or treat deficiencies of vitamin B12, folate and vitamin B6. These vitamins support normal red blood cell formation, nerve function and DNA production.

How does it work?
Methylcobalamin, L-methylfolate and pyridoxal-5-phosphate are active forms of B vitamins. They help support blood-cell production, healthy nerve function and normal cellular processes.

How to take/use it
Take the capsule exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Swallow it with water and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache or skin rash may occur. Serious reactions are uncommon.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to any of its ingredients. Tell a doctor about other medicines or supplements being taken. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist or if a severe rash, swelling or breathing difficulty occurs.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent and treat dehydration caused by diarrhoea, vomiting, or other fluid loss. It replaces water and important salts lost from the body.

How does it work?
The sodium and glucose help the intestines absorb water more effectively. Potassium and citrate help replace lost electrolytes and support the body's fluid and acid balance.

How to take/use it
Dissolve the powder in the exact amount of clean water stated on the package or provided instructions. Do not mix it with less or more water, and do not take the powder dry. Sip the prepared solution frequently and follow the product instructions for storage and use.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, bloating, or mild stomach discomfort may occur, especially if taken too quickly.

Precautions
Seek medical help for signs of severe dehydration, such as extreme weakness, confusion, very little or no urine, or inability to drink. Medical advice is also needed for persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or diarrhoea in a very young child. People with kidney disease, heart failure, or conditions requiring restricted salt or potassium should consult a doctor before use.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of painful muscle and joint conditions associated with muscle stiffness or spasm, such as back pain, sprains and strains.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces pain and inflammation, while paracetamol provides additional pain relief. Chlorzoxazone acts as a muscle relaxant to help reduce muscle spasm.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow it with water. Do not take more than the recommended dose or combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol or NSAIDs unless advised by a doctor. It may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving if affected.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if allergic to any of its ingredients or if it has previously caused an asthma or allergic reaction. Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, or regular alcohol use. Avoid alcohol and seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin reactions, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or unusual sleepiness. It should generally be avoided during the last three months of pregnancy unless specifically prescribed.

What is it used for?
Aceclofenac 100 mg + Paracetamol 325 mg is used to relieve pain, swelling and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions. It can also help reduce fever associated with pain.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the body chemicals that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and reduce fever.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor, preferably with or after food, and swallow it with water. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness and headache may occur. Stop taking it and seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, facial swelling or breathing difficulty.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, asthma triggered by painkillers, or an allergy to painkillers. Avoid excessive alcohol. It should generally be avoided during the last three months of pregnancy and used during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Aceclofenac 100 mg + Paracetamol 325 mg is used to relieve pain, swelling and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and reduce fever.

Seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe skin reactions, breathing difficulty or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of painful muscle and joint conditions associated with muscle spasm, such as back pain, sprains and strains. It helps reduce pain, inflammation and muscle tightness.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac and paracetamol help reduce pain and inflammation. Thiocolchicoside acts as a muscle relaxant to relieve muscle stiffness and spasm.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by a doctor, preferably with or after food and with water. Do not take more or use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol or additional painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe liver or kidney disease, allergy to painkillers such as NSAIDs, or seizures, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless prescribed. Avoid alcohol, and do not drive or operate machinery if dizzy or drowsy. Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe rash, breathing difficulty or yellowing of the skin or eyes.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and swelling, especially in muscle, joint, bone, dental or other painful inflammatory conditions. It may also help reduce fever because it contains paracetamol.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever, while serratiopeptidase may help reduce inflammatory swelling.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a healthcare professional, preferably with or after food. Swallow the tablet whole with water. Do not take additional paracetamol-containing products or other painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache. Serratiopeptidase may also cause stomach upset.

Seek urgent medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin rash.

What is it used for?
It is used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and swelling associated with muscle and joint problems, injuries, or other painful conditions when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps relieve pain and fever, while serratiopeptidase may help reduce swelling.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with water, preferably with or after food, to reduce stomach irritation. Do not take additional paracetamol- or NSAID-containing medicines unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dizziness or headache may occur.

Avoid this medicine or seek medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure, or allergy or asthma triggered by painkillers. What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of pain, swelling and muscle spasm associated with painful musculoskeletal conditions, such as back, neck or joint pain. It should be used only as prescribed.

How does it work?
Aceclofenac reduces pain and inflammation. Thiocolchicoside helps relax painful, tight muscles and reduce muscle spasm.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and swallow it with water. Do not take it for longer than recommended or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or diclofenac unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea, dizziness and drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is an allergy to NSAID painkillers, a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, or severe kidney, liver or heart disease unless specifically advised by a doctor. Inform the doctor about asthma, high blood pressure, seizures, or use of blood thinners. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless prescribed. Avoid driving or alcohol if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Seek urgent medical help for vomiting blood, black stools, severe allergic symptoms or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, and itchy or watery eyes. It may also be used to relieve itching and hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It is an antihistamine that blocks the action of histamine, a substance released during an allergic reaction. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the package or by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water. Avoid taking it with fruit juice, as this may reduce its effect. If using aluminium- or magnesium-containing antacids, separate them from fexofenadine as advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, dizziness, and mild drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Tell a doctor or pharmacist if there is kidney disease, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Do not take it if allergic to fexofenadine or any of its ingredients. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, persistent, or worsening.

What is it used for?
Fexofenadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or itchy nose, itchy or watery eyes, and skin hives (urticaria).

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a chemical involved in allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the label or by a doctor. Swallow the tablet with water. Avoid taking it with apple, orange or grapefruit juice, as these may reduce its effect. If using antacids containing aluminium or magnesium, ask a pharmacist or doctor about separating their use from fexofenadine.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, dizziness and mild tiredness may occur. Drowsiness is uncommon but possible.

Precautions
Tell a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Avoid driving or operating machinery if dizziness or drowsiness occurs. Seek medical advice if allergy symptoms are severe, persistent or associated with breathing difficulty or swelling of the face, lips or throat.

What is it used for?
Artesunate injection is used for the emergency treatment of severe malaria, including malaria affecting the brain or other organs. It is given in a hospital or healthcare facility and is usually followed by a complete course of oral antimalarial treatment when the patient can take medicines by mouth.

How does it work?
Artesunate rapidly kills malaria parasites in the blood, helping to reduce the severity of the infection.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. It must not be self-administered. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the severity of malaria and must be decided by the treating doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, fever, and pain or reactions at the injection site may occur. Rarely, serious allergic reactions or delayed breakdown of red blood cells can occur.

Precautions
Severe malaria requires urgent hospital treatment. Tell the doctor about any previous reaction to artesunate or other antimalarial medicines. Medical monitoring is needed during and after treatment because delayed anaemia or breakdown of red blood cells may occur. Seek urgent medical attention for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe weakness, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or dark urine.

What is it used for?
Atorvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol and triglyceride levels. It also helps reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It reduces the liver’s production of cholesterol by blocking an enzyme involved in cholesterol formation. This lowers LDL (bad) cholesterol and triglycerides and may increase HDL (good) cholesterol.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Take it regularly and do not stop it without medical advice. Continue any recommended low-fat diet, exercise, and other lifestyle measures.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, indigestion, and muscle aches or joint pain may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, thyroid problems, or a history of muscle problems. Seek medical help for unexplained or severe muscle pain, weakness, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. Inform the doctor about all other medicines because some can interact with atorvastatin. It should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Atorvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol and triglyceride levels. It also helps reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme needed to make cholesterol in the liver. This lowers harmful LDL cholesterol and helps improve the balance of blood fats.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Take it regularly and do not stop it without medical advice. Continue any recommended diet and exercise measures.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, diarrhoea, indigestion, and muscle aches may occur. Seek medical advice promptly for severe or unexplained muscle pain or weakness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, thyroid problems, or a history of muscle problems. Discuss all medicines being taken, as some can interact with atorvastatin. It should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor. Liver tests may be recommended during treatment.

What is it used for?
Atorvastatin is used to lower high cholesterol and triglyceride levels. It also helps reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people at increased cardiovascular risk.

How does it work?
It reduces the liver’s production of cholesterol and helps remove excess cholesterol from the blood.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually once daily, with or without food. Swallow the tablet with water and take it at the same time each day. Continue dietary and lifestyle advice given by the healthcare professional. Do not stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, indigestion, diarrhoea, constipation, and muscle aches may occur. Contact a healthcare professional promptly for unexplained or severe muscle pain, weakness, or dark urine.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about liver disease, heavy alcohol use, thyroid problems, kidney problems, or a history of muscle problems. Avoid use during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless specifically advised. Some medicines and grapefruit products may interact with atorvastatin; check before starting new medicines or supplements. Liver tests may be recommended during treatment.

What is it used for?
Used to manage high cholesterol and elevated triglyceride levels in the blood, helping reduce the risk of cardiovascular complications.

How does it work?
Atorvastatin reduces cholesterol production in the liver, while Fenofibrate helps lower triglycerides and improve cholesterol levels.

How to take/use it
Take orally as prescribed by the doctor. Follow the prescribed schedule and do not change the dose yourself.

Common side effects
Muscle pain, headache, nausea, stomach discomfort and increased liver enzymes.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about liver or kidney problems and any history of muscle disorders. Report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness.

What is it used for?
Amikacin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including certain infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, blood, bones and joints. It is usually used when other antibiotics may not be suitable. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from making proteins needed for their growth and survival.

How to take/use it
Amikacin 100 mg is usually given as an injection or infusion by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment length depend on the type and severity of infection, body weight and kidney function. Do not self-inject or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Pain or redness at the injection site, nausea and vomiting may occur. Serious effects can include reduced urine output, hearing changes, ringing in the ears, dizziness or problems with balance.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Kidney function and, when needed, hearing should be monitored during treatment. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially those that may affect the kidneys or hearing. Seek medical help promptly for hearing loss, severe dizziness, unusual weakness or reduced urination.

What is it used for?
Amikacin is a prescription antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections caused by bacteria that are sensitive to it. It is generally used when other antibiotics may not be suitable or effective.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which prevents them from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Amikacin is usually given by a healthcare professional, and the dose and treatment duration depend on the type of infection and kidney function. Do not self-administer or stop treatment early unless advised.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include pain at the injection site, nausea, dizziness, ringing in the ears, hearing changes and reduced urine output. Kidney damage and hearing or balance problems can be serious.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, hearing or balance problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Kidney function and hearing may need monitoring during treatment. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially other medicines that may affect the kidneys or hearing. Seek medical help for reduced urination, severe dizziness, ringing in the ears or hearing loss.

What is it used for?
Amikacin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including certain infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, blood, bones and joints. It is usually used in hospitals or under close medical supervision when other antibiotics may not be suitable.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins, which kills the bacteria and helps control the infection.

How to take/use it
Amikacin 500 mg is given as an injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The exact dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, body weight and kidney function. Do not self-administer it or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, pain at the injection site and headache may occur. Serious effects can include hearing or balance problems, ringing in the ears, reduced urine output and unusual weakness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney problems, hearing or balance problems, dehydration, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and any allergy to aminoglycoside antibiotics. Kidney function and sometimes hearing should be monitored during treatment. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially those that can affect the kidneys or hearing. Seek medical help promptly for reduced urine, swelling, ringing in the ears, hearing loss, severe dizziness or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Azithromycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the chest, throat, ears, skin and sexually transmitted infections. It does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food unless otherwise directed. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, stomach pain and headache may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to azithromycin or other macrolide antibiotics. Inform the doctor about liver disease, heart rhythm problems, a history of prolonged QT interval, or medicines being taken. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, or signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Azithromycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the chest, throat, sinuses, skin and ears, and some sexually transmitted infections. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, and complete the prescribed course even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food unless otherwise directed. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain, vomiting and headache. These are usually mild.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to azithromycin or other macrolide antibiotics, liver disease, or a history of irregular heartbeat or heart rhythm problems. Seek medical help for severe or persistent diarrhoea, yellowing of the skin or eyes, a fast or irregular heartbeat, or signs of a serious allergic reaction. Inform the doctor about all other medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Azithromycin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some infections of the throat, ears, sinuses, chest, skin and reproductive system. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

It stops susceptible bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the prescribed dose and treatment duration, and complete the course even if symptoms improve. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain and headache may occur.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is a prescription anabolic steroid used mainly to help treat osteoporosis and, in some cases, certain anaemias or conditions involving muscle and protein loss. Its use must be decided by a specialist; it should not be used for bodybuilding or muscle enhancement without medical supervision.

How does it work?
It acts like an anabolic androgen hormone, helping increase protein production and support bone and muscle tissue. It may also stimulate the production of red blood cells.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as a deep injection into a muscle by a healthcare professional. The dose and injection schedule depend on the condition being treated and must be followed exactly as prescribed.

Common side effects
Acne, oily skin, fluid retention, changes in mood or sexual desire, and changes in menstrual periods may occur. Women may develop increased facial or body hair, a deeper voice, or other masculine changes. Liver problems and changes in cholesterol or blood counts can also occur.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about liver, kidney, heart, prostate or breast problems, high blood pressure, diabetes, or a history of abnormal blood counts. Women should report voice deepening, excess hair growth, or menstrual changes promptly, as some effects may be irreversible. Regular medical check-ups and blood tests may be needed. Keep this medicine away from non-medical use or performance enhancement.

What is it used for?
Nandrolone decanoate is an injectable anabolic steroid used under specialist supervision to help manage osteoporosis and, in selected cases, certain types of anemia. It is not intended for bodybuilding or non-medical muscle gain.

How does it work?
It acts on androgen receptors to increase protein production and support bone and muscle tissue. It may also stimulate red blood cell production.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as an injection by a doctor or trained healthcare professional. The dose and treatment schedule depend on the condition being treated; do not self-inject or use it without a prescription.

Common side effects
Acne or oily skin, swelling, changes in mood or sex drive, injection-site discomfort, menstrual changes, increased facial or body hair, and deepening of the voice in women. It may also cause changes in liver function or cholesterol levels.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically directed by a specialist. Tell the doctor about prostate or breast cancer, liver, kidney or heart disease, or any hormonal disorder. Women should report voice changes, increased facial hair or menstrual changes promptly, as some effects may be permanent. Regular medical check-ups and blood tests may be required.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of acidity, heartburn, indigestion and discomfort caused by excess stomach acid. The dimethicone component may also help relieve gas-related bloating and fullness.

How does it work?
Aluminium hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide neutralise excess stomach acid. Dimethicone helps gas bubbles combine and pass more easily, which can reduce bloating.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Antacids may affect the absorption of other medicines, so check with a pharmacist about how to space them apart.

Common side effects
Constipation, loose stools or diarrhoea, nausea, stomach cramps or abdominal discomfort. Side effects are usually mild when used as directed.

Precautions
Ask a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain or unexplained weight loss. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist, worsen or frequently recur. Tell a doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines being taken, as antacids can interact with some medicines. Do not use for a prolonged period without medical advice.

What is it used for?
This supplement helps meet calcium, vitamin D3 and vitamin B12 needs. It supports bone health and may help prevent or correct nutritional deficiencies when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Calcium helps maintain strong bones and supports normal muscle and nerve function. Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium, while vitamin B12 supports normal nerve function and red blood cell formation.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Tell a healthcare professional about all other medicines and supplements being taken.

Common side effects
Constipation, stomach discomfort, bloating, nausea or vomiting may occur. Excessive calcium intake may increase the risk of kidney stones or high calcium levels.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, or high calcium levels. Calcium can affect the absorption of some medicines, including certain thyroid medicines, antibiotics and iron supplements; ask a pharmacist or doctor about suitable separation. Do not take additional calcium or vitamin D supplements unless advised.

What is it used for?
Vitamin D3 60,000 IU is used to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency. It helps support calcium absorption and maintain healthy bones and muscles.

How does it work?
Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium and phosphate from food. These minerals are important for maintaining strong bones and normal muscle function.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Take it by mouth if the product is intended for oral use, and do not take it more often or for longer than recommended. Do not combine it with other vitamin D or calcium supplements unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Usually none when used as directed. Excessive intake may cause nausea, vomiting, constipation, stomach discomfort, unusual thirst, frequent urination or weakness due to high calcium levels.

Precautions
Tell a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high blood calcium levels, or a condition that may increase calcium levels. Avoid taking high-dose vitamin D regularly without medical advice. Seek medical advice if symptoms of excessive calcium intake occur. Inform the doctor about other medicines, especially digoxin, calcium supplements or other vitamin D products.

What is it used for?
Vitamin D3 60,000 IU is used to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency. It helps maintain strong bones and teeth by supporting the body's absorption of calcium.

How does it work?
Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium and phosphate from food. These minerals are needed for healthy bones and muscles.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed or as stated on the product label. This is a high-strength vitamin D product, so do not take it more often or for longer than recommended. Do not take additional vitamin D supplements unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated when used as directed. Excessive intake may cause nausea, vomiting, constipation, stomach pain, weakness, increased thirst or frequent urination.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or a condition that increases calcium levels. Avoid taking more than the recommended amount. Seek medical advice if symptoms of excessive calcium, such as persistent nausea, vomiting, unusual thirst or frequent urination, occur.

What is it used for?
This supplement provides calcium, vitamin D3, vitamin K2, magnesium and zinc to support normal bone and teeth health and help meet nutritional needs when dietary intake is insufficient. It may be used as part of bone-health support, but it is not a substitute for treatment prescribed for osteoporosis or nutrient deficiency.

How does it work?
Calcium and vitamin D3 support bone mineralisation, while vitamin K2 helps activate proteins involved in bone health. Magnesium and zinc support normal bone and mineral metabolism.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Taking it with food may improve tolerance. Keep a gap from other medicines when advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Some people may experience constipation, nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating or diarrhoea. Excessive intake may cause symptoms related to high calcium levels, such as vomiting, unusual thirst or frequent urination.

Precautions
Seek medical advice before use if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, high calcium levels or other mineral-balance problems. Vitamin K2 may interact with warfarin and other vitamin K-sensitive blood thinners. Calcium and magnesium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, including levothyroxine, certain antibiotics and osteoporosis medicines; ask a doctor or pharmacist about suitable timing. Do not combine with other calcium or vitamin D supplements without medical advice.

What is it used for?
Vitamin D3 60,000 IU is used to prevent or treat vitamin D deficiency. It helps support calcium absorption, healthy bones and normal muscle function.

How does it work?
Vitamin D3 helps the body absorb calcium and phosphate from food. These nutrients are important for maintaining strong bones and teeth.

How to take/use it
Take it only in the dose and schedule prescribed by a doctor. This is a high-strength vitamin D product and should not be taken more often than advised. Follow the product instructions regarding food or liquid form.

Common side effects
Usually none when taken as prescribed. Excessive vitamin D may cause nausea, vomiting, constipation, stomach pain, excessive thirst, frequent urination or weakness.

Precautions
Do not take extra vitamin D or calcium supplements without medical advice. Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels or other conditions affecting calcium balance. Seek medical advice if symptoms of excessive calcium develop.

What is it used for?
Used to provide calcium, active vitamin D and zinc supplementation, helping maintain strong bones and teeth and manage or prevent calcium or vitamin D deficiency when prescribed. It may also be used as part of treatment for certain bone conditions.

How does it work?
Calcium supports bones, teeth, muscles and nerves. Calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D, helps the body absorb calcium, while zinc supports normal tissue repair and immune function.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use additional calcium or vitamin D supplements unless advised. Follow the product instructions regarding food and other medicines.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea may occur. Excess calcium can cause increased thirst, frequent urination, weakness or confusion.

Precautions
Use only under medical advice if there is kidney disease, kidney stones, high calcium levels, or a disorder affecting calcium balance. Avoid extra calcium or vitamin D unless recommended. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, as calcium can affect the absorption of some medicines. Seek medical advice if persistent nausea, severe constipation, unusual thirst or frequent urination occurs.

What is it used for?
Used as a calcium and vitamin D supplement to support strong bones and teeth and help prevent or correct low calcium or vitamin D levels.

How does it work?
Calcium provides the mineral needed for bones, teeth, muscles and nerves. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and supports bone health.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than recommended, and check before using other calcium or vitamin D supplements.

Common side effects
Constipation, gas, nausea or stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
Tell a healthcare professional if there is kidney disease, a history of kidney stones, or high calcium levels. Calcium may affect the absorption of some medicines, including certain antibiotics, iron supplements and thyroid medicines; seek advice about suitable spacing. Seek medical advice if severe constipation, vomiting, unusual thirst or frequent urination occurs.

What is it used for?
Hydrocortisone is a corticosteroid used on prescription to replace the body’s natural cortisol or to reduce severe inflammation and overactive immune responses. The exact use depends on the prescribed formulation and medical condition.

How does it work?
It acts like the natural adrenal hormone cortisol. It reduces inflammation and suppresses excessive immune activity.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor and follow the instructions for the supplied formulation and route. Do not self-administer or change the dose. If used for a longer period, it should not usually be stopped suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Possible side effects include indigestion, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, increased blood sugar, fluid retention and increased susceptibility to infections. Side effects depend on the dose, duration and route of use.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, osteoporosis, mental health conditions or any current infection. Avoid close contact with people who have contagious infections and seek medical advice if signs of infection develop. This medicine may mask symptoms of infection and may interact with other medicines or vaccines.

What is it used for?
Triamcinolone acetonide is a corticosteroid injection used to reduce inflammation and allergic reactions. It may be prescribed for inflammatory joint or soft-tissue conditions, severe allergies, and certain skin or other inflammatory conditions, depending on the treatment plan.

How does it work?
It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation, swelling, redness and allergic symptoms.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by a doctor or other trained healthcare professional. The injection route, dose and treatment schedule depend on the condition being treated. Do not self-inject.

Common side effects
Pain or irritation at the injection site, facial flushing, mood changes, difficulty sleeping, indigestion, increased blood sugar and increased blood pressure may occur. Repeated or high-dose treatment can cause other corticosteroid-related effects.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma, osteoporosis, stomach ulcers, mental health conditions or any infection. Corticosteroids can reduce resistance to infection and may affect blood sugar. Avoid live vaccines unless specifically approved by the doctor. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of dry cough along with cold or allergy symptoms such as runny nose and sneezing.

How does it work?
Dextromethorphan reduces the urge to cough. Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that helps relieve symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not take more than recommended, and avoid using it with other cough, cold or allergy medicines containing the same ingredients.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, nausea or stomach discomfort.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol until its effects are known. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitor medicines or within 14 days of stopping them; consult a doctor before use with antidepressants or other serotonin-affecting medicines. Seek medical advice before use in glaucoma, difficulty passing urine or prostate problems. Check suitability for children, pregnancy or breastfeeding with a doctor. Consult a doctor for a persistent, worsening or phlegmy cough.

What is it used for?
Fluoxetine is an antidepressant used mainly to treat depression. It may also be prescribed for obsessive-compulsive disorder, panic disorder, bulimia nervosa and premenstrual dysphoric disorder, as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It increases the availability of serotonin, a chemical messenger in the brain that helps regulate mood and emotions.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Take it at the same time each day. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice, even if feeling better.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, headache, nervousness, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, tiredness, sweating and sexual problems may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about bipolar disorder, seizures, liver disease, bleeding problems or pregnancy. Do not use it with monoamine oxidase inhibitors or certain other medicines unless specifically advised. Seek urgent medical help for suicidal thoughts, severe agitation, unusual mood elevation, serotonin syndrome symptoms such as fever, confusion, muscle stiffness or tremors, or a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to provide iron, folic acid, vitamin B12, calcium and zinc. It may be used to help prevent or treat iron-deficiency anaemia and related nutritional deficiencies when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It supplies nutrients needed for haemoglobin production and healthy red blood cell formation. Calcium and zinc support normal bone, immune and other body functions.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Take with water. If it causes stomach upset, taking it with food may help. Do not take more than recommended, and ask a pharmacist about spacing it from antacids, thyroid medicines or certain antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, diarrhoea and dark-coloured stools may occur.

Precautions
Keep out of reach of children; an iron overdose can be dangerous. Tell a healthcare professional about other medicines or supplements being taken, especially antacids, thyroid medicines and antibiotics. Seek medical advice if anaemia symptoms persist or if severe stomach pain, vomiting or an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Iron 100 mg is used to prevent or treat iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anaemia, which can cause tiredness, weakness and pale skin. It should be used when iron supplementation is recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It supplies iron needed to make haemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around the body.

How to take/use it
Use exactly as directed on the package or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than recommended. Iron products may be taken with food if they cause stomach upset, but follow the product instructions because food and some medicines can reduce absorption.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, diarrhoea and dark or black stools.

Precautions
Keep out of reach of children; accidental iron overdose can be dangerous. Do not use without medical advice if there is iron overload or another type of anaemia. Iron can interact with antacids, calcium supplements, some antibiotics and thyroid medicines, so separate doses as advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice if side effects are severe or persistent.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron, folic acid and vitamin B12 deficiency, including anaemia caused by these deficiencies.

How does it work?
Iron helps the body make haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood. Folic acid and vitamin B12 support the production of healthy red blood cells.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Swallow with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Tea, coffee, milk and calcium-containing products may reduce iron absorption, so avoid taking them at the same time. Ask a pharmacist about the correct timing if taking other medicines.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and dark-coloured stools may occur.

Precautions
Keep out of reach of children, as an iron overdose can be dangerous. Tell a doctor if there is unexplained anaemia, iron overload, stomach or intestinal disease, or a history of allergic reaction to these ingredients. Iron may interact with antacids, calcium supplements, some antibiotics and thyroid medicines; medical advice may be needed about spacing doses. Seek medical advice if side effects are severe or persistent.

What is it used for?
Used to prevent or treat iron and folic acid deficiency, which can contribute to iron-deficiency anaemia. It also provides zinc supplementation when these nutrients are needed.

How does it work?
Iron helps the body make haemoglobin for carrying oxygen in the blood. Folic acid supports the formation of healthy blood cells, while zinc supports normal immune function and other body processes.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than recommended. Iron absorption may be reduced by tea, coffee, milk, calcium supplements or antacids; ask a pharmacist about suitable spacing if using these products.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, diarrhoea and a metallic taste may occur. Iron may make stools appear dark or black.

Precautions
Do not use iron supplements for unexplained anaemia or iron overload unless advised by a healthcare professional. Keep out of reach of children, as accidental iron overdose can be dangerous. Tell a healthcare professional about other medicines or supplements being used, especially antacids, calcium products or antibiotics.

What is it used for?
Ceftriaxone is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as certain infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood, bones and joints, and meningitis. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming a protective cell wall.

What is it used for?

Cefpodoxime stops susceptible bacteria from building their protective cell wall. Clavulanic acid helps protect cefpodoxime from enzymes made by some resistant bacteria, allowing it to work more effectively.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?

It increases the alkalinity of urine, reducing its acidity. This can help relieve irritation and may help prevent or dissolve uric acid crystals.

Use exactly as prescribed or stated on the product label. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. It does not replace antibiotics when a urinary infection is present.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, or a bloated feeling may occur.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice if there is kidney disease, heart failure, high blood pressure, or a need to restrict salt or sodium. Seek medical attention for fever, severe back or side pain, blood in the urine, or persistent urinary symptoms.

What is it used for?

May cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol until the effects are known. Do not use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors or within 14 days of stopping them. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, prostate or urination problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not use in children unless specifically advised. Seek medical advice if the cough lasts or worsens.

What is it used for?
Used as a digestive supplement to help break down food and support digestion. It may be useful when digestive enzyme supplementation is recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
Digestive enzymes help break down carbohydrates, proteins and fats into smaller components that the body can absorb. The vitamins and amino acids provide nutritional supplementation.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Digestive enzyme products are generally taken with meals. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating, gas, diarrhoea or constipation may occur. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Check the ingredients before use, especially if there is a known allergy. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, in children, or if there is an ongoing digestive problem. Consult a healthcare professional if symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
Used as a nutritional supplement to provide vitamins and L-lysine. Its digestive enzymes may help support the breakdown and digestion of food.

How does it work?
Digestive enzymes help break down food into nutrients that the body can absorb. The multivitamins and L-lysine supplement nutrients needed for normal body functions.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Measure the syrup with the provided measuring device, and do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating, loose stools or constipation may occur. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction develop.

Precautions
Check the ingredients before use if there is a known allergy. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other vitamin supplements without medical advice. Seek professional advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is an existing medical condition or regular medication use.

What is it used for?
Used to support digestion and help relieve symptoms such as indigestion, bloating, fullness and gas.

How does it work?
Alpha-amylase helps digest carbohydrates and papain helps break down proteins. Dill, anise and caraway oils have carminative properties that may help reduce intestinal gas and discomfort.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Mild stomach discomfort, nausea, loose stools or diarrhoea may occur. Allergic reactions are possible.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to papain, papaya, dill, anise, caraway or any ingredient. Stop use and seek medical help if swelling, breathing difficulty or a severe rash occurs. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or if symptoms are severe, persistent or recurrent.

What is it used for?
Amoxicillin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as infections of the ear, nose, throat, chest, urinary tract, skin and teeth. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by stopping them from making their protective cell wall, which prevents the infection from growing and spreading.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food; taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics with others.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to amoxicillin, penicillin or related antibiotics. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, or a severe blistering rash. Contact a doctor if diarrhoea is severe, persistent or bloody. Tell the doctor about kidney problems or previous antibiotic-related allergic reactions.

What is it used for?
Enalapril is mainly used to treat high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed to help manage heart failure and reduce strain on the heart.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of an enzyme that narrows blood vessels. This relaxes the blood vessels, lowers blood pressure and makes it easier for the heart to pump.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea and a dry, persistent cough may occur. Dizziness may be more noticeable when starting treatment or after a dose increase.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney disease, dehydration, low blood pressure or high potassium levels. Enalapril must not be used during pregnancy and should be reviewed promptly if pregnancy occurs. Seek urgent medical help for swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing. Blood pressure, kidney function and potassium levels may need monitoring. Tell the doctor about all medicines, especially potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes, diuretics and anti-inflammatory painkillers.

What is it used for?
Enalapril is used mainly to treat high blood pressure. It may also be prescribed to help manage heart failure and reduce strain on the heart.

How does it work?
It is an ACE inhibitor that relaxes and widens blood vessels. This lowers blood pressure and makes it easier for the heart to pump blood.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day. It may be taken with or without food. Do not stop treatment suddenly without medical advice.

Common side effects
Dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea and a dry, persistent cough may occur. Dizziness may be more likely when starting treatment or changing position quickly.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy, especially after the first trimester; inform the doctor immediately if pregnancy occurs. Tell the doctor about kidney disease, low blood pressure, high potassium levels, dehydration or previous swelling of the face, lips or tongue. Seek urgent medical help for difficulty breathing or swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat. Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-containing salt substitutes unless advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Cefotaxime is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious infections caused by susceptible bacteria, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin, abdomen, blood or brain. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills bacteria by preventing them from forming the protective cell wall they need to survive.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given by injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, age, kidney function and medical condition. Use it only as prescribed and complete the treatment as directed.

Common side effects
Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; vomiting; skin rash or itching.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any allergy to cefotaxime, cephalosporins or penicillin-type antibiotics, and about kidney or liver problems. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe skin rash. Contact the doctor if severe or persistent diarrhoea develops during or after treatment. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Cefotaxime is an injectable antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, such as infections of the lungs, urinary tract, abdomen, skin, blood, and brain (meningitis), when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming a protective cell wall. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How to take/use it
Cefotaxime 1000 mg is given as an injection into a vein or muscle by a doctor or nurse. The dose, injection method, and treatment duration depend on the infection and kidney function; use it only as prescribed and complete the recommended course.

Pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site; diarrhoea; nausea; vomiting; and skin rash. Serious allergic reactions can occur rarely.

Precautions
Tell the healthcare professional about any allergy to cefotaxime, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or other beta-lactam antibiotics. Dose adjustment may be needed in kidney disease. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea, especially with blood or fever. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of common cold and flu symptoms such as fever, headache, body aches, blocked or stuffy nose, runny nose and sneezing.

Paracetamol helps reduce fever and pain. Phenylephrine helps relieve nasal blockage, while diphenhydramine reduces allergy-like symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing; caffeine may enhance pain relief.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Do not combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol, diphenhydramine, decongestants or similar cold remedies.

Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, blurred vision, restlessness, difficulty sleeping, increased heartbeat or raised blood pressure may occur.

Precautions

Use medical advice if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, prostate or urinary difficulty, liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, worsen or do not improve. Avoid use with monoamine oxidase inhibitors and check with a healthcare professional before combining with other medicines.

What is it used for?
Cetirizine 5 mg is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny or blocked nose, itchy or watery eyes, and itching or hives on the skin.

How does it work?
It blocks the action of histamine, a substance released during allergic reactions. This helps reduce allergy symptoms and itching.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the package or by a doctor. It may be taken with or without food. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Use the measuring device supplied if it is a liquid medicine.

Common side effects
Sleepiness or drowsiness, tiredness, headache, dry mouth, and nausea.

Precautions
Cetirizine may cause drowsiness in some people; avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid or limit alcohol, as it may increase sleepiness. Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, or during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for signs of a serious allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Trypsin + chymotrypsin is used as an adjunct to help reduce swelling and inflammation associated with soft-tissue injuries, trauma, or after surgery. It should be used only when recommended by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
These are protein-digesting enzymes that are thought to help break down proteins involved in inflammatory swelling, which may support recovery from tissue injury.

Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor. If supplied as a tablet, swallow it whole with water and do not crush or chew it unless instructed. Follow the product instructions about taking it with or without food.

Precautions

What is it used for?
Ciprofloxacin is a prescription antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including some urinary, gastrointestinal, respiratory, skin and other infections. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking enzymes they need to copy and repair their DNA.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course, even if symptoms improve. Swallow with plenty of water. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc; ask a pharmacist how to separate these products. Do not use leftover antibiotics or share them with others.

Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and dizziness. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea.

Precautions
Stop taking it and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, allergic reactions, or irregular heartbeat. Use with caution in people with a history of tendon problems, seizures, heart-rhythm problems, kidney disease or myasthenia gravis. Tell the prescriber about pregnancy, breastfeeding and all other medicines. Avoid unnecessary strenuous exercise during treatment and for some time afterwards because of tendon injury risk.

What is it used for?
This topical medicine is used only when prescribed for certain inflamed skin conditions in which a fungal and/or bacterial infection is present or suspected. It helps reduce inflammation, itching and infection on the affected skin.

How does it work?
Clobetasol reduces skin inflammation and itching. Miconazole acts against fungi, while neomycin acts against some bacteria.

For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the affected area exactly as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Wash hands before and after use, unless treating the hands. This medicine may cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol until its effects are known. What is it used for?
Clopidogrel is an antiplatelet medicine used to help prevent harmful blood clots. It may be prescribed after a heart attack, stroke, certain heart-related conditions, or a coronary stent, as directed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It makes platelets in the blood less likely to stick together and form clots. This helps reduce the risk of further heart attacks and strokes.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. It may be taken with or without food. Take it regularly and do not stop it without medical advice, especially after a heart procedure. Do not take an extra dose if a dose is missed without checking with a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Easy bruising, prolonged bleeding from small cuts, nosebleeds, indigestion, stomach discomfort, or diarrhoea may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of stomach ulcers, bleeding problems, liver disease, or an upcoming surgery or dental procedure. Inform the doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines, especially blood thinners, painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin, and acid-reducing medicines such as omeprazole or esomeprazole. Seek urgent medical help for heavy or unusual bleeding, black stools, blood in vomit or urine, or sudden weakness, confusion, or difficulty speaking.

What is it used for?
Deflazacort is a corticosteroid used to reduce inflammation and calm an overactive immune system. It may be prescribed for certain autoimmune, allergic, inflammatory and other medical conditions, depending on the doctor's diagnosis.

It reduces the activity of substances in the body that cause inflammation and immune reactions.

What is it used for?
Domperidone is used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also help improve symptoms related to slow movement of the stomach when prescribed by a healthcare professional.

What is it used for?

It blocks dopamine signals involved in triggering vomiting and helps increase movement of the upper digestive tract, allowing food to pass through the stomach more easily.

This medicine is used for breathing problems with narrowed airways and thick mucus, such as in asthma, chronic bronchitis or other obstructive airway conditions. It helps relieve breathing difficulty and makes mucus easier to clear.

Doxofylline relaxes the muscles around the airways to help open them. Ambroxol thins and loosens mucus, making it easier to cough out.

It relaxes the muscles around the airways, helping them open and making breathing easier.

It helps small blood vessels resist leakage and supports the action of platelets, which help form blood clots.
