It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from building their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor, following the directions on the label. Complete the prescribed course unless advised otherwise. The dose, timing and duration depend on the infection and the product form.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if there has been a serious allergy to penicillin or related antibiotics. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial or throat swelling, or a severe skin rash. Contact a doctor if severe or persistent diarrhoea develops. Use under medical advice in people with liver or kidney problems.

What is it used for?
This capsule is a dietary supplement used to provide vitamins, minerals, lycopene and antioxidant support when the diet may not provide enough of these nutrients. It is not intended to treat a specific disease unless prescribed by a healthcare professional.

How does it work?
The vitamins and minerals help support normal body functions. Lycopene and other antioxidants help protect cells from oxidative stress.

How to take/use it
Take it only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount or take it with other multivitamin supplements unless advised.

Common side effects
It may cause nausea, stomach upset, constipation or loose stools in some people.

Precautions
Check with a doctor or pharmacist before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is kidney or liver disease or any other medical condition. Tell the healthcare professional about all medicines and supplements being taken, as some vitamins and minerals can interact with medicines. Stop use and seek medical advice if an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Xylometazoline nasal spray is used for short-term relief of a blocked or stuffy nose caused by the common cold, sinus congestion or allergic rhinitis.

How does it work?
It narrows swollen blood vessels inside the nose, reducing swelling and helping air pass more easily.

How to take/use it
Use in the nose exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not use it more often or for longer than recommended, as this can make nasal congestion return or worsen.

Common side effects
Nasal dryness, irritation, burning or discomfort, headache, and sneezing. Congestion may worsen after prolonged or excessive use.

Precautions
Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, hyperthyroidism, diabetes, glaucoma, or pregnancy. Do not share the nasal spray. Seek medical advice if congestion persists or worsens.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and fever, such as body aches, muscle or joint pain, dental pain, or pain after minor injuries.

How does it work?
Nimesulide reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor, preferably after food, and swallow with water. Do not take more than prescribed or use it for longer than advised. Do not combine it with other paracetamol-containing medicines or additional painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is liver disease, severe kidney disease, stomach ulcer or bleeding, or an allergy to its ingredients, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Avoid alcohol and other medicines containing paracetamol. Nimesulide may rarely cause serious liver problems; stop taking it and seek medical help if yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe tiredness, persistent nausea or abdominal pain occurs. Tell a doctor if pregnant, breastfeeding, or taking other medicines.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and fever, including muscle or joint pain, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Nimesulide reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed. Swallow with water, preferably after food. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Do not combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol or nimesulide unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, indigestion, diarrhoea and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Avoid use or seek medical advice if there is liver disease, kidney disease, stomach ulcer or bleeding, allergy to painkillers, or regular alcohol use. Avoid taking other paracetamol-containing painkillers or NSAIDs without medical advice. Stop the medicine and seek medical help if yellowing of the eyes or skin, dark urine, severe skin rash, breathing difficulty, unusual bleeding or severe stomach pain occurs. Use during pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in children only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Nimesulide is used for short-term relief of pain, inflammation and fever, such as muscle or joint pain, toothache or painful injuries. It should be used only as directed by a doctor because of its risk of liver problems.

How does it work?
It is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine (NSAID). It reduces the production of substances that cause pain, swelling and fever.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with or after food, and do not use it for longer than advised. Do not take it together with other painkillers or NSAIDs unless a doctor recommends this.

Common side effects
Nausea, indigestion, stomach pain, diarrhoea, dizziness and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is liver disease, severe kidney disease, a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, or an allergy to NSAIDs, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Avoid alcohol and seek medical help for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, vomiting blood, black stools, breathing difficulty or a serious rash. It is generally avoided during pregnancy, especially the last three months, and should not be used in children unless prescribed.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to treat certain bacterial and protozoal infections, especially infections of the stomach and intestines that may cause infectious diarrhoea or dysentery. It should be used only when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
Norfloxacin stops susceptible bacteria from multiplying. Tinidazole damages the DNA of certain bacteria and parasites, helping eliminate the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course. Swallow with water. Avoid taking it with milk or yoghurt, and keep antacids, iron, calcium or zinc supplements separate as advised by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not drink alcohol during treatment or for 3 days after the last dose.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and a metallic taste.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to norfloxacin, other quinolone antibiotics or tinidazole. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe dizziness, unusual nerve symptoms, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney or liver problems, epilepsy, or use of other medicines. Avoid driving if dizzy or less alert.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 200 mg is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, such as urinary tract, respiratory, skin and other infections when the bacteria are susceptible. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by blocking enzymes they need to multiply and survive.

How to take/use it
Take it only when prescribed and follow the doctor’s instructions. Swallow with water and complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not take it at the same time as antacids or mineral supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, calcium, iron or zinc; separate them as advised by a doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and difficulty sleeping may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it for viral infections or without medical advice. Stop taking it and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, severe or persistent diarrhoea, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, rash, breathing difficulty or a fast or irregular heartbeat. Use only under medical supervision if pregnant, breastfeeding, under 18, or if there is a history of seizures, tendon problems, heart-rhythm disorders or kidney disease. Avoid excessive sun exposure and tell the doctor about all medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections. It does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making the genetic material they need to grow and multiply.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with water, and complete the prescribed course. Do not take it with antacids or mineral supplements containing aluminium, magnesium, iron or zinc at the same time; follow the recommended separation advised by the prescriber or pharmacist. Do not self-medicate or share this antibiotic.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and sleep disturbances may occur.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice. Tell the prescriber about kidney disease, a history of tendon problems, seizures, heart rhythm problems, or pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop the medicine and seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve-related symptoms, fainting, severe diarrhoea, or an allergic reaction. Avoid driving if dizzy or affected.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin 200 mg in sodium chloride 0.9% is an intravenous antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections caused by bacteria that are sensitive to ofloxacin. It does not treat viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic that stops bacteria from making the DNA they need to grow and survive.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given as a slow intravenous infusion by a doctor or nurse. The dose, frequency and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection and the patient's condition. Complete the prescribed course unless a healthcare professional advises otherwise.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, sleep disturbance and pain or irritation at the injection site may occur.

Precautions
Use only under medical supervision. Tell the doctor about allergy to quinolone antibiotics, tendon problems, kidney disease, seizures, heart rhythm problems, diabetes, or pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or nerve symptoms, a serious rash or breathing difficulty, severe or persistent diarrhoea, or palpitations. Avoid unnecessary exposure to strong sunlight during treatment.

What is it used for?
Ofloxacin infusion is an antibiotic used in a hospital or clinic to treat certain serious bacterial infections caused by bacteria sensitive to ofloxacin. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
Ofloxacin stops susceptible bacteria from making and repairing their genetic material, which prevents them from growing and surviving.

How to take/use it
This medicine is given slowly into a vein by a doctor or nurse. The dose and treatment duration depend on the type and severity of infection, kidney function and medical advice. Do not self-administer or stop treatment early unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness and sleep disturbance may occur. Infusion-site discomfort may also occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about allergy to ofloxacin or other quinolone antibiotics, kidney disease, seizures, heart rhythm problems, diabetes, tendon disorders or nerve problems. Seek medical help for tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, severe mood or neurological changes, irregular heartbeat, severe allergic symptoms or persistent watery or bloody diarrhoea. Avoid driving if dizzy or affected by vision or nervous-system symptoms.

What is it used for?
Used as a dietary supplement to provide omega-3, omega-6 and omega-9 fatty acids and support general nutritional wellness. It is not a substitute for a balanced diet or prescribed treatment.

How does it work?
It supplies essential and non-essential fatty acids that the body uses for normal cell structure and other body functions. Flaxseed oil is a plant source of omega-3 fatty acid, mainly alpha-linolenic acid (ALA).

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label. Do not exceed the recommended amount. It may be taken with food if it causes stomach discomfort.

Common side effects
Mild stomach upset, nausea, loose stools or bloating may occur. Allergic reactions are possible in sensitive individuals.

Precautions
Speak to a doctor before use if taking blood-thinning medicines, having a bleeding disorder or scheduled for surgery. Stop use and seek medical help if signs of an allergic reaction occur. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Omeprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), and stomach or duodenal ulcers. It may also be used with antibiotics to help treat Helicobacter pylori infection, as prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It blocks the stomach’s acid-producing proton pumps, reducing the amount of acid released into the stomach. This helps relieve acid-related symptoms and allows ulcers or irritation to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually before a meal. Swallow the capsule or tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not change the dose or duration without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, constipation, and gas.

Precautions
Tell a doctor about any allergy to omeprazole or other acid-reducing medicines, pregnancy or breastfeeding, liver disease, or long-term use. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss, persistent vomiting, or severe or ongoing symptoms. Omeprazole can interact with some medicines, including certain HIV medicines, blood thinners, and antiplatelet medicines; provide a complete list of medicines being taken.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve acidity and acid reflux symptoms such as heartburn, sour regurgitation and indigestion. It may also help when these symptoms are accompanied by nausea, bloating or a feeling of fullness.

How does it work?
Omeprazole reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Domperidone helps stomach contents move forward and can reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed by the doctor. It is generally taken before food. Swallow the medicine whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not take an extra dose if one is missed without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, stomach pain or discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, nausea, dizziness and dry mouth may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about heart rhythm problems, heart or liver disease, or any history of stomach or intestinal blockage or bleeding. Inform the doctor about all medicines being taken, especially medicines that can affect heart rhythm. Seek urgent medical help for fainting, a fast or irregular heartbeat, vomiting blood or black stools. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin to relieve pain and inflammation in muscles and joints, including sprains, strains and arthritis-related pain.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling or warming sensation that may help soothe the painful area.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the painful area and gently rub in, following the product label or healthcare professional’s instructions. Wash hands after use, unless the hands are being treated. Do not apply to broken, infected or irritated skin, or cover tightly with a bandage.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or rash at the application site. Stop use if severe irritation or an allergic reaction occurs.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other mucous membranes. Do not use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other NSAIDs or salicylates. Avoid using with other diclofenac, pain-relief or NSAID products unless advised by a healthcare professional. Ask a healthcare professional before use during pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, or while breastfeeding. Keep away from children and avoid applying heat over the treated area.

What is it used for?
Used on the skin for temporary relief of muscle and joint pain, including pain from sprains, strains and arthritis.

How does it work?
Diclofenac helps reduce pain and inflammation. Menthol and methyl salicylate provide a cooling or warming sensation that may help relieve discomfort.

How to take/use it
For external use only. Apply a thin layer to the painful area and gently rub in, following the product label or medical advice. Wash hands after use unless the hands are being treated. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin.

Common side effects
Mild skin irritation, redness, itching, burning or a cooling/warming sensation at the application site.

Precautions
Avoid contact with the eyes, mouth and other sensitive areas. Do not use under a tight bandage or with heating pads. Stop use if severe skin irritation, rash, swelling or breathing difficulty occurs. Avoid use if allergic to diclofenac, aspirin, other NSAID painkillers or salicylates. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy, especially in the last three months, or if breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Cephalexin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the skin, throat, ears, urinary tract and respiratory tract. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food; taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, diarrhoea, stomach pain and vomiting may occur. Mild skin rash can also occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous allergy to cephalexin, penicillins or other antibiotics. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea. Dose adjustment or medical monitoring may be needed in kidney disease. Use only when prescribed, especially during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

What is it used for?
Cephalexin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the skin, throat, ears, urinary tract and respiratory tract. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming a protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food; taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is an allergy to cephalexin, penicillins or other cephalosporin antibiotics, or if there is kidney disease. Seek urgent medical help for breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a severe rash. Contact a doctor if severe, persistent or bloody diarrhoea develops during or after treatment. Use only when prescribed, as unnecessary antibiotic use can lead to resistance.

What is it used for?
Cephalexin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the skin, throat, ears, urinary tract and respiratory tract. It does not work for viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming a protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the full course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food; taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain and skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cephalexin or other cephalosporin antibiotics. Tell the doctor about any allergy to penicillin or other antibiotics, kidney problems, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Cephalexin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections, including infections of the skin, throat, lungs, ears and urinary tract. It does not work against viral infections such as colds or flu.

How does it work?
It kills susceptible bacteria by preventing them from forming their protective cell wall.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. It may be taken with or without food; taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Do not share leftover antibiotics or use them without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain and mild skin rash.

Precautions
Do not take it if there has been a serious allergy to cephalexin, penicillin or other cephalosporin antibiotics unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about kidney disease or a previous history of severe antibiotic-related diarrhoea. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, swelling of the face or throat, severe rash, or severe or persistent diarrhoea.

What is it used for?
Orlistat is used with a reduced-calorie diet and physical activity to help manage obesity and support weight loss in suitable adults.

How does it work?
It blocks enzymes that digest dietary fat in the intestine. This reduces the amount of fat absorbed by the body, so some undigested fat leaves the body in the stools.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed, usually with meals as directed. Follow a reduced-calorie, lower-fat diet to reduce stomach and bowel-related side effects. Do not take more than prescribed. A doctor may recommend a multivitamin because orlistat can reduce absorption of vitamins A, D, E and K.

Common side effects
Oily or fatty stools, increased bowel movements, sudden urge to pass stools, loose stools, gas with discharge, and stomach discomfort or cramps.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor if there is chronic malabsorption, reduced bile flow, liver or kidney disease, or if taking medicines such as warfarin, ciclosporin, thyroid medicines or medicines for seizures. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or allergic symptoms.

What is it used for?
Orlistat is used with a reduced-calorie diet and physical activity to help manage obesity and overweight in suitable adults. It helps reduce the amount of dietary fat absorbed by the body.

How does it work?
Orlistat blocks enzymes in the intestine that digest fat. This prevents some of the fat from being absorbed and removes it from the body in the stool.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, usually with a main meal that contains fat. Follow the product label or doctor’s instructions, and do not take more than recommended. A balanced, reduced-calorie diet is important during treatment.

Common side effects
Oily or fatty stools, loose stools, increased bowel movements, urgent need to pass stool, gas with discharge, abdominal discomfort and accidental leakage of stool. These effects may be worse after high-fat meals.

Precautions
Do not use during pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor if there is chronic malabsorption, cholestasis, gallbladder disease, kidney disease or diabetes. Orlistat can reduce absorption of vitamins and may interact with medicines such as ciclosporin, warfarin, levothyroxine and some medicines for seizures or HIV. Discuss all medicines and supplements with a doctor or pharmacist.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of pain and discomfort from mouth ulcers, sore gums and minor irritation inside the mouth.

How does it work?
Choline salicylate helps reduce pain and inflammation. Lignocaine is a local anaesthetic that temporarily numbs the painful area.

How to take/use it
For use inside the mouth only. Apply a small amount to the affected area as directed on the product label or by a dentist or doctor. Do not swallow large amounts, and wash hands after application.

Common side effects
Temporary numbness or altered sensation in the mouth, mild irritation or stinging at the application site, and changes in taste.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to salicylates, aspirin, lignocaine or other local anaesthetics. Avoid eating or drinking hot food and beverages while the mouth is numb. Use in children only if specifically advised by a doctor or dentist. Stop use and seek medical help if swelling, rash, breathing difficulty or other signs of an allergic reaction occur. Seek dental advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

What is it used for?
Used as an oral rinse to help reduce dental plaque and gum inflammation (gingivitis), while fluoride helps strengthen tooth enamel and protect against tooth decay. Zinc may also help reduce unpleasant mouth odour.

How does it work?
Chlorhexidine reduces the growth of bacteria that contribute to plaque and gum problems. Sodium fluoride strengthens tooth enamel, and zinc can help control odour-causing compounds in the mouth.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a dentist. Rinse around the mouth and spit it out; do not swallow. Do not use more often or for longer than recommended. Keep it separate from toothbrushing if advised, as some toothpaste ingredients may reduce chlorhexidine's effect.

Common side effects
Temporary staining of the teeth or tongue, altered taste, mouth irritation, dryness, or increased tartar may occur, particularly with prolonged chlorhexidine use.

Precautions
Do not swallow. Stop use and seek medical advice if swelling, rash, breathing difficulty, or other signs of allergy occur. Chlorhexidine may cause noticeable staining, so inform the dentist if it is being used for an extended period. Keep out of reach of children, as swallowing fluoride-containing products can be harmful.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used for short-term relief of painful abdominal cramps and spasms, where pain is associated with tightening of the intestinal muscles. Use it only when prescribed, as abdominal pain can have many causes.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain and inflammation. Dicyclomine relaxes the muscles of the intestine, helping to reduce cramping and spasms.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food and a full glass of water to reduce stomach irritation. Swallow the tablet whole and do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Avoid taking other diclofenac, ibuprofen or similar painkillers unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Stomach pain or indigestion, nausea, heartburn, diarrhoea or constipation, dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision and headache may occur.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, severe kidney, liver or heart disease, or allergy or asthma triggered by aspirin or similar painkillers, unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, especially the last 3 months, breastfeeding, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, or use of blood thinners. Avoid alcohol and driving if dizzy or experiencing blurred vision. Seek medical care for black stools, vomiting blood, severe allergic reactions, chest pain, or persistent or worsening abdominal pain.

What is it used for?
Pantoprazole is used to reduce excess stomach acid and treat acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), and stomach or duodenal ulcers. It may also be used with antibiotics to help treat Helicobacter pylori-related ulcers, when prescribed.

How does it work?
It reduces the amount of acid produced in the stomach by blocking the stomach’s acid-producing pumps. This helps relieve heartburn and allows acid-related irritation or ulcers to heal.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually before a meal. Swallow the tablet whole with water; do not crush or chew it. Do not continue long-term use without medical advice.

Common side effects
Headache, diarrhoea, nausea, stomach pain, vomiting, constipation, and gas may occur.

Precautions
Tell a doctor if there is liver disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or a history of allergy to pantoprazole or similar medicines. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss, persistent vomiting, or chest pain. Long-term use should be medically supervised, as it may affect magnesium, vitamin B12, or bone health and may interact with some medicines.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 650 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, body pain, toothache and muscle aches.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of certain chemicals in the brain that cause pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth with water, with or without food, as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than recommended, and do not use it for longer than advised. Avoid taking other medicines that contain paracetamol at the same time.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when used as directed. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not exceed the recommended amount, as too much paracetamol can cause serious liver damage. Consult a doctor before use if there is liver disease, regular alcohol consumption, or use of other medicines containing paracetamol. Stop use and seek urgent medical help for severe skin rash, swelling, breathing difficulty, or symptoms of overdose.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol is used to relieve mild to moderate pain, such as body aches or headache, and to reduce fever.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as directed on the package or by a healthcare professional. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and do not use it together with other medicines containing paracetamol.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when used correctly. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Ask a healthcare professional before use if there is liver disease, regular alcohol use, or use of other medicines. Do not exceed the recommended amount, as too much paracetamol can cause serious liver damage. Stop use and seek medical help for signs of an allergic reaction or a severe skin rash.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 150 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, headache, toothache and pain from minor injuries.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances involved in pain and fever, helping lower temperature and relieve discomfort.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. The appropriate dose depends on age, weight and the product formulation. Do not take more than recommended, and do not use it together with other medicines containing paracetamol.

Common side effects
Paracetamol is usually well tolerated. Nausea, vomiting or a skin rash may occur. Serious allergic reactions are rare.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to paracetamol. Seek medical advice before use if there is liver disease, regular alcohol use or severe malnutrition. Avoid taking other paracetamol-containing products at the same time. Taking more than the recommended amount can cause serious liver damage; seek urgent medical help after an overdose, even if feeling well.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, headache, toothache and muscle pain.

How does it work?
It reduces the production of substances in the body that cause pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take or give it exactly as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not take more than recommended or use it with other medicines containing paracetamol. The appropriate dose may depend on age, weight and the product form.

Common side effects
Side effects are uncommon when used correctly. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to paracetamol. Seek medical advice before use in liver disease, regular alcohol use or severe malnutrition. Do not exceed the recommended dose, as an overdose can cause serious liver damage. Seek urgent medical help if too much has been taken, even if there are no symptoms.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of fever and mild to moderate pain, such as body aches, headache, toothache, muscle pain and pain associated with colds.

How does it work?
Ibuprofen reduces the production of substances that cause pain, swelling and fever. Paracetamol also helps reduce pain and fever through a different mechanism.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Do not take it with other medicines containing ibuprofen or paracetamol.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, indigestion, stomach discomfort, abdominal pain, dizziness or headache.

Precautions
Avoid use if allergic to ibuprofen, paracetamol, aspirin or other NSAIDs. Seek medical advice before use with a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, kidney or liver disease, dehydration, or heart problems. Avoid during the last 3 months of pregnancy unless specifically advised by a doctor. Stop and seek medical help for signs of stomach bleeding, severe allergic reaction, or skin rash.

What is it used for?
Paracetamol 500 mg is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, such as headache, toothache, body pain, muscle pain and period pain.

How does it work?
It helps reduce the production of chemicals in the body that cause pain and fever.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth with or without food, exactly as directed on the package or by a doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it with other medicines containing paracetamol.

Common side effects
Usually well tolerated. Nausea, stomach discomfort or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Do not use if allergic to paracetamol. Seek medical advice before use if there is liver disease, regular heavy alcohol use, or severe malnutrition. Avoid taking other paracetamol-containing products at the same time, as an overdose can cause serious liver damage. Stop use and seek urgent medical help for a severe rash, breathing difficulty, or signs of liver problems.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine reduces excess stomach acid. It is used for acidity and heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), and stomach or duodenal ulcers when prescribed.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the production of stomach acid.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more or use it for longer than recommended. Swallow the tablet with water. Seek medical advice if symptoms continue or return.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhoea, or constipation may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver problems and all other medicines being taken. Seek medical advice for difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools, unexplained weight loss, or persistent symptoms. Ranitidine products have been withdrawn or restricted in many places because of impurity concerns; use only a product approved and supplied by a healthcare professional or pharmacy.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine reduces excess stomach acid. It is used for acidity and heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), and stomach or duodenal ulcers when prescribed by a doctor.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the amount of acid produced.

Take it only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water and do not take more or use it for longer than advised. Ranitidine has been withdrawn or restricted in some countries because of safety concerns; use only a product approved and prescribed in the relevant country.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation, or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, porphyria, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. What is it used for?
Ranitidine reduces excess stomach acid and is used for acidity, heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), and stomach or duodenal ulcers.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the amount of acid produced.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist and follow the product label. Swallow with water and do not exceed the recommended amount. Ranitidine products have been withdrawn or restricted in many countries; use it only if it has been specifically prescribed and is legally approved for use.

Headache, nausea, constipation, diarrhoea, or stomach discomfort.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or other medicines being taken. What is it used for?
Ranitidine reduces excess stomach acid and is used for acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also be prescribed for stomach or duodenal ulcers.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the production of stomach acid.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or pharmacist. Swallow the tablet with water and do not change the dose or treatment duration without medical advice. Ranitidine products have been withdrawn or restricted in many countries because of contamination concerns; do not use old stock and check with a pharmacist that the product is approved and current.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea, and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney or liver disease, a history of porphyria, or an allergy to ranitidine. Seek medical advice for persistent symptoms, difficulty swallowing, unexplained weight loss, vomiting blood or black stools. Check with a doctor or pharmacist before combining it with other medicines.

What is it used for?
This combination is used for acidity, heartburn and acid reflux. It may also help relieve related indigestion, nausea or a feeling of fullness when delayed stomach emptying is involved.

How does it work?
Ranitidine reduces the production of stomach acid. Domperidone helps improve movement of the stomach and intestine and can reduce nausea and vomiting.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the medicine with water and do not take more than the recommended amount. Do not continue it for longer than advised. If a dose is missed, follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist.

Common side effects
Headache, dry mouth, stomach cramps, diarrhoea, constipation or dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Inform the doctor about heart rhythm problems, liver disease, kidney disease, electrolyte imbalance, stomach or intestinal blockage, or gastrointestinal bleeding. Domperidone can rarely cause serious heart rhythm problems; seek urgent medical help for a fast or irregular heartbeat, fainting or severe dizziness. Tell the doctor about all other medicines, especially those that affect heart rhythm or interact with domperidone. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only on medical advice.

What is it used for?
Ranitidine reduces excess stomach acid and is used for acidity, heartburn, acid reflux and stomach or duodenal ulcers.

How does it work?
It blocks histamine H2 receptors in the stomach, reducing the production of stomach acid.

How to take/use it
Use only as prescribed by a doctor. Follow the instructions on the product label; do not change the dose or duration yourself. If this is an injectable product, it should be administered by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach discomfort, constipation or diarrhoea.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about kidney or liver disease, porphyria, allergies, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being used. Seek medical advice for persistent heartburn, difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, black stools or unexplained weight loss. Ranitidine availability or use may be restricted in some countries because of contamination concerns; confirm with a doctor or pharmacist before use.

What is it used for?
This urine pregnancy test card is used to detect human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) in urine, which may indicate pregnancy.

How does it work?
The test detects hCG, a hormone produced during pregnancy, in a urine sample. A visible test result indicates whether hCG has been detected.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the pack. Test with a urine sample, check the result within the stated time, and confirm that the control line appears. Testing too early or using diluted urine may give a false-negative result. If the result is negative but pregnancy is still suspected, repeat the test after a few days or consult a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
This test does not usually cause side effects.

Precautions
Check the expiry date and follow the package instructions carefully. A positive result should be confirmed with a healthcare professional. Medicines containing hCG and testing very early may affect results. Seek medical advice for severe abdominal pain, heavy bleeding or other concerning symptoms, regardless of the test result.

What is it used for?
Rifaximin is an antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections in the intestines, including some cases of infectious diarrhoea or traveller’s diarrhoea. It should be used only when prescribed for the diagnosed condition.

How does it work?
It acts mainly inside the intestine and stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins needed for their growth. Very little of the medicine is absorbed into the bloodstream.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and complete the recommended course. It may generally be taken with or without food, but follow the instructions provided by the doctor or pharmacist. Do not self-medicate for diarrhoea without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, abdominal pain or discomfort, bloating, flatulence, headache and dizziness may occur.

Precautions
Do not use it if allergic to rifaximin or other rifamycin antibiotics. Seek medical advice promptly if diarrhoea is accompanied by high fever, blood in the stool, severe abdominal pain, dehydration, or does not improve. Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop and seek help if signs of a serious allergic reaction occur.

What is it used for?
Rifaximin is a minimally absorbed antibiotic used mainly for certain bacterial intestinal infections that cause diarrhoea, including some cases of travellers’ diarrhoea. It may also be prescribed for irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhoea or to help prevent repeated episodes of hepatic encephalopathy, depending on the doctor’s assessment.

How does it work?
It stops susceptible bacteria from making essential proteins needed for their growth. Very little of the medicine is absorbed into the bloodstream, so it mainly acts inside the intestine.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet with water. It may be taken with or without food unless advised otherwise. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach or abdominal pain, bloating, headache, dizziness and tiredness.

Precautions
Do not use it if there is a known allergy to rifaximin or other rifamycin antibiotics. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, fever, blood or mucus in the stool, or diarrhoea that develops during or after treatment. Tell the doctor about liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being used. Stop and seek urgent help for severe rash, swelling or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Rifaximin 550 mg is mainly used to reduce the recurrence of episodes of overt hepatic encephalopathy, a brain-related complication of serious liver disease. It may also be prescribed for irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhoea (IBS-D) in some adults.

How does it work?
It is an antibiotic that acts mainly inside the intestine and reduces the growth of certain gut bacteria. This can help lower the production of substances that contribute to hepatic encephalopathy and may reduce diarrhoea-related symptoms in IBS-D.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet whole with water. It may generally be taken with or without food, but follow the instructions provided by the prescriber. Do not start, stop or repeat treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, abdominal pain or discomfort, bloating, constipation, diarrhoea, headache, dizziness and tiredness may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about an allergy to rifaximin or other rifamycin antibiotics, severe liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent diarrhoea, fever or blood in the stool, as antibiotic-associated bowel inflammation can occur. Use only under medical supervision, especially when treating hepatic encephalopathy or when liver function is significantly reduced.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to help prevent heart attacks, strokes and other heart-related problems in people with established coronary artery disease, often after a heart attack or coronary stent. It lowers cholesterol and helps prevent harmful blood clots. Use only under medical supervision.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin lowers harmful LDL cholesterol. Aspirin and clopidogrel reduce the ability of platelets to stick together, helping prevent blood clots.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed, at the same time each day, with or without food unless advised otherwise. Do not stop it suddenly or change the dose without medical advice, particularly after a heart attack or stent. Do not take additional aspirin or blood-thinning medicines unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Easy bruising, nosebleeds or other minor bleeding, indigestion, stomach discomfort, nausea, headache and muscle aches.

Precautions
This medicine can increase the risk of serious bleeding. Seek urgent medical help for bleeding that does not stop, black stools, vomiting blood, severe headache or unusual weakness. Tell the doctor about stomach ulcers, bleeding problems, liver or kidney disease, planned surgery or dental procedures. Report unexplained severe muscle pain, weakness or dark urine. Inform the doctor about all medicines, especially blood thinners, painkillers such as ibuprofen, and medicines that interact with clopidogrel. It is generally avoided during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless specifically advised.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to help prevent further heart attacks, strokes and blood-clot-related heart problems in people with coronary artery disease or other established cardiovascular disease. It may also be prescribed after angioplasty or placement of a heart stent. The exact reason for use should be confirmed with the prescribing doctor.

How does it work?
Rosuvastatin lowers harmful LDL cholesterol. Aspirin and clopidogrel reduce the ability of platelets to stick together, helping prevent harmful blood clots.

How to take/use it
Take exactly as prescribed and swallow the tablet whole with water. Take it at the same time each day if possible. Do not stop it without medical advice, especially after a heart stent. Do not take extra doses if one is missed; follow the doctor’s instructions.

Common side effects
Easy bruising or bleeding, indigestion, stomach discomfort, nausea, headache, dizziness and muscle aches may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, liver or kidney disease, bleeding disorders, aspirin allergy, or planned surgery or dental treatment. Avoid starting painkillers such as ibuprofen or other blood thinners unless advised by a doctor. Report unusual or prolonged bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe muscle pain or weakness, or yellowing of the skin or eyes urgently. Rosuvastatin should not be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless specifically advised by a doctor.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold and flu symptoms such as fever, headache, body aches, blocked or runny nose, sneezing and nasal congestion.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and relieve pain. Phenylephrine reduces nasal congestion, while chlorpheniramine helps relieve runny nose and sneezing.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Do not take more than the recommended amount. Do not combine it with other medicines containing paracetamol or similar cold and allergy ingredients.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, blurred vision, nervousness or difficulty sleeping. It may also cause a faster heartbeat or increased blood pressure.

Precautions
Avoid driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy, and avoid alcohol. Consult a doctor before use if there is liver disease, high blood pressure, heart disease, thyroid disease, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine. Seek medical advice during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not combine with other paracetamol-containing medicines.

What is it used for?
This medicine provides temporary relief from common cold symptoms such as blocked or stuffy nose, runny nose, sneezing, headache, body aches and fever.

How does it work?
Paracetamol reduces fever and relieves pain. Phenylephrine helps reduce nasal congestion, while diphenhydramine helps relieve runny nose and sneezing; caffeine may enhance pain relief.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the package or by a doctor. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or other cold and flu ingredients. Do not exceed the recommended amount or duration.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, stomach discomfort, difficulty sleeping, nervousness or palpitations may occur.

Precautions
Avoid driving or operating machinery if drowsy or dizzy. Avoid alcohol. Ask a doctor before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, thyroid disease, difficulty urinating or prostate enlargement. Seek medical advice before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Consult a doctor if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold symptoms such as fever, body aches, runny nose, sneezing and blocked nose.

How does it work?
Paracetamol reduces fever and relieves pain. Chlorpheniramine reduces allergy-like symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose, while phenylephrine helps relieve nasal blockage.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor. Use the supplied measuring device if it is a liquid. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or other cold and flu ingredients.

Common side effects
Sleepiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea and stomach discomfort. Some people may experience a fast heartbeat or restlessness.

Precautions
May cause sleepiness; avoid driving and alcohol until its effects are known. Consult a doctor before use in liver disease, high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma, thyroid problems or difficulty passing urine. Check with a doctor or pharmacist before giving it to children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Do not exceed the recommended dose.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of common cold symptoms such as fever, body aches, headache, blocked or runny nose, sneezing and related nasal congestion.

How does it work?
Paracetamol helps reduce fever and pain. Phenylephrine helps relieve nasal congestion, while chlorpheniramine reduces allergy-like symptoms such as sneezing and a runny nose.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Do not take it with other medicines containing paracetamol or other cold and decongestant ingredients. Do not use it for longer than recommended.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea, stomach discomfort, headache or a fast heartbeat may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving and alcohol if affected. Seek medical advice before use if there is high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine or prostate problems. Ask a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Keep out of children's reach, and seek medical help if symptoms are severe, worsen or do not improve as expected.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve stomach and intestinal cramps or spasms associated with gas, bloating and other digestive discomfort.

How does it work?
Dicyclomine relaxes the muscles of the intestine and reduces painful spasms. Dimethicone helps combine gas bubbles, making trapped gas easier to pass.

How to take/use it
Take by mouth exactly as prescribed or directed on the product label. Do not take more than recommended or use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, nausea and constipation may occur. Dimethicone is generally well tolerated.

Precautions
Use only after medical advice if there is glaucoma, difficulty passing urine or prostate enlargement, intestinal blockage, severe ulcerative colitis, or myasthenia gravis. Dizziness or blurred vision may affect driving. Seek medical advice for severe or persistent abdominal pain, vomiting, swelling, or constipation.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve pain and cramps, especially menstrual cramps. It may also help reduce pain associated with spasms in the abdomen.

How does it work?
Mefenamic acid reduces the production of substances that cause pain and inflammation. Dicyclomine relaxes intestinal and abdominal muscles to reduce spasms and cramping.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Take with or after food and swallow with water. Do not take more than the recommended amount or combine it with other painkillers such as ibuprofen or aspirin unless advised by a doctor.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhoea or constipation, dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision and drowsiness.

Precautions
Avoid this medicine or seek medical advice if there is a history of stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney or liver disease, heart disease, asthma triggered by painkillers, glaucoma, or difficulty passing urine. Inform the doctor if pregnant, especially during the last three months, or breastfeeding. Stop taking it and seek medical help for black stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, breathing difficulty, facial swelling or a serious skin rash.

What is it used for?
It is used to relieve abdominal pain and cramps caused by spasms in the stomach or intestines.

How does it work?
Dicyclomine relaxes spasming muscles in the digestive tract, while paracetamol helps reduce pain.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed or as directed on the label. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and avoid taking other medicines containing paracetamol at the same time.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, constipation, nausea, and drowsiness may occur.

Precautions
Use only with medical advice if there is liver disease, glaucoma, difficulty passing urine or prostate problems, intestinal blockage, or myasthenia gravis. Dizziness or blurred vision may affect driving. Avoid excess alcohol, and seek medical help if severe abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or an allergic reaction occurs.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of abdominal pain and cramps caused by spasms of the intestine or stomach. It helps reduce both the pain and the muscle spasms.

How does it work?
Paracetamol relieves pain, while dicyclomine relaxes the muscles of the stomach and intestine to reduce cramping.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than the recommended amount, and avoid using other medicines containing paracetamol at the same time.

Common side effects
Dry mouth, dizziness, blurred vision, nausea, constipation, or stomach discomfort may occur. Drowsiness or difficulty urinating can also occur.

Precautions
Avoid alcohol and seek medical advice before use if there is liver disease, glaucoma, difficulty urinating, prostate enlargement, bowel blockage, or myasthenia gravis. Avoid driving if dizzy, drowsy, or experiencing blurred vision. Seek medical attention for severe, persistent, or unexplained abdominal pain, or if pain is accompanied by vomiting, blood in the stool, or fever. Do not exceed the recommended paracetamol amount, as overdose can seriously damage the liver.

What is it used for?
Prochlorperazine 5 mg is used to relieve nausea and vomiting. It may also be prescribed for vertigo, which can cause dizziness or a spinning sensation.

How does it work?
It blocks certain chemical signals in the brain involved in nausea and vomiting. It also helps reduce abnormal signals that contribute to vertigo.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed. Swallow the tablet with water, with or without food, unless advised otherwise. Do not take more than prescribed, and do not stop regular treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation and difficulty sleeping may occur.

Precautions
It may cause drowsiness or dizziness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known. Avoid alcohol, as it can worsen drowsiness. Tell the doctor if there is Parkinson’s disease, glaucoma, epilepsy, prostate or urination problems, heart rhythm problems, or severe liver disease. Seek urgent medical help for severe muscle stiffness, uncontrolled movements, fainting, or a high fever with confusion.

What is it used for?
Terbinafine 250 mg is an oral antifungal medicine used to treat fungal infections of the skin, scalp and nails, including ringworm, athlete’s foot, jock itch and fungal nail infections.

How does it work?
It blocks an enzyme that fungi need to make their protective cell membrane. This stops the growth of the fungus and helps clear the infection.

How to take/use it
Take it by mouth exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not take more or use it for longer than directed.

Common side effects
Headache, nausea, stomach upset, diarrhoea, indigestion, rash and changes in taste or smell may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about liver or kidney disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and all other medicines being taken. Liver problems can rarely occur; seek medical advice promptly for yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, unusually pale stools, persistent nausea or severe tiredness. Stop the medicine and seek urgent advice for a severe rash, swelling or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Tramadol 50 mg is a prescription opioid pain reliever used to treat moderate to moderately severe pain when other pain medicines are not sufficient.

How does it work?
It reduces pain by acting on opioid receptors in the brain and spinal cord. It also changes certain chemical signals involved in how the body senses pain.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, with or without food. Do not take more than prescribed or use it for longer than directed. Do not stop regular treatment suddenly without medical advice. Avoid driving or operating machinery until its effects are known.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, constipation, dizziness, drowsiness, headache, dry mouth and tiredness.

Precautions
Tramadol can cause dependence, serious sleepiness and slowed breathing. Avoid alcohol and do not combine it with sleeping tablets, sedatives or other opioid medicines unless specifically advised by a doctor. Tell the doctor about seizure disorders, breathing problems, liver or kidney disease, pregnancy, or use of antidepressants. Seek urgent medical help for very slow or difficult breathing, extreme sleepiness, seizures, confusion or agitation with sweating and fever.

What is it used for?
Tranexamic acid is used to reduce excessive bleeding, especially heavy menstrual bleeding. It may also be prescribed for certain nosebleeds, dental procedures, surgery or other conditions where a doctor needs to control bleeding.

How does it work?
It helps prevent blood clots from breaking down too quickly, allowing bleeding to stop more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor and swallow the tablet with water. Do not take it for unexplained bleeding or use it for longer than advised. The dose and duration depend on the cause of bleeding.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort and headache may occur. Seek medical help for sudden vision changes, chest pain, breathing difficulty, or painful swelling in a leg.

Precautions
Tell the doctor before use if there is a history of blood clots, kidney disease, vision problems, or irregular menstrual bleeding. Medical advice is important during pregnancy or breastfeeding and when using medicines or contraceptives that may increase the risk of blood clots. Stop the medicine and seek urgent medical attention if symptoms of a blood clot or significant vision changes occur.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to reduce heavy menstrual bleeding, including excessive bleeding during periods. It should be used for abnormal or unexplained bleeding only after medical advice.

How does it work?
Tranexamic acid helps prevent the breakdown of blood clots, while etamsylate helps reduce bleeding from small blood vessels and supports clot formation.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not change the dose or duration yourself. If heavy or irregular bleeding continues or returns, seek medical advice to identify the cause.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache, dizziness, or skin rash may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any history of blood clots, stroke, clotting problems, kidney disease, vision problems, or allergy to these medicines. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, leg swelling or pain, or sudden changes in vision. Medical advice is especially important if using combined hormonal contraceptives or if the bleeding is unexplained.

What is it used for?
Tranexamic acid is used to reduce or control excessive bleeding, including heavy menstrual bleeding and bleeding after surgery, injury or dental procedures. The exact use depends on the medical condition and doctor's advice.

How does it work?
It helps prevent blood clots from breaking down too quickly, allowing bleeding to stop more effectively.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed, and swallow the tablet with water. The dose and treatment duration depend on the reason for treatment. Do not take more than prescribed or use it for unexplained bleeding without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about any previous blood clots, kidney disease, seizures or vision problems. Seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, painful leg swelling, severe headache or changes in vision. Seek medical advice if bleeding is unusually heavy, persistent or unexplained.

What is it used for?
This medicine is used to reduce heavy menstrual bleeding and relieve period pain or cramps.

How does it work?
Tranexamic acid helps reduce bleeding by helping blood clots remain in place. Mefenamic acid reduces the substances that cause pain, inflammation and menstrual cramps.

How to take/use it
Take it only as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the tablet with water, preferably with or after food, and do not take more than the recommended amount. Do not use it for longer than advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, indigestion, stomach discomfort, headache and dizziness.

Precautions
Tell the doctor before use if there is a history of blood clots, kidney disease, stomach ulcer or bleeding, asthma triggered by painkillers, or allergy to NSAID painkillers. Inform the doctor about use of blood thinners or hormonal contraceptives. Stop the medicine and seek urgent medical help for chest pain, sudden breathlessness, leg swelling, severe allergic symptoms or vision changes.

What is it used for?
This combination is generally used as a urinary tract health supplement and may help reduce the recurrence of urinary tract infections (UTIs). It is not a substitute for antibiotics when a UTI is present.

How does it work?
D-mannose and cranberry compounds may help reduce the attachment of some bacteria to the urinary tract lining. Potassium magnesium citrate provides citrate salts, which can help make urine less acidic.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Do not exceed the recommended amount. Drink adequate fluids unless fluid restriction has been advised.

Common side effects
Nausea, stomach discomfort, bloating or loose stools may occur. Excessive use may disturb potassium or magnesium levels.

Precautions
Consult a doctor before use if there is kidney disease, heart disease, high potassium levels, or use of medicines that affect potassium or kidney function. Seek medical care for fever, chills, back or side pain, blood in the urine, or persistent burning or urinary symptoms. Use during pregnancy or breastfeeding only after medical advice.

What is it used for?
Nitrofurantoin is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial urinary tract infections (UTIs), especially bladder infections. It is not used for viral infections.

How does it work?
It is concentrated in the urine, where it damages important parts of susceptible bacteria and stops them from growing.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed, preferably with food or milk to reduce stomach upset. Complete the prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Do not change the dose or stop treatment without medical advice.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, diarrhoea, headache, and dark yellow or brown urine may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor if there is kidney disease, G6PD deficiency, liver or lung disease, anaemia, nerve problems, pregnancy, or breastfeeding. Seek medical help for breathing difficulty, persistent cough, yellowing of the skin or eyes, numbness or tingling, severe diarrhoea, or an allergic reaction.

What is it used for?
Ursodeoxycholic acid is used to treat certain liver and bile-flow disorders, including primary biliary cholangitis. It may also be prescribed to dissolve some cholesterol gallstones when the gallbladder is functioning properly.

How does it work?
It improves the composition and flow of bile and reduces the amount of cholesterol released into bile. This can help protect liver cells and gradually dissolve certain cholesterol gallstones.

How to take/use it
Take it exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Swallow the capsule or tablet with water, preferably with food if advised. Treatment may need regular liver tests and follow-up. Do not stop it without medical advice.

Common side effects
Diarrhoea or loose stools, abdominal discomfort, nausea and constipation may occur.

Precautions
Tell the doctor about gallstones, bile-duct blockage, acute gallbladder inflammation or other liver problems. It may not be suitable for calcified stones or a poorly functioning gallbladder. Seek medical advice if severe or persistent abdominal pain, jaundice or worsening diarrhoea occurs. Tell the doctor about pregnancy, breastfeeding and all other medicines; antacids containing aluminium and some cholesterol-binding medicines may reduce its absorption.

What is it used for?
Used for short-term relief of pain and inflammation, especially in muscle, joint and arthritis-related conditions. It may also be prescribed for other painful conditions.

How does it work?
Diclofenac reduces the substances that cause pain, swelling and inflammation. Paracetamol helps reduce pain and fever through a different action.

How to take/use it
Take only as prescribed by a doctor. Take with or after food and swallow with water. Do not take it with other medicines containing diclofenac, paracetamol or other NSAID painkillers unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Indigestion, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, heartburn, dizziness or headache.

Precautions

Tell the doctor if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, an overactive thyroid, or a history of seizures. Seek medical help for worsening breathing difficulty, chest pain, severe palpitations, or an allergic or blistering skin reaction. Consult a doctor before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if allergic to any ingredient.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cough, including cough associated with a cold. It may help soothe throat irritation and loosen mucus.

How does it work?
Diphenhydramine helps reduce cough and allergy-related symptoms, while ammonium chloride and sodium citrate help loosen and clear mucus. Menthol provides a cooling, soothing effect in the throat.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a doctor or pharmacist. Measure the liquid with the supplied measuring device and do not exceed the recommended amount. Do not use for longer than advised if the cough does not improve.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, thickened mucus, nausea or stomach discomfort.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol until the effect is known. Use carefully in older adults and in people with glaucoma, difficulty passing urine, breathing problems or severe liver disease. Check with a doctor or pharmacist before use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Use in children only as directed on the label or by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice for breathing difficulty, high fever, coughing up blood, or a persistent or worsening cough.

What is it used for?
Used for temporary relief of cough and throat irritation, particularly with the common cold. It may help suppress coughing and loosen mucus.

How does it work?
Diphenhydramine helps reduce the urge to cough and may cause drowsiness. Ammonium chloride helps loosen mucus, while sodium citrate and menthol soothe throat irritation.

How to take/use it
Take only as directed on the product label or by a healthcare professional. Use a proper measuring device if it is supplied as a liquid. Do not exceed the recommended amount.

Common side effects
Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, blurred vision, nausea or stomach discomfort may occur.

Precautions
May cause drowsiness; avoid driving, operating machinery and alcohol. Do not combine with other medicines that cause drowsiness unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek advice before use in young children, during pregnancy or breastfeeding, or if there is asthma, breathing difficulty or persistent cough. Seek medical care if the cough is severe, lasts several days or is accompanied by high fever or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
Used to relieve a wet or productive cough with thick mucus and to help open the airways when wheezing or bronchospasm is present.

How does it work?
Ambroxol and guaifenesin help loosen and clear mucus from the airways. Terbutaline relaxes the airway muscles, helping improve airflow.

How to take/use it
Use only as directed by a doctor or according to the product label. Do not take more than the recommended amount or use it for longer than advised. Do not combine with other cough or cold medicines unless advised by a healthcare professional.

Common side effects
Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, diarrhoea, headache, tremors, nervousness, palpitations or a fast heartbeat.

Precautions
Use only on medical advice if there is heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, overactive thyroid, seizures or a history of irregular heartbeat. Consult a doctor during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Stop using it and seek medical help for rash, swelling, severe breathing difficulty or a very fast or irregular heartbeat. Seek medical advice if the cough worsens, lasts several days or is associated with high fever or breathing difficulty.

What is it used for?
A digital thermometer is used to measure body temperature and help identify fever.

How does it work?
It detects body temperature using an electronic sensor and displays the reading on a digital screen.

How to take/use it
Use the thermometer according to the manufacturer’s instructions and the recommended body site. Clean the sensor before and after use, and wait for the reading to stabilise or for the device to signal completion.

Common side effects
None expected when used correctly.

Precautions
Do not use if the thermometer is damaged. Keep it away from children unless supervised, and do not allow them to chew or swallow any part. Follow the manufacturer’s cleaning, storage and battery instructions.

What is it used for?

Its therapeutic action cannot be explained reliably without knowing the product’s dosage form, route of use and approved indication.

Confirm the intended use and route before using. Do not use during pregnancy, in children, or on broken skin unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice if symptoms are severe, persistent or worsening.

What is it used for?
The intended therapeutic use cannot be reliably determined from the ingredients alone. Check the product label or ask a pharmacist before using it.

The action of this combination depends on the product’s formulation and intended use, which cannot be confirmed from the supplied information.

What is it used for?
The supplied ingredient list alone is not sufficient to reliably determine the product’s intended therapeutic use. Check the product label or package directions before use.

The action depends on the product’s intended use and dosage form, which cannot be confirmed from the ingredient list alone.

Use only according to the instructions on the product label. Do not guess the dose, frequency, duration or route of use.

Possible irritation or an allergic reaction may occur in people sensitive to herbal ingredients or essential oils. A reliable side-effect profile cannot be provided without knowing the product form and intended use.

Check the label carefully before use. Avoid use if allergic to any ingredient. Stop using it and seek medical advice if irritation, swelling, breathing difficulty or another allergic reaction occurs.
